ACC 200.title: Introduction to Accounting I
ACC 200.subject: ACC
ACC 200.description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part I.
ACC 200.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

ACC 210.title: Introduction to Accounting II
ACC 210.subject: ACC
ACC 210.description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part II.

ACC 321.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
ACC 321.subject: ACC
ACC 321.description: Accounting process and the application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of cash, receivables, inventories, property plant and equipment, depreciation and depletion, intangibles, and current liabilities.
ACC 321.prereq_raw: ACC 200 and ACC 210 , or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better).

ACC 323.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
ACC 323.subject: ACC
ACC 323.description: Application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of long-term liabilities, investments, contributed capital, retained earnings, accounting changes and errors, income recognition, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and statement of cash flows.

ACC 395.title: Accounting Internship
ACC 395.subject: ACC
ACC 395.description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Term paper and meetings with faculty advisor required.

ACC 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
ACC 399.subject: ACC
ACC 399.description: Reading and research of a special area in major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

ACC 401.title: Federal Individual Income Taxation
ACC 401.subject: ACC
ACC 401.description: Examines federal income tax concepts, such as gross income, exclusions, deductions, exemptions, and tax credits, especially for sole proprietors. Introduces taxation of property transactions. Development of professional writing skills is integral to this course.
ACC 401.prereq_raw: ACC 200 and ACC 210 , or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better).

ACC 407.title: Taxation of Business Entities
ACC 407.subject: ACC
ACC 407.description: A survey of the general concepts, rules, and practices involved in the taxation of sole-proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, and subchapter S corporations.

ACC 409.title: Accounting Information Systems
ACC 409.subject: ACC
ACC 409.description: Accounting systems analysis, control and design in manual and computerized environments. Knowledge and skills of information technology for auditing AIS systems. Hands-on experience with microcomputers and a computerized accounting system.
ACC 409.prereq_raw: ACC 323 (with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 (with C or better).

children.text: ( with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 ( with C or better )

ACC 413.title: Law for the Accountant
ACC 413.subject: ACC
ACC 413.description: Intensive study of areas of law of importance to accountants. Particular attention is given to principles of law relating to contracts, sales, commercial paper, secured transactions, property, legal entities, agency, securities, and accountant’s legal liability.

ACC 415.title: Advanced Financial Accounting
ACC 415.subject: ACC
ACC 415.description: Accounting topics relating to consolidation requirements and introduction to the fundamentals of fund accounting, including the general fund, restricted funds, debt service funds, enterprise funds, general long-term account group, general fixed assets accounting group, and accounting entries for encumbrances.

ACC 416.title: Special Topics in Accounting
ACC 416.subject: ACC
ACC 416.description: Addresses current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester.

ACC 418.title: Auditing
ACC 418.subject: ACC
ACC 418.description: Auditing concepts including standards, objectives and ethics for external auditors. Emphasis on reporting standards, internal control, evidence, statistical sampling, IT audits and assurance. Development of professional writing skills is an integral part of this course.
ACC 418.prereq_raw: ACC 323 and ACC 409 , both with C- or better.

ACC 425.title: Forensic Accounting
ACC 425.subject: ACC
ACC 425.description: Theoretical and real life aspects of forensic accounting. Includes discussions of the legal environment, types of forensic engagements such as, lost earnings, business valuations, fraud, and real world forensic cases.

ACC 465B.title: Accounting Capstone: Managerial Accounting-Tax-Ethics
ACC 465B.subject: ACC
ACC 465B.description: Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Lectures, discussions, case analysis. (B) managerial-tax-ethics; emphasis on instruction in writing; (C) financial-auditing-accounting information systems.
ACC 465B.prereq_raw: ACC 401 (or concurrent) and ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (B); ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (C).

ACC 465C.title: Accounting Capstone: Financial Accounting-Auditing-Accounting Information Systems
ACC 465C.subject: ACC
ACC 465C.description: Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Lectures, discussions, case analysis. (B) managerial-tax-ethics; emphasis on instruction in writing; (C) financial-auditing-accounting information systems.
ACC 465C.prereq_raw: ACC 401 (or concurrent) and ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (B); ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (C).

ACC 602.title: CPA Review-Audit and Attestation
ACC 602.subject: ACC
ACC 602.description: Auditing and Attestation (AUD) section covers the entire auditing process, including auditing procedures, generally accepted auditing standards, standards related to attest engagements, and the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct.

ACC 603.title: CPA Review-The Business Environment and Concepts
ACC 603.subject: ACC
ACC 603.description: The Business Environment and Concepts (BEC) section focuses on business concepts and the significance of a CPA’s professional duties and responsibilities within the larger context of the business environment.

ACC 604.title: CPA Review-The Financial Accounting and Reporting
ACC 604.subject: ACC
ACC 604.description: The (FAR) section focuses on U.S. GAAP, including concepts and standards for financial statements, typical items in financial statements, specific types of transactions and events, accounting and reporting for governmental and other entities.

ACC 605.title: CPA Review-The Regulation
ACC 605.subject: ACC
ACC 605.description: The Regulation section focuses on federal taxation, especially taxation of business entities; individuals, and property taxation, but also tests on business law, business ethics, and professional and legal responsibilities.

ACC 610.title: International Corporate Governance
ACC 610.subject: ACC
ACC 610.description: Understanding of complex and critical issues of international corporate governance, financial reporting, and ethical conduct. Includes corporate governance in the U.S., major European markets, and Asia. Emphasis on internal and external stakeholders, regulators, and gatekeepers.
ACC 610.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ACC 616.title: Accounting Theory and Development
ACC 616.subject: ACC
ACC 616.description: History and theoretical background of accounting standards. Including accounting theories, formulating and testing theories; scientific, pragmatic, syntactic and semantic theories; normative and positive theories. Literature supportive and critical of accounting theories and standards.
ACC 616.prereq_raw: ACC 323 with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 619.title: Information and Assurance and Analytics
ACC 619.subject: ACC
ACC 619.description: Focus on auditing processes, standards, and guidance specific to IT risks. Exposure to advanced IT audit software and its practical application and real world IT audit issues.
ACC 619.prereq_raw: ACC 418 with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 620.title: Global Accounting
ACC 620.subject: ACC
ACC 620.description: Theory and fundamental causes of international variations in accounting. Special emphasis on problems such variations create for financial reporting, control, and decision-making within multinational business enterprises.
ACC 620.prereq_raw: ACC 323 with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 625.title: Accounting and Tax Research
ACC 625.subject: ACC
ACC 625.description: In-depth examination of tax and accounting research, IRC, and SEC procedures. Extensive practice in issue identification, reading and analyzing primary authority, and communicating results. Business Administration students only.
ACC 625.prereq_raw: ACC 460E (or concurrent) with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 631.title: Tax of Partners/Partnerships
ACC 631.subject: ACC
ACC 631.description: Examines advanced topics in federal taxation of partners and partnerships regarding the contribution, operation, and distribution from partnerships and transfers of partnership interests.
ACC 631.prereq_raw: ACC 407 with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 635.title: Advanced Public Sector Accounting
ACC 635.subject: ACC
ACC 635.description: Provides the tools necessary for understanding the principles of fiscal accountability and reporting in governmental and not-for-profit organizations.
ACC 635.prereq_raw: ACC 415 with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 638.title: Estate and Gift Taxation and Planning
ACC 638.subject: ACC
ACC 638.description: Examines estate and gift tax provisions and basic estate planning techniques to save taxes and avoid probate. Overviews generation-skipping transfer taxes and income taxes on estates and trusts.
ACC 638.prereq_raw: ACC 401 with C- or better, or consent.

ACC 639.title: Multijurisdictional Taxation
ACC 639.subject: ACC
ACC 639.description: Examines international, state, and local tax issues. Topics include U.S. International taxation of in- and out-bound transactions, sourcing of income and deductions and nexus.

ACC 648.title: Financial Statements Analysis
ACC 648.subject: ACC
ACC 648.description: Analyses of a firm’s profitability, liquidity, and solvency using ratios and common size financial statements. Students are expected to find strengths and weaknesses of the firm based on their analysis.

ACC 649.title: Data Analytics for Accountants
ACC 649.subject: ACC
ACC 649.description: Introduction to visual analytics. Tableau and Power BI for Excel. Introduction to data processing and blending, data visualization and other visualization techniques. Introduction to PowerQuery, PowerPivot, PowerView, and PowerMap.

ACC 660.title: Analysis and Decision-Making
ACC 660.subject: ACC
ACC 660.description: Integrates learning through analysis and communication of comprehensive business problems. Stresses research, critical thinking, and analytical and communication skills applied to contemporary accounting and tax issues.
ACC 660.prereq_raw: ACC 625 with C- or better (or concurrent), no waiver.

ACC 690.title: Current Topics in Accounting
ACC 690.subject: ACC
ACC 690.description: Concentration on current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester.

ACC 695.title: Accounting Internship
ACC 695.subject: ACC
ACC 695.description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Necessary evaluation reports and meetings with faculty advisor required.

ACC 700.title: Thesis Research
ACC 700.subject: ACC
ACC 700.description: Required for Plan A candidates only; six credit hours required, one must be taken during semester that degree is being awarded.
ACC 700.prereq_raw: MAcc student and School of Accountancy Director approval.

ACC 701.title: Financial Accounting Research
ACC 701.subject: ACC
ACC 701.description: Provides an overview of financial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc.
ACC 701.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD students in Business Administration only.

ACC 702.title: Managerial Accounting Research
ACC 702.subject: ACC
ACC 702.description: Provides an overview of managerial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only.

ACC 703.title: Research in Behavioral Accounting
ACC 703.subject: ACC
ACC 703.description: Provides an overview of accounting research in behavioral accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only.

ACC 704.title: Research in Accounting Information Systems
ACC 704.subject: ACC
ACC 704.description: Provides an overview of accounting research in accounting information systems topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only.

ACC 705.title: Research in Auditing and International Accounting
ACC 705.subject: ACC
ACC 705.description: Provides an overview of accounting research in Auditing and International Accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc.
ACC 705.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

ACC 799.title: Directed Reading and Research
ACC 799.subject: ACC
ACC 799.description: Reading and research in an area of accounting under the direction of faculty member(s).
ACC 799.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD students in Business Administration only.

AMST 110.title: Introduction to American Studies
AMST 110.subject: AMST
AMST 110.description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing through analyses of contemporary American culture and to the main themes and approaches used in American studies and the humanities.

AMST 111.title: Introduction to American Studies Writing
AMST 111.subject: AMST
AMST 111.description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing and information literacy with a focus on American culture and society.

AMST 150.title: America and the World
AMST 150.subject: AMST
AMST 150.description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

AMST 150A.title: America and the World
AMST 150A.subject: AMST
AMST 150A.description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

AMST 201.title: American Experience: Institutions and Movements
AMST 201.subject: AMST
AMST 201.description: Emergence and transformation of laws, ideologies, institutions, and social movements from the 17th-21st centuries. Emphasis on relationships among structures of power, representational practices, belief systems, and social action. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

AMST 202.title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
AMST 202.subject: AMST
AMST 202.description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

AMST 202A.title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
AMST 202A.subject: AMST
AMST 202A.description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

AMST 211.title: Contemporary American Domestic Issues
AMST 211.subject: AMST
AMST 211.description: Current debates in the U.S. over individual rights and nationalism; civil rights, citizenship, and sovereignty; sexuality, law, and religion; economic, racial, and gender equality; public health and environmental justice. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

AMST 212.title: Contemporary American Global Issues
AMST 212.subject: AMST
AMST 212.description: Interdisciplinary and transnational perspectives on global issues including international law and diplomacy; war, diaspora, and refugees; economic underdevelopment and environmental racism; globalization, race, and the feminization of poverty. Writing emphasis.

AMST 220.title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
AMST 220.subject: AMST
AMST 220.description: Histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of Indigenous peoples in U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, Samoans. Emphasis on Hawaiʻi and its relationship to other Indigenous nations.

AMST 220A.title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
AMST 220A.subject: AMST
AMST 220A.description: Histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of Indigenous peoples in U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, Samoans. Emphasis on Hawaiʻi and its relationship to other Indigenous nations.

AMST 225.title: Art and Social Change
AMST 225.subject: AMST
AMST 225.description: Emphasis on students’ oral and written responses to literary, visual, and performing arts, including poetry, visual art, music, film, and dance, with particular attention to the influence of art upon social and political movements.

AMST 301.title: Hip-Hop and American Culture
AMST 301.subject: AMST
AMST 301.description: Survey tracing hip-hop from its Afro-Carribean musical beginnings to contemporary adaptations and interpretations. Students will analyze various materials and will pay attention to the relationships between hip-hop and contemporary social forms.
AMST 301.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

AMST 308.title: Justice and Asian America: Social Movements and the Law in American History
AMST 308.subject: AMST
AMST 308.description: Examination of demands for and the changing nature of justice, historical and contemporary, through court cases, legislation, presidential orders, and social movements that address legal, social, and political definitions of Asian America. Sophomore standing or higher.

AMST 310.title: Japanese Americans: History, Culture, Lifestyles
AMST 310.subject: AMST
AMST 310.description: Explores experiences of Japanese Americans in Hawaiʻi and the U.S.: historical and cultural heritage, biographical portraits, changing family ties, ethnic lifeways, gender relations, local identity, and the future of island living. Emphasis: oral communication skills.

AMST 313.title: African Americans: Issues, Culture, History
AMST 313.subject: AMST
AMST 313.description: Traces the history and culture of African Americans and outlines contemporary issues. Topics include: slavery and racism, community formation and resistance, cultural expression, African American diversity, civil rights, gender and class relations.

AMST 316.title: U.S. Women’s History
AMST 316.subject: AMST
AMST 316.description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work, women in social movements, changing norms regarding gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences of women. Emphasis on ethical issues and oral communication.

AMST 317.title: American Music and Culture
AMST 317.subject: AMST
AMST 317.description: Analysis of a variety of American musical genres and histories through focused writing assignments (record and performance reviews, personal narratives, interviews, research proposals, research papers).
AMST 317.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: second year standing or consent.

AMST 318.title: Asian America
AMST 318.subject: AMST
AMST 318.description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation. Emphasis on ethics.
AMST 318.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

AMST 319.title: America, Hawaiʻi and World War II
AMST 319.subject: AMST
AMST 319.description: Examines WWII as a watershed in American and Hawaiʻi history and culture. Topics include: Pearl Harbor, Japanese American internment, sex and racial tensions, Anti-Semitism and the Holocaust, and the dawn of the Atomic Age.

AMST 320.title: American Environments: Survey
AMST 320.subject: AMST
AMST 320.description: Survey of social, political, and cultural relations in diverse, contemporary American environments, including: island societies, urban centers, suburbs, Indian reservations, farming communities, and national parks. Special emphasis on contemporary environmental issues in Hawaiʻi.

AMST 325.title: Religion and Law in the U.S.
AMST 325.subject: AMST
AMST 325.description: Surveys church-state jurisprudence since the 1940s, with special attention to difficulty of defining religion, and applies the religion clauses to current issues.
AMST 325.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or higher standing, or consent.

AMST 326.title: American Folklore and Folklife
AMST 326.subject: AMST
AMST 326.description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism. Junior standing or higher.

AMST 334.title: Digital America: Online Communities and Virtual Worlds
AMST 334.subject: AMST
AMST 334.description: Seminar on the impact of the digital revolution and virtual communities on American culture and society, with an emphasis on questions of identity and participatory democracy. Open to nonmajors.
AMST 334.prereq_raw: one DH, DA, or DL course, sophomore standing, or consent.

AMST 339.title: Religions in America
AMST 339.subject: AMST
AMST 339.description: Examination of American religious traditions, both historical and contemporary, with an emphasis on the principles of religious liberty, non-establishment, and pluralism. Emphasis on writing and ethics.
AMST 339.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

AMST 340.title: War and Media
AMST 340.subject: AMST
AMST 340.description: Examination of a range of media, including photography, film, print journalism, television, video games, and the internet, as they have shaped popular representations and experiences of war in America from the Civil War through the present.

AMST 343.title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
AMST 343.subject: AMST
AMST 343.description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship with the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of Reconstruction.

AMST 344.title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
AMST 344.subject: AMST
AMST 344.description: Continuation of AMST 343 - American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century .
AMST 344.prereq_raw: AMST 150 or AMST 201 or AMST 202 or AMST 211 or AMST 212 or HIST 151 or HIST 152 ; or consent.

AMST 345.title: Religion and Conflict in American History
AMST 345.subject: AMST
AMST 345.description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion. Sophomore standing or higher.

AMST 348.title: American Design: An Historical Survey
AMST 348.subject: AMST
AMST 348.description: Examination of design in American culture over the last century. Readings in industrial, graphic, interior, architectural, landscape, and user interface design used to study issues of gender, race, and class in the U.S.
AMST 348.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Open to all class standings.

AMST 349.title: Contemporary American Design
AMST 349.subject: AMST
AMST 349.description: Investigates design in contemporary American culture. Graphic, industrial, urban, and user-interface design practices are situated within broader social and economic forces. Modes of design practice, production, and consumption studied as reflection of American society today.
AMST 349.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Open to all class standings.

AMST 350.title: Culture and the Arts in America
AMST 350.subject: AMST
AMST 350.description: Study of the role of the arts in American society and diverse cultural practices in historical and contemporary contexts.

AMST 352.title: Screening Asian Americans
AMST 352.subject: AMST
AMST 352.description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship.
AMST 352.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 353.title: Indigenous Lands and Waters
AMST 353.subject: AMST
AMST 353.description: Examines indigenous practices born of and located in Indigenous places. Analyzes how indigenous knowledge of place informs Indigenous cultural, linguistic, intellectual, and political survivance and sovereignty, and resistance.

AMST 354.title: American Travel Writing
AMST 354.subject: AMST
AMST 354.description: Survey examines the roles that travel writing plays in American identity- and nation-formation, from early colonial history to the present.
AMST 354.prereq_raw: AMST 110 , AMST 150 , AMST 201 , AMST 202 , AMST 211 , or AMST 212 .

AMST 360.title: American Cinema
AMST 360.subject: AMST
AMST 360.description: Introductory history of American cinema from the silent to the digital era, with an emphasis on criticism, genre and style, as well as cultural and sociopolitical context.

AMST 365.title: American Empire
AMST 365.subject: AMST
AMST 365.description: Examines an “American culture of empire” in the context of Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific, exploring ethical issues of settler colonialism and decolonial movements. Emphasis on teaching writing/oral communication.

AMST 373.title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
AMST 373.subject: AMST
AMST 373.description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.

AMST 383.title: Critical Research Methods
AMST 383.subject: AMST
AMST 383.description: Overview of methods and methodologies drawn from various fields (including history, politics, literature, art, law and race, Indigenous, gender, and sexuality studies) for conducting interdisciplinary research. Models of writing from AMST faculty; emphasis on writing.

AMST 401.title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
AMST 401.subject: AMST
AMST 401.description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.
AMST 401.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 405.title: Indigenous Literature and Film
AMST 405.subject: AMST
AMST 405.description: Interdisciplinary, comparative course examining native literary texts (novels, short fiction, poetry), films, etc. that address issues of representation and how native peoples actively resist colonial ideology.

AMST 410.title: Asian American Music Cultures
AMST 410.subject: AMST
AMST 410.description: An exploration of how Asian American music making is related to community formation, labor migration, and cultural sensibilities throughout the 20th century.

AMST 411.title: Japanese Americans: Research Topics
AMST 411.subject: AMST
AMST 411.description: Research and thematic seminar on Japanese American culture, issues, and history.
AMST 411.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 412.title: Gender, Sexuality, and the Geopolitics of Korean Popular Culture
AMST 412.subject: AMST
AMST 412.description: Using South Korean popular culture as a case study, this lecture/discussion/seminar examines the relationship between popular culture and a range of forces including: politics, international relations, military, social movements, fandoms, and industries.
AMST 412.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

AMST 413.title: Regionalism: The South
AMST 413.subject: AMST
AMST 413.description: Definition of a Southern identity and its relation to the larger U.S. culture, using literary and polemical works of 19th- and 20th-century.

AMST 418.title: Hawaiʻi’s Multiculturalism
AMST 418.subject: AMST
AMST 418.description: A multidisciplinary examination of the dynamics of the Hawaiian Islands’ racial and cultural diversity from the perspectives of historical trends, social processes, and contemporary political, social, and economic issues as they impact interracial relations.

AMST 420.title: American Ideas of Nature
AMST 420.subject: AMST
AMST 420.description: The natural world in American thought from Native Americans to modern ecologists.

AMST 423.title: History of American Architecture
AMST 423.subject: AMST
AMST 423.description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.

AMST 425.title: American Environmental History
AMST 425.subject: AMST
AMST 425.description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

AMST 431.title: History of American Workers
AMST 431.subject: AMST
AMST 431.description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

AMST 432.title: Slavery and Freedom
AMST 432.subject: AMST
AMST 432.description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

AMST 433.title: Islands, Empires, and the Arts
AMST 433.subject: AMST
AMST 433.description: Colonialism, neocolonialism, and cultures of resistance in the Caribbean and its North American diaspora through literature, film, and the arts. Focus on political dissent; nation building; historical memory; construction of gender, race. Writing emphasis. Junior standing or higher.

AMST 434.title: Politics in Hawaiʻi
AMST 434.subject: AMST
AMST 434.description: Discussion of modern politics against the background of recent history and major contemporary issues.

AMST 435.title: History of Crime and Punishment
AMST 435.subject: AMST
AMST 435.description: History of American crime and punishment from 18th century to the present. Topics: changing crime patterns, evolving punishment methods, penal reform movements, convict resistance, growth of prison industrial complex, racism, class, and gender.
AMST 435.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 436.title: Gender, Justice and Law
AMST 436.subject: AMST
AMST 436.description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.
AMST 436.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 381 , or consent.

AMST 437.title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
AMST 437.subject: AMST
AMST 437.description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration. Junior standing or higher.

AMST 438.title: Women and Globalization in Asia
AMST 438.subject: AMST
AMST 438.description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
AMST 438.prereq_raw: one of AMST 310 , AMST 316 , AMST 318 , AMST 373 , AMST 455 , POLS 339 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 361 , WGSS 439 ; or consent.

AMST 440.title: Race and Racism in America
AMST 440.subject: AMST
AMST 440.description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

AMST 442.title: Social Movements
AMST 442.subject: AMST
AMST 442.description: Examination of mass mobilization in U.S. history from the Revolution forward, including abolitionism, feminism, civil rights, labor, and more. Concludes with analysis of various community organizing efforts today.

AMST 445.title: Racism, American Culture and Film/ Media
AMST 445.subject: AMST
AMST 445.description: An exploration of the critique of racial ideologies in American film. The course also examines how aggrieved communities develop cultural sensibilities, aesthetic choices and politicized identities through film, video and media work.

AMST 446.title: Gender in Action Cinema
AMST 446.subject: AMST
AMST 446.description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

AMST 448.title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawaiʻi
AMST 448.subject: AMST
AMST 448.description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai’i. The course develops written communication skills.
AMST 448.prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

AMST 448.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

AMST 450.title: Victims, Virtue, and Violence: Studies in American Melodrama
AMST 450.subject: AMST
AMST 450.description: Examination of the history and significance of melodrama as a dominant mode of American cultural production from the early republic to the present, with a focus on issues of race, gender, and national identity.

AMST 451.title: Popular Culture
AMST 451.subject: AMST
AMST 451.description: Major themes, modes, and media of popular or mass culture in the U.S.; emphasis on cultural trends and social implications.

AMST 452.title: The ‘20s and ‘30s
AMST 452.subject: AMST
AMST 452.description: Novelists, painters, poets, jazz musicians as examples of culture of the 1920s and 1930s in America.

AMST 453.title: Culture, Society, and Literature
AMST 453.subject: AMST
AMST 453.description: Literary and non-fictive exploration of the intellectual and moral response of Americans to institutions and culture of 20th-century marketplace economy.

AMST 454.title: Fashioning America
AMST 454.subject: AMST
AMST 454.description: Examines linkages between American identity, representation, labor and capital through fashion theory, clothing discourses and other practices of textile production over history.
AMST 454.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 455.title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
AMST 455.subject: AMST
AMST 455.description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

AMST 457.title: Museum Interpretations
AMST 457.subject: AMST
AMST 457.description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Emphasizes written communication and strategies of interpretive engagement with ethical and social justice issues.

AMST 458.title: Film in American Culture
AMST 458.subject: AMST
AMST 458.description: Comprehensive survey of varieties of film experience from historical and contemporary points of view. Significant attention paid to the development of writing skills and to ethical issues.

AMST 459.title: Sports in America
AMST 459.subject: AMST
AMST 459.description: Sports as reflected in literature, films, and TV. Focus on ethical dimensions of sports and sporting cultures; writing emphasis.

AMST 460.title: Early 20th Century American Art
AMST 460.subject: AMST
AMST 460.description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

AMST 461.title: America’s World Role
AMST 461.subject: AMST
AMST 461.description: Examination of America’s role in modern world affairs, against the background of history, perceptions, and values.

AMST 464.title: America and Africa
AMST 464.subject: AMST
AMST 464.description: American attitudes toward Africa, as well as how Africa has functioned within the dynamics of American culture and history.

AMST 465.title: American Experience in Asia
AMST 465.subject: AMST
AMST 465.description: Examination of various forms of U.S. engagement with Asia, with particular attention to the role of Hawaiʻi as the site, agent, and object of engagement. Emphasis on developing critical reading and expository writing skills.

AMST 469.title: Religion, Sex, and Gender in the U.S.
AMST 469.subject: AMST
AMST 469.description: Examines religious and ethical conflicts about sexuality and gender nonconformity in contemporary America. Students gain knowledge, practical wisdom, and communication skills to negotiate moral disagreement in a pluralistic society.
AMST 469.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 474.title: Preservation: Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific
AMST 474.subject: AMST
AMST 474.description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.
AMST 474.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

AMST 475.title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
AMST 475.subject: AMST
AMST 475.description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/ Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER).
AMST 475.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: AMST, ARCH, and HIS majors only.

AMST 484.title: Senior Research and Community Project
AMST 484.subject: AMST
AMST 484.description: Guides students through a substantial research or community project. Required for AMST majors and open to any student interested in conducting an original project related to American history, society, and culture.

AMST 489.title: World Maritime History
AMST 489.subject: AMST
AMST 489.description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

AMST 490B.title: Topics in American Studies: social structure and interaction
AMST 490B.subject: AMST
AMST 490B.description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment.
AMST 490B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent for (D).

AMST 490D.title: Topics in American Studies: arts and environment
AMST 490D.subject: AMST
AMST 490D.description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment.
AMST 490D.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent for (D).

AMST 499.title: Readings in American Studies
AMST 499.subject: AMST
AMST 499.description: Directed readings and research for majors.

AMST 600.title: Approaches to American Studies
AMST 600.subject: AMST
AMST 600.description: Introductory survey of methodological issues underlying research in American studies and professional academic practices.

AMST 601.title: Patterns of American Cultures
AMST 601.subject: AMST
AMST 601.description: Survey of key texts in American Studies, focusing on cultural origins and development, and advancing professional development.

AMST 610.title: Early America
AMST 610.subject: AMST
AMST 610.description: Interdisciplinary approach to understanding early American culture and history.
AMST 610.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

AMST 611.title: Asian America
AMST 611.subject: AMST
AMST 611.description: The Asian American experience from an interdisciplinary and humanities perspective. Asian American history, literature, media, and theater arts. Comparative study of Hawaiʻi and the Continental U.S.

AMST 612.title: Women in American Culture
AMST 612.subject: AMST
AMST 612.description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

AMST 613.title: Introduction to Cultural Studies
AMST 613.subject: AMST
AMST 613.description: Graduate seminar designed to introduce history students to the multidisciplinary theories that are appropriate to cultural studies.

AMST 614.title: Advanced Topics: American West
AMST 614.subject: AMST
AMST 614.description: Examination of the U.S. colonization of the American West. Topics include: European-indigenous relations, migration and labor, regional literature, frontier ideology, ethnic conflict, and new community formation.
AMST 614.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

AMST 615.title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
AMST 615.subject: AMST
AMST 615.description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

AMST 616.title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
AMST 616.subject: AMST
AMST 616.description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance.
AMST 616.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

AMST 617.title: Social and Cultural Diversity in America
AMST 617.subject: AMST
AMST 617.description: Examination of selected subcultures in America.

AMST 618.title: American Sexualities
AMST 618.subject: AMST
AMST 618.description: Aspects of sexual identity within the context of American culture.

AMST 619.title: Slavery and Modern Memory
AMST 619.subject: AMST
AMST 619.description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts.
AMST 619.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

AMST 620.title: Indigenous Identity
AMST 620.subject: AMST
AMST 620.description: Interdisciplinary and comparative focus on how Indigenous identity is constructed, negotiated, asserted, ascribed, and deconstructed within and without Indigenous communities with attention to the U.S.
AMST 620.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

AMST 623.title: American Architecture
AMST 623.subject: AMST
AMST 623.description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

AMST 624.title: Wilderness in America
AMST 624.subject: AMST
AMST 624.description: American wilderness as both physical setting and social construction.
AMST 624.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

AMST 625.title: Material Culture
AMST 625.subject: AMST
AMST 625.description: Physical artifacts considered as documents of American cultural and regional development.

AMST 626.title: Environment and Society
AMST 626.subject: AMST
AMST 626.description: Technological development in cultural perspective; its relation to the American environment, science, capitalism, public policy, and values.

AMST 632.title: Mass Media
AMST 632.subject: AMST
AMST 632.description: Appraisal of major media of communications in American society with attention to political, educational, cultural, and ethical implications.

AMST 634.title: Technologies of War and Media
AMST 634.subject: AMST
AMST 634.description: Critical examination of the relationship between war and media with particular attention to the overlapping histories of technologies of perception and destruction in the modern era and to the military-entertainment complex today.
AMST 634.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

AMST 635.title: Public History and Commemoration
AMST 635.subject: AMST
AMST 635.description: Approaches to public presentations of history and examination of various ways in which historic memory is constructed in sites such as museums, memorials, and theme parks.

AMST 638.title: American Punishment
AMST 638.subject: AMST
AMST 638.description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex.

AMST 639.title: Advanced Topics in American History: Foreign Relations
AMST 639.subject: AMST
AMST 639.description: Seminar in advanced research and readings: foreign relations.

AMST 640.title: Writing for Publication
AMST 640.subject: AMST
AMST 640.description: Advanced seminar designed to convert graduate research projects into publishable scholarly articles.

AMST 643.title: Revolutions and Social Movements
AMST 643.subject: AMST
AMST 643.description: Examines the role of social movements in transforming American society and culture.

AMST 645.title: Historic Preservation
AMST 645.subject: AMST
AMST 645.description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawaiʻi and the region.

AMST 646.title: Advanced Topics: Social/Cultural/ Intellectual
AMST 646.subject: AMST
AMST 646.description: Readings and research on American social and intellectual history.
AMST 646.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

AMST 647.title: Advanced Topics: Business/Labor/ Technology
AMST 647.subject: AMST
AMST 647.description: Readings and research on American business, labor, and technological history.
AMST 647.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

AMST 649.title: American Intellectual Traditions
AMST 649.subject: AMST
AMST 649.description: Examination of intellectual figures and movements in American history.

AMST 650.title: Field Mastery
AMST 650.subject: AMST
AMST 650.description: Prepares students to achieve specialization in an American Studies-related academic field.
AMST 650.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

AMST 656.title: Topics in American Cinema
AMST 656.subject: AMST
AMST 656.description: Investigation of the formal, social, and industrial development of American cinema, alongside key critical and methodological approaches to the impact and significance of film as a cultural medium.

AMST 659.title: Arts in America: Modern to Post-Modern
AMST 659.subject: AMST
AMST 659.description: Survey of the literature of the field.

AMST 664.title: Transpacific Studies
AMST 664.subject: AMST
AMST 664.description: Critical analysis of regional formation in and across the Pacific and the role of the U.S. therein; migrations within and across the Pacific; political, military, economic, cultural, and environmental dynamics of transpacific exchanges.

AMST 668.title: Globalization and Transnationalism
AMST 668.subject: AMST
AMST 668.description: Examines the socioeconomic and cultural meanings of globalization and transnationalism. Emphasis on how the deployment and flows of power beyond the nation-state have an impact on regional, national, and/or local communities and cultures.

AMST 669.title: Advanced Topics: America and the World
AMST 669.subject: AMST
AMST 669.description: Historical and contemporary issues in America’s global relationships.

AMST 670.title: Comparative Methods in American Studies
AMST 670.subject: AMST
AMST 670.description: Examines approaches to American studies that use comparison as a primary method. Comparison of histories, institutions, of phenomena between the U.S. and another country as well as among communities in the U.S. Graduate standing only.
AMST 670.coreq_raw: AMST 600 or AMST 601 or AMST 602, or consent.

AMST 671.title: Indigenous Curation and Museums: Practice Meets Theory
AMST 671.subject: AMST
AMST 671.description: Seminar explores the history, evolution, and contemporary movement towards indigenous curation within museums, emphasis on the Americas and Oceania, as shaped by colonialism, globalization, multiculturalism, self-determination, and nationalism.

AMST 672.title: 20th Century U.S. Literature
AMST 672.subject: AMST
AMST 672.description: Selected works of 20th-century literature as cultural documents.

AMST 673.title: African American Literature
AMST 673.subject: AMST
AMST 673.description: Cultural and social imagination of blacks and whites as revealed in literature, poetry, and drama.

AMST 679.title: Elements of Style
AMST 679.subject: AMST
AMST 679.description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

AMST 680.title: Historic Building Technology
AMST 680.subject: AMST
AMST 680.description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600-c.1960.

AMST 681.title: Vernacular Architecture
AMST 681.subject: AMST
AMST 681.description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes, and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

AMST 683.title: Museums: Theory, History, Practice
AMST 683.subject: AMST
AMST 683.description: History and theory of museums and related institutions (art galleries, historic houses, zoos, parks). Relationship between museums, collections, and communities. Introduction to governance, planning, legal, and ethical concerns.

AMST 684.title: Museums and Collections
AMST 684.subject: AMST
AMST 684.description: Work of museums and professionals (registrars, collections managers, conservators, curators and others) in the care of collections, interpretive studies of museum displays; field trips.

AMST 685.title: Museums and Education
AMST 685.subject: AMST
AMST 685.description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects.

AMST 686.title: Museum Studies Practicum
AMST 686.subject: AMST
AMST 686.description: Applies coursework in museum studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Museum studies certificate students only.

AMST 688.title: Indigenous Studies Practicum
AMST 688.subject: AMST
AMST 688.description: Applies course work in Indigenous studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty.
AMST 688.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

AMST 690.title: Research Seminar
AMST 690.subject: AMST
AMST 690.description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies graduate courses; emphasis upon research methods.

ANAT 545C.title: Unit VII Anatomy Electives: topics in reproductive biology
ANAT 545C.subject: ANAT
ANAT 545C.description: Advanced study of human anatomy by dissection and individual observation of surgical procedures. (C) topics in reproductive biology.
ANAT 545C.prereq_raw: FMCH 531, MED 531, OBGN 531, PED 531, PSTY 531, SURG 531 or FMCH 532 , MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532 , PSTY 532 , SURG 532 ; or consent.

ANAT 599B.title: Independent Study in Anatomy: Human Gross Anatomy
ANAT 599B.subject: ANAT
ANAT 599B.description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

ANAT 599C.title: Independent Study in Anatomy: Histology
ANAT 599C.subject: ANAT
ANAT 599C.description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

ANAT 599D.title: Independent Study in Anatomy: Research in Anatomy and Developmental Biology
ANAT 599D.subject: ANAT
ANAT 599D.description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

ANAT 603.title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
ANAT 603.subject: ANAT
ANAT 603.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
ANAT 603.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

ANAT 604.title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
ANAT 604.subject: ANAT
ANAT 604.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
ANAT 604.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

ANAT 607.title: Human Embryology
ANAT 607.subject: ANAT
ANAT 607.description: Systematic study of human development, including implantation, placentation, basics of development of each organ system with reference to pertinent congenital anomalies and their surgical repair.
ANAT 607.prereq_raw: ANAT 603 or ANAT 604 . Recommended: gross anatomy course.

ANAT 612.title: Seminar in Anatomy Teaching
ANAT 612.subject: ANAT
ANAT 612.description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses in anatomical sciences, development and evaluation of exams, experience in teaching with audiovisual/computer aids. Open to graduate students in physiology or KRS.

ANSC 200.title: Humans, Animals, and Agriculture
ANSC 200.subject: ANSC
ANSC 200.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to animal agriculture, animal science, and the use of animals by humans. Ethics and importance of human use of animals in agriculture are emphasized.

ANSC 201.title: Principles and Practices of Animal Science
ANSC 201.subject: ANSC
ANSC 201.description: Biology, behavior, and management of animals of economic and social importance. Topics include physiology, genetics, nutrition, reproduction, behavior, care, and management to achieve productivity, performance, and welfare. (lecture, discussion, and field trips)

ANSC 244.title: Comparative Nutrition
ANSC 244.subject: ANSC
ANSC 244.description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.
ANSC 244.prereq_raw: ( ANSC 200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C.

ANSC 301.title: Anatomy of Domestic Animals
ANSC 301.subject: ANSC
ANSC 301.description: Micro and gross anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
ANSC 301.prereq_raw: ANSC 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C.

ANSC 301L.title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
ANSC 301L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 301L.description: Laboratory to accompany ANSC 301 , with an emphasis on teaching scientific and technical writing. Dissection and identification of anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
ANSC 301L.prereq_raw: ANSC 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C.

ANSC 321.title: Applied Animal Nutrition
ANSC 321.subject: ANSC
ANSC 321.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of the principles of nutrition to feeding of farm animals; composition and nutritional value of feed stuffs; nutritional requirements of beef cattle, dairy cattle, horses, poultry, and swine.
ANSC 321.prereq_raw: ( ANSC 201 (or concurrent), and ANSC 244 or FSHN 244 ) with a minimum grade of C.

ANSC 350.title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
ANSC 350.subject: ANSC
ANSC 350.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.
ANSC 350.prereq_raw: ANSC 200 or ANSC 201 or FSHN 181 or FSHN 185 .

ANSC 353.title: Horses and Horsemanship
ANSC 353.subject: ANSC
ANSC 353.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Origin of species, breeds, nutrition, care, management. Lab on management practices with work on light horses.

ANSC 387.title: Laboratory Skills in Animal Science
ANSC 387.subject: ANSC
ANSC 387.description: Provides students with basic and essential laboratory skills required in various fields of animal science such as nutrition, genetics, reproductive physiology, meat science, clinical pathology, parasitology, and animal handling.
ANSC 387.prereq_raw: ( ANSC 200 or ANSC 201 , and BIOL 171 and BIOL 171L and CHEM 161 ) with a minimum grade of D-.

ANSC 430.title: Poultry Production
ANSC 430.subject: ANSC
ANSC 430.description: Students will learn about poultry health and hygiene, husbandry, production, biosecurity, hands-on skills, and recent advances in poultry farming systems for meat and egg production.
ANSC 430.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ANSC 431.title: Beef Production
ANSC 431.subject: ANSC
ANSC 431.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of economic beef production, including beef breeds, selection, breeding, management systems, feeding, and marketing under tropical conditions.
ANSC 431.prereq_raw: ( ANSC 321 and ANSC 445 ) with a minimum grade of C.

ANSC 432.title: Swine Production
ANSC 432.subject: ANSC
ANSC 432.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of efficient pork production, including comparative breed evaluation, breeding, feeding, management, marketing, and business aspects. Problems and practices associated with tropical environment emphasized.

ANSC 433.title: Tropical Dairying
ANSC 433.subject: ANSC
ANSC 433.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles involved in economical milk production in the tropics, including management, recordkeeping, breeds, breeding, selection, culling, feeding, housing, milking, quality control, and raising young animals.

ANSC 445.title: Genetics and Animal Breeding
ANSC 445.subject: ANSC
ANSC 445.description: Review and application of genetic principles to livestock, poultry, companion, aquatic, and laboratory research animals. Current practices and future developments.
ANSC 445.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L or ZOOL 101 / ZOOL 101L , and MATH 140X or higher) with a minimum grade of C. Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent.

children.text: Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent

ANSC 446.title: Genes and Animal Biology
ANSC 446.subject: ANSC
ANSC 446.description: An understanding of animal biology at the level of genes and their regulations; emphasis on gene structure, recombinant DNA, transgenic animals and functional genomics being used for agricultural, nutritional and biomedical sciences. Open to nonmajors.
ANSC 446.prereq_raw: ( ANSC 301 , BIOL 171 or ZOOL 101 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

ANSC 450.title: Aquaculture Production
ANSC 450.subject: ANSC
ANSC 450.description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
ANSC 450.prereq_raw: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445 : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher

ANSC 451.title: Physiology of Domestic Animals
ANSC 451.subject: ANSC
ANSC 451.description: Functions and relationships of organs and organ systems of domestic animals excluding reproduction and lactation. Problem-based learning and case studies are emphasized.
ANSC 451.prereq_raw: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

ANSC 453.title: Animal Diseases and Their Control
ANSC 453.subject: ANSC
ANSC 453.description: Disease problems of livestock, poultry, and companion animals; their economic significance, causes, public health implications, and control.
ANSC 453.prereq_raw: ANSC 200 (or concurrent), and BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L or ZOOL 101 / ZOOL 101L .

ANSC 454.title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology
ANSC 454.subject: ANSC
ANSC 454.description: Development, growth, function, carcass evaluation of muscle tissue.

ANSC 454L.title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology Lab
ANSC 454L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 454L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Livestock and poultry slaughter, carcass evaluation, meat chemistry, muscle physiology and biochemistry, meat microbiology, and meat processing.

ANSC 455.title: Companion Animals and Society
ANSC 455.subject: ANSC
ANSC 455.description: Explore human and companion animal relationships in biological, social, cultural, economic, legal, health, and welfare contexts to prepare students for careers in the various animal-related fields in Hawaiʻi, the Pacific rim, and worldwide. Sophomore standing or higher.
ANSC 455.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

ANSC 460.title: Biology and Culture of Shrimp and Prawns
ANSC 460.subject: ANSC
ANSC 460.description: Aspects of the biology and culture of the freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii and marine shrimp Penaeus (sp) species. Scientific research results and case studies presented and analyzed.

ANSC 462.title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination
ANSC 462.subject: ANSC
ANSC 462.description: Introductory exploration of anatomy, development, and physiology of reproduction of domestic animals and artificial insemination.
ANSC 462.prereq_raw: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C).

ANSC 462L.title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination Lab
ANSC 462L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 462L.description: Reproductive anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, estorus synchronization, breeding soundness, and artificial insemination laboratory, field trips. One week off-island field trip.
ANSC 462L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors or consent.

ANSC 465L.title: Aquaculture Production Laboratory
ANSC 465L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 465L.description: Intensive, hands-on course involving the culture of larvae and juveniles of marine shrimp, freshwater prawns, molluscs, fish, and their food. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing and flexible time for continuous live animal care. Lab fee required.

ANSC 472.title: Comparative Endocrinology
ANSC 472.subject: ANSC
ANSC 472.description: Structure and function of endocrine systems across vertebrate groups, surveying how hormones mediate adaptive responses to dynamic environments and coordinate key aspects of growth, development, metabolism, osmoregulation, and stress.
ANSC 472.prereq_raw: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C).

ANSC 490.title: Aquaculture Business Planning and Entrepreneurship
ANSC 490.subject: ANSC
ANSC 490.description: Practical aspects of planning and developing an aquaculture business from conceptualization to a final business plan. Topics include species/technology, project planning, business structuring, permitting, contracts, production plans, financial planning and analysis, market/competition analysis, capital acquisition, intellectual property and legal issues.
ANSC 490.prereq_raw: ANSC 450 or OCN 450 . Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care.

children.text: Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care

ANSC 491.title: Topics in Animal Sciences
ANSC 491.subject: ANSC
ANSC 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.
ANSC 491.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing.

ANSC 492.title: Field Experience
ANSC 492.subject: ANSC
ANSC 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.
ANSC 492.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior standing in ANSC.

ANSC 499.title: Directed Study or Research
ANSC 499.subject: ANSC
ANSC 499.description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students, generally with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major. Exceptions may be granted for students with high achievement in last three semesters.
ANSC 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing.

ANSC 601.title: The Science of Food Systems
ANSC 601.subject: ANSC
ANSC 601.description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.
ANSC 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANSC 603.title: Experimental Design
ANSC 603.subject: ANSC
ANSC 603.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design of experiments and variance analyses in biological and agricultural research.
ANSC 603.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANSC 641.title: Seminar in Animal Sciences
ANSC 641.subject: ANSC
ANSC 641.description: Topics of current interest and current research related to nutrition, genetics, and physiology.

ANSC 642.title: Advanced Animal Nutrition
ANSC 642.subject: ANSC
ANSC 642.description: An advanced course in the nutrition of mono-gastric, ruminant, avian, and aquatic species. Topics include digestive system structures, utilization of nutrients, energy metabolism, and experimental techniques used in the study of animal nutrition.
ANSC 642.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANSC 643.title: Physiology of Reproduction
ANSC 643.subject: ANSC
ANSC 643.description: Comparative differentiation, development, growth, and function of the reproductive systems of mammals and birds; external factors that influence response; artificial insemination.
ANSC 643.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANSC 644.title: Growth Biology of Meat Animals
ANSC 644.subject: ANSC
ANSC 644.description: Growth and development of meat-producing animals; skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone; protein turnover, lipid metabolism, and bioenergetics; regulation of animal growth.
ANSC 644.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANSC 645.title: Advanced Entomophagy
ANSC 645.subject: ANSC
ANSC 645.description: This advanced course examines the scientific, technological, and socio-economic dimensions of entomophagy–the use of insects and insect-derived materials as sustainable sources of food and feed for an expanding global population.
ANSC 645.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ANSC 650.title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
ANSC 650.subject: ANSC
ANSC 650.description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.
ANSC 650.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANSC 652.title: Information Research Skills
ANSC 652.subject: ANSC
ANSC 652.description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

ANSC 657.title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
ANSC 657.subject: ANSC
ANSC 657.description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR
ANSC 657.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students only; others with consent.

ANSC 660.title: Micronutrients: Vitamins and Minerals
ANSC 660.subject: ANSC
ANSC 660.description: Covers selected vitamins and minerals, their discovery history and research use, why selected animal models are chosen for studying micronutrients, how micronutrients are metabolized within the body, their interactions, and environmental concerns.
ANSC 660.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FSHN, CMB, ASNC, MB, and MBBE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ANSC 682.title: Advanced Topics in Animal Sciences
ANSC 682.subject: ANSC
ANSC 682.description: Advanced topics in animal sciences, from basic to applied research, including current issues and critical analysis of current research literature.

ANSC 687.title: Advanced Laboratory Techniques
ANSC 687.subject: ANSC
ANSC 687.description: (1 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.
ANSC 687.prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent and MBBE 402 / MBBE 402L , and FSHN 477 ; or BIOC 441 .

ANSC 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
ANSC 695.subject: ANSC
ANSC 695.description: Plan B students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend before a three-person faculty committee a report of work the student has produced in the project.

ANTH 151.title: Emerging Humanity
ANTH 151.subject: ANTH
ANTH 151.description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Open to nonmajors, recommended for majors.

ANTH 151A.title: Emerging Humanity
ANTH 151A.subject: ANTH
ANTH 151A.description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Restricted to students in the Honors Program.

ANTH 152.title: Culture and Humanity
ANTH 152.subject: ANTH
ANTH 152.description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order.
ANTH 152.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors, required for ANTH majors.

ANTH 152A.title: Culture and Humanity
ANTH 152A.subject: ANTH
ANTH 152A.description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order. Restricted to students in the Honors Program.

ANTH 175.title: Polynesian Surf Culture
ANTH 175.subject: ANTH
ANTH 175.description: Examines environmental and cultural factors in the development of Polynesian surf culture, surfing’s decline due to Western influence, and its revitalization as a modern recreational activity. Business practices of the surfing industry are critically analyzed.

ANTH 175L.title: Polynesian Surf Culture Field Lab
ANTH 175L.subject: ANTH
ANTH 175L.description: Surfing sites are visited, ancient and modern Polynesian surfing practices and surfboard design and technology are discussed. Shoreline assessments emphasize ocean safety. Social issues surrounding surfing sites in Hawaiʻi are analyzed.

ANTH 204.title: Historical Ecology of Hawaiʻi
ANTH 204.subject: ANTH
ANTH 204.description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

ANTH 210.title: Archaeology
ANTH 210.subject: ANTH
ANTH 210.description: Introduction to prehistoric archaeology; methods and techniques of excavation and laboratory analysis; brief survey of theory in relation to change and diversity in prehistoric human groups.

ANTH 215.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
ANTH 215.subject: ANTH
ANTH 215.description: Human evolution, primatology, human genetics, biological variation, human adaptability, growth and development.

ANTH 220.title: Quantitative Reasoning for Anthropologists
ANTH 220.subject: ANTH
ANTH 220.description: Achieve basic quantitative literacy and to familiarize them with statistical reasoning so that they are prepared to carry out anthropological (and other social science) research.

ANTH 230.title: Anthropology of Sports
ANTH 230.subject: ANTH
ANTH 230.description: Explores sports from anthropological viewpoint: biological, cultural, linguistic, and archaeological. Open to nonmajors. Sophomore standing only.

ANTH 231.title: Anthropology of Love
ANTH 231.subject: ANTH
ANTH 231.description: Explores love from multiple anthropological viewpoints: biological, cultural, archaeological.

ANTH 300.title: Contemporary Social Issues
ANTH 300.subject: ANTH
ANTH 300.description: Contemporary issues in the field of anthropology and in society, including race, ethnicity, gender, inequality, colonialism and decolonization, health disparities and environmental change, from the perspective of cultural anthropology, biological anthropology and archaeology.

ANTH 301.title: Culture and Health
ANTH 301.subject: ANTH
ANTH 301.description: Social and cultural aspects of medicine; the relationship of medicine to the beliefs, social systems, ecological adaptations, and cultural changes of human groups.

ANTH 308.title: Evolutionary Medicine
ANTH 308.subject: ANTH
ANTH 308.description: Using an evolutionary perspective, examines how diseases and other medical issues came to be and how they can be prevented or treated.

ANTH 310.title: Human Origins
ANTH 310.subject: ANTH
ANTH 310.description: Theory of evolution, evolutionary systematics, and taxonomy; evolutionary biology of primates; fossil records for primate and human evolution. Laboratory included.

ANTH 313.title: Visual Anthropology
ANTH 313.subject: ANTH
ANTH 313.description: Historical development of documentary films of non-Western peoples; critical examination of ways in which ethnographic films represent different cultures.

ANTH 315.title: Sex and Gender
ANTH 315.subject: ANTH
ANTH 315.description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual differences; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

ANTH 316.title: Anthropology of Tourism
ANTH 316.subject: ANTH
ANTH 316.description: Anthropological perspectives on the subject of the global phenomenon of tourism. Includes issues of cultural performance, identity, and commoditization. Open to nonmajors.

ANTH 323.title: Pacific Islands Archaeology
ANTH 323.subject: ANTH
ANTH 323.description: Origins of Pacific peoples; chronology of settlement; sequences of culture in Australia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia.
ANTH 323.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

ANTH 325.title: Origins of Cities
ANTH 325.subject: ANTH
ANTH 325.description: Combined lecture/ discussion on the emergence and development of ancient cities in comparative perspective and the dynamics of (pre)modern urban life. Examples are drawn from the Near East, Mediterranean, Africa, India, China, and the Americas.
ANTH 325.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

ANTH 326.title: American Folklore and Folklife
ANTH 326.subject: ANTH
ANTH 326.description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 327.title: Ethnohistory
ANTH 327.subject: ANTH
ANTH 327.description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e., the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history.

ANTH 328.title: Food Origins, Food Culture
ANTH 328.subject: ANTH
ANTH 328.description: Lectures and discussion offer an anthropological introduction to how humans created and transformed food through time. Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 329.title: Indigenous Peoples and Cultures of North America
ANTH 329.subject: ANTH
ANTH 329.description: Survey of Indigenous peoples of North America. Integrates documentary records, ethnography, and archaeology to explore variability among native communities. Contemporary topics include political recognition and self-determination, health and education, and natural resources and economic development.

ANTH 332.title: Anthropology of Surfing
ANTH 332.subject: ANTH
ANTH 332.description: Applies cultural anthropology to assess surfing as an indigenous Hawaiian and modern globalized activity. Discusses the history of surfing, surfing culture, and the impacts of surfing tourism on coastal development, reef ecology, and ocean safety.

ANTH 333.title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
ANTH 333.subject: ANTH
ANTH 333.description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future.

ANTH 335.title: Society and Environment
ANTH 335.subject: ANTH
ANTH 335.description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

ANTH 338.title: Historical Ecology
ANTH 338.subject: ANTH
ANTH 338.description: Examines the recursive relationship between humans and the environment across deep time.

ANTH 341.title: Anthropology of Virtual Worlds
ANTH 341.subject: ANTH
ANTH 341.description: Anthropological study of computer mediated interaction. Focus on the ethnography of massively multiplayer online games, text-based chat rooms, and blogs.
