ANTH 345.title: Aggression, War, and Peace
ANTH 345.subject: ANTH
ANTH 345.description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

ANTH 350.title: Pacific Island Cultures
ANTH 350.subject: ANTH
ANTH 350.description: Introduction to cultures of Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia from time of first settlement to emergence of modern nation states.
ANTH 350.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

ANTH 360.title: Primate Behavioral Ecology
ANTH 360.subject: ANTH
ANTH 360.description: As primates are our closest living relatives, studying the range of variation in areas like life history, diet, communication, and social systems within the order primates can inform on how we ourselves evolved.

ANTH 368.title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
ANTH 368.subject: ANTH
ANTH 368.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households. Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 369.title: Household Archaeology
ANTH 369.subject: ANTH
ANTH 369.description: Focuses on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between households that comprised ancient communities and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 370.title: Ethnographic Field Techniques
ANTH 370.subject: ANTH
ANTH 370.description: Problems and techniques of social-cultural anthropological fieldwork; ethnographic literature; work with informants.

ANTH 372B.title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Mesoamerica
ANTH 372B.subject: ANTH
ANTH 372B.description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
ANTH 372B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

ANTH 372C.title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Andean South America
ANTH 372C.subject: ANTH
ANTH 372C.description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
ANTH 372C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

ANTH 375.title: Race and Human Variation
ANTH 375.subject: ANTH
ANTH 375.description: Human genetic and physical variation; latitudinal, longitudinal, and altitudinal variation across human populations; history of racism; contemporary issues in race and racism.
ANTH 375.prereq_raw: sophomore standing, recommend ANTH 152 and ANTH 215 ; or consent.

ANTH 379.title: Archaeology Practicum
ANTH 379.subject: ANTH
ANTH 379.description: Students will gain practical archaeological experience (e.g., materials processing, analysis, documentation, conservation) under the direction of practicing archaeological professionals in the local community and in collaboration with supervising archaeological faculty.
ANTH 379.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANTH majors or minors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 380.title: Archaeological Lab Techniques
ANTH 380.subject: ANTH
ANTH 380.description: Laboratory analysis and evaluation of field data; preservation and restoration of artifacts. Preparation for publication.

ANTH 381.title: Archaeological Field Techniques
ANTH 381.subject: ANTH
ANTH 381.description: Archaeological survey and excavations; field trips, mapping, photography. May focus on terrestrial or underwater. May be taught entirely in the field at a national or international archaeological site.

ANTH 382.title: How Archaeology Works
ANTH 382.subject: ANTH
ANTH 382.description: Uses archaeological examples to illustrate social science research techniques. Students learn how to create, analyze, and evaluate data through lab-based exercises, and examine ethical issues inherent in anthropological practice.
ANTH 382.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 384.title: Skeletal Biology
ANTH 384.subject: ANTH
ANTH 384.description: Introduction to the human skeleton and methods for analyzing archaeological human remains including age, sex, ethnicity, paleodemography, skeletal and dental variation, paleopathology, population studies.

ANTH 385B.title: Undergraduate Seminar: archacology
ANTH 385B.subject: ANTH
ANTH 385B.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

ANTH 385C.title: Undergraduate Seminar: ethnography
ANTH 385C.subject: ANTH
ANTH 385C.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

ANTH 385D.title: Undergraduate SeminarD social anthropoloogy
ANTH 385D.subject: ANTH
ANTH 385D.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

ANTH 385E.title: Undergraduate Seminar: applied
ANTH 385E.subject: ANTH
ANTH 385E.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

ANTH 385F.title: Undergraduate Seminar: psychological
ANTH 385F.subject: ANTH
ANTH 385F.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

ANTH 385G.title: Undergraduate Seminar: biological
ANTH 385G.subject: ANTH
ANTH 385G.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

ANTH 399.title: Directed Reading or Research
ANTH 399.subject: ANTH
ANTH 399.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: major or minor in Anthropology.

ANTH 410.title: Ethics in Anthropology
ANTH 410.subject: ANTH
ANTH 410.description: Seminar surveying ethical cases, problems, issues and questions from the inception of anthropology to the present. Junior standing or higher or consent.

ANTH 413.title: Language and Gender
ANTH 413.subject: ANTH
ANTH 413.description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required.

ANTH 414.title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
ANTH 414.subject: ANTH
ANTH 414.description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

ANTH 416.title: Wealth, Culture, and Economic Anthropology
ANTH 416.subject: ANTH
ANTH 416.description: Analysis of economic activities in non-Western, non-industrial societies; production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a variety of cultures.

ANTH 417.title: Political Anthropology
ANTH 417.subject: ANTH
ANTH 417.description: Character of political institutions and their development in non- Western and non-industrial societies.

ANTH 419.title: Indigenous Anthropology
ANTH 419.subject: ANTH
ANTH 419.description: Exploration of how anthropology studies indigenous groups throughout the world. An examination of the changing contexts of anthropological practice as calls for reflexivity lead anthropology of all backgrounds to bring insights from their “homes.” Issues include the question of objectivity, the emicetic distinction, and the ethics of different kinds of anthropological research and the role of anthropologists in indigenous self-determination.

ANTH 422.title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
ANTH 422.subject: ANTH
ANTH 422.description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

ANTH 423.title: Social and Cultural Change
ANTH 423.subject: ANTH
ANTH 423.description: Various approaches to examples of social and cultural change in non-literate societies; evolution, diffusion, acculturation, revolution, etc. Historical features and social processes of colonialism.

ANTH 424.title: Islands as Model Systems: Human Biogeography of the Pacific
ANTH 424.subject: ANTH
ANTH 424.description: Applying the concept of islands as “model systems;” explores the impacts of human populations on the natural ecosystems of oceanic islands, and the reciprocal effects of anthropogenic change on human cultures.

ANTH 426.title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
ANTH 426.subject: ANTH
ANTH 426.description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.
ANTH 426.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 427.title: Food, Health, and Society
ANTH 427.subject: ANTH
ANTH 427.description: How human groups identify, collect, create, and transform foods; how they shape those into dietary behaviors, and the influence of those behaviors on health.
ANTH 427.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher or consent.

ANTH 428.title: Anthropology of the Body
ANTH 428.subject: ANTH
ANTH 428.description: Exploration of the history and development of theories of the body via topics such as phenomenology, perception, bodily rituals, gender, sex, race, colonialism, power, pain, medicalization, immunology, reproductive health and cyborgs.

ANTH 429.title: Anthropology of Consumer Cultures
ANTH 429.subject: ANTH
ANTH 429.description: Examines the practices and meanings of consumption in the contemporary world. Topics include social class, branding, fandom, global-local nexus.

ANTH 431.title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
ANTH 431.subject: ANTH
ANTH 431.description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems.
ANTH 431.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 440.title: The Agriculture of Identity: Food and Farming in Anthropological Perspective
ANTH 440.subject: ANTH
ANTH 440.description: Exploration of agriculture from the perspective of anthropology, with a focus on alternatives to industrial agriculture, especially in the context of Hawaiʻi. Readings include academic writing and also literary non-fiction and journalism.

ANTH 442.title: Globalization and Identity in the Himalayas
ANTH 442.subject: ANTH
ANTH 442.description: Examines the influence of local culture and global flows on identity formation in the Himalayan region. Topics include: Hindu caste and gender, constructions of ethnicity, Tibetans and tourists, Sherpas and mountaineers, development ideologies, and consumerism.
ANTH 442.prereq_raw: ANTH 152 or ANTH 301 or ASAN 202 or consent.

ANTH 443.title: Anthropology of Buddhism
ANTH 443.subject: ANTH
ANTH 443.description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

ANTH 444.title: Spiritual Ecology
ANTH 444.subject: ANTH
ANTH 444.description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism.
ANTH 444.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 445.title: Sacred Places
ANTH 445.subject: ANTH
ANTH 445.description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects.
ANTH 445.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 446.title: Southeast Asian Cultures
ANTH 446.subject: ANTH
ANTH 446.description: Cultures of Southeast Asia from hunting and gathering groups to high civilizations; kinship, economic, political, and religious systems; recent developments.
ANTH 446.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 447.title: Polynesian Cultures
ANTH 447.subject: ANTH
ANTH 447.description: Analysis of Polynesian cultures from their origins to contemporary states.
ANTH 447.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 449.title: Anthropology of Melanesia
ANTH 449.subject: ANTH
ANTH 449.description: Close study of cultures of Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Fiji through anthropological ethnography.

ANTH 451.title: Decolonizing Anthropology Through South Africa
ANTH 451.subject: ANTH
ANTH 451.description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology explored through the archaeology and ethnography of South Africa. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 458.title: Forensic Anthropology
ANTH 458.subject: ANTH
ANTH 458.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of physical anthropology to problems in human identification. Determination of age, sex, ancestry, etc., of the skeleton and preparation of reports for legal medicine.

ANTH 459.title: Extinctions
ANTH 459.subject: ANTH
ANTH 459.description: An extraordinary number of plants and animals have gone extinct. Delves deeply into the primary literature that focuses on extinction and conservation from the beginning of the earth to the present day.

ANTH 460.title: Asian Paleoanthropology
ANTH 460.subject: ANTH
ANTH 460.description: Neogene- Quaternary paleoenvironmental reconstructions; human evolution in East Asia during the Pleistocene; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.
ANTH 460.prereq_raw: sophomore standing, recommend ANTH 310 , or consent.

ANTH 461.title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
ANTH 461.subject: ANTH
ANTH 461.description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.
ANTH 461.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 462.title: East Asian Archaeology
ANTH 462.subject: ANTH
ANTH 462.description: Prehistory and protohistory of China, Japan, and Korea from earliest human occupation to historic times. Geographical emphasis may vary between China and Japan/Korea.
ANTH 462.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 463.title: Anthropology of Global Health and Development
ANTH 463.subject: ANTH
ANTH 463.description: Seminar explores the definitions and histories of development and global health initiatives in developing countries from an anthropological perspective. Reading materials include scholarly and popular texts that propose and critique solutions to global poverty. Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 464.title: Hawaiian Archaeology
ANTH 464.subject: ANTH
ANTH 464.description: Archaeological perspective in Hawaiʻi’s past; origins of Hawaiians; early settlement and culture change; settlement patterns and material culture; historic sites preservation.
ANTH 464.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing and consent.

ANTH 465.title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
ANTH 465.subject: ANTH
ANTH 465.description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 466.title: Quantitative Archaeology
ANTH 466.subject: ANTH
ANTH 466.description: Combined lecture/lab. Introduction to the basic principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. Exploratory data analysis approach.
ANTH 466.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANTH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 467.title: Biomedicine and Culture
ANTH 467.subject: ANTH
ANTH 467.description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies and practices of modern medicine. This course develops written communication skills.
ANTH 467.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, ANTH 152 , or consent.

ANTH 471.title: Field Mapping
ANTH 471.subject: ANTH
ANTH 471.description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
ANTH 471.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

ANTH 473.title: Lithic Artifact Assemblage Analysis
ANTH 473.subject: ANTH
ANTH 473.description: Combined lecture/lab on the manufacture and analysis of stone tools. Students work with experimental collections and engage in stone tool production. The ways in which lithics enlighten us about past human behavior are discussed.

ANTH 475.title: Faunal Analysis in Archaeology
ANTH 475.subject: ANTH
ANTH 475.description: Analysis of archaeologically recovered faunal collections with emphasis on identification and interpretation of nonhuman vertebrate remains.

ANTH 477.title: Spatial Analysis in Archaeology
ANTH 477.subject: ANTH
ANTH 477.description: Introduction to the use of Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistics in archaeological research. Topics include: map creation; spatial database management; spatial analysis; image processing, data reporting; and data display. Junior standing or higher.
ANTH 477.prereq_raw: ANTH 466 or ANTH 666 , or instructor approval.

ANTH 478.title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
ANTH 478.subject: ANTH
ANTH 478.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

ANTH 481.title: Applied Anthropology
ANTH 481.subject: ANTH
ANTH 481.description: The application of anthropological methods and concepts to solving practical human problems such as homelessness, domestic violence, maternal morbidity, conflict over resources, and the loss of indigenous languages. Includes a significant service-learning component.

ANTH 482.title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
ANTH 482.subject: ANTH
ANTH 482.description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

ANTH 483.title: Japanese Culture and Behavior
ANTH 483.subject: ANTH
ANTH 483.description: Sociocultural factors in Japanese behavior. Social structure; traditional institutions.

ANTH 484.title: Japanese Popular Culture
ANTH 484.subject: ANTH
ANTH 484.description: Explores contemporary Japanese popular culture through themes such as gender, consumerism, globalization and nostalgia. Rather than a survey of popular culture genres, the course is organized thematically around issues and problematics.

ANTH 485.title: Pre-European Hawaiʻi
ANTH 485.subject: ANTH
ANTH 485.description: Pre-European society and culture from an anthropological viewpoint.
ANTH 485.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 486.title: Peoples of Hawaiʻi
ANTH 486.subject: ANTH
ANTH 486.description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawaiʻi using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.
ANTH 486.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ANTH 488.title: Chinese Culture: Ethnography
ANTH 488.subject: ANTH
ANTH 488.description: Critical interpretations of ethnographic and biographic texts depicting individual and family lives in different socioeconomic circumstances, geographical regions, and historical periods of modern China.

ANTH 490.title: History of Anthropology
ANTH 490.subject: ANTH
ANTH 490.description: Development of anthropological ideas, focusing on theoretical issues concerning culture, society, and human nature. Required of majors.

ANTH 491.title: Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History: Monuments and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
ANTH 491.subject: ANTH
ANTH 491.description: Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. Monuments and nationalism in Southeast Asia.

ANTH 493.title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
ANTH 493.subject: ANTH
ANTH 493.description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project.

ANTH 495.title: Senior Thesis I
ANTH 495.subject: ANTH
ANTH 495.description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. First semester of a two-semester sequence with ANTH 496 . May be taken concurrently with ANTH 496 . Optional for majors.

ANTH 496.title: Senior Thesis II
ANTH 496.subject: ANTH
ANTH 496.description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. Second semester of a two-semester sequence with ANTH 495 . May be taken concurrently with ANTH 495 . Optional for majors.

ANTH 601.title: Ethnology
ANTH 601.subject: ANTH
ANTH 601.description: Survey, in historical perspective, of theory in social and cultural anthropology, from the origin of anthropology to 1976. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 602.title: Linguistic Anthropology
ANTH 602.subject: ANTH
ANTH 602.description: Investigation of mutual influences of linguistic theory and methodology and anthropological theory and methodology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 603.title: Archaeology
ANTH 603.subject: ANTH
ANTH 603.description: Development of critical and analytical skills in assessment of archaeological literature; emphasis on the science, theory, explanation, and paradigms that comprise archaeology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 604.title: Biological Anthropology Core
ANTH 604.subject: ANTH
ANTH 604.description: Human evolution and human variability in extant and previously existing populations; emphasis on history of physical anthropology, evolutionary systematics, primate biology and behavior, paleontology, anthropological genetics, climatic adaptation, growth, and nutrition. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 605.title: Discursive Practices
ANTH 605.subject: ANTH
ANTH 605.description: Emphasizes linguistic, semantic, and interactional aspects of culture, exploring ways that discourse constructs social action and social realities, examining processes by which culture is produced as meaningful behavior in actual situations.

ANTH 606.title: Anthropology of Infectious Disease
ANTH 606.subject: ANTH
ANTH 606.description: The role of human behavior, including its social and cultural determinants, in understanding the distribution of infectious diseases and in shaping preventive and therapeutic strategies.

ANTH 608.title: History and Memory
ANTH 608.subject: ANTH
ANTH 608.description: History and collective memory as culturally formed and politically contested realities. The role of narrative, ritual, and media technologies in shaping representations of the past.

ANTH 610.title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
ANTH 610.subject: ANTH
ANTH 610.description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawaiʻi, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

ANTH 611.title: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
ANTH 611.subject: ANTH
ANTH 611.description: Graduate seminar that examines the history of theory in sociocultural anthropology from 1960 to present. Designed to be taken in sequence after ANTH 601 .

ANTH 620B.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: kinship
ANTH 620B.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620B.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620C.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: cognitive systems
ANTH 620C.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620C.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620D.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: religion
ANTH 620D.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620D.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620E.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: political institutions
ANTH 620E.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620E.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620F.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: law and social control
ANTH 620F.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620F.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620G.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: economics
ANTH 620G.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620G.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620H.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: ecology
ANTH 620H.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620H.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 620I.title: Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology: other
ANTH 620I.subject: ANTH
ANTH 620I.description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

ANTH 623.title: Advanced Pacific Islands Archaeology
ANTH 623.subject: ANTH
ANTH 623.description: Advanced theoretical and methodological examination of archaeological research in Oceania, a region including the islands of Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.

ANTH 640B.title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: analytical
ANTH 640B.subject: ANTH
ANTH 640B.description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

ANTH 640C.title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: environment/landscape
ANTH 640C.subject: ANTH
ANTH 640C.description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

ANTH 640D.title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: applied archaeology
ANTH 640D.subject: ANTH
ANTH 640D.description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

ANTH 640E.title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: economic/resources
ANTH 640E.subject: ANTH
ANTH 640E.description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

ANTH 640F.title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: survey/locational
ANTH 640F.subject: ANTH
ANTH 640F.description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

ANTH 645.title: Historic Preservation
ANTH 645.subject: ANTH
ANTH 645.description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawaiʻi and the region.

ANTH 651.title: Decolonizing Anthropology
ANTH 651.subject: ANTH
ANTH 651.description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology with a focus on South Africa and its relevance for the Pacific and U.S. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence.

ANTH 659.title: Advances in Extinctions
ANTH 659.subject: ANTH
ANTH 659.description: To delve deeply into the primary literature that focuses on the subjects of extinction and conservation broadly speaking, with particular emphasis on the 6 mass extinction events, including the Anthropocene.

ANTH 660.title: Paleoanthropology of Asia
ANTH 660.subject: ANTH
ANTH 660.description: Survey of the Asian paleoanthropological record, particularly in its paleoenvironmental setting; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.
ANTH 660.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing and relevant background in anthropology or related field.

ANTH 661.title: Archaeological Perspectives on Southeast Asia
ANTH 661.subject: ANTH
ANTH 661.description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia, and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.
ANTH 661.prereq_raw: background in archaeology or Southeast Asian history or consent.

ANTH 663.title: Anthropology of Global Aid
ANTH 663.subject: ANTH
ANTH 663.description: Examines ideologies of development, humanitarian, and global health interventions from an anthropological perspective. Explores the disjuncture between discourses that portrays global aid as easing suffering and those that accuse it of maintaining relationships of domination.

ANTH 664.title: Advanced Hawaiian Archaeology
ANTH 664.subject: ANTH
ANTH 664.description: An advanced theoretical and methodological examination of past and current archaeological research in the Hawaiian Islands.

ANTH 666.title: Archaeological Data Analysis
ANTH 666.subject: ANTH
ANTH 666.description: Advanced introduction to the fundamental principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data.

ANTH 667.title: Biomedicine and Culture
ANTH 667.subject: ANTH
ANTH 667.description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies, and practices of modern medicine.

ANTH 668.title: Archaeology Field Methods
ANTH 668.subject: ANTH
ANTH 668.description: (5 7-hr Lab) Laboratory and field training in the principles and practice of methods of archaeology-survey, mapping, excavation, conservation.

ANTH 669.title: Advanced Household Archaeology
ANTH 669.subject: ANTH
ANTH 669.description: Focus on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between the households that comprised ancient communities, and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change.
ANTH 669.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ANTH 670.title: Applied Archaeology Practicum
ANTH 670.subject: ANTH
ANTH 670.description: Applies course work in archaeology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. MA track in Applied Archaeology students only.

ANTH 671.title: Applied Method and Theory in Hawaiian Archaeology
ANTH 671.subject: ANTH
ANTH 671.description: Graduate seminar focused on method and theory in the practice of applied archaeology in Hawaiʻi.
ANTH 671.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ANTH 676.title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
ANTH 676.subject: ANTH
ANTH 676.description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.
ANTH 676.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

ANTH 681.title: Applied Cultural Anthropology
ANTH 681.subject: ANTH
ANTH 681.description: Theory, methods, and results of application of cultural anthropological concepts to practical problems.
ANTH 681.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ANTH 682.title: Applied Cultural Anthropology Practicum
ANTH 682.subject: ANTH
ANTH 682.description: Applies course work in cultural anthropology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty.

ANTH 695.title: Professional Skills Develop in Anthropology
ANTH 695.subject: ANTH
ANTH 695.description: Seminar prepares graduate students for entry into profession, including employment opportunities, research, presentations, ethics and outreach. Required of all Plan B students.

ANTH 699.title: Directed Reading or Research
ANTH 699.subject: ANTH
ANTH 699.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

ANTH 710.title: Seminar in Research Methods in Cultural Anthropology
ANTH 710.subject: ANTH
ANTH 710.description: Ethnographic research methods. Introduction to the approaches and techniques of participatory research, including the collection, analysis, and interpretation of social and cultural data. Politics and ethics of research practice.
ANTH 710.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in anthropology or consent.

ANTH 711.title: Seminar in Research Design and Proposal Writing
ANTH 711.subject: ANTH
ANTH 711.description: Research design and proposal writing. For students preparing for advanced research.
ANTH 711.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

ANTH 720.title: Anthropology of Japan
ANTH 720.subject: ANTH
ANTH 720.description: Japan examined through three dimensions of cultural anthropology: cultural/symbolic, social/organizational, and individual/psychological. Selected topics analyzed and interpreted in terms of conjunctions of these dimensions.

ANTH 750B.title: Research Seminar: Archaeology
ANTH 750B.subject: ANTH
ANTH 750B.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.

ANTH 750C.title: Research Seminar: medical
ANTH 750C.subject: ANTH
ANTH 750C.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.

ANTH 750D.title: Research Seminar: ethnography
ANTH 750D.subject: ANTH
ANTH 750D.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.

ANTH 750E.title: Research Seminar: social
ANTH 750E.subject: ANTH
ANTH 750E.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.

ANTH 750G.title: Research Seminar: biological
ANTH 750G.subject: ANTH
ANTH 750G.description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.

ARAB 101.title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 101.subject: ARAB
ARAB 101.description: Designed to provide students with basic knowledge of Modern Standard Arabic. Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language, as well as formal spoken Arabic.

ARAB 102.title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 102.subject: ARAB
ARAB 102.description: Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language as well as formal spoken Arabic. It introduces a wide range of situation-based texts and topics that build vocabulary, grammar, and general communicative competence.

ARAB 201.title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 201.subject: ARAB
ARAB 201.description: Designed for students who have successfully completed a year of Elementary Arabic. Focus is on acquisition of more complex grammatical structures, expanding vocabulary, and developing competence in a wide range of communicative situations.

ARAB 202.title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 202.subject: ARAB
ARAB 202.description: Designed for students who have successfully completed three semesters of Arabic. Focus is on intensive practice of interactive functional skills such as listening comprehension and fundamental conversation strategies.

ARAB 301.title: Third-Level Arabic I
ARAB 301.subject: ARAB
ARAB 301.description: Develop proficiency in reading/listening comprehension in Modern Standard Arabic. The instructional materials consist of authentic written, visual and audio materials. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

ARAB 302.title: Third-Level Arabic II
ARAB 302.subject: ARAB
ARAB 302.description: Continuation of third-level Arabic I. Emphasis on developing writing and interaction ability at advanced levels of proficiency. Course includes extensive reading, composition exercises, listening skills, conversation practice and extensive review of Arabic grammar. Developing fluency is the main objective of this course. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

ARCH 100.title: Introduction to the Built Environment
ARCH 100.subject: ARCH
ARCH 100.description: Introduction to the breadth of design in today’s global culture. Exploration of human responses to place, climate, culture, communication, and technology, with emphasis on the impact of scientific knowledge on environmental design. Open to nonmajors.

ARCH 101.title: Design Fundamentals Studio I
ARCH 101.subject: ARCH
ARCH 101.description: Introduction to creative design processes focusing on the investigation of composition within defining perceivable space. Hands-on exploration of materials and structures as an introduction to design processes.

ARCH 102.title: Design Fundamentals Studio II
ARCH 102.subject: ARCH
ARCH 102.description: Continued exploration of design processes. Introduction to CAD technologies, material exploration, and creative exploration including the relationship between digital, physical, and materials aspects of design.

ARCH 201.title: Beginning Design Studio I
ARCH 201.subject: ARCH
ARCH 201.description: Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, represent, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and computer graphic techniques.

ARCH 202.title: Beginning Design Studio II
ARCH 202.subject: ARCH
ARCH 202.description: Development of designs and processes to study precedents and explore solutions responding to human needs in built and natural environments. Analysis and representation of architectonic space and form using hand and computer techniques.

ARCH 210.title: Tectonics for Environmental Design: Materials & Methods
ARCH 210.subject: ARCH
ARCH 210.description: Introduction to essential knowledge, terminology, and techniques related to materials, processes, and systems used in the construction of built environments, with a focus on applications in design practices.

ARCH 220.title: Introduction to Environmental Systems A
ARCH 220.subject: ARCH
ARCH 220.description: Introduction to building systems, including structural, environmental, life-safety, building envelope, building materials and building assemblies. Development of design skills with emphasis on elevating skills in assessing and selecting appropriate building systems.
ARCH 220.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 271.title: World Architecture and Urbanism A
ARCH 271.subject: ARCH
ARCH 271.description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture in the world’s major cultural regions, from early agricultural settlements to 1500 C.E. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.
ARCH 271.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 272.title: World Architecture and Urbanism B
ARCH 272.subject: ARCH
ARCH 272.description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture from the 15th century C.E. to the present. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.
ARCH 272.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 321.title: Introduction to Environmental Systems B
ARCH 321.subject: ARCH
ARCH 321.description: Introduction to environmentalism; focusing on the impact of building systems of the global environment; the role of environmental regulations/certifications, and understanding of sustainable principles (economic, social, and natural systems).
ARCH 321.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 330.title: Tectonics for Environmental Design: Integrated Systems
ARCH 330.subject: ARCH
ARCH 330.description: Application of fundamental structural principles and systems, materials and assemblies, building envelope systems, and environmental control systems, with an emphasis on their integration within the built environment through project-based exercises.

ARCH 341.title: Intermediate Design Studio I
ARCH 341.subject: ARCH
ARCH 341.description: Building and site design with emphasis on site development, analysis, and climatic response. Introduction to sustainable design, land use ordinances, description and delineation of property and land features, and urban and community design influences.

ARCH 342.title: Intermediate Design Studio II
ARCH 342.subject: ARCH
ARCH 342.description: Architectural design with emphasis on space planning, building materials, technology, climatic responses, and codes including complex functional requirements, multistory design issues, vertical transportation, structure, and finishes. Production of complete schematic design documents. Detailed writing instruction.

ARCH 352.title: Landscape Architecture History
ARCH 352.subject: ARCH
ARCH 352.description: Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes.
ARCH 352.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

ARCH 353.title: Landscape Graphics Studio
ARCH 353.subject: ARCH
ARCH 353.description: Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics.
ARCH 353.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 354.title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
ARCH 354.subject: ARCH
ARCH 354.description: Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale.
ARCH 354.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 371.title: Design Theory
ARCH 371.subject: ARCH
ARCH 371.description: Examination of theories, movements, and periods in architectural history focusing on contemporary issues. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of writing, and three oral communication assignments.
ARCH 371.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 381.title: Landform and Water
ARCH 381.subject: ARCH
ARCH 381.description: Essential topographic site design concepts and skills needed to reshape the land for human use, circulation, water management, and resilience. Topics will be reinforced through problem sets and analytical, computational, graphical, and technical exercises.
ARCH 381.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

ARCH 399.title: Directed Work
ARCH 399.subject: ARCH
ARCH 399.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 415.title: Concentration Design Studio
ARCH 415.subject: ARCH
ARCH 415.description: Professional experience combined with scholarly and research activity occurring in an off-campus location with a focus on architectural concentration areas.
ARCH 415.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 416.title: Advanced Design Studio
ARCH 416.subject: ARCH
ARCH 416.description: Studio focused on advanced critical issues related to architecture and the built environments with an emphasis on collaborative or immersive place-based projects in local or global contexts.

ARCH 418.title: Capstone Design Studio
ARCH 418.subject: ARCH
ARCH 418.description: Culminating design studio with focus on the development of a comprehensive design project integrating all major aspects of prior environmental design education.

ARCH 432.title: Construction Project Management
ARCH 432.subject: ARCH
ARCH 432.description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.
ARCH 432.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 433.title: Professional Practice Law and Ethics
ARCH 433.subject: ARCH
ARCH 433.description: Knowledge of professional standards and a broad understanding of the practice of architecture, including professionalism; ethical conduct; public, client, consultant, contractor, and government relations; project administration, contracts, procedures, and compensation; land use and construction law.

ARCH 434.title: Digital Design Synthesis
ARCH 434.subject: ARCH
ARCH 434.description: Investigation of processes for generating architectonic form using current digital technologies. Making advanced geometric models including investigation of morphological transformations. Study of design optimization, digital fabrication, information modeling, and generative algorithms.
ARCH 434.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 436.title: Design Exchange
ARCH 436.subject: ARCH
ARCH 436.description: Seminar centered on academic and cultural exchanges, focused on advanced topics related to the design of built environments.

ARCH 472.title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
ARCH 472.subject: ARCH
ARCH 472.description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, and sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER).
ARCH 472.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH, ENVD, and AMST majors only.

ARCH 473.title: History of American Architecture
ARCH 473.subject: ARCH
ARCH 473.description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.
ARCH 473.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 474.title: Preservation: Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific
ARCH 474.subject: ARCH
ARCH 474.description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.
ARCH 474.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ARCH 483.title: Urban Ecological Analysis and Design
ARCH 483.subject: ARCH
ARCH 483.description: Applied urban and landscape ecology principles and strategies for analysis, design, and management of urban regions and sites; emphasis on structure, functions, and processes that form urban landscapes at multiple scales and in diverse contexts.
ARCH 483.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

ARCH 484.title: Plants in Design
ARCH 484.subject: ARCH
ARCH 484.description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples.
ARCH 484.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

ARCH 490.title: Special Topics
ARCH 490.subject: ARCH
ARCH 490.description: Selected topics in any aspect of architecture. Content to be announced.
ARCH 490.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 491.title: Special Topics in Architecture History
ARCH 491.subject: ARCH
ARCH 491.description: Specialized work on the history and theory of architecture.
ARCH 491.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 492.title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
ARCH 492.subject: ARCH
ARCH 492.description: Specialized investigation of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.
ARCH 492.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 493.title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
ARCH 493.subject: ARCH
ARCH 493.description: Work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.
ARCH 493.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

ARCH 494.title: Explore Furniture Design
ARCH 494.subject: ARCH
ARCH 494.description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice and an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience.

ARCH 496.title: Special Topics in Architecture and Writing
ARCH 496.subject: ARCH
ARCH 496.description: Reading, research, and work on topics in architecture and design. Includes an intensive writing component. May include specialized research and/ or studio experience in architecture, design, and the history and theory of architecture and design.

ARCH 623.title: American Architecture
ARCH 623.subject: ARCH
ARCH 623.description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

ARCH 628.title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
ARCH 628.subject: ARCH
ARCH 628.description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

ARCH 631.title: Design Communication for Landscape Architects
ARCH 631.subject: ARCH
ARCH 631.description: Theory and application in design communication, including drawing and presentation skills; emphasis on the design process and critical thinking through analog and digital media, diagramming, three-dimensional modeling, and various other presentation techniques.

ARCH 633.title: Computer Applications in Landscape Architecture
ARCH 633.subject: ARCH
ARCH 633.description: Introduction to the use of computers in landscape architecture, emphasizing two- and three-dimensional computer-aided drawings and graphics suitable to landscape architectural design and practice.

ARCH 634.title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
ARCH 634.subject: ARCH
ARCH 634.description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawaiʻi and the tropics.

ARCH 635.title: Landscape Materials and Construction
ARCH 635.subject: ARCH
ARCH 635.description: Examination of materials and methods of landscape construction from source, extraction, and manufacturing, to use and reuse. Assignments include drawing standard construction details and a report on the history of material use, properties, and qualities.

ARCH 636.title: Landscape Architectural Professional Practice
ARCH 636.subject: ARCH
ARCH 636.description: Introduction of practices and core methods of the landscape architecture profession. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, professional relationships, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics.

ARCH 641.title: Land Use Planning
ARCH 641.subject: ARCH
ARCH 641.description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

ARCH 645.title: Historic Preservation
ARCH 645.subject: ARCH
ARCH 645.description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawaiʻi and the region.

ARCH 650.title: Vernacular Architecture
ARCH 650.subject: ARCH
ARCH 650.description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

ARCH 651.title: Fundamentals of Landscape Design Studio
ARCH 651.subject: ARCH
ARCH 651.description: Theory and application of foundational landscape design principles, programming, and physical analysis to site-based design problems. Visual, formal, spatial, and functional design principles are applied to ecological and cultural influences in landscape design.

ARCH 652.title: Site Design Studio
ARCH 652.subject: ARCH
ARCH 652.description: Landscape project design at the site scale; from concept development through detailed design. Synthesis of foundational skills into more complex, layered spatial, and functional problems. Emphasis on site research and design methods.

ARCH 656.title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
ARCH 656.subject: ARCH
ARCH 656.description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design.
ARCH 656.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND and TPSS majors only.

ARCH 658.title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
ARCH 658.subject: ARCH
ARCH 658.description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes.

ARCH 674.title: Preservation Field Seminar
ARCH 674.subject: ARCH
ARCH 674.description: Provides participants with basic knowledge of the field of historic preservation as well as the fundamental knowledge of how to document, conserve, and preserve both tangible and intangible cultural properties.

ARCH 676.title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
ARCH 676.subject: ARCH
ARCH 676.description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.
ARCH 676.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

ARCH 677.title: Historic Preservation Planning
ARCH 677.subject: ARCH
ARCH 677.description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

ARCH 679.title: Elements of Style
ARCH 679.subject: ARCH
ARCH 679.description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

ARCH 680.title: Historic Building Technology
ARCH 680.subject: ARCH
ARCH 680.description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600-c.1960.

ARCH 682.title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
ARCH 682.subject: ARCH
ARCH 682.description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises.
ARCH 682.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only.

ARCH 685B.title: Preservation Field Study: Hawaiʻi
ARCH 685B.subject: ARCH
ARCH 685B.description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.

ARCH 685C.title: Preservation Field Study: Asia
ARCH 685C.subject: ARCH
ARCH 685C.description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.

ARCH 685D.title: Preservation Field Study: Pacific
ARCH 685D.subject: ARCH
ARCH 685D.description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.

ARCH 686.title: Historic Preservation Practicum
ARCH 686.subject: ARCH
ARCH 686.description: Applies course work in historic preservation to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and University faculty. Historic preservation certificate students only.
ARCH 686.prereq_raw: ARCH 628 / PLAN 675 and ARCH 645 / ANTH 645 / AMST 645

ARCH 687.title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
ARCH 687.subject: ARCH
ARCH 687.description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

ARCH 690.title: Special Topics Seminar
ARCH 690.subject: ARCH
ARCH 690.description: Seminar on a wide range of architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty.
ARCH 690.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

ARCH 692.title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
ARCH 692.subject: ARCH
ARCH 692.description: Specialized investigation at an advanced level of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.

ARCH 693.title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
ARCH 693.subject: ARCH
ARCH 693.description: Intensive work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.

ARCH 694.title: Special Topics in Furniture Design and Fabrication
ARCH 694.subject: ARCH
ARCH 694.description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice, an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience. Additionally, a survey of 20th Century furniture design.

ARCH 695.title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
ARCH 695.subject: ARCH
ARCH 695.description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. ARCH and LAND majors only, or consent.
ARCH 695.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ARCH 696.title: Special Topics in Landscape Architecture
ARCH 696.subject: ARCH
ARCH 696.description: Seminar on a wide range of landscape architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty.
ARCH 696.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

ARCH 699.title: Directed Work
ARCH 699.subject: ARCH
ARCH 699.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

ARCH 700.title: MLA Thesis
ARCH 700.subject: ARCH
ARCH 700.description: Landscape architectural thesis research and design inquiry. Limited to MLA students under Plan A.

ARCH 715.title: Asia-Pacific Architectural History and Theory
ARCH 715.subject: ARCH
ARCH 715.description: Study of the history and theory of culture and the built environment with particular focus on the Asia-Pacific region.

ARCH 716.title: Architecture and Urban Design Theory
ARCH 716.subject: ARCH
ARCH 716.description: Detailed investigation of major theories in architecture and urban design and examination of their impact on contemporary architectural practice in varied geo-political contexts.

ARCH 722.title: Architecture Systems I: Introduction to Systems
ARCH 722.subject: ARCH
ARCH 722.description: Study of building materials, assemblies, and integrated design including structural, environmental, life-safety, and building envelope systems. Development of ability to design, analyze and assess appropriate systems.

ARCH 723.title: Architecture Systems II: Qualitative Bioclimatic and Structural Performance
ARCH 723.subject: ARCH
ARCH 723.description: Introduction to the theory of bioclimatic principles and structural systems and the ability to analyze, assess, select, design, and integrate them as initial determinants into the building design.
ARCH 723.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate status.

ARCH 724.title: Architecture Systems III: Quantitative Structural Analysis and Design
ARCH 724.subject: ARCH
ARCH 724.description: Introduction to procedures and wood, steel, concrete, and masonry material properties used for structural analysis and design of individual structural elements and building structural systems.

ARCH 725.title: Architecture Systems IV: Environmental Technology, Sustainability, and Analysis
ARCH 725.subject: ARCH
ARCH 725.description: Application and analysis of high-performance building design principles. Emphasis on climate-appropriate passive design, energy-efficient lighting and conditioning strategies, innovative water systems, and renewable energy production.

ARCH 726.title: Architecture Systems V: Building Systems Integration
ARCH 726.subject: ARCH
ARCH 726.description: Properties, evolution, and range of building materials, assemblies, and systems and their applications in integrated high-performance building design with a focus on the role of detail and systems in the design process.

ARCH 731.title: Advanced Design Communication I
ARCH 731.subject: ARCH
ARCH 731.description: Exploration of digital technologies, their relationship to design, and their application to architectural analysis, conceptualization, design processes, communication, representation, and construction.

ARCH 733.title: Advanced Design Communication II
ARCH 733.subject: ARCH
ARCH 733.description: An interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to digital technology and its applications to current developments in practice and research within architecture and design.

ARCH 734.title: Forms and Frames of Practice
ARCH 734.subject: ARCH
ARCH 734.description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice within the global context with emphasis on the Asia Pacific region. Exploration of information technology systems, materials and design process research, construction technology, computer aided manufacturing, and entrepreneurial approaches.

ARCH 737.title: Advanced Design Communications III
ARCH 737.subject: ARCH
ARCH 737.description: Interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to architectural presentation techniques, particularly oral and written, to current developments in architectural practice.

ARCH 739.title: Research Methods Seminar
ARCH 739.subject: ARCH
ARCH 739.description: Comprehensive assessment of objectives and function of research in architecture and landscape architecture. Lecture, seminar, independent work with emphasis on research project topic and proposal development.
ARCH 739.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

ARCH 740.title: Architecture Studio I: Intro to Design
ARCH 740.subject: ARCH
ARCH 740.description: Design theories and systematic analytic and synthetic methodologies applied to creation of building and site spaces responsive to environmental and human needs. Several individual projects.

ARCH 742.title: Architecture Studio III
ARCH 742.subject: ARCH
ARCH 742.description: Design of complex, large scale building and site engaging social, cultural, code, sustainable systems, and acoustic issues. Production of schematic and design development documents.
ARCH 742.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

ARCH 743.title: Architecture Studio IV: Urban Design
ARCH 743.subject: ARCH
ARCH 743.description: Urban design focused on Asian cities investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response.
ARCH 743.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

ARCH 744.title: Architecture Studio V: Comprehensive Design
ARCH 744.subject: ARCH
ARCH 744.description: Design and programming for a moderately complex building and site. Production of design development and partial construction documents describing sustainable building assemblies and construction cost.

ARCH 745.title: Advanced Practice
ARCH 745.subject: ARCH
ARCH 745.description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.

ARCH 747B.title: Professional Studio: business
ARCH 747B.subject: ARCH
ARCH 747B.description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) practicum; (T) China.
ARCH 747B.prereq_raw: ARCH 744 , and ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (B), (G), and (T); ARCH 744 and ARCH 745 for (H); ARCH 726 , ARCH 744 , ARCH 745 , ARCH 750G , and ARCH 781 for (C), (E), and (P).
ARCH 747B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).

ARCH 747T.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).
