ARCH 749C.subject: ARCH
ARCH 749C.description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (C) China; (G) global.

ARCH 749G.title: Research Studio in Professional Setting: global
ARCH 749G.subject: ARCH
ARCH 749G.description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (C) China; (G) global.

ARCH 750C.title: Architecture Studio: China
ARCH 750C.subject: ARCH
ARCH 750C.description: Urban design focused on investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response. (C) China; (G) design research.
ARCH 750C.prereq_raw: ARCH 744 for (C); ARCH 739 and ARCH 743 for (G).
ARCH 750C.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH Global Track only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

ARCH 750G.title: Architecture Studio: design research
ARCH 750G.subject: ARCH
ARCH 750G.description: Urban design focused on investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response. (C) China; (G) design research.
ARCH 750G.prereq_raw: ARCH 744 for (C); ARCH 739 and ARCH 743 for (G).
ARCH 750G.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH Global Track only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

ARCH 754.title: Research Seminar
ARCH 754.subject: ARCH
ARCH 754.description: Varied topics furthering knowledge and ability needed for professional design practice emphasizing communication methods for collaborative and integrated design using digital technologies.

ARCH 755.title: Advanced Global Practice
ARCH 755.subject: ARCH
ARCH 755.description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.

ARCH 761.title: Ecology, Community, and Design
ARCH 761.subject: ARCH
ARCH 761.description: Exploration of the interaction of landscape and community necessities in urban ecological design. Studio problems, design research projects, lectures, and discussion applied to the integration of ecological and social factors in urban contexts. LAND majors only.
ARCH 761.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ARCH 763.title: Advanced Project Design Studio: Comprehensive
ARCH 763.subject: ARCH
ARCH 763.description: Design and programming for a complex, medium-scale, multi-layered urban landscape architecture project. Iterative, advanced design inquiry and materials exploration. Production of in-depth, comprehensive design development and partial construction documents.

ARCH 764D.title: Capstone Studio: design
ARCH 764D.subject: ARCH
ARCH 764D.description: Advanced landscape architectural design inquiry and applied research investigation. Serves as a capstone experience, synthesizing theory, values, and practice. Limited to MLA students under Plan B. (D) design (6 credits); (R) research (3 credits).

ARCH 764R.title: Capstone Studio: research
ARCH 764R.subject: ARCH
ARCH 764R.description: Advanced landscape architectural design inquiry and applied research investigation. Serves as a capstone experience, synthesizing theory, values, and practice. Limited to MLA students under Plan B. (D) design (6 credits); (R) research (3 credits).

ARCH 771.title: Architecture History
ARCH 771.subject: ARCH
ARCH 771.description: Investigation of architectural history and theory in the world from antiquity to present. Examining social, political, technological, material, and environmental forces.

ARCH 781.title: Advanced Research Methods and Design Inquiry
ARCH 781.subject: ARCH
ARCH 781.description: Individual development of a Doctorate Project or MArch Capstone proposal that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design.

ARCH 782.title: Case Study and Analysis
ARCH 782.subject: ARCH
ARCH 782.description: Individual development of a case study project that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions.

ARCH 783D.title: MArch Capstone Studio: design
ARCH 783D.subject: ARCH
ARCH 783D.description: Advanced capstone architectural design research synthesizing theory and practice. (D) design; (R) research.

ARCH 783R.title: MArch Capstone Studio: research
ARCH 783R.subject: ARCH
ARCH 783R.description: Advanced capstone architectural design research synthesizing theory and practice. (D) design; (R) research.

ARCH 784H.title: Doctorate Project I: Hawaiʻi
ARCH 784H.subject: ARCH
ARCH 784H.description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji.
ARCH 784H.prereq_raw: ARCH 747C or ARCH 747P or ARCH 747E for (H); ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (T).

ARCH 784T.title: Doctorate Project I: Tongi
ARCH 784T.subject: ARCH
ARCH 784T.description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji.
ARCH 784T.prereq_raw: ARCH 747C or ARCH 747P or ARCH 747E for (H); ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (T).

ARCH 786H.title: Doctorate Project II: Hawaiʻi
ARCH 786H.subject: ARCH
ARCH 786H.description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji.

ARCH 786T.title: Doctorate Project II: Tongi
ARCH 786T.subject: ARCH
ARCH 786T.description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji.

ARCH 788.title: Doctorate Project II Extension
ARCH 788.subject: ARCH
ARCH 788.description: Extension of the development of a doctorate project with an approved committee that advances architectural knowledge through research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions.

AREC 610.title: Biosystems Modeling
AREC 610.subject: AREC
AREC 610.description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system modes, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
AREC 610.prereq_raw: one of MATH 215 , MATH 241 , MATH 251A ; or consent.

AREC 626.title: Econometrics I
AREC 626.subject: AREC
AREC 626.description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.
AREC 626.prereq_raw: NREM 310 or ECON 321 , and MATH 241 ; or consent.

AREC 634.title: Econometrics II
AREC 634.subject: AREC
AREC 634.description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference, and forecasting of economic models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

ART 101.title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
ART 101.subject: ART
ART 101.description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice.
ART 101.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: (Not for art majors or minors)

ART 101A.title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
ART 101A.subject: ART
ART 101A.description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice.
ART 101A.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: (Not for art majors or minors)

ART 104.title: Introduction to Printmaking
ART 104.subject: ART
ART 104.description: Foundation explorations in the processes of relief, intaglio, and stencil printmaking. Direct workshop studio experience in the basic techniques and concepts of wood cut, linoleum cut, drypoint, monotype, and basic stencil processes.

ART 107B.title: Introduction to Photography: Black & White Darkroom
ART 107B.subject: ART
ART 107B.description: Studio/lecture combining history, theory and practice of photography. (B) film and darkroom, students must have 35mm film-based camera with adjustable shutter speed, aperture, and light meter; (D) digital, students must have digital camera with manual control and image editing software.

ART 107D.title: Introduction to Photography: Digital
ART 107D.subject: ART
ART 107D.description: Studio/lecture combining history, theory and practice of photography. (B) film and darkroom, students must have 35mm film-based camera with adjustable shutter speed, aperture, and light meter; (D) digital, students must have digital camera with manual control and image editing software.

ART 113.title: Introduction to Drawing
ART 113.subject: ART
ART 113.description: Descriptive, expressive, and formal aspects of visual language through drawing practice.

ART 116.title: Introduction to Three-Dimensional Composition
ART 116.subject: ART
ART 116.description: Basic concepts, elements, and principles of art.

ART 123.title: Introduction to Painting
ART 123.subject: ART
ART 123.description: Theory and practice of painting; material and technical procedures. A standalone course aimed at non-majors. ART majors should start with ART 223 after taking ART 113 .

ART 130.title: Introduction to Glass
ART 130.subject: ART
ART 130.description: Basic techniques of working with cold and molten glass. Theory of glass studio operation and introduction to glass theory.

ART 175.title: Survey of Global Art I
ART 175.subject: ART
ART 175.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 175A.title: Survey of Global Art I
ART 175A.subject: ART
ART 175A.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 176.title: Survey of Global Art II
ART 176.subject: ART
ART 176.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 176A.title: Survey of Global Art II
ART 176A.subject: ART
ART 176A.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 189.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Art
ART 189.subject: ART
ART 189.description: Integrated beginning studio art course, which offers students the opportunity to understand and express Hawaiian cultural perspectives through contemporary art practice.

ART 201.title: Introduction to Electronic Arts
ART 201.subject: ART
ART 201.description: Theory and practice course investigating language common to all arts activity particularly as related to the contemporary arts.
ART 201.prereq_raw: any studio art course; or consent.

ART 202.title: Introduction to Digital Imaging
ART 202.subject: ART
ART 202.description: Combined theory and practice examining major techniques, concepts, and aesthetics in contemporary digital image production. Direct studio experience in essential software, printing techniques and hardware necessary in producing the gallery quality inkjet print.

ART 207.title: Intermediate Photo (Black and White Darkroom)
ART 207.subject: ART
ART 207.description: Black and white photography emphasizing communication and self-expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and projects. Student must supply camera and material.
ART 207.prereq_raw: ART 107 B (with a minimum grade of B).

ART 213.title: Intermediate Drawing
ART 213.subject: ART
ART 213.description: Extension of the observational foundation established in ART 113 to address contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches to drawing.

ART 214.title: Introduction to Life Drawing
ART 214.subject: ART
ART 214.description: Investigations of the figure concerning anatomical construction, light, space, diagramatic analysis, and thematic content.

ART 215.title: Intaglio Printmaking
ART 215.subject: ART
ART 215.description: Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from metal plates including etching, engraving, aquatint, and drypoint.

ART 217.title: Screenprinting
ART 217.subject: ART
ART 217.description: Studio practice in screenprinting on paper. Copy camera and basic photo-stencil techniques introduced.

ART 218.title: Relief Printmaking
ART 218.subject: ART
ART 218.description: Studio practice in the techniques and concepts of woodblock, linoleum cut, monotype, and calligraph printmaking. Emphasis on both traditional and contemporary practices.

ART 223.title: Approaches to Painting
ART 223.subject: ART
ART 223.description: Theory and practice of painting; contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches.

ART 225.title: Painting/Water-Based Media
ART 225.subject: ART
ART 225.description: An introduction to water-based media. Traditional transparent color, gouache and acrylics.

ART 230.title: Glass Casting: Sand and Metal Molds
ART 230.subject: ART
ART 230.description: Expressive explorations in glass casting with wet sand, bonded sand, and metal molds.

ART 234.title: Cold Glass Fabrication
ART 234.subject: ART
ART 234.description: Expressive explorations using architectural sheet glass. Development of 2D and 3D forms using engraving, sandblasting, and cold joinery techniques.

ART 242.title: Introduction to Ceramics
ART 242.subject: ART
ART 242.description: Three-dimensional concepts in clay; hand-building and wheel-throwing techniques. Projects, lectures, and demonstrations.

AS 101.title: United States Air Force Heritage and Values I
AS 101.subject: AS
AS 101.description: Develops Department of the Air Force writing, speaking, and briefing skills while examining warfare, joint operations, command structures, and professionalism, enabling students to communicate clearly in operational military environments across the force.

AS 101L.title: Initial Military Training I
AS 101L.subject: AS
AS 101L.description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps.
AS 101L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to all majors.

AS 102.title: Competition and Security
AS 102.subject: AS
AS 102.description: Introductory-level exploration of national security, encompassing a broad perspective on the military’s involvement in all facets of national security, ranging from cooperation to armed conflict.

AS 102L.title: Initial Military Training II
AS 102L.subject: AS
AS 102L.description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps.
AS 102L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to all majors.

AS 201.title: Team and Leadership Fundamentals I
AS 201.subject: AS
AS 201.description: Provides a fundamental understanding of both leadership and team building. The course flow is designed to prepare students for field training and leadership positions.
AS 201.prereq_raw: AS 101 and AS 101L and AS 102 and AS 102L ; or instructor approval.

AS 201L.title: Basic Cadet Leader I
AS 201L.subject: AS
AS 201L.description: Laboratory consists of preparing second-year AFROTC cadets with the skills needed to successfully complete AFROTC Field Training. Students will learn basic military skills, Field Training skills, and participate in physical fitness training.

AS 202.title: Team and Leadership Fundamentals II
AS 202.subject: AS
AS 202.description: Continuation of AS 201 . Provides a fundamental understanding of both leadership and team building. This course is designed to prepare students for field training and leadership positions.

AS 301.title: Leading People and Effective Communication I
AS 301.subject: AS
AS 301.description: Utilizes students’ field training experience to take a more in-depth look at leadership. Special emphasis placed on enhancing communication skills and refining ethical thought as a leader. Leadership and management techniques implemented in supervised environment.

AS 301L.title: Intermediate Cadet Leader I
AS 301L.subject: AS
AS 301L.description: Laboratory consists of demonstration of leadership and management skills needed to successfully function as an Air Force officer. Instruction will include lessons covering planning, organizational and communication skills, and the ability to use available resources to complete an assigned task.
AS 301L.prereq_raw: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent.

children.text: must have completed AFROTC Field Training;

AS 302.title: Leading People and Effective Communication II
AS 302.subject: AS
AS 302.description: Continuation of AS 301 . Takes a more in-depth look at leadership, with special emphasis on enhancing communication skills and its relationship to leadership, developing leadership and management techniques in a supervised environment.

AS 302L.title: Intermediate Cadet Leader II
AS 302L.subject: AS
AS 302L.prereq_raw: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent.

children.text: must have completed AFROTC Field Training;

AS 401.title: National Security and Preparation for Active Duty I
AS 401.subject: AS
AS 401.description: Provides students a foundational understanding of their role as military officers and how they directly tie to US National Security. Covers social and political issues facing the military profession commensurate with the senior college level.
AS 401.prereq_raw: AS 301 and AS 301L and AS 302 and AS 302L ; or instructor approval.

AS 401L.title: Senior Cadet Leader I
AS 401L.subject: AS
AS 401L.description: Laboratory consists of providing prospective Air Force officers opportunities to continue to develop leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills. Instruction will include preparation for active duty.
AS 401L.prereq_raw: must have completed AS 301 and AS 302L ; or consent.

AS 402.title: National Security and Preparation for Active-Duty II
AS 402.subject: AS
AS 402.description: Continuation of AS 401 . Provides college seniors guidance in their role as military officers and how they are tied to US national security, over-viewing complex social and political issues facing the military profession.

AS 402L.title: Senior Cadet Leader II
AS 402L.subject: AS
AS 402L.description: Laboratory consists of providing prospective Air Force officers opportunities to continue to develop leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills. Instruction will include preparation for active duty.
AS 402L.prereq_raw: must have completed AS 301 and AS 302L ; or consent.

ASAN 101.title: Introduction to Asian Studies
ASAN 101.subject: ASAN
ASAN 101.description: Introductory course focuses on change and continuity in the history, culture, values, and political institutions of South, East, and Southeast Asia, and the region’s interrelationships with the rest of the world.

ASAN 120.title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Asia
ASAN 120.subject: ASAN
ASAN 120.description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in Asia through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions.

ASAN 150.title: Introduction to Research and Writing in Asian Studies
ASAN 150.subject: ASAN
ASAN 150.description: Introduction to research and writing in Asian Studies provides a structured overview of the research and writing process from an interdisciplinary perspective, focused on Asia.

ASAN 201.title: Introduction to Asian Studies: East Asia
ASAN 201.subject: ASAN
ASAN 201.description: Understanding East Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

ASAN 202.title: Introduction to Asian Studies: South/ Southeast Asia
ASAN 202.subject: ASAN
ASAN 202.description: Understanding South and Southeast Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

ASAN 259.title: East Asian Popular Cultures
ASAN 259.subject: ASAN
ASAN 259.description: East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective.

ASAN 303.title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
ASAN 303.subject: ASAN
ASAN 303.description: Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization.

ASAN 305.title: Career Pathways in Asian Studies
ASAN 305.subject: ASAN
ASAN 305.description: Explore the range of careers related to Asian Studies and develop skills and materials to build your academic success into a meaningful career. Students create a job search portfolio they can share with prospective employers.

ASAN 308.title: Chinese Political Economy
ASAN 308.subject: ASAN
ASAN 308.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of the social and political issues in China, the interchange between state and society in national policies, relationships between cultural tradition and technological modernization in the social transformation process. Emphasis on writing instruction.
ASAN 308.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

ASAN 310.title: Studying Asia Culturally
ASAN 310.subject: ASAN
ASAN 310.description: Multidisciplinary. Classics of literature, philosophy, and religion shaping Asian beliefs and values.
ASAN 310.prereq_raw: ASAN 201 and ASAN 202 are recommended, but not required.

ASAN 312.title: Contemporary Asia
ASAN 312.subject: ASAN
ASAN 312.description: Multidisciplinary examination of problems and issues affecting peoples and institutions of contemporary Asia: ethnic, language, religious, and cultural differences; population growth; public health; economic development; political and social change; environmental problems; etc.
ASAN 312.prereq_raw: ASAN 201 and ASAN 202 are recommended, but not required.

ASAN 320C.subject: ASAN
ASAN 320C.description: Multidisciplinary examination of major Asian countries; cultural, social, economic, and political lives of their peoples. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (O) Okinawa; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other.

ASAN 323.title: The Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
ASAN 323.subject: ASAN
ASAN 323.description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills.

ASAN 324.title: Chado-the Way of Tea Practicum
ASAN 324.subject: ASAN
ASAN 324.description: Practice Japanese tea ceremony as host and guest. Learn to sit and move in the tearoom, how to serve and receive sweets and tea. Active participation in every class, including performing for classmates, is required.

ASAN 325B.title: Japanese Film: Art and History: 1900-1960
ASAN 325B.subject: ASAN
ASAN 325B.description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
ASAN 325B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

ASAN 325C.title: Japanese Film: Art and History: 1960-present
ASAN 325C.subject: ASAN
ASAN 325C.description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
ASAN 325C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

ASAN 325D.title: Japanese Film: Art and History: special topics
ASAN 325D.subject: ASAN
ASAN 325D.description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
ASAN 325D.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

ASAN 326.title: Media, Advertising & Desire in East Asia
ASAN 326.subject: ASAN
ASAN 326.description: Examines concepts of beauty and desire in East Asian cultures within historical and contemporary media contexts. Uses critical theory and in-depth case studies to explore how images, language, and branding work in contemporary Asian societies.

ASAN 330.title: Chinese Film: Art and History
ASAN 330.subject: ASAN
ASAN 330.description: Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts.

ASAN 336.title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
ASAN 336.subject: ASAN
ASAN 336.description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course.

ASAN 356.title: Geography of Southeast Asia
ASAN 356.subject: ASAN
ASAN 356.description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change. Sophomore standing or higher.

ASAN 360.title: Buddhist Philosophy
ASAN 360.subject: ASAN
ASAN 360.description: Survey of central thinkers and schools.

ASAN 361.title: Topics in Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
ASAN 361.subject: ASAN
ASAN 361.description: This course explores traditional and modern Southeast Asian literature, focusing on key texts from various periods and genres. It emphasizes developing written communication skills through writing instruction.

ASAN 364.title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
ASAN 364.subject: ASAN
ASAN 364.description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
ASAN 364.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

ASAN 393C.subject: ASAN

ASAN 406.title: Modern Philippines
ASAN 406.subject: ASAN
ASAN 406.description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

ASAN 407.title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawaiʻi
ASAN 407.subject: ASAN
ASAN 407.description: History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. Junior standing only.

ASAN 410.title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
ASAN 410.subject: ASAN
ASAN 410.description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

ASAN 411.title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
ASAN 411.subject: ASAN
ASAN 411.description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies. Junior standing or higher.

ASAN 412.title: Gender, Sexuality, and the Geopolitics of Korean Popular Culture
ASAN 412.subject: ASAN
ASAN 412.description: Using South Korean popular culture as a case study, this lecture/discussion/seminar examines the relationship between popular culture and a range of forces including: politics, international relations, military, social movements, fandoms, and industries.
ASAN 412.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ASAN 413.title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
ASAN 413.subject: ASAN
ASAN 413.description: Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions.
ASAN 413.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher.

ASAN 420.title: Korean Cinema
ASAN 420.subject: ASAN
ASAN 420.description: Develop an understanding of Korean culture and society through visual, narrative, and contextual analysis of Korean films. Topics include post-Korean War experience, compressed modernity, authoritarianism, and post-authoritarian transformation. Special attention to independent films.

ASAN 422.title: Contested Issues Korea and Japan
ASAN 422.subject: ASAN
ASAN 422.description: In-depth understanding of Korean-Japanese relations in the past and present by examining conflicting views and interpretations by Japanese, Korean, and Western scholars on important issues that divide the people of East Asia.

ASAN 438.title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
ASAN 438.subject: ASAN
ASAN 438.description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.
ASAN 438.prereq_raw: ASAN 310 or ASAN 312 or PLAN 310 , or consent.

ASAN 443.title: Statecraft and Diplomacy in East Asia
ASAN 443.subject: ASAN
ASAN 443.description: Examines the history and architecture of diplomacy and statecraft in East Asia.

ASAN 449.title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
ASAN 449.subject: ASAN
ASAN 449.description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
ASAN 449.prereq_raw: ASAN 310 or PLAN 310 or ASAN 312 , or consent.

ASAN 461.title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
ASAN 461.subject: ASAN
ASAN 461.description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.
ASAN 461.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ASAN 462.title: Contested Issues in Contemporary Japan
ASAN 462.subject: ASAN
ASAN 462.description: Familiarizes students with public discourse in Japan by analyzing key current issues widely debated in the Japanese media and in public forums in light of their political, historical, cultural, social and economic contexts.

ASAN 463.title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
ASAN 463.subject: ASAN
ASAN 463.description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g., with class, religion, ethnicity).

ASAN 464.title: K-pop and J-pop: Korean and Japanese Popular Music and Society
ASAN 464.subject: ASAN
ASAN 464.description: Examines modern Japan and South Korea through popular music. Examines genres from early popular music, today’s K-pop and J-pop music.

ASAN 465.title: Japan Cool: Anime, Manga, and Film
ASAN 465.subject: ASAN
ASAN 465.description: Focus on Japanese anime, manga, and films with an emphasis on oral communication. What can one learn about Japanese issues of gender, national identity, and race?

ASAN 466.title: Transpacific Youth Pop Culture: From K-pop to Tiktok
ASAN 466.subject: ASAN
ASAN 466.description: Examines ties between East Asian and Asian American digital media, including comics, movies, TV shows, music, and video games, to examine the dreams, fears, and aspirations of young Asians and Asian Americans.

ASAN 473.title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture-Chinese Diaspora
ASAN 473.subject: ASAN
ASAN 473.description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term.
ASAN 473.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course or consent.

ASAN 474.title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
ASAN 474.subject: ASAN
ASAN 474.description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism.
ASAN 474.prereq_raw: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course.

ASAN 476.title: Perspectives on Chinese Cinema
ASAN 476.subject: ASAN
ASAN 476.description: Introduction to Chinese cinema studies, with emphasis on the theoretical and critical approaches to Chinese film.
ASAN 476.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

ASAN 478C.subject: ASAN
ASAN 478C.description: The study of a musical culture area. (C) China; (D) Japan; (E) Korea; (F) Indonesia; (G) Philippines; (H) India.

ASAN 484.title: Political Violence in Modern Southeast Asia
ASAN 484.subject: ASAN
ASAN 484.description: Why do Southeast Asian governments and political movements engage in mass killings? How do their perpetrators justify these atrocities? How do survivors deal with their trauma and get their voices heard?

ASAN 485.title: Contemporary Chinese Development
ASAN 485.subject: ASAN
ASAN 485.description: Development and planning in contemporary China: economic policy and institutional structure in the development and urbanization process; urban and rural transformation in a socialist economy.

ASAN 492.title: Women and Revolution
ASAN 492.subject: ASAN
ASAN 492.description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

ASAN 494.title: Food, Culture, and Politics in Asia
ASAN 494.subject: ASAN
ASAN 494.description: Examines Asia’s role in the development of global foodways. Topics include the relationship between spices and imperialism, global popularity of Asian cuisines, Asian-influenced “hapa” cuisine in Hawaiʻi, McDonaldization in Asia, and food security and sustainability.

ASAN 496.title: Religions of Island Southeast Asia
ASAN 496.subject: ASAN
ASAN 496.description: A comparative, interdisciplinary examination of indigenous beliefs, Islam, Christianity, and Hinduism in island Southeast Asia, and how they have been adjusted because of economic and social change.

ASAN 600C.subject: ASAN
ASAN 600C.description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. ASAN 600K.subject: ASAN
ASAN 600K.description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

ASAN 600P.title: Approaches to Asian Studies: Philippines
ASAN 600P.subject: ASAN
ASAN 600P.description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

ASAN 600S.title: Approaches to Asian Studies: Southeast Asia
ASAN 600S.subject: ASAN
ASAN 600S.description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

ASAN 600Z.title: Approaches to Asian Studies: Inter-Asia
ASAN 600Z.subject: ASAN
ASAN 600Z.description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

ASAN 601.title: Advanced Research and Writing in Asian Studies
ASAN 601.subject: ASAN
ASAN 601.description: Provides a structured overview of research and writing process, focused on Asia. Topics include research questions, abstracts, literature reviews, arguments, conceptualization, incorporating evidence, research ethics, and style. Students are required to produce a research paper.

ASAN 608.title: Politics and Development: China
ASAN 608.subject: ASAN
ASAN 608.description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

ASAN 611.title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
ASAN 611.subject: ASAN
ASAN 611.description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies.

ASAN 612.title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
ASAN 612.subject: ASAN
ASAN 612.description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required.

ASAN 620.title: Problems/Issues of Contemporary Asia
ASAN 620.subject: ASAN
ASAN 620.description: Analysis from multidisciplinary perspective: rural development, urbanization, international relations, ethnicity, religion, language, etc.

ASAN 623.title: Gender in Asian Performing Arts
ASAN 623.subject: ASAN
ASAN 623.description: Performance is a rich site for gender construction, critique, and articulation in Asia. This seminar examines gender reflected in traditional music, dance, and theatre, including character role and performer persona; approaches of performance and culture studies, and an “Asian way.”

ASAN 624.title: Culture and Colonialism
ASAN 624.subject: ASAN
ASAN 624.description: Analysis of theories and debates (cultural studies, feminist writings, post-colonial issues). Case studies of the transformation and creation of “traditional” cultures under colonialism.

ASAN 626.title: Capitalism in Contemporary Asia
ASAN 626.subject: ASAN
ASAN 626.description: Historically grounded theoretical examination of capitalism in 20th-century Asia; multidisciplinary approach to fundamental change in political and economic structures and institutions, prospects for the future.

ASAN 627.title: Ethnic Nationalism in Asia
ASAN 627.subject: ASAN
ASAN 627.description: Contemporary theories of ethnic and cultural nationalism from perspective of Asia. Issues of nation-state, power hierarchies, modernity, and identity in contemporary societies.

ASAN 629.title: Asian Security Cultures
ASAN 629.subject: ASAN
ASAN 629.description: Comparative study of conceptualizations, practices and institutions of national security in Asia in light of their geographic and historic contexts.

ASAN 630.title: Southeast Asia Now
ASAN 630.subject: ASAN
ASAN 630.description: Examines the ways global influences are shaping the cultural developments in the diverse societies of contemporary Southeast Asia.

ASAN 636.title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
ASAN 636.subject: ASAN
ASAN 636.description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

ASAN 640.title: Topics in Japanese Literature
ASAN 640.subject: ASAN
ASAN 640.description: Intensive study of selected topics in Japanese literature, primarily of the modern period. English translations of original texts will be provided whenever available.

ASAN 647.title: Contemporary Chinese Documentary: Record, Expression, Cultural Space
ASAN 647.subject: ASAN
ASAN 647.description: Introduction to contemporary Chinese independent documentary with these goals: to achieve in-depth understanding of Chinese society through documentary; be familiar with theoretical debates on documentary form; and understand documentary as a cultural discourse.

ASAN 649.title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
ASAN 649.subject: ASAN
ASAN 649.description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

ASAN 650.title: Marriage and Family in East Asia
ASAN 650.subject: ASAN
ASAN 650.description: Examines gendered/generational practices, expectations, and ideologies of marriage, childrearing, and caregiving; state’s role in legitimizing certain kinds of families; how transnational marriage migration is changing notions of belonging, relatedness, and national identity in East Asia. Graduate standing or consent.

ASAN 651.title: East Asia Now
ASAN 651.subject: ASAN
ASAN 651.description: Views East Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic and political themes including various experiences with the West. Focus upon present state of the region.

ASAN 653.title: Major Authors in Modern Korean Literature
ASAN 653.subject: ASAN
ASAN 653.description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature.

ASAN 654.title: South Asia Now
ASAN 654.subject: ASAN
ASAN 654.description: Views South Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic, and political themes, including global interactions. Focus upon present state of the region.
ASAN 654.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASAN 658.title: Telecom and the Internet in East Asia
ASAN 658.subject: ASAN
ASAN 658.description: Offers interdisciplinary approach to study of internet and telecommunications in East Asia. Examines growth and development of telecommunications networks in China, Japan, South and North Korea. Focuses on contemporary social media and government policy.

ASAN 664.title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
ASAN 664.subject: ASAN
ASAN 664.description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical socio-cultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history.

ASAN 665.title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
ASAN 665.subject: ASAN
ASAN 665.description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective.

ASAN 670.title: Southeast Asia and its Neighbors
ASAN 670.subject: ASAN
ASAN 670.description: Examines how Southeast Asian nations have recalibrated their international relationships in accordance with past experience and new concerns, focusing on interactions with Japan, China, and India, while integrating both global and domestic imperatives.

ASAN 686.title: Law and Society in China
ASAN 686.subject: ASAN
ASAN 686.description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

ASAN 687.title: Conflict and Cooperation in Asia
ASAN 687.subject: ASAN
ASAN 687.description: Explores conflict and cooperation among Asian nations. Topics may include economic integration, business networks, space and cyberspace, military alliances, territorial disputes, transnational crime, environmental cooperation, soft power, and regional institutional architecture.
ASAN 687.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASAN 688.title: Chinese Foreign Policy
ASAN 688.subject: ASAN
ASAN 688.description: Examination of China’s rise and world view, review of China’s regional relations, China and U.S. relations, formation of a new world order.
ASAN 688.prereq_raw: ASAN 600 , ASAN 608 , or POLS 645C , or consent.

ASAN 689.title: International Relations in Asia
ASAN 689.subject: ASAN
ASAN 689.description: How well do international relations theories explain interstate relations in Asia? How do international issues interact with domestic politics? Covers Japan, China, Korea, ASEAN nations, India, and touches on Russia, Australia, and New Zealand.
ASAN 689.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASAN 693.title: Field Study in Asia
ASAN 693.subject: ASAN
ASAN 693.description: With prior consent and supervision of an Asian Studies faculty, students design, conduct, and write the results of a field research project.
ASAN 693.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASAN 694.title: Topics in Buddhist Studies
ASAN 694.subject: ASAN
ASAN 694.description: Seminar on selected topics in Buddhist studies.
ASAN 694.prereq_raw: PHIL 360 , PHIL 406 , REL 475 , or REL 490 ; or consent.

ASAN 695.title: Asian Studies Master’s Plan B Culminating Experience
ASAN 695.subject: ASAN
ASAN 695.description: Students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend a portfolio of work produced in seminars before a three-person faculty committee.
ASAN 695.prereq_raw: any ASAN 600(Alpha) or ASAN 601 with a minimum grade of B-.

ASAN 705.title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
ASAN 705.subject: ASAN
ASAN 705.description: Bibliography, reference tools, and research methods in sources on Asia in Western and Asian languages. Discussion of published and archival repositories.

ASAN 710.title: MAIA Capstone
ASAN 710.subject: ASAN
ASAN 710.description: Capstone experience for MAIA students that emphasizes practical applications of Asia knowledge. Should be taken in final semester or after completion of all or most of MAIA core requirements.

ASAN 792.title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
ASAN 792.subject: ASAN
ASAN 792.description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.
ASAN 792.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ASL 101.title: Elementary American Sign Language I
ASL 101.subject: ASL
ASL 101.description: Development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 102.title: Elementary American Sign Language II
ASL 102.subject: ASL
ASL 102.description: Continued development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 201.title: Intermediate American Sign Language I
ASL 201.subject: ASL
ASL 201.description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 202.title: Intermediate American Sign Language II
ASL 202.subject: ASL
ASL 202.description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 301.title: Advanced American Sign Language I
ASL 301.subject: ASL
ASL 301.description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL).

ASL 302.title: Advanced American Sign Language II
ASL 302.subject: ASL
ASL 302.description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL).

ASTR 110.title: Survey of Astronomy
ASTR 110.subject: ASTR
ASTR 110.description: Introduction to the astronomical universe: sky and celestial objects, planetary motion, planets and the Solar System, Sun and stars, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology and the universe.

ASTR 110L.title: Survey of Astronomy Laboratory
ASTR 110L.subject: ASTR
ASTR 110L.description: Observations of constellations and the night sky, the sun and moon, planets, stars, and deep-sky objects; laboratory and observational experiments illustrating basic concepts in astronomy.

ASTR 130.title: Introduction to Archaeoastronomy
ASTR 130.subject: ASTR
ASTR 130.description: Astronomy and celestial lore in ancient cultures: Neolithic Europe, Mayan, Mesoamerican, Egyptian, Mesopotamian, American Indian, Chinese, and Polynesian. Concepts of the cosmos, calendars, eclipse predictions, motion of celestial bodies, and navigation. Construction of simple observing tools.

ASTR 150.title: Voyage through the Solar System
ASTR 150.subject: ASTR
ASTR 150.description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

ASTR 185.title: Introduction to Astronomical Research
ASTR 185.subject: ASTR
ASTR 185.description: Introduction to astronomical research, including literature resources, basic computing skills, software tools, data analysis, scientific communication, and research opportunities. Prepares students for effective internships and directed research projects.
ASTR 185.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR and ASTP majors only.

ASTR 210.title: Foundations of Astronomy
ASTR 210.subject: ASTR
ASTR 210.description: A rigorous overview of modern astronomy: solar system, stellar, galactic and extragalactic astronomy and cosmology.
ASTR 210.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: For science and engineering students.

ASTR 241.title: Foundations of Astrophysics I: The Solar System
ASTR 241.subject: ASTR
ASTR 241.description: Solar system astrophysics. Dynamics of planets, satellite systems, asteroids and comets; planetary atmospheres and internal structure; thermal balance; the Sun as a star. Introduces numerical computing.
ASTR 241.prereq_raw: PHYS 170 , MATH 242 or MATH 252A , and PHYS 272 (or concurrent).

ASTR 242.title: Foundations of Astrophysics II: Galaxies and Stars
ASTR 242.subject: ASTR
ASTR 242.description: Stellar and galactic astrophysics. Stellar magnitudes, colors, distances, and spectra. Galactic structure and evolution, active nuclei, large-scale structure, Big-Bang cosmology. Stellar interiors, nuclear “burning,” main-sequence and evolved stars. Introduces computer programming.
ASTR 242.prereq_raw: ASTR 241 , PHYS 274 (or concurrent), and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

ASTR 280.title: Evolution of the Universe
ASTR 280.subject: ASTR
ASTR 280.description: The Big Bang, origin of the elements, formation and evolution of galaxies and stars.
ASTR 280.prereq_raw: ASTR 110 or ASTR 210 or ASTR 241 or ASTR 242 , or consent

ASTR 281.title: Astrobiology
ASTR 281.subject: ASTR
ASTR 281.description: Are we alone in the universe? Astronomical, biological, and geological perspectives on this fundamental question. Course discusses with a writing emphasis: habitability, resources, space exploration, searches for life on Mars, solar system moons, and exoplanets.

ASTR 300.title: Observational Astronomy
ASTR 300.subject: ASTR
ASTR 300.description: Principles and techniques of optical and near-infrared astronomical observation. Astronomical coordinate systems. Telescopes, cameras, spectrographs, and detectors. Astrometry, photometry, and spectroscopy of astronomical objects.
ASTR 300.prereq_raw: ASTR 210 or ASTR 242 ; PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

ASTR 300L.title: Observational Astronomy Laboratory
ASTR 300L.subject: ASTR
ASTR 300L.description: Optical and near-infrared astronomy laboratory. Error analysis, properties of light, data, and image processing. Astrometric, photometric, and spectroscopic measurement.
ASTR 300L.prereq_raw: ASTR 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; PHYS 152L or PHYS 274L ; MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

ASTR 301.title: Observational Astronomy Projects
ASTR 301.subject: ASTR
ASTR 301.description: Astronomical observational research projects. Students use astronomical data and process telescopic observations to produce scientific results, and present these orally and in writing. Students prepare for independent research projects and present research plans orally.

ASTR 320.title: Astronomical Spectroscopy
ASTR 320.subject: ASTR
ASTR 320.description: Introduction to astronomical spectroscopy. Stellar atmospheres, line formation, elements of radiative transfer. Phases of interstellar medium. Emission line diagnostics. Doppler shift and kinematics.
ASTR 320.prereq_raw: ASTR 210 or ASTR 242 ; PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

ASTR 326.title: Modern Extragalactic Astronomy
ASTR 326.subject: ASTR
ASTR 326.description: Use of astronomical surveys to map large-scale distribution of galaxies. Internal structure & dynamics of galaxies. Evolution of galaxy populations over cosmic time. Theoretical understanding of galaxy formation in context of modern Big Bang cosmology.
ASTR 326.prereq_raw: ASTR 210 or ASTR 242 ; and ASTR 300 (or concurrent); and PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 . Recommended: ASTR 280

ASTR 380.title: History of Cosmology and Scientific Thought
ASTR 380.subject: ASTR
ASTR 380.description: History and intellectual context of astronomical discovery; the evolution of ideas of space, time, and motion from the Babylonians to relativistic cosmologies; emphasis on the interaction of astronomy with the history of ideas.

ASTR 399.title: Directed Study
ASTR 399.subject: ASTR
ASTR 399.description: Individual reading, observation, or experimentation in astronomy and astrophysics.

ASTR 423.title: Stellar Astrophysics
ASTR 423.subject: ASTR
ASTR 423.description: Advanced survey of stellar astrophysics, including application of astrometry, photometry, and spectrometry to determine fundamental stellar properties; stellar structure and evolution of single and binary stars; astrophysical distance determination methods; stellar nucleosynthesis.

ASTR 426.title: Galaxies & Cosmology
ASTR 426.subject: ASTR
ASTR 426.description: Survey of extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, including: galaxy morphology and kinematics; luminosity functions; dark matter; properties of galaxy groups/clusters; gravitational lensing; redshifts; cosmological models; the Big Bang; thermal history of the Universe; structure formation.
ASTR 426.prereq_raw: ASTR 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A .

ASTR 430.title: The Solar System
ASTR 430.subject: ASTR
ASTR 430.description: Observations and physical nature of planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and other small bodies; formation of the Solar System; discovery of other planetary systems; solar activity.
ASTR 430.prereq_raw: ASTR 300 ; and PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; and MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

ASTR 470.title: General Relativity & Cosmology
ASTR 470.subject: ASTR
ASTR 470.description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation.
ASTR 470.prereq_raw: PHYS 274 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: ASTR 242 .

ASTR 494.title: Senior Research Project
ASTR 494.subject: ASTR
ASTR 494.description: Seminar focusing on development of professional skills for astronomical research, and on scientific writing as a tool for organizing research. A final paper describing a supervised research project is required.
ASTR 494.prereq_raw: ASTR 301 , ASTR 399 (or concurrent) or PHYS 399 (or concurrent).

ASTR 601.title: Being a Professional Astronomer
ASTR 601.subject: ASTR
ASTR 601.description: Seminar for beginning graduate students focusing on professional skills needed for astronomy and discussing possible research opportunities.
ASTR 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASTR 622.title: The Interstellar Medium
ASTR 622.subject: ASTR
ASTR 622.description: Astrophysics of diffuse matter, HII regions, molecular clouds, etc.

ASTR 623.title: Stellar Interiors and Evolution
ASTR 623.subject: ASTR
ASTR 623.description: Structure and evolution; energy sources, radiative processes; relations to observables.

ASTR 626.title: Galaxies
ASTR 626.subject: ASTR
ASTR 626.description: Observations and stellar dynamics of elliptical and spiral galaxies including our galaxy, globular clusters, and dark matter. Galaxy formation and evolution.

ASTR 627.title: Cosmology
ASTR 627.subject: ASTR
ASTR 627.description: Geometry and evolution of the universe. Dark matter. Early universe. Formation of large-scale structure, galaxies, and clusters. Cosmological models.

ASTR 630.title: The Solar System
ASTR 630.subject: ASTR
ASTR 630.description: Survey of observational data and physical concepts on planets and smaller bodies; formation of planetary systems; solar activity.

ASTR 631.title: Radiative Transfer Stellar Atmospheres
ASTR 631.subject: ASTR
ASTR 631.description: Excitation, ionization, and radiative transfer in stellar atmospheres; model atmospheres, formation of line and continuum radiation.

ASTR 633.title: Astrophysical Techniques
ASTR 633.subject: ASTR
ASTR 633.description: Telescopes, positional astronomy, photon detection, error analysis, photometry, spectroscopy.

ASTR 634.title: Astronomical Instrumentation
ASTR 634.subject: ASTR
ASTR 634.description: Design and operation of astronomical instrumentation. Physics of optical and infrared detectors. Wavefront sensors and adaptive optics. Radio and infrared interferometry. Optical design: methods and software.
ASTR 634.prereq_raw: ASTR 633 (with a minimum grade of B-).

ASTR 635.title: Fundamentals of Astrophysics
ASTR 635.subject: ASTR
ASTR 635.description: Applications of fundamental physics to astrophysical situations. Elements of general relativity. Basics of hydrodynamics and shock waves. Radiative processes, high energy astrophysics. Modern dynamics.

ASTR 640.title: General Relativity
ASTR 640.subject: ASTR
ASTR 640.description: Introduction to gravity and general relativity. Tensor basics, classical scalar, vector and tensor field theories. Exact symmetric Einstein equation, gravito-magnetic weak field, and radiation solutions.

ASTR 641.title: Active Galaxies
ASTR 641.subject: ASTR
ASTR 641.description: Phenomenology of active galactic nuclei, black holes, accretion flows and jets, emission mechanisms, host galaxies, and cosmic evolution.

ASTR 657.title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
ASTR 657.subject: ASTR
ASTR 657.description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

ASTR 707.title: Exoplanet Astronomy
ASTR 707.subject: ASTR
ASTR 707.description: Accelerated survey of exoplanet astronomy and planetary systems using data from the field’s leading edge, introduction to key theoretical concepts, application of analytic and numerical tools, and development of teamwork, presentation and publishing skills.
ASTR 707.prereq_raw: ASTR 633 with a minimum grade of B, or instructor permission.

ASTR 734.title: Astronomy Seminar I
ASTR 734.subject: ASTR
ASTR 734.description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

ASTR 735.title: Astronomy Seminar II
ASTR 735.subject: ASTR
ASTR 735.description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

ASTR 736.title: Astronomy Seminar III
ASTR 736.subject: ASTR
ASTR 736.description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

ASTR 740.title: Astrobiology Seminar: Origin, Evolution and the Role of Water for Life in the Universe
ASTR 740.subject: ASTR
ASTR 740.description: Interdisciplinary research topics in astrobiology as they relate to the theme of water: formation in space, role in creating pre-biotic molecules, delivery to earth, and terrestrial planet habitability.
ASTR 740.prereq_raw: graduate level sciences and ideas, or consent.

ASTR 750.title: Scientific Grant Writing
ASTR 750.subject: ASTR
ASTR 750.description: Principles of scientific grant writing are taught by working on draft proposals through a mix of lectures, discussions, and hands on activities. The final proposal will be reviewed and evaluated via a review panel.
ASTR 750.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASTR 758.title: Programming and Algorithms for Astronomers
ASTR 758.subject: ASTR
ASTR 758.description: Distillation of modern computer science fundamentals and paradigms, with applications to astronomy. Common algorithms and essential programming techniques. Assignments include extensive Python programming practice. Open to graduate students in any physical science.
ASTR 758.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ASTR 760.title: Modern General Relativity
ASTR 760.subject: ASTR
ASTR 760.description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques.
ASTR 760.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR.

ASTR 777.title: Star Formation
ASTR 777.subject: ASTR
ASTR 777.description: Molecular clouds, collapse processes, physics of circumstellar disks and accretion, properties of young stars, outflows and jets, formation of binaries, extrasolar planets and planet formation, meteorites and the early solar system.
ASTR 777.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ASTR 790.title: Astro-ph Seminar
ASTR 790.subject: ASTR
ASTR 790.description: Seminar discussions of the most recent research papers covering all areas of astronomy. Students lead discussion sessions and discuss papers of their choice during the semester.

ASTR 791.title: Cosmology Seminar
ASTR 791.subject: ASTR
ASTR 791.description: Students and researchers will review and discuss the most important and exciting cosmological results in depth.
ASTR 791.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR and PHYS majors only.

ASTR 792.title: Stars and Planets Lunch and Talks (SPLAT) Seminar
ASTR 792.subject: ASTR
ASTR 792.description: Seminar for graduate students and researchers discussing the latest results on solar, stellar, and exoplanet research.
ASTR 792.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ATMO 101.title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
ATMO 101.subject: ATMO
ATMO 101.description: Introductory physical science course for all undergraduates in any major. A non-mathematical introduction to basic atmospheric variables, Earth’s past climates, global warming, air pollution, El Nino, hurricanes, tornadoes, and forecasting weather in Hawaiʻi.

ATMO 101L.title: Introduction to Weather and Climate Lab
ATMO 101L.subject: ATMO
ATMO 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Exercises with meteorological data and measurement systems. Characteristics of Hawaiian winds, temperatures, and rainfall.

ATMO 102.title: Pacific Climates and Cultures
ATMO 102.subject: ATMO
ATMO 102.description: Highlights the interface between the observed weather and climate of the Pacific and the past and future culture of the people of the Hawaiian and Pacific islands.

ATMO 199.title: Introduction to MET Undergraduate Directed Research
ATMO 199.subject: ATMO
ATMO 199.description: Students gain familiarity with ATMO research. Students can select 1-3 credits per semester for maximum 6 credits over 4 semesters. Students must pre-arrange research and reading content with instructor.
ATMO 199.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Freshman and sophomore standing only.

ATMO 200.title: Atmospheric Processes and Phenomena
ATMO 200.subject: ATMO
ATMO 200.description: Atmospheric variables, gas laws, radiation processes, thermodynamics, conservation laws, dynamic approximations, clouds and precipitation, convection, atmospheric circulations, mid-latitude and tropical weather systems, forecasting, climate.

ATMO 300.title: Atmospheric Energy and Circulation
ATMO 300.subject: ATMO
ATMO 300.description: Conceptual introduction to atmospheric structure and motion, focusing on thermodynamics and dynamics. Emphasizes physical intuition, real-world examples, and visual tools over math. Topics include cloud formation, atmospheric stability, wind systems, and weather patterns.

ATMO 302.title: Atmospheric Physics
ATMO 302.subject: ATMO
ATMO 302.description: Energy and thermodynamics, statics and stability, physical processes of cloud formation, radiation and Earth-atmosphere heat balance, kinetic theory, optical effects.
ATMO 302.prereq_raw: ATMO 200 , MATH 242 , and PHYS 272 ; or consent.

ATMO 303.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Dynamics
ATMO 303.subject: ATMO
ATMO 303.description: Scalar and vector development of basic laws of hydrodynamics, equations of motion, kinematics, divergence and vorticity, viscosity and turbulence, introduction to numerical weather prediction, general circulation.

ATMO 304.title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
ATMO 304.subject: ATMO
ATMO 304.description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawaiʻi. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only.

ATMO 305.title: Meteorological Instruments and Observations
ATMO 305.subject: ATMO
ATMO 305.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Each week targets a different meteorological instrument and culminates in a lab exercise and report. The focus is on accurate measurement and scientific-style writing.

ATMO 310.title: Global Environmental Change
ATMO 310.subject: ATMO
ATMO 310.description: Delve into global environmental change issues such as geometric population growth, food production, plastic waste, and global warming that are of growing interest and importance to our society. Designed for non-GES majors.
ATMO 310.prereq_raw: ATMO 200 , OCN 201 , or similar environmental/ natural sciences course.

ATMO 320.title: Programming for Meteorologists
ATMO 320.subject: ATMO
ATMO 320.description: Scientific programming in Fortran 77, graphics software and meteorological applications.
ATMO 320.prereq_raw: ATMO 302 (or concurrent) and MATH 241 ; or consent.

ATMO 395.title: Undergraduate Internship
ATMO 395.subject: ATMO
ATMO 395.description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.
ATMO 395.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior/ senior standing and consent.

ATMO 399.title: Undergraduate Directed Reading
ATMO 399.subject: ATMO
ATMO 399.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior and senior standing only.

ATMO 402.title: Applied Atmospheric Dynamics
ATMO 402.subject: ATMO
ATMO 402.description: Advanced concepts in dynamics: vorticity, cyclogenesis, jet streams, fronts, mesoscale circulations.

ATMO 405.title: Synoptic Satellite Meteorology
ATMO 405.subject: ATMO
ATMO 405.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Satellite applications to synoptic meteorology and forecasting, including orbital elements, ephemerides, viewing geometry, radiation, satellite sensors, and interpreting satellite data.

ATMO 406.title: Tropical Meteorology
ATMO 406.subject: ATMO
ATMO 406.description: History; tropical clouds and hydrometeors; typhoons; monsoons; local and diurnal effects.

ATMO 412.title: Meteorological Analysis Lab
ATMO 412.subject: ATMO
ATMO 412.description: (2 4-hr Lab) Techniques and methods of forecasting extratropical systems with analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems. Students will be instructed on how to communicate and discuss a weather forecast and how to present a research paper.

ATMO 416.title: Tropical Analysis Lab
ATMO 416.subject: ATMO
ATMO 416.description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Techniques of portraying and analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems in tropical and equatorial regions; forecasting tropical systems.

ATMO 449.title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis, and Applications
ATMO 449.subject: ATMO
ATMO 449.description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results.

ATMO 452.title: Special Topics in Weather & Climate
ATMO 452.subject: ATMO
ATMO 452.description: Concentrated studies on selected weather and climate topics.

ATMO 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
ATMO 499.subject: ATMO
ATMO 499.description: Capstone for senior Meteorology majors. Undergraduate thesis project includes literature review, experiment or research design, data collection and analysis, technical writing of a final thesis paper and oral presentation of the paper. Junior and senior standing only.

ATMO 600.title: Atmospheric Dynamics I
ATMO 600.subject: ATMO
ATMO 600.description: Governing equations for moist atmospheric motions, approximations, basic theoretical models, boundary layer dynamics, atmospheric waves, quasi-geostrophic theory for mid-latitudes.
ATMO 600.prereq_raw: ATMO 402 , and either MATH 402 or MATH 405 ; or consent.

ATMO 601.title: Atmospheric Dynamics II
ATMO 601.subject: ATMO
ATMO 601.description: Overview of dynamic meteorology, numerical weather prediction, geophysical fluid instabilities, approximate dynamical systems, atmospheric general circulation, stratospheric dynamics.

ATMO 606.title: Cumulus Dynamics
ATMO 606.subject: ATMO
ATMO 606.description: Dynamics of convective systems: tornadoes, waterspouts, squall lines. Interactions with synoptic scale.

ATMO 607.title: Mesoscale Meteorology
ATMO 607.subject: ATMO
ATMO 607.description: Scale analysis. Observational and theoretical aspects of mesoscale circulation systems.

ATMO 610.title: Tropical Climate and Weather
ATMO 610.subject: ATMO
ATMO 610.description: Climate and general circulation of the tropics; El Niño and Southern Oscillation; intraseasonal oscillation; trade winds; tropical weather systems; energy balance; typhoons.

ATMO 611.title: Satellite Data Applications
ATMO 611.subject: ATMO
ATMO 611.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Principles and practices of satellite remote sensing as used in the atmospheric sciences, specifically clouds, aerosols, precipitation, ocean and land cover datasets from various satellites. Develop skills including data manipulation, analysis, and visualization using Matlab.

ATMO 614.title: Tropical Cyclones
ATMO 614.subject: ATMO
ATMO 614.description: Lecture covering fundamentals of tropical cyclone structure, motion, and impacts on society. Observations from satellites, aircraft, ships and buoys, and numerical simulations focusing on storm structure and track. Some forecasting exercises.

ATMO 616.title: Monsoon Meteorology
ATMO 616.subject: ATMO
ATMO 616.description: Synoptic components of monsoons, regional and temporal variability, numerical models, research exercises.

ATMO 620.title: Physical Meteorology
ATMO 620.subject: ATMO
ATMO 620.description: Molecular kinetics, atmospheric thermodynamics, cloud physics, precipitation processes, atmospheric electricity, scattering and absorption of solar radiation, absorption and emission of infrared radiation, radiative transfer.

ATMO 628.title: Radar Meteorology
ATMO 628.subject: ATMO
ATMO 628.description: (2 Lec, 1-3 hr. Lab) Radar hardware, electromagnetic propagation and scattering, radar equation, signal processing, precipitation estimation and polarimetric applications, Multi- Doppler wind synthesis, mobile and spaceborne radars, forecasting, and data assimilation applications.
ATMO 628.prereq_raw: ATMO 620 (with a minimum grade of B- or higher) or consent.

ATMO 631.title: Statistical Meteorology
ATMO 631.subject: ATMO
ATMO 631.description: Probability; frequency distributions of atmospheric variables; linear models; time series analysis (frequency and time domain); principal component analysis; statistical weather forecasting and verification.

ATMO 632.title: Advanced Statistical Methods in the Geosciences
ATMO 632.subject: ATMO
ATMO 632.description: Methods for numerous multivariate analyses will include singular spectrum, extended empirical orthogonal function, singular-value decomposition, canonical correlation, discriminant and cluster analysis. Other advanced topics include wavelet analysis, statistical downscaling and Bayesian analysis.

ATMO 640.title: Paleoclimate Model-Proxy Synthesis
ATMO 640.subject: ATMO
ATMO 640.description: Basics of Earth System Model development, parameterizations, intermodel variability and design of paleoclimate simulations. Types of proxies, tools and techniques for paleoclimate record development and reconstructions. Hypothesis testing and methods for proxy-model comparison studies.
ATMO 640.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO, GEO, EPET, NREM, OCN, and ORE majors only.

ATMO 665.title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
ATMO 665.subject: ATMO
ATMO 665.description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
ATMO 665.prereq_raw: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either ATMO 600 or OCN 620 ; or consent.

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either ATMO 600 or OCN 620 ; or consent

ATMO 666.title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
ATMO 666.subject: ATMO
ATMO 666.description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Niño/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

ATMO 702.title: Numerical Weather Prediction
ATMO 702.subject: ATMO
ATMO 702.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental methods and techniques in numerical weather prediction: time differencing, spatial finite differencing, spectral methods, numerical stability, explicit and implicit methods. Modern operational and research forecast models. Hands-on laboratory includes simple to complex dynamic models, with a term project.
ATMO 702.prereq_raw: ATMO 600 or OCN 620 ; MATH 407 or MATH 408 ; or consent.

ATMO 704.title: Climate and Climate Variability
ATMO 704.subject: ATMO
ATMO 704.description: Physical basis of climate, numerical climate models, paleoclimatic indicators, modern instrumental climate records, assessment of human impact on climate, predictions of future climate.

ATMO 706.title: Tropical Climate Dynamics and Modeling
ATMO 706.subject: ATMO
ATMO 706.description: Overview of current progress in tropical climate dynamics with a particular focus on large-scale atmosphere-ocean interactions; introduction of basic numerical techniques for students to construct and run immediate tropical atmosphere and ocean models.

ATMO 708.title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
ATMO 708.subject: ATMO
ATMO 708.description: Theory, observations, large-scale analyses, and global model simulations that describe characteristic largescale circulation of the Earth’s atmosphere. Includes zonally averaged climatology, asymmetric features of the general circulation, and El Nino-Southern Oscillation phenomenon.

ATMO 752.title: Special Topics in Meteorology
ATMO 752.subject: ATMO
ATMO 752.description: Concentrated studies on selected atmospheric problems.

ATMO 765.title: Seminar in Meteorology
ATMO 765.subject: ATMO
ATMO 765.description: Participation in departmental seminars and presentation of a seminar on research results. Includes written critiques of departmental seminars.

BE 110.title: Introduction to Sustainable Engineering
BE 110.subject: BE
BE 110.description: Sustainability and its social and technical significance; global population growth; resource management and quantification; designs for sustainable society; challenges interfacing technology and culture/religion; green and ecological engineering; life cycle analyses; engineering ethics; selected case studies.

BE 120.title: Introduction to Quantitative Biology
BE 120.subject: BE
BE 120.description: Quantitative approach to applied topics in biology including synthesis and metabolism, kinetics, physiological systems, cellular processes and signaling, informatics, and emerging technologies for health, biological production/processing, and discovery.
BE 120.prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) and CHEM 162 (or concurrent), or consent.

BE 150.title: Introduction to Biological Engineering
BE 150.subject: BE
