BE 150.description: Discussion and experimental investigation of physical and chemical principles underlying representative biological processes and systems. Bioproduction, energy conversion processes, physiological systems, biological treatment, biosensors, biomechanics, and related natural and engineered systems.

BE 191.title: Introduction to Applications in Biological Engineering
BE 191.subject: BE
BE 191.description: Discussion and investigation of special topics, problems and applications of biological engineering.

BE 260.title: Mass and Energy Balances
BE 260.subject: BE
BE 260.description: Introduction of the principles of mass and energy conservation; development of systematic approaches to apply these principles in calculations for design and analysis of biochemical, chemical, and physical processes.
BE 260.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 , CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , PHYS 170 , and MATH 242 or MATH 252A ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

BE 350.title: Dynamic Systems Modeling
BE 350.subject: BE
BE 350.description: Introduction to analytical and numerical solutions for systems of differential equations. Modeling and computer simulation of representative dynamic systems encountered in biological engineering.
BE 350.prereq_raw: ( BE 260 , ECE 110 or ECE 160 , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , CEE 270 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

BE 350L.title: Dynamic Systems Modeling Laboratory
BE 350L.subject: BE
BE 350L.description: Industry field trips and lab experiences to illustrate behavior of representative dynamic systems in biological engineering. Data acquisition and model validation.

BE 373.title: Transport Phenomena
BE 373.subject: BE
BE 373.description: Fundamental principles and applications relating to mass, momentum, and energy transfers in biosystems and other systems for engineers and scientists.
BE 373.prereq_raw: BE 260 , CEE 270 , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , ME 311 (or concurrent).

BE 405.title: Engineering Economics
BE 405.subject: BE
BE 405.description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.
BE 405.prereq_raw: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or ECON 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing.
BE 405.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CEM, CNST, ECE, and ME majors only.

BE 410.title: Biomass Conversion to Biofuels and Bioenergy
BE 410.subject: BE
BE 410.description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production; fundamental concepts in biofuel/bioenergy production; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel/ bioenergy; biodiesel production; environmental impacts, economics and life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies.
BE 410.prereq_raw: BE 373 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

BE 411.title: Food Engineering
BE 411.subject: BE
BE 411.description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
BE 411.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 , CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

BE 420.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
BE 420.subject: BE
BE 420.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
BE 420.prereq_raw: ( ECE 160 , ECE 211 , and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

BE 431.title: Environmental Biotechnology
BE 431.subject: BE
BE 431.description: Environmental impact and control; the micro-organism and its nutrition and growth conditions; microbial growth and substrate removal kinetics; bioreactors; biological treatment systems; biodegredation of xenobiotic organic chemicals; case studies.

BE 437.title: Biosystems Unit Operations
BE 437.subject: BE
BE 437.description: Introduction to unit operations in biological, environmental, food, and manufacturing processes. Integration of biology and chemistry into engineering using basic concepts in mass and energy conservation and transport in reacting and non-reacting systems.
BE 437.prereq_raw: BE 373 ; and either CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent); or consent.

BE 440.title: Bioremediation: Principles and Practices
BE 440.subject: BE
BE 440.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Soil environment, fate and transport of contaminants; microbial ecology, metabolism, and energy production; biodegradation of selected compounds. In situ treatment, solid-phase bioremediation, slurry-phase bioremediation, and vapor-phase biological treatment. Open to nonmajors.

BE 447.title: Artificial Intelligence for Bioprocesses
BE 447.subject: BE
BE 447.description: Explores how artificial intelligence can be integrated with bioprocess techniques. Using real-world data and hands-on coding, delves into how machine learning can be used to generate practical insights.
BE 447.prereq_raw: ( MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A and ECE 110 or ECE 160 or ICS 111 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

BE 460.title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
BE 460.subject: BE
BE 460.description: Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures.
BE 460.prereq_raw: BE 373 or CEE 320 or ME 322 ; or consent.

BE 470.title: Bioprocess Design and Analysis
BE 470.subject: BE
BE 470.description: Combined lecture/computer lab on theory and practice of bioprocess design and analysis, involving biological basics and engineering principles of bioprocessing, computer-aided unit operations, process integration, and economic evaluation.
BE 470.prereq_raw: BE 373 , or BE 437 (or concurrent) or BE 460 (or concurrent); or consent.

BE 481.title: Senior Engineering Design I
BE 481.subject: BE
BE 481.description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) First course in a two-semester major open-ended design experience for senior students in biological engineering, with heavy emphasis on teaching written/oral engineering communication. Design process; project management; methodology; modeling; optimization; engineering economics.
BE 481.prereq_raw: ( BE 350 / BE 350L , BE 373 , CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent), ME 311 , ECE 211 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

BE 482.title: Senior Engineering Design II
BE 482.subject: BE
BE 482.description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Continuation of BE 481 with emphasis on written/oral communication and engineering ethics. Properties of biological materials; risk and reliability; guest lectures on design by engineers; project completion with submission of a final design report. A-F only. Pre: 481 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.
BE 482.prereq_raw: BE 481 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

BE 491.title: Biological Engineering Topics
BE 491.subject: BE
BE 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

BE 492.title: Internship
BE 492.subject: BE
BE 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

BE 499.title: Directed Research
BE 499.subject: BE
BE 499.description: Research in the area of biosystems engineering.

BE 606.title: Instrumentation and Measurement
BE 606.subject: BE
BE 606.description: Measurement concepts and operating principles applied to the selection and use of instruments important to scientists and engineers dealing with biological systems, including automatic data acquisition and processing.
BE 606.prereq_raw: CHEM 151 , MATH 241 , and ME 311 ; or consent.

BE 610.title: Biofuel and Bioenergy
BE 610.subject: BE
BE 610.description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production, biorefinery concept; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel; biodiesel production; algal-biofuel; environmental impacts, life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies; term paper and presentation.

BE 622.title: Experimental Methods in Cause-Effect Modeling
BE 622.subject: BE
BE 622.description: Factorial designs and fractional factorial designs for screening variable and response optimization. Response surface methodology. Experimental designs appropriate to building and testing multi-variable behavior relationships. Sequential experimental designs.

BE 625.title: Biological Instrumentation
BE 625.subject: BE
BE 625.description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers.

BE 634.title: Biological Treatment
BE 634.subject: BE
BE 634.description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

BE 638.title: Biosystems Modeling
BE 638.subject: BE
BE 638.description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system models, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
BE 638.prereq_raw: one of MATH 215 , MATH 241 , MATH 251A ; or consent.

BE 664.title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
BE 664.subject: BE
BE 664.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

BE 750.title: Seminar
BE 750.subject: BE
BE 750.description: Use of computer and video technology in technical presentation, review of current biosystems engineering research.

BIOC 141.title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
BIOC 141.subject: BIOC
BIOC 141.description: Biological chemistry stressing integration of concepts of general, inorganic, and biochemistry and application to life chemistry.
BIOC 141.prereq_raw: beginning algebra and high school science.

BIOC 341.title: Elements of Biochemistry
BIOC 341.subject: BIOC
BIOC 341.description: Biochemical principles and concepts as applied to living systems, including sufficient organic chemistry to understand these principles.

BIOC 441.title: Basic Biochemistry
BIOC 441.subject: BIOC
BIOC 441.description: Principles of biochemistry, applicable to medicine and real-life situations, involving metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Taught by biomedical researchers. Evaluated based on exams, quizzes, homework, and group presentation.

BIOC 499.title: Directed Research and Reading
BIOC 499.subject: BIOC
BIOC 499.description: Independent research or selected reading of current literature in the area of biochemistry and biophysics.

BIOC 545.title: Topics in Biochemistry
BIOC 545.subject: BIOC
BIOC 545.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students take an in-depth study of selected topics in biochemistry.
BIOC 545.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: fourth-year medical student or consent.

BIOC 595.title: Highlights of Organ-System Biochemistry
BIOC 595.subject: BIOC
BIOC 595.description: Provides highly interactive, small group discussions on concepts of biochemistry important to the various organ systems; such as cardiac, respiratory, hematology, gastrointestinal, endocrine, musculoskeletal and neurological systems, and relevant to clinical medicine.

BIOL 101.title: Biology and Society
BIOL 101.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101.description: Characteristics of science, historical development of scientific concepts, and interaction of society with science illustrated by topics from biological science. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 101L.title: Biology & Society Laboratory
BIOL 101L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawaiʻi. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 104.title: Marine Option Program Seminar
BIOL 104.subject: BIOL
BIOL 104.description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 108.title: Current Topics in Biomedical Research Seminar
BIOL 108.subject: BIOL
BIOL 108.description: Overview of contemporary laboratory- and population-based studies of disease. Discussion of career pathways in human health sciences. Public health and epidemiology of cancer.

BIOL 123.title: Hawaiian Environment Science
BIOL 123.subject: BIOL
BIOL 123.description: Characteristics of science and interaction with society illustrated by topics in geology, astronomy, oceanography, and biology of Hawaiian Islands. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 171.title: Introduction to Biology I
BIOL 171.subject: BIOL
BIOL 171.description: Introductory biology for all life science majors. Cell structure and chemistry; growth, reproduction, genetics, evolution, viruses, bacteria, and simple eukaryotes.
BIOL 171.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, or consent.

BIOL 171L.title: Introduction to Biology I Lab
BIOL 171L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 171L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 171 . A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
BIOL 171L.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, and BIOL 171 (or concurrent) or consent.

BIOL 172.title: Introduction to Biology II
BIOL 172.subject: BIOL
BIOL 172.description: Anatomy, physiology, and systematics of plants and animals; behavior; ecosystems, populations, and communities.
BIOL 172.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, or consent.

BIOL 172L.title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
BIOL 172L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 172L.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, and BIOL 172 (or concurrent) or consent.

BIOL 220.title: Biostatistics
BIOL 220.subject: BIOL
BIOL 220.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
BIOL 220.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or BOT 101 ; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam.

BIOL 265.title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
BIOL 265.subject: BIOL
BIOL 265.description: Principles of ecology and evolution for life science majors stressing integrated approach and recent advance.
BIOL 265.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 , BIOL 172L (or concurrent).

BIOL 265L.title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Lab
BIOL 265L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 265L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 265 . A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
BIOL 265L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 (or concurrent).

BIOL 275.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
BIOL 275.subject: BIOL
BIOL 275.description: Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology.
BIOL 275.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L and CHEM 272 .

BIOL 275L.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Lab
BIOL 275L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 275L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory for Cell and Molecular Biology.
BIOL 275L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 (or concurrent) and CHEM 272 .

BIOL 295.title: Service Learning for Biology Majors
BIOL 295.subject: BIOL
BIOL 295.description: Directed participation on tutorials and related activities in public schools and approved community and UH Mānoa organizations.
BIOL 295.prereq_raw: BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L , BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L , and consent.

BIOL 301.title: Marine Ecology and Evolution
BIOL 301.subject: BIOL
BIOL 301.description: Ecological and evolutionary factors creating and maintaining patterns of biological diversity in major marine ecosystems. Emphasis on the biphasic life histories of many marine organisms. The development of quantitative skills and critical thinking.
BIOL 301.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 , BIOL 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201 ; or consent.

BIOL 301L.title: Marine Ecology and Evolution Lab
BIOL 301L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 301L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 301 . A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
BIOL 301L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 (or concurrent).

BIOL 304.title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
BIOL 304.subject: BIOL
BIOL 304.description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering.
BIOL 304.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

BIOL 305.title: Ecology
BIOL 305.subject: BIOL
BIOL 305.description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

BIOL 306.title: Ethology
BIOL 306.subject: BIOL
BIOL 306.description: Introduction to animal and human ethology and sociobiology; emphasis on social and interspecific behavior, its causes and adaptive significance. Lab optional.
BIOL 306.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 171L and BIOL 172 and BIOL 172L or ANSC 201 ; or consent.

BIOL 306L.title: Ethology Lab
BIOL 306L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 306L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of methods in the study of animal behavior by demonstrations, labs and projects.

BIOL 310.title: Environmental Issues
BIOL 310.subject: BIOL
BIOL 310.description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
BIOL 310.prereq_raw: one of BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 , or GEO 101 ; or consent.

BIOL 325.title: Biology of the Vertebrates
BIOL 325.subject: BIOL
BIOL 325.description: Introduction to the evolution and systematics of vertebrates, with emphasis on comparative morphology, physiology, and ecology.

BIOL 331.title: Marine Mammal Biology
BIOL 331.subject: BIOL
BIOL 331.description: Overview of marine mammal science, significance and roles of marine mammals in their ecosystems, and marine conservation issues. Current research topics in marine mammal science will also be covered.
BIOL 331.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , and BIOL 265 ; or consent.

BIOL 340.title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
BIOL 340.subject: BIOL
BIOL 340.description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society. Not a BIOL major elective.
BIOL 340.prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent.

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

BIOL 345.title: Parasitology
BIOL 345.subject: BIOL
BIOL 345.description: Animal parasites of man, and domestic and wild animals; systematics, comparative morphology, life history, pathology, treatment, control.

BIOL 350.title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
BIOL 350.subject: BIOL
BIOL 350.description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

BIOL 360.title: Island Ecosystems
BIOL 360.subject: BIOL
BIOL 360.description: Characteristics of island biota; examples from Hawaiʻi and the Pacific. Impact of island and continental cultures; policy and ecosystem endangerment; contemporary legislation, policy, and management practices.
BIOL 360.prereq_raw: one semester of biological science or consent. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 363.title: Biological Field Studies
BIOL 363.subject: BIOL
BIOL 363.description: Biological survey, collection, and analysis techniques will be reviewed and applied through field studies. Students will be introduced to the uniqueness of the Hawaiian environment and its diversity of life. Emphasis on diversity, evolution and ecology.
BIOL 363.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L (or equivalent), or consent.

BIOL 375.title: Genetics
BIOL 375.subject: BIOL
BIOL 375.description: Genetic concepts at advanced undergraduate level; genetic transmission, recombination, gene action, mutation, population and evolutionary genetics.

BIOL 375L.title: Genetics Laboratory
BIOL 375L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 375L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments with a variety of organisms to illustrate principles discussed in BIOL 375 .
BIOL 375L.prereq_raw: BIOL 275L / BIOL 275 , BIOL 375 (or concurrent) or consent.

BIOL 390.title: Communicating in Biological Sciences
BIOL 390.subject: BIOL
BIOL 390.description: Combined lecture/lab impart essential knowledge and skills in technical writing, poster design, and oral presentations for effective communication for life science majors. Research papers, lab reports, project proposals, conference presentations are covered.
BIOL 390.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , and ENG 100 .

BIOL 395B.title: Teaching Internship: general
BIOL 395B.subject: BIOL
BIOL 395B.description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication.

BIOL 395C.title: Teaching Internship: oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication
BIOL 395C.subject: BIOL
BIOL 395C.description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication.

BIOL 400.title: Ocean Internships and Research
BIOL 400.subject: BIOL
BIOL 400.description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance.
BIOL 400.prereq_raw: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal.

children.text: in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent , project proposal

BIOL 401.title: Molecular Biotechnology
BIOL 401.subject: BIOL
BIOL 401.description: General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues.
BIOL 401.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 or consent.

BIOL 401L.title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
BIOL 401L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 401L.description: (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 401 . Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
BIOL 401L.prereq_raw: BIOL 275L or BIOL 375L , or MBBE 304 , or MBBE 375 ; or consent.

BIOL 402.title: Principles of Biochemistry
BIOL 402.subject: BIOL
BIOL 402.description: Molecular basis of living processes in bacteria, plants, and animals; emphasis on metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.
BIOL 402.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L , and CHEM 273 ; or consent.

BIOL 403.title: Field Problems in Marine Biology
BIOL 403.subject: BIOL
BIOL 403.description: Integrated program of intensive lectures, laboratory experiments, and field research that focus on the biological processes that shape the lives of marine organisms. Limited space enrollment by consent; GPA considered.
BIOL 403.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 / BIOL 301L and consent.

BIOL 404.title: Advanced Topics in Marine Biology
BIOL 404.subject: BIOL
BIOL 404.description: Current themes in marine biology and experience in scientific assessment. Emphasis on teaching writing and oral communication.
BIOL 404.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 / BIOL 301L or consent.

BIOL 406.title: Biology of Marine Organisms
BIOL 406.subject: BIOL
BIOL 406.description: Biology, physiology, and ecology of marine organisms and marine ecosystems, and the physical and chemical factors, which influence them. Cannot be used to satisfy BS-MB major requirements. Credit granted for only one of ZOOL 200 , BIOL 301 , or BIOL 406. Junior standing or consent.

BIOL 407.title: Molecular Cell Biology I
BIOL 407.subject: BIOL
BIOL 407.description: Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level.
BIOL 407.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and CHEM 273 , or consent.

BIOL 408.title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
BIOL 408.subject: BIOL
BIOL 408.description: Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules.
BIOL 408.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 407 ; or consent.

BIOL 408L.title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Biology Laboratory
BIOL 408L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 408L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) A laboratory to accompany BIOL 407 and BIOL 408 .

BIOL 410.title: Human Role in Environmental Change
BIOL 410.subject: BIOL
BIOL 410.description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
BIOL 410.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 or GEO 101 and either BIOL 310 or GEO 322 ; or consent.

BIOL 411.title: Corals and Coral Reefs
BIOL 411.subject: BIOL
BIOL 411.description: The biogeography, evolution, ecology, and physiology of corals and coral reefs, and the application of this information to the management of coral reefs. Emphasis will be placed on processes such as dispersal, the evolution and operation of mutualisms, calcification, reproduction, and the maintenance of diversity.

BIOL 425.title: Wildlife and Plant Conservation
BIOL 425.subject: BIOL
BIOL 425.description: Principles of conservation biology and wildlife management techniques, illustrated with animal, plant, and ecosystem examples. Examination of ethical, cultural, legal, political, and socio-economic issues impinging on conservation policy and practice. Group project and field trips.
BIOL 425.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L or consent.

BIOL 430.title: The Biology of Fungi
BIOL 430.subject: BIOL
BIOL 430.description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
BIOL 430.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 172 or BOT 201 with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

BIOL 430L.title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
BIOL 430L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 430L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

BIOL 440.title: Psychoactive Drug Plants
BIOL 440.subject: BIOL
BIOL 440.description: Taxonomy, ecology, biochemistry, distribution, cultural history, and contemporary use of mind-altering drug plants; examples from primitive, traditional, and modern societies.
BIOL 440.prereq_raw: junior standing, one semester of biological science, and either ANTH 200 or GEO 151; or consent.

BIOL 454.title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
BIOL 454.subject: BIOL
BIOL 454.description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
BIOL 454.prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level.

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

BIOL 465.title: Fish Diversity
BIOL 465.subject: BIOL
BIOL 465.description: Survey of fish biodiversity focusing on major lineages, their phylogenetic relationships, and their geographic distribution in light of evolutionary history.
BIOL 465.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

BIOL 465L.title: Fish Diversity Laboratory
BIOL 465L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 465L.description: (2 2-hr Lab) Overview of the major orders and families of fishes of the world; introduction to local Hawaiian fishes; coverage of basic fish anatomy; introduction to field and laboratory techniques in fish research.
BIOL 465L.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

BIOL 468.title: The Rise of Fishes: An Evolutionary History
BIOL 468.subject: BIOL
BIOL 468.description: The origins and early evolution of fishes, with a focus on morphological innovations that have led to lineage divergence and adaptive radiation, and the nature of underlying processes associated with novel character trait evolution.

BIOL 470.title: Evolutionary Biology
BIOL 470.subject: BIOL
BIOL 470.description: Process of evolution: genetic basis, natural selection, population genetics, speciation, the fossil record.
BIOL 470.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 , and BIOL 172 or BOT 201 . Recommended: a BIOL, ZOOL, or BOT course at 300 or 400 level.

children.text: Recommended: a BIOL, ZOOL, or BOT course at 300 or 400 level

BIOL 472.title: The Biology of Cancer
BIOL 472.subject: BIOL
BIOL 472.description: Integrative study of the molecular basis of cancer, progression of disease, current treatments, and ethical implications of research. Analysis of published studies through written and small group discussions. Structured training in writing scientific review papers.
BIOL 472.prereq_raw: BIOL 407 (or concurrent) and BIOL 408 (or concurrent) or consent.
BIOL 472.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MCB or BIOL majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

BIOL 472L.title: Cancer Research Laboratory
BIOL 472L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 472L.description: Project-based training in molecular cell biology techniques focused on cancer. Application of scientific method in study design, experimentation, and data analysis. Development of competency reading scientific literature. Strengthening written and oral skills through scientific presentations.

BIOL 480.title: Life in the Soil Environment
BIOL 480.subject: BIOL
BIOL 480.description: An interdisciplinary study of the diverse life in the soil beneath our feet that includes bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, invertebrate, viruses, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
BIOL 480.prereq_raw: BIOL 375 or PEPS 371 / SUST 371 / TPSS 371 , or MICR 351 , or consent.

BIOL 480L.title: Life in the Soil Environment Lab
BIOL 480L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 480L.description: Laboratory to accompany BIOL 480 . Technical examination of bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, and other invertebrate, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
BIOL 480L.prereq_raw: BIOL 171L and BIOL 172L , or MICR 351L , or consent.

BIOL 483.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Topics for Biologists
BIOL 483.subject: BIOL
BIOL 483.description: Focuses on the use of computational tools and approaches to analyze the enormous amount of biological data (DNA, RNA, protein) available today.
BIOL 483.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 (or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C , or consent

BIOL 485.title: Biology of the Invertebrates
BIOL 485.subject: BIOL
BIOL 485.description: Body plans, development, cellular construction, physiological integration, natural history, and ecology of invertebrate animals. Emphasis on marine species, especially local ones.

BIOL 487.title: Biogeography and Evolution
BIOL 487.subject: BIOL
BIOL 487.description: Study of the fundamental role that geography plays in evolution and maintenance of species diversity.
BIOL 487.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and one of BIOL 172 or BOT 101 .

BIOL 490.title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
BIOL 490.subject: BIOL
BIOL 490.description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
BIOL 490.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher and consent.

BIOL 499.title: Biological Directed Research
BIOL 499.subject: BIOL
BIOL 499.description: Development and completion of a research project under the direction of a faculty advisor.
BIOL 499.prereq_raw: 2.5 GPA minimum, written proposal and consent.

BIOL 501B.title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: biotechnology
BIOL 501B.subject: BIOL
BIOL 501B.description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
BIOL 501B.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

BIOL 501C.title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: ecology, evoloution and conservation
BIOL 501C.subject: BIOL
BIOL 501C.description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
BIOL 501C.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

BIOL 501D.title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: marine biology
BIOL 501D.subject: BIOL
BIOL 501D.description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
BIOL 501D.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

BIOL 501F.title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: general biology
BIOL 501F.subject: BIOL
BIOL 501F.description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
BIOL 501F.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

BIOL 601.title: Life Sciences Colloquium
BIOL 601.subject: BIOL
BIOL 601.description: Seminars presented with the School of Life Sciences; topics will vary across the biological sciences.
BIOL 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT, MBIO, MICR, ZOOL majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students only.

BIOL 603.title: Molecular Ecology
BIOL 603.subject: BIOL
BIOL 603.description: Practical introduction to molecular methods used to address ecological and evolutionary questions. Advanced undergraduate/graduate level. Focus on methods and application to independent research project.
BIOL 603.prereq_raw: BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L (or equivalent) or BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L (or equivalent), and BIOL 375 / BIOL 375L , and consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L ( or equivalent), and BIOL 375 / BIOL 375L , and consent

BIOL 650.title: Population Genetics
BIOL 650.subject: BIOL
BIOL 650.description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations.

BIOM 499.title: Directed Research and Reading
BIOM 499.subject: BIOM
BIOM 499.description: To provide elective courses for undergraduates in the biomedical sciences specialties.

BIOM 601.title: Global Health and Medicine: Emerging Problems and Impact
BIOM 601.subject: BIOM
BIOM 601.description: Analysis of emerging problems and impact in countries on a multidimensional perspective.
BIOM 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BIOM, NURS, PH, SPA majors only.

BIOM 615.title: Introduction to Clinical Nutrition
BIOM 615.subject: BIOM
BIOM 615.description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions.
BIOM 615.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or ZOOL 141 or consent.
BIOM 615.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

BIOM 641.title: Legal and Regulatory Issues and Bioethics
BIOM 641.subject: BIOM
BIOM 641.description: Ethical dilemmas in clinical research are identified and resolved in cases, research on human subjects regulation are discussed. Research misconduct is defined. Ethical considerations in protocol developed in the Designing Clinical Research course are resolved.

BIOM 645.title: Clinical Protocol Development
BIOM 645.subject: BIOM
BIOM 645.description: Provides training in proposal development. Governance structures of funding agencies; funding opportunities and decisions; review processes; NIH application and processes; reading RFAs; compliance issues; cultural sensitivity; and types of questions using databases are addressed.

BIOM 648.title: Foundations of Biomedical Ethics
BIOM 648.subject: BIOM
BIOM 648.description: Explores the foundations of biomedical ethics via small group seminars and discussion, presentations. Enrolled in MS or PhD in Biomedical Sciences program only.

BIOM 649.title: Advanced Ethics in Biomedical Research II
BIOM 649.subject: BIOM
BIOM 649.description: Develop biomedical ethics through case studies to incite discussions on topics such as gene therapy, gene enhancement, genetic counseling, informed consent, health care professional/patient and investigator/student participant communication, advanced directives and living wills, clinical research in developing countries, clinical research in ethnic minority and socio-economically disadvantaged populations, and non-discrimination in health care and research settings.

BIOM 650.title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research II
BIOM 650.subject: BIOM
BIOM 650.description: Explore topics in cultural competence in greater depth, encouraging trainees to address issues from a unified yet flexible conceptual framework. Involves building knowledge, skills and action plans to address a range of learning styles and to appreciate and benefit from diversity.

BIOM 651.title: PhD Team Building Seminar
BIOM 651.subject: BIOM
BIOM 651.description: Seminar focuses on teaching participants to work independently and collaborate in order to accomplish specific results. Students will be exposed to group dynamics, communication, healthy competition, conflict resolution, and innovative means of crossing boundaries between departments, organizations, industries and disciplines.

BIOM 660.title: Mentored Research Practicum
BIOM 660.subject: BIOM
BIOM 660.description: Conduct research under the direction of a mentor. Participants will be responsible for submission of a proposal, acquisition of IRB approval, and conduct of the project.

BIOM 667.title: Advanced Biostatistics for Clinical Research
BIOM 667.subject: BIOM
BIOM 667.description: Current methods for analyzing longitudinal and clustered, clinical data through lectures, discussions, and a group analysis. Topic areas include multi-level, multi-state, multi-process, and structural equation models.

BIOM 699.title: Directed Research
BIOM 699.subject: BIOM
BIOM 699.description: Students may register on approval of department.

BIOM 701.title: Disasters and Pandemics: Medical and PH Management and Risk Communication
BIOM 701.subject: BIOM
BIOM 701.description: Assess impact on health in disasters and diseases. Enhances research skills related to management and communication.
BIOM 701.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BIOM, PH, NURS, and SPA majors only.

BLAW 200.title: Legal Environment of Business
BLAW 200.subject: BLAW
BLAW 200.description: Introduction to the legal environment of business operations with particular attention to business law and ethics and to principles of law relating to contracts, agency, partnerships, and corporations.

BLAW 311.title: Business Enterprise and Government
BLAW 311.subject: BLAW
BLAW 311.description: Critical study of the legal environment of business administration including competition, monopolies, mergers, securities, taxation, and regulatory agencies.

BLAW 360.title: International Business Law
BLAW 360.subject: BLAW
BLAW 360.description: Overview of international and national law as it applies to international trade. Readings and case studies focus on the legal environment of selected areas in the Asia Pacific region and strategies for doing business overseas.

BLAW 604.title: Social and Legal Aspects of Management
BLAW 604.subject: BLAW
BLAW 604.description: Study of the legal environment of management with particular attention to the sources, principles, and form of the law; contracts, business organizational structures, agency, and partnership.

BOT 100.title: Freshman Seminar
BOT 100.subject: BOT
BOT 100.description: Discussion of hot topics in botany, including conservation of rare plants, invasive species, marine botany, ethnobotany, poisonous plants, evolution in action, fungal networks, and careers in botany with emphasis on Hawaiian examples. Students should enroll in BOT 100 and BOT 101 / BOT 101L , or BOT 100 and BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L .

BOT 101.title: General Botany
BOT 101.subject: BOT
BOT 101.description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

BOT 101A.title: General Botany
BOT 101A.subject: BOT
BOT 101A.description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

BOT 101L.title: General Botany Lab
BOT 101L.subject: BOT
BOT 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab observations and experiments illustrating basic principles of plant biology.

BOT 107.title: Plants, People, and Culture
BOT 107.subject: BOT
BOT 107.description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

BOT 107A.title: Plants, People, and Culture
BOT 107A.subject: BOT
BOT 107A.description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

BOT 130.title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance
BOT 130.subject: BOT
BOT 130.description: Introduction to the native flora of Hawaiʻi, its origin, evolution and ecology, and the observation, identification, and systematics of the Hawaiian flora.

BOT 130L.title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance Lab
BOT 130L.subject: BOT
BOT 130L.description: The exploration of concepts and the process of science through hands-on experience in studying Hawaiian and introduced plants, their ecology, and cultural significance.

BOT 135.title: Magical Mushrooms and Mystical Molds
BOT 135.subject: BOT
BOT 135.description: Impact of fungi in nature and on humankind. Selected historical events in which fungi played a significant role, their activities as decomposers and pathogens, and their uses as sources for mind altering drugs in religious ceremonies and in food and beverage production in various societies.

BOT 160.title: Campus Plants
BOT 160.subject: BOT
BOT 160.description: Nontechnical course emphasizing recognition of the many interesting tropical plants seen on campus; origin, status in Hawaiʻi, and cultural and economic uses of campus plants.

BOT 200.title: Sophomore Seminar
BOT 200.subject: BOT
BOT 200.description: Presentations by faculty highlighting research in tropical ecosystems. Topics include alien species, biodiversity, ecosystem services, ethnobotany, marine ecology, plant-animal interactions, and systematics of Hawaiian species. Assigned reading and writing exercises from papers in current journals.

BOT 201.title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity
BOT 201.subject: BOT
BOT 201.description: Significance of evolutionary trends in the plant world, including reproductive, morphological, and life history adaptations by algae, fungi, and vascular plants.

BOT 201L.title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity Lab
BOT 201L.subject: BOT
BOT 201L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab exercises in the morphology and systematics of land plants, fungi, and algae.

BOT 220.title: Biostatistics
BOT 220.subject: BOT
BOT 220.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
BOT 220.prereq_raw: BOT 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 ; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam.

BOT 300.title: Conservation Ethics
BOT 300.subject: BOT
BOT 300.description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.

BOT 301.title: Plant Conservation Biology
BOT 301.subject: BOT
BOT 301.description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-in-practice in Hawaiʻi and elsewhere.

BOT 301L.title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
BOT 301L.subject: BOT
BOT 301L.description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

BOT 305.title: Ecology
BOT 305.subject: BOT
BOT 305.description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

BOT 310.title: Field Botany
BOT 310.subject: BOT
BOT 310.description: Combined lecture-laboratory with intensive field experience for observational and experimental field work in native/impacted Hawaiian ecosystems. Field experience typically held during spring break. Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine habitats considered.

BOT 350.title: Resource Management and Conservation in Hawaiʻi
BOT 350.subject: BOT
BOT 350.description: Management of native Hawaiian organisms and terrestrial ecosystems with particular attention to strategies, planning, research, and management actions necessary to control alien influences and promote native species.

BOT 357.title: Tropical forest Ecology
BOT 357.subject: BOT
BOT 357.description: Introduction to the ecological processes and principles of tropical ecosystems, and to conservation issues facing tropical forests, with a particular emphasis on the neotropics.
BOT 357.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 , or BOT 101 ; and BIOL 265 .

BOT 400.title: Senior Seminar
BOT 400.subject: BOT
BOT 400.description: Current research themes in botany presented in discussion format; reading current research papers. Oral presentations of primary research.
BOT 400.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing and consent.

BOT 420.title: Plant Form and Function
BOT 420.subject: BOT
BOT 420.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lecture/laboratory to examine the anatomy, physiology, morphology, and functional ecology of plants. Labs will develop skills in microscopy, experimental techniques for studying plant physiology, and basic functional ecology.

BOT 430.title: The Biology of Fungi
BOT 430.subject: BOT
BOT 430.description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
BOT 430.prereq_raw: BOT 201 or BIOL 172 with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

BOT 430L.title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
BOT 430L.subject: BOT
BOT 430L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

BOT 442.title: Medical Ethnobotany
BOT 442.subject: BOT
BOT 442.description: Survey and theory of plants used as medicines, cultural perspectives of herbal medicine, and the botanical/chemical basis of allopathic and naturopathic medicine. Lecture/ discussion, term paper or project.

BOT 444.title: Biocultural Ecology and Conservation
BOT 444.subject: BOT
BOT 444.description: Examines some perspectives on ecology within the context of Indigenous and Local Knowledge systems, and some approaches to conservation by Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities.
BOT 444.prereq_raw: BIOL 265 or BIOL 301 or BIOL 305 / BOT 305 or consent.

BOT 446.title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
BOT 446.subject: BOT
BOT 446.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

BOT 456.title: Plant-Animal Interactions
BOT 456.subject: BOT
BOT 456.description: Interdependence of plants and animals, emphasizing the influence of animals on plant fitness and evolution. Topics include pollination, fruit/seed dispersal, herbivory, and ant-plant mutualisms.

BOT 457.title: ʻĀina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
BOT 457.subject: BOT
BOT 457.description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawaiʻi.
BOT 457.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or consent.

BOT 458.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
BOT 458.subject: BOT
BOT 458.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
BOT 458.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

BOT 459.title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
BOT 459.subject: BOT
BOT 459.description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O’ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.
BOT 459.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

BOT 461.title: Systematics of Vascular Plants
BOT 461.subject: BOT
BOT 461.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) “Hands-on” experience with Hawaiʻi’s unique tropical flora; emphasis on recognition and identification of vascular plant families and the principles and methodologies that define them; evolution of biodiversity.

BOT 475.title: Plant Ecology
BOT 475.subject: BOT
BOT 475.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ecological principles and process that determine patterns of plant distribution and abundance. Lectures cover theory and examples from primary literature. Labs cover study design, descriptive and experimental techniques, field skills, and data analysis and interpretation.

BOT 480.title: Algal Diversity and Evolution
BOT 480.subject: BOT
BOT 480.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of algal diversity, structure, and evolution. Identification of common Hawaiian algae. Develops written communication skills with significant attention paid to developing writing skills and emphasis on writing instruction.
BOT 480.prereq_raw: one of BOT 101 , BIOL 172 , MICR 351 , ZOOL 101 ; or consent.

BOT 600.title: Grant Writing and Your Career in Science
BOT 600.subject: BOT
BOT 600.description: Scientific grant writing from inception through management to completion; students will write a DDIG and participate in a panel. Professional skills including “rules,” job applications, interviews, transitioning from graduate student to academic or non-academic job.
BOT 600.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: current standing as a graduate student, or consent.

BOT 601.title: Foundations of Current Botany I
BOT 601.subject: BOT
BOT 601.description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in history of science, plant diversity, plant interactions with the environment, and plant integration.
BOT 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in BOT or consent.

BOT 603.title: Darwin’s Origin of Species
BOT 603.subject: BOT
BOT 603.description: Study and discussion of Charles Darwin’s Origin of Species, 1st edition 1859, and related current literature.
BOT 603.prereq_raw: BA or BS in BOT, BIOL, GEOL, or related field; or consent.
BOT 603.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

BOT 610.title: Botanical Seminar
BOT 610.subject: BOT
BOT 610.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in botany.

BOT 612.title: Advanced Botanical Problems
BOT 612.subject: BOT
BOT 612.description: Investigation of any botanical problem; reading and laboratory work.

BOT 644.title: Ethnoecological Methods
BOT 644.subject: BOT
BOT 644.description: Field techniques for assessing the ecological effects of cultural uses of plants. Emphasis on documenting traditional and local patterns of plant use and measuring the effects on plant individuals, populations, communities, and landscapes.
BOT 644.prereq_raw: previous course work in anthropology or biology.

BOT 652.title: Population Biology
BOT 652.subject: BOT
BOT 652.description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology.
BOT 652.prereq_raw: one of BOT 456 , NREM 680 , PEPS 671 , ZOOL 620 , ZOOL 623 ; or consent.

BOT 660.title: Ecological Statistics with R
BOT 660.subject: BOT
BOT 660.description: Learn how to choose appropriate statistical methods to test hypotheses in ecology, evolution, and conservation biology and applications using R as a platform. Lecture/ discussion, term paper.

BOT 661.title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
BOT 661.subject: BOT
BOT 661.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

BOT 662.title: High Throughput Sequencing Approaches to Ecology and Evolution
BOT 662.subject: BOT
BOT 662.description: Fundamentals of experimental design, lab techniques and data analysis to conduct research using high throughput sequencing. Students will work in groups to conduct an amplicon sequencing study with ten samples.

BOT 669.title: Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution
BOT 669.subject: BOT
BOT 669.description: Molecular approaches to evolution, phylogenetics, and systematics. Basic use of chloroplast DNA, mitochondrial DNA, nuclear DNA, and electrophoresis. Phylogenetic analysis using parsimony, distance, and comparative methods.

BOT 670.title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
BOT 670.subject: BOT
BOT 670.description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques.
BOT 670.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only.

BOT 680.title: Marine Macrophytes Seminar
BOT 680.subject: BOT
BOT 680.description: Discussion of current literature in physiological ecology, cellular and molecular adaptations to environmental factors by marine plants.

BOT 682.title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants
BOT 682.subject: BOT
BOT 682.description: Discussion of current studies in morphological, physiological, cellular, and molecular adaptation to marine environments by macroalgae, phytoplankton, and seagrasses.
BOT 682.prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, BOT 480 (or equivalent), or consent.

BUS 345.title: Strategic Management

BUS 475.description: Analysis of business environment and business issues through study of businesses, governmental entities, and nongovernmental organizations in specific geographic areas in non-U.S. settings.

BUS 476.subject: BUS
BUS 476.description: Analysis of business environment and business issues through study and direct observation of businesses, governmental entities, and non-governmental organizations in non-U.S. settings. Involves group travel to selected international business cities. Travel sites will vary.

BUS 477.title: Dynamics of Asian Finance
BUS 477.subject: BUS
BUS 477.description: Analysis of selected key industries of Asian countries: business/ economic trends, shifting product mix, technological changes, joint ventures, international competition, and productivity strategy, including contrasting management styles, worker/management relationships, and decision-making processes under different cultural settings. Industry observations conducted in Asian countries for three weeks during the summer.
BUS 477.prereq_raw: 6 credit hours of economics or business, PAMI participant; or consent.

BUS 601.title: Professional Development
BUS 601.subject: BUS
BUS 601.description: Professional development course designed to focus and improve the career development and leadership skills of MBA students. Students learn from guest speakers through site visits, intensive workshops, and hands-on experience. MBA students only or advisor approval.

BUS 618.title: Sustainable Business Management
BUS 618.subject: BUS
BUS 618.description: Overview of sustainable business management in the firm’s functional areas, including sustainable strategic planning, climate risk assessment, sustainable asset financing, supply chain management, fair trade, and green/ethical consumption behavior management.
BUS 618.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

BUS 619.title: Data Analytics and Statistics for Business
BUS 619.subject: BUS
BUS 619.description: Data analytical and statistical tools for the MBA with emphasis on descriptive and predictive quantitative analytical methods, including time series and regression. Completing an additional six contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. MBA students only or advisor approval.

BUS 620.title: Micro- and Macro-economic Foundations for Managers
BUS 620.subject: BUS
BUS 620.description: Applications of micro- and macro-economic principles to managerial decisions. Microeconomic focuses on economic foundations of business strategies. Macroeconomics focuses on the external economic environment including regulatory and international trends and issues. Admission to MBA program. Complete an additional 3 contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. MBA students only or advisor approval.

BUS 621.title: Business Statistics
BUS 621.subject: BUS
BUS 621.description: Statistical tools for the MBA with emphasis on quality control, time series, and forecasting using regression.

BUS 622.title: Economic Foundations of Strategy
BUS 622.subject: BUS
BUS 622.description: Microeconomic principles that provide structure to solve managerial problems, and to suggest strategies for success. Evaluation of the microeconomic competitive environment in which organizations operate.

BUS 623.title: Marketing Management
BUS 623.subject: BUS
BUS 623.description: Concepts and issues in marketing within the global environment of business. Ethical dimensions and social responsibilities; market research; consumer segmentation and positioning. Strategic marketing planning. MBA students only or advisor approval.

BUS 624.title: Accounting for Decision-making
BUS 624.subject: BUS
BUS 624.description: Accounting tools for business professionals focusing on the role of accounting information in capital markets, managerial decision-making and corporate governance. Completing an additional 12 contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. With instructor approval, the tutorial requirement may be waived if student has successfully completed an accounting course (ex. ACC 200 (with a minimum grade of C-)) or ACC 201 (with a minimum grade of C-) or an approved online tutorial.

BUS 625.title: Digital Transformation with Information Systems and Technology
BUS 625.subject: BUS
BUS 625.description: Practices, techniques, and tools for managing digital innovation in markets, firms, and enterprise systems through information technologies and applications.
BUS 625.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA students only or advisor approval.

BUS 626.title: Leadership and Organizational Behavior
BUS 626.subject: BUS
BUS 626.description: Personal leadership and communications development and the contributions of the behavioral sciences to understanding human behavior in organizations with a focus on leading organizations in times of change. MBA students only or advisor approval.

BUS 627.title: Business, Government, and External Environment
BUS 627.subject: BUS
BUS 627.description: Important issues related to the external environment of business. This includes international trade and finance, regulatory environment, social impacts of business.

BUS 628.title: Ethics
BUS 628.subject: BUS
BUS 628.description: Assists students in developing an awareness of major ethical issues which affect business decisions, and encourages a socially responsible consideration of those issues and being able to express their views.

BUS 629.title: Managerial Finance

BUS 629.prereq_raw: BUS 619 , BUS 620 , and BUS 624 ; or consent.

BUS 630.title: Managing Information Technology for Strategic Advantage

BUS 631.title: Operations and Supply Chain Management

BUS 632.title: Business Policy and Strategy

BUS 791.title: Seminar in International Business

BUS 791.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: student status in PhD in business administration or consent.

CAM 101.title: Introductory Khmer I

CAM 302.title: Advanced Khmer II

CAM 401.title: Fourth-Level Khmer

CAM 402.title: Fourth-Level Khmer

CEE 220.title: Surveying/Geodesy/Geomatics

CEE 220.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, and PREN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

CEE 271.title: Applied Mechanics II
CEE 271.subject: CEE
CEE 271.description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
CEE 271.prereq_raw: C or better in CEE 270 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).
CEE 271.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only.

CEE 305.title: Applied Probability and Statistics
CEE 305.subject: CEE
CEE 305.description: Description of sample data; correlation and regression; probability and statistical distributions; estimations of population parameters; fitting distributions to histograms; hypothesis testing.

CEE 320.title: Fluid Mechanics Fundamentals
CEE 320.subject: CEE
CEE 320.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Compressible and incompressible fluid properties; fluid statics; kinematics, energy and momentum considerations in steady flows; application of steady flow concepts to various fluid processes; with an emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

CEE 330.title: Environmental Engineering
CEE 330.subject: CEE
CEE 330.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Parameters and indices of environmental quality; materials balances; chemical kinetics; ideal reactor models; water and air pollution control; solid and hazardous waste management; emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

CEE 355.title: Geotechnical Engineering I
CEE 355.subject: CEE
CEE 355.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to geotechnical engineering: soil characterization, index properties, seepage and flow in soil, stresses in soils, compressibility, consolidation, shear strength. Substantial emphasis on writing lab reports.
CEE 355.prereq_raw: CEE 320 and CEE 370 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 361.title: Fundamentals of Transportation
CEE 361.subject: CEE
CEE 361.description: Transportation modes: land, air, water, pipelines. Tourist, urban transportation. Geometric design, human factors, vehicular flow models, capacity analysis. Overview: traffic impact, air quality, parking studies.

CEE 370.title: Mechanics of Solids
CEE 370.subject: CEE
CEE 370.description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, constitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading.
CEE 370.prereq_raw: C or better in all of the following: CEE 270 ; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

CEE 370L.title: Mechanics of Solids Lab
CEE 370L.subject: CEE
CEE 370L.description: Tension, compression, and torsion of bars, and bending of beams. Emphasis on writing lab reports.
CEE 370L.prereq_raw: CEE 370 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of D-).

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of D- )

CEE 370L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE and CNST majors only.

CEE 375.title: Construction Materials
CEE 375.subject: CEE
CEE 375.description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Concrete properties, role of aggregates, concrete mix design, supplementary cementitious materials, chemical admixtures, behavior of concrete, concrete testing, field practices. Emphasis on writing instruction.
CEE 375.prereq_raw: CEE 305 and CEE 370 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 381.title: Structural Analysis
CEE 381.subject: CEE
CEE 381.description: Analysis of statically determinate plane and space trusses and frames; deflections; introduction to matrix methods; computer applications.
CEE 381.prereq_raw: CEE 370 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 405.title: Engineering Economics
CEE 405.subject: CEE
CEE 405.description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.
CEE 405.prereq_raw: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or ECON 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing.
CEE 405.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CEM, CNST, EE, and ME majors only.

CEE 417.title: Computer Methods in Engineering Systems
CEE 417.subject: CEE
CEE 417.description: Numerical solutions of engineering problems using digital computers. Regression analysis; numerical differentiation and integration; solutions of algebraic, transcendental, and differential equations; and analysis of large structural systems.

CEE 421.title: Engineering Hydraulics
CEE 421.subject: CEE
CEE 421.description: Hydraulics of closed conduits and open channels with emphasis on engineering applications. Topics also include pump hydraulics, bridge hydraulics, urban drainage engineering, and flood plain management.
CEE 421.prereq_raw: CEE 320 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 422.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
CEE 422.subject: CEE
CEE 422.description: Introduction to basic concepts of pollutant transport phenomenon through theoretical modeling, lab and field experiments and observations. Specific topics include mass balance, jets and plumes, mixing and transport in rivers, reservoirs, groundwater and estuaries; non point course pollution.
CEE 422.prereq_raw: CEE 320 (with a minimum grade of D-), and MATH 244 or MATH 253A (or equivalent).

CEE 424.title: Applied Hydrology
CEE 424.subject: CEE
CEE 424.description: Surface water hydrology topics include hydrologic cycle, hydrographs, regression methods, urban rain-runoff process, flood frequency analysis, flood routing and hydrology for detention basin design. Groundwater hydrology topics include seawater intrusion, theory of groundwater flow and solutions to steady and unsteady aquifer flows.
CEE 424.prereq_raw: CEE 305 and CEE 320 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 431.title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
CEE 431.subject: CEE
CEE 431.description: Hydrologic fundamentals of water demand and supply; water and wastewater distribution; collection systems; quality characterization; analytical methods for water quality management.

CEE 440.title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
CEE 440.subject: CEE
CEE 440.description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation. Senior standing or higher.

CEE 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
CEE 441.subject: CEE
CEE 441.description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. Junior standing or higher.

CEE 449.title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
CEE 449.subject: CEE
CEE 449.description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results.

CEE 455.title: Geotechnical Engineering II
CEE 455.subject: CEE
CEE 455.description: Continuation of CEE 355 field exploration, lateral earth pressures, bearing capacity theory, slope stability, use of geosynthetics.

CEE 461.title: Pavement Engineering
CEE 461.subject: CEE
CEE 461.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design principles of flexible and rigid pavements; HMA mixture design, equipment and construction; and application of life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) in pavement engineering. Includes laboratory sessions for aggregate testing and Superpave mix design.
CEE 461.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of D-), CEE 375 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of D-), and CEE 361 (with a minimum grade of C or better).

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of D- ) , CEE 375 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of D- ) , and CEE 361 ( with a minimum grade of C or better )

CEE 462.title: Traffic Engineering
CEE 462.subject: CEE
CEE 462.description: Design/analysis of signalized, unsignalized intersections, urban networks. Traffic impact studies; analysis steps and applications. Design/redesign options. Parking studies: demand, alternative designs (lot layouts).
CEE 462.prereq_raw: CEE 361 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 464.title: Urban and Regional Transportation Planning
CEE 464.subject: CEE
CEE 464.description: Application of travel demand forecasting models to transportation planning. Evaluation and decision-making. Term projects.
CEE 464.prereq_raw: CEE 361 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 471.title: Construction Methods
CEE 471.subject: CEE
CEE 471.description: Methods of construction, primarily buildings. Construction types: light and heavy wood; steel; plain, reinforced, and prestressed concrete; masonry. Foundations; associated details of frames, walls, roofs, floors, openings, finishes. Disasters, failures, and their causes. Industrialization of the building process.
CEE 471.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CEM, CNST, EE, ME majors only.

CEE 472.title: Construction Project Management
CEE 472.subject: CEE
CEE 472.description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.
CEE 472.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CEM, CNST, EE, and ME majors only.

CEE 473.title: Construction Equipment and Methods
CEE 473.subject: CEE
CEE 473.description: Methods and equipment used on horizontal/ heavy engineering projects. Available equipment, their production, and how they are used to excavate, move, process, and place the earth.

CEE 474.title: Construction Estimating and Bidding
CEE 474.subject: CEE
CEE 474.description: Estimating science; techniques of estimating quantities and pricing of work for construction contracting; classification of costs, analysis of plans and specifications for estimating; computerized estimating; cash flow, bidding strategy, preparation and submission.
CEE 474.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, EE, ME, OE majors only.

CEE 476.title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
CEE 476.subject: CEE
CEE 476.description: To teach the theory and the practice of planning, scheduling, and reporting a construction project through the use of bar chart and CPM. Format to include lectures, text, outside speakers, site visits, discussions, case study, and computers.

CEE 478.title: Construction Safety
CEE 478.subject: CEE
CEE 478.description: Safety and health concepts, laws and requirements for civilian and contractor personnel in construction, including applications in project management and construction activities.
CEE 478.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CNST, CE majors only.

CEE 479.title: Construction Law
CEE 479.subject: CEE
CEE 479.description: In-depth exploration of the legal regimes governing construction. Construction contracts, contractors, and subcontractors. Breach of contracts, claims and litigation in construction projects.
CEE 479.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

CEE 481.title: Undergraduate Structural Research
CEE 481.subject: CEE
CEE 481.description: Individual research project for undergraduate students in the structures track. Topic to be determined by consultation with structural faculty advisor.
CEE 481.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

CEE 484.title: Structural Loads
CEE 484.subject: CEE
CEE 484.description: Introduction to the minimum load requirements for buildings and other structures used in current structural design codes. Derive and apply dead, live, rain, soil, snow, wind, earthquake, flood, inundation, and other loads to structural systems.
CEE 484.prereq_raw: CEE 305 and CEE 381 with a minimum grade of C or better.

CEE 485.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
CEE 485.subject: CEE
CEE 485.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Behavior and design of reinforced concrete beams, one-way slabs and columns. Laboratory section includes design and hands-on manufacturing and testing of reinforced concrete members.

CEE 486.title: Structural Steel Design
CEE 486.subject: CEE
CEE 486.description: Basic properties of steel; behavior and design of steel beams, columns, and connections; introduction to rigid frames.

CEE 489.title: Senior Design Project & Professional Ethics
CEE 489.subject: CEE
CEE 489.description: Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills are assessed through multiple presentations to an industry. Engineering ethics, ethical decision making and deliberation.
CEE 489.prereq_raw: CEE 220 (with a minimum grade of D-), CEE 250 (with a minimum grade of D-), and CEE 305 (with a minimum grade of C).
CEE 489.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE or CNST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing.

CEE 490.title: Senior Design Project
CEE 490.subject: CEE
CEE 490.description: Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills will be assessed through multiple presentations to an industry panel.
CEE 490.prereq_raw: senior standing in CEE or CNST and CEE 489B.

children.text: in CEE or CNST and CEE 489B

CEE 491.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
CEE 491.subject: CEE
CEE 491.description: Will reflect special interests of visiting and/or permanent faculty.
CEE 491.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing, and consent.

CEE 499.title: Special Problems
CEE 499.subject: CEE
CEE 499.description: Individual investigation in civil and environmental engineering topics as approved by instructor.
CEE 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior standing, and minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum GPA of 3.0 in engineering.

CEE 601.title: Operations Management
CEE 601.subject: CEE
CEE 601.description: Linear programming, simplex method, graphical representation: dual; degeneracy; transportation problem; assignment problems; data envelopment analysis; applications; case studies; managerial reporting; LINDO software.
CEE 601.prereq_raw: CEE 476 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and consent

CEE 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CEE 604.title: Cost Engineering and Quality Control
CEE 604.subject: CEE
CEE 604.description: Study and applications of cost/schedule control systems criteria, earned value analysis, probabilistic cost estimating, construction risk management, construction quality control, and operations research in construction.
CEE 604.prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 472 or CEE 474 , or consent.

CEE 610.title: Machine Learning in Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Science
CEE 610.subject: CEE
CEE 610.description: Statistical machine learning and deep learning methods. Script languages for data-driven model training, validation and test. Analysis with linear algebra and statistics. Applications to engineering and earth science problems.
CEE 610.prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of Python Programming desirable.

CEE 612.title: Risk Analysis and Decision Making
CEE 612.subject: CEE
CEE 612.description: Risk analysis and decision making are fundamental areas of construction and project management. Students will benefit from analyzing risks and learning various decision making techniques for real-time applications.
CEE 612.prereq_raw: CEE 472 (with a minimum grade of B) and CEE 474 (with a minimum grade of B), or consent.

CEE 614.title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
CEE 614.subject: CEE
