CEE 614.description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice-negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR.

CEE 618.title: Parallel Computing for Engineers
CEE 618.subject: CEE
CEE 618.description: Concepts and techniques in high performance parallel computing. Topics include parallel language and algorithms, parallelizing pre-existing serial codes, statistical analysis, and techniques up to increase computational speed and accuracy for problems requiring large memory size.

CEE 620.title: Organizations: Theory and Change
CEE 620.subject: CEE
CEE 620.description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations.
CEE 620.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BE, CEE, ECE, ME majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CEE 621.title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
CEE 621.subject: CEE
CEE 621.description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
CEE 621.prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

CEE 622.title: Fluid Mechanics
CEE 622.subject: CEE
CEE 622.description: Theory of fluid dynamics in differential form, covering equation of motion, vortex generation, flow in rotating frame, potential theory, laminar flow, and introduction to turbulence.

CEE 623.title: Groundwater Modeling
CEE 623.subject: CEE
CEE 623.description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.
CEE 623.prereq_raw: CEE 627 with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

CEE 624.title: Coastal Modeling
CEE 624.subject: CEE
CEE 624.description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

CEE 625.title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
CEE 625.subject: CEE
CEE 625.description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

CEE 626.title: Surface Water Hydrology
CEE 626.subject: CEE
CEE 626.description: Deterministic and probabilistic methods include reliability of empirical distributions, multiple regression analysis, extreme value analysis and domain of attraction. Short-memory models for stochastic simulation of streamflows include autoregressive, Markov chain and moving average models. Time series analysis of hydrologic data is discussed.

CEE 627.title: Groundwater Hydrology
CEE 627.subject: CEE
CEE 627.description: Groundwater occurrence, movement, quality, and resource evaluation, development, and management. Emphasis on saltwater encroachment, well evaluation, aquifer protection, recharge with wastewater, and Hawaiʻi type hydrology.

CEE 633.title: Physical and Chemical Treatment
CEE 633.subject: CEE
CEE 633.description: Introduction to physical and chemical processes for water and wastewater treatment: Review of momentum and mass transfer, chemical reactions, colloidal chemistry, coagulation and flocculation, granular filtration, sedimentation, carbon adsorption, gas transfer, disinfection and oxidation.

CEE 634.title: Biological Treatment
CEE 634.subject: CEE
CEE 634.description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

CEE 635.title: Environmental Chemistry
CEE 635.subject: CEE
CEE 635.description: Basic concepts of chemistry as related to the environment, with more emphasis on water. Topics include chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acid-base, precipitation and dissolution redox reactions, sorption, organic chemicals in the environment.

CEE 636.title: Environmental Microbiology
CEE 636.subject: CEE
CEE 636.description: Combined lecture-discussion on major topics in environmental microbiology, microbial ecology, and a broad understanding of microbial processes in natural and engineered environments.
CEE 636.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in CEE or consent. CEE majors only.

CEE 641.title: Applied Mathematics for Engineers
CEE 641.subject: CEE
CEE 641.description: Application of advanced mathematics to engineering phenomena; linear algebra, Eigen systems; partial differentiation and multiple integrals; vector/tensor analysis; Fourier series/transforms and Laplace transform; ordinary/partial differential equations; probability and statistics.
CEE 641.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, ME, ORE, and ECE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CEE 643.title: Hazardous Waste Remediation
CEE 643.subject: CEE
CEE 643.description: Introduces the national problems dealing with the contamination of groundwater and presents remedial measures. Such measures include pump and treat (PAT) technology, in-situ bioremediation, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, electrokinetics, hydraulic fracturing, reactive walls, and phytoremediation.

CEE 644.title: Water Quality Modeling
CEE 644.subject: CEE
CEE 644.description: Mathematical formulation of pollutant transport and mixing in the water environment. Kinetics formulation and parameter identification, model calibration and verification. Design projects.
CEE 644.prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 422 and CEE 431 , or consent.

CEE 648.title: Membrane Separations
CEE 648.subject: CEE
CEE 648.description: Applications of membrane separations to desalination, power generation, and ultrapure water systems. Discussion of reverse osmosis, osmosis-driven processes, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, electrodialysis and ion exchange technologies. Membrane fouling and concentration polarization from practical/theoretical standpoints.

CEE 650.title: Seepage, Drainage, and Dewatering
CEE 650.subject: CEE
CEE 650.description: Theory of seepage, field and laboratory methods of measurement; graphical and numerical methods; design of drainage structures; construction dewatering.
CEE 650.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

CEE 651.title: Deep Foundations
CEE 651.subject: CEE
CEE 651.description: Analysis and design of deep foundations; driven piles and drilled shafts.
CEE 651.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and CEE 455 (with a minimum grade of D).

CEE 652.title: Numerical Methods in Geotechnical Engineering
CEE 652.subject: CEE
CEE 652.description: Finite element and finite difference formulation and analyses to solve problems in geotechnical engineering. Also covers constitutive modelling.
CEE 652.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of C) and CEE 455 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

CEE 653.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
CEE 653.subject: CEE
CEE 653.description: Soil continuum mechanics principles; elastic, plastic, and Cam clay soil behavior; critical state and strength; interpretation of laboratory test results.
CEE 653.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

CEE 655.title: Slope and Earth Structures
CEE 655.subject: CEE
CEE 655.description: Classification of landslides and triggering mechanisms; field investigation procedures; limit equilibrium slope stability methods; numerical techniques; seepage and dynamic considerations; case studies.
CEE 655.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

CEE 656.title: Marine Geotechnics
CEE 656.subject: CEE
CEE 656.description: Principles of geotechnical engineering applied to marine environments; marine geology; surveying and sampling methods; seabed sediment types, properties, and behavior; coastal and offshore foundations.
CEE 656.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

CEE 658.title: Earth Pressures
CEE 658.subject: CEE
CEE 658.description: Estimation of lateral earth pressures; analysis and design of retaining walls and excavation support systems.
CEE 658.prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and CEE 455 (with a minimum grade of D).

CEE 660.title: Systems Analysis for Engineers
CEE 660.subject: CEE
CEE 660.description: Optimization used in design and management of systems for minimizing resources or optimizing outcomes. Evaluation of alternatives, economic efficiency and effectiveness analysis. Logistics. Open to engineering students. Computer applications and labs.
CEE 660.prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 462 or CEE 464 , or consent.

CEE 661.title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
CEE 661.subject: CEE
CEE 661.description: Definition, technologies and their attributes. Analysis and implementation based on FHWA’s User Services. Automated incident detection algorithms. Machine vision applications to traffic engineering.
CEE 661.prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 462 or CEE 464 , or consent.

CEE 664.title: Advanced Transportation Modeling and Statistics
CEE 664.subject: CEE
CEE 664.description: Demand modeling, discrete choice and activity-based modeling. Demand forecasting by simulation. Transportation surveys and sampling methods. Application of cluster, factor, regression, logistic and ARIMA analyses to transportation.
CEE 664.prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 305 and CEE 464 , or consent.

CEE 665.title: Pavement Design and Rehabilitation
CEE 665.subject: CEE
CEE 665.description: Pavement engineering with emphasis given to understanding fundamental issues such as historical development of pavement design, approaches used for design of new pavements and overlays, understanding of construction issues and their effects on pavement performance, and various design factors: environmental, loading and materials characterization. Introduction of pavement management systems.

CEE 671.title: Continuum Mechanics
CEE 671.subject: CEE
CEE 671.description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics; coordinate transformations; analysis of stress and strain; principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations; constitutive relations; field equations. Problems in elasticity.
CEE 671.prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 370 or ME 371 , or consent.

CEE 672.title: Project Management Systems
CEE 672.subject: CEE
CEE 672.description: Project integration and PMIS; organizational power; conflict, strategic, and life-cycle management in construction management; matrix structure compared to projectized structure; project success; team building; change and culture in construction organizations; competitive bidding.

CEE 673.title: Negotiation
CEE 673.subject: CEE
CEE 673.description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

CEE 674.title: Working with Entrepreneurs and Startups
CEE 674.subject: CEE
CEE 674.description: Project-oriented course in which a team of students will work with a real local startup and entrepreneur to develop a business idea and/or viable business plan.
CEE 674.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CEE 675.title: Structural Dynamics I
CEE 675.subject: CEE
CEE 675.description: Response of single and multi degree-of-freedom systems due to dynamic forces. Direct integration of equations of motion. Response spectrum analysis. Application to earthquake loading. Systems with distributed mass and elasticity.

CEE 676.title: Structural Dynamics II
CEE 676.subject: CEE
CEE 676.description: Elastic and inelastic response of structures due to earthquakes. Seismic design criteria. Code design procedures. Advanced topics in time- and frequency-domain dynamic analysis of structures.

CEE 677.title: Smart Structures Technology
CEE 677.subject: CEE
CEE 677.description: Fundamentals of sensor technologies for structural engineering applications. Control devices and strategies for protection of structures against extreme events, i.e. earthquakes, strong winds, etc. Structural health monitoring and smart sensor networks. Smart materials for civil structures.

CEE 681.title: Modern Structural Analysis
CEE 681.subject: CEE
CEE 681.description: Fundamentals of modern structural analysis theory, with emphasis on frame structures. Virtual work. Member stiffness/flexibility. Matrix formulation of stiffness and flexibility methods. Computer modeling issues.

CEE 683.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Design
CEE 683.subject: CEE
CEE 683.description: Slender columns; biaxial bending; combined shear and torsion. Building lateral load resisting frame analysis and design-shearwalls, rigid frames. Floor system analysis and design-flat slabs, joist systems. Computer applications.

CEE 685.title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
CEE 685.subject: CEE
CEE 685.description: Load and resistance factored design (LRFD); steel building modeling and analysis; moment-resisting frames; bracing systems; beam-columns; moment connections; composite construction; and plate girders.

CEE 686.title: Finite Elements in Structures
CEE 686.subject: CEE
CEE 686.description: Finite element method in structural engineering. Extension of structural theory. Virtual work. One- two-, and three-dimensional elements; axisymmetric elements; plate bending. Application to linear problems.

CEE 687.title: Prestressed Concrete
CEE 687.subject: CEE
CEE 687.description: Behavior of prestressed concrete members, including prestress losses. Analysis and design of prestressed beams, slabs, and composite sections. Anchorage zone design; continuous systems.

CEE 688.title: Advanced Concrete Technology
CEE 688.subject: CEE
CEE 688.description: Composition and hydration of concrete, chemical, and mineral admixtures, fresh and hardened properties, mix proportions, high performance concretes, durability and retrofitting technology, non-destructive testing, and advanced material characterization techniques.
CEE 688.prereq_raw: CEE 375 (with a minimum grade of C).

CEE 691.title: Seminar in Civil and Environmental Engineering
CEE 691.subject: CEE
CEE 691.description: Discussions and reports on literature, research, developments and activities in civil engineering. One unit of all graduate students for each graduate degree. Student presentations are required.
CEE 691.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

CEE 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
CEE 695.subject: CEE
CEE 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
CEE 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CEE or consent.

CEE 696.title: Selected Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
CEE 696.subject: CEE
CEE 696.description: Highly specialized topics in structures, soils, hydraulics, sanitary, water resources, applied mechanics, transportation.

CEE 800.title: Dissertation Research
CEE 800.subject: CEE
CEE 800.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Candidacy for PhD in civil engineering.

CHAM 101.title: Elementary Chamorro
CHAM 101.subject: CHAM
CHAM 101.description: Introduction to Chamorro, emphasis on listening and speaking, language structure. Meets three hours weekly.

CHAM 102.title: Elementary Chamorro
CHAM 102.subject: CHAM
CHAM 102.description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills; emphasis on oral and reading proficiency. Meets five hours weekly.

CHAM 201.title: Intermediate Chamorro
CHAM 201.subject: CHAM
CHAM 201.description: Continuation of CHAM 102 . Emphasis on comprehension and language production (speaking). Meets five hours weekly.

CHAM 202.title: Intermediate Chamorro
CHAM 202.subject: CHAM
CHAM 202.description: Continuation of CHAM 201 . Emphasis on comprehension and language production.

CHEM 100.title: Chemistry and Society
CHEM 100.subject: CHEM
CHEM 100.description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of basic chemistry concepts and their application to everyday life. No credit for science and engineering majors. Students who successfully completed CHEM 110 / SUST 120 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 100 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 110 / SUST 120 without instructor override.

CHEM 100L.title: Chemistry and Society Laboratory
CHEM 100L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 100L.description: Laboratory to accompany CHEM 100 , CHEM 110 , or SUST 120 . Lab introduces fundamental applications of chemistry, with special emphasis on relevant topics and how chemistry relates to the real world. (For students in non-science fields.)
CHEM 100L.prereq_raw: CHEM 100 (or concurrent), CHEM 110 (or concurrent), or SUST 120 (or concurrent).

CHEM 110.title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
CHEM 110.subject: CHEM
CHEM 110.description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. Students who successfully completed CHEM 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 110/ SUST 120 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 110/ SUST 120 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 100 without instructor override.

CHEM 131.title: Preparation for General Chemistry
CHEM 131.subject: CHEM
CHEM 131.description: For students lacking preparation in chemistry. Provides background in algebra and elementary concepts of chemistry in preparation for entering the General Chemistry sequence.

CHEM 151.title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry
CHEM 151.subject: CHEM
CHEM 151.description: Nonrigorous but adequate background in fundamentals. Preparation for technical training in life sciences.

CHEM 151L.title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry Lab
CHEM 151L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 151L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments introducing laboratory techniques and illustrating chemical principles.

CHEM 152.title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry
CHEM 152.subject: CHEM
CHEM 152.description: Structure, nomenclature, properties, reactions of organic compounds emphasizing those of practical importance in related fields.

CHEM 152L.title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry Lab
CHEM 152L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 152L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Techniques of preparation, purification, identification of organic compounds.
CHEM 152L.prereq_raw: CHEM 151L , CHEM 162L , or CHEM 171L ; and CHEM 152 (or concurrent).

CHEM 161.title: General Chemistry I
CHEM 161.subject: CHEM
CHEM 161.description: Basic principles of chemistry, including stoichiometry. Introduction to solution phase chemistry. Gas phase chemistry. Thermodynamics, including enthalpies of formation and reaction. Atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular structure. Students who successfully completed CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 161 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 161 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A without instructor override.
CHEM 161.prereq_raw: C (not C-) in CHEM 131 or C (not C-) in CHEM 151 or successful completion of placement exam, or consent.

CHEM 161L.title: General Chemistry Lab I
CHEM 161L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 161L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 161 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 161 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A without instructor override.

CHEM 162.title: General Chemistry II
CHEM 162.subject: CHEM
CHEM 162.description: Continuation of CHEM 161 . Liquids and solids. Solutions and colligative properties. Continuation of thermodynamics, including entropy and free energy. Principles and applications of chemical equilibrium, including acid-base chemistry (titrations, buffers). Kinetics. Redox reactions and electrochemistry.
CHEM 162.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 161 .

CHEM 162L.title: General Chemistry Lab II
CHEM 162L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 162L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry.
CHEM 162L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 161L and CHEM 162 (or concurrent).

CHEM 171.title: Principles of Chemistry
CHEM 171.subject: CHEM
CHEM 171.description: Principles, theories, elementary analytical methods of chemistry. Intended for physical science majors and engineers. Students who successfully completed CHEM 161 or CHEM 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 161 or CHEM 181A without instructor override.
CHEM 171.prereq_raw: Satisfactory Placement Exam score, and MATH 241 or MATH 242 or MATH 243 or MATH 251A or MATH 252A or MATH 253A .

CHEM 171L.title: Principles of Chemistry Lab
CHEM 171L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 171L.description: (1 3.5- hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed CHEM 161L or CHEM 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 161L or CHEM 181A without instructor override.

CHEM 181A.title: Honors General Chemistry
CHEM 181A.subject: CHEM
CHEM 181A.description: Rigorous, in-depth introduction to chemical principles with emphasis on experimental and applied aspects of modern chemistry. Students who successfully completed CHEM 161 or CHEM 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 181A without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 161 or CHEM 171 without instructor override.
CHEM 181A.prereq_raw: satisfactory placement exam score and MATH 215 (or concurrent) or MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C.

CHEM 181L.title: Honors General Chemistry Laboratory
CHEM 181L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 181L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating chemical principles involving advanced techniques and modern instrumentation. Students who successfully completed CHEM 161L or CHEM 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 181L without instructor override. Students who successfully complete CHEM 181L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in CHEM 161L or CHEM 171L without instructor override.

CHEM 272.title: Organic Chemistry I
CHEM 272.subject: CHEM
CHEM 272.description: Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.
CHEM 272.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A .

CHEM 272L.title: Organic Chemistry I Lab
CHEM 272L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 272L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
CHEM 272L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 162L , CHEM 171L , or CHEM 181L ; and C (not C-) or better in CHEM 272 (or concurrent).

CHEM 273.title: Organic Chemistry II
CHEM 273.subject: CHEM
CHEM 273.description: Continuation of CHEM 272 . Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.
CHEM 273.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 272 .

CHEM 273L.title: Organic Chemistry II Lab
CHEM 273L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 273L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
CHEM 273L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 272L and CHEM 273 (or concurrent).

CHEM 274.title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry
CHEM 274.subject: CHEM
CHEM 274.description: Selected methods and principles, e.g., phase equilibria, ionic equilibria, electrode equilibria, separations, spectroscopy, automation, and process control.
CHEM 274.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A .

CHEM 274L.title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry Lab
CHEM 274L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 274L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Phase separations, chromatography, titrimetry, spectrophotometry, etc.
CHEM 274L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in CHEM 162L or CHEM 171L or CHEM 181L ; and CHEM 274 (or concurrent).

CHEM 351.title: Physical Chemistry I
CHEM 351.subject: CHEM
CHEM 351.prereq_raw: CHEM 274 , CHEM 274L , PHYS 272 , PHYS 272L , and MATH 243 or MATH 253A .

CHEM 352L.title: Physico-Chemical Measurements
CHEM 352L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 352L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory on instrumentation, measurements, and data analysis in thermodynamics, spectroscopy, and other areas of physical chemistry. Emphasis on instruction in scientific reporting writing.

CHEM 372.title: Bioorganic Chemistry
CHEM 372.subject: CHEM
CHEM 372.description: Mechanism of biochemical reactions, biophysical structure, techniques for studying biochemical reactions.
CHEM 372.prereq_raw: CHEM 273 (with a grade of C or better) or graduate standing with consent, or departmental approval.

CHEM 380.title: Professional Ethics for Chemists
CHEM 380.subject: CHEM
CHEM 380.description: Student team-led discussions of contemporary ethical issues and ethical decision making in chemistry using case studies and additional examples from the media.
CHEM 380.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CHEM or BIOC majors only.

CHEM 399.title: Directed Reading
CHEM 399.subject: CHEM
CHEM 399.description: Directed reading and discussion of scientific journal articles culminating in a written literature review.
CHEM 399.prereq_raw: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0.
CHEM 399.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CHEM or BIOC majors only.

CHEM 399L.title: Directed Research
CHEM 399L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 399L.description: Directed laboratory research culminating in a written research report.
CHEM 399L.prereq_raw: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0.
CHEM 399L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CHEM or BIOC majors only.

CHEM 425.title: Synthesis and Analysis of Inorganic Compounds
CHEM 425.subject: CHEM
CHEM 425.description: Lecture on advanced methods of preparation and characterization of inorganic compounds and materials.

CHEM 425L.title: Preparation and Analysis of Inorganic Compounds Laboratory
CHEM 425L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 425L.description: Laboratory on preparative methods and analytical techniques and instruments in inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 435.title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
CHEM 435.subject: CHEM
CHEM 435.description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods-theory and hands-on experience.

CHEM 445.title: Synthesis and Analysis of Organic Compounds
CHEM 445.subject: CHEM
CHEM 445.description: Introduction to multi-step synthesis and instruments/analytical techniques used to characterize organic compounds. Retrosynthesis and diastereoselective reactions; spectroscopy (optical methods, NMR), mass spectrometry. Chromatography (GC, HPLC) and coupled techniques (GCMS, LCMS).
CHEM 445.prereq_raw: CHEM 273 with a grade of C (not C-) or better, or departmental approval.

children.text: ( not C-) or better, or departmental approval

CHEM 445.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CHEM or BIOC majors only.

CHEM 445L.title: Preparation and Analysis of Organic Compounds Laboratory
CHEM 445L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 445L.description: Laboratory on the preparation of organic compounds and physical methods for their characterization. Includes optical methods (UV-vis, IR), chromatography (HPLC, GC), mass spectrometry (GCMS and LCMS) and NMR.
CHEM 445L.prereq_raw: CHEM 273L with a grade of C (not C-) or better, or departmental approval.

children.text: ( not C-) or better, or departmental approval

CHEM 461.title: Physical Biochemistry
CHEM 461.subject: CHEM
CHEM 461.description: Biochemical thermodynamics, chemical and enzyme kinetics, biomolecular structure, and biomolecular spectroscopy.
CHEM 461.prereq_raw: CHEM 162 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 242 or MATH 252A with a grade of C or better for prerequisites.

CHEM 462.title: Advanced Biochemistry
CHEM 462.subject: CHEM
CHEM 462.description: Advanced topics in biochemistry including nucleic acid replication, transcription, and translation; genetic and epigenetic regulation; bioenergetics and control of metabolism; alternative metabolic strategies; and enzyme structure and mechanism.

CHEM 462L.title: Advanced Biochemistry Lab
CHEM 462L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 462L.description: Advanced biochemistry lab techniques: protein purification and characterization, identification of unknown proteins, enzyme kinetics, ligand binding, enzyme kinetics, protein structure, and spectroscopy, with instruction in writing scientific reports.
CHEM 462L.prereq_raw: CHEM 274L , CHEM 372 , CHEM 462 (or concurrent), and BIOL 275L .

CHEM 600.title: Introduction to Research
CHEM 600.subject: CHEM
CHEM 600.description: Introduction to field-specific methods and skills needed for success in graduate research. Includes training modules for safety, ethics, and library resources. Short faculty research overviews may also be given.

CHEM 601.title: Theory of Chemical Bonding
CHEM 601.subject: CHEM
CHEM 601.description: Application of quantum mechanics and symmetry principles to descriptions of chemical bonding.
CHEM 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CHEM.

CHEM 602.title: Chemical Applications of Spectroscopy
CHEM 602.subject: CHEM
CHEM 602.description: Introduction to magnetic resonance, infrared, UV, and visible spectroscopy, emphasizing applications to organic and inorganic chemistry. Three topics each semester-1 credit hour per topic.
CHEM 602.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CHEM.

CHEM 622.title: Organometallics I
CHEM 622.subject: CHEM
CHEM 622.description: Reactivity and reaction mechanisms of compounds containing metal-carbon bonds.

CHEM 623.title: Coordination Chemistry
CHEM 623.subject: CHEM
CHEM 623.description: Survey of Lewis acids and bases, coordination numbers, geometries, stereochemistry, ligand field theory, formation constants, and bioinorganic chemistry.

CHEM 624.title: Organometallics II
CHEM 624.subject: CHEM
CHEM 624.description: Introduction to the principles of catalysis and the classes of catalytic reactions effected by organometallic compounds.
CHEM 624.prereq_raw: CHEM 622 and a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B.

children.text: a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B

CHEM 631.title: Methods of Instrumental Analysis
CHEM 631.subject: CHEM
CHEM 631.description: Theory, instrumentation, applications. Three areas each semester-one credit hour per area.
CHEM 631.prereq_raw: CHEM 333 and graduate standing in CHEM or consent.

CHEM 641.title: Organic Structure Determination
CHEM 641.subject: CHEM
CHEM 641.description: Interpretation of chemical and physical (primarily spectral) data in the identification of organic compounds.
CHEM 641.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

CHEM 642.title: Organic Synthesis I
CHEM 642.subject: CHEM
CHEM 642.description: Modern synthetic methods with emphasis on the design and execution of multi-step sequences.
CHEM 642.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

CHEM 643.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
CHEM 643.subject: CHEM
CHEM 643.description: Theory of molecular structure, stereochemistry, and reaction mechanisms.

CHEM 647.title: Organic Synthesis II
CHEM 647.subject: CHEM
CHEM 647.description: Continuation of CHEM 642 , and is the second half of a two-semester course in Modern Organic Synthesis.
CHEM 647.prereq_raw: CHEM 642 and a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B.

children.text: a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B

CHEM 651.title: Chemical Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
CHEM 651.subject: CHEM
CHEM 651.description: Includes statistical thermodynamics, with application to chemical systems.
CHEM 651.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CHEM.

CHEM 652.title: Chemical Kinetics and Reaction Dynamics
CHEM 652.subject: CHEM
CHEM 652.description: Kinetics and chemical reaction dynamics of elementary reactions relevant to combustion processes, astrochemistry, chemical vapor deposition and planetary sciences.
CHEM 652.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CHEM.

CHEM 653.title: Quantum Chemistry
CHEM 653.subject: CHEM
CHEM 653.description: Rigorous introduction to quantum mechanics, including operator formalism, matrix formation, group theory, and perturbation theory; introduction to the electronic structure of atoms and molecules.
CHEM 653.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CHEM.

CHEM 657.title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
CHEM 657.subject: CHEM
CHEM 657.description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

CHEM 658.title: Crystallography
CHEM 658.subject: CHEM
CHEM 658.description: Crystal symmetry. Elementary x-ray physics. Diffraction theory and its application to crystal and molecular structure determination.

CHEM 661.title: Enzyme Reaction Mechanisms
CHEM 661.subject: CHEM
CHEM 661.description: The chemical mechanisms of reactions catalyzed by enzymes in biochemical pathways, with an emphasis on the major types of cofactor and metal catalyzed reactions.
CHEM 661.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

CHEM 662.title: Computational Modeling in Chemistry
CHEM 662.subject: CHEM
CHEM 662.description: Theory and application of computational modeling in chemistry. Statistical theory behind molecular dynamics simulations, application to modeling chemical systems, computer programming, and analysis of results.
CHEM 662.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CHEM 691D.title: Chemistry Seminar I: physical
CHEM 691D.subject: CHEM
CHEM 691D.description: Current topics in (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 691E.title: Chemistry Seminar I: organic
CHEM 691E.subject: CHEM
CHEM 691E.description: Current topics in (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 691Q.title: Chemistry Seminar I: biochemistry
CHEM 691Q.subject: CHEM
CHEM 691Q.description: Current topics in (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 691Z.title: Chemistry Seminar I: inorganic chemistry
CHEM 691Z.subject: CHEM
CHEM 691Z.description: Current topics in (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 692D.title: Chemistry Seminar II: physical
CHEM 692D.subject: CHEM
CHEM 692D.description: Continuation of CHEM 691D . Current topics in: (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 692E.title: Chemistry Seminar II: organic
CHEM 692E.subject: CHEM
CHEM 692E.description: Continuation of CHEM 691E . Current topics in: (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 692Q.title: Chemistry Seminar II: biochemistry
CHEM 692Q.subject: CHEM
CHEM 692Q.description: Continuation of CHEM 691Q . Current topics in: (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 692Z.title: Chemistry Seminar II: inorganic chemistry
CHEM 692Z.subject: CHEM
CHEM 692Z.description: Continuation of CHEM 691Z . Current topics in: (D) physical; (E) organic; (Q) biochemistry; (Z) inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 700.title: Thesis Research
CHEM 700.subject: CHEM
CHEM 700.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for MS degree and consent of thesis chair.

CHEM 800.title: Dissertation Research
CHEM 800.subject: CHEM
CHEM 800.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD degree and consent of dissertation chair.

CHN 101.title: Elementary Mandarin I
CHN 101.subject: CHN
CHN 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets one hour, four times a week.

CHN 103.title: Accelerated Elementary Mandarin
CHN 103.subject: CHN
CHN 103.description: Content of CHN 101 and CHN 102 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week.

CHN 105.title: Elementary Chinese for Business Professionals
CHN 105.subject: CHN
CHN 105.description: Accelerated, intensive elementary course focusing on everyday listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

CHN 111.title: Elementary Conversational Mandarin I
CHN 111.subject: CHN
CHN 111.description: Development of basic skills (listening, speaking and grammar) of spoken Mandarin with application to some familiar everyday topics.

CHN 201.title: Intermediate Mandarin I
CHN 201.subject: CHN
CHN 201.description: Continuation of CHN 101 and CHN 102 . Meets one hour a day, four times a week.
CHN 201.prereq_raw: CHN 102 or CHN 103 or CHN 105 ; or consent.

CHN 204.title: Accelerated Intermediate Mandarin
CHN 204.subject: CHN
CHN 204.description: Content of CHN 201 and CHN 202 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week.
CHN 204.prereq_raw: placement test and CHN 102 or CHN 103 or CHN 105 ; or consent.

CHN 205.title: Intermediate Chinese for Business Professionals
CHN 205.subject: CHN
CHN 205.description: Accelerated, intensive intermediate course focusing on everyday listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

CHN 211.title: Intermediate Conversational Mandarin I
CHN 211.subject: CHN
CHN 211.description: Further development of listening and speaking skills in Mandarin. The student is expected to be able to comprehend and produce speech at the paragraph level.
CHN 211.prereq_raw: CHN 102 or CHN 103 or CHN 112 , or consent.

CHN 251.title: Reading and Writing Chinese I
CHN 251.subject: CHN
CHN 251.description: For students who have completed the conversational Mandarin courses up through CHN 212 and wish to continue on to CHN 301 , or others who can handle daily conversation in Mandarin but cannot read or write in the language.

CHN 301.title: Third-Level Mandarin I
CHN 301.subject: CHN
CHN 301.description: Vocabulary building and extended mastery of sentence structures of modern Chinese through reading and related conversation. Meets one hour a day, three times a week.
CHN 301.prereq_raw: CHN 202 or CHN 204 or CHN 205 or CHN 252 ; or consent.

CHN 303.title: Accelerated Third-Level Mandarin
CHN 303.subject: CHN
CHN 303.description: Content of CHN 301 and CHN 302 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, three times a week.
CHN 303.prereq_raw: CHN 202 or CHN 204 or CHN 205 or CHN 252 ; or consent.

CHN 305.title: Third-Year Chinese for Business Professionals
CHN 305.subject: CHN
CHN 305.description: Accelerated, intensive advanced course focusing on general advanced listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

CHN 311.title: Mandarin Conversation I
CHN 311.subject: CHN
CHN 311.description: Systematic practice on everyday topics of conversation. Lab work.
CHN 311.prereq_raw: CHN 202 or CHN 204 or CHN 252 ; or consent.

CHN 319.title: Chinese Dialect Studies
CHN 319.subject: CHN
CHN 319.description: Advanced Cantonese or other Chinese dialects.

CHN 331.title: Advanced Chinese Listening and Writing
CHN 331.subject: CHN
CHN 331.description: Web-based training in Chinese listening, reading, and writing to develop skills at the advanced level. Activities combine independent work with communicative activities on the course website. Features language exchange with native speakers.

CHN 332.title: Advanced Chinese Reading and Writing
CHN 332.subject: CHN
CHN 332.description: Web-based training in Chinese reading and writing to develop skills at the advanced level. Activities combine independent work with communicative activities on the course web site. Ideal for in-service professionals seeking language development and maintenance.

CHN 399.title: Directed Third-Level Reading
CHN 399.subject: CHN
CHN 399.description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in their area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses.

CHN 401.title: Fourth-Level Mandarin I
CHN 401.subject: CHN
CHN 401.description: Extensive reading in academic topics. Meets one hour a day, three times a week.
CHN 401.prereq_raw: CHN 302 or CHN 303 or CHN 305 ; or consent.

CHN 404.title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Mandarin
CHN 404.subject: CHN
CHN 404.description: Content of CHN 401 and CHN 402 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, three times a week.
CHN 404.prereq_raw: CHN 302 or CHN 303 or CHN 305 ; or consent.

CHN 405.title: Fourth-Year Chinese for Business Professionals
CHN 405.subject: CHN
CHN 405.description: Accelerated, intensive advanced course focusing on specialized advanced listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

CHN 409.title: High-Advanced Chinese I
CHN 409.subject: CHN
CHN 409.description: Authentic reading, writing, speaking, and listening with Advanced-high and Superior level discourse, content, and genres to build Superior Chinese proficiency and broaden knowledge of Chinese culture. Significant attention paid to developing Chinese writing skills.
CHN 409.prereq_raw: CHN 402 or CHN 404 or CHN 405 , or instructor consent.

CHN 410.title: High-Advanced Chinese II
CHN 410.subject: CHN
CHN 410.description: Aims to build Superior Level Chinese proficiency in reading, speaking, writing, and listening using authentic texts covering Chinese education, and economy, philosophy, while broadening and deepening knowledge of Chinese culture.
CHN 410.prereq_raw: CHN 402 , CHN 404 , CHN 405 , or instructor consent.

CHN 411.title: Advanced Mandarin Conversation I
CHN 411.subject: CHN
CHN 411.description: Systematic practice on academic topics of conversation. Lab work.

CHN 421B.title: Chinese Translation: Chinese-English
CHN 421B.subject: CHN
CHN 421B.description: Training in techniques; theory of translation. (B) Chinese-English; (C) English-Chinese.

CHN 421C.title: Chinese Translation: English-Chinese
CHN 421C.subject: CHN
CHN 421C.description: Training in techniques; theory of translation. (B) Chinese-English; (C) English-Chinese.

CHN 422.title: Media Analysis in Chinese
CHN 422.subject: CHN
CHN 422.description: Use authentic materials, including texts, videos, and postings from social media with Advanced and Superior level discourse and content to build Superior Chinese proficiency and social media literacy, and understand society and contemporary issues.
CHN 422.prereq_raw: CHN 402 , or CHN 404 , or CHN 405 , or instructor consent.

CHN 441.title: Fourth Year Reading and Writing: Advanced Topics
CHN 441.subject: CHN
CHN 441.description: Asynchronous web-based course with focuses on (i) reading selected texts across a broad range of genres, and (ii) writing expository and argumentative essays by referencing and reflecting on the readings, along with interacting with peers.
CHN 441.prereq_raw: CHN 401 (or concurrent) or equivalent or consent.

CHN 442.title: Fourth Year Reading and Writing: Contemporary Social Issues
CHN 442.subject: CHN
CHN 442.description: Asynchronous web-based course with focuses on (i) authentic texts covering a variety of contemporary social issues, and (ii) writing expository/argumentative essays by referencing and reflecting on the readings, along with interacting with peers.

CHN 451.title: Chinese Language and Linguistics
CHN 451.subject: CHN
CHN 451.description: Covers major areas of linguistic description as applied to Chinese language, with significant attention paid to developing writing skills on demonstrating knowledge of the basics of Chinese linguistic features and analyzing Chinese language phenomena.
CHN 451.prereq_raw: CHN 202 , CHN 204 , or CHN 205 ; or consent.

CHN 452.title: Structure of Chinese
CHN 452.subject: CHN
CHN 452.description: Introduction to syntax and semantics of Mandarin Chinese; some discussion of usage and linguistic geography.

CHN 455.title: Chinese Pragmatics and Discourse
CHN 455.subject: CHN
CHN 455.description: Introduction to pragmatics and discourse analysis of Mandarin Chinese; some discussion of usage and linguistic geography.

CHN 456.title: Chinese Semantics and Communication
CHN 456.subject: CHN
CHN 456.description: Study of the meaning of Chinese sentences in isolation, in discourse contexts, and in written texts. Pays equal attention to theoretical issues and practical problems in Chinese semantics and communication.

CHN 457.title: Chinese Words and the Lexicon
CHN 457.subject: CHN
CHN 457.description: Defines properties of the Chinese lexicon, introduces its principles, approaches, and methodologies in Chinese lexicology, outlines similarities and differences between the Chinese and English lexicons, and advances students’ Chinese language proficiency.

CHN 461.title: Introduction to Classical Chinese
CHN 461.subject: CHN
CHN 461.description: Analysis of basic structural patterns through selected readings in various texts.

CHN 470.title: Language and Culture of China
CHN 470.subject: CHN
CHN 470.description: Extensive exposure-chiefly through tape recordings, classroom conversation, and outside readings-to history, culture, and institutions.

CHN 485.title: Professional Chinese
CHN 485.subject: CHN
CHN 485.description: Focus on academic and professional reading, writing, speaking, and listening in order to train students to the Superior (according to ACTFL standards) level of language proficiency.

CHN 486.title: Academic Chinese
CHN 486.subject: CHN
CHN 486.description: Focus on academic reading, writing, speaking, and listening with emphasis on writing instruction in order to train students to the Superior (according to ACTFL standards) level of language proficiency.

CHN 487B.title: Readings in 20th Century Chinese Literature: short stories
CHN 487B.subject: CHN
CHN 487B.description: Representative works of writers from People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. (B) short stories; (C) poetry and drama; (D) novels and essays.

CHN 487C.title: Readings in 20th Century Chinese Literature: poetry and drama
CHN 487C.subject: CHN
CHN 487C.description: Representative works of writers from People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. (B) short stories; (C) poetry and drama; (D) novels and essays.

CHN 487D.title: Readings in 20th Century Chinese Literature: novels and essays
CHN 487D.subject: CHN
CHN 487D.description: Representative works of writers from People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. (B) short stories; (C) poetry and drama; (D) novels and essays.

CHN 488.title: Flagship Rhetoric and Composition Abroad
CHN 488.subject: CHN
CHN 488.description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of and ability to use Chinese to effectively communicate in writing.

CHN 489.title: Flagship Media and Society Abroad
CHN 489.subject: CHN
CHN 489.description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of Chinese media, how it operates, and its effects on Chinese society.

CHN 490.title: Flagship Experience Abroad
CHN 490.subject: CHN
CHN 490.description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will take two courses taught in Chinese in their field at Nanjing or Beijing Union University.

CHN 491.title: Oral Fluency Through Chinese Films
CHN 491.subject: CHN
CHN 491.description: Increasing Chinese proficiency through film, which offers authentically rich cultural contexts. Focus on oral communication.

CHN 495.title: Internship Program
CHN 495.subject: CHN
CHN 495.description: Faculty supervised participation in the operations of an organization in a position making use of students’ Chinese language skills in Hawaiʻi. Students must achieve a grade of B- in CHN 302 to take this course.
CHN 495.prereq_raw: CHN 302 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent.
CHN 495.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CHN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior/senior standing only.

CHN 496.title: Overseas Internship in China
CHN 496.subject: CHN
CHN 496.description: Supervised internships in a Chinese-speaking institution in China. Students must pass CHN 486 with a B- or higher and be accepted to the Flagship Capstone Year in China to take this.
CHN 496.prereq_raw: CHN 461 and CHN 485 and CHN 486 (with a minimum grade of B- or better) and proficiency assessment and acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China.

children.text: acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China

CHN 499.title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
CHN 499.subject: CHN
CHN 499.description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses.
CHN 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Primarily for graduate students from other departments.

CHN 601.title: Introduction to Study of Contemporary Chinese Linguistics
CHN 601.subject: CHN
CHN 601.description: Panoramic overview of major perspectives in contemporary Chinese linguistics. Readings on recent developments of fields. Report on selected research papers and present analysis of linguistic phenomena of interest.

CHN 610B.title: Chinese Poetry: ancient (to 5th century)
CHN 610B.subject: CHN
CHN 610B.description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th-10th century).
CHN 610B.prereq_raw: CHN 461 or consent for (B), 610B or consent for (C).

CHN 610C.title: Chinese Poetry: medieval (5th-10th century)
CHN 610C.subject: CHN
CHN 610C.description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th-10th century).
CHN 610C.prereq_raw: CHN 461 or consent for (B), CHN 610B or consent for (C).

CHN 612.title: Traditional Chinese Fiction
CHN 612.subject: CHN
CHN 612.description: Formal and thematic analysis of short stories, historical romances, and novels.

CHN 631B.title: History of Chinese Language: phonology
CHN 631B.subject: CHN
CHN 631B.prereq_raw: CHN 451 , LING 421 , or consent for (B); CHN 452 or consent for (C).

CHN 631C.title: History of Chinese Language: syntax
CHN 631C.subject: CHN
CHN 631C.prereq_raw: CHN 451 , LING 421 , or consent for (B); CHN 452 or consent for (C).

CHN 633.title: Chinese Dialects
CHN 633.subject: CHN
CHN 633.description: Synchronic description of a Chinese dialect other than Cantonese and Mandarin; contrastive and comparative studies with Mandarin.

CHN 634.title: Chinese Syntax and Semantics
CHN 634.subject: CHN
CHN 634.description: Verbal categories, aspects, focus devices, resultative and directional compounds, coverbial constructions. Interaction between syntax and semantics.

CHN 642.title: Contrastive Analysis of Mandarin and English
CHN 642.subject: CHN

CHN 643.title: Methods in Teaching Chinese as Second Language
CHN 643.subject: CHN
CHN 643.description: Problems in language learning and teaching. Practice in preparing and presenting lessons with materials based on comparative linguistic analysis. Materials, teaching aids, test construction.

CHN 645.title: Practicum: Teaching Chinese Language
CHN 645.subject: CHN
CHN 645.description: For graduate students pursuing teaching Chinese language. Students gain practical skills and hands-on experiences in creating instructional and assessment materials and teaching an actual Chinese language class using the self-developed materials effectively.

CHN 650B.title: Topics in Chinese Language: teaching and testing
CHN 650B.subject: CHN
CHN 650B.description: Extensive studies of selected topics (B) teaching and testing: specific problems in teaching Chinese including characters and cultural elements; proficiency and communicative ability; (C) cognitive grammar.

CHN 650C.title: Topics in Chinese Language: cognitive grammar
CHN 650C.subject: CHN
CHN 650C.description: Extensive studies of selected topics (B) teaching and testing: specific problems in teaching Chinese including characters and cultural elements; proficiency and communicative ability; (C) cognitive grammar.

CHN 655.title: Current Topics in Chinese Grammar
CHN 655.subject: CHN
CHN 655.description: Current approaches to Chinese grammar and related issues and debates, focusing on the papers published by leading Chinese linguists employing these approaches.
CHN 655.prereq_raw: CHN 452 , CHN 455 , or CHN 456 ; or consent.

CHN 660.title: Second Semester Classical Chinese
CHN 660.subject: CHN
CHN 660.description: Builds on the foundation laid in CHN 461 ; introduces complex syntactic patterns, advanced vocabulary; teaches sophisticated reading strategies and cultural literary contexts; exposes students to a wide range of intermediate level texts.

CHN 750B.title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: teaching methods
CHN 750B.subject: CHN
CHN 750B.description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
CHN 750B.prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

CHN 750C.title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: structure
CHN 750C.subject: CHN
CHN 750C.description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
CHN 750C.prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

CHN 750D.title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: classical grammar
CHN 750D.subject: CHN
CHN 750D.description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
CHN 750D.prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

CHN 750E.title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: sociolinguistics
CHN 750E.subject: CHN
CHN 750E.description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
CHN 750E.prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

CHN 753M.title: Research Seminar in Chinese Literature: modern
CHN 753M.subject: CHN
CHN 753M.description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional.
CHN 753M.prereq_raw: EALL 611 , WGSS 613 , WGSS 615 , or WGSS 650 ; or consent for (M); CHN 612 , or consent for (T).

CHN 753T.title: Research Seminar in Chinese Literature: traditional
CHN 753T.subject: CHN
CHN 753T.description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional.
CHN 753T.prereq_raw: EALL 611 , WGSS 613 , WGSS 615 , or WGSS 650 ; or consent for (M); CHN 612 , or consent for (T).

CINE 210.title: Introduction to Cinematic Digital Production
CINE 210.subject: CINE
CINE 210.description: Introduction to the basic techniques of cinematic digital production and allows students to explore their personal voice in this process.

CINE 215.title: Introduction to 3D Animation
CINE 215.subject: CINE
CINE 215.description: A basic overview of the 3D animation production process, including modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, lighting, and rendering.

CINE 216.title: Introduction to 2D Animation
CINE 216.subject: CINE
CINE 216.description: Introduction to traditional styles and methods of hand drawn 2D, digital, and stop motion animation through theory and practice.

CINE 255.title: Introduction to Cinema and Digital Media
CINE 255.subject: CINE
CINE 255.description: Introduction to the study of cinema: history, aesthetics, and cultural impact.

CINE 310.title: Cinematic Narrative Production
CINE 310.subject: CINE
CINE 310.description: Production-intensive course with collaborative as well as individual projects. Theories and application of basic digital cinema productions, including camera, lighting, sound, and editing.

CINE 312.title: Cinematography
CINE 312.subject: CINE
CINE 312.description: Comprehensive course in visual styles supporting screen narratives through a study of principles of camera elements, operations, lighting, color and composition. Professional role and responsibilities of cinematographer. Project-oriented.

CINE 314.title: Experimental Art and Animation
CINE 314.subject: CINE
CINE 314.description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
CINE 314.prereq_raw: CINE 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or CINE 353 / DNCE 353 / THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE 356 / DNCE 356 / THEA 356 (or concurrent).
CINE 314.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

CINE 315.title: 3D Modeling
CINE 315.subject: CINE
CINE 315.description: Essential principles of 3D modeling in order to create both organic character models and hard surface models. Students will create high-quality, animation-ready 3D models with textures and poses.

CINE 316.title: 3D Animation
CINE 316.subject: CINE
CINE 316.description: Creating the illusion of life through the principles of 3D animation.

CINE 317.title: 3D Lighting, Camera, and Rendering
CINE 317.subject: CINE
CINE 317.description: Students develop the ability to manipulate light, shadow, and color within a virtual 3D space. Rendering and cinematography for 3D animation.

CINE 321.title: Storyboarding and Animatics
CINE 321.subject: CINE
CINE 321.description: Exposes students to the history, application, format, styles, and methods of creating storyboards and animatics. Visual storytelling will be analyzed by examining the foundational components of the visual language of a film.

CINE 322.title: Visual Development for Animation
CINE 322.subject: CINE
CINE 322.description: Visual design and development for animated characters and environments. Students will create concept art, character and prop designs, movement styles, backgrounds, and layouts for animation pre-production.

CINE 323.title: Movement Study for Animation
CINE 323.subject: CINE
CINE 323.description: Creating the illusion of life and expressive movement through the principles of 2D animation: timing, spacing, physics, staging, anatomy, attitude, and acting.

CINE 325.title: Motion Graphics
CINE 325.subject: CINE
CINE 325.description: A project-based introduction to motion graphics using Adobe After Effects.

CINE 330.title: Independent Producing
CINE 330.subject: CINE
CINE 330.description: Fundamentals of producing for independent filmmaking, focusing on business acumen and role of the producer through various stages of production. Topics include proposal writing, script breakdowns, budgeting, scheduling, legal issues, festival strategy, and distribution.
CINE 330.prereq_raw: CINE 255 ; and one of CINE 215 , CINE 216 , or CINE 310 .

CINE 350.title: Screenwriting
CINE 350.subject: CINE
CINE 350.description: Introduction to the basics of writing a short narrative screenplay for film or animation. Students learn the fundamentals and format of screenwriting as well as basic elements of storytelling and character development.

CINE 352.title: Screening Asian Americans
CINE 352.subject: CINE
CINE 352.description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship.
CINE 352.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

CINE 353.title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
CINE 353.subject: CINE
CINE 353.description: Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process.
CINE 353.prereq_raw: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent. (Consent required for production experience option).

children.text: ( Consent required for production experience option)

CINE 355.title: Oral Tradition to Screenplay
CINE 355.subject: CINE
CINE 355.description: Adapting the stories, styles, and cultural values of oral tradition storytelling to cinematic narratives.

CINE 356.title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
CINE 356.subject: CINE
CINE 356.description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices.

CINE 360.title: Indigenous Aesthetics
CINE 360.subject: CINE
CINE 360.description: Aesthetic theories and practices of indigenous cultures of the Pacific and their adaptation to the screen in cinematic storytelling.

CINE 370.title: Directing the Actor on Screen
CINE 370.subject: CINE
CINE 370.description: Introduction of the screen-director to the craft of acting for the camera. Students will develop communication skills and learn practical techniques to elicit spontaneous and relaxed performances with actors from the Theatre program.
CINE 370.prereq_raw: CINE 215 , CINE 216 , or CINE 310 ; and CINE 350 (or concurrent).

CINE 372.title: Editing for Cinema
CINE 372.subject: CINE
CINE 372.description: Advanced course examining the theory, techniques, and practices of motion picture editing; use of non-linear digital editing systems; and practical experience in digital editing projects.

CINE 374.title: Post-Production Sound
CINE 374.subject: CINE
CINE 374.description: Practical course on the theory, art, and techniques of sound recording, editing, and design for cinema. Students work on projects involving dialogue and sound effects in post-production.

CINE 375.title: Directing the Camera for the Screen
CINE 375.subject: CINE
CINE 375.description: Detailed analysis of cinematic grammar, placement, movement, focus, and effects of the camera to create the mise-en-scene. Practical exercises to apply theory to individual creative work and in collaboration with actors from the Theatre program.
CINE 375.prereq_raw: ( CINE 310 , or CINE 215 and CINE 216 ), and CINE 350 , and CINE 370 .

CINE 376.title: Dialogue Replacement and Foley
CINE 376.subject: CINE
CINE 376.description: This project-based, collaboration-oriented course examines the procedures and practices of recording and editing dialogue replacement tracks (ADR or looping) and sound effects tracks (Foley) in film, video, or animation productions.

CINE 377.title: Environmental Filmmaking
CINE 377.subject: CINE
CINE 377.description: Analysis and community co-production of environmental films covering story development and structure, production, post-production, distribution, and outreach.

CINE 380.title: Genre and Narrative Theory in Cinematic Arts
CINE 380.subject: CINE
CINE 380.description: Focus on the concept of genre, genre films, genre film criticism, and popular genres such as the Western, film noir, and Chinese martial arts.

CINE 381.title: Documentary Studies
CINE 381.subject: CINE
CINE 381.description: In-depth study of the nature, history, and impact of documentary filmmaking traditions around the world, focusing on the interplay between filmmaker, subject, and audience.

CINE 382.title: Authors in Cinematic Arts
CINE 382.subject: CINE
CINE 382.description: In-depth study of the auteur theory and specific application to the authors in cinematic arts, such as film directors, animators, or screenwriters.

CINE 384B.title: Study Abroad: Cinematic Studies
CINE 384B.subject: CINE
CINE 384B.description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or cinematic production in the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location. (B) cinematic studies; (C) cinematic practice.

CINE 384C.title: Study Abroad: Cinematic Practice
CINE 384C.subject: CINE
CINE 384C.description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or cinematic production in the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location. (B) cinematic studies; (C) cinematic practice.

CINE 385.title: Topics in Cinematic Arts
CINE 385.subject: CINE
CINE 385.description: Topics of study and critical inquiry in a variety of areas in the cinematic arts. Taught by regular and visiting faculty.

CINE 386.title: Techniques in Cinematic Arts
CINE 386.subject: CINE
CINE 386.description: Specialized techniques in the creation of digital media: taught by regular and visiting faculty.

CINE 390.title: Workshop in Cinematic Arts
CINE 390.subject: CINE
CINE 390.description: Intensive workshop in focused area of cinematic arts production.

CINE 399.title: Independent Group Project
CINE 399.subject: CINE
CINE 399.description: Participation in a group research or creative project under supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of CINE 399/ CINE 499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.
CINE 399.prereq_raw: CINE 350 and consent; and one of the following: CINE 310 , CINE 315 , CINE 316 , CINE 317 , CINE 321 , CINE 322 , CINE 323 , or CINE 330 .

CINE 405.title: Documentary Production
CINE 405.subject: CINE
CINE 405.description: Analysis and practical knowledge of the documentary process including, but not limited to, research, organization and story structure, shooting, camera coverage, and editing.
CINE 405.prereq_raw: CINE 310 , CINE 350 , and one of the following: CINE 312 , CINE 330 , CINE 370 , CINE 372 , or CINE 374 .

CINE 410.title: Advanced Cinematic Production
CINE 410.subject: CINE
CINE 410.description: Production of a major cinematic/digital narrative project. Working in groups, each student takes on creative and technical role and responsibilities of a principal crew position. Emphasis on artistic form in narrative development; timely execution from pre- to post-production.
CINE 410.prereq_raw: CINE 310 , CINE 350 , and one of CINE 312 , CINE 330 , CINE 370 , CINE 372 , or CINE 374 .

CINE 412.title: Advanced Cinematography
CINE 412.subject: CINE
CINE 412.description: Applies the basic foundations, techniques, and theory of cinematography (covered in CINE 312 ) to a more informed and crafted practice with Camera and Lighting Scene study workshops, and research exercises and film projects.

CINE 418.title: Animation Production I
CINE 418.subject: CINE
CINE 418.description: Students work independently to produce a short, animated film. Emphasis on visual storytelling and character animation.
CINE 418.prereq_raw: CINE 317 or ( CINE 321 , CINE 322 , and CINE 323 ); and CINE 350 .

CINE 419.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
CINE 419.subject: CINE
CINE 419.description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.
CINE 419.prereq_raw: any CINE 215 or ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 .

CINE 420.title: Animation Production II
CINE 420.subject: CINE
CINE 420.description: Student teams produce a short, animated film. Prior knowledge of 2D and 3D media authoring tools and animation techniques is necessary.
CINE 420.prereq_raw: CINE 317 or ( CINE 321 , CINE 322 , and CINE 323 ); and CINE 350 .

CINE 450.title: Advanced Screenwriting
CINE 450.subject: CINE
CINE 450.description: Application of narrative principles of character development, story structure, and thematic spine to screenplays for live action and animated short films, television, or transmedia projects. Emphasis on writing instruction.

CINE 455.title: Indigenous Filmmaking
CINE 455.subject: CINE
CINE 455.description: Theories and studies of indigenous films and creation of a cinematic project based in indigenous cultural and value systems.
CINE 455.prereq_raw: CINE 310 , CINE 350 , and one of CINE 312 , CINE 330 , CINE 370 , CINE 372 , CINE 374 .

CINE 460.title: Ethics and Film
CINE 460.subject: CINE
CINE 460.description: Ethical theory and dilemmas as reflected in film and filmmaking. Social responsibility for filmmakers.

CINE 470.title: Directing the Motion Picture
CINE 470.subject: CINE
CINE 470.description: Students direct a narrative live-action short film from pre- through post-production, learning how to develop a directorial vision and how to implement it through storyboarding, scheduling, and collaborative skill sets.

CINE 475.title: Screenwriting Capstone
CINE 475.subject: CINE
CINE 475.description: Culmination of beginning and advanced screenwriting classes. Students will write a treatment and first act for a feature-length project or pilot script and series bible for a television project.

CINE 480.title: Oceanic Media and Culture
CINE 480.subject: CINE
CINE 480.description: Involves close textual analysis of film, TV and multimedia content. The course includes cinematic and television screenings. Junior standing or higher.

CINE 484.title: Data Visualization
CINE 484.subject: CINE
CINE 484.description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher.

CINE 485.title: Seminar in Cinematic Arts
CINE 485.subject: CINE
CINE 485.description: Intellectual issues in cinematic arts. Conducted by regular and visiting faculty with extensive student participation and scholarly presentation.
CINE 485.prereq_raw: CINE 255 and junior standing, or consent.

CINE 486.title: Capstone Cinematic Production
CINE 486.subject: CINE
CINE 486.description: Emphasis on advanced production skills in creating a capstone project in live-action fiction film, animation, documentary, or new media. Screenwriting students may also develop a feature screenplay or television pilot and series bible.
CINE 486.prereq_raw: CINE 405 or CINE 410 or CINE 420 or CINE 455 or CINE 475 .

CINE 487.title: Video Game Design and Development
CINE 487.subject: CINE
CINE 487.description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher.
CINE 487.prereq_raw: any CINE 215 or ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 .

CINE 490.title: Global Media
CINE 490.subject: CINE
CINE 490.description: Close textual analysis and strategic analysis of global media dynamics with an emphasis on transnational media corporations.

CINE 495.title: Cinematic Arts Internship
CINE 495.subject: CINE
CINE 495.description: Internship in professional cinematic, television, animation and/or digital media production company under professional and faculty supervision.
CINE 495.prereq_raw: CINE 350 and consent; and one of the following: CINE 310 , CINE 315 , CINE 316 , CINE 317 , CINE 321 , CINE 322 , CINE 323 , or CINE 330 .

CINE 499.title: Directed Study
CINE 499.subject: CINE
CINE 499.description: Independent research or creative project under the supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of CINE 399 /499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.
CINE 499.prereq_raw: CINE 350 and consent, and one of CINE 310 , CINE 315 , CINE 316 , CINE 317 , CINE 321 , CINE 322 , CINE 323 , CINE 330 .

CIS 701.title: Communication/Information Theories of Society
CIS 701.subject: CIS
CIS 701.description: A critical review of major theoretical and empirical traditions in communication and information sciences. Focus on European, American, Third World, and applied research.

CIS 702.title: Communication/Information Technologies
CIS 702.subject: CIS
CIS 702.description: Technological concepts underlying data communications; information processing and computers; communication channels and networks, information storage and retrieval, and computer hardware and software.

CIS 703.title: Communication/Information Research Methods
CIS 703.subject: CIS
CIS 703.description: Current research methodologies in decision sciences, computer science, library science, and communication. Emphasis on methodologies suitable for interdisciplinary analysis.

CIS 704.title: Special Topics in Communication and Information Sciences
CIS 704.subject: CIS
CIS 704.description: Seminar reflecting research interests of faculty and current interdisciplinary topics in communication and information sciences.
CIS 704.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CIS 705.title: Data Science Foundations
CIS 705.subject: CIS
CIS 705.description: All aspects of data science: the methodology and processes; ethics and regulatory issues; programming tools; data acquisition, cleaning, analysis and mining; visualization, publication, curation, and preservation; applications in various fields.
CIS 705.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CIS 720.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Communication and Information Sciences
CIS 720.subject: CIS
CIS 720.description: Exploration of relationships between disciplines in social sciences, science and technology, and humanities. Faculty and student presentations.

CIS 799.title: Directed Reading and/or Research
CIS 799.subject: CIS
CIS 799.description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses.
CIS 799.prereq_raw: consent. Plan must include goals and rationale.

children.text: Plan must include goals and rationale

CLAS 121.title: Ancient Egypt: Mummies, Pharaohs, and Gods
CLAS 121.subject: CLAS
CLAS 121.description: An overview of ancient Egyptian civilization through lectures and class discussion on Egyptian literature, archaeology, history, religion and society.

CLAS 122.title: Greek, Roman, and Ancient Mythology
CLAS 122.subject: CLAS
CLAS 122.description: Combines readings and analyses of myths from the ancient world including Europe, Asia, Africa, and Hawaiʻi, with an emphasis on comparative analysis of cultures and religions.

CLAS 123.title: Greek and Latin Elements in English
CLAS 123.subject: CLAS
CLAS 123.description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a literary vocabulary.

CLAS 124.title: Greek and Latin Elements in Scientific Terminology
CLAS 124.subject: CLAS
CLAS 124.description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a scientific vocabulary.

CLAS 153.title: Introduction to World Mythology
CLAS 153.subject: CLAS
CLAS 153.description: Reading and analysis of myths and legends from around the globe, from before the dawn of writing to 1500 C.E. Students will learn to interpret traditional stories from several theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

CLAS 211.title: Understanding Ancient Religions
CLAS 211.subject: CLAS
CLAS 211.description: Comparative and historical survey of the religious beliefs and practices in ancient times throughout Egypt, Mesopotamia, Syria-Canaan, Anatolia, Persia, Greece, and Rome.

CLAS 300.title: Myth, Religion, and Society
CLAS 300.subject: CLAS
CLAS 300.description: Survey of major theories and methods for analyzing myth, ritual, and religious practice, drawing on anthropology, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, and sociology. Emphasis on developing core analytical skills.
CLAS 300.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

CLAS 301.title: Biblical Hebrew I
CLAS 301.subject: CLAS
CLAS 301.description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible.
CLAS 301.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

CLAS 302.title: Biblical Hebrew II
CLAS 302.subject: CLAS
CLAS 302.description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; essay-based analysis of literary forms, with attention given both to stories important to the development of the Abrahamic religions and writing-based interpretation of religious traditions.
CLAS 302.prereq_raw: CLAS 301 / REL 301 with C- or better.

CLAS 304.title: Indigenous & Decolonial Approaches to Religion and Culture
CLAS 304.subject: CLAS
CLAS 304.description: Introduction to indigenous and decolonial approaches to the study of religion and culture. Includes a critical assessment of tools and terminology traditionally used in academia. Sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 305.title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics I
CLAS 305.subject: CLAS
CLAS 305.description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts.

CLAS 306.title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics II
CLAS 306.subject: CLAS
CLAS 306.description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts, including Tale of Sinuhe.

CLAS 321.title: History of the Written Word
CLAS 321.subject: CLAS
CLAS 321.description: A hands-on history of writing beginning in Ancient Greece and Rome. Content includes the development of the alphabet, scripts, books, libraries, and writing in ancient culture. Sophomore standing or consent.

CLAS 322.title: Classics Ancient and Modern
CLAS 322.subject: CLAS
CLAS 322.description: Provides an in-depth introduction to a major work of classical literature and its impact on both ancient and modern poetry, prose, art, and intellectual history. Sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 323.title: Greek and Roman Drama
CLAS 323.subject: CLAS
CLAS 323.description: Survey of Greek and Roman drama, both tragedies and comedies, tracing the history of a genre that contains some of the wittiest and most agonizing moments in ancient literature.
CLAS 323.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 324.title: Nature in the Ancient World
CLAS 324.subject: CLAS
CLAS 324.description: Study of the relationship between the Greeks and Romans and the natural environment. Particular attention will be given to the place of nature in ancient science, philosophy, literature, and “real life.” Assignments are essay-based.
CLAS 324.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 325.title: Greek and Roman War Literature
CLAS 325.subject: CLAS
CLAS 325.description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world.
CLAS 325.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.
