CLAS 326.title: The Greek and Roman Novel
CLAS 326.subject: CLAS
CLAS 326.description: Survey of Greek and Roman novels, a collection of highly entertaining texts that offer windows into various aspects of life in the ancient world.
CLAS 326.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 327.title: Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
CLAS 327.subject: CLAS
CLAS 327.description: Major writers: emphasis on Homer, drama, and philosophy. Assignments are essay-based and attention is given to developing academic writing skills.
CLAS 327.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher or consent.

CLAS 328.title: Ancient Roman Literature in Translation
CLAS 328.subject: CLAS
CLAS 328.description: Major writers: emphasis on Vergil, satire, and novel.
CLAS 328.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher or consent.

CLAS 329.title: Greek and Roman Epic
CLAS 329.subject: CLAS
CLAS 329.description: A survey of Greek and Roman epic literature, beginning with Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey and proceeding through the Hellenistic Greek and Roman periods.
CLAS 329.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

CLAS 332.title: Topics in Ancient Greek Thought
CLAS 332.subject: CLAS
CLAS 332.description: Explore ancient Greek philosophy and literature through themes, thinkers, and monumental texts. Course instruction will emphasize the development of writing skills through regular writing, feedback, and such techniques as peer editing and revision.

CLAS 355.title: Archaeology of Ancient Greece
CLAS 355.subject: CLAS
CLAS 355.description: Introduction to the field of Greek archaeology and methods of archaeological research in the Mediterranean.
CLAS 355.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 356.title: Archaeology of Ancient Rome
CLAS 356.subject: CLAS
CLAS 356.description: Examines the archaeology of the Roman world from the Etruscan period to the reign of the emperor Constantine.
CLAS 356.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

CLAS 362.title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
CLAS 362.subject: CLAS
CLAS 362.description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. Junior standing or higher.

CLAS 366.title: Literatures of Ancient India
CLAS 366.subject: CLAS
CLAS 366.description: Survey of South Asia literature from ancient times to the early medieval period; focusing on Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Tamil poetry traditions. Readings in English translation. Emphasis on written communication.

CLAS 373.title: Art of Greece and Rome
CLAS 373.subject: CLAS
CLAS 373.description: Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome.

CLAS 430.title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
CLAS 430.subject: CLAS
CLAS 430.description: Writing and oral presentation-based historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states and the Roman Empire.

CMB 351.title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
CMB 351.subject: CMB
CMB 351.description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society.
CMB 351.prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent. Not a BIOL major elective.

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

CMB 411.title: Human Genetics
CMB 411.subject: CMB
CMB 411.description: Principles of human genetics. Designed for pre-medical or pre-dental students or others who require a course with emphasis on human genetics.

CMB 499.title: Genetical Problems
CMB 499.subject: CMB
CMB 499.description: Directed reading and research in genetics.

CMB 515.title: Unit V Topics in Genetics
CMB 515.subject: CMB
CMB 515.description: First-year elective course in which medical students may take an in-depth study of genetics.
CMB 515.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: first-year medical student or consent.

CMB 526.title: Bioethics
CMB 526.subject: CMB
CMB 526.description: Prepare medical students to identify and resolve ethical dilemmas in medical career and biomedical research, and to maintain integrity and professionalism in accordance with relevant ethical principles, policies, and laws.

CMB 599.title: Research Topics in Cell Molecular Biology
CMB 599.subject: CMB

CMB 601.title: Optical Analysis in Cell and Molecular Biology
CMB 601.subject: CMB
CMB 601.description: Lecture, laboratory, and directed reading course providing the theoretical and practical knowledge to utilize conventional and emerging light microscopy and flow cytometry technologies in the field of biomedical research.
CMB 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Cell and molecular biology students only, or consent.

CMB 604.title: Evolutionary Genetics
CMB 604.subject: CMB
CMB 604.description: Genetic changes involved in the processes of adaptation and in species formation.
CMB 604.prereq_raw: CMB 411 . Recommended: population and/or quantitative genetics.

children.text: Recommended: population and / or quantitative genetics

CMB 606.title: Introduction to Neurosciences
CMB 606.subject: CMB
CMB 606.description: An interdisciplinary overview of the central nervous system, drawn from current knowledge and research on vertebrate and invertebrate neurobiology.

CMB 610.title: Public Health Biology
CMB 610.subject: CMB
CMB 610.description: Writing-intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management.

CMB 611.title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
CMB 611.subject: CMB
CMB 611.description: Presentation and discussion of research topics in biomedical science.
CMB 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

CMB 621.title: Cell Molecular Biology I
CMB 621.subject: CMB
CMB 621.description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
CMB 621.prereq_raw: BIOL 402 or MBBE 402 ; and BIOC 441 , BIOL 408 , and graduate standing; or consent. Recommended: CHEM 351 .

CMB 622.title: Cell Molecular Biology II
CMB 622.subject: CMB
CMB 622.description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
CMB 622.prereq_raw: CMB 621 , BIOC 441 , and BIOL 408 ; and either BIOL 402 or MBBE 402 ; or consent.

CMB 625.title: Advanced Topics in Genetics
CMB 625.subject: CMB
CMB 625.description: Advanced treatment of frontiers in genetics.
CMB 625.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

CMB 626.title: Ethics in Biomedical Research
CMB 626.subject: CMB
CMB 626.description: Topics include responsible data management, recording, reporting, misconduct and scientific fraud, conflicts of interest, critical use of animals and human issues and subjects in research, genetic screening, stem cell and gene therapy and patenting.

CMB 631.title: Research Rotations
CMB 631.subject: CMB
CMB 631.description: Individualized research project in three laboratories of CMB faculty with a written report on each project. Faculty laboratories will be selected by consultation with student’s graduate committee and individual faculty.
CMB 631.prereq_raw: CMB 621 (or concurrent), CMB 622 (or concurrent); or consent.

CMB 640.title: Neuropharmacology
CMB 640.subject: CMB
CMB 640.description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling.
CMB 640.prereq_raw: CMB 606 , or consent from the course director.

CMB 641.title: Introductory Biostatistics for the Bench Biologist
CMB 641.subject: CMB
CMB 641.description: Lecture and example-based introduction to the critical biostatistics skills commonly required of the bench life scientist. Technical literacy and basic practical application are the goals. Problem sets will be scored.

CMB 642.title: Introductory Bioinformatics for the Bench Biologist
CMB 642.subject: CMB
CMB 642.description: Modern biomolecular and genomic concepts are explored through brief guided hands-on web-based bioinformatic projects using public domain resources. Understanding key concepts and algorithms, technical literacy, and operational confidence are goals. Programming skill development is student-optional.

CMB 650.title: Population Genetics
CMB 650.subject: CMB
CMB 650.description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations.

CMB 652.title: Literature Analysis and Scientific Writing
CMB 652.subject: CMB
CMB 652.description: Aims to improve the skills of graduate students in Biomedical Sciences in literature search, analysis, and management, as well as in scientific writing and other forms of scientific communication.
CMB 652.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

CMB 654B.title: Genetics Seminar: molecular genetics
CMB 654B.subject: CMB
CMB 654B.description: Research and topical literature reports in genetics. (B) molecular genetics; (C) molecular biology of cancer; (D) human genetics; (E) cytogenetics; (F) evolutionary genetics; (G) molecular biology of the cell; (H) drosophila genetics; (I) population/statistical genetics; (J) developmental genetics; (K) insect molecular biology; (M) genetics and molecular biology of fungi.
CMB 654B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

CMB 654C.description: Research and topical literature reports in genetics. CMB 654K.description: Research and topical literature reports in genetics. (B) molecular genetics; (C) molecular biology of cancer; (D) human genetics; (E) cytogenetics; (F) evolutionary genetics; (G) molecular biology of the cell; (H) drosophila genetics; (I) population/statistical genetics; (J) developmental genetics; (K) insect molecular biology; (M) genetics and molecular biology of fungi.

CMB 654M.title: Genetics Seminar: genetics and molecular biology of fungi
CMB 654M.subject: CMB
CMB 654M.description: Research and topical literature reports in genetics. (B) molecular genetics; (C) molecular biology of cancer; (D) human genetics; (E) cytogenetics; (F) evolutionary genetics; (G) molecular biology of the cell; (H) drosophila genetics; (I) population/statistical genetics; (J) developmental genetics; (K) insect molecular biology; (M) genetics and molecular biology of fungi.
CMB 654M.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

CMB 669.title: Essentials in Grant Writing
CMB 669.subject: CMB
CMB 669.description: (1 2-hr Lec) Presentation and discussion of hypothesis-driven research and grant writing. May be repeated. Topics include the process of proposal, submission, and review. Course work includes writing, critiquing, and revising a proposal.
CMB 669.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

CMB 671.title: Techniques in Genetics
CMB 671.subject: CMB
CMB 671.description: Laboratory training in procedures used in diagnosis of genetic diseases, cytogenetics, immunogenetics, and dermatoglyphics.
CMB 671.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in genetics or consent.

CMB 695.title: Capstone in Premedical Sciences
CMB 695.subject: CMB
CMB 695.description: Seminar and clinical shadowing for students completing a capstone project for a premedical science certificate.

CMB 699.title: Directed Research
CMB 699.subject: CMB
CMB 699.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

CMB 705.title: Special Topics in Neurosciences
CMB 705.subject: CMB
CMB 705.description: Advanced topics in neuroscience, from basic neurobiology to clinical neurology and psychiatry. Emphasis on current investigations at the cellular or molecular level.

COA 206.title: Introduction to Applied Gerontology: Helping Yourself and Others to Thrive in Later Life
COA 206.subject: COA
COA 206.description: Introduction to essential information on aging and the field of gerontology. Counters ageist stereotypes, develops skills for translating research into practice, and provides an introductory survey course for the undergraduate certificate in aging.

COA 305.title: Ethics, Aging & Society
COA 305.subject: COA
COA 305.description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging.

COA 334.title: Middle Age and Aging
COA 334.subject: COA
COA 334.description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences.

COA 342.title: Adult Development and Aging
COA 342.subject: COA
COA 342.description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death.

COA 353.title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
COA 353.subject: COA
COA 353.description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research.
COA 353.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

COA 394.title: On Death and Dying
COA 394.subject: COA
COA 394.description: Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves.

COA 399.title: Directed Reading and Research for Freshmen and Sophomores
COA 399.subject: COA
COA 399.description: Individual reading or research under supervision of COA-affiliated faculty.
COA 399.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Freshmen and sophomores only.

COA 411.title: Aging and Disability Policy: Intersections in Health
COA 411.subject: COA
COA 411.description: Examines health programs and policies that help kupuna and persons with disabilities stay healthy and independent, including Medicare. Will engage with local community partners for meaningful intergenerational activities and project-based learning.

COA 435.title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
COA 435.subject: COA
COA 435.description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
COA 435.prereq_raw: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200 ; or consent.

COA 449.title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
COA 449.subject: COA
COA 449.description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society. Junior standing or higher.

COA 499.title: Directed Reading and Research for Juniors and Seniors
COA 499.subject: COA
COA 499.description: Individual reading or research under supervision of COA-affiliated faculty.
COA 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Juniors and seniors only.

COM 201.title: Introduction to Communication
COM 201.subject: COM
COM 201.description: An overview of communication emphasizing intercultural, organizational and international communication and media arts with introduction to multimedia, ICTs, and public relations perspectives.

COM 272.title: Introduction to Digital Media for the Social Sciences
COM 272.subject: COM
COM 272.description: Incorporates hands on instruction for creating informational media content, to include learning how to use camera and sound equipment, learning how to edit and create graphics, and learning presentation techniques.
COM 272.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

COM 310.title: Media Arts
COM 310.subject: COM
COM 310.description: Combined lecture-discussion on theories and criticism of visual media, covering aesthetic development and delivery through multimedia and cinematic principles.
COM 310.prereq_raw: COM 201 with a minimum grade of B- (or concurrent) or consent.

COM 320.title: Communication and Communities
COM 320.subject: COM
COM 320.description: Combined lecture-discussion on communication within organizational communities and between organizations and their communities with attention to intercultural issues in local, global, and online interactions.

COM 325.title: Communicating Sustainability
COM 325.subject: COM
COM 325.description: Application of project-based science communication, strategic communication, and digital media techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.

COM 330.title: Information and Communication Technology Concepts
COM 330.subject: COM
COM 330.description: Combined lecture-discussion on basic technical concepts related to ICTs embedded in sociocultural context.

COM 331.title: Techniques of Video and Digital Cinema
COM 331.subject: COM
COM 331.description: Orientation to techniques of production. Emphasis on history, language, and theory of the creative process and application to media productions.

COM 337.title: Media Arts Techniques
COM 337.subject: COM
COM 337.description: Combined lecture-lab providing an orientation to, and examination of, procedures and techniques of media arts production. Emphasis on new media literacy, human-computer interaction, and basic electronic media tools for communication design.

COM 339.title: Public Relations Writing
COM 339.subject: COM
COM 339.description: Enhance students’ professional writing skills in the contemporary public relations field and equip students with the foundations of essential techniques for persuasive communication. COM majors or consent.
COM 339.prereq_raw: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B).

COM 340.title: Intercultural Communication
COM 340.subject: COM
COM 340.description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of intercultural contexts. Focus on theory, research, and managing intercultural effectiveness.

COM 345.title: Information Technology and Health Communication
COM 345.subject: COM
COM 345.description: Combined lecture-discussion on the application of ICTs for health communication from the aspect of technologies, systems, services, and policies.

COM 350.title: Computer-Mediated Communication
COM 350.subject: COM
COM 350.description: Combined lecture-discussion on the evolution of computer-mediated communication from the 1970s to current day. Examines the development of online communities, technologies, and their networked online and offline social practices.

COM 355.title: Digital Cultures
COM 355.subject: COM
COM 355.description: Introduction to the social, cultural, and ethical implications of information and communication technologies by studying new and emerging media including games, interactive media, and virtual worlds. COM majors or consent.

COM 367.title: Digital Media Ethics
COM 367.subject: COM
COM 367.description: Ethical decision-making approaches for contemporary ethical issues related to digital media and communication, including social media and digital marketing, artificial intelligence, digital inclusion, free speech, and indigenous perspectives.

COM 369.title: Esports and Society
COM 369.subject: COM
COM 369.description: Introduction to professional and collegiate esports (electronic sports) in global context, including theories related to leisure and gaming, and current academic and industry developments. No previous technical or gaming experience is required.

COM 380.title: Media Communications and Conflict
COM 380.subject: COM
COM 380.description: Uses an ethical lens to see the role of news media in influencing conflict, and introduces conflict-sensitive communication movements working to resolve conflicts. Writing/discussion used as mediums for reflecting on ethical dilemmas. Sophomore standing or higher.

COM 392.title: Emerging Topics in Communication
COM 392.subject: COM
COM 392.description: Emerging communication topics of interest to faculty and students.

COM 401.title: Survey of Inquiry Methods in Communication
COM 401.subject: COM
COM 401.description: Exploration of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication studies and related professional work.

COM 420.title: Communication in Multicultural Organizations
COM 420.subject: COM
COM 420.description: Cultural diversity in multicultural and multinational organizations is examined regarding communication-related aspects of working life.
COM 420.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 421.title: Public Relations Strategies
COM 421.subject: COM
COM 421.description: Exploring the practice and effects of public relations. Strategic management functions, including the use of communication technologies, communication with diverse publics, ethics and social responsibility will be emphasized.
COM 421.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 422.title: Public Relations Campaigns
COM 422.subject: COM
COM 422.description: Synthesizing and applying the principles and techniques of public relations to create comprehensive campaigns.
COM 422.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only, or consent.

COM 425.title: Filming Social Change
COM 425.subject: COM
COM 425.description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
COM 425.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

COM 428.title: Environmental Storytelling Through an Indigenous Lens
COM 428.subject: COM
COM 428.description: Through media arts storytelling techniques, course will focus on reframing perspectives and creativity from an Indigenous lens to communicate environmental-centric stories geared toward improving our communities’ quality of life.
COM 428.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 431.title: Studio Production
COM 431.subject: COM
COM 431.description: Studio production ranging from three-camera studio production to broadcast and magazine show formats to on-line web production. Fundamental knowledge of lighting, sound, blocking, and equipment competency.

COM 432.title: Social Media
COM 432.subject: COM
COM 432.description: Combined lecture-discussion on the sociocultural, political, psychological, historical and policy dimensions of social media for societies past, contemporary, and future.
COM 432.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 433.title: Video Scriptwriting
COM 433.subject: COM
COM 433.description: Application of communication theory to creating and revising commercial and dramatic script material for video production.

COM 436.title: Media Effects
COM 436.subject: COM
COM 436.description: Social, political, economic, and cultural effects of mediated communication are examined to understand their impact on human behavior.
COM 436.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 438.title: Telecommunication in the Pacific Hemisphere
COM 438.subject: COM
COM 438.description: Development of international telecommunication, with special emphasis on the evolution of wireless communication, the internet, and emerging technologies.
COM 438.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 444.title: Communication and Gender
COM 444.subject: COM
COM 444.description: Theories and issues related to gender and communication applied to organizational, intercultural, and technology mediated communication.
COM 444.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 452.title: Building Communication Theory
COM 452.subject: COM
COM 452.description: Major theories of communication in terms of requirements for a theory, theory development, associated research, and application.
COM 452.prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent.

COM 459.title: Special Topics in Communication
COM 459.subject: COM
COM 459.description: Topics of relevance to the focus areas of Communication in Communities, Media Arts, and ICTs & Policy; taught by regular and visiting faculty.
COM 459.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM majors only or consent.

COM 465.title: Political Communication in the Digital Era
COM 465.subject: COM
COM 465.description: An examination of how various aspects of digital media platforms, such as affordances and communication processes impact political outcomes. COM majors or consent. Sophomore standing or higher.

COM 477.title: Capstone in Media Arts Design and Development
COM 477.subject: COM
COM 477.description: Design, development, and evaluation of computer-based media arts communication. Emphasizes authoring and production of such media elements as video, audio, and graphics.
COM 477.prereq_raw: COM 310 and COM 320 and COM 330 and COM 337 , or consent.

COM 478.title: Capstone in Communication in Communities
COM 478.subject: COM
COM 478.description: Synthesize knowledge, apply research findings in service to community, and develop proposal for intervention or campaign through assignments that emphasize the development of writing skills.
COM 478.prereq_raw: COM 310 and COM 320 and COM 330 ; and COM 340 or COM 421 ; or consent.

COM 479.title: Capstone Project in ICTs and Policy
COM 479.subject: COM
COM 479.description: Written research or media project focused on specific ICT and policy problems, including social media, digital games, and the internet.
COM 479.prereq_raw: COM 310 and COM 320 and COM 330 ; and COM 432 or COM 438 ; or consent.

COM 480.title: Communication Seminar
COM 480.subject: COM
COM 480.description: Application of theoretic and methodological criteria to researchable questions. Topics will vary.
COM 480.prereq_raw: COM 201 and senior standing, or consent.

COM 489.title: Communicating Creativity
COM 489.subject: COM
COM 489.description: The role of communication in fostering or inhibiting creativity. Exploration of theoretical bases for shared scientific or artistic creativity in communication research. COM major or consent.
COM 489.prereq_raw: COM 201 and senior standing, or consent.

COM 490.title: Senior Thesis Project
COM 490.subject: COM
COM 490.description: Completion of the thesis project appropriate to the selected focus area within the context of a seminar. Emphasis on ongoing process of writing, editing, review, and revision.
COM 490.prereq_raw: COM major and senior standing, or consent.

COM 495B.title: Communication Internship: community setting
COM 495B.subject: COM
COM 495B.description: Application of communication skills and knowledge. Under faculty supervision, interns participate in operations of an organization and analyze communication processes and effects; (B) community setting; (C) Communication program activity.

COM 495C.title: Communication Internship: communication program activity
COM 495C.subject: COM
COM 495C.description: Application of communication skills and knowledge. Under faculty supervision, interns participate in operations of an organization and analyze communication processes and effects; (B) community setting; (C) Communication program activity.

COM 499.title: Special Problems
COM 499.subject: COM
COM 499.description: Independent study of selected topics under faculty supervision.
COM 499.prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent.

COM 611.title: Communication Theories
COM 611.subject: COM
COM 611.description: Systematic study of major theories of communication and current status of communication research.

COM 612.title: Communication Inquiry
COM 612.subject: COM
COM 612.description: Introduction to inquiry and the array of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication.

COM 623.title: Strategic Organizational Communication
COM 623.subject: COM
COM 623.description: Theories, concepts, and applications of strategic communication and public relations to achieve organizational goals.

COM 633.title: Information and Communication Technologies
COM 633.subject: COM
COM 633.description: Information and communication technologies, structures, processes, and networks as an area of research and study in the social sciences.

COM 634.title: Social Media
COM 634.subject: COM
COM 634.description: Systematic study from a social science perspective of current and emerging social media. Attention to user needs and impact.

COM 643.title: Intercultural Communication
COM 643.subject: COM
COM 643.description: Problems and opportunities of intercultural communication from theory and research, consulting and training, and policy and program perspectives.

COM 644.title: Global Communication and Journalism
COM 644.subject: COM
COM 644.description: Analysis of the emerging global media landscape as digital technologies enable the sharing of news, information, and commentary across geographical and cultural borders. Focuses on causes, characteristics, and consequences.

COM 645.title: Digital Storytelling
COM 645.subject: COM
COM 645.description: Focus on development of narrative-based creative activities in all mediums (text, audio, video, etc.) within communication contexts, i.e., journalism, film, public relations, etc.

COM 646.title: Intervention in Multicultural Organizations
COM 646.subject: COM
COM 646.description: Describes the array of communication-related intervention programs designed to enhance effectiveness in multicultural organizations at home and abroad.
COM 646.prereq_raw: COM 611 (with B or better or concurrent) or consent.

children.text: ( with B or better or concurrent) or consent

COM 652.title: Media Effects
COM 652.subject: COM
COM 652.description: Critical examination of major media effects theories and topic areas.
COM 652.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM or CIS majors only.

COM 658.title: Public Diplomacy and Communication
COM 658.subject: COM
COM 658.description: Analysis of the emerging trends in international relations from communication and public relations perspectives. Focuses on factors, characteristics, and processes.

COM 660.title: ICT Policy and Planning
COM 660.subject: COM
COM 660.description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

COM 691.title: Communication Topics
COM 691.subject: COM
COM 691.description: Coverage in depth of some area of theory and research.

COM 692.title: Communication Research Seminar
COM 692.subject: COM
COM 692.description: General research seminar in communication. In-depth coverage of specific research methods to develop, refine, or interpret graduate students’ thesis or dissertation projects.
COM 692.prereq_raw: COM 611 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.
COM 692.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COM, CIS majors only.

COM 695.title: Communication Practicum
COM 695.subject: COM
COM 695.description: Supervised work experience, study of an organization, and career planning. Required of Plan B students in the main communication program.

COMG 102.title: Everyday Communication with Numbers: A Survival Guide
COMG 102.subject: COMG
COMG 102.description: Understanding, communicating, and evaluating quantitative information in everyday contexts. Topics include describing and interpreting data, basic statistics, and evaluating the validity of results.

COMG 151.title: Personal and Public Speech
COMG 151.subject: COMG
COMG 151.description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

COMG 151A.title: Personal and Public Speech
COMG 151A.subject: COMG
COMG 151A.description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

COMG 170.title: Introduction to Nonverbal Communication
COMG 170.subject: COMG
COMG 170.description: Beginning course on the fundamental components of nonverbal communication. Aspects of body movements, facial expressions, eye behavior, physical appearance, voice, touch, space, smell, time, and environmental features will be examined in a lecture/discussion format. Extensive practice in skills.

COMG 181.title: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication
COMG 181.subject: COMG
COMG 181.description: Introduction to basic principles of interaction between two people. Emphasis is on enhancement of skills in a variety of interpersonal contexts.

COMG 185.title: Multicultural Communication Skills
COMG 185.subject: COMG
COMG 185.description: Expose students to practical skills needed for effective intercultural communication. Offer guidelines for improvement in diverse cultural settings such as business, education, counseling, and healthcare.

COMG 251.title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
COMG 251.subject: COMG
COMG 251.description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

COMG 251A.title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
COMG 251A.subject: COMG
COMG 251A.description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

COMG 290.title: Interviewing
COMG 290.subject: COMG
COMG 290.description: Principles and practice; training in informational, persuasive, employment, appraisal, and research interviewing.
COMG 290.prereq_raw: one of COMG 151 , COMG 170 , COMG 181 , COMG 185 , COMG 251 or COMG 301 ; or consent.

COMG 301.title: Introduction to Communicological Theories
COMG 301.subject: COMG
COMG 301.description: Introduction to the theoretical perspectives that are the foundations of the communication discipline.

COMG 302.title: Research Methods
COMG 302.subject: COMG
COMG 302.description: Introduction to methods of inquiry in the field of communication. Topics include research design and problem formulation, sampling, analytic and observational techniques, and data interpretation. Ethical issues in communication research will be discussed.

COMG 321.title: Instructional Communication
COMG 321.subject: COMG
COMG 321.description: Analysis of and practice in using models of communication in the classroom. Extends application of oral communication skills to various instructional and teaching contexts. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

COMG 351.title: Professional Presentations
COMG 351.subject: COMG
COMG 351.description: Extends application of public speaking skills to professional contexts: group sales, press conferences, and corporate annual reports. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

COMG 352.title: Group Decision-Making and Leadership
COMG 352.subject: COMG
COMG 352.description: Study of decision-making within the small group. Effects of organization, leadership, membership, and goals on achieving group purposes.

COMG 353.title: Argumentation and Debate
COMG 353.subject: COMG
COMG 353.description: Adapting communication theory to forensic strategies for social action. Practice in formal argument.

COMG 361.title: Leadership and Organizational Communication
COMG 361.subject: COMG
COMG 361.description: Principles and practices of organizational communication and its relationship to networks, leadership, power, conflict, cultures, and other contemporary views of organizational work, change, and development.

COMG 364.title: Persuasion
COMG 364.subject: COMG
COMG 364.description: Theories, concepts, strategies, and processes of persuasion and social influence in contemporary society. Focus on analyzing, developing, and resisting persuasive messages.

COMG 371.title: Creating Understanding
COMG 371.subject: COMG
COMG 371.description: Introduction to theory and research on human communication, comprehension, creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories. Topics include prediction, inference-making, communication systems, and deception.

COMG 380.title: Family Communication
COMG 380.subject: COMG
COMG 380.description: Focuses on the role of interaction patterns (both constructive and destructive) in the evolution of family communications. The impact of family dynamics upon these interaction patterns is given equal attention.

COMG 381.title: Interpersonal Relations
COMG 381.subject: COMG
COMG 381.description: Theory and research on the development, maintenance, and termination of interpersonal relationships.

COMG 385.title: Culture and Communication
COMG 385.subject: COMG
COMG 385.description: Survey of major factors affecting interpersonal communication between members of different cultures. Emphasis upon interaction between U.S. and Asian-Pacific peoples.

COMG 386.title: Special Topics in Culture and Communication
COMG 386.subject: COMG
COMG 386.description: Contemporary research and theory on intercultural communication.

COMG 390.title: Interrogation and Interviewing
COMG 390.subject: COMG
COMG 390.description: Survey of theory and research on the communicative demands of obtaining reliable information from others.

COMG 392.title: Evolution and Human Communication
COMG 392.subject: COMG
COMG 392.description: Analysis of the role of human communication in mate attraction, intrasexual competition, cooperation, family dynamics, and coalition formation; discussion on the biological function of language, laughter, yawning, and emotion expressions.

COMG 395.title: Research on Communication Behavior
COMG 395.subject: COMG
COMG 395.description: Survey of research on communication behavior. Verbal and nonverbal data collection; analysis of research data. Students design and implement a research project.

COMG 399.title: Internship
COMG 399.subject: COMG
COMG 399.description: Analysis and application of communication knowledge and behaviors in organizational settings.

COMG 452.title: Social Identity and Intergroup Communication
COMG 452.subject: COMG
COMG 452.description: Surveys theory and research on communication between members of different social groups, highlighting how communication influences and is influenced by social identity. Applies concepts to intergenerational, health, family, educational, multilingual, and computer-mediated contexts.

COMG 454.title: Political Communication
COMG 454.subject: COMG
COMG 454.description: Survey of interpersonal and mass communication theories in the political context. Topics may include communication in public opinion processes, elections, debates, political campaigning and advertising.

COMG 455.title: Conflict Management
COMG 455.subject: COMG
COMG 455.description: Examination of the theories, assumptions, practices, models, and techniques of managing interpersonal conflicts.

COMG 462.title: Science Communication
COMG 462.subject: COMG
COMG 462.description: Introduction to principles for communicating science information effectively to a variety of audiences including the general public, policymakers, and professional peers. Application of these principles to create written and oral science communication products.

COMG 464.title: Human Communication and Technology
COMG 464.subject: COMG
COMG 464.description: Analysis of evolving communicative exchanges in the Internet age including how people communicate with computer technology: focus on personal, interpersonal, and cultural effects associated with technology use.

COMG 465.title: Theories and Research in Strategic Communication
COMG 465.subject: COMG
COMG 465.description: An in-depth overview of theories related to strategic communication and scientific approaches to attitude formation and changes. Junior standing or higher.

COMG 470.title: Nonverbal Communication
COMG 470.subject: COMG
COMG 470.description: Understanding communication beyond the words themselves. Review of theory and research on gestures, facial expressions, touch, personal space, and physical appearance.

COMG 471.title: Verbal Communication
COMG 471.subject: COMG
COMG 471.description: Roles of language in human communication and social relationships; language variation, change, and social consequences.

COMG 472.title: Deceptive Communication
COMG 472.subject: COMG
COMG 472.description: Survey of major social scientific theories, concepts, and research findings on deceptive communication, in a lecture/ discussion format. Emphasis is on how people create deceptive messages, induce deception, and strategies used to detect deception.

COMG 481.title: Relational Management
COMG 481.subject: COMG
COMG 481.description: Survey and critical discussion of current theory and research in relational management. Focus on written analysis of the role of communication in the initiation, maintenance, decline, and dissolution of different types of relationships.

COMG 490.title: Communicating Social Support
COMG 490.subject: COMG
COMG 490.description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships and professional relationships.

COMG 493.title: Teaching Speech
COMG 493.subject: COMG
COMG 493.description: For communicology majors who lead, under supervision, a freshman seminar section of communicology.
COMG 493.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

COMG 495.title: Health Communication
COMG 495.subject: COMG
COMG 495.description: Develop understanding of the process through which communication influences health outcomes, and learn how to design effective health communication programs using theory and research.

COMG 499.title: Directed Reading
COMG 499.subject: COMG
COMG 499.description: Pre: consent of department chair and instructor.

COMG 600.title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
COMG 600.subject: COMG
COMG 600.prereq_raw: master’s Plan B candidate and consent.

COMG 601.title: Theories in Communicology
COMG 601.subject: COMG
COMG 601.description: Survey and examination of theories addressing human communication. Social scientific theoretical foundations of creating understanding, interpersonal communication, and persuasion. Emphasis on scholarly writing.

COMG 602.title: Research Methods in Communicology
COMG 602.subject: COMG
COMG 602.description: Design and analysis of quantitative research in communicology. Focus on measurement issues, research design, descriptive and inferential statistics.

COMG 612.title: Advanced Research Methods in Communicology
COMG 612.subject: COMG
COMG 612.description: Advanced focus on survey, laboratory, and field study design, data collection, and data analysis. Emphasis on control of variance through design and statistical analysis. Appropriate preparation for graduate theses and dissertations.

COMG 620.title: Practicum for Instructional Communication
COMG 620.subject: COMG
COMG 620.description: Combined seminar and lecture/ discussion format on techniques and procedures for teaching communication skills and their related components in a laboratory setting.

COMG 660.title: Business Communication
COMG 660.subject: COMG
COMG 660.description: Analysis of communication issues in business through discussion of verbal/nonverbal messages, interpersonal relationships, conflict, and persuasion. Focus on interviewing, group communication, and public speaking skills.
COMG 660.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

COMG 664.title: Persuasion and Social Influence
COMG 664.subject: COMG
COMG 664.description: Theories of persuasion and resistance to persuasion; assessment of attitudes and measurement of change.
COMG 664.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent) or consent.

COMG 670.title: Creating Understanding
COMG 670.subject: COMG
COMG 670.description: Theory and research on human communication, social cognition, comprehension, and creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories, metacognition, prediction, inference-making, and communication systems.
COMG 670.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

COMG 681.title: Relational Communication
COMG 681.subject: COMG
COMG 681.description: Major models and theories of interpersonal communication; research on interpersonal relationships; interaction and functions of human communication.
COMG 681.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

COMG 685.title: Foundations of Intercultural Communication
COMG 685.subject: COMG
COMG 685.description: Major models, theories, and concepts of intercultural communication; basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to intercultural communication; research on intercultural communication. Graduate standing only.
COMG 685.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

COMG 721.title: Approaches to Instructional Communication
COMG 721.subject: COMG
COMG 721.description: Seminar on communication theories and models in instructional environment; emphasis on message processing, classroom dynamics, cognitive and metacognitive processes associated with learning, and learning assessment.
COMG 721.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

COMG 752.title: Research in Intergroup Communication
COMG 752.subject: COMG
COMG 752.description: Theory, concepts, research, and application of communication processes between members of different social groups.
COMG 752.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

COMG 760.title: Seminar in Special Topics in Communicology
COMG 760.subject: COMG
COMG 760.description: Substantive areas in communication that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other COMG courses. Topics vary each semester. Content to be announced.
COMG 760.prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B), or consent.

COMG 764.title: Seminar in Persuasion and Influence
COMG 764.subject: COMG
COMG 764.description: Contemporary research in persuasion and influence.
COMG 764.prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

COMG 770.title: Issues in Creating Understanding
COMG 770.subject: COMG
COMG 770.description: Contemporary research in verbal and nonverbal message processing.
COMG 770.prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

COMG 781.title: Seminar in Relational Communication
COMG 781.subject: COMG
COMG 781.prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

COMG 785.title: Research on Intercultural Communication
COMG 785.subject: COMG
COMG 785.description: Functional approach to the study of communication in intercultural settings. Examination of culture-based variables and their impact on social influence, relational management, and message processing.
COMG 785.prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

COMG 787.title: Artificial Intelligence and Communication
COMG 787.subject: COMG
COMG 787.description: Comprehensive understanding of the role and function of computer technology (including. A.I.) within the field of communication. Basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to semi-intelligent artifacts as information source or receiver. COMG majors or consent.
COMG 787.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.
COMG 787.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

COMG 795.title: Seminar in Health Communication Research
COMG 795.subject: COMG
COMG 795.description: Contemporary interpersonal and/or public communication issues in health communication research. Topics include communication functions such as information management, interpersonal influence, relational management, emotional management, social influence.
COMG 795.prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

CSD 431.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
CSD 431.subject: CSD
CSD 431.description: Will overview anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing. Students gain exposure to structures and functions of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, deglutition, and hearing systems required for normal communication and swallowing.

CSD 432.title: Phonetics
CSD 432.subject: CSD
CSD 432.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of phonetic and phonological development. International Phonetic Alphabet Transcription of English speech sounds; phonological developments and models; cultural variations; analysis interpretation and other considerations related to speech sound development and production.

CSD 433.title: Speech and Language Development
CSD 433.subject: CSD
CSD 433.description: Will develop an understanding of children’s acquisition of speech, language, and normal communication development from birth through adolescence.

CSD 434.title: Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Speech and Hearing
CSD 434.subject: CSD
CSD 434.description: Provides an understanding of the fundamental processes underlying the production and perception of speech. Students gain an understanding of the physical and psychological aspects of sound and their measurement.

CSD 435.title: Introduction to Clinical Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
CSD 435.subject: CSD
CSD 435.description: Provides observation and discussion of the clinical management of individuals with communication disorders, and practical experience related to clinical procedures and requirements.

CSD 436.title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
CSD 436.subject: CSD
CSD 436.description: Information and theoretical foundations serve as an introduction to the field of communication disorders. Will provide an overview of the normal processes and disorders of speech, language, hearing, and swallowing.

CSD 437.title: Introduction to Audiometry and Auditory Disorders
CSD 437.subject: CSD
CSD 437.description: Covers anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, acoustic, basic knowledge of auditory disorders and testing procedures, and introduction to rehabilitative audiology.

CSD 438.title: Basic Statistics for Health-Related Professionals
CSD 438.subject: CSD
CSD 438.description: Provides students from behavioral sciences and health-related professions with an overview of normal distribution, central tendency, variability, sampling, hypothesis testing, frequency distribution, correlation, regression, and t-test.

CSD 600.title: Research Methods
CSD 600.subject: CSD
CSD 600.description: Research methods applicable to the field of speech-language pathology and audiology; analysis and reporting of data. Required of all CSD graduate students.
CSD 600.prereq_raw: previous coursework in inferential statistics and consent.

CSD 601.title: Neuroscience in Communication Sciences and Disorders
CSD 601.subject: CSD
CSD 601.description: Explores the neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the human nervous system as it relates to communication and swallowing and how neurological pathologies lead to behavioral deficits in those areas.

CSD 603.title: Audiological Foundations for Speech- Language Pathology
CSD 603.subject: CSD

CSD 604.title: Seminar in Motor Speech Disorders
CSD 604.subject: CSD
CSD 604.description: Provides in-depth examination of various motor speech disorders, including apraxia of speech and dysarthria. Emphasis is on assessment/treatment of these diagnoses. Review of current treatment literature, anatomy/physiology, practical exercises in treatment planning.

CSD 610.title: Disorders of Phonology and Articulation
CSD 610.subject: CSD
CSD 610.description: Study of the etiology, assessment, and remediation of disorders and articulation.

CSD 612.title: Child Language Disorders
CSD 612.subject: CSD
CSD 612.description: Study of the etiology, behavioral characteristics and treatment methods for child language disorders. Examination of methods, test, and instruments employed in diagnosis of child language disorders. Includes identification of language deficits and writing intervention goals.

CSD 613.title: Language Development for Children with Hearing Deficiencies
CSD 613.subject: CSD
CSD 613.description: Language acquisition by hard-of-hearing and deaf children; methods of stimulating growth.

CSD 616.title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology I
CSD 616.subject: CSD
CSD 616.description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.

CSD 617.title: Audiology Practicum for Speech-Language Pathology
CSD 617.subject: CSD
CSD 617.description: Clinical practice in administering tests, interpreting results; counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

CSD 620.title: Voice Disorders
CSD 620.subject: CSD
CSD 620.description: Contemporary development and theoretical issues in the diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of vocal system disorders in children and adults; current literature and clinical practice issues are addressed.

CSD 622.title: Adult Neurogenic Language and Cognitive-Communication Disorders
CSD 622.subject: CSD
CSD 622.description: Study of acquired adult language and cognitive-communication disorders associated with stroke, traumatic brain injury, and dementia. Application of evidence-based procedures and strategies for assessment and intervention, review of current literature, and discussion of professional issues.

CSD 695.title: Research-Speech Pathology
CSD 695.subject: CSD
CSD 695.description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing speech-language pathology.

CSD 696.title: Research-Audiology
CSD 696.subject: CSD
CSD 696.description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing audiology.

CSD 699B.title: Directed Study: language pathology
CSD 699B.subject: CSD
CSD 699B.description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area.

CSD 699C.title: Directed Study: audiology
CSD 699C.subject: CSD
CSD 699C.description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area.

CSD 701.title: Amplification: Assessment and Applications
CSD 701.subject: CSD
CSD 701.description: Comprehensive study of amplification. Assessment, fitting, evaluation, electroacoustic evaluation, dispensing. Personal instruments and instructional-educational systems.

CSD 702.title: Disorders of Fluency
CSD 702.subject: CSD
CSD 702.description: Contemporary developments and theoretical issues in diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of disorders of fluency such as stuttering in both children and adults.

CSD 703.title: Electrophysiologic Audiometry
CSD 703.subject: CSD
CSD 703.description: Study of early, middle, and late auditory evoked potentials with emphasis on the auditory brainstem response.

CSD 709.title: Dysphagia: Disorders of Swallowing
CSD 709.subject: CSD
CSD 709.description: Explores the dynamics of normal and disordered swallowing across the life span with emphasis on the adult population.
CSD 709.prereq_raw: CSD 601 (with a minimum grade of B-).

CSD 710B.title: Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology: study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology
CSD 710B.subject: CSD
CSD 710B.description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology.

CSD 710C.title: Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology: study of contemporary developments in audiology
CSD 710C.subject: CSD
CSD 710C.description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology.

CSD 716.title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology II
CSD 716.subject: CSD
CSD 716.description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.

CSD 717.title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology II
CSD 717.subject: CSD
CSD 717.description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results; counseling individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

CSD 721.title: Seminar in Audiology-Diagnostic Procedures
CSD 721.subject: CSD
CSD 721.description: Study of diagnostic procedures as reflected in current literature.

CSD 723.title: Seminar in Audiology-Rehabilitative Procedures
CSD 723.subject: CSD
CSD 723.description: Procedures and philosophies presented in recent literature dealing with rehabilitative phases of audiology.

CSD 724.title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology III
CSD 724.subject: CSD
CSD 724.description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedure with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.

CSD 725.title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology III
CSD 725.subject: CSD
CSD 725.description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results, counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

CUL 609.title: Faculty Seminar Series
CUL 609.subject: CUL
CUL 609.description: Seminar consists of a series of presentations by certificate faculty on topics of ongoing research. Presentations will open current debates about theory and method in cultural studies.

CUL 610.title: International Cultural Studies: History and Theory
CUL 610.subject: CUL
CUL 610.description: Seminar on the history and theory of interdisciplinary cultural studies. The politics of culture are examined in comparative perspective, focusing on their significance for identity formation, intercultural relations, and global flows of images, people and capital. Approaches to the study of media and popular culture are taken up in terms of their relevance for contemporary issues, especially in Hawaiʻi and the Asia/ Pacific/U.S. region.

CUL 750.title: International Cultural Studies: Research Project
CUL 750.subject: CUL
CUL 750.description: Directed reading and research culminating in a project that engages issues in international cultural studies. Types of projects include scholarly essays, community-based projects, performances or exhibitions. Written statement of purpose and self-evaluation required.

DATA 102.title: Introduction to Data Science
DATA 102.subject: DATA
DATA 102.description: Overview of the field of data science. Introduction to subjects such as data format, processing, visualization, and storage. Special emphasis on historical and wider context, and simple practical examples.

DATA 110P.title: Introduction to Computer Programming: Python
DATA 110P.subject: DATA
DATA 110P.description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (P) Python.

DATA 235.title: Machine Learning Methods
DATA 235.subject: DATA
DATA 235.description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning.

DATA 422.title: Network Science Methodology
DATA 422.subject: DATA
DATA 422.description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages.

DATA 434.title: Data Science Fundamentals
DATA 434.subject: DATA
DATA 434.description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist.

DATA 435.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
DATA 435.subject: DATA
DATA 435.description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory.

DATA 438.title: Big Data Analytics
DATA 438.subject: DATA
DATA 438.description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.

DATA 484.title: Data Visualization
DATA 484.subject: DATA
DATA 484.description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization.
DATA 484.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

DH 231.title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology
DH 231.subject: DH
DH 231.description: The study of the structure and functions of the head and neck with emphasis on structures in or related to the oral cavity; of tooth morphology.
DH 231.prereq_raw: PHYL 141 , PHYL 141 , and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161 ; or equivalent.

DH 231L.title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology Lab
DH 231L.subject: DH
DH 231L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of DH 231 didactic concepts to laboratory activities and practices.
DH 231L.prereq_raw: PHYL 141 , PHYL 141L , PHYL 142 , PHYL 142L , and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161 .

DH 238.title: Basic Dental Hygiene I
DH 238.subject: DH
DH 238.description: Relationship to dentistry, problems, trends, issues; role and functions of dental hygienists to prevent and control chronic oral diseases; preliminary dental hygiene clinical, includes team concepts in dentistry. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession.

DH 238L.title: Basic Dental Hygiene I Lab
DH 238L.subject: DH
DH 238L.description: Application of preliminary dental hygiene clinical and support procedures including instrumentation, vital signs, and team concepts in dentistry.

DH 240.title: Basic Dental Hygiene II
DH 240.subject: DH
DH 240.description: Basic dental hygiene theory and skills including competencies in health history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, plaque control and support procedures.

DH 240L.title: Basic Dental Hygiene II Lab/Clinic
DH 240L.subject: DH
DH 240L.description: Laboratory and clinical experiences in basic dental hygiene skills and competencies including history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, and clinic procedures.

DH 250.title: General Histology
DH 250.subject: DH
DH 250.description: Cells, tissues, the organs they make up, and their embryologic origin.

DH 251.title: Oral Histology and Embryology
DH 251.subject: DH
DH 251.description: Cells and tissues as they relate to the oral cavity and the embryological development of the head, neck, and related oral structures.

DH 281.title: Dental Radiography
DH 281.subject: DH
DH 281.description: Basic principles of radiation and fundamental information to understand and safely use radiation in dental radiography.

DH 281L.title: Dental Radiography Lab/Clinic
DH 281L.subject: DH
DH 281L.description: (1 3-hr Lab/Clinic) Preparation and evaluation of radiographic survey of patients with varying dentition; methods, and indications of safety considerations in clinical application of roentgen rays.

DH 361.title: Health Education and Promotion
DH 361.subject: DH
DH 361.description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups and the larger public.
DH 361.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

DH 366.title: General Pathology
DH 366.subject: DH
DH 366.description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases and tissue alterations associated with the human body organ systems.

DH 367.title: Oral Pathology
DH 367.subject: DH
DH 367.description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases affecting the teeth and the structures of the oral cavity.

DH 369.title: Dental Materials
DH 369.subject: DH
DH 369.description: Science of dental materials and its application to dentistry and dental hygiene.

DH 369L.title: Dental Materials Lab/Clinic
DH 369L.subject: DH
DH 369L.description: Laboratory and clinical application of concepts in the science of dental materials.

DH 370.title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene
DH 370.subject: DH
DH 370.description: Basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

DH 370L.title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene Lab/Clinic
DH 370L.subject: DH
DH 370L.description: (2 1.5-hr Lab/Clinic) Application of basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

DH 375.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I
DH 375.subject: DH
DH 375.description: Development of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.
DH 375.prereq_raw: DH 240 , DH 240L , DH 281 , DH 281L , and DH 389 .

DH 375L.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I Clinic
DH 375L.subject: DH
DH 375L.description: Clinical instruction and application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing, and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.
DH 375L.prereq_raw: DH 240 , DH 240L , DH 281 , DH 281L , and DH 389 .

DH 380.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II
DH 380.subject: DH
DH 380.description: Continued development of dental hygiene concepts, skills, emergency procedures, team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating oral hygiene care of patients. Review and analyze dental periodicals and conduct a case study. Emphasis on writing.

DH 380L.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
DH 380L.subject: DH
DH 380L.description: Continuation of DH 375 . Clinical application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care to patients.

DH 389.title: Pain Control and Local Anesthesia in Dentistry
DH 389.subject: DH
DH 389.description: Basic concepts of pain control and local anesthesia in dentistry with appropriate emphasis on psychological preparation, pharmacological preparation, and safe and effective administration of anesthesia in the practice of dental hygiene.

DH 390.title: Periodontology I
DH 390.subject: DH
DH 390.description: Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing.

DH 391.title: Periodontology II
DH 391.subject: DH
DH 391.description: Continuation of DH 390 . Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing.

DH 473.title: Community Health
DH 473.subject: DH
DH 473.description: Introduction and application of principles of health education and dental public health (assess, plan, implement and evaluate) into practice in schools, community agencies, and private dental offices; epidemiology and biostatistics. Emphasis on writing.

DH 475.title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene I
DH 475.subject: DH
DH 475.description: An in-depth knowledge and clinical application of expanded function in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

DH 475L.title: Advanced Dental Hygiene I Clinic
DH 475L.subject: DH
DH 475L.description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

DH 480.title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II
DH 480.subject: DH
DH 480.description: In-depth knowledge, communicated via oral delivery, on development of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modifications in behavior.

DH 480L.title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
DH 480L.subject: DH
DH 480L.description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

DH 484.title: Pediatric Growth and Development
DH 484.subject: DH
DH 484.description: Focus on the normal growth and development of children based on current clinical practice guidelines and evidence in pediatric research.

DH 485.title: Advanced Health and Diagnostic Assessment for Pediatric Patients
DH 485.subject: DH
DH 485.description: Focus on advanced health and diagnostic assessment for pediatric patients. Includes behavior management techniques as well as oral habits and subsequent malocclusions and speech difficulties.

DH 486.title: Pharmacological Principles and Clinical Therapeutics in Pediatric Dental Care
DH 486.subject: DH
DH 486.description: Focus on pharmacological principles and clinical therapeutics in pediatric dental care. DH majors only.

DH 487.title: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Simulation Lab
DH 487.subject: DH
DH 487.description: Focus on interprofessional practice principles and competencies while providing students an opportunity to participate in interprofessional team simulations to address health care issues of children.

DH 488.title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical I
DH 488.subject: DH
DH 488.description: Field experience. Clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.

DH 489.title: Management of Pediatric Dental Emergencies
DH 489.subject: DH
DH 489.description: Focus on the management of dental emergencies in children.

DH 490.title: Community-Based Dental Hygiene Care of Vulnerable and Special Needs Children
DH 490.subject: DH
DH 490.description: Emphasizes community-based oral health promotion, dental disease risk reduction and management in children 0-5 years of age with a focus on vulnerable and special needs populations.

DH 491.title: Community-Based Practice Capstone
DH 491.subject: DH
DH 491.description: Provides an opportunity to synthesize, analyze, and develop solutions to an oral health care problem affecting children ages 0-5 years. Requires one credit to be spent in fieldwork to meet course requirements.

DH 492.title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical II
DH 492.subject: DH
DH 492.description: Advanced clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.

DH 499.title: Directed Reading, Field Work, or Research
DH 499.subject: DH
DH 499.description: Individualized program of directed reading, field work, or research for major under supervision in related areas of dentistry and dental hygiene.

DIS 380.title: Foundations in Disability and Diversity
DIS 380.subject: DIS
DIS 380.description: Focuses on disability as a category of diversity and identity, as well as diversity within disability. Different strategies used to increase the freedom or liberty of people with disabilities are critically examined.

DIS 382.title: Accessible Learning Technology
DIS 382.subject: DIS
DIS 382.description: Focuses on creating accessible technology and instructional media, developing long-term resources, advancing accessible social interaction between students and students with instructors, and using case studies as examples of good practices.

DIS 383.title: Disability History and Culture: From Homer to Hip Hop
DIS 383.subject: DIS
DIS 383.description: How have people over many centuries, and from broad geographical perspectives perceived and treated individuals with disabilities? An overview of the history of the conditions in which people with disabilities lived.

DIS 606.title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
DIS 606.subject: DIS
DIS 606.description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, Action Research, mixed methods, and Curriculum Based Assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal.

DIS 650.title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
DIS 650.subject: DIS
DIS 650.description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawaiʻi and our global community.

DIS 651.title: Sexuality & Health
DIS 651.subject: DIS
DIS 651.description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

DIS 675.title: Supporting Multilingual Learners
DIS 675.subject: DIS
DIS 675.description: Strategies for identifying and adopting best practices that support all students in inclusive learning environments with an emphasis on STEM curriculum for English Language Learners; (B) science; (C) technology; (D) math.

DIS 678.title: Applied Disability Service Practicum
DIS 678.subject: DIS
DIS 678.description: Supervised field experience in applied disability service. The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

DIS 680.title: Disability History Through the Ages
DIS 680.subject: DIS
DIS 680.description: A historical overview of disability that visits diverse perspectives, attitudes, and treatment toward individuals with disabilities through many centuries, societies, and cultures throughout the world; and how people with disabilities perceived themselves.

DIS 681.title: Multicultural Issues in Disabilities
DIS 681.subject: DIS
DIS 681.description: Provides background and understanding of various Pacific Rim cultural issues in the conceptualization and treatment of individuals with disabilities and their families.

DIS 682.title: Special Topics in Disability and Diversity Studies
DIS 682.subject: DIS
DIS 682.description: Explores disability and diversity across time to gain an understanding and context of issues such as difference, culture, identity, community, privilege, and oppression and how the past affects the present and future.

DIS 683.title: Interdisciplinary Disability and Diversity Issues
DIS 683.subject: DIS
DIS 683.description: Develop understanding of current issues faced by individuals with disabilities and their families within the disability paradigm and across cultures.

DIS 684.title: Interdisciplinary Team Development
DIS 684.subject: DIS
DIS 684.description: Develop knowledge and skills to participate effectively on interdisciplinary teams for the common goal of promoting service integration and coordination of education, social, health, mental health, and other services with individuals with disabilities and their families.

DIS 685.title: Interdisciplinary Assessment
DIS 685.subject: DIS
DIS 685.description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS).

DIS 686.title: Advanced Interdisciplinary Assessment
DIS 686.subject: DIS
DIS 686.description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS).

DIS 687.title: Seminar on Disability Issues
DIS 687.subject: DIS
DIS 687.description: In-depth explorations of current and compelling interdisciplinary topics related to advancing the social, political, educational, and economic integration of individuals with disabilities of all ages.

DIS 688.title: Portfolio/Field Work
DIS 688.subject: DIS
DIS 688.description: Interdisciplinary community experience and portfolio in disability and diversity studies.

DIS 780.title: Mixed Methods Research Design
DIS 780.subject: DIS
DIS 780.description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal.

DNCE 100.title: Introduction to Stage, Screen, and New Media Writing
DNCE 100.subject: DNCE
DNCE 100.description: Introduction to college level writing and information literacy for and about the stage (theatre, dance, performance), the screen (film, television), and new media (digital platforms, social media).

DNCE 140.title: Hip Hop Dance
DNCE 140.subject: DNCE
DNCE 140.description: Introductory lecture/ lab geared towards those with or without Hip Hop dance experience. Students will learn the fundamentals of various Hip Hop dance styles.

DNCE 142.title: Ballroom Dance
DNCE 142.subject: DNCE
DNCE 142.description: Introduction to those with or without ballroom dance experience. Students will learn the fundamentals of various ballroom dances.

DNCE 150.title: Introduction to Dance

DNCE 150.description: Survey the development of major dance styles and their relationship to contemporary choreography, emphasis on teaching writing.

DNCE 151.title: Music Theory for Dancers

DNCE 151.description: Elements of music and relationship to dance; emphasis on rhythmic analysis.

DNCE 152.title: Live on Stage

DNCE 152.description: Students view locally-produced theatre and dance productions and write performance reviews. Readings, writing, and class discussion will guide students to understand each performance. Performances include theatre, dance, musical theatre, opera, and performance art.

DNCE 188.title: Beginning Hula
DNCE 188.subject: DNCE
DNCE 188.description: Designed for students with no hula experience. Introduces students to the basic foundational skills of hula and emphasizes the importance of language, basic body movements and vocal techniques.
