DNCE 388.description: Advanced level hula course for students with hula experience that builds upon existing cultural knowledge, performance and language skills presented in DNCE 288 / THEA 288 .

DNCE 458.title: Field Experiences in Dance
DNCE 458.subject: DNCE
DNCE 458.description: Field experiences in relevant contexts under professional and faculty supervision.
DNCE 458.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing and consent.

DNCE 459.title: Topics in Dance
DNCE 459.subject: DNCE
DNCE 459.description: Readings, research, and/or field and movement experiences.

DNCE 460.title: Teaching Dance Technique
DNCE 460.subject: DNCE
DNCE 460.description: Principles, techniques, and materials used in the teaching of dance technique.

DNCE 470.title: Dance Performance
DNCE 470.subject: DNCE
DNCE 470.description: Performance in various dance styles and settings.

DNCE 480.title: Dance Repertory
DNCE 480.subject: DNCE
DNCE 480.description: Preparation of standard and new works for performance.
DNCE 480.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DANC, DNTH, THDN majors only.

DNCE 488.title: Advanced Hula II: Traditional and Modern Hula Choreography
DNCE 488.subject: DNCE
DNCE 488.description: Advanced hula course designed for students with extensive hula and language experience. It shares hula choreography of the same hula in both hula kahiko and hula auana.

DNCE 490.title: Creative Dance
DNCE 490.subject: DNCE
DNCE 490.description: Dance activities for young people. Appropriate for teachers, group workers, recreation majors, and others working with children. Also adults with special needs. Supervised field activities.

DNCE 495.title: Senior Project
DNCE 495.subject: DNCE
DNCE 495.description: Individual senior project; BFA student choreographs creative project and performs; BA student develops capstone and presents.

DNCE 615.title: Performance Theory
DNCE 615.subject: DNCE
DNCE 615.description: Introduction to key texts and concepts of performance studies.

DNCE 626.title: Advanced Topics in Performance
DNCE 626.subject: DNCE
DNCE 626.description: Readings, discussion, research, and/or performance work.
DNCE 626.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

DNCE 651.title: Seminar in Dance Research
DNCE 651.subject: DNCE
DNCE 651.description: Research materials and methods; preparation for thesis and scholarly research reporting. Required for graduate concentrations in dance.

DNCE 652.title: Seminar: Dance Theory and Criticism
DNCE 652.subject: DNCE
DNCE 652.description: Major theories of dance and dance criticism; emphasis on Western ideas.

DNCE 654.title: Dance and Performance Theory: Asia
DNCE 654.subject: DNCE
DNCE 654.description: Dance content and historico-social context of principal dance traditions.
DNCE 654.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

DNCE 655.title: Dance and Performance Theory: Oceania
DNCE 655.subject: DNCE
DNCE 655.description: Dance content and historico-social context of principal dance traditions.
DNCE 655.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

DNCE 658.title: Business for the Arts
DNCE 658.subject: DNCE
DNCE 658.description: Seminar offering overview and foundation for launching or advancing enterprises in the arts. A focus on the processes and method for creating economically successful grants and project development applications.

DNCE 659.title: Advanced Topics in Dance
DNCE 659.subject: DNCE
DNCE 659.description: Readings, research, and/or field movement experiences.
DNCE 659.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DANC, DNTH, THDN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

DNCE 660.title: Movement Analysis
DNCE 660.subject: DNCE
DNCE 660.description: Movement analysis in indigenous, critical race, critical dance frameworks for enhancing scholarly and artistic abilities.
DNCE 660.prereq_raw: DNCE 260 (or concurrent) and DNCE 360 (or concurrent); or consent.

DNCE 668.title: Advanced Topics in Performance in Hawaiʻi
DNCE 668.subject: DNCE
DNCE 668.description: Analysis of Hawai’i’s indigenous performance traditions, the contemporary multicultural landscape of theatre in Ko Hawai’i Pae ‘āina, and the representation of Kanaka Maoli and settler voices on Hawai’i’s stages.
DNCE 668.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

DNCE 672.title: Dance Performance
DNCE 672.subject: DNCE
DNCE 672.description: Graduate performance in various dance styles and settings. By audition only.

DNCE 673.title: Advanced Dance Technology and Live Performance
DNCE 673.subject: DNCE
DNCE 673.description: Advanced skills in dance and technology in live performance. Emphasis on New Media.
DNCE 673.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

DNCE 674.title: Interdisciplinary Collaborations
DNCE 674.subject: DNCE
DNCE 674.description: Hybrid performance works for dancers, musicians, actors, visual artists, poets, and writers to explore the nature of the collaboration process in various settings.
DNCE 674.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, MUS, ART, ENG, THDN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

DNCE 676.title: Seminar in Choreographic Methods
DNCE 676.subject: DNCE
DNCE 676.description: Graduate level course designed for students with prior choreographic experience. Students will research, create, revise, and perform new works based on a variety of choreographic methodologies.

DNCE 679.title: Directed Choreography
DNCE 679.subject: DNCE
DNCE 679.description: Concert choreography for selected performance settings under the direction of a faculty advisor.
DNCE 679.prereq_raw: DNCE 372 (or concurrent) or DNCE 671 (or concurrent), or consent.

DNCE 688.title: Hula Genealogy: Lineage & Legacy
DNCE 688.subject: DNCE
DNCE 688.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

DNCE 691.title: Seminar in Teaching Dance/Theater
DNCE 691.subject: DNCE
DNCE 691.description: Pedagogy and classroom experience in teaching technique and theory.

DNCE 692.title: Practicum in Teaching
DNCE 692.subject: DNCE
DNCE 692.description: Supervised teaching experience at the introductory or undergraduate level. Students will teach an appropriate level course in their field of expertise under faculty supervision.
DNCE 692.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

DNCE 693.title: Internship: Youth Theater/Dance
DNCE 693.subject: DNCE
DNCE 693.description: Supervised leadership experiences in dance/theater program with children. Students spend nine hours per week in supervised setting and three hours in weekly class meeting.
DNCE 693.prereq_raw: DNCE 490 , THEA 470 , or THEA 476 ; or consent.
DNCE 693.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DANC, DNTH, THDN majors only.

DNCE 695.title: Dance Colloquium
DNCE 695.subject: DNCE
DNCE 695.description: Forum for presentation and discussion of current intellectual and artistic activities in the dance field.

DNCE 696B.title: Professional Internship: entertainment design: costume, lighting, scenery, props, sound, or other related disciplines
DNCE 696B.subject: DNCE
DNCE 696B.description: Internship program where students will work for or with a professional theatre company under supervision of a UH faculty member, plus possible supervisor(s) from the theatre company. Students must participate hands-on in production activities of that company and receive a satisfactory (or better) review from their supervisor(s); (B) entertainment design: costume, lighting, scenery, props, sound, or other related disciplines; (C) performance: acting, directing, dance, choreography, or other related disciplines.
DNCE 696B.prereq_raw: DNCE 345 or DNCE 353 or DNCE 356 for (B); 621 or 682 or DNCE 371 for (C).

DNCE 696C.title: Professional Internship: performance: acting, directing, dance, choreography, or other related disciplines
DNCE 696C.subject: DNCE
DNCE 696C.description: Internship program where students will work for or with a professional theatre company under supervision of a UH faculty member, plus possible supervisor(s) from the theatre company. Students must participate hands-on in production activities of that company and receive a satisfactory (or better) review from their supervisor(s); (B) entertainment design: costume, lighting, scenery, props, sound, or other related disciplines; (C) performance: acting, directing, dance, choreography, or other related disciplines.
DNCE 696C.prereq_raw: DNCE 345 or DNCE 353 or DNCE 356 for (B); 621 or 682 or DNCE 371 for (C).

DRB 601.title: Fertilization and Early Development
DRB 601.subject: DRB
DRB 601.description: Lecture on the basics of vertebrate and invertebrate fertilization and early embryonic development.
DRB 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Open to all graduate students.

DRB 613.title: Seminar in Developmental and Reproductive Biology I
DRB 613.subject: DRB
DRB 613.description: Presentations of current research carried out by developmental and reproductive biology graduate program faculty.

DRB 614.title: Developmental and Reproductive Biology Scientific Investigations
DRB 614.subject: DRB
DRB 614.description: Discussion of current research in developmental and reproductive biology.

DRB 650.title: Stem Cell Biology
DRB 650.subject: DRB
DRB 650.description: Seminar designed to teach graduate students and advanced undergraduate students about current topics relating to stem cell biology, as well as the application of stem cells to modern medicine.

DRB 651.title: Biology of Aging
DRB 651.subject: DRB
DRB 651.description: Teaches graduate and advanced (fourth year) undergraduate students about current topics relating to the biology of aging, as well as the practical applications for therapy to enhance healthy aging.

DRB 666.title: Applied Developmental and Reproductive Biology
DRB 666.subject: DRB
DRB 666.description: Combined lecture-lab on current technologies and methods for mammalian reproduction and developmental biology.
DRB 666.prereq_raw: DRB 601 (or concurrent), DRB 613 / DRB 614 (or concurrent); or consent.

DRB 695.title: DRB Research Rotation
DRB 695.subject: DRB
DRB 695.description: Introductory laboratory research experience under the supervision of faculty.

DRB 699.title: Directed Research
DRB 699.subject: DRB
DRB 699.description: Research experience in developmental and reproductive biology.

EALL 100.title: Writing East Asia
EALL 100.subject: EALL
EALL 100.description: An introduction to writing analytically and cross-culturally about East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) and various aspects of East Asian culture.

EALL 140.title: Introduction to Chinese Language and Culture
EALL 140.subject: EALL
EALL 140.description: Provides students with interesting perspectives on and some general knowledge of Chinese language, literature, and culture.

EALL 271.title: Japanese Literature in Translation- Traditional
EALL 271.subject: EALL
EALL 271.description: Survey of all major forms from the earliest era to mid-19th century.

EALL 272.title: Japanese Literature in Translation- Modern
EALL 272.subject: EALL
EALL 272.description: Survey from mid-19th century to present; emphasis on fiction.

EALL 273.title: Survey of Japanese Literature-KIC
EALL 273.subject: EALL
EALL 273.description: Survey of traditional and modern Japanese literature in translation, covering all major genres. Only offered at Konan University in Japan. Not open to students with 271 or 272.

EALL 281.title: Korean Literature in Translation- Traditional
EALL 281.subject: EALL
EALL 281.description: Survey of Korean literature from earliest times with emphasis on development and cultural context; all readings in English translation. Emphasis on writing instruction.

EALL 282.title: Korean Literature in Translation-Modern
EALL 282.subject: EALL
EALL 282.description: Survey of 20th-century Korean literature with emphasis on development and cultural context; all readings in English translation. Students write essays about the readings.

EALL 320.title: Topics in Korean Culture
EALL 320.subject: EALL
EALL 320.description: Multidisciplinary and historically-located study of Korean culture through the examination of literary and visual texts. Topics will depend upon the term.
EALL 320.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

EALL 325B.title: Japanese Film: Art and History: 1900-1960
EALL 325B.subject: EALL
EALL 325B.description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
EALL 325B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

EALL 325C.title: Japanese Film: Art and History: 1960-present
EALL 325C.subject: EALL
EALL 325C.description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
EALL 325C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

EALL 325D.title: Japanese Film: Art and History: special topics
EALL 325D.subject: EALL
EALL 325D.description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
EALL 325D.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

EALL 330.title: Chinese Film: Art and History
EALL 330.subject: EALL
EALL 330.description: Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts.

EALL 360.title: Literary Traditions of East Asia
EALL 360.subject: EALL
EALL 360.description: Selected works of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean literature in English; relationships and parallels.
EALL 360.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 361.title: Chinese Literature: Ancient
EALL 361.subject: EALL
EALL 361.description: Survey of all major genres from antiquity until the ninth century. Emphasis on writing instruction.
EALL 361.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 362.title: Chinese Literature: Pre-modern
EALL 362.subject: EALL
EALL 362.description: Survey of all major genres from the ninth century till the end of the Qing.
EALL 362.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 364.title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
EALL 364.subject: EALL
EALL 364.description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
EALL 364.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 365B.title: Traditional Chinese Fiction in Translation: short story
EALL 365B.subject: EALL
EALL 365B.description: Survey of pre-modern Chinese fiction in translation. (B) short story; (C) novel.
EALL 365B.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 365C.title: Traditional Chinese Fiction in Translation: novel
EALL 365C.subject: EALL
EALL 365C.description: Survey of pre-modern Chinese fiction in translation. (B) short story; (C) novel.
EALL 365C.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 366.title: The City in Modern Chinese Literature and Visual Arts
EALL 366.subject: EALL
EALL 366.description: Study of the fictional and visual representations of the city in the changing contexts of Chinese modernization from the late imperial age to the beginning of the 21st century.
EALL 366.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 371.title: Topics in Traditional Japanese Literature
EALL 371.subject: EALL
EALL 371.description: Reading and analysis of English translations of selected important works in the classical tradition. No knowledge of Japanese required.

EALL 372.title: Topics in Modern Japanese Literature
EALL 372.subject: EALL
EALL 372.description: Reading and analysis of English translations of selected important works in modern Japanese literature. No knowledge of Japanese required.

EALL 375.title: Topics in Japanese Cultural Studies
EALL 375.subject: EALL
EALL 375.description: Multi-disciplinary and historically located study of Japanese culture through the examination of literary and visual texts. Specific topics will depend upon the term.
EALL 375.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 384.title: Modern Korean Women Writers and Culture
EALL 384.subject: EALL
EALL 384.description: Study of fiction by modern Korean women writers in the changing context of Korean culture.
EALL 384.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

EALL 472.title: East-West Cultural Encounters
EALL 472.subject: EALL
EALL 472.description: Critical examination of encounters between Western and East Asian cultures across time. In addition to literary texts, the course may use sources from other media, and focus on a specific era, region, or genre.
EALL 472.prereq_raw: an EALL course at 200 level or above; or a DH or DL course at 200 level or above; or consent.

EALL 473.title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture-Chinese Diaspora
EALL 473.subject: EALL
EALL 473.description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term.
EALL 473.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course or consent.

EALL 474.title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
EALL 474.subject: EALL
EALL 474.description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism.
EALL 474.prereq_raw: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course.

EALL 476.title: Perspectives on Chinese Cinema
EALL 476.subject: EALL
EALL 476.description: Introduction to Chinese cinema studies, with emphasis on the theoretical and critical approaches to Chinese film.
EALL 476.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

EALL 491.title: Senior Colloquium in East Asian Literature
EALL 491.subject: EALL
EALL 491.description: Comparative perspectives; some works studied in the original.

EALL 601.title: Current Issues in East Asian Language Pedagogy
EALL 601.subject: EALL
EALL 601.description: Survey on East Asian language pedagogy designed to develop students’ familiarity with and facility in addressing the major issues, initiatives, and innovations in the field.
EALL 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

EALL 602.title: Introduction to East Asian Linguistics
EALL 602.subject: EALL
EALL 602.description: Introduction to cross-linguistic comparison of the writing systems, dialects, history, phonology, morphology, and syntax of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
EALL 602.prereq_raw: CHN 451 and CHN 452 , or JPN 451 , or KOR 451 and KOR 452 ; or consent.

EALL 603C.title: Bibliographical and Research Methods: Chinese
EALL 603C.subject: EALL
EALL 603C.description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
EALL 603C.prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

EALL 603J.title: Bibliographical and Research Methods: Japanese
EALL 603J.subject: EALL
EALL 603J.description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
EALL 603J.prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

EALL 603K.title: Bibliographical and Research Methods: Korean
EALL 603K.subject: EALL
EALL 603K.description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
EALL 603K.prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

EALL 611.title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
EALL 611.subject: EALL
EALL 611.description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required.

EALL 647.title: Contemporary Chinese Documentary: Record, Expression, Cultural Space
EALL 647.subject: EALL
EALL 647.description: Introduction to contemporary Chinese independent documentary with these goals: to achieve in-depth understanding of Chinese society through documentary; be familiar with theoretical debates on documentary form; and understand documentary as a cultural discourse.

EALL 665.title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
EALL 665.subject: EALL
EALL 665.description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective.

EALL 735.title: Seminar in Comparative East Asian Literature
EALL 735.subject: EALL
EALL 735.description: Comparison of authors, modes, topics, and genres in poetry and prose; theoretical and practical criticism.

EALL 750.title: Seminar in Comparison of East Asian Languages
EALL 750.subject: EALL
EALL 750.description: Comparison of lexicon, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, etc., of two or more East Asian languages, contact influence on them.
EALL 750.prereq_raw: CHN 451 , CHN 452 , or JPN 451 ; or consent.

ECE 101.title: Electrical Engineering Skills
ECE 101.subject: ECE
ECE 101.description: Electrical engineering subjects in a skill acquisition context at the freshman level. Learning, creative problem solving, brainstorming, technical information assimilation, and presentation skills development.

ECE 110.title: Introduction to Engineering Computation
ECE 110.subject: ECE
ECE 110.description: Engineering problem solving using MATLAB. Basic programming concepts include input/output, branching, looping, functions, file input/output, and data structures such as arrays and structures. Matrix operations for solving linear equations. Engineering computations and visualization.
ECE 110.prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent.
ECE 110.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE and CENG majors only.

ECE 160.title: Programming for Engineers
ECE 160.subject: ECE
ECE 160.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to computer programming and modern computing environments with an emphasis on algorithm and program design, implementation, and debugging. Includes a hands-on laboratory to develop and practice programming skills.
ECE 160.prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent.
ECE 160.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CENG, EE, ME, PREN, CNST, and ENGS majors only.

ECE 196.title: Freshman Project
ECE 196.subject: ECE
ECE 196.description: Freshman level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. This project provides early student entry into ECE hands-on project activity providing practical skills, ECE subject exposure and experience. Second semester freshman standing required.
ECE 196.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CENG, EE, and PREN majors only.

ECE 205.title: Object Oriented Programming
ECE 205.subject: ECE
ECE 205.description: Second programming for computer engineers. System programming language, such as C. Object-oriented programming paradigm, definition and use of classes, fundamentals of object-oriented design, such as C++. Common data structures. Common searching and sorting algorithms.
ECE 205.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE, CENG, EE, ME, PREN majors only.

ECE 211.title: Basic Circuit Analysis I
ECE 211.subject: ECE
ECE 211.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Linear passive circuits, time domain analysis, transient and steady-state responses, phasors, impedance and admittance; power and energy, frequency responses, resonance.
ECE 211.prereq_raw: MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent), and PHYS 272 (or concurrent); or consent.
ECE 211.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CENG, EE, ME, PREN, and ENGS majors only.

ECE 213.title: Basic Circuit Analysis II
ECE 213.subject: ECE
ECE 213.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Laplace transforms and their application to circuits, Fourier transforms and their applications to circuits, frequency selective circuits, introduction to and design of active filters, convolution, and state space analysis of circuits.
ECE 213.prereq_raw: ECE 211 , and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent.

ECE 260.title: Introduction to Digital Design
ECE 260.subject: ECE
ECE 260.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the design of digital systems with an emphasis on design methods and the implementation and use of fundamental digital components.
ECE 260.prereq_raw: ECE 160 or ECE 110 or ICS 111 or consent.

ECE 296.title: Sophomore Project
ECE 296.subject: ECE
ECE 296.description: Sophomore level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills.
ECE 296.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CENG, EE, and PREN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

ECE 315.title: Signal and Systems Analysis
ECE 315.subject: ECE
ECE 315.description: Discrete-time and continuous time signals and systems, linear systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transform, sampling.
ECE 315.prereq_raw: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; or consent.

ECE 323.title: Microelectronic Circuits I
ECE 323.subject: ECE
ECE 323.description: Semiconductor structures, operating principles and characteristics of diodes and amplifying devices. Their application as circuit elements in building basic digital, analog, and integrated circuit subsystems.

ECE 323L.title: Microelectronic Circuits I Lab
ECE 323L.subject: ECE
ECE 323L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments on linear and logic properties of diodes and transistor networks.

ECE 324.title: Physical Electronics
ECE 324.subject: ECE
ECE 324.description: Review of quantum mechanics fundamentals, H-atom, and chemical bonding. Introduction to band structure models and materials. Semiconductor doping, charge carrier statistics and charge transport, including ambipolar transport. Metal-semiconductor and PN junctions.
ECE 324.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and PHYS 274 ; or consent.

ECE 326.title: Microelectronic Circuits II
ECE 326.subject: ECE
ECE 326.description: Principles and design of linear electronic circuits including differential, operational, feedback, and tuned amplifiers; integrated circuits, current mirrors, signal generators, filters, and stability.

ECE 326L.title: Microelectronic Circuits II Lab
ECE 326L.subject: ECE
ECE 326L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 326 , experiments on linear and analog electronics. Includes an emphasis on writing laboratory reports.

ECE 327.title: Theory and Design of IC Devices
ECE 327.subject: ECE
ECE 327.description: Band structure models and carrier transport physics review. Theory and design of semiconductor IC devices: Schottky diodes, bipolar devices (PN junction diodes, BJTs), FETs (MOSFETs, JFETs, and MESFETs).
ECE 327.prereq_raw: ECE 324 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A ; or consent.

ECE 328.title: Microcircuit Fabrication
ECE 328.subject: ECE
ECE 328.description: Technology principles, materials, and methods for the design and fabrication of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, and microelectromechanical systems.

ECE 328L.title: Microcircuit Fabrication Lab
ECE 328L.subject: ECE
ECE 328L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on laboratory where students make various electronic and electromechanical micro-devices using IC technology. Devices are also tested and analyzed.

ECE 342.title: Probability and Statistics
ECE 342.subject: ECE
ECE 342.description: Probability, statistics, random variables, distributions, densities, expectations, limit theorems, and applications to electrical engineering.
ECE 342.prereq_raw: ECE 315 (or concurrent) and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; or consent.

ECE 343.title: Introduction to Communication Systems
ECE 343.subject: ECE
ECE 343.description: Signal representation, Fourier analysis; amplitude and angle modulated systems; sampling theorems, pulse and digital modulation systems; carrier modulation by digital signals.

ECE 343L.title: Communication Systems Lab
ECE 343L.subject: ECE
ECE 343L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of communication systems. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

ECE 344.title: Networking I
ECE 344.subject: ECE
ECE 344.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Covers 4 semesters from the Cisco Networking Academy plus supplementary material; hands-on experience with routers and switches; prepares students for the CCNA. Topics include TCP/IP, LANs, WANs, routing protocols, network security; PPP; ISDN, frame relay.

ECE 345.title: Linear Algebra and Machine Learning
ECE 345.subject: ECE
ECE 345.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Mathematical and algorithmic fundamentals of linear algebra and their applications and illustrations to machine learning. Lab introduces programming with data and uses machine learning libraries for an introduction to commonly used technologies.
ECE 345.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MATH, CENG, EE, CE, ME, ICS majors only.

ECE 351.title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems
ECE 351.subject: ECE
ECE 351.description: Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

ECE 351L.title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems Lab
ECE 351L.subject: ECE
ECE 351L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Provides experience in applying theoretical tools to analyze linear systems. Extensive use is made of computer-aided analysis and design packages study system performance.

ECE 361.title: Digital Systems and Computer Design
ECE 361.subject: ECE
ECE 361.description: Design methodology, processor design, control design, memory organization, system organization.

ECE 361L.title: Digital Systems and Computer Design Lab
ECE 361L.subject: ECE
ECE 361L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 361 , experiments on digital systems and interfacing. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

ECE 362.title: Discrete Math for Engineers
ECE 362.subject: ECE
ECE 362.description: Logic, sets, number theory, properties of functions, properties of relations, methods of proofs, recursion, counting, probability, trees, graphs, analysis of algorithms, finite state autonoma.

ECE 366.title: CMOS VLSI Design
ECE 366.subject: ECE
ECE 366.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the design of very large scale integrated (VLSI) systems and use of CAD tools and design languages. Lab includes hands-on use of CAD tools and experiments with field programmable logic devices.

ECE 367.title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms
ECE 367.subject: ECE
ECE 367.description: Design and analysis of data structures and algorithms, including correctness and performance. Topics include time complexity, hash tables, sorting, search trees, self-balancing trees, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms.
ECE 367.prereq_raw: ( ECE 205 or ICS 212 ) and ( ECE 362 or ICS 241 ).

ECE 367L.title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms Lab
ECE 367L.subject: ECE
ECE 367L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 367 . Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

ECE 368.title: Cyber-Physical Systems and the Internet of Things
ECE 368.subject: ECE
ECE 368.description: Topics include General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO), serial communications, sensors, actuators, low-power wireless communications. TCP/IP networking, dynamic service discovery, distributed network messaging, machine-to-machine communication and cloud-computing interaction.

ECE 369.title: Computational Media Systems
ECE 369.subject: ECE
ECE 369.description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.
ECE 369.prereq_raw: ECE 160 or any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or instructor approval.
ECE 369.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

ECE 371.title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
ECE 371.subject: ECE
ECE 371.description: Transient and steady-state waves on transmission lines. Plane wave solutions of Maxwell’s equations. Application of Maxwell’s equations under static and time-varying conditions.

ECE 372.title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
ECE 372.subject: ECE
ECE 372.description: Solution of Maxwell’s equations under various boundary conditions. Introduction to radiation, guided waves, and principles of optics.
ECE 372.prereq_raw: ECE 371 and PHYS 274 (or concurrent); or consent.

ECE 372L.title: Engineering Electromagnetics Lab
ECE 372L.subject: ECE
ECE 372L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of electromagnetics and optics.
ECE 372L.prereq_raw: ECE 371 and PHYS 274 (or concurrent), or consent.

ECE 396.title: Junior Project
ECE 396.subject: ECE
ECE 396.description: Junior level individual or team project under EE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. It may be a continuation of ECE 296 or a new project.
ECE 396.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ECE 405.title: Introduction to Large-Scale Artificial Intelligence Systems
ECE 405.subject: ECE
ECE 405.description: Introduces large language models, focusing on practical aspects of building engineering systems with AI capabilities. Provides hands-on experience with the necessary tools for model development, deployment and integration.
ECE 405.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering, ICS, math, business, and economics majors only.

ECE 406.title: Introduction to Computer and Network Security
ECE 406.subject: ECE
ECE 406.description: Review basic network mechanisms, introduce basic cryptography concepts, and study algorithms and protocols used in computer and network security. Discuss practical security mechanisms.
ECE 406.prereq_raw: ECE 361 or ICS 312 or ICS 331 or instructor consent.

ECE 415.title: Digital Signal Processing
ECE 415.subject: ECE
ECE 415.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Discrete-time signals and systems, sampling, Z-transform, transform, transform analysis of linear time-invariant systems, filter design, discrete Fourier transform, and computation of discrete Fourier transform.
ECE 415.prereq_raw: ECE 315 and ECE 342 (or concurrent), or consent.

ECE 416.title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
ECE 416.subject: ECE
ECE 416.description: Digital image representation, intensity transformations, spatial filtering, filtering in the frequency domain, image restoration, color spaces and transformations, the fast wavelet transform, image compression.

ECE 417.title: Introduction to Optimization
ECE 417.subject: ECE
ECE 417.description: Application of linear, nonlinear and integer optimization models and algorithms to communications, control, signal processing, computer networking, financial engineering, manufacturing, production and distribution systems.
ECE 417.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CENG, EE, ME, or CBA majors only.

ECE 422.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
ECE 422.subject: ECE
ECE 422.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
ECE 422.prereq_raw: ( ECE 160 , ECE 211 , and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

ECE 423.title: Computer-Aided Analysis and Design
ECE 423.subject: ECE
ECE 423.description: Algorithms and techniques used in computer-aided analysis and design of electronic circuits. Circuit simulation with interactive computers.

ECE 425.title: Electronic Instrumentation II
ECE 425.subject: ECE
ECE 425.description: Instrumentation systems and circuits for measurement, control, signal processing, transmission, and detection. Noise and interference, ADC/DAC, modulation demodulation, high-frequency and high-speed techniques, IC applications.

ECE 426.title: Advanced Si IC and Solid State Devices
ECE 426.subject: ECE
ECE 426.description: State of the art Si-based devices including advanced bipolar and MOS devices, heterojunction devices, new device trends. Topics from the most current literature included.
ECE 426.prereq_raw: ECE 327 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A , or consent.

ECE 427.title: Computer-Aided Circuit Design
ECE 427.subject: ECE
ECE 427.description: Application of the computer to the analysis, design, simulation, and construction of analog and digital circuits.

ECE 435.title: Electric Power Systems
ECE 435.subject: ECE
ECE 435.description: Design/operation of “the grid.” History of electric power systems, three-phrase power, real and reactive power, transformers, transmission, distribution, circuit analysis, protection, load flow, load frequency control, optimal power flow, and renewable energy integration.

ECE 438.title: Renewable Energy
ECE 438.subject: ECE
ECE 438.description: Fundamentals of power, electric power grid and conventional electricity generation. Wind and solar power systems. Photovoltaic materials and systems. Distributed generation and energy storage.
ECE 438.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ECE 442.title: Digital Communications
ECE 442.subject: ECE
ECE 442.description: Baseband transmission, intersymbol interference and pulse shaping, partial response signaling, equalization, bandpass modulation and demodulation, channel coding, synchronization, multiplexing and multiple access, spread spectrum techniques.

ECE 445.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
ECE 445.subject: ECE
ECE 445.description: Foundation for algorithms, practice, and theory behind common machine-learning applications. Includes projects, statistical programming, and an introduction to the unique challenges of high-dimensional problems.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and MATH 307 ( or equivalent)

ECE 445.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE, CENG, CEE, ME, MATH, ICS majors only.

ECE 446.title: Information Theory and Coding
ECE 446.subject: ECE
ECE 446.description: Models of communication systems. Channel noise, measurement, and coding of information. Intrinsic limits of performance of communication systems.

ECE 449.title: Computer Communication Networks
ECE 449.subject: ECE
ECE 449.description: ISO Reference Model. Physical Layer, Data Link Layer, Network Layer and Transport Layer protocols. Wired and wireless local-area networks. Structure and operation of the Internet including routing, congestion control and flow control.
ECE 449.prereq_raw: ECE 315 and one of ECE 342 , or MATH 371 or MATH 471 ; or consent.

ECE 452.title: Digital Control Systems
ECE 452.subject: ECE
ECE 452.description: Sampling/reconstruction, Z-transform, DT transfer function. Reachability/observability. State and output feedback, observer design, input-output models, diophantine equations. Implementation procedures.

ECE 453.title: Modern Control Theory
ECE 453.subject: ECE
ECE 453.description: Analysis and synthesis of nonlinear control systems by means of Lagrange’s equation, state space techniques, maximum principle. Lyapunov’s theorems, the phase plane, and Z-transform techniques. Optimization and adaptation by means of gradient methods, calculus of variations, dynamic programming.

ECE 455.title: Design of Intelligent Robots
ECE 455.subject: ECE
ECE 455.description: Study of the design principles of computer-controlled, intelligent robots such as roving vehicles, hand-eye systems.

ECE 461.title: Computer Architecture
ECE 461.subject: ECE
ECE 461.description: Structure of stored program machines, data flow machines, pipelining, fault-tolerant computing, instruction set design, effects of compilation on architecture, RISC vs. CISC architecture, uses of parallelism.

ECE 467.title: Object-oriented Software Engineering
ECE 467.subject: ECE
ECE 467.description: Introduction to advanced techniques for designing, implementing, and testing computer software with a particular focus on using object-oriented design, analysis, and programming to produce high-quality computer programs that solve non-trivial problems.

ECE 468.title: Introduction to Operating Systems
ECE 468.subject: ECE
ECE 468.description: Computer system organization; multiprocessor systems, memory hierarchies, assemblers, compilers, operating systems, virtual machine, memory management, processor management; information management. Emphasis on written communication through written assignments on relevant topics.
ECE 468.prereq_raw: ECE 361 (or concurrent) and ECE 367 or consent.

ECE 469.title: Wireless Data Networks
ECE 469.subject: ECE
ECE 469.description: Mobile agent’s platforms and systems, mobile agent-based service implementation, middleware, and configuration, wireless local area networks, wireless protocols, network architecture supporting wireless applications, routing protocols in mobile and wireless networks, handoff in mobile and wireless networks.

ECE 470.title: Physical Optics
ECE 470.subject: ECE
ECE 470.description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
ECE 470.prereq_raw: ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-) or PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) or PHYS 450 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) , or consent

ECE 471.title: Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
ECE 471.subject: ECE
ECE 471.description: Introduction to computational methods used to simulate/solve engineering design problems focusing on electromagnetics. Finite difference, method of moments, and finite elements methods will be described; students will write computer programs in each.
ECE 471.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BE, CENG, EE, ENGR majors only.

ECE 473.title: Microwave Engineering
ECE 473.subject: ECE
ECE 473.description: Passive and active microwave devices and circuits for RF and wireless applications. Scattering parameters, signal-flow graphs, and computer-aided design.

ECE 474.title: Antennas
ECE 474.subject: ECE
ECE 474.description: Electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and ionized media. Geomagnetic and solar effects on the ionosphere. Absorption and dispersion. Antenna arrays, apertures, horns, impedance. Design of antenna systems.

ECE 475.title: Optical Communications
ECE 475.subject: ECE
ECE 475.description: Principles and applications of optical fibers and waveguides. Fundamentals of optical communication systems (optical links, high-speed systems, wavelength-division-multiplexing networks, and network elements) and optical components (guided-wave circuits, lasers, detectors, and optical amplifiers). System and network integration issues.

ECE 477.title: Fundamentals of Radar, Sonar, and Navigation Systems
ECE 477.subject: ECE
ECE 477.description: Discussion of basic radar detection and position- and velocity-measurement principles. Applications to various types of radar and sonar systems. Modern navigation aids.
ECE 477.prereq_raw: ECE 371 (or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory.

children.text: ( or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory

ECE 480.title: Introduction to Biomedical and Clinical Engineering
ECE 480.subject: ECE
ECE 480.description: Application of engineering principles and technology to biological and medical problems. Introduction to human anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, clinical measurements. Systems modeling, physiological control systems, computer applications, health-related problems.
ECE 480.prereq_raw: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A .

ECE 480L.title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
ECE 480L.subject: ECE
ECE 480L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Measurement of bioelectrical signals, computer and electronic simulation of biological systems, design and evaluation of electronic circuits for biomedical measurements, evaluation of instruments for patient safety.

ECE 481.title: Bioelectric Phenomena
ECE 481.subject: ECE
ECE 481.description: Study of electrical phenomena in living systems. Mechanisms underlying bioelectric activity. Membrane and transepithelial potentials, skin impedance, electrocardiography, neuroelectric signals, diagnostic considerations, laboratory demonstrations.

ECE 482.title: Biomedical Instrumentation
ECE 482.subject: ECE
ECE 482.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, applications, and design of biomedical instrumentation. Transducers, IC and microcomputer applications, patient safety.

ECE 491B.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering: artificial intelligence
ECE 491B.subject: ECE
ECE 491B.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty; to be oriented toward juniors and seniors. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (G) computer vision; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

(B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (G) computer vision; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

ECE 494.title: Provisional Topics
ECE 494.subject: ECE
ECE 494.description: Upper division course with subject matter to be announced.

ECE 495.title: Ethics in Electrical Engineering
ECE 495.subject: ECE
ECE 495.description: Equip electrical engineers with the necessary background for ethical reasoning, as it pertains to technology, society, workplace issues, and the environment.
ECE 495.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CENG and EE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

ECE 496.title: Capstone Design Project
ECE 496.subject: ECE
ECE 496.description: Significant project integrating multiple aspects of the design process: reliability, safety, economics, environment, social, ethics, teamwork. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral and written communication.

ECE 499.title: Directed Reading
ECE 499.subject: ECE
ECE 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

ECE 601.title: Graph Theory and Its Applications
ECE 601.subject: ECE
ECE 601.description: Graphs and subgraphs, trees and treelike graphs, planar graphs, connectivity and edge-connectivity, applications.

ECE 602.title: Algorithm I
ECE 602.subject: ECE
ECE 602.description: Design and evaluation of machine representations, techniques and algorithms for sorting, pattern processing, computational geometry, mathematical computations, and engineering applications. Introduction to computational issues of time, space, communication, and program correctness.

ECE 604.title: Artificial Intelligence
ECE 604.subject: ECE
ECE 604.description: LISP for machine intelligence applications, or related constraint object and logic-oriented languages.

ECE 605.title: Advanced Large-Scale Artificial Intelligence Systems
ECE 605.subject: ECE
ECE 605.description: Explains the technical challenges of developing, deploying, and using large language models. Equips students with the skills to conduct AI research in academia or industry, emphasizing advanced techniques, rigorous evaluation, and ethical considerations in applications.
ECE 605.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering, ICS, math, business, and economics majors only.

ECE 606.title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
ECE 606.subject: ECE
ECE 606.description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
ECE 606.prereq_raw: ECE 467 or ICS 313 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent

ECE 607.title: Advanced Network Algorithms
ECE 607.subject: ECE
ECE 607.description: Network algorithms, protocols, and packet switching systems for the internet including TCP/IP, routing algorithms, transmission scheduling, link management, buffer management, and simple network management.

ECE 608.title: Optical Networks
ECE 608.subject: ECE
ECE 608.description: Propagation of signals in fibers, components, modulation and demodulation, transmission system engineering, network systems and architectures, network design, control and management and packet switching.
ECE 608.prereq_raw: ECE 342 , ECE 367 , and ECE 371 ; or consent.

ECE 609.title: Computer and Network Security
ECE 609.subject: ECE
ECE 609.description: Basic security theory, current practices, and emerging research issues. First covering the fundamentals of computer and network security, then will work on research projects on computer and network security.

ECE 615.title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing
ECE 615.subject: ECE
ECE 615.description: An advanced course in digital processing. Topics include fast DFT algorithms, multirate systems and filter banks, power spectrum estimation, linear prediction, optimum linear filters, and adaptive filtering.

ECE 616.title: Digital Image Processing
ECE 616.subject: ECE
ECE 616.description: Human visual perception, image formation, sampling and quantization, enhancement and restoration, color image processing, wavelets and multiresolution representations, image and video compression.

ECE 617.title: Linear and Convex Optimization
ECE 617.subject: ECE
ECE 617.description: Algorithms for linear, nonlinear, and convex optimization. Emphasis is on methodology and the underlying mathematical structures. Topics include simplex method, network flow methods, optimality conditions, duality, Newton’s method and interior point methods.
ECE 617.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, ME, MIS and MATH majors only.

ECE 618.title: Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control
ECE 618.subject: ECE
ECE 618.description: Sequential decision-making via dynamic programming. Optimal control of stochastic dynamic systems. Applications in linear-quadratic control, inventory control, resource allocation, scheduling, and control of queues. Rollout and other suboptimal methods. Value and policy iteration.
ECE 618.prereq_raw: ECE 342 or MATH 371 or MATH 471 , or consent.

ECE 620.title: Advanced Electronic Circuits
ECE 620.subject: ECE
ECE 620.description: Electronic circuits for precision measurement, computation, and signal processing. Low noise and interference reduction techniques. High-frequency and high-speed techniques. Micro-processor and biomedical applications.

ECE 621.title: Advanced Solid-State Devices
ECE 621.subject: ECE
ECE 621.description: Advanced physical principles and design of modern solid-state electronic devices. Heterostructures, photodetectors, LED, junction lasers, and other devices of current importance identified from the current literature.

ECE 622.title: Optical Electronics I
ECE 622.subject: ECE
ECE 622.description: Fundamentals of optical radiation, including stimulated and spontaneous processes. Optical electronics including optical resonators, lasers, optical detectors, light-guiding, and applications.

ECE 623.title: Optical Electronics II
ECE 623.subject: ECE
ECE 623.description: Electro-optics, noise detection, light and sound dielectric waveguide phenomena, lasers, optics, phase conjugation.

ECE 624.title: Microsensors and Microactuators I
ECE 624.subject: ECE
ECE 624.description: Technology methods and physical principles of microsensors and microactuators. Vacuum technology, thin film deposition and characterization techniques, solid mechanics, micromachining, acoustics, piezoelectricity and principles of current microtransducers.

ECE 626.title: Rapid Prototyping of Electrophysical Devices
ECE 626.subject: ECE
ECE 626.description: Hands on experience in designing, fabricating, testing, and iterating according to rapid-prototyping principles. Students learn state-of-the-art equipment for making their designs, software for simulating designs, and working in design teams.
ECE 626.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ECE 627.title: Advanced Topics in Physical Electronics
ECE 627.subject: ECE
ECE 627.description: Recent developments in phenomena and devices of physical electronics.

ECE 628.title: Analysis and Design of Integrated Circuits
ECE 628.subject: ECE
ECE 628.description: Fabrication constraints and design guidelines for integrated circuits. Nonlinear model of integrated circuit transistor. Design and analysis of integrated logic circuits and linear circuits.

ECE 635.title: Smart Grids and Renewable Energy Integration
ECE 635.subject: ECE
ECE 635.description: Challenges and solutions for integrating intermittent renewable energy sources into the power system, with a focus on “smart grid” approaches and demand-response. Using linear programming and other modeling techniques to answer policy-relevant questions.
ECE 635.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ECE 640.title: Applied Random Processes
ECE 640.subject: ECE
ECE 640.description: Random variables, multivariate distributions, random sequences, stochastic convergence, stationary and nonstationary processes, spectral analysis, Karhunen-Loeve expansion, Markov processes, mean square estimation, Kalman filters.

ECE 641.title: Queueing Theory
ECE 641.subject: ECE
ECE 641.description: Poisson, Markov, and renewal processes, M/G/1 queue, G/M/1 queue, queueing networks, simulation, and performance evaluation of computer systems and communication networks.
ECE 641.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, ICS, MATH majors only.

ECE 642.title: Detection and Estimation Theory
ECE 642.subject: ECE
ECE 642.description: Fundamentals of signal detection and estimation theory. Hypothesis testing, parametric and nonparametric detection, sequential detection, parametric estimation, linear estimation, robust detection and estimation, and applications to communication systems.

ECE 643.title: Communication System Performance
ECE 643.subject: ECE
ECE 643.description: Fundamental performance limits, signal detection and estimation, modulation, intersymbol interference, equalization adaptive filtering, sequence detection, synchronization, fading multipath channels, spread spectrum.

ECE 644.title: Computer Communication Networks
ECE 644.subject: ECE
ECE 644.description: Fundamentals of computer communication networks including modeling, performance evaluation, routing, flow control, local area networks, distributed algorithms, and optimization algorithms.

ECE 645.title: Machine Learning
ECE 645.subject: ECE
ECE 645.description: Learning theory, pattern recognition and regression; gradient based algorithms and least square algorithms; Kernel methods; Bayesian learning algorithms; ensemble learning and boosting; principal component analysis; independent component analysis, and clustering; reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming.
ECE 645.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, ME, ICS, MATH majors only.

ECE 646.title: Advanced Information Theory
ECE 646.subject: ECE
ECE 646.description: Measure of information, coding for discrete sources, discrete memoryless channels and capacity, the noisy channel coding theorem, source coding with fidelity criterion, rate-distortion theory, multiuser channels.

ECE 647.title: Source Coding
ECE 647.subject: ECE
ECE 647.description: Theory and applications of source coding, rate-distortion theory, companding, lattice coding, tree coding, trellis coding, entropy-constrained coding, asymptotic theory, predictive and differential encoding, combined source/channel coding, vector quantization.

ECE 648.title: Error-Control Coding I
ECE 648.subject: ECE
ECE 648.description: Linear block codes, soft and hard decision decodings, correction of random errors, cyclic codes, BCH codes, Reed-Solomon codes, majority logic decodable codes, burst-error correcting codes, concatenated codes.

ECE 649.title: Error-Control Coding II
ECE 649.subject: ECE
ECE 649.description: Convolutional codes, Viterbi algorithm, coded modulation, multistage decoding, concatenated coded modulation, probabilistic decoding, turbo codes, low density parity check codes and iterative decoding.

ECE 650.title: Linear System Theory
ECE 650.subject: ECE
ECE 650.description: State space theory of linear systems, controllability, observability, stability, irreducible realizations.

ECE 651.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
ECE 651.subject: ECE
ECE 651.description: Digital simulations, phase-plane analysis, limit cycles and amplitude bounds, Lyapunov’s theorem, circle criterion of stability, lure systems, Popov’s stability theorem.

ECE 652.title: Optimal Control Systems
ECE 652.subject: ECE
ECE 652.description: Optimal controls introduced through parametric optimization, calculus of variations, Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton-Jacobi equations, Pontryagin’s maximum principle, minimum-time and minimum-fuel problems, dynamic programming, applications.

ECE 655.title: Robust Control
ECE 655.subject: ECE
ECE 655.description: Multivariable frequency response design, signals and systems, linear fractional transformations, LQG Control, Full Information H-infinity Controller Synthesis, H-infinity filtering, model reduction, the four-block problem.

ECE 660.title: Computer Architecture I
ECE 660.subject: ECE
ECE 660.description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.
ECE 660.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CECE, ECE, and ME majors only.

ECE 665.title: Computer Systems
ECE 665.subject: ECE
ECE 665.description: Modern operating system software, process communication, distributed systems, device drivers. Software development and maintenance, integration of software packages. Projects reflecting special interests of faculty.

ECE 668.title: Telecommunication Networks
ECE 668.subject: ECE
ECE 668.description: Telecommunication-network architecture; switching, broadcast, and wireless networks; protocols, interfaces, routing, flow- and congestion-control techniques; intelligent network architecture; service creation capabilities; multimedia, voice, data, and video networks and services.

ECE 669.title: Wireless and Mobile Security
ECE 669.subject: ECE
ECE 669.description: Security and privacy design principles and application in wireless and mobile devices, networks, and services, as well as research methodology in wireless and mobile security.

ECE 671.title: Electromagnetic Theory and Applications
ECE 671.subject: ECE
ECE 671.description: Solutions of Maxwell’s equations and applications to radiation and propagation of electromagnetic waves.

ECE 673.title: Advanced Microwave Engineering
ECE 673.subject: ECE
ECE 673.description: Advanced RF and microwave circuit design for wireless applications.

ECE 675.title: Advanced Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
ECE 675.subject: ECE
ECE 675.description: Develop comprehensive understanding of computations techniques for solving engineering electromagnetic problems formulated in terms of integral or differential equations. Eigenvalue problems, radiation, and electromagnetics scattering problems will be discussed and computer programming is required.
ECE 675.prereq_raw: ECE 471 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.
ECE 675.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, BE, and CENG majors only.

ECE 680.title: Biomedical Engineering Systems
ECE 680.subject: ECE
ECE 680.description: Systems analysis and electronic instrumentation methods in biomedicine. Network and control-loop modeling, computer simulation, biological transducers, and analysis of electronic and physiological systems.
ECE 680.prereq_raw: ECE 326 , ECE 326L , and ECE 371 ; or consent.

ECE 681.title: Biosensors and Bioelectronics
ECE 681.subject: ECE
ECE 681.description: Advanced topics in the design of biological detection technologies. Topics include fundamentals of electrochemistry, electrochemical biosensors, DNA and protein biochips, and bioelectronics for bio-signal conditioning and processing.

ECE 682.title: Biomedical Microdevices
ECE 682.subject: ECE
ECE 682.description: Design and fabrication of micro- and nanodevices for biomedical applications. Topics include micro- and nanoscale physics, microfluidic physics and microfluidic devices, and micro- and nanoscale fabrication techniques.

ECE 685.title: Biomedical Signal Processing and Analysis
ECE 685.subject: ECE
ECE 685.description: Biomedical signals, digital filters and filter banks, spike train analysis, time-scale and time-frequency representations, nonlinear techniques, Lomb’s algorithm and the Hilbert transform, modeling, Volterra series, Wiener series, Poisson-Wiener series, multichannel data, causality.
ECE 685.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, ECE, ME, ICS majors only and any graduate student in JABSOM who has a suitable technical background.

ECE 693B.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering: artificial intelligence
ECE 693B.subject: ECE
ECE 693B.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

ECE 693C.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering: circuits
ECE 693C.subject: ECE
ECE 693C.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

ECE 693H.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering: control
ECE 693H.subject: ECE
ECE 693H.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

ECE 693I.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

ECE 693J.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.
