ECE 693K.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

ECE 699.title: Directed Reading or Research
ECE 699.subject: ECE
ECE 699.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

ECE 700.title: Thesis Research
ECE 700.subject: ECE
ECE 700.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for MS in electrical and computer engineering.

ECE 790.title: Directed Instruction
ECE 790.subject: ECE
ECE 790.description: Student assists in classroom instruction under direction and close supervision of faculty member.

ECE 800.title: Dissertation Research
ECE 800.subject: ECE
ECE 800.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD in electrical and computer engineering.

ECON 120.title: Introduction to Economics
ECON 120.subject: ECON
ECON 120.description: One-semester survey of the principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics to enable students in all disciplines to understand current economic events.

ECON 130.title: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON 130.subject: ECON
ECON 130.description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

ECON 130A.title: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON 130A.subject: ECON
ECON 130A.description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

ECON 131.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON 131.subject: ECON
ECON 131.description: An introduction to macroeconomics-the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

ECON 131A.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON 131A.subject: ECON
ECON 131A.description: An introduction to macroeconomics-the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

ECON 256.title: Data Analysis and Visualization
ECON 256.subject: ECON
ECON 256.description: Develops basic techniques of data analysis and visualization. Introduces sources of economic data; methods of preparing data from various file/data formats for analysis; methods of visualization: bubble plots, scatterplot matrices, heatmaps, hexbins, rug plots, etc.

ECON 300.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
ECON 300.subject: ECON
ECON 300.description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts used to study the overall macroeconomy and policies that affect it. Study the determinants of national income and long-run growth; causes and consequences of unemployment, inflation, and business cycle fluctuations; determination of foreign exchange rates and current account imbalances, and the role of government policy in various settings.

ECON 301.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
ECON 301.subject: ECON
ECON 301.description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory. Learn to use economic reasoning to understand the social consequences of decisions made by individual consumers, producers, and governments. Analyze the nature of market outcomes under alternative market structures, and further discuss possible welfare-improving government policies when markets fail to be efficient. Special attention is paid to the analysis of strategic behavior and markets with public goods and externalities.

ECON 311.title: The Economy of Hawaiʻi
ECON 311.subject: ECON
ECON 311.description: Descriptive understanding of the history of development of Hawaiʻi’s economy; current economic problems; future prospects. Emphasizes the written communication of the intuition behind economic concepts in practice in Hawaiʻi.
ECON 311.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 317.title: The Japanese Economy
ECON 317.subject: ECON
ECON 317.description: Analysis of Japan’s growth past and present. Does Japan’s economy look different in terms of its international trade structure, industrial structure, labor market, savings patterns, government policies, etc.? Does it matter?

ECON 320.title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
ECON 320.subject: ECON
ECON 320.description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.
ECON 320.prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 ; consent.

ECON 321.title: Introduction to Statistics
ECON 321.subject: ECON
ECON 321.description: Basic elements; descriptive statistics, probability, inference, distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and correlation analysis.

ECON 332.title: Economics of Global Climate Change
ECON 332.subject: ECON
ECON 332.description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
ECON 332.prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 , or consent.

ECON 336.title: Energy Economics and Policy
ECON 336.subject: ECON
ECON 336.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

ECON 340.title: Financial Markets and Institutions
ECON 340.subject: ECON
ECON 340.description: The determination of asset prices; the risk and term structure of interest rates; efficient markets hypothesis; risk management and financial derivatives, asymmetric information models of financial market structure, innovation, regulation and deregulation; and financial crises.
ECON 340.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 341.title: Comparative Economic History
ECON 341.subject: ECON
ECON 341.description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

ECON 342.title: The History of Economic Thought
ECON 342.subject: ECON
ECON 342.description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy.

ECON 350.title: Sustainable Development
ECON 350.subject: ECON
ECON 350.description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawaiʻi. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.
ECON 350.prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 , or consent.

ECON 355.title: Network Economics
ECON 355.subject: ECON
ECON 355.description: Fundamental questions about the connections in the social, economic, and technological worlds. Topics include: matching markets, traffic, financial and social networks; and the political and economic consequences of the internet and other large networks.

ECON 356.title: Games and Economic Behavior
ECON 356.subject: ECON
ECON 356.description: Introduces students to the study of strategic behavior with applications to economics, business, and public policy. Simple economic models of strategic decision making are used to analyze provision of public goods; competition, cooperation, and coordination among firms; bargaining between employers and labor unions; international trade negotiations; reputation as a competitive advantage, and others.
ECON 356.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 358.title: Environmental Economics
ECON 358.subject: ECON
ECON 358.description: Nature and causes of environmental degradation/economic solutions, with emphasis on relevant ethical issues and decision-making. Topics include air and water pollution, toxic waste, deforestation, soil erosion, biodiversity, global warming, and sustainable development.
ECON 358.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 361.title: Seminar: Women and International Development
ECON 361.subject: ECON
ECON 361.description: Topics: Women’s role, status, work and treatment; ethical considerations of economic development, changing work/family roles, agriculture and business, improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World global feminization of poverty.
ECON 361.prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent.

ECON 362.title: Trade Policy and Globalization
ECON 362.subject: ECON
ECON 362.description: Political economy of the world trading system. Case studies of trade cooperation and conflict under the World Trade Organization and other institutions. Future challenges, including investment policies, environmental and labor standards.
ECON 362.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 390.title: Internship for Economics
ECON 390.subject: ECON
ECON 390.description: Economics majors and minors work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. Students combine academic work with practical experience.

ECON 391.title: Cooperative Education
ECON 391.subject: ECON
ECON 391.description: Economics majors and minors, under the supervision of faculty members, work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. The Econ
ECON 391.coreq_raw: Co-op integrates academics with practical work experience.

ECON 396.title: Contemporary Topics in Economics
ECON 396.subject: ECON
ECON 396.description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester.

ECON 399.title: Directed Reading
ECON 399.subject: ECON
ECON 399.description: Economics majors and minors participate in faculty supervised reading of economic literature. Enables students to self-study topics not covered in the department’s scheduled course offerings.

ECON 409.title: The Ocean Economy
ECON 409.subject: ECON
ECON 409.description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

ECON 412.title: Economic History of the United States
ECON 412.subject: ECON
ECON 412.description: U.S. economy from colonial times: government policies, institutions, industries, financial markets, economic growth, economic crises.
ECON 412.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 414.title: Global Economic Crisis and Recovery
ECON 414.subject: ECON
ECON 414.description: Causes and consequences of financial and economic crises: crisis origins and global transmission; macroeconomic and regulatory policy responses; recovery challenges.
ECON 414.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 or consent.

ECON 415.title: Asian Economic Development
ECON 415.subject: ECON
ECON 415.description: History and economic development. Resources, population, and income, saving, investment, and consumption patterns. Role of government and private enterprise.
ECON 415.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 416.title: The Chinese Economy
ECON 416.subject: ECON
ECON 416.description: The Chinese economy during the imperial and republican periods, under Mao, and into the present reform era, with a brief comparison to Taiwan and Hong Kong.
ECON 416.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 418.title: Pacific Island Economies
ECON 418.subject: ECON
ECON 418.description: Historical and current economic development of the Pacific islands (excluding Hawaiʻi). Analysis of selected economic issues such as tourism, population growth, etc.
ECON 418.prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

ECON 420.title: Mathematical Economics
ECON 420.subject: ECON
ECON 420.description: Mathematical techniques applied to theories of the consumer, the firm, markets. Linear programming, inputoutput analysis.
ECON 420.prereq_raw: ECON 300 , ECON 301 ; MATH 203 , MATH 215 , MATH 241 , or MATH 251A .

ECON 425.title: Introduction to Econometrics I: Data Exploration and Regression Analysis
ECON 425.subject: ECON
ECON 425.description: Types of data, exploratory data analysis, generalizing from random samples, simple and multivariate regression, non-linear relationships, measurement error, extreme values, weights, correlated and heteroskedastic errors, instrumental variables, models for binary or discrete dependent variables.
ECON 425.prereq_raw: ECON 321 or MATH 241 or BUS 310 or NREM 310 or ( MATH 251A and NREM 203 ) or ( MATH 371 and MATH 373 ) or ( MATH 471 and MATH 472 ); or consent.

ECON 427.title: Introduction to Econometrics II: Prediction and Causal Inference
ECON 427.subject: ECON
ECON 427.description: Prediction types, error measures, training and test data, cross validation, machine learning, regression trees, random forests, boosting, classification, forecasting time series, modelbased versus design-based causality, potential outcomes framework, matching, difference-in-differences, panel data, synthetic controls.
ECON 427.prereq_raw: ECON 425 (with a minimum grade of B- or better).

ECON 429.title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
ECON 429.subject: ECON
ECON 429.description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
ECON 429.prereq_raw: ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and ECON 321 or NREM 310 ; or consent.

ECON 430.title: Labor Economics
ECON 430.subject: ECON
ECON 430.description: Economic analysis of labor market. Investment in human capital, education, health, migration, etc.

ECON 432.title: Economics of Population
ECON 432.subject: ECON
ECON 432.description: Determinants and consequences of growth and structure of human populations. Relationships between economic factors and fertility, population growth and economic growth.

ECON 434.title: Health Economics
ECON 434.subject: ECON
ECON 434.description: Private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; efficient production and utilization of services; models of hospital and physician behavior; optimal public policy.

ECON 440.title: Monetary Theory and Policy
ECON 440.subject: ECON
ECON 440.description: Microfoundations and critical analysis of monetary and macroeconomic theory and policy. Topics include the causes and consequences of inflation, optimal monetary policy and international monetary systems, bank risk and insurance, and national debt and taxation.

ECON 442.title: Development Economics
ECON 442.subject: ECON
ECON 442.description: Theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for analyzing key issues facing today’s developing world. Topics include characteristics of underdeveloped economies, economic growth, structural change, poverty, inequality, education, population growth, foreign aid and financial sector.

ECON 444.title: Economics of Happiness
ECON 444.subject: ECON
ECON 444.description: Topics covered include: measuring happiness, what individual and country characteristics contribute to individual well-being, what are the consequences of happiness on behavior, and whether happiness is a cause or an effect.

ECON 445.title: Health in Developing Economies
ECON 445.subject: ECON
ECON 445.description: Theoretical and analytical tools from economics to study (1) the relationship between health and economic development and (2) the determinants of health improvement in developing economies.
ECON 445.prereq_raw: ECON 321 (or concurrent) and ECON 301 , or consent.

ECON 450.title: Public Economics
ECON 450.subject: ECON
ECON 450.description: Welfare economics, public expenditure and policy evaluation, public finance by debt and taxes.

ECON 452.title: State and Local Finance
ECON 452.subject: ECON
ECON 452.description: Fiscal institutions, operations, and policy questions within state and local governments in U.S. grant programs and other links with central government.

ECON 458.title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
ECON 458.subject: ECON
ECON 458.description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

ECON 460.title: International Trade and Welfare
ECON 460.subject: ECON
ECON 460.description: Theory of international specialization and exchange; general equilibrium, tariffs, quotas, common markets.

ECON 461.title: International Macroeconomics
ECON 461.subject: ECON
ECON 461.description: The determination of output, price levels, exchange rates and the balance of payments for economies that are integrated with the global economy; theory and application to historical and/or contemporary policy issues.

ECON 470.title: Industrial Organization
ECON 470.subject: ECON
ECON 470.description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of contemporary topics in industrial organization. Uses economic theory to analyze important issues facing firms, and examines the practical challenges of empirical applications of theory.

ECON 476.title: Law and Economics
ECON 476.subject: ECON
ECON 476.description: Legal issues of property rights, contracts, torts, and crime. Efficiency of U.S. legal process. Economics of law enforcement, juries, prosecutors; evolution of legal rules.

ECON 495.title: Land and Housing Economics
ECON 495.subject: ECON
ECON 495.description: Microeconomics explains urban land and housing phenomena, and analyzes selected land and housing issues relevant to Honolulu.

ECON 496.title: Contemporary Economic Issues
ECON 496.subject: ECON
ECON 496.description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester, e.g., environmental pollution, crime control, racial discrimination, traffic congestion.

ECON 499.title: Advanced Directed Research
ECON 499.subject: ECON
ECON 499.description: Economics majors and minors conduct research, under faculty supervision, on a topic of their choice.
ECON 499.prereq_raw: minimum GPA of 3.0 in economics and consent.

ECON 604.title: Microeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
ECON 604.subject: ECON
ECON 604.description: Theory of the consumer, firm, and market. Perfect competition and efficiency. Market power and firm strategy. Market efficiencies. Role of the government.

ECON 605.title: Macroeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
ECON 605.subject: ECON
ECON 605.description: Topics on production, consumption, labor market, asset market, economic growth, and business cycles are discussed with emphasis on real-economy applications and policy analysis. Implications of monetary, fiscal, and international finance and economic policies are explored.

ECON 606.title: Microeconomic Theory I
ECON 606.subject: ECON
ECON 606.description: Theory of the firm: production, costs, duality; theory of the market: competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition; theory of the consumer: preferences, expenditures, duality; expected utility theory.

ECON 607.title: Macroeconomic Theory I
ECON 607.subject: ECON
ECON 607.description: Neoclassical theory of real and monetary equilibrium, economics of J. M. Keynes, standard IS/LM models and aggregate demand/supply analysis in the closed and open economy, theory of rational expectations.

ECON 608.title: Microeconomic Theory II
ECON 608.subject: ECON
ECON 608.description: General equilibrium analysis: production, consumption and Walrasian equilibria; Pareto efficiency, fundamental theorems of welfare economics; externalities; public goods; game theory; information theory.

ECON 609.title: Macroeconomic Theory II
ECON 609.subject: ECON
ECON 609.description: Models of economic growth and fluctuations; stochastic and dynamic macroeconomic models; econometric testing of rational expectations models; theory of public debt; current topics in macroeconomic theory.

ECON 610.title: Economic Development
ECON 610.subject: ECON
ECON 610.description: Nature and causes of economic growth and structural change. Roles of macroeconomic policy and foreign trade.

ECON 611.title: Economic Development Policy
ECON 611.subject: ECON
ECON 611.description: Analysis of policies for the promotion of industrial and agricultural development. Project evaluation, industrial regulation, public administration, investment and capital market policies, land-use policies, trade policies, pricing, and stabilization.

ECON 614.title: Economic Development of Japan
ECON 614.subject: ECON
ECON 614.description: Analysis of growth from Meiji period to present. Problems of population change, capital formation, income distribution, industrial structure.

ECON 620.title: Microeconomic Theory III
ECON 620.subject: ECON
ECON 620.description: Game theory and strategic behavior. Economics of information and incentives principal-agent theory. Economic design. Applications include: theory of contracts; incentive compatible mechanism for provision of public goods; auction theory.

ECON 621.title: Macroeconomic Theory III
ECON 621.subject: ECON
ECON 621.description: Will equip students with the ability to understand, undertake, and critically evaluate theoretical and quantitative research in modern macroeconomics with a focus on the application of the search and matching methodology.

ECON 627.title: Mathematics for Economics
ECON 627.subject: ECON
ECON 627.description: Sets, functions, limits, convexity, continuity; constrained and unconstrained optimization; difference and differential equations; matrix algebra; simultaneous equations; comparative statics; Kuhn-Tucker theory; game theory; mathematical programming.

ECON 628.title: Econometrics I
ECON 628.subject: ECON
ECON 628.description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.

ECON 629.title: Econometrics II
ECON 629.subject: ECON
ECON 629.description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference and forecasting of econometric models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

ECON 630.title: Econometrics III
ECON 630.subject: ECON
ECON 630.description: Will equip students with the ability to undertake, understand, and critically assess empirical research using state-of-the-at econometric methods.

ECON 635.title: Disasters and Economic Policy
ECON 635.subject: ECON
ECON 635.description: Economic analysis of disasters. The economics of prevention and mitigation, as well as post-disaster economic consequences and policy, will be examined.
ECON 635.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ECON 636.title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
ECON 636.subject: ECON
ECON 636.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
ECON 636.prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent.

ECON 637.title: Resource Economics
ECON 637.subject: ECON
ECON 637.description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

ECON 638.title: Environmental Resource Economics
ECON 638.subject: ECON
ECON 638.description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

ECON 639.title: Marine Resource Economics
ECON 639.subject: ECON
ECON 639.description: Seminar on the economics of the marine environment. Topics include fisheries management, ocean recreation, shipping, and coral reef protection.

ECON 650.title: Foundations of Public Policy
ECON 650.subject: ECON
ECON 650.description: Microeconomic principles for expenditure and tax policies. Externalities, public goods, non-convexities, regulation; cost-benefit analysis, general equilibrium, shadow-pricing; rent-seeking, corruption; optimal taxation, incidence, excess burden; dynamic public finance, national debt, social security.

ECON 651.title: Public Economics
ECON 651.subject: ECON
ECON 651.description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of public-sector allocation. Adverse selection, moral hazard, networks, auctions, public choice and political mechanisms; tax and mandate incidence; economics of education and local public goods; social insurance programs.

ECON 660.title: International Trade and Welfare
ECON 660.subject: ECON
ECON 660.description: Classical and new theories of international trade: why nations trade, gains from trade, patterns of trade, and trade policy effects under perfect and imperfect competition. Empirical trade and other special topics.

ECON 661.title: Advanced International Trade and Investment
ECON 661.subject: ECON
ECON 661.description: Surveys theoretical and empirical research on topics such as regionalism and multilateralism, trade and wages, foreign direct investment and multinational firms, trade and the environment, and trade and economic growth.

ECON 662.title: International Macroeconomics
ECON 662.subject: ECON
ECON 662.description: Advanced international monetary and macroeconomic theory: balance of payments, output, price and exchange rate determination, international aspects of growth and economic fluctuations, alternative exchange rate regimes, international capital flows.

ECON 664.title: Applied International Finance
ECON 664.subject: ECON
ECON 664.description: Surveys empirical research in international macroeconomics, finance and econometric methods: including balance of payments adjustment, international equilibrium, international prices, interest rates and exchange rates, models of exchange rate determination, capital flows, balance of payments crises.
ECON 664.prereq_raw: ECON 607 and ECON 629 (or concurrent), or consent.

ECON 670.title: Labor Economics and Policy
ECON 670.subject: ECON
ECON 670.description: Supply of and demand for labor; implications for labor markets and unemployment level.

ECON 672.title: Economics of Population
ECON 672.subject: ECON
ECON 672.description: Economic determinants and consequences of population change.

ECON 674.title: Health Economics and Policy
ECON 674.subject: ECON
ECON 674.description: Economic analysis of health-care policy; efficient design of health-care financing schemes; private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; provider behavior.
ECON 674.prereq_raw: ECON 604 (or concurrent) or ECON 606 (or concurrent), or consent.

ECON 686.title: Strategic Behavior and Experimental Economics
ECON 686.subject: ECON
ECON 686.description: Experimental economics: methodology. Experimental game theory. Market experiments. Applications include: topics in industrial organization, provision of public goods, asset markets, auctions.

ECON 696.title: Advanced Topics in Economics
ECON 696.subject: ECON
ECON 696.description: Reflects interests of visiting and permanent faculty, focusing on specialized methods or topics in economics.

ECON 730.title: Research Seminar
ECON 730.subject: ECON
ECON 730.description: Selected issues emphasizing research techniques. Required for students who have passed the two theory qualifying exams and have not passed the comprehensive exam.

ECON 732.title: MA Capstone Research
ECON 732.subject: ECON
ECON 732.description: Student applies theoretical and quantitative techniques, critical thinking, and communicative skills to prepare a written and oral presentation of original research on a topic of his or her choice.
ECON 732.prereq_raw: ECON 606 , ECON 607 , ECON 627 , ECON 628 , and consent of graduate chair.

EDCS 415.title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years)
EDCS 415.subject: EDCS
EDCS 415.description: Emphasizes interrelated historical and philosophical roots and socio-cultural context and their influence on policy and practice in early childhood education settings.

EDCS 415L.title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years) Lab
EDCS 415L.subject: EDCS
EDCS 415L.description: Direct experience with children in early childhood settings in order to apply concepts from EDCS 415 and gain perspective on the role of the practitioner in ECE settings.

EDCS 416.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
EDCS 416.subject: EDCS
EDCS 416.description: Continuation of STE 415 : focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children.

EDCS 416L.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
EDCS 416L.subject: EDCS

EDCS 417.title: STEM Pedagogy
EDCS 417.subject: EDCS
EDCS 417.description: Introduction to STEM education pedagogy with emphasis on ethical issues and effective oral communication. Designed to integrate educational theory, pedagogy, content, and practical concerns into teaching practices in the STEM fields.

EDCS 431.title: Collaborative Language and Learning
EDCS 431.subject: EDCS
EDCS 431.description: Examination of language (talking, reading, and writing) processes within a collaborative teaching framework in the secondary curriculum. Field experience may be required.

EDCS 432.title: Adolescent Literature and Literacy
EDCS 432.subject: EDCS
EDCS 432.description: Selection and interpretation of young adult literature, including multicultural literature for middle level and high school students. Theory and teaching strategies for integrating literacy instruction in the literature program for diverse student populations.

EDCS 433.title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
EDCS 433.subject: EDCS
EDCS 433.description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

EDCS 440.title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education
EDCS 440.subject: EDCS
EDCS 440.description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawaiʻi as our place of learning and teaching.

EDCS 450.title: Methods and Materials in Science
EDCS 450.subject: EDCS
EDCS 450.description: Selecting and using methods and materials, demonstrations and simulations, open-ended experimentation, inquiry and discovery, task analysis measurement tools and techniques, activities from various curricula, opportunity for individualized goals and projects.
EDCS 450.prereq_raw: STE 323 , STE 404H , teaching experience; or consent.

EDCS 451.title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
EDCS 451.subject: EDCS
EDCS 451.description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers, including criteria for evaluation and planning.
EDCS 451.prereq_raw: ( HDFS 230 (or concurrent), HDFS 331 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent.

EDCS 453.title: Gender Issues in Education
EDCS 453.subject: EDCS
EDCS 453.description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper.

EDCS 480.title: Issues in Computer Education
EDCS 480.subject: EDCS
EDCS 480.description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

EDCS 494.title: Problem Solving in Mathematics Education
EDCS 494.subject: EDCS
EDCS 494.description: Experiencing and learning to teach heuristics of solving mathematical problems; designing curricula, classroom organization, evaluative measures for problem solving.

EDCS 495.title: Difficulties in Learning Mathematics
EDCS 495.subject: EDCS
EDCS 495.description: Identification, analysis, and remediation of difficulties in learning mathematics.

EDCS 600.title: Language, Learning and Teaching
EDCS 600.subject: EDCS
EDCS 600.description: Examines the role that language plays in the social construction of knowledge within various disciplines, K-adult. Collaborative group learning strategies will be modeled.
EDCS 600.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

EDCS 601.title: Advanced Topics in Reading
EDCS 601.subject: EDCS
EDCS 601.description: Current theories and teaching strategies of reading throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Topics include psychological, sociological, and cultural foundations of reading; 21st century literacies; emergent literacy; diversity; multilingual learners, formative assessment; state/national initiatives.
EDCS 601.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

EDCS 602.title: Advanced Topics in Writing and Oral Language
EDCS 602.subject: EDCS
EDCS 602.description: Current theories and teaching strategies of writing and oral language throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Focus on teaching writing and oral language as tools for learning and to demonstrate learning.
EDCS 602.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

EDCS 603.title: Children’s Literature in the Elementary Curriculum
EDCS 603.subject: EDCS
EDCS 603.description: In-depth examination of traditional and current books/media, birth through young adult, with emphasis on applications in schools or other educational contexts. Focus on use of narrative, exposition, and other genres across the curriculum.
EDCS 603.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

EDCS 604.title: Effective Writing Practices
EDCS 604.subject: EDCS
EDCS 604.description: Analysis and practical application of principles and strategies of effective writing and informed writing instruction in K-12 classrooms.

EDCS 605.title: Literacy Coaching and Leadership
EDCS 605.subject: EDCS
EDCS 605.description: Exploration and application of literacy specialist roles. Includes teaching, coaching, providing resources, advocating for all students, and collaborating with other professionals.

EDCS 606.title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
EDCS 606.subject: EDCS
EDCS 606.description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, action research, mixed methods, and curriculum based assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/ Thesis proposal.

EDCS 607.title: New Literacies Leadership
EDCS 607.subject: EDCS
EDCS 607.description: New approaches to analyzing 21st century literacies K-12, including visual, media, digital, and critical literacies as well as developing leadership practices in multi-literacies pedagogy.

EDCS 608.title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
EDCS 608.subject: EDCS
EDCS 608.description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts.
EDCS 608.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

EDCS 610.title: Early Career Teaching, K-12
EDCS 610.subject: EDCS
EDCS 610.description: Focuses on research and practice related to the first five years of teaching. Especially recommended for beginning teachers and graduate students interested in this stage of teaching development.

EDCS 617.title: Early Literacy and Language Development
EDCS 617.subject: EDCS
EDCS 617.description: Theory and practice for PK-3 early literacy and language development. Focus is on content knowledge and pedagogical strategies that support the optimal development of oral language, reading, and writing skills in PK-3 classrooms.

EDCS 618.title: Early Childhood Education: Advanced Topics
EDCS 618.subject: EDCS
EDCS 618.description: Analysis and practical application of selected early childhood education program and/or instructional materials. Restricted to majors.

EDCS 619.title: Social and Cultural Constructions of Childhood
EDCS 619.subject: EDCS
EDCS 619.description: Seminar examines the interrelated socially constructed concepts of children and childhood and places them in the larger contexts informed by sociological, anthropological, historical, critical, and technological perspectives.
EDCS 619.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

EDCS 622B.title: Curriculum Leadership: early childhood
EDCS 622B.subject: EDCS
EDCS 622B.description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

EDCS 622D.title: Curriculum Leadership: middle school
EDCS 622D.subject: EDCS
EDCS 622D.description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

EDCS 622G.title: Curriculum Leadership: K-14
EDCS 622G.subject: EDCS
EDCS 622G.description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

EDCS 623.title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
EDCS 623.subject: EDCS
EDCS 623.description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

EDCS 624.title: School Mathematics Curriculum
EDCS 624.subject: EDCS
EDCS 624.description: Analysis of research related to teaching and learning school mathematics, application of research to classroom practices. Appraisal of recent curriculum trends; critical examination of assumptions underlying proposed curriculum changes.

EDCS 625.title: Social Studies Curriculum
EDCS 625.subject: EDCS
EDCS 625.description: Examination and evaluation of social science content, societal values and research findings as basis for development and revision of social studies materials, texts, curriculum guides, methodology.
EDCS 625.prereq_raw: STE 322 or equivalent, social studies teaching experience, or consent.

EDCS 626.title: Art Education K-12
EDCS 626.subject: EDCS
EDCS 626.description: Principles, goals, and objectives in teaching and learning art K-12; curriculum, instruction, and assessment in art education; laboratory experiences in art media.

EDCS 627.title: Teaching and Learning with Art Objects, Museums, Collections, and Site Visits
EDCS 627.subject: EDCS
EDCS 627.description: Interdisciplinary inquiry and examination of the role of physical objects and site visits in schools and other educational contexts, through visits to local art museums and related sites.

EDCS 628.title: Function of Play in Early Childhood Education
EDCS 628.subject: EDCS
EDCS 628.description: Review of research and theory illuminating the nature, purposes, and meaning of play as a critical aspect of early childhood education.

EDCS 630.title: Cultural Diversity and Education
EDCS 630.subject: EDCS
EDCS 630.description: Examines issues, theories, perspectives and practices in multicultural education and promotes awareness, encourages knowledgeable reflection and develops skills necessary for multicultural practitioners.

EDCS 632.title: Qualitative Research Methods
EDCS 632.subject: EDCS
EDCS 632.description: Methods of qualitative research in education or related social science from an interdisciplinary framework.

EDCS 635.title: Autoethnography in Education
EDCS 635.subject: EDCS
EDCS 635.description: Exploration and application of autoethnography as a self-reflexive research method that utilizes the retelling of lived experience and emotion to examine historical, critical, and social topics.
EDCS 635.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

EDCS 638B.title: Curriculum and Instruction in Studio Art: painting, drawing, printing
EDCS 638B.subject: EDCS
EDCS 638B.description: Understanding art methods and materials related to art education for teachers grades K-12. Writing curricula, integrating visual arts across the curriculum, developing evaluation methods observing stages of artistic growth among students of multiple ages/abilities. (B) painting, drawing, printing; (C) fiber arts, ceramics, sculpture; (D) photography, technology, collage; (E) Combination of any three of B, C, and/or D. Previous BA, BS, BEd, and BFA only.

EDCS 644.title: Multilingual/EL Pedagogy
EDCS 644.subject: EDCS
EDCS 644.description: Examines practices, theories, research, and perspectives on multilingual/EL teaching approaches. Topics include culturally and linguistically responsive approaches, collaboration, lesson planning, and adapting materials to promote the growth and development of multilingual/ EL learners.

EDCS 645.title: Seminar In Multicultural Literacy
EDCS 645.subject: EDCS
EDCS 645.description: Interdisciplinary examination of research and issues in the teaching and learning of literacy in diverse multicultural settings.

EDCS 646.title: Literacy Assessment, Instruction, and Intervention

EDCS 646.description: Application of formative assessments to better monitor/guide struggling readers and writers. Topics include diversity and state/national initiatives.

EDCS 647B.title: Classroom and School Literacy Assessment: general
EDCS 647B.subject: EDCS
EDCS 647B.description: Advanced use of formative and summative assessments to monitor/lead classroom and school literacy programs. EDCS 647C.subject: EDCS

EDCS 648.title: Reading for English Language Learners
EDCS 648.subject: EDCS
EDCS 648.description: Presents key concepts and theories in teaching reading to K-12 English language learners. Topics include instructional decisions in teaching reading to ELLs, the interrelationship of language skills, strategies, and teaching academic content.

EDCS 649.title: Theory/Practice in Cooperative Occupational Education
EDCS 649.subject: EDCS
EDCS 649.description: Theory and practices of coordinating cooperative education in high school and community college.

EDCS 650.title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
EDCS 650.subject: EDCS
EDCS 650.description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawaiʻi and our global community.

EDCS 654.description: Research and practice in ethnomathematics from an interdisciplinary framework. EDCS 656.description: Concepts and inquiry regarding the application of early childhood educational principles and approaches to programs serving children between birth and age five. EDCS 670.title: Indigenous and Postcolonial Perspectives in Education
EDCS 670.subject: EDCS
EDCS 670.description: Examination of historical impacts of U.S. and European imperialism and Western education on Indigenous communities across the globe. Additional emphasis on contemporary Indigenous efforts towards cultural reclamation and educational sovereignty.

EDCS 671.title: Contemporary Native Hawaiian Education
EDCS 671.subject: EDCS
EDCS 671.description: Explores the landscapes, purposes, successes, and challenges of contemporary Native Hawaiian education. EDCS 677.title: Curriculum Design in Early Childhood Education

EDCS 677.description: Designed to help classroom teachers understand sources and principles of curriculum in early childhood education and to provide experience in evaluating, selecting, and developing appropriate curriculum for young children.

EDCS 685.title: Museums and Education

EDCS 686.title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources

EDCS 690.title: School and District Literacy Leadership
EDCS 690.subject: EDCS
EDCS 690.description: Exploration and application of school and districtwide roles of the literacy specialist, such as collaborating with other educators to: (1) design and implement literacy programs, and (2) provide research-supported professional development.

EDCS 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project

EDCS 696.title: Graduate Certificate Capstone

EDEF 676.title: The Politics of Education
EDEF 676.subject: EDEF
EDEF 676.description: Examination of the ways in which education can be viewed as political, arising from its connection to the larger political system including local, state, and federal governments.

EDEF 678.title: Approaches to Educational Inquiry
EDEF 678.subject: EDEF
EDEF 678.description: Overview of different research methods in educational inquiry with an opportunity to explore through practice one or more methods (ex: case study, interviewing, narrative construction, practitioner inquiry.) Preparation for MEd or PhD proposals.

EDEF 680.title: Seminar on Race, Law, and Education
EDEF 680.subject: EDEF
EDEF 680.description: Introduction to educational law and the way it relates to issues of race and ethnicity. Particular focus on how the U.S. courts have dealt with the question of educational inequality in a multiracial/multiethnic society.
EDEF 680.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

EDEF 683.title: Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
EDEF 683.subject: EDEF
EDEF 683.description: Focuses on the interplay of class, race, gender and ethnicity in school and community settings. Social praxis, educational reform and policy are considered.

EDEF 684.title: Education and World Order
EDEF 684.subject: EDEF
EDEF 684.description: Focuses on the challenges educators face in identifying appropriate pedagogical frameworks and practices in global education that address the impact of globalization in our society today.

EDEF 685.title: International Development Education
EDEF 685.subject: EDEF
EDEF 685.description: Introduction to international development education in Asian and Pacific nations. Students explore links between education and development. Emphasis is on cross-cultural perception of development.

EDEF 686.title: Environmental Education
EDEF 686.subject: EDEF
EDEF 686.description: Focuses on the development of an ecological consciousness through a cultural and environmental approach to teaching and learning in schooling and everyday life.

EDEF 725.title: Education and Social Change
EDEF 725.subject: EDEF
EDEF 725.description: Study of classical and contemporary theories of social change as these relate to school, the profession of teaching, planning of change, and social stability.

EDEF 751.title: Recent History of American Education
EDEF 751.subject: EDEF
EDEF 751.description: Contemporary American education in recent historical perspective; focuses on the educational changes brought about by WW II, the Cold War, civil rights and other social movements.

EDEF 761.title: History of American Higher Education
EDEF 761.subject: EDEF
EDEF 761.description: Genesis and evolution of college and university from colonial America to present.

EDEF 762.title: Seminar on the Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
EDEF 762.subject: EDEF
EDEF 762.description: Examination of social, political, and cultural issues affecting educational policy with special emphasis on methods of inquiry and theoretical constructs.

EDEF 764.title: Advanced Seminar in Philosophy of Education
EDEF 764.subject: EDEF
EDEF 764.description: Advanced studies in philosophical inquiry. Examination of philosophically based methods of analysis and interpretation and their influence in educational research and practice.

EDEF 766.title: Seminar in History of Education
EDEF 766.subject: EDEF
EDEF 766.description: Aspects of the history of education. Application of historiography to educational problems and policy.

EDEF 767.title: Seminar on the Educational System
EDEF 767.subject: EDEF
EDEF 767.description: Examination of the structure and dynamics of educational system. Particular focus on how educational policy interacts with principles that explain educational system behavior.

EDEF 771.title: Seminar in Comparative/International Education
EDEF 771.subject: EDEF
EDEF 771.description: Advanced reading, research and writing in selected topics dealing with comparative and international education, including such themes as policy studies, minority education and educational reform.

EDEP 201.title: Introduction to Teaching as a Career
EDEP 201.subject: EDEP
EDEP 201.description: An experience-based introduction to teaching as a career.

EDEP 311.title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
EDEP 311.subject: EDEP
EDEP 311.description: Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research. Develops knowledge and written communication skills through an introduction to classroom assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing.

EDEP 327.title: Self-Regulated Learning
EDEP 327.subject: EDEP
EDEP 327.description: Theory and use of self-regulated learning strategies in academic contexts.

EDEP 408.title: Fundamentals of Research in Education
EDEP 408.subject: EDEP
EDEP 408.description: Introduction to the methodology of systematic study of problems in education: principles of research design, data processing, technical writing, and evaluation of research proposals and reports.

EDEP 411.title: Seminar in Contemporary Perspectives in Educational Psychology
EDEP 411.subject: EDEP
EDEP 411.description: In-depth analysis of contemporary issues in education from the theoretical and methodological perspectives of the faculty in educational psychology. Focuses on oral communication and intensive writing skills.

EDEP 416.title: Student Assessment
EDEP 416.subject: EDEP
EDEP 416.description: Introduction to basic concepts and issues in assessment and measurement, development of formative and summative assessment procedures, descriptive statistics, scales of measurement, and standardizing testing.

EDEP 429.title: Introductory Statistics
EDEP 429.subject: EDEP
EDEP 429.description: Introduction to concepts and logics of statistical reasoning and statistical literacy. Topics include descriptive statistics, sampling distribution, and inferential statistics such as z-test, t-tests, correlation, and one-way ANOVA.

EDEP 432.title: Human Motivation and Education
EDEP 432.subject: EDEP
EDEP 432.description: Application of motivation theory and research to understanding and increasing human motivation for education.

EDEP 489.title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
EDEP 489.subject: EDEP
EDEP 489.description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research.

EDEP 601.title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods
EDEP 601.subject: EDEP
EDEP 601.description: Introductory graduate-level statistics in education and social sciences. Topics on descriptive and inferential statistics including central tendency, variability, sampling distribution, z-test, t-test, correlation, simple linear regression, and one-way ANOVA. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

EDEP 602.title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
EDEP 602.subject: EDEP
EDEP 602.description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

EDEP 603.title: Design and Analysis of Psychological Experiments
EDEP 603.subject: EDEP
EDEP 603.description: Analysis of variance and other models of assessing results of experiments. Relation of analysis to design.

EDEP 604.title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
EDEP 604.subject: EDEP
EDEP 604.description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.
EDEP 604.prereq_raw: EDEP 601 or EDEA 629 (with a grade of B), or consent.

EDEP 606.title: Multivariate Methods
EDEP 606.subject: EDEP
EDEP 606.description: Builds on prior knowledge of multiple regression and will include applications of MANOVA, canonical correlation, logistic regression, discriminant function analysis, cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling, and mixture models.

EDEP 607.title: Nonparametric Methods for Behavioral Science
EDEP 607.subject: EDEP
EDEP 607.description: Conditions for valid applications of nonparametric statistical techniques in education and behavioral sciences; theoretical and methodological perspectives.

EDEP 608.title: Introduction to Educational Research
EDEP 608.subject: EDEP
EDEP 608.description: Fundamental design and evaluation procedures in educational research. Topics include an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research, the review of literature, developing research questions, research design, instrumentation, data collection, and writing a research proposal.
EDEP 608.prereq_raw: EDEP 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B or higher) or consent.

EDEP 611.title: Graduate Introduction to Educational Psychology
EDEP 611.subject: EDEP
EDEP 611.description: Graduate level introduction to educational psychology theories, research, and topics.

EDEP 612.title: Multilevel Modeling for Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data
EDEP 612.subject: EDEP
EDEP 612.description: Theories and applications of multilevel model to analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal data. Topics include two-level and three-level models, growth models, and multilevel logistic regression.
EDEP 612.prereq_raw: EDEP 604 , PSY 610 , 612 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or consent.

EDEP 613.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education
EDEP 613.subject: EDEP
EDEP 613.description: Introduction to methods of qualitative research in education. (Meets PhD common core requirement.)

EDEP 616.title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
EDEP 616.subject: EDEP
EDEP 616.description: Measurement and psychometric theories and applications using psychometric programs. Topics include classical test theory, reliability, validity, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, item bias, and item response theory.

EDEP 618.title: Categorical Data Analysis
EDEP 618.subject: EDEP
EDEP 618.description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables; analysis of contingency tables, loglinear models, introduction to generalized linear models for binary, nominal, ordinal, and count outcomes in cross-sectional and longitudinal data sets.

EDEP 625.title: Structural Equation Modeling
EDEP 625.subject: EDEP
EDEP 625.description: Theories and applications to test models with manifest and latent variables. Topics include path analysis, factor analysis, latent variable model, multi-group analysis, latent means model, and other advanced topics in SEM.

EDEP 626.title: Psychometric Methods
EDEP 626.subject: EDEP
EDEP 626.description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, and current issues in psychometrics.
EDEP 626.prereq_raw: EDEP 604 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

EDEP 631.title: Adolescence and Education
EDEP 631.subject: EDEP
EDEP 631.description: Discussion-based course presenting an overview of educational psychology applied to teaching adolescents, including theory and research on human learning, adolescent development and its social context, and student assessment.

EDEP 633.title: Foundations of School Counseling
EDEP 633.subject: EDEP
EDEP 633.description: Explores school counseling history, philosophy, and ASCA Model. Covers delivery systems, interventions, roles, and ethics. Examines contemporary challenges and resources in supporting student development. (Meets EdD common core elective.)

EDEP 634.title: Human Development Across the Lifespan
EDEP 634.subject: EDEP
EDEP 634.description: Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Major theories and related research on human development; applications in policy planning and service delivery in counseling.

EDEP 635.title: Counseling: Theory and Practice
EDEP 635.subject: EDEP
EDEP 635.description: Overview of major counseling theories, techniques, and evidence-based practices as preparation for practicum and internship. Explores integrative approaches and theoretical concepts. Application to diverse populations in school, rehabilitation, and community settings.

EDEP 637.title: Introduction to Practicum
EDEP 637.subject: EDEP
EDEP 637.description: Theory and techniques of counseling as preparation for practicum and internship. Emphasis on counseling relationships and basic skill development. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

EDEP 638.title: Career Development and Vocational Counseling
EDEP 638.subject: EDEP
EDEP 638.description: Theory and practice in career development and vocational counseling with individuals and groups; utilization of educational, vocational, and social resources in career counseling.

EDEP 639.title: Research and Evaluation in Counseling
EDEP 639.subject: EDEP
EDEP 639.description: Framework for understanding basic statistics, methodology, and evaluation of research in counseling and related fields. Students will analyze research, conceptualize research, and apply research to practice.

EDEP 640.title: Counseling: Group Theory and Practice
EDEP 640.subject: EDEP
EDEP 640.description: Theories and techniques of group counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.
EDEP 640.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and KRS 606 / EDEP 635 , and consent.

EDEP 641.title: Assessment and Appraisals in Counseling
EDEP 641.subject: EDEP
EDEP 641.description: Assessment methods and tools for evaluating aptitudes, achievements, and interests. Applications to educational, instructional, and career counseling.

EDEP 642.title: School Counseling Approaches to Transition and Adjustment
EDEP 642.subject: EDEP
EDEP 642.description: Principles of behavior affecting interpersonal relationships in school with emphasis on application to actual situations.

EDEP 643.title: Theory and Assessment of Intelligence
EDEP 643.subject: EDEP
EDEP 643.description: Theory and supervised experience in individual intelligence testing, psychological report writing; psychometric and social issues in intelligence testing.

EDEP 644.title: Trauma and Crisis Counseling
EDEP 644.subject: EDEP
EDEP 644.description: Crisis intervention strategies and counseling skills for schools. Trauma-informed approaches for crises like suicide and violence. Focus on age-appropriate interventions, resilience, and school collaboration.

EDEP 645.title: Multicultural Counseling
EDEP 645.subject: EDEP
EDEP 645.description: Significance of cultural factors in counseling relationships, delivery of counseling services in multicultural settings with attention to Hawaiʻi. Emphasis on process of cultural learning and implications for counselor roles and functions.

EDEP 648.title: Principles and Practice of Rehabilitation Counseling
EDEP 648.subject: EDEP
EDEP 648.description: Principles, practices of rehabilitation counseling; review of history and influence of legislation on vocational rehabilitation; current issues, developments, with emphasis on local situation.

EDEP 649.title: Medical and Psychosocial Aspects of Disability
EDEP 649.subject: EDEP
EDEP 649.description: Functional implications of chronic illnesses and disabilities on psychological, social and vocational areas of an individuals life. Case studies and presentations will stimulate discussion and help students to apply theoretical information into practical everyday context.

EDEP 650.title: Case Management in Rehabilitation
EDEP 650.subject: EDEP
EDEP 650.description: Knowledge and skills required in case and case-load management in public as well as private sector rehabilitation sites. Emphasis on professional/client relationship, interviewing process, decision-making, goal-setting, recording/documentation, time management, and other tasks.

EDEP 651.title: Psychopathology in Counseling
EDEP 651.subject: EDEP
EDEP 651.description: Discussion-oriented course (potentially Web-based). Examination of theory and practice of diagnosis in the assessment and treatment of mental disorders and the use of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) multi-axial system. Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues.

EDEP 652.title: Ethical and Legal Issues in Counseling
EDEP 652.subject: EDEP
EDEP 652.description: Developing ethical reasoning capabilities for resolution of ethical dilemmas likely to be encountered in counseling, psychology, and specialty practices (e.g., community, rehabilitation, school, mental health, alcohol and substance abuse, marriage and family counseling, and the like).

EDEP 653.title: Vocational Evaluation and Assessment in Rehabilitation
EDEP 653.subject: EDEP
EDEP 653.description: Theory, process, and techniques of vocational evaluation and assessment. Assessment methods and processes as they relate to vocational choice and adjustment of special groups.

EDEP 655.title: Theory and Techniques of Job Placement
EDEP 655.subject: EDEP
EDEP 655.description: Theory, process, and techniques of job readiness, job development, and job placement.

EDEP 657.title: Introduction to Program Evaluation
EDEP 657.subject: EDEP
EDEP 657.description: Introduction to concepts and issues related to program evaluation. Topics include preparing for an evaluation, formative and summative uses, and qualitative and quantitative design approaches.

EDEP 661.title: Development and Learning
EDEP 661.subject: EDEP
EDEP 661.description: Theories and research on learning and development and their educational applications. Analysis of how learning and development are interrelated.

EDEP 662.title: Social Context of Learning
EDEP 662.subject: EDEP
EDEP 662.description: Analysis of the social context in the learning process and education, including peer, family, community, and cultural influences.

EDEP 663.title: Models of Cognitive Learning
EDEP 663.subject: EDEP
EDEP 663.description: Cognitive models of knowledge acquisition, organization, and utilization; theory and research relating learning and cognition to interactive instructional models.

EDEP 664.title: Instructional Psychology
EDEP 664.subject: EDEP
EDEP 664.description: Application of learning theory and cognitive skills training in instructional settings.

EDEP 665.title: Social Cognition and Competence
EDEP 665.subject: EDEP
EDEP 665.description: Systematic analysis of social reasoning abilities conjunctive with or prerequisite to effective social interaction in educational settings.

EDEP 685.title: Capstone Project in Educational Psychology
EDEP 685.subject: EDEP
EDEP 685.description: To be taken in the final semester or the second to last semester to complete the certificate. Students are expected to integrate, extend, critique and apply knowledge learned in the certificate program.

EDEP 703C.title: Practicum in Counseling: community service
EDEP 703C.subject: EDEP
EDEP 703C.description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
EDEP 703C.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

EDEP 703E.title: Practicum in Counseling: elementary
EDEP 703E.subject: EDEP
EDEP 703E.description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
EDEP 703E.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

EDEP 703H.title: Practicum in Counseling: secondary
EDEP 703H.subject: EDEP
EDEP 703H.description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
EDEP 703H.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

EDEP 703R.title: Practicum in Counseling: rehabilitation
EDEP 703R.subject: EDEP
EDEP 703R.description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
EDEP 703R.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

EDEP 703U.title: Practicum in Counseling: college
EDEP 703U.subject: EDEP
EDEP 703U.description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
EDEP 703U.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

EDEP 704.title: Contemporary Issues in Counseling
EDEP 704.subject: EDEP
EDEP 704.description: Current issues and problems. (Meets EdD common required elective.)

EDEP 711.title: Practicum in Educational Psychology
EDEP 711.subject: EDEP
EDEP 711.description: Supervised practicum in teaching or program evaluation as each is reflected by professional activities of the members of the faculty.

EDEP 733C.title: Internship I: community service
EDEP 733C.subject: EDEP
EDEP 733C.description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 733E.title: Internship I: elementary
EDEP 733E.subject: EDEP
EDEP 733E.description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 733H.title: Internship I: secondary
EDEP 733H.subject: EDEP
EDEP 733H.description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 733R.title: Internship I: rehabilitation
EDEP 733R.subject: EDEP
EDEP 733R.description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 733U.title: Internship I: college
EDEP 733U.subject: EDEP
EDEP 733U.description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 734C.title: Internship II: community service
EDEP 734C.subject: EDEP
EDEP 734C.description: Supervised post-internship I experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 734E.title: Internship II: elementary
EDEP 734E.subject: EDEP
EDEP 734E.description: Supervised post-internship I experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
