EDEP 734H.subject: EDEP
EDEP 734H.description: Supervised post-internship I experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 734R.title: Internship II: rehabilitation
EDEP 734R.subject: EDEP
EDEP 734R.description: Supervised post-internship I experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 734U.title: Internship II: college
EDEP 734U.subject: EDEP
EDEP 734U.description: Supervised post-internship I experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

EDEP 741.title: Seminar in School Counseling
EDEP 741.subject: EDEP
EDEP 741.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in school counseling.
EDEP 741.prereq_raw: KRS 703 / EDEP 703 (E or H) and consent.

EDEP 745.title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
EDEP 745.subject: EDEP
EDEP 745.description: Analysis of psychology of adult learner; forces that affect learning in dynamics of individual, group, and organizational behavior; concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities.

EDEP 768B.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: general
EDEP 768B.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768B.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 768C.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: learning
EDEP 768C.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768C.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 768D.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: measurement
EDEP 768D.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768D.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 768E.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: statistics
EDEP 768E.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768E.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 768F.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: psycho-social development
EDEP 768F.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768F.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 768G.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: educational evaluation
EDEP 768G.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768G.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 768H.title: Seminar in Educational Psychology: research methodology
EDEP 768H.subject: EDEP
EDEP 768H.description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.

EDEP 781.title: Seminar in Rehabilitation Counseling
EDEP 781.subject: EDEP
EDEP 781.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in rehabilitation counseling.

EDUC 615.title: Action Research in Education
EDUC 615.subject: EDUC
EDUC 615.description: Theory and practice in collaborative action research; critical inquiry into current educational work in schools with goals of improvement of teaching and participation in school and curriculum reform.

EDUC 710.title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Consultancy Project
EDUC 710.subject: EDUC
EDUC 710.description: Practicum in the EdD program in professional practice; involves a group consultancy project requiring independent research and reflective activity embedded in a group project dealing with a problem of practice.
EDUC 710.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

EDUC 720.title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Individual Applied Research Project
EDUC 720.subject: EDUC
EDUC 720.description: Practicum in conducting individual practitioner research within the EdD. Includes the formulation of individual applied research project, developing a plan of action, selection of appropriate methods, implementation of plan and composition of practitioner research report.
EDUC 720.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

EDUC 730.title: EdD Conference
EDUC 730.subject: EDUC
EDUC 730.description: Capstone for the Doctoral Degree in Professional Education Practice. Involves a conference presentation of research project results to an audience of faculty, fellow graduate students, and interested members of the public. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

EDUC 740.title: Field Project
EDUC 740.subject: EDUC
EDUC 740.description: Practicum experience in area of specialization. Variable credit: minimum of 3 credit hours, maximum of 6 credit hours.

EDUC 799.title: Internship in College Teaching
EDUC 799.subject: EDUC
EDUC 799.description: Introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as apprentices to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, planning and evaluation.
EDUC 799.prereq_raw: admission to PhD candidacy and consent.

ELI 070.title: Intermediate Academic Listening and Speaking
ELI 070.subject: ELI
ELI 070.description: Introduction to the academic English-language listening/speaking demands required at the university. Instruction and practice of effective note-taking skills, listening strategies, delivery of presentations, and participation in academic discussions. Designed as a bridge to ELI 080 .

ELI 075.title: Intermediate Academic Literacy
ELI 075.subject: ELI
ELI 075.description: Introduction to the academic English-language literacy demands required at the university. Extensive practice in academic reading, writing, and vocabulary development. Designed as a bridge to advanced-level ELI courses in reading and writing.

ELI 080.title: Advanced Academic Listening and Speaking
ELI 080.subject: ELI
ELI 080.description: Further development of the academic English-language listening/speaking skills and strategies required at the university. Instruction and practice of effective note-taking skills, critical listening strategies, delivery of effective academic presentations and leading of academic discussions.

ELI 082.title: Advanced Academic Reading
ELI 082.subject: ELI
ELI 082.description: Further development of skills and strategies for dealing with the high demands of academic reading by focusing on becoming efficient and autonomous readers. Instruction and practice of developing critical reading strategies and building field-specific vocabulary.

ELI 083.title: Advanced Academic Writing for Graduate Students
ELI 083.subject: ELI
ELI 083.description: Introduction to academic writing conventions common at the graduate level. Students explore academic writing in their disciplines, develop clarity of written expression, and improve command over textual, rhetorical, and discursive conventions common in academic writing.

ELI 111.title: Practicum for International Teaching Assistants
ELI 111.subject: ELI
ELI 111.description: Extensive practice for international teaching assistants in speaking in classroom situations with emphasis on oral skills, American cultural expectations and classroom management.

ENG 100.title: Composition I
ENG 100.subject: ENG
ENG 100.description: Introduction to the rhetorical, conceptual and stylistic demands of writing at the university level; instruction in composing processes, search strategies, and writing from sources.
ENG 100.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Registration restricted to undergraduates.

ENG 100A.title: Composition I
ENG 100A.subject: ENG
ENG 100A.description: Introduction to the rhetorical, conceptual and stylistic demands of writing at the university level; instruction in composing processes, search strategies, and writing from sources.
ENG 100A.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Registration restricted to undergraduates.

ENG 200.title: Composition II
ENG 200.subject: ENG
ENG 200.description: Further study of rhetorical, conceptual, and stylistic demands of writing; instruction develops the writing and research skills covered in Composition I .

ENG 209.title: Business Writing
ENG 209.subject: ENG
ENG 209.description: Practice in informative, analytical, persuasive writing.
ENG 209.prereq_raw: FW. Students may not earn credit for both ENG 209 and BUS 209 .

ENG 764.title: Seminar in Life Writing
ENG 764.subject: ENG
ENG 764.description: Intensive study of critical and theoretical issues raised by various forms of life writing (biography, autobiography, oral history, diaries, etc.) and of their history and methodology.

ENG 800.title: Dissertation Research

ENG 800.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

ENGR 100.title: Engineering Freshman Seminar
ENGR 100.subject: ENGR
ENGR 100.description: Overview of the engineering field, the different disciplines, and opportunities. Success strategies for studying engineering.

ENGR 101.title: Introduction to Engineering
ENGR 101.subject: ENGR
ENGR 101.description: Topics include the engineering disciplines, the development of problem solving and technical communication skills, the design process and analysis methods using a team design project, and introduction to programming in Matlab for engineering applications.
ENGR 101.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshman standing only.

ENGR 102.title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
ENGR 102.subject: ENGR
ENGR 102.description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors.
ENGR 102.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR and BUS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshmen only.

ENGR 196.title: Freshman Vertically Integrated Project
ENGR 196.subject: ENGR
ENGR 196.description: Team-based research project for freshman-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a sophomore ( ENGR 296 ).

ENGR 250.title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
ENGR 250.subject: ENGR
ENGR 250.description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders.

ENGR 296.title: Sophomore Vertically Integrated Project
ENGR 296.subject: ENGR
ENGR 296.description: Team-based research project for sophomore-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a junior ( ENGR 396 ). Sophomore standing or higher.

ENGR 350.title: Career Development Seminar
ENGR 350.subject: ENGR
ENGR 350.description: Introduction to career development as it pertains to engineering and business industry; client relations, networking, job skills, career assessment and direction.

ENGR 396.title: Junior Vertically Integrated Project
ENGR 396.subject: ENGR
ENGR 396.description: Team-based research project for junior-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a senior.
ENGR 396.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ENGR 401.title: Engineering Management
ENGR 401.subject: ENGR
ENGR 401.description: Introduction to engineering management of projects and its outcomes. Development of professional skills for the systematic formulation of problems and solutions to efficiently deduce project viability. Emphasis on collaborative teamwork and performance evaluations and improvements. Senior standing or higher.

ENGR 493.title: Field Experience
ENGR 493.subject: ENGR
ENGR 493.description: Supervised internship in engineering practice under professional and faculty direction.
ENGR 493.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: junior standing in engineering and consent.

EPET 201.title: Space Exploration
EPET 201.subject: EPET
EPET 201.description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication.

EPET 301.title: Space Science and Instrumentation
EPET 301.subject: EPET
EPET 301.description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation. Significant oral and written communication is required.
EPET 301.prereq_raw: EPET 201 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107 ; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272 .

EPET 321.title: Introduction to Human Spaceflight
EPET 321.subject: EPET
EPET 321.description: Effects of spaceflight conditions on human physiology and psychology. Astronaut selection, training, crew composition. Ethics of space exploration. Politics & sociology of public and private human space flight. Selection of capstone project. Significant written communication.

EPET 400.title: Space Mission Design
EPET 400.subject: EPET
EPET 400.description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission.

EPET 401.title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
EPET 401.subject: EPET
EPET 401.description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing.

EPET 420.title: Human Spaceflight Mission Elements
EPET 420.subject: EPET
EPET 420.description: Engineering aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, and budgets for human spaceflight missions. Design of environmental control and life support systems. Capstone project design. Significant oral and written communication.

EPET 421.title: Capstone Project - Human Spaceflight Analog Mission
EPET 421.subject: EPET
EPET 421.description: Science experiments in space and human space flight engineering. Human spaceflight capstone project with a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, and social scientists. Concurrent disciplinary and multidisciplinary methodologies. Human spaceflight analog mission. Significant written communication.

ERTH 101.title: Dynamic Earth
ERTH 101.subject: ERTH
ERTH 101.description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

ERTH 101A.title: Dynamic Earth
ERTH 101A.subject: ERTH
ERTH 101A.description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

ERTH 101L.title: Dynamic Earth Laboratory
ERTH 101L.subject: ERTH
ERTH 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on study of minerals, rocks, and topographic maps. Examine volcanism, hydrology, coastal processes and hazards, geologic time and earthquakes. Field trips to investigate landslides, beaches and Oʻahu geology.

ERTH 102.title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
ERTH 102.subject: ERTH
ERTH 102.description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

ERTH 103.title: Geology of the Hawaiian Islands
ERTH 103.subject: ERTH
ERTH 103.description: Hawaiian geology and geologic processes: origin of Hawaiian islands, volcanism, rocks and minerals, landforms, stream and coastal processes, landslides, earthquakes and tsunamis, groundwater, geologic and environmental hazards. Field trip.

ERTH 104.title: Volcanoes in the Sea
ERTH 104.subject: ERTH
ERTH 104.description: Lecture with field trips covering the manner in which geological conditions, resources, and events have affected past and present circum-Pacific societies.

ERTH 105.title: Voyage through the Solar System
ERTH 105.subject: ERTH
ERTH 105.description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

ERTH 106.title: Humans and the Environment
ERTH 106.subject: ERTH
ERTH 106.description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

ERTH 107.title: Solar System Studio
ERTH 107.subject: ERTH
ERTH 107.description: Explore the wonders of the Solar System through hands-on experience of science. Will study satellite images, evaluate planetary surface observations, analyze data of objects in our Solar System, conduct experiments, and communicate their findings.

ERTH 110.title: Voyage of the Vicariance: Earth and Life through Time
ERTH 110.subject: ERTH
ERTH 110.description: Exploration of Earth history via an imaginary sailing voyage around the world and back in time to Earth’s formation and the origin of life. Introduces fundamental concepts in geology, paleontology, living systems, and evolutionary biology.

ERTH 111.title: Introduction to Volcanoes
ERTH 111.subject: ERTH
ERTH 111.description: Examines the origin and classification of volcanoes, volcanic eruptions, and volcanic deposits. Includes the history of volcanic studies, myths, and legends. Emphasis on volcanic eruptions, eruptive products, volcanic hazards, and risk management.

ERTH 130.title: Geological Hazards
ERTH 130.subject: ERTH
ERTH 130.description: Introductory course covering the causes of, and effects from, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, landslides, rockfalls, and other natural geologic phenomena. Field trips.

ERTH 135.title: Natural Disasters and Human History
ERTH 135.subject: ERTH
ERTH 135.description: Examines how natural hazards have affected the course of human culture and societies from pre-history to the present in Hawaiʻi/Oceania, Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

ERTH 170.title: Physical Geology
ERTH 170.subject: ERTH
ERTH 170.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Structure, composition and evolution of Earth; processes responsible for formation, deformation and transformation of rocks; plate tectonics. Emphasis on quantitative methods, problem solving and critical thinking to geology. Laboratory and field trips required.

ERTH 199.title: Introduction to Directed Research
ERTH 199.subject: ERTH
ERTH 199.description: Lower division reading and research in any area of ERTH under the direction of a faculty member.

ERTH 200.title: Geological Inquiry
ERTH 200.subject: ERTH
ERTH 200.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Origin and age of the solar system and earth: interior of the earth; plate tectonics and records of biological evolution and past environments. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
ERTH 200.prereq_raw: ERTH 101L and one of ERTH 101 , ERTH 103 , ERTH 104 , ERTH 106 , or ERTH 130 ; or consent. ERTH 101L may be taken concurrently.
ERTH 200.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors.

ERTH 201.title: Climate Change
ERTH 201.subject: ERTH
ERTH 201.description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors.
ERTH 201.prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102 , or consent.

ERTH 250.title: Scientific Programming
ERTH 250.subject: ERTH
ERTH 250.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to solving scientific problems by computer programming. Overview of the MatLab programming language and environment. Emphasis placed on good style, logical reasoning, and applied mathematics.

ERTH 300.title: Physical Volcanology
ERTH 300.subject: ERTH
ERTH 300.description: Volcanic eruptions and their consequences. Includes models for volcanic eruptions including explosive eruptions and lava flows, monitoring of active volcanoes, evaluation and impacts of volcanic hazards, and mitigation of volcanic risk. Field trips. Normally fall. ERTH and GEOL majors or consent.
ERTH 300.prereq_raw: ( ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 ) with a minimum grade of B or consent.

ERTH 301.title: Mineralogy
ERTH 301.subject: ERTH
ERTH 301.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the chemistry, crystalline structure, geologic occurrence, and physical properties of minerals. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
ERTH 301.prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 and ( CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or CHEM 171 / CHEM 171L ). or consent.

ERTH 302.title: Igneous Petrology
ERTH 302.subject: ERTH
ERTH 302.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Survey of composition, classification, and occurrence of igneous rocks. Hand-specimen identification and optical petrography of igneous rocks. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.

ERTH 303.title: Natural Hazards & Geomechanics
ERTH 303.subject: ERTH
ERTH 303.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Dynamic behavior of Earth’s surface, physical processes driving geohazards, and the risks posed to society. Theory, practical techniques, and data visualization to measure, analyze, and interpret hazards and implications.
ERTH 303.prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 130 , MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A , and PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ; or consent.

ERTH 305.title: Geological Field Methods
ERTH 305.subject: ERTH
ERTH 305.description: Methods used in geological investigations in the field. Eight hours on Saturday in the field.

ERTH 306.title: Work of Water
ERTH 306.subject: ERTH
ERTH 306.description: Physical properties of water, geological aspects of surface water and ground water occurrence, surface water and groundwater resources, use, and problems.

ERTH 309.title: Sedimentology Processes and Environments
ERTH 309.subject: ERTH
ERTH 309.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Modern and past terrestrial and oceanic processes and environments that form sediments and sedimentary rocks, and their interpretation in Earth history. Incorporates properties, principles and applications of sedimentology, sedimentary petrology, geochemistry and stratigraphy.
ERTH 309.prereq_raw: ERTH 200 , ERTH 201 or consent, and ERTH 333 or consent.

ERTH 312.title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
ERTH 312.subject: ERTH
ERTH 312.description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

ERTH 313.title: Plate Tectonics and Geodynamics
ERTH 313.subject: ERTH
ERTH 313.description: Mechanics of lithosphere deformation related to plate convergence, rifting and strike-slip faulting, and the evolution of mountain belts. Use of theory and skill-building techniques to measure, describe, analyze, and interpret structures on Earth.
ERTH 313.prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 ; and ERTH 250 ; and MATH 241 or MATH 251A ; and PHYS 170 .

ERTH 323.title: Physics of Earth and Planets
ERTH 323.subject: ERTH
ERTH 323.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Essentials of geophysics: application of physics understanding Earth, planetary, and solar dynamics. Topics include heat flow, gravity, geodesy, electromagnetism, seismology. Applications to core and mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, volcanoes, hydrology, environmental concerns, and archaeology.
ERTH 323.prereq_raw: ERTH 250 , ERTH 303 , ERTH 313 (or concurrent), MATH 242 , and PHYS 272 , PHYS 272L ; or consent.

ERTH 325.title: Geochemistry
ERTH 325.subject: ERTH
ERTH 325.description: Theory and applications of chemical principles and chemical analysis to Earth, ocean and environmental sciences; chemistry of hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere system, origin/ differentiation of Earth/Solar system, volcanic processes, natural radioactivity, organic/inorganic chemistry.
ERTH 325.prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 , and MATH 241 or MATH 251A , and CHEM 162 (or concurrent); or consent.

ERTH 333.title: Earth Materials and Structures
ERTH 333.subject: ERTH
ERTH 333.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lecture and lab that covers formation, occurrence, and identification of common minerals, rocks, and geologic structures. Lab work will include study of hand-samples, thin-sections, and field experiences.

ERTH 395.title: Undergraduate Internship
ERTH 395.subject: ERTH
ERTH 395.description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.
ERTH 395.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior/ senior standing and consent.

ERTH 396.title: Undergraduate Research in Earth Sciences
ERTH 396.subject: ERTH
ERTH 396.description: Research experience for Earth Science undergraduates. Under the guidance of a mentor, the student will conduct research and write a report on the background, methods, data, interpretations, and conclusions of the work.
ERTH 396.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Earth Sciences majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ERTH 399.title: Directed Reading
ERTH 399.subject: ERTH
ERTH 399.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior/ Senior standing only.

ERTH 401.title: Introduction to Mineral Physics
ERTH 401.subject: ERTH
ERTH 401.description: Scientific study of the materials that make up the Earth. Properties of minerals on micro- and macro-scales; their properties and behavior.

ERTH 402.title: Hawaiian Geology
ERTH 402.subject: ERTH
ERTH 402.description: Consists of lectures, discussions, and field trips on the geologic processes and geologic history of the Hawaiian islands, with emphasis on writing communication.

ERTH 404.title: Remote Compositional Analysis: Spectroscopy, Mineralogy, and Geochemistry of Planetary Surfaces
ERTH 404.subject: ERTH
ERTH 404.description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces. Comparative studies of fundamental planetary science phenomena. Planetary surface science discoveries. Sustainability of planetary environments.
ERTH 404.prereq_raw: ( ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L , or ERTH 105 or ERTH 107 or ASTR 150 ; and CHEM 161 ; and PHYS 272 ) with a minimum grade of C+; or consent.

ERTH 406.title: Natural Disasters: Geoethics and the Layman
ERTH 406.subject: ERTH
ERTH 406.description: Evaluates ethical practice of geoscience as it relates to studies of natural disasters that result from geological and meteorological phenomena and the means that earth scientists interact with the laymen.

ERTH 407.title: Energy and Mineral Resources
ERTH 407.subject: ERTH
ERTH 407.description: Lecture and discussion on the origin, distribution and exploitation of fossil fuels, renewable energy resources and ore deposits. Coverage and detail will depend partly on student interest and background.

ERTH 410.title: Undergraduate Seminar
ERTH 410.subject: ERTH
ERTH 410.description: Gain professional training and practical experience giving scientific presentations emphasizing Earth and planetary sciences, including analysis of associated ethical issues. Grading is distributed 60/40 between three oral communication assignments and related ethics content.

ERTH 412.title: Earth: A Model Planet
ERTH 412.subject: ERTH
ERTH 412.description: Integrative course that explores the interactions between the solid earth, oceans, atmosphere, and space environment, and introduces methodology and tools for computer modeling of the Earth as a system and its long-term climate and habitability.
ERTH 412.prereq_raw: ( ERTH 101 and ERTH 250 , and at least one of ERTH 302 , ERTH 309 , ERTH 313 , ERTH 323 , ERTH 325 , or ERTH 333 ) with a minimum grade of B.

ERTH 413.title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
ERTH 413.subject: ERTH
ERTH 413.description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data.
ERTH 413.prereq_raw: ERTH 250 and MATH 242 (or concurrent) or consent.

ERTH 420.title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
ERTH 420.subject: ERTH
ERTH 420.description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites.
ERTH 420.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

ERTH 423.title: Marine Geology
ERTH 423.subject: ERTH
ERTH 423.description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

ERTH 425.title: Environmental Geochemistry
ERTH 425.subject: ERTH
ERTH 425.description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

ERTH 440.title: Coastal Geochemistry
ERTH 440.subject: ERTH
ERTH 440.description: Covers aqueous geochemistry at the land-ocean interface, including the distribution of major and minor ions, trace metals, organic chemicals, and nutrients.
ERTH 440.prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 , CHEM 162 , and MATH 241 or MATH 251A ; or consent.

ERTH 444.title: Plate Tectonics
ERTH 444.subject: ERTH
ERTH 444.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

ERTH 451.title: Earthquakes and Crustal Deformation
ERTH 451.subject: ERTH
ERTH 451.description: Earthquakes and crustal deformation through modern seismological and geodetic observations; elastic properties of rocks, seismic waves, causes, detection, and location of earthquakes; crustal motions of the earthquake cycle; tsunami generation, liquefaction, and planetary observations.

ERTH 454.title: Engineering Geology
ERTH 454.subject: ERTH
ERTH 454.description: Solutions of geotechnical problems by geologists and engineers through recognition, characterization, evaluation, and assessment of geologic processes that impact people, engineering structures, and engineering operations. Group format.
ERTH 454.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH, GEOL, and CEE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing and higher.

ERTH 455.title: Hydrogeology
ERTH 455.subject: ERTH
ERTH 455.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Occurrence, characteristics, movement, quality, development, and contamination of water in the Earth’s crust.
ERTH 455.prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 , and MATH 215 or MATH 241

ERTH 460.title: Geological Remote Sensing
ERTH 460.subject: ERTH
ERTH 460.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab on the concepts behind, geologic uses for, and techniques of satellite and airborne remote sensing. Lab work will consist of computer image processing. Field trips. Open to nonmajors.

ERTH 461.title: Geospatial Information
ERTH 461.subject: ERTH
ERTH 461.description: Combined lecture/lab covering the collection, analysis and use of geospatially registered field data.

ERTH 466.title: Planetary Geology
ERTH 466.subject: ERTH
ERTH 466.description: Comparative geology of the terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, tectonism, geomorphology, weathering; manned and unmanned space exploration.

ERTH 468.title: Lunar Geology
ERTH 468.subject: ERTH
ERTH 468.description: Introduction to the basics of the geology and spectroscopy of our Moon.

ERTH 469.title: Origin of the Solar System
ERTH 469.subject: ERTH
ERTH 469.description: Exploration of the origin and evolution of our solar system. Understanding the composition of the universe and its constituents (planets, asteroids, stars, comets, and meteorites).
ERTH 469.prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 130 and CHEM 161 and PHYS 170 .

ERTH 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
ERTH 499.subject: ERTH
ERTH 499.description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

ERTH 593.title: Earth and Planetary Sciences Workshops
ERTH 593.subject: ERTH
ERTH 593.description: Designed for in-service school professionals to learn new approaches and concepts in the fields of earth and planetary sciences.

ERTH 600.title: Equations of Geophysics
ERTH 600.subject: ERTH
ERTH 600.description: Least-square approximation of functions by orthogonal series; potential, wave heat flow equations; boundary value problems; Bessel Hankel functions, spherical harmonics, potential theory, plane waves, spherical waves; emphasis on geophysics application.
ERTH 600.prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , PHYS 400 , or consent.

ERTH 601.title: Explosive Volcanism
ERTH 601.subject: ERTH
ERTH 601.description: Explosive volcanic eruptions: from causes to consequences. Review of current physical volcanology including ascent and fragmentation of magma, transport and deposition processes in pyroclastic eruptions, volcanic crisis management and volcanic eruption scenarios. Seven-day field trip.

ERTH 602.title: Theoretical Petrology
ERTH 602.subject: ERTH
ERTH 602.description: Derivation of phase diagrams from basic thermodynamics principles. Equilibria of natural silicate systems. Crystal chemistry, kinetics, diffusion, etc., applied to igneous and metamorphic petrology.
ERTH 602.prereq_raw: ERTH 302 , ERTH 325 , and CHEM 351 (or concurrent); or consent.

ERTH 603.title: Petrology of Ocean Lithosphere
ERTH 603.subject: ERTH
ERTH 603.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Petrogenesis of the oceanic lithosphere, including mantle processes and rocks from mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, oceanic hotspots, back-arc basins, and intra-oceanic arcs.

ERTH 604.title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
ERTH 604.subject: ERTH
ERTH 604.description: Combined lecture/discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning.

ERTH 605.title: Lava Flow Rheology and Morphology
ERTH 605.subject: ERTH
ERTH 605.description: Effusion eruptions: from eruption to final flow form. Includes: rheology, effusion rate, heat loss, and field measurements, followed by inflation, flow forms, lava lakes, domes, flow hazard and modeling. Field trips to Kilauea and Makapuu.

ERTH 606.title: Current Events in Volcanology
ERTH 606.subject: ERTH
ERTH 606.description: Discussion of active areas of volcanism and new publications on volcanology.

ERTH 607.title: Submarine Volcanoes
ERTH 607.subject: ERTH
ERTH 607.description: Seminar exploring different aspects of submarine effusive and explosive volcanism, hydrothermal activity, and volcano-hosted ecosystems.

ERTH 608.title: Isotopes and Trace Elements
ERTH 608.subject: ERTH
ERTH 608.description: Principles of radiogenic and stable isotope, and trace element geochemistry as applied to igneous petrology, mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, and terrestrial evolution.

ERTH 609.title: Graduate Teaching Geology
ERTH 609.subject: ERTH
ERTH 609.description: For ERTH graduate students who lead, under faculty supervision, a scheduled class in Geology and Geophysics. The instructor will define the student’s responsibilities when offering ERTH 609, and these responsibilities must be met for a passing grade. As the consent to take the class must also be granted by the department chair, the chair will also review the responsibilities required by the instructor.
ERTH 609.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair.
ERTH 609.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH graduate students only.

ERTH 610.title: Graduate Seminar
ERTH 610.subject: ERTH
ERTH 610.description: Seminar in which students present a 15- to 20-minute talk on their research or a related topic. Meets once a week with two to three talks per meeting. Graduate students are required to register for this course once per year.

ERTH 611.title: Accelerated Introduction to Earth Sciences I
ERTH 611.subject: ERTH
ERTH 611.description: Lecture presenting a rapid-paced survey of earth sciences for graduate students. Includes origin of the Solar System, tectonics, volcanology, whole-earth composition, phase transformations, petrology (igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary), historical geology, and hydrology. Saturday field trips.

ERTH 613.title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
ERTH 613.subject: ERTH
ERTH 613.description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data. Credit earned only one time for either ERTH 413 or 613.
ERTH 613.prereq_raw: ERTH 250 and MATH 242 (or concurrent), or consent.

ERTH 615.title: Literate Programming With R and RStudio
ERTH 615.subject: ERTH
ERTH 615.description: Literate programming with R, RStudio, and R Markdown for data analysis and research. Introduction to Matlab for rapid modeling. Emphasis on the preparation of research papers for scholarly publication in the Earth and environmental sciences.
ERTH 615.prereq_raw: competence in basic differential and integral calculus.

ERTH 616.title: How to Write a Scientific Paper
ERTH 616.subject: ERTH
ERTH 616.description: Designed for students who have collected data and want to know how to publish their work in a scientific journal. Covers the essential parts of paper preparation and submission.

ERTH 617.title: Summer Fieldschool Program: Hydrogeophysics in Volcanic Environments
ERTH 617.subject: ERTH
ERTH 617.description: Will cover the full hydrogeophysical workflow including theory, acquisition design, field data acquisition, data processing, data inversion, and hydrogeological interpretation. Methods include ambient seismic, 3D electrical resistivity tomography and induced polarization, and self-potential.

ERTH 620.title: Coastal Geology
ERTH 620.subject: ERTH
ERTH 620.description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.

ERTH 621.title: Electron Microprobe Analysis
ERTH 621.subject: ERTH
ERTH 621.description: Combined lecture-lab on principles and procedures for textural and geochemical analysis by the SOEST electron microprobe. Hands-on experience with the microprobe operation. Each student will complete one individual research project using the microprobe.

ERTH 623.title: Introduction to Earth and Planetary Geophysics
ERTH 623.subject: ERTH
ERTH 623.description: Introductory geophysics course integrating theory, data analysis, and field methods to study Earth, planetary, and solar dynamics. Methods of seismology, gravity, geodesy, and electromagnetism, with field applications in tectonics, geomorphology, archeology, volcanism, and hydrology.
ERTH 623.prereq_raw: ERTH 250 and MATH 242 and PHYS 272 ; or equivalents.

ERTH 625.title: Advanced Environmental Geochemistry
ERTH 625.subject: ERTH
ERTH 625.description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system and remediation methods. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase and isotope chemistry of environmental contaminants.

ERTH 630.title: Numerical Modeling of Physical Systems
ERTH 630.subject: ERTH
ERTH 630.description: Finite difference, finite element, and other modeling techniques applied to geological and geophysical problems. Physical modeling of heat flow, molecular diffusion, solidification and melting, deformation, fluid flow, wave propagation, and other phenomena.

ERTH 631.title: Geophysics-Solid, Fluid, and Wave Mechanics
ERTH 631.subject: ERTH
ERTH 631.description: Continuum mechanics in geophysics, as applied to the deformation of Earth materials (elastic, viscous, viscoelastic, and plastic deformations) and seismic wave propagation (body waves, surface waves, anisotropy, and attenuation).
ERTH 631.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent).

children.text: for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

ERTH 632.title: Geophysics-Gravity, Magnetics, and Heat Transfer
ERTH 632.subject: ERTH
ERTH 632.description: Fundamental theory and practical applications of the use of gravity, magnetics, and heat conduction to probing the structure of the Earth; heat transfer via mantle convection is a major control on Earth’s internal structure.
ERTH 632.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent).

children.text: for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

ERTH 635.title: Seismology
ERTH 635.subject: ERTH
ERTH 635.description: Elasticity, wave equations, body waves, surface waves, free oscillations, seismometry, seismogram interpretation, tectonics, inversion, source theory, and waveform modeling.

ERTH 638.title: Earth System Science and Global Change
ERTH 638.subject: ERTH
ERTH 638.description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmospheric-sediment system and coevolution of the biota.
ERTH 638.prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus; or consent.

ERTH 639.title: Stable Isotope Biogeochemistry
ERTH 639.subject: ERTH
ERTH 639.description: Stable isotope geochemistry applied to questions of biogeochemical cycling in the oceans, sediment diagenesis, paleoceanography, environmental geochemistry and ecology.

ERTH 640.title: Coastal Geochemistry
ERTH 640.subject: ERTH
ERTH 640.description: Geochemistry at the land-ocean interface: coastal hydrology, subterranean estuaries and coastal mixing and their importance in governing the distribution of selected radiotracers, trace metals and nutrients. Combined lecture-lab with field trips and group projects.
ERTH 640.prereq_raw: CHEM 162 , and MATH 241 or MATH 251A ; or consent.

ERTH 641.title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
ERTH 641.subject: ERTH
ERTH 641.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

ERTH 642.title: Elemental Composition Changes
ERTH 642.subject: ERTH
ERTH 642.description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

ERTH 644.title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
ERTH 644.subject: ERTH
ERTH 644.description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.
ERTH 644.prereq_raw: CHEM 171 , or CHEM 161 and CHEM 162 ; PHYS 152 ; and MATH 242 or MATH 252A ; and consent.

ERTH 651.title: Geomagnetism and Cosmic Magnetism
ERTH 651.subject: ERTH
ERTH 651.description: Magnetic fields of Earth, planets, stars, and galaxies; dynamo theories; paleomagnetism; terrestrial and lunar rock magnetism; planetary, regional, and local geomagnetic sounding.

ERTH 654.title: Groundwater Contamination
ERTH 654.subject: ERTH
ERTH 654.description: Principles of groundwater chemistry; chemical evolution in natural groundwater flow systems; sources of contamination; mass transport processes; hydrochemical behavior of contaminants.

ERTH 656.title: Groundwater Modeling
ERTH 656.subject: ERTH
ERTH 656.description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.

ERTH 657.title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
ERTH 657.subject: ERTH
ERTH 657.description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

ERTH 666.title: Planetary Surfaces
ERTH 666.subject: ERTH
ERTH 666.description: Comparative geology of terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, geomorphology; remote sensing; manned and unmanned space exploration.

ERTH 669.title: Cosmochemistry
ERTH 669.subject: ERTH
ERTH 669.description: Formation and evolution of planets as astrophysical objects, geologic bodies, and abodes of life; current understanding from studies of the Solar System, star formation, meteorites, exoplanets; theory of formation and dynamics; atmospheres, oceans, habitability, biosignatures.
ERTH 669.prereq_raw: ERTH 325 or CHEM 351 (or equivalent); or consent.

ERTH 671B.title: Remote Sensing: planets
ERTH 671B.subject: ERTH
ERTH 671B.description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

ERTH 671C.title: Remote Sensing: volcanoes
ERTH 671C.subject: ERTH
ERTH 671C.description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

ERTH 672.title: Seminar in Tectonics
ERTH 672.subject: ERTH
ERTH 672.description: Evolution of ocean basins, margins, foldbelts, and platforms, from plate tectonics and regional syntheses of structure, petrology, geophysics, and stratigraphy.

ERTH 673B.title: Extraterrestrial Material: meteorites
ERTH 673B.subject: ERTH
ERTH 673B.description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

ERTH 673C.title: Extraterrestrial Material: petrology of the Moon and Mars
ERTH 673C.subject: ERTH
ERTH 673C.description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

ERTH 674.title: Paleoceanography
ERTH 674.subject: ERTH
ERTH 674.description: Study of the paleoceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere and biosphere.

ERTH 675.title: The Generic Mapping Tools
ERTH 675.subject: ERTH
ERTH 675.description: Introduction to the Generic Mapping Tools (GMT). Processing of scientific data and the automated preparation of maps and illustrations using GMT on UNIX workstations, with introduction to UNIX and the C shell environment.

ERTH 691.title: Data Analysis in the Earth and Space Sciences
ERTH 691.subject: ERTH
ERTH 691.description: Advanced data analysis in Earth and Space sciences, including time-series and frequency-domain methods, Bayesian statistics, Monte Carlo simulations, clustering and machine learning. Term project required.
ERTH 691.prereq_raw: ERTH 613 , OCN 760 , or ASTR 633 or equivalent is highly recommended.

ERTH 695.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
ERTH 695.subject: ERTH
ERTH 695.description: Linear and nonlinear techniques for model selection, parameter estimation, simulation and forecasting, from Bayesian principles with particular attention to large data sets and sparse noisy data.

ERTH 701.title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
ERTH 701.subject: ERTH
ERTH 701.description: Interpretation of geophysical and laboratory data to understand elastic and anelastic properties, composition, phase relationships, temperature distribution in the Earth.

ERTH 703.title: Fractures and Faults
ERTH 703.subject: ERTH
ERTH 703.description: Lecture on elasticity theory, fracture mechanics and boundary element modeling, with application to faults and fractures in the Earth.

ERTH 707.title: Exoplanet Astronomy
ERTH 707.subject: ERTH
ERTH 707.description: Accelerated survey of exoplanet astronomy and planetary systems using data from the field’s leading edge, introduction to key theoretical concepts, application of analytic and numerical tools, and development of teamwork, presentation, and publishing skills.
ERTH 707.prereq_raw: ASTR 633 with a minimum grade of B, or instructor permission.

ERTH 710.title: Selected Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
ERTH 710.subject: ERTH

ERTH 711.title: Special Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
ERTH 711.subject: ERTH

ERTH 740.title: MGeo Seminar
ERTH 740.subject: ERTH
ERTH 740.description: Seminar to improve student awareness of trends and practices in geoscience professions, and develop ability to prepare, deliver, and evaluate a professional scientific presentation. Targets abstract writing, oral presentation, and technical criticism.

ERTH 750.title: MGeo Professional Project
ERTH 750.subject: ERTH
ERTH 750.description: Practical hands-on professional experience, typically with a local company or agency, and involving a final written report and an oral presentation. A grade of credit is assigned when the internship presentations are satisfactorily completed.

ES 101.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
ES 101.subject: ES
ES 101.description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.

ES 101A.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
ES 101A.subject: ES
ES 101A.description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.

ES 213.title: Race, Class, Gender in Popular Culture
ES 213.subject: ES
ES 213.description: Contemporary issues of race, class, and gender in popular culture (film, television, music, social media, sports, etc.). Introduction to critical media analysis and social science theories and methods. Emphasis on writing instruction.

ES 214.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
ES 214.subject: ES
ES 214.description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

ES 221.title: Hawaiians
ES 221.subject: ES
ES 221.description: The social system, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians in a Pacific context. Transformation of the Hawaiian system by a capitalist economy. Native Hawaiian regeneration and quest for sovereign governance as an Oceanic society.

ES 233.title: Filipinos in Diaspora
ES 233.subject: ES
ES 233.description: Introduction to Filipinos in diaspora. Topics include: race, empire, migration, representation, cultural production, identity formation, and decolonization.

ES 301.title: Ethnic Identity
ES 301.subject: ES
ES 301.description: Individual and group problems of identity, identity conflict, culture conflict, inter-ethnic relations. Critical review of available material on Hawaiʻi.

ES 305.title: African American Experience I
ES 305.subject: ES
ES 305.description: Afrocentric perspective. Analysis of the black political/cultural diaspora, including ancient African kingdoms, the slavery experience, organized resistance, emancipation struggles, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

ES 306.title: African American Experience II
ES 306.subject: ES
ES 306.description: Black sociopolitical perspectives of the Reconstruction period, Jim Crow, intellectual and cultural awakenings, civil rights movements, and contemporary issues as examined through students’ written analysis and creative projects.

ES 308.title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
ES 308.subject: ES
ES 308.description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
ES 308.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

ES 310.title: Ethnicity and Community: Hawaiʻi
ES 310.subject: ES
ES 310.description: Site visits to museums, social welfare units, etc., as well as guest lecturers from the community including police, health, education.

ES 318.title: Asian America
ES 318.subject: ES
ES 318.description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation. Emphasis on ethics.
ES 318.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ES 320.title: Hawaiʻi and the Pacific
ES 320.subject: ES
ES 320.description: Hawaiʻi as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

ES 330.title: Japanese and Okinawans in Hawaiʻi
ES 330.subject: ES
ES 330.description: Transoceanic context of Japanese and Okinawan migration; their history in labor, politics, and business; politics of gender, race, ethnicity, and class; contemporary ethical issues in light of changing economic, social, and political conditions in Hawaiʻi.

ES 331.title: Power and Place: Chinatowns
ES 331.subject: ES
ES 331.description: Historical and contemporary experiences of Chinese in Hawaiʻi and the U.S. continent with a focus on Chinatowns; urbanization; economic development, community organizing; comparative racialization.

ES 333.title: Filipinos in Hawaiʻi
ES 333.subject: ES
ES 333.description: Historical and contemporary experiences; immigration; traditional culture and values; plantation experience; labor organizing; development of Filipino community; racism; discrimination; and ethnic identity. This course develops oral communication skills.

ES 338.title: American Indian Experience
ES 338.subject: ES
ES 338.description: Provides a comprehensive look at the indigenous foundation of life and society in the Americas and elaborates on historical and contemporary importance of American Indian rights issues. Emphasis on teaching ethical issues and writing.

ES 339.title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
ES 339.subject: ES
ES 339.description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation.
ES 339.prereq_raw: one ES or WGSS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent.

ES 340.title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawaiʻi
ES 340.subject: ES
ES 340.description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

ES 345.title: The Sounds of Race and Inequality
ES 345.subject: ES
ES 345.description: Explore inequality as manifested and contested in silence, music, dialect, nature, voice, and acoustic space by listening through a matrix of race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexualities. Combination of hands-on work and current scholarship.

ES 350.title: Economic Change and Hawaiʻi’s People
ES 350.subject: ES
ES 350.description: Hawaiʻi’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

ES 360.title: Immigration to Hawaiʻi and U.S.
ES 360.subject: ES
ES 360.description: Historical and current immigration discourses and policies in Hawai’i and the US; oceanic concepts of migration; experiences of various ethnic groups; immigrant-led movements for justice. Course develops written communication ranging from storytelling to research papers.

ES 365.title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawaiʻi
ES 365.subject: ES
ES 365.description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawaiʻi; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
ES 365.prereq_raw: one ANTH, SOC, or WGSS course.

ES 370.title: Literatures of Hawaiʻi
ES 370.subject: ES
ES 370.description: Writings of various ethnic groups in Hawaiʻi, ancient to contemporary. Songs, stories, poetry, fiction, essays that illustrate the social history of Hawaiʻi.
ES 370.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

ES 372.title: Asian American Literature
ES 372.subject: ES
ES 372.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Asian American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds.
ES 372.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

ES 373.title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
ES 373.subject: ES
ES 373.description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.

ES 375.title: Issues of Diversity in Higher Education
ES 375.subject: ES
ES 375.description: Examines issues of diversity within higher education. Examines different dimensions of diversity including ethnicity, gender, national origin, age, and sexual orientation. Will utilize national and local case studies.
ES 375.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior class standing or higher.

ES 380.title: Fieldwork in Ethnic Studies
ES 380.subject: ES
ES 380.description: Supervision of individual student research projects pertinent to ethnic studies, including service learning, civic engagement, internship, oral history, or supervised practicum experience in teaching select ethnic studies courses.

ES 381.title: Social Movements in Hawaiʻi
ES 381.subject: ES
ES 381.description: Examines, through writing and collaboration, interethnic movement building among Native Hawaiian, other Pacific Islander, and Asian peoples of Hawai’i through intersectional theories of social change to evaluate strategies to create just and sustainable futures.

ES 390.title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
ES 390.subject: ES
ES 390.description: Intersecting processes of racial and gender oppression and privilege; institutional contexts and lived experiences; ethical issues in past and present anti-racist feminist thought and activism in the United States and in Hawaiʻi.
ES 390.prereq_raw: ES 101 or WGSS 151 or junior standing.

ES 391.title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
ES 391.subject: ES
ES 391.description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific.
ES 391.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.
ES 391.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ES 392.title: Change in the Pacific-Polynesia
ES 392.subject: ES
ES 392.description: Impact of cultural and physical change and their interrelationship.

ES 395.title: Multiethnic Popular Culture: Hip Hop
ES 395.subject: ES
ES 395.description: Historical, social, cultural, and political aspects of the formation and development of Hip Hop in Hawaiʻi and elsewhere in Oceania with special attention to cultural interactions and connections. This course develops oral communication skills.
ES 395.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.
ES 395.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ES 400.title: Ethnic Studies in the Digital World
ES 400.subject: ES
ES 400.description: The digitally networked world mediates race and ethnicity-and vice-versa. We will challenge racism and discrimination manifested in social media, changing notions of identity and group belonging, ewaste, gaming, big data, and more.

ES 410.title: Race, Class, and the Law
ES 410.subject: ES
ES 410.description: Historical context and implications of landmark court decisions and legal issues affecting social change in ethnic communities in Hawaiʻi and the continental U.S.
ES 410.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.

ES 418.title: Gender and Work
ES 418.subject: ES
ES 418.description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
ES 418.prereq_raw: one 300-level ES or WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

ES 420.title: American Ethnic and Race Relations
ES 420.subject: ES
ES 420.description: Surveys ethnic and race relations in the U.S. Focus on historical conflicts and critical issues such as racism, immigration, affirmative action, economy, government, and systemic change. Develops written communication skills.

ES 422.title: Mixed Race Identities, Multiracial Experiences
ES 422.subject: ES
ES 422.description: Critically examines historical and contemporary issues surrounding mixed race identities and experiences through themes that resonate in localized contexts within the continental U.S. and Oceania.
ES 422.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

ES 425.title: Filming Social Change
ES 425.subject: ES
ES 425.description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
ES 425.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

ES 440.title: Contemporary Diasporas in Comparative Perspective
ES 440.subject: ES
ES 440.description: Compares the circumstances under which contemporary Asian, Pacific Islander, or African migrants form diasporas across the globe; focus on a particular ethnic group to examine its site-specific experiences.

ES 443.title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
ES 443.subject: ES
ES 443.description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.
ES 443.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ES 450.title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawaiʻi
ES 450.subject: ES
ES 450.description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai’i. The course develops written communication skills.
ES 450.prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

ES 450.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ES 451.title: Raciolinguistics
ES 451.subject: ES
ES 451.description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere.

ES 455B.title: Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict: Middle East
ES 455B.subject: ES
ES 455B.description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
ES 455B.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

ES 455C.title: Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict: Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context
ES 455C.subject: ES
ES 455C.description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
ES 455C.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

ES 456.title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawaiʻi
ES 456.subject: ES
ES 456.description: Historical and contemporary social processes involved in race, racism, and inter-ethnic relations in Hawaiʻi. Focus on intersection of Asian and/or Pacific Island cultures with Native Hawaiian culture.
ES 456.prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent.

ES 457.title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
ES 457.subject: ES
ES 457.description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.
ES 457.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , or WGSS 202 ; or consent.

ES 460.title: Global Ethnic Conflict
ES 460.subject: ES
ES 460.description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment.
ES 460.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.
ES 460.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ES 470.title: Latinx Experience in Hawaiʻi
ES 470.subject: ES
ES 470.description: Examines historical, socio-cultural, and contemporary Latinx presence; relations among Latinx, other immigrant, and Indigenous communities; causes and patterns of immigration; racism and discrimination; ethnicity and identity issues; struggles for justice.
ES 470.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

ES 480.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Oceanic Ethnic Studies
ES 480.subject: ES
ES 480.description: Engagement with theoretical elements and qualitative research methods of Oceanic Ethnic Studies.
ES 480.prereq_raw: one upper division ES or SOCS course or consent.

ES 486.title: Peoples of Hawaiʻi
ES 486.subject: ES
ES 486.description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawaiʻi using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.
ES 486.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

ES 492.title: Politics of Multiculturalism
ES 492.subject: ES
ES 492.description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
ES 492.prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent.

ES 493.title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
ES 493.subject: ES
ES 493.description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project.

ES 495.title: Hawaiʻi’s Labor History
ES 495.subject: ES
ES 495.description: Conditions of work under varying political, social, and economic transformations in Hawaiʻi; anthropological, sociological, and historic data.
ES 495.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.

ES 496.title: Special Topics in Ethnic Studies
ES 496.subject: ES
ES 496.description: Selected themes in ethnic studies exploring current issues and new topics; taught by regular and visiting faculty.

ESEE 310.title: Learner in the Environment I: Social and Cultural Contexts for Learning
ESEE 310.subject: ESEE
ESEE 310.description: Knowledge and skills related to the context of teaching. Teacher candidates will examine the impact of culture, family, school, classroom, and individual characteristics on learning, and orally present, in varied formats, acquired knowledge and competencies.

ESEE 311.title: Learner in the Environment II: Classroom and Behavior Management
ESEE 311.subject: ESEE
ESEE 311.description: Teacher candidates explore the ethical implications for establishing, maintaining, and restoring the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning.

ESEE 312.title: Learner in the Environment III: Behavior Project Implementation
ESEE 312.subject: ESEE
ESEE 312.description: Teacher candidates demonstrate the ability to establish, maintain, and (when necessary) restore the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning. Candidates demonstrate ability to identify maladaptive student behaviors and implement effective, research-based interventions.

ESEE 320.title: Assessment I: Foundations of Assessment
ESEE 320.subject: ESEE
ESEE 320.description: Introduction to foundational aspects of assessment and emphasizes the importance of linking assessment with planning and instruction. Candidates develop knowledge, skills, and dispositions important for designing, implementing, and analyzing effective assessments for diverse learners.

ESEE 321.title: Assessment II: Formal Assessment
ESEE 321.subject: ESEE
ESEE 321.description: Understand techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment is stressed. Significant instruction on writing individualized education programs.

ESEE 330.title: Planning and Instruction: Introduction to Inclusive Teaching
ESEE 330.subject: ESEE
ESEE 330.description: Teacher candidates engage in reflective, procedural, and research writing to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

ESEE 331.title: Planning and Instruction: Science
ESEE 331.subject: ESEE
ESEE 331.description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to the teaching and learning of science in elementary settings, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, using evidence-based practices.

ESEE 332.title: Planning and Instruction: Mathematics in Inclusive Settings
ESEE 332.subject: ESEE
ESEE 332.description: Prepares beginning elementary school teachers of mathematics, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

ESEE 333.title: Planning and Instruction: STEM
ESEE 333.subject: ESEE
ESEE 333.description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to teaching and learning of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) content for inclusive elementary classrooms, K-6. Teacher candidates focus on planning, teaching, and assessing STEM.

ESEE 334.title: Planning and Instruction: Integrating Social Studies and the Performing Arts
ESEE 334.subject: ESEE
ESEE 334.description: Social Studies and Performing Arts integrated content in diverse K-6 classrooms. Teacher candidates engage with social issues through collaborative, expressive, aesthetic, creative, and critical pedagogy. Candidates perform, present, and teach to develop oral communication skills.

ESEE 340.title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy I: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, K-3
ESEE 340.subject: ESEE
ESEE 340.description: Overview of principles and practices for teaching reading (phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) to diverse students, grades K-3; including planning, instruction, and assessment. Writing assignments include lesson reflections, case studies, modules, and reading responses.

ESEE 341.title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy II: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, Grades 4-6
ESEE 341.subject: ESEE
ESEE 341.description: Teacher candidates demonstrate essential reading comprehension strategies, engaging students in complex text by planning, instructing, and assessing elementary students in grades 4-6, in inclusive settings. Emphasis on writing instruction.

ESEE 342.title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy III: Writing and Visual Arts in Inclusive Settings, K-6
ESEE 342.subject: ESEE
ESEE 342.description: Methods, programs, and strategies for planning, teaching, and assessing writing for elementary students in inclusive settings, grades K-6. Visual arts methods are integrated to develop visual literacy.

ESEE 350.title: Field Experience I: Response to Intervention in Reading
ESEE 350.subject: ESEE
ESEE 350.description: Teacher candidates in this field based course will use an evidence-based practice in reading within a response to intervention (Rtl) framework. Supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

ESEE 351.title: Field Rounds
ESEE 351.subject: ESEE
ESEE 351.description: Field-based course engages teacher candidates in a variety of purposeful observation and reflection activities aligned with course work. Field settings are appropriate to concurrent classes; supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

ESEE 352.title: Field Experience II: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
ESEE 352.subject: ESEE
ESEE 352.description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

ESEE 353.title: Field Experience III: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
ESEE 353.subject: ESEE
ESEE 353.description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

ESEE 354.title: Student Teaching in Elementary and Special Education Classrooms
ESEE 354.subject: ESEE
ESEE 354.description: Full-time student teaching in grades K-6 in an elementary school inclusion classroom, or a combination of general education and special education settings. The experience is directed by a qualified mentor teacher and has university-provided supervision.

ESEE 355.title: Seminar for Student Teaching
ESEE 355.subject: ESEE
ESEE 355.description: Seminar to support student teaching experiences and prepare teacher candidates to transition into a full time teacher, examine ethical issues in the field, prepare for employment, and demonstrate ability to meet professional standards.

ESL 100.title: Composition I for Second Language Writers
ESL 100.subject: ESL
ESL 100.description: Extensive practice in writing expository essays; linguistic devices that make an essay effective. (Fulfills composition requirement for nonnative speakers of English only.)

FDM 101.title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
FDM 101.subject: FDM
FDM 101.description: Introduction to the fields of apparel design and merchandising including theories of fashion change, apparel industry operations, current industry issues, literature of the field, professional competencies, careers in apparel and related businesses.

FDM 200.title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
FDM 200.subject: FDM
FDM 200.description: Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance.

FDM 205.title: Basic Apparel Construction
FDM 205.subject: FDM
FDM 205.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, concepts, and procedures for quality construction and custom fitting of clothing.

FDM 210.title: Fashion History
FDM 210.subject: FDM
FDM 210.description: Historic study of dress as related to customs and cultures in the Western world, in sociohistorical and contemporary contexts. Emphasis on 19th and 20th centuries.

FDM 215.title: Block Pattern Design
FDM 215.subject: FDM
FDM 215.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of pattern making for women’s apparel through manipulation of pattern blocks.

FDM 221.title: Textiles I
FDM 221.subject: FDM
FDM 221.description: Introduction to fibers, fabric structure, and finishes related to selection and care. Interrelationship between textile characteristics, properties, and end uses.

FDM 269.title: Costumes/Cultures of East Asia
FDM 269.subject: FDM
FDM 269.description: Development of ethnic dress of China, Japan, and Korea as a visual manifestation of culture. Students will be trained in written communication skills to describe and report important designs of these ethnic dresses related to culture.

FDM 301.title: Fashion Forecasting/Marketing
FDM 301.subject: FDM
FDM 301.description: Principles and practices in fashion trend forecasting, including environment analysis, consumer research, competitive analysis, color and textile forecasting, style directions, and digital marketing trends. Adapting fashion trend forecasts to apparel lines.
FDM 301.prereq_raw: one FW or FG course, or consent.
FDM 301.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

FDM 315.title: Draping
FDM 315.subject: FDM
FDM 315.description: Principles of pattern making through draping muslin models on standard garment forms.

FDM 316.title: Group Collection Development
FDM 316.subject: FDM
FDM 316.description: Advanced study in the specialty market design, pattern making, and construction for fashion design majors. Different specialty designs, such as swimwear, menswear, or others, will be offered each semester.
