FDM 316.prereq_raw: FDM 215 , FDM 221 , and FDM 301 . Recommended: FDM 315 , FDM 330 .

FDM 330.title: Advanced Construction
FDM 330.subject: FDM
FDM 330.description: Principles of advanced techniques for pattern development and garment construction with emphasis on difficult-to-handle fabrics and custom fits.

FDM 338.title: 2D/3D Computer Aided Design
FDM 338.subject: FDM
FDM 338.description: Exploration of CAD applications from the design to the pattern-making process. Use of Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop for fashion illustration. Use of OptiTex PDS pattern design software featuring 2D and 3D CAD.

FDM 339.title: 3D Retail Store Design
FDM 339.subject: FDM
FDM 339.description: Visual merchandising concepts and planning; use of a virtual 3D store modeling software package. Visual Retailing/Mockshop, to design store interiors, fixtures, lighting, signage, window displays, and planograms.

FDM 360.title: Writing for the Fashion Industry
FDM 360.subject: FDM
FDM 360.description: Analysis and creation of different types of writing in the fashion industry, with emphasis on creating a professional writing style.
FDM 360.prereq_raw: FDM 101 , FDM 200 or FDM 210 , and FDM 221 .

FDM 367.title: Branding
FDM 367.subject: FDM
FDM 367.description: Study of principles and practices in brand architecture and effective brand-building strategies; analysis of a case study and application of the concepts of brand management.
FDM 367.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

FDM 371.title: Retail Buying and Merchandising
FDM 371.subject: FDM
FDM 371.description: Theories and procedures in selecting, buying and selling apparel and textiles. Types of merchandising organizations, analysis of consumer demand, brick-and-click opportunities and challenges, development of an image, operation location, store and floor layout.

FDM 375.title: Merchandise Planning and Control
FDM 375.subject: FDM
FDM 375.description: Theories, problems, and procedures of financial and assortment planning and control of merchandise inventories.
FDM 375.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors and merchandising minors only.

FDM 411.title: Product Lifecycle Management
FDM 411.subject: FDM
FDM 411.description: Application of principles of apparel production management, including methods engineering (detail construction for ordering), story boards and color tables, production measurements, costing, and PLM computer applications.

FDM 430.title: Apparel Manufacturing
FDM 430.subject: FDM
FDM 430.description: Application of principles and procedures related to the promotion of fashion apparel. Preparation and presentation of fashion information through shows, displays, media, and written communications.

FDM 437.title: Entrepreneurship in Retail
FDM 437.subject: FDM
FDM 437.description: Application of principles, procedures and techniques of organizing a small retail business in a brick-and-click world. Students develop, write, and evaluate business plans creatively using low and high tech resources and oral communication skills.
FDM 437.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors only Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

FDM 460.title: Fashion Museum Management
FDM 460.subject: FDM
FDM 460.description: Investigation of skills and techniques needed for handling textile and apparel artifacts in museums and other collections. Active involvement in documenting, researching, interpreting, and exhibiting costumes and textiles. Involves written work and oral presentations.

FDM 471.title: Global Trade and Sourcing
FDM 471.subject: FDM
FDM 471.description: Theories, concepts, problems of international trade of textile and apparel products. Issues of importing and exporting apparel products globally. Social, economic, and ethical factors affecting textile and apparel trade.

FDM 491.title: Topics in Fashion
FDM 491.subject: FDM
FDM 491.description: Study and discussion of special topics, problems. Offered by staff and visiting faculty.

FDM 492.title: Internship and Capstone Portfolio
FDM 492.subject: FDM
FDM 492.description: Examination of issues and opportunities associated with careers in fashion and related businesses and industries. Topics include interpersonal skills development, job search and interview strategies, and ethical issues in the workplace.
FDM 492.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

FDM 496.title: Field Study in the Fashion Industry
FDM 496.subject: FDM
FDM 496.description: Study tours to various centers of the world to examine historical and modern apparel and textiles. Merchandising and design methods and operations examined.

FIL 101.title: Beginning Filipino
FIL 101.subject: FIL
FIL 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

FIL 201.title: Intermediate Filipino
FIL 201.subject: FIL
FIL 201.description: Continuation of FIL 102 . Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

FIL 224.title: Filipino for Education
FIL 224.subject: FIL
FIL 224.description: Continuation of FIL 102 . Lessons focus on various aspects of Philippine culture and specialized topics that cater to the needs of teachers intending to teach Filipino immigrant students or teach Filipino as a second language. Meets five hours a week; daily lab work.

FIL 301.title: Third-Level Filipino I
FIL 301.subject: FIL
FIL 301.description: Conversation, advanced reading and composition on traditional culture and indigenous knowledge. Includes emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 302.title: Third-Level Filipino II
FIL 302.subject: FIL
FIL 302.description: Conversation, advanced reading, and composition on contemporary issues. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 315.title: Filipino Aural Comprehension
FIL 315.subject: FIL
FIL 315.description: Training in comprehension of spoken authentic/simulated authentic materials presented in news broadcasts, songs, documentary narration, formal lectures, radio and television soap operas, etc.

FIL 330.title: Filipino Film: Art and History
FIL 330.subject: FIL
FIL 330.description: Study and analysis of Filipino films: its history, forms, development and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic context.

FIL 401.title: Fourth-Level Filipino I
FIL 401.subject: FIL
FIL 401.description: Advanced reading in traditional literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced oral communication and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 402.title: Fourth-Level Filipino II
FIL 402.subject: FIL
FIL 402.description: Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced conversation and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 415.title: Advanced Filipino Aural Comprehension
FIL 415.subject: FIL
FIL 415.description: Continuation of FIL 315 . Training in comprehension and analysis/criticism of spoken authentic materials through films.

FIL 435.title: Filipino Translation Techniques
FIL 435.subject: FIL
FIL 435.description: Techniques of bilingual translation: Filipino to English and English to Filipino.

FIL 461.title: Filipino Contemporary Literature
FIL 461.subject: FIL
FIL 461.description: Selected readings in poetry, short stories, and plays from early 1900s to present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

FIL 462.title: Filipino Contemporary Literature: 1980s-Present
FIL 462.subject: FIL
FIL 462.description: Survey of literature from the 80s (1986) to the present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

FIN 301.title: Personal Financial Planning
FIN 301.subject: FIN
FIN 301.description: Focuses on principles and techniques for handling personal financial decisions, including: personal budgeting, obtaining credit, life and casualty insurance, buying a home, buying an automobile, savings and investments, and retirement planning.

FIN 305.title: Problems of Business Finance
FIN 305.subject: FIN
FIN 305.description: Application of financial principles to cases involving important financial decisions; emphasis on writing.

FIN 307.title: Corporate Financial Management
FIN 307.subject: FIN
FIN 307.description: Development and analysis of modern financial theory and its implications for management decisions: market efficiency, capital asset pricing, firm investment decisions, capital structure, dividend policy, and cost of capital.

FIN 311.title: Investments
FIN 311.subject: FIN
FIN 311.description: Introduction to various investment media and capital markets. Topics include the analysis of security returns using techniques such as beta, filter rules, and portfolio theory.

FIN 321.title: International Business Finance
FIN 321.subject: FIN
FIN 321.description: Financial management of foreign and international business operations: the regulatory environment of international finance, financing international transactions, international capital markets, taxation. Financial decision-making in the firm.

FIN 331.title: International Banking
FIN 331.subject: FIN
FIN 331.description: Commercial, investment, and merchant banking. Includes theory and practical applications. Topics include international lending, Euromarkets, global gap management, Forex activities, and global risk management.

FIN 341.title: Financial Aspects of New Ventures
FIN 341.subject: FIN
FIN 341.description: Examination of underlying business models for new ventures, how to determine corresponding financial requirements, and approaches to resource acquisition. Students explore a range of financing sources and related issues of valuation and deal structure. College restriction: Shidler students only.
FIN 341.prereq_raw: junior standing and BUS 314 , or consent.

FIN 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
FIN 399.subject: FIN
FIN 399.description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

FIN 412.title: Options and Other Derivatives
FIN 412.subject: FIN
FIN 412.description: Options and other derivatives. Equity options, index options and options on futures. Black-Scholos Model. Trading strategies and tactics. Contemporary developments in financial engineering.

FIN 415.title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
FIN 415.subject: FIN
FIN 415.description: Security analysis and portfolio management from standpoint of the professional analyst and institutional investor. Recent advances in security valuation models, portfolio selection, and techniques for appraising portfolio performance. College restriction: Shidler students only.

FIN 430.title: Bank Financial Management
FIN 430.subject: FIN
FIN 430.description: Analysis of financial institution management within the domestic economy and regulatory environment. Topics include federal reserve activities, interest rates, regulation, lending, investments, and asset/liability management.

FIN 435.title: Banking and Capital Markets
FIN 435.subject: FIN
FIN 435.description: Covers the analytical skills necessary to work in the financial services industry, in particular in the bank treasury department or the fixed income capital market sector.

FIN 444.title: Asian Finance
FIN 444.subject: FIN
FIN 444.description: Financial systems, regulatory structure over financial institutions in the Asia-Pacific region. Major financial policy issues for financial sector reforms in the region. Seminar format.

FIN 450.title: Enterprise Risk Management
FIN 450.subject: FIN
FIN 450.description: Overview analyzing various primary risks faced by corporations and developing important risk management techniques with an emphasis on enterprise risk management. Combined lectures, case studies, and discussions.

FIN 456.title: Sustainable Finance
FIN 456.subject: FIN
FIN 456.description: Explores criticism and defense of the traditional profit maximization business model. Economic theory, recent trends, and case studies will refine students’ understanding of this cutting-edge field.

FIN 460.title: Special Topics in Finance, Real Estate or Insurance
FIN 460.subject: FIN
FIN 460.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of finance and finance-related fields.
FIN 460.prereq_raw: BUS 314 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

FIN 467.title: Seminar in Financial Planning
FIN 467.subject: FIN
FIN 467.description: A capstone course for financial services and planning track. This is a case study course intended to provide students the opportunity to integrate concepts from earlier courses and develop a comprehensive view of the financial planning process.
FIN 467.prereq_raw: FIN 301 and FIN 311 and two of the following courses: FIN 490E , FIN 490F , ACC 401 , INS 300 .

children.text: two of the following courses: FIN 490E

FIN 490B.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: investment banking
FIN 490B.subject: FIN
FIN 490B.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. (B) investment banking; (C) Japanese financial management; (D) financial analysis; (E) retirement and employee benefit planning; (F) finance estate planning.
FIN 490B.prereq_raw: BUS 314 for (B); BUS 314 or BUS 629 for (C); FIN 311 or 629, or consent for (D); FIN 301 for (E) and (F).
FIN 490B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Shidler College of Business students only.

FIN 490C.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: Japanese financial management
FIN 490C.subject: FIN
FIN 490C.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. (B) investment banking; (C) Japanese financial management; (D) financial analysis; (E) retirement and employee benefit planning; (F) finance estate planning.
FIN 490C.prereq_raw: BUS 314 for (B); BUS 314 or BUS 629 for (C); FIN 311 or 629, or consent for (D); FIN 301 for (E) and (F).
FIN 490C.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Shidler College of Business students only.

FIN 490D.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: financial analysis
FIN 490D.subject: FIN
FIN 490D.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. (B) investment banking; (C) Japanese financial management; (D) financial analysis; (E) retirement and employee benefit planning; (F) finance estate planning.
FIN 490D.prereq_raw: BUS 314 for (B); BUS 314 or BUS 629 for (C); FIN 311 or 629, or consent for (D); FIN 301 for (E) and (F).
FIN 490D.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Shidler College of Business students only.

FIN 490E.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: retirement and employee benefit planning
FIN 490E.subject: FIN
FIN 490E.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. (B) investment banking; (C) Japanese financial management; (D) financial analysis; (E) retirement and employee benefit planning; (F) finance estate planning.
FIN 490E.prereq_raw: BUS 314 for (B); BUS 314 or BUS 629 for (C); FIN 311 or 629, or consent for (D); FIN 301 for (E) and (F).
FIN 490E.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Shidler College of Business students only.

FIN 490F.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: finance estate planning
FIN 490F.subject: FIN
FIN 490F.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance. (B) investment banking; (C) Japanese financial management; (D) financial analysis; (E) retirement and employee benefit planning; (F) finance estate planning.
FIN 490F.prereq_raw: BUS 314 for (B); BUS 314 or BUS 629 for (C); FIN 311 or 629, or consent for (D); FIN 301 for (E) and (F).
FIN 490F.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Shidler College of Business students only.

FIN 625.title: International Monetary Systems and Global Financial Markets
FIN 625.subject: FIN
FIN 625.description: Supply and demand for capital in national and international markets. Nature of capital movements and role of capital in industrialization of regions and nations.

FIN 633.title: Problems in Business Finance
FIN 633.subject: FIN
FIN 633.description: Application of financial principles and analytical techniques to financial problems. Case method.

FIN 634.title: Investment Analysis and Management
FIN 634.subject: FIN
FIN 634.description: Techniques of security analysis, theories of investment, and the analysis of investment decisions related to portfolio planning.

FIN 635C.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: Japanese Financial Management
FIN 635C.subject: FIN
FIN 635C.description: Major current financial issues and problems. (C) Japanese financial management; (D) portfolio management theory; (F) stocks, bonds, and modern instruments.

FIN 635D.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: Portfolio Management Theory
FIN 635D.subject: FIN
FIN 635D.description: Major current financial issues and problems. (C) Japanese financial management; (D) portfolio management theory; (F) stocks, bonds, and modern instruments.

FIN 635F.title: Advanced Topics in Finance: Stocks, Bonds, and Modern Instruments
FIN 635F.subject: FIN
FIN 635F.description: Major current financial issues and problems. (C) Japanese financial management; (D) portfolio management theory; (F) stocks, bonds, and modern instruments.

FIN 636.title: Financial Analysis and Valuation
FIN 636.subject: FIN
FIN 636.description: Introduces the standard financial analysis framework and develops skills in analysis of financial information, evaluation of firms’ business risks and earnings prospects, and related applications in valuation.

FIN 637.title: International Financial Management
FIN 637.subject: FIN
FIN 637.description: Financial decision-making in an international setting: analysis of direct foreign investment; economic, accounting, and regulatory environments, including taxation; international money and capital markets; import and export financing; multinational working capital management; and risk aspects of international finance.

FIN 639.title: International Banking
FIN 639.subject: FIN
FIN 639.description: Commercial, investment, and merchant banking in the international arena. Includes international lending, Euromarkets, global gap management, Forex activities, and international risk management.

FIN 641.title: Entrepreneurial Finance
FIN 641.subject: FIN
FIN 641.description: Assessment of financial needs, arranging venture financing, assessing value to the entrepreneur and the investor(s), financial aspects of strategic planning, analyzing the tradeoffs between alternative financing choices and flexibility and control, harvesting the investment.

FIN 645.title: Advanced Capital Markets
FIN 645.subject: FIN
FIN 645.description: Regulatory structure over capital market institutions, market developmental issues, market microstructure issues, and corporate governance, and creation of capital market infrastructure. Seminar format.

FIN 651.title: PDEs and Stochastic Calculus
FIN 651.subject: FIN
FIN 651.description: Covers PDEs (Partial Differential Equations) and calculus in a stochastic environment.
FIN 651.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 652.title: Programming in Finance
FIN 652.subject: FIN
FIN 652.description: Addresses programming principles, and programming languages used in financial modeling.
FIN 652.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 653.title: Portfolio Optimization
FIN 653.subject: FIN
FIN 653.description: Introduces students to principles of capital markets, classical portfolio theory, and focus on portfolio optimization.
FIN 653.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 654.title: Financial Derivatives
FIN 654.subject: FIN
FIN 654.description: Will familiarize the students with the mathematical foundation and the application of Futures, Swaps, and Options.
FIN 654.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 655.title: Quantitative Methods in Finance
FIN 655.subject: FIN
FIN 655.description: Focus on financial forecasting and financial econometrics as volatility and correlation modeling.
FIN 655.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 656.title: Insurance and Risk Management
FIN 656.subject: FIN
FIN 656.description: Introduces students to topics in the actuarial science and latest developments in risk management.
FIN 656.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 657.title: Interest Rate/Credit Models
FIN 657.subject: FIN
FIN 657.description: Addresses specific properties of interest rate modelling as mean reversion as well as latest developments in credit risk modelling.
FIN 657.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 658.title: Financial Modelling
FIN 658.subject: FIN
FIN 658.description: Addresses advanced techniques in financial modelling and related fields.
FIN 658.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 659.title: Mortgage/Weather Derivatives
FIN 659.subject: FIN
FIN 659.description: Covers the real estate market, mortgage backed securities (MBSs) and real estate derivatives. Focuses on modelling weather, climate change, and weather derivatives.
FIN 659.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 660.title: Seminar in Finance
FIN 660.subject: FIN
FIN 660.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance.

FIN 661.title: Research Seminar
FIN 661.subject: FIN
FIN 661.description: Students either program a model or write a paper with high practical or scientific merit. Outcome enhances the chances for employment. Represents the culminating experience for students in this program.
FIN 661.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

FIN 688.title: Healthcare Financial Management
FIN 688.subject: FIN
FIN 688.description: Focus on important accounting and financial management principles relevant to management of health services organizations. Designed around a series of cases that examine the issues that confront healthcare managers.

FIN 701.title: Foundations of Finance
FIN 701.subject: FIN
FIN 701.description: First PhD course in finance. Covers basic theory and empirical methodology in asset pricing, provides a concise framework of conceptual knowledge to understand the literature on financial theory and related empirical evidence.
FIN 701.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students only.

FIN 702.title: Seminar in Investments
FIN 702.subject: FIN
FIN 702.description: Covers research issues in investments. Topics include empirical asset pricing tests, characteristics of asset returns, behavioral finance, and investment issues that overlaps with corporate finance, accounting, and economics, etc.
FIN 702.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration, or consent.

FIN 703.title: Corporate Finance
FIN 703.subject: FIN
FIN 703.description: Covers research issues in corporate finance and financial markets. Topics include capital structure theory, corporate governance, corporate innovations, and mergers and acquisitions, etc. Student develop academic research papers that lead to dissertation work.
FIN 703.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: student status in PhD in business administration, or consent.

FIN 704.title: Asian Finance
FIN 704.subject: FIN
FIN 704.description: Provides in-depth review of scholarly journal articles and working papers relevant to Asian-Pacific financial markets to prepare PhD students for scholarly research work focusing on market microstructure, corporate finance, investments.
FIN 704.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration, or consent.

FIN 799.title: Directed Reading and Research
FIN 799.subject: FIN
FIN 799.description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by department chair and the faculty advisor.
FIN 799.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management, or consent.

FISH 600.title: Short Course for Sustainable Fisheries Extension in the Pacific Islands
FISH 600.subject: FISH
FISH 600.description: Introduces students to diverse aspects of the field of fisheries within Hawaiʻi and the Pacific Islands, while building cohort connections and offering the opportunity to network with collaborators.
FISH 600.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FISH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FISH 601.title: Fish and Fisheries
FISH 601.subject: FISH
FISH 601.description: Overview of fish biology, ecology, and fisheries of the world, with an emphasis on the tropical Pacific. Material will range from fish life history to climate impacts on stock assessment.
FISH 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FISH 602.title: Human Dimensions of Fisheries
FISH 602.subject: FISH
FISH 602.description: Students will be exposed to fisheries topics related to marine policy, economics, law, governance, and human health and well-being. Students will build on the material from FISH 601 - Fish and Fisheries .
FISH 602.prereq_raw: FISH 601 with a minimum grade of B.
FISH 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FISH 603.title: Community Fisheries in Oceania
FISH 603.subject: FISH
FISH 603.description: Explores Pacific communities’ fisheries management, cultural practices, and reciprocal relationships, highlighting their beliefs, traditions, and innovations in sustaining marine resources for present and future generations.

FISH 615.title: Bayesian Methods for Fisheries
FISH 615.subject: FISH
FISH 615.description: Provides an introduction to statistical modeling in a Bayesian framework using computation tools with applications to fisheries sciences.
FISH 615.prereq_raw: B or better in BIOL 220 or ECON 321 or MATH 372 , or their equivalent, or instructor approval.
FISH 615.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FISH 620.title: Marine Species Distribution Models
FISH 620.subject: FISH
FISH 620.description: Introduction to marine species distribution models (SDMs) using geographic information systems (GIS). Students will learn the theoretical basis for SDMs, pre-processing geospatial data, using SDM methods, and evaluating model outputs.

FISH 625.title: The Western Pacific Regional Fishery Management Council
FISH 625.subject: FISH
FISH 625.description: Introduces the scientific and policy basis for federal fisheries management in the Western Pacific region. Students learn about the management process and attend a Council meeting to interact with stakeholders.

FISH 630.title: Tropical Fisheries Field Studies
FISH 630.subject: FISH
FISH 630.description: Introduces the complexities of tropical marine fisheries through an intensive field study experience. Students learn foundational concepts in fish biology and fisheries ecology, fishery stock assessment and management, and social-ecological methods in an immersive environment.

FISH 660.title: Fisheries Oceanography: From Physics to Landings
FISH 660.subject: FISH
FISH 660.description: Overview of how oceanographic processes influence the distribution, life history, and abundance of fishery-relevant species. Topics will largely center on applications to Hawaiʻi, tropical/sub-tropical ecosystems, and the broader Pacific.
FISH 660.prereq_raw: C or better in OCN 620 or OCN 621 , and a background in biological oceanography and/or physical oceanography required.

FISH 750.title: Topics in Sustainable Fisheries
FISH 750.subject: FISH
FISH 750.description: Lecture and discussion on topics in sustainable fisheries, including fisheries biology, fisheries science, fisheries policy, fisheries of Oceania and their cultural setting.
FISH 750.prereq_raw: B or better in FISH 600 and FISH 601 , or consent.

FMCH 532.title: Family Medicine and Community Health Longitudinal Clerkship
FMCH 532.subject: FMCH
FMCH 532.description: 5.5-month ambulatory clerkship. Students learn history taking, physical exam skills, and management of family medicine patients. Emphasis on behavioral care, caring for the underserved, sports medicine, preventive care, and common acute/chronic ambulatory problems.
FMCH 532.coreq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.

FMCH 545B.title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health: primary care preceptorship
FMCH 545B.subject: FMCH
FMCH 545B.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6).
FMCH 545B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MED majors only for (G).

FMCH 545C.title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health: topics in community health
FMCH 545C.subject: FMCH
FMCH 545C.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6).
FMCH 545C.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MED majors only for (G).

FMCH 545D.title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health: sub-internship in family medicine
FMCH 545D.subject: FMCH
FMCH 545D.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6).
FMCH 545D.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MED majors only for (G).

FMCH 545E.title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health: extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneious
FMCH 545E.subject: FMCH
FMCH 545E.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6).
FMCH 545E.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MED majors only for (G).

FMCH 545F.title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health: sports medicine preceptorship
FMCH 545F.subject: FMCH
FMCH 545F.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6).
FMCH 545F.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MED majors only for (G).

FMCH 545G.title: Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health: longitudinal underserved care preceptorship
FMCH 545G.subject: FMCH
FMCH 545G.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6).
FMCH 545G.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MED majors only for (G).

FR 110.title: Intensive French-Elementary
FR 110.subject: FR
FR 110.description: Content of FR 101 - FR 102 covered in one semester.

FR 210.title: Intensive French-Intermediate
FR 210.subject: FR
FR 210.description: Content of FR 201 - FR 202 covered in one semester.

FR 258.title: Intermediate French Abroad
FR 258.subject: FR
FR 258.description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the second-year level in French language and culture in a French-speaking country.

FR 301.title: French Phonetics
FR 301.subject: FR
FR 301.description: Analysis of phonological system; methods of teaching pronunciation; understanding various types of spontaneous speech. Drills in pronunciation, intonation, stress, and rhythm.
FR 301.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 302.title: Reading in French
FR 302.subject: FR
FR 302.description: Development of language skills through reading of cultural and literary texts.
FR 302.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 306.title: Structure of French
FR 306.subject: FR
FR 306.description: Structure of contemporary French as analyzed by descriptive linguists.
FR 306.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 309.title: Business French
FR 309.subject: FR
FR 309.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 311.title: Conversation
FR 311.subject: FR
FR 311.description: Systematic practice for control of spoken French. Further development of vocabulary for accurate, mature expression.
FR 311.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 312.title: Composition
FR 312.subject: FR
FR 312.description: Emphasis on strengthening facility with language through further training in syntax, structure, and composition writing.
FR 312.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 321.title: Advanced Conversation
FR 321.subject: FR
FR 321.description: Systematic and advanced practice for control of spoken French, advanced development for accurate, mature expression.

FR 331.title: Survey of French Literature
FR 331.subject: FR
FR 331.prereq_raw: FR 311 (or concurrent) and FR 312 ; only FR 311 may be concurrent.

FR 332.title: Survey of French Literature
FR 332.subject: FR
FR 332.prereq_raw: FR 311 (or concurrent) and FR 312 ; only FR 311 may be concurrent.

FR 358.title: Third-Level French Abroad
FR 358.subject: FR
FR 358.description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in French language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a French-speaking country.
FR 358.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 360.title: Intensive Third-Level French Abroad
FR 360.subject: FR
FR 360.description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in French language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a French-speaking country.
FR 360.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 361.title: Contemporary French Civilization
FR 361.subject: FR
FR 361.description: Survey of culture and institutions of modern France.
FR 361.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 364.title: Survey of French Civilization
FR 364.subject: FR
FR 364.description: A historical survey of the development of French culture. The course is interdisciplinary, focusing on the relations between politics, literature, science, and the arts.
FR 364.prereq_raw: FR 202 or FR 210 or FR 259 or consent.

FR 391B.title: Topics in French Literature: French film
FR 391B.subject: FR
FR 391B.description: (B) French film; (C) the Fantastic; (D) Francophone literature.

FR 391C.title: Topics in French Literature: the Fantastic
FR 391C.subject: FR
FR 391C.description: (B) French film; (C) the Fantastic; (D) Francophone literature.

FR 391D.title: Topics in French Literature: Francophone literature
FR 391D.subject: FR
FR 391D.description: (B) French film; (C) the Fantastic; (D) Francophone literature.

FR 399.title: Directed Reading
FR 399.subject: FR
FR 399.description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision.

FR 405.title: Advanced Oral and Written Expression
FR 405.subject: FR
FR 405.description: Further development of listening, comprehension, speaking, and writing skills through viewing of French videotapes, reading French newspapers, frequent oral and written reports.
FR 405.prereq_raw: FR 311 and FR 312 , or FR 306 , or FR 358 , or FR 360 ; or consent.

FR 406.title: French-English Translation
FR 406.subject: FR
FR 406.description: Practice in techniques based on contrastive linguistics. Translation of texts from various fields from French into English and the reverse.
FR 406.prereq_raw: FR 306 or FR 309 , and FR 312 ; or consent.

FR 408.title: Masterpieces of Medieval Literature
FR 408.subject: FR
FR 408.description: Samplings from epic, novel, verse and prose, tale, lyric poetry, chronicle, theater, didactic literature. Elementary readings in original text in editions giving modern French translation.

FR 409.title: Advanced Language Study: French
FR 409.subject: FR
FR 409.description: Advanced course in spoken and written French with intensive review of alternative grammatical structures and shades of meaning in the modern language. Graduates who have not taken prerequisites may request consent.
FR 409.prereq_raw: FR 306 or FR 405 (or equivalent); or consent.

FR 410.title: Masterpieces of 16th-Century Literature
FR 410.subject: FR
FR 410.description: Samplings from all major writers of the period. Readings in original text in editions giving modern French equivalents for difficult words.

FR 411.title: Masterpieces of 17th-Century Literature
FR 411.subject: FR
FR 411.description: Principal works of major dramatists: Corneille, Moliere, Racine. Principal movements and major authors of nondramatic prose and poetry.

FR 417.title: 19th Century French Prose and Poetry
FR 417.subject: FR
FR 417.description: Study of representative prose and poetry of the major trends of 19th century France: romanticism, realism, symbolism, aestheticism.

FR 421.title: 20th-Century French Theater
FR 421.subject: FR
FR 421.description: Major French playwrights and their works: Claudel, Giraudoux, Anouilh, Sartre, Camus, etc.

FR 423.title: 20th Century French Prose and Poetry
FR 423.subject: FR
FR 423.description: Study of representative prose and poetry of the major trends of 20th century France: modernism, surrealism, existentialism, postmodernism and multiculturalism.

FR 458.title: Fourth-Level French Abroad
FR 458.subject: FR
FR 458.description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the fourth-year level in French linguistics, civilization, culture, and literature in a French-speaking country.

FR 460.title: Intensive Fourth-Level French Abroad
FR 460.subject: FR
FR 460.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-year level in French language, culture and literature in a French-speaking country. For semester programs only.

FR 491B.title: Seminar in French Literature: French literature by period
FR 491B.subject: FR
FR 491B.description: (B) French literature by period; (C) Francophone literature; (D) French film; (E) topic in French literature.
FR 491B.prereq_raw: FR 331 (or concurrent) and FR 332 (or concurrent), or consent.

FR 491C.title: Seminar in French Literature: Frncophone literature
FR 491C.subject: FR
FR 491C.description: (B) French literature by period; (C) Francophone literature; (D) French film; (E) topic in French literature.
FR 491C.prereq_raw: FR 331 (or concurrent) and FR 332 (or concurrent), or consent.

FR 491D.title: Seminar in French Literature: French film
FR 491D.subject: FR
FR 491D.description: (B) French literature by period; (C) Francophone literature; (D) French film; (E) topic in French literature.
FR 491D.prereq_raw: FR 331 (or concurrent) and FR 332 (or concurrent), or consent.

FR 491E.title: Seminar in French Literature: topic in French literature
FR 491E.subject: FR
FR 491E.description: (B) French literature by period; (C) Francophone literature; (D) French film; (E) topic in French literature.
FR 491E.prereq_raw: FR 311 (or concurrent) and FR 332 (or concurrent), or consent.

FR 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
FR 499.subject: FR
FR 499.description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision.

FSHN 112.title: Food Service Safety and Sanitation
FSHN 112.subject: FSHN
FSHN 112.description: Principles and procedures of sanitation and safety in the food service industry, including the study of foodborne illnesses, biological, chemical, physical hazards and cross-contamination as they may occur during the flow of food.

FSHN 141.title: Culture and Cuisine: The Global Diversity of Food
FSHN 141.subject: FSHN
FSHN 141.description: A timeline of the world history of food and how it relates to culture, diversity, ethnicity, and religion. International food demonstrations and tastings included.

FSHN 181.title: Introduction to Food Preparation
FSHN 181.subject: FSHN
FSHN 181.description: Lectures, discussions, and demonstrations on how food components contribute to the functional, sensory, and safety characteristics of foods, and what changes occur in foods due to preparation, processing, and storage.

FSHN 181L.title: Food Preparation Lab
FSHN 181L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 181L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments in foods emphasizing ingredient function and standard preparation methods for food groups.

FSHN 185.title: The Science of Human Nutrition
FSHN 185.subject: FSHN
FSHN 185.description: Integration of natural science concepts basic to the study of human nutrition. Emphasis on nutrient requirements of healthy individuals, food sources, functions of nutrients through a Pacific context.

FSHN 244.title: Comparative Nutrition
FSHN 244.subject: FSHN
FSHN 244.description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.
FSHN 244.prereq_raw: ( ANSC 200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C.

FSHN 311.title: Food Service Systems Management
FSHN 311.subject: FSHN
FSHN 311.description: Critical and essential aspects of management and effective leadership practices to direct and delivery quality foodservices. Focus on the role and competencies of the Registered Dietitian (RD) working in these environments.
FSHN 311.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 181 and FSHN 181L (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

FSHN 312.title: Food Service Production and Operations
FSHN 312.subject: FSHN
FSHN 312.description: Principles and procedures of menu planning, quantity food production, production scheduling, recipe adaptation, equipment operation, and formula costing. Principles of procurement including purchasing, selection, storage of equipment and quantity foods.
FSHN 312.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 181 and FSHN 181L ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

FSHN 322.title: Marketing Nutrition and Food
FSHN 322.subject: FSHN
FSHN 322.description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental marketing principles applied to nutrition and food. Will include concepts such as the psychology of food purchasing decisions and consumer behavior. Field trips and group projects included.
FSHN 322.prereq_raw: FSHN 181 / FSHN 181L , FSHN 185 , FSHN 312 ; or consent.

FSHN 350.title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
FSHN 350.subject: FSHN
FSHN 350.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.
FSHN 350.prereq_raw: FSHN 181 or FSHN 185 or ANSC 200 or ANSC 201 .

FSHN 360.title: Applied Professional Skills in Nutrition
FSHN 360.subject: FSHN
FSHN 360.description: Will apply skills in technology, research, and career development to nutrition. Students will identify evidence-based nutrition information and demonstrate their academic skill sets for future professional success through technology.
FSHN 360.prereq_raw: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

FSHN 370.title: Lifespan Nutrition
FSHN 370.subject: FSHN
FSHN 370.description: Physiological changes and nutritional requirements during human life stages: prepregnancy, pregnancy, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
FSHN 370.prereq_raw: B or better in FSHN 185 ; C or better in CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ; C or better in PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L (or concurrent).

FSHN 381.title: Experimental Foods
FSHN 381.subject: FSHN
FSHN 381.description: Experimental approach to study food preparation problems. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports. Subject matter used to practice critical thinking and problem solving skills.
FSHN 381.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 181 / FSHN 181L , CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C.

FSHN 381L.title: Experimental Foods Laboratory
FSHN 381L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 381L.description: Experimental approach to study food preparation, food formulation, and sensory evaluation with laboratory exercises in a certified kitchen environment. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports.
FSHN 381L.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 181 / FSHN 181L , CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of D.

FSHN 389.title: Nutritional Assessment
FSHN 389.subject: FSHN
FSHN 389.description: Addresses concepts and uses of nutrition assessment tools at individual and community levels. Students will be introduced to national surveys and new, more sophisticated body composition measurements. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
FSHN 389.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 185 and FSHN 370 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.

FSHN 403.title: Microbiology of Foods
FSHN 403.subject: FSHN
FSHN 403.description: Microorganisms encountered in foods; types of food spoilage; microbial hazards in food; methods of food preservation.
FSHN 403.prereq_raw: ( MICR 130 and MICR 140L , or MICR 351 and MICR 351L ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

FSHN 411.title: Food Engineering
FSHN 411.subject: FSHN
FSHN 411.description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
FSHN 411.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 , CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

FSHN 420.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
FSHN 420.subject: FSHN
FSHN 420.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
FSHN 420.prereq_raw: ( ECE 160 , ECE 211 , and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

FSHN 430.title: Food Chemistry
FSHN 430.subject: FSHN
FSHN 430.description: Chemical properties of food constituents studied in relationship to their effects on processing, nutrition, and spoilage.

FSHN 430L.title: Food Chemistry Lab
FSHN 430L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 430L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical methods in the study of food constituents-proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, pigments, enzymes, etc.

FSHN 440.title: Food Safety
FSHN 440.subject: FSHN
FSHN 440.description: Discussion of potential microbiological, parasitic, chemical, and natural food hazards; food laws and standards; and related aspects of consumer protection.
FSHN 440.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 181 , BIOL 171 , and CHEM 272 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

FSHN 445.title: Food Quality Control
FSHN 445.subject: FSHN
FSHN 445.description: Fundamental principles of quality control in the food industry: measurement of quality parameters, utilization and integration of the individual test procedures into grades and standards of quality, sampling, and reporting results.

FSHN 451.title: Community Nutrition and Nutrition Education
FSHN 451.subject: FSHN
FSHN 451.description: (4 Lec) Concepts and methods of nutrition program planning and nutrition education; analysis of nutritional problems of local, national, and international communities; strategies used to educate groups or individuals.
FSHN 451.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 370 and either HDFS 380 or NREM 310 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

FSHN 454.title: Foundation of Childhood Obesity Prevention in the Pacific
FSHN 454.subject: FSHN
FSHN 454.description: Provide students with a basic overview of the causes and effects of childhood obesity, evidence-based approaches, community-based research, and policies to prevent childhood obesity as it relates to the Pacific region.
FSHN 454.prereq_raw: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

FSHN 455.title: Childhood Anthropometric and Dietary Assessment Field Techniques
FSHN 455.subject: FSHN
FSHN 455.description: Teaches techniques for measuring anthropometry and collecting dietary intake in children. Online course imitates hands-on training through partnering with local organizations and the use of technology.
FSHN 455.prereq_raw: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

FSHN 456.title: Child Health and Nutrition Monitoring
FSHN 456.subject: FSHN
FSHN 456.description: Covers topics related to health and nutritional status monitoring and surveillance, including epidemiology, biostatistics, health and nutrition surveillance systems, and the uses of technology for conducting these activities.
FSHN 456.prereq_raw: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

FSHN 457.title: Culture and Child Health in the Pacific
FSHN 457.subject: FSHN
FSHN 457.description: In-depth study of Pacific culture, land, people, and history and its relationship to child health. Explores cultural competency, cultural safety, and multidisciplinary approaches to promote a healthy Pacific. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.
FSHN 457.prereq_raw: FSHN 185 (with a minimum grade of B).

FSHN 460.title: Food Processing Operations
FSHN 460.subject: FSHN
FSHN 460.description: Principles and applications of food dehydration, thermal processing, low temperature preservation, chemical and biochemical preservation, irradiation, packaging, manufacturing, plant sanitation, water and waste management.

FSHN 467.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
FSHN 467.subject: FSHN
FSHN 467.description: Development of dietary, anthropometric and clinical lab assessment skills measuring nutritional status. Understanding pathophysiology of disease processes, medical terminology and nutritional intervention, utilizing case studies.
FSHN 467.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 389 and FSHN 486 ) with a minimum grade of C or consent.

FSHN 468.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
FSHN 468.subject: FSHN
FSHN 468.description: Understanding of the pathophysiology of disease processes and nutritional intervention, using medical terminology and case studies.
FSHN 468.prereq_raw: HWST 467 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

FSHN 469.title: Nutrition Counseling Skills
FSHN 469.subject: FSHN
FSHN 469.description: Theory and practice in nutritional counseling. Combined lecture and discussion on nutrition/dietary counseling. Knowledge and theories. Application through lab experiences including role playing, case presentations, and performing actual counseling sessions.

FSHN 475.title: Applied Human Nutrition
FSHN 475.subject: FSHN
FSHN 475.description: Application of basic nutrition principles; includes sources and functions of essential nutrients and food patterns compatible with nutrient needs, health, disease prevention, and sustainability. Intended for undergraduate and graduate students.
FSHN 475.prereq_raw: CHEM 161 (or higher) or BIOC 241 (or higher); PHYL 141 , BIOL 171 ; or consent.

FSHN 476.title: Cultural Aspects of Food Habits
FSHN 476.subject: FSHN
FSHN 476.description: Study of eating from behavioral perspectives. Implications for health practitioners and health education.
FSHN 476.prereq_raw: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher or SOC 100 or higher or PSY 100 or higher.

children.text: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher

FSHN 477.title: Food Analysis
FSHN 477.subject: FSHN
FSHN 477.description: Principles of sample preparation and chemical and physical analysis of food components using current methodology.
FSHN 477.prereq_raw: FSHN 430 ; and CHEM 162 or higher; and BIOL 402 or MBBE 402 or PEPS 402.

FSHN 477L.title: Food Analysis Lab
FSHN 477L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 477L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical and physical methods for the identification and quantitation of food components.

FSHN 480.title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
FSHN 480.subject: FSHN
FSHN 480.description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.
FSHN 480.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 185 , and PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 or PHYL 301 ) with a minimum grade of C.

FSHN 485.title: Nutritional Biochemistry I
FSHN 485.subject: FSHN
FSHN 485.description: Metabolism and biochemistry of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, cellular/molecular functions in human nutrition; integration of metabolic pathways; energy metabolism and balance, including relevance to chronic disease.
FSHN 485.prereq_raw: FSHN 185 ; PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L or PHYL 302 / PHYL 302L ; BIOC 341 or higher (or concurrent) or MBBE 402 (or concurrent); or consent.

FSHN 486.title: Nutritional Biochemistry II
FSHN 486.subject: FSHN
FSHN 486.description: Metabolism and biochemistry of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, and cellular/molecular functions in human nutrition; relevance to establishing nutrient requirements and to mechanisms of chronic disease.
FSHN 486.prereq_raw: FSHN 485 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

FSHN 488.title: Obesity, Science, and Issues
FSHN 488.subject: FSHN
FSHN 488.description: In-depth study of obesity, including research, etiology, treatment, and prevention.
FSHN 488.prereq_raw: FSHN 485 with a minimum grade of C.

FSHN 491.title: Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition
FSHN 491.subject: FSHN
FSHN 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems, or laboratory experiments.

FSHN 492.title: Field Experience
FSHN 492.subject: FSHN
FSHN 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.
FSHN 492.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior standing in FSHN.

FSHN 494.title: Food Science Capstone
FSHN 494.subject: FSHN
FSHN 494.description: Field practicum designed to integrate knowledge from previous FSHN courses to develop novel and innovative food products. Students deal with shelflife, marketing, packaging, labeling, sensory evaluation, and quality assurance.
FSHN 494.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 381 and FSHN 460 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

FSHN 601.title: The Science of Food Systems
FSHN 601.subject: FSHN
FSHN 601.description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.
FSHN 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

FSHN 607.title: Advanced Food Science I
FSHN 607.subject: FSHN
FSHN 607.description: Advanced topics in chemical and physical characteristics of foods as well as their role in human nutrition.
FSHN 607.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent.

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics,
biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected;

FSHN 608.title: Advanced Food Science II
FSHN 608.subject: FSHN
FSHN 608.description: Advances in sensory quality and evaluation, deterioration of foods and food safety, as well as food processing technology.
FSHN 608.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent.

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics,
biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected;

FSHN 609.title: Advanced Food Safety
FSHN 609.subject: FSHN
FSHN 609.description: Real and perceived food hazards, their ethical issues and implications, advanced emerging topics in food safety, and controls, including laws and regulations of food safety issues and public perception of food safety will be discussed.
FSHN 609.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in biochemistry, microbiology, food processing, physics and organic chemistry. Basic food science knowledge is required; or consent.

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in biochemistry, microbiology, food processing, physics
organic chemistry. Basic food science knowledge is required;

FSHN 633.title: International Nutrition
FSHN 633.subject: FSHN
FSHN 633.description: Analysis of major nutrition problems in developing countries. Comparative review of the design, implementation, and evaluation of programs to intervene in the development of malnutrition.

FSHN 641.title: Dietetics Management in Food and Nutrition Services
FSHN 641.subject: FSHN
FSHN 641.description: Focuses on the role and competencies of the Registered Dietitian working in these environments. Managing human resources, food, equipment, and facilities to deliver quality products and services are an integral component in the dietetics profession.

FSHN 642.title: Dietetics Management in Food Production and Operations
FSHN 642.subject: FSHN
FSHN 642.description: Principles and procedures of menu planning, quantity food production, production scheduling, recipe adaptation, equipment operation, and formula costing. Principles of procurement including purchasing, selection, storage of equipment and quantity foods.

FSHN 650.title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
FSHN 650.subject: FSHN
FSHN 650.description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included.
FSHN 650.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

FSHN 652.title: Information Research Skills
FSHN 652.subject: FSHN
FSHN 652.description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

FSHN 657.title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
FSHN 657.subject: FSHN
FSHN 657.description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review.

FSHN 660.title: Micronutrients: Vitamins and Minerals
FSHN 660.subject: FSHN
FSHN 660.description: Covers selected vitamins and minerals, their discovery history and research use, why selected animal models are chosen for studying micronutrients, how micronutrients are metabolized within the body, their interactions, and environmental concerns.
FSHN 660.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FSHN, CMB, ASNC, MB, and MBBE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FSHN 667.title: Dietetics Supervised Practice
FSHN 667.subject: FSHN
FSHN 667.description: ISPP activities and assignments completed at designed facilities in community, clinical, food service, and other settings that stress planning, delivery, and evaluation of dietetics services to individuals and populations.
FSHN 667.prereq_raw: admission to the Individualized Supervised Practice Pathway program and consent.

children.text: admission to the Individualized Supervised Practice Pathway program

FSHN 667.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MS Nutritional Sciences students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FSHN 668.title: Advanced Topics in Dietetics
FSHN 668.subject: FSHN
FSHN 668.description: Advanced topics in professional dietetics practice. Students will further their knowledge and skills in professional practice areas of dietetics; including clinical, community, and food systems management.
FSHN 668.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MS Nutritional Sciences students only.

FSHN 681.title: Seminar in Food and Nutritional Sciences
FSHN 681.subject: FSHN
FSHN 681.description: Student presentation of literature reviews and research.

FSHN 682.title: Topics in Nutritional Sciences
FSHN 682.subject: FSHN
FSHN 682.description: Advanced topics in nutritional sciences, from basic to applied research, including current issues in nutrition and critical analysis of current research literature.

FSHN 683.title: Global Nutrition
FSHN 683.subject: FSHN
FSHN 683.description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

FSHN 684.title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
FSHN 684.subject: FSHN
FSHN 684.description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.

FSHN 685.title: Nutrition and Disease: Cellular and Molecular Aspects
FSHN 685.subject: FSHN
FSHN 685.description: In-depth lecture, discussion, and student presentations on selected topics relating nutrition to the etiology and prevention of chronic diseases at the cellular and molecular level.
FSHN 685.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 485 and FSHN 486 ) with a minimum grade of C; statistics; or consent.

FSHN 686.title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
FSHN 686.subject: FSHN
FSHN 686.description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutritionrelated issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

FSHN 687.title: Advanced Lab Techniques
FSHN 687.subject: FSHN
FSHN 687.description: (1 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.
FSHN 687.prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent and FSHN 477 and MBBE 402 / MBBE 402L ; or BIOC 441 .

FSHN 688.title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
FSHN 688.subject: FSHN
FSHN 688.description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored.
FSHN 688.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

FSHN 689.title: Nutritional Epidemiology
FSHN 689.subject: FSHN
FSHN 689.description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

FSHN 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
FSHN 695.subject: FSHN
FSHN 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B Master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
FSHN 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in nutritional sciences.

FSHN 701.title: Topics in Food Science
FSHN 701.subject: FSHN
FSHN 701.description: Advanced topics in food science and technology, from basic to applied research, including current issues in food science and technology and critical analysis of current research literature.
FSHN 701.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

FSHN 749.title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
FSHN 749.subject: FSHN
FSHN 749.description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.
FSHN 749.prereq_raw: 663 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent.

FSHN 784.title: Dietary Fiber, Bioactive Food Components and Health
FSHN 784.subject: FSHN
FSHN 784.description: Lecture/discussion of current research on gut physiology, gut microbes, dietary fiber, bioactive food components, and their impact on health, including colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, heart disease, diabetes, and immune function.
FSHN 784.prereq_raw: FSHN 485 and FSHN 486 (or equivalent), statistics, physiology; or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent), statistics, physiology; or consent

FSHN 785.title: Diet and Cancer Seminar
FSHN 785.subject: FSHN
FSHN 785.description: Presentation-discussion of selected research topics in the field of diet-cancer relationships including: nutritional epidemiology of cancer, diet and supplement intervention trials, and cellular/molecular effects of diet on cancer pathophysiology.

FSHN 800.title: Dissertation Research
FSHN 800.subject: FSHN
FSHN 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation in nutrition.
FSHN 800.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD in Nutrition. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

GEO 101.title: The Natural Environment
GEO 101.subject: GEO
GEO 101.description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards.

GEO 101L.title: The Natural Environment Lab
GEO 101L.subject: GEO
GEO 101L.description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers.

GEO 102.title: World Regional Geography
GEO 102.subject: GEO
GEO 102.description: World’s major cultural regions; geographic aspects of contemporary economic, social, political conditions.

GEO 104.title: Digital Earth
GEO 104.subject: GEO
GEO 104.description: Cartographic representation and meaning in a digital age. Earth models, map projections, coordinate systems, scale, distance, and direction. Data types and transformations in graphic and digital representation. Manual, automated, and web-based map making and analysis.

GEO 151.title: Geography and Contemporary Society
GEO 151.subject: GEO
GEO 151.description: Elements of economic geography and resource management, population and urban geography; application to current problems of developed and underdeveloped worlds.

GEO 300.title: Introduction to Climatology
GEO 300.subject: GEO
GEO 300.description: Elements and controls of climate. World patterns of insolation, temperature, evaporation, precipitation, atmospheric circulation. Climatic classifications.
GEO 300.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 , or consent.

GEO 302.title: Global Environmental Issues
GEO 302.subject: GEO
GEO 302.description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment.

GEO 303.title: General Geomorphology
GEO 303.subject: GEO
GEO 303.description: Introduction to geomorphological concepts, process mechanics, and relationships between forms and processes. Emphasis on various subdisciplines of geomorphology: coastal hillslopes, fluvial, aeolean, and glacial.
GEO 303.prereq_raw: ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L .

GEO 305.title: Water and Society
GEO 305.subject: GEO
GEO 305.description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
GEO 305.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 309.title: Introduction to Biogeography
GEO 309.subject: GEO
GEO 309.description: Introduction to ecosystem concept; environmental adaptations for energy and nutrient transfer; characteristics, dynamics, productivity, and distribution of principal vegetation communities. Human dominance.
GEO 309.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 310.title: Introduction to Planning
GEO 310.subject: GEO
GEO 310.description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawaiʻi planning-research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.
GEO 310.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

GEO 320.title: Economic Geography
GEO 320.subject: GEO
GEO 320.description: Examines how factors of production like land, labor and capital; economic activities like consumption, trade, production, and investments; and institutions like state, markets, and corporations alter economic space.

GEO 322.title: Globalization and Environment
GEO 322.subject: GEO
GEO 322.description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change. Junior standing or higher.

GEO 324.title: Geography of Global Tourism
GEO 324.subject: GEO
GEO 324.description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. Emphasis on Writing.
GEO 324.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

GEO 325.title: Geography, Environment, and Society
GEO 325.subject: GEO
GEO 325.description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems.

GEO 330.title: Culture and Environment
GEO 330.subject: GEO
GEO 330.description: Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures.

GEO 333.title: Islands and Archipelagos
GEO 333.subject: GEO
GEO 333.description: Applies an island studies perspective to critically evaluate the commonalities and differences across islands and archipelagos in several world regions. Examines how island geographies influence social identities and movements and are impacted by environmental conditions. Sophomore standing or higher.

GEO 335.title: Politics, Nations, and States
GEO 335.subject: GEO
GEO 335.description: Examines the political organization of space in the sovereign state system. Contemporary and historical analyses of boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, nations, nationalism, and territory. Emphasis on written instruction.
GEO 335.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 340.title: Geography of North America
GEO 340.subject: GEO
GEO 340.description: Overview of the physical and cultural geography. Regions and characters. Patterns of population, natural resources, industry, agriculture, and transportation/communication networks.
GEO 340.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 102 or GEO 151 , or consent.

GEO 343.title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
GEO 343.subject: GEO
GEO 343.description: Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality.

GEO 352.title: Geography of Japan
GEO 352.subject: GEO
GEO 352.description: Regional synthesis of physical and cultural features; economic, social, political geography; origins and development of cities.

GEO 353.title: Geography of China
GEO 353.subject: GEO
GEO 353.description: Topics: environmental parameters and resource base, ecological control and resource management, institutional and technological transformation of agriculture, industrial potential and industrial location, settlement patterns and rural urban symbiosis.

GEO 355.title: Geography of South Asia
GEO 355.subject: GEO
GEO 355.description: An interdisciplinary course on South Asia covering contemporary debates and social movements pertaining to caste, gender, class, religion, region, labor, law, and development. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

GEO 356.title: Geography of Southeast Asia
GEO 356.subject: GEO
GEO 356.description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change.

GEO 365.title: Geography of the Pacific
GEO 365.subject: GEO
GEO 365.description: Physical character of the Pacific; cultural, political, economic geography of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia (except Hawaiʻi).

GEO 366.title: Geography of Honolulu
GEO 366.subject: GEO
GEO 366.description: Development of Honolulu and Oʻahu from 1778. Evolution of function, land use, and social patterns. Contemporary planning and environmental issues arising from urban growth.

GEO 368.title: Geography of Hawaiʻi
GEO 368.subject: GEO
GEO 368.description: Regional, physical, cultural geography. Detailed study of people and resources.

GEO 370.title: UAV and Aerial Photography
GEO 370.subject: GEO
GEO 370.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle systems) and the measurement, interpretation, analysis, and use of photography acquired by UAV and other aerial systems.

GEO 375.title: Introduction to Cartography and Air Photo
GEO 375.subject: GEO
GEO 375.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of cartography: compilation and measurement from aerial photographs, alternate forms of data presentation, symbolism, design, and map projection.

GEO 376.title: Map Design and Production
GEO 376.subject: GEO
GEO 376.description: (3 2-hr Lab) Compilation, design and production of maps for presentations, research, and illustration using artists and mapping software.
GEO 376.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 380.title: Statistical Methods in Geography
GEO 380.subject: GEO
GEO 380.description: Quantitative statistical methods will be explored for describing and interpreting geographic/environmental phenomena. Topics will include data display, measurement, sampling, spatial statistics, dimensional analysis, nonparametric and parametric models.
GEO 380.prereq_raw: ( GEO 101 or GEO 102 or GEO 151 ) or concurrent or consent.

GEO 388.title: Introduction to GIS
GEO 388.subject: GEO
GEO 388.description: Design, implementation, and use. Database construction and documentation. Techniques for spatial data manipulation and display. Evaluation of existing systems. Student research projects.

GEO 399.title: Directed Reading
GEO 399.subject: GEO
GEO 399.description: Limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in geography.

GEO 400.title: Vegetation and the Climate System
GEO 400.subject: GEO
GEO 400.description: Role of vegetation in the climate system; links to hydrology and biogeochemical cycling; vegetation and climate history; evolution of terrestrial ecosystems; effects of global warming.
GEO 400.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

GEO 401.title: Climate Change
GEO 401.subject: GEO
GEO 401.description: Approaches to the study of past and future climate change.
GEO 401.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

GEO 402.title: Agricultural Climatology
GEO 402.subject: GEO
GEO 402.description: Analyzing climatic data; relation to photosynthesis, phenological development, and crop yields. Crop-weather models as guides to improved land-use planning and agronomic practices.
GEO 402.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

GEO 403.title: Fluvial Geomorphology
GEO 403.subject: GEO
GEO 403.description: Introduction to the single most important geomorphic agent shaping the terrestrial environment. Focus on fluvial process, fluvial dynamics, fluvial landforms, and sediment transport.
GEO 403.prereq_raw: GEO 101 / GEO 101L or GEO 303 or ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L .

GEO 404.title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
GEO 404.subject: GEO
GEO 404.description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control.
GEO 404.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 405.title: Water in the Environment
GEO 405.subject: GEO
GEO 405.description: Water fluxes in the environment. Occurrence and movement of water; methods of quantification. Water balance of soil-plant system: precipitation, interception, infiltration, runoff, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and groundwater recharge.
GEO 405.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

GEO 408.title: Conservation and Evolutionary Biogeography
GEO 408.subject: GEO
GEO 408.description: Theories and techniques for the analysis of spatial microevolutionary patterns, taught from an interdisciplinary perspective. Examples and readings emphasize Hawaiʻi and the Pacific region.
GEO 408.prereq_raw: either GEO 309 , BIOL 265 or BIOL 487 , or consent.

GEO 409.title: Cultural Biogeography
GEO 409.subject: GEO
GEO 409.description: Coevolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens.
GEO 409.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 410.title: Human Role in Environmental Change
GEO 410.subject: GEO
GEO 410.description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
