GEO 410.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of GEO 101 , BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 and either GEO 322 or BIOL 310 ; or consent.

GEO 411.title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
GEO 411.subject: GEO
GEO 411.description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
GEO 411.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 412.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
GEO 412.subject: GEO
GEO 412.description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
GEO 412.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 413.title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
GEO 413.subject: GEO
GEO 413.description: Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions.
GEO 413.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher.

GEO 414.title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
GEO 414.subject: GEO
GEO 414.description: Investigation of the forces behind natural and technological hazards, and human actions that reduce or increase vulnerability to natural disasters. Junior standing or higher.

GEO 415.title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
GEO 415.subject: GEO
GEO 415.description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

GEO 421.title: Urban Geography
GEO 421.subject: GEO
GEO 421.description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.
GEO 421.prereq_raw: GEO 102 or GEO 151 or GEO 330 , or consent.

GEO 422.title: Agriculture, Food and Society
GEO 422.subject: GEO
GEO 422.description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to nonmajors.
GEO 422.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 423.title: Marine Policy
GEO 423.subject: GEO
GEO 423.description: Introduction to the law and policies concerning the marine environment, commerce and security. Role of science, law and politics in historical and current policies for maritime trades, navigation safety, marine resources, and marine exploration.
GEO 423.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 424.title: Regional Analysis
GEO 424.subject: GEO
GEO 424.description: Spatial dynamics and environmental implications of urban and rural development. Concepts of regions, process of regional development, patterns of spatial interaction, and theoretical bases for development strategies; emphasis on Hawaiʻi.
GEO 424.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 425.title: Geographies of Popular Culture
GEO 425.subject: GEO
GEO 425.description: Examines contemporary geographical debates related to concepts of discourse, identity, space/place, power, representation, and popular culture. Considers various landscapes of popular culture and how popular culture mediate a sense of place, geopolitics, and identity formation.
GEO 425.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 426.title: Environment, Resources and Society
GEO 426.subject: GEO
GEO 426.description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

GEO 432.title: Tea and Culture
GEO 432.subject: GEO
GEO 432.description: Examines cultural practices of tea in different parts of the world, focusing on history and culture of tea in China, Japan, and England. Also includes changing technologies and economies of tea worldwide. Junior standing or higher.

GEO 433.title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
GEO 433.subject: GEO
GEO 433.description: Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication.

GEO 435.title: Political Geography of Oceans
GEO 435.subject: GEO
GEO 435.description: The geopolitics of oceans and the law of the sea as applied to regions of conflict and cooperation historically and in the present. Emphasis on teaching written communication.
GEO 435.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 436.title: Geography of Peace and War
GEO 436.subject: GEO
GEO 436.description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
GEO 436.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 468.title: Topics in Geography
GEO 468.subject: GEO
GEO 468.description: Selected topics in geography not offered in the regular geography curriculum.
GEO 468.prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 102 or GEO 151 , or consent.

GEO 470.title: Remote Sensing
GEO 470.subject: GEO
GEO 470.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the principles of remote sensing and image processing skills. Topics include electromagnetic spectrum, sensors, aerial photo and satellite imagery interpretation, geometric and radiometric correction, digital image processing. Research project, lab.

GEO 471.title: 3D Mapping and Analysis
GEO 471.subject: GEO
GEO 471.description: Environmental mapping and analysis using 3-dimensional geographical data acquired from high resolution remote sensing systems. Junior standing or higher.

GEO 472.title: Field Mapping
GEO 472.subject: GEO
GEO 472.description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
GEO 472.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

GEO 476.title: Web Mapping
GEO 476.subject: GEO
GEO 476.description: (3 2-hr Lab) Introduction to interactive web mapping techniques for sharing and visualizing various forms of geospatial data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

GEO 487.title: GIS and Spatial Analysis for Social Sciences
GEO 487.subject: GEO
GEO 487.description: Introduction to spacial analysis and GIS for social science studies, using open-source GIS tools to collect, visualize, and analyze social data; public health, socio-economic and social media data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

GEO 489.title: GIS for Environmental Sciences
GEO 489.subject: GEO
GEO 489.description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr lab) Applications of GIS technologies to solve real-world problems in natural and environmental sciences. Research project, lab.

GEO 490.title: Senior Thesis
GEO 490.subject: GEO
GEO 490.description: Preparation of research paper under individual faculty supervision. Recommended for admission to graduate program.
GEO 490.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior GEO major and consent.

GEO 492.title: Practicum in Geography
GEO 492.subject: GEO
GEO 492.description: Internship in applied geography under professional and faculty supervision. Field placement integrated with academic study.
GEO 492.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior major and consent.

GEO 493.title: Capstone Undergraduate Seminar
GEO 493.subject: GEO
GEO 493.description: Current and historical geographic literature provides a background for local and global issues. Through discussion, written reviews, and research reports, the geographic perspective in modern life will be explored.

GEO 499.title: Directed Research
GEO 499.subject: GEO
GEO 499.description: Geography majors conduct research under faculty supervision on a topic of their choice. Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent.
GEO 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GEO majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

GEO 600.title: Seminar in Climatology
GEO 600.subject: GEO
GEO 600.description: Methods of determining energy budget and water balance; applications in agriculture, hydrology, climatic classifications. Theory of climatic change. Bibliography.
GEO 600.prereq_raw: GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 or ATMO 320 ; or consent.

GEO 610.title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
GEO 610.subject: GEO
GEO 610.description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawaiʻi, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

GEO 618.title: Human Environment Systems
GEO 618.subject: GEO
GEO 618.description: Role and potential of systems science in analysis of human environment interaction, especially resource management. Framework and methodology for problem structuring; overview of techniques.
GEO 618.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing with consent.

GEO 620.title: Theories and Policies of Development
GEO 620.subject: GEO
GEO 620.description: Will critically examine what constitutes progress, advancement, or betterment in this highly uneven world, where inter-regional, inter-class, inter-group, and inter-gender differences in development are expanding. Graduate standing only.

GEO 621.title: Coastal Planning and Management
GEO 621.subject: GEO
GEO 621.description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture.

GEO 622.title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
GEO 622.subject: GEO
GEO 622.description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

GEO 637.title: Environment and Development
GEO 637.subject: GEO
GEO 637.description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

GEO 639.title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
GEO 639.subject: GEO
GEO 639.description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy.
GEO 639.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

GEO 654.title: Seminar in Geography of Southeast Asia
GEO 654.subject: GEO

GEO 665.title: Seminar in Geography of the Pacific
GEO 665.subject: GEO
GEO 665.description: Investigation of geographic problems of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia.

GEO 680.title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
GEO 680.subject: GEO
GEO 680.description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included.

GEO 685.title: Human Geography Research Methods
GEO 685.subject: GEO
GEO 685.description: Introduction to research methods in human geography. Explores and provides guided practical experience with research methods and analysis.

GEO 692.title: Faculty Seminar Series
GEO 692.subject: GEO
GEO 692.description: Graduate seminar required of all department MA students and PhD students. Single credit course in which faculty present ongoing research in their fields.

GEO 695.title: Concepts and Theories in Geography
GEO 695.subject: GEO
GEO 695.description: Concepts, theory, models. Geographic approaches to spatial and environmental problems. Required of entering graduate students unless waived by department.

GEO 696.title: Research Design/Methods in Geography
GEO 696.subject: GEO
GEO 696.description: Elements of research design, practical field experience, exposure to research and ideologies, broad exposure to heritage and ethos of the discipline.

GEO 703.title: Geomorphology
GEO 703.subject: GEO
GEO 703.description: Current understanding of geomorphological concepts, processes, and the dynamic relationship between human landscape modification and system response.

GEO 710B.title: Special Topics: regional and locational analysis
GEO 710B.subject: GEO
GEO 710B.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

GEO 710C.title: Special Topics: geography, environment, and culture
GEO 710C.subject: GEO
GEO 710C.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

GEO 710H.title: Special Topics: Multi-objective decision analysis
GEO 710H.subject: GEO
GEO 710H.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

GEO 725.title: Political Ecology
GEO 725.subject: GEO
GEO 725.description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

GEO 728.title: Seminar: Resource Management in Asia-Pacific
GEO 728.subject: GEO
GEO 728.description: Examination of resource management problems in Asia and the Pacific. Problems of resource use-agriculture, forestry, energy, minerals, ocean, air quality.

GEO 735.title: Seminar: Political Geography
GEO 735.subject: GEO
GEO 735.description: Topics vary; may include borders, boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, identity politics, nations and nationalism, social categorization, the sovereign state system, territoriality.
GEO 735.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

GEO 745.title: Seminar: Geographies of Migration
GEO 745.subject: GEO
GEO 745.description: Topics vary; may include immigration, borders, refugees, asylum, climate change, and displacement.

GEO 766.title: Society and Space
GEO 766.subject: GEO
GEO 766.description: Advanced seminar on social production of space. Topics include spatial metaphor in social theory; western spatiality from the renaissance through the enlightenment, modernity and post modernity; and geography of the body, home, landscape, and nation.
GEO 766.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

GEO 788.title: Seminar in Geographical Information Science
GEO 788.subject: GEO
GEO 788.description: Graduate-level seminar in Geographic Information Science.
GEO 788.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

GER 110.title: Intensive Elementary German
GER 110.subject: GER
GER 110.description: Combined content of GER 101 and GER 102 covered in one intensive course.

GER 260.title: Intensive Intermediate German Abroad
GER 260.subject: GER
GER 260.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the second-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

GER 301.title: Phonetics and Pronunciation Practice
GER 301.subject: GER
GER 301.description: Analysis of the German phonological system and practice in pronunciation.
GER 301.prereq_raw: GER 202 (or concurrent with consent) or GER 260 .

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) or GER 260

GER 302.title: Structure of Modern German
GER 302.subject: GER
GER 302.description: Study of syntactic and morphological structures and basic pragmatic principles. Focuses on spoken and written Modern German.

GER 303.title: Reading and Writing
GER 303.subject: GER
GER 303.description: Further development of reading and writing skills through the study of short texts, focusing on modern German short stories, fairy tales, poems and song lyrics.

GER 304.title: Business German
GER 304.subject: GER
GER 304.description: Advanced German conversation, reading, and writing with a special emphasis on the vocabulary and cultural context of the German business world.

GER 305.title: Contemporary Topics in Media
GER 305.subject: GER
GER 305.description: Development of listening and speaking, reading and writing skills through analysis and discussion of media: newspaper articles, radio, and television programs and online sources.

GER 306.title: Conversation
GER 306.subject: GER
GER 306.description: Intensive practice in spoken German designed to increase vocabulary and improve oral proficiency.
GER 306.prereq_raw: GER 202 (or concurrent with consent) or GER 260 .

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) or GER 260

GER 307.title: Modern Readings: Wanderlust, Love, and Desire
GER 307.subject: GER
GER 307.description: Development of reading skills through the study of authentic modern texts (short stories; articles from newspapers, magazines, and the internet) with topics relating to culture, society, and history.

GER 308.title: Modern Readings: Freedom, Happiness and Free Body Culture
GER 308.subject: GER
GER 308.description: Further expansion and improvement of reading skills through the study of authentic modern texts (short stories; newspaper articles, and internet) with topics relating to culture, society, and history, e.g., FKK Freikörperkultur, or free body culture.

GER 312.title: Introduction to German Literature 1750-1914:
GER 312.subject: GER
GER 312.description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1750 to 1914.

GER 313.title: Introduction to German Literature 1914-Present
GER 313.subject: GER
GER 313.description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1914 to present.

GER 320.title: German Cinema
GER 320.subject: GER
GER 320.description: Study of German film history, film analysis, film theory, and film study. Lecture/discussion.

GER 360.title: Intensive Third-Level German Abroad
GER 360.subject: GER
GER 360.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the third-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

GER 361.title: Germanic Civilization to World War II
GER 361.subject: GER
GER 361.description: German cultural heritage and history in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland until World War II.

GER 362.title: Modern German Culture
GER 362.subject: GER
GER 362.description: Modern culture in post-World War II Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

GER 371.title: Practical German for use in Hawaiʻi
GER 371.subject: GER
GER 371.description: Use of German in practical situations in Hawaiʻi, e.g., in travel industry.

GER 409.title: Enlightenment-Sturm und Drang
GER 409.subject: GER
GER 409.description: Lessing and his contemporaries; early dramas of Goethe and Schiller; Goethe’s early lyrics.

GER 410.title: Classicism
GER 410.subject: GER
GER 410.description: Classical writings of Goethe and Schiller; some reference to other writers.

GER 411.title: Romanticism
GER 411.subject: GER
GER 411.description: Novalis, Tieck, E. T. A. Hoffmann, Eichendorff, etc.

GER 416.title: German Literature, Culture and Film: 1989 to Present
GER 416.subject: GER
GER 416.description: Study of German literature, culture and film, 1989 to present. Credit cannot be earned for both GER 416 and LLEA 416 .

GER 460.title: Intensive Fourth-Level German Abroad
GER 460.subject: GER
GER 460.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-level in German language and culture in a German-speaking country.

GERI 541.title: Geriatric & Palliative Medicine
GERI 541.subject: GERI
GERI 541.description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

GERI 542.title: Geriatric Medicine Research
GERI 542.subject: GERI
GERI 542.description: Medical students will have the opportunity to complete a research project in the field of epidemiology of aging, and present an abstract at a local meeting. Basic principles of epidemiology and statistics will be taught.

GERI 545.title: Geriatric and Palliative Medicine Elective
GERI 545.subject: GERI
GERI 545.description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

GERI 595.title: Medical Student Training in Aging Program
GERI 595.subject: GERI
GERI 595.description: Introduces medical students to clinical, research, and academic experiences in geriatrics, under the mentorship of faculty members.

GERI 599.title: Directed Reading and Research
GERI 599.subject: GERI
GERI 599.description: One-on-one independent study for students interested in geriatrics and/or palliative medicine. Students will work with a faculty mentor to define an area of interest and meet regularly for guidance and feedback.

GES 100.title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
GES 100.subject: GES
GES 100.description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST.
GES 100.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Restricted to GES majors.

GES 102.title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
GES 102.subject: GES
GES 102.description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

GES 102L.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
GES 102L.subject: GES
GES 102L.description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
GES 102L.prereq_raw: GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent) or SUST 112 (or concurrent).

GES 302.title: GES Thesis Proposal
GES 302.subject: GES
GES 302.description: Supports GES majors in producing a thesis proposal that outlines and describes the timeline, required resources, etc. of the degree-required project.
GES 302.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

GES 304.title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
GES 304.subject: GES
GES 304.description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawaiʻi.
GES 304.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only.

GES 311.title: The Changing Earth and Climate System
GES 311.subject: GES
GES 311.description: Covers the Earth system, including mass and energy transfers, biogeochemical cycles, natural and anthropogenic changes on regional and global scale.
GES 311.prereq_raw: MATH 241 , GES 302 (or concurrent), and OCN 201 (or concurrent).

GES 319L.title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
GES 319L.subject: GES
GES 319L.description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311 . Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
GES 319L.prereq_raw: GES 311 , MATH 242 , PHYS 170 / PHYS 170L , and CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ; or consent.

GES 320.title: Aquatic Pollution
GES 320.subject: GES
GES 320.description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives. This course develops written communication skills.

GES 371.title: Environmental Data Science
GES 371.subject: GES
GES 371.description: Provides an introduction to environmental data science by applying python-based programming techniques to Earth science datasets.
GES 371.prereq_raw: MATH 242 , and ICS 110P or ICS 110C or ERTH 250 .

GES 399.title: Directed Reading
GES 399.subject: GES
GES 399.description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

GES 401.title: Biogeochemical Systems
GES 401.subject: GES
GES 401.description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills.
GES 401.prereq_raw: OCN 201 , GES 311 , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L , ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L , GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES 499 / OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent.
GES 401.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

GES 454.title: Earth’s Microbiome
GES 454.subject: GES
GES 454.description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
GES 454.prereq_raw: OCN 201 or BOT 305 / BIOL 305 or BOT 201 or BIOL 275 or MICR 351 or consent.

GES 454L.title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
GES 454L.subject: GES
GES 454L.description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
GES 454L.prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305 , or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 .

GES 463.title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
GES 463.subject: GES
GES 463.description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.

GES 471.title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
GES 471.subject: GES
GES 471.description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with Bayesian inference, make predictions using artificial neural networks, and analyze data in space and time using the Python language with biological and geophysical datasets.

GES 490.title: Communication of Research Results
GES 490.subject: GES
GES 490.description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material.
GES 490.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only in their final semester.

GES 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
GES 499.subject: GES
GES 499.description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

GRK 101.title: Elementary Greek
GRK 101.subject: GRK
GRK 101.description: Grammar and vocabulary, with reading of simple Greek.

GRK 201.title: Intermediate Greek
GRK 201.subject: GRK
GRK 201.description: Development of reading and translation skills. Emphasis on prose.

GRK 202.title: Intermediate Greek
GRK 202.subject: GRK
GRK 202.description: Continuation of GRK 201 : emphasis on poetry.

GRK 303.title: Greek Historians
GRK 303.subject: GRK
GRK 303.description: Selections from Herodotus, Xenophon, and others.

GRK 304.title: Greek Epic
GRK 304.subject: GRK
GRK 304.description: Selections from Homer, Hesiod, and others.

GRK 325.title: Greek Philosophy
GRK 325.subject: GRK
GRK 325.description: Selections from Plato, Aristotle, and others.

GRK 332.title: Greek Drama
GRK 332.subject: GRK
GRK 332.description: Selections from Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides.

GRK 333.title: Greek Lyric
GRK 333.subject: GRK
GRK 333.description: Selections from Sappho, Alcaeus, and others.

GRK 490.title: Seminar in Greek Studies
GRK 490.subject: GRK
GRK 490.description: Study of an author or phase in Greek studies.
GRK 490.prereq_raw: any two 300-level GRK courses, or consent.

HAW 100.title: Language in Hawaiʻi: A Microcosm of Global Language Issues
HAW 100.subject: HAW
HAW 100.description: Survival kit for life in Hawaiʻi: Introduction to Hawaiian and language related issues enhancing communicative experience in Hawaiʻi. Examination of social, cultural, political, and linguistic cross-cultural interaction locally and globally. Taught in English/Hawaiʻi Creole English.

HAW 101.title: Elementary Hawaiian I
HAW 101.subject: HAW
HAW 101.description: Introductory course in Hawaiian language focused on the foundational skills of language acquisition: speaking, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding.

HAW 105.title: Intensive Elementary Hawaiian
HAW 105.subject: HAW
HAW 105.description: Content of HAW 101 - Elementary Hawaiian I and HAW 102 - Elementary Hawaiian II covered in one semester.

HAW 200.title: I Ka ʻŌlelo Nō Ke Ola
HAW 200.subject: HAW
HAW 200.description: Accelerated lecture/lab to bridge fluent speakers mainly from Kula Kaiapuni into Kawaihuelani’s system of Hawaiian that reflects a Hawaiian worldview, including HAW 101 - HAW 201 content, grammar, writing, and spelling conventions. Students matriculate into HAW 202 .

HAW 201.title: Intermediate Hawaiian I
HAW 201.subject: HAW
HAW 201.description: Continuation of HAW 102 with continued development in the foundational skills of language acquisition: speaking, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Increased emphasis on reading of traditional texts.
HAW 201.prereq_raw: HAW 102 or HAW 105 or exam or consent.

HAW 206.title: Intensive Intermediate Hawaiian
HAW 206.subject: HAW
HAW 206.description: Content of HAW 201 - Intermediate Hawaiian I and HAW 202 - Intermediate Hawaiian II covered in one semester.

HAW 261.title: Hawaiian Literature in Translation
HAW 261.subject: HAW
HAW 261.description: Survey of Hawaiian literature, including prose narration and poetry with reference to Polynesian and Western themes and forms.

HAW 284.title: Papa Mele I (Mele in the Hawaiian Language Classroom)
HAW 284.subject: HAW
HAW 284.description: The incorporation of mele and the performance thereof for the enhancement of second language acquisition in Hawaiian.

HAW 301.title: Third-Level Hawaiian I
HAW 301.subject: HAW
HAW 301.description: Continuation of HAW 202 with emphasis on increasing proficiency in speaking/ conversation, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Conducted in Hawaiian.
HAW 301.prereq_raw: HAW 202 or HAW 206 or exam, or consent.

HAW 321.title: Hawaiian Conversation
HAW 321.subject: HAW
HAW 321.description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Hawaiian.

HAW 325.title: Moʻolelo Pōkole
HAW 325.subject: HAW
HAW 325.description: Development of reading comprehension, pronunciation, vocabulary, and Hawaiian cultural knowledge through reading of Hawaiian language short stories. Short stories are from primary and secondary sources written by a variety of authors across different time periods.

HAW 331.title: Hawaiian Composition
HAW 331.subject: HAW
HAW 331.description: Intensive work in the grammatical, semantic, and pragmatic dimensions of composition writing in Hawaiian.

HAW 332.title: Listening Comprehension and Transcription
HAW 332.subject: HAW
HAW 332.description: Development of listening comprehension through transcription and discussion of tape recordings.

HAW 345.title: Ulu ka Hoi
HAW 345.subject: HAW
HAW 345.description: Lecture offering focused study and creation of Hawaiian language newspapers with a concentration on the characteristics of writing in this genre. Students will produce a monthly newsletter in Hawaiian.

HAW 373.title: Ka Moʻomeheu Hawaiʻi
HAW 373.subject: HAW
HAW 373.description: A survey course on the study of traditional Hawaiian culture including origins, the socioeconomic system, land tenure, religion, values, and the arts. The course will be taught in Hawaiian.

HAW 383.title: Hana ʻOe a Kani Pono-Hawaiian Radio Broadcasting
HAW 383.subject: HAW
HAW 383.description: Combined lecture/lab involving students in the planning and production of a weekly Hawaiian language radio broadcast. Includes research, writing, and voicing of mele and their stories on live radio.
HAW 383.prereq_raw: HAW 302 or HAW 384 (or concurrent with consent), or consent.

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) , or consent

HAW 384.title: Ka Haku Mele
HAW 384.subject: HAW
HAW 384.description: Composers and Their Compositions. Provides a venue which will allow students to analyze, dissect and discuss mele (song, poetry and chant), paying close attention to the style of composition by identifying reoccurring nuances found in mele composed by the same as well as various authors.

HAW 401.title: Fourth-Level Hawaiian I
HAW 401.subject: HAW
HAW 401.description: Advanced speaking/conversation, discussion, listening comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Conducted in Hawaiian. Transcribing and translating recordings of native speakers in Hawaiian.

HAW 425.title: Moʻolelo Hawaiʻi
HAW 425.subject: HAW
HAW 425.description: Survey of the major works by Hawaiian scholars writing about the history and culture of Hawaiʻi including David Malo, Kamakau, Kepelino, and John Papa Īʻī.

HAW 426.title: Kaʻao Hawaiʻi
HAW 426.subject: HAW
HAW 426.description: Survey of the core literature written by Hawaiian scholars, including both historical and mythological epics and folk tales.

HAW 427.title: I Leʻa Ka Hula I Ka Hoʻopaʻa (Moʻolelo, Kaʻao, Mele and Hula)
HAW 427.subject: HAW
HAW 427.description: The incorporation of mele and hula performance with moʻolelo and kaʻao.

HAW 428.title: Ka Manaʻo Politika Hawaiʻi-Political Thought in Hawaiian
HAW 428.subject: HAW
HAW 428.description: Intensive study of Hawaiian political thought in writing and speech.

HAW 429.title: Ka Hōʻike Honua
HAW 429.subject: HAW
HAW 429.description: Study of Hawaiian land tenure practices through readings and discussions of audiotapes, written primary sources, maps, wind names, rain names, ʻŌlelo noʻeau (wise sayings), and mele (poetry). Readings are drawn from 19th and 20th century Hawaiian newspapers and other primary sources.

HAW 430.title: Ma Ka Hana Ka ʻIke
HAW 430.subject: HAW
HAW 430.description: Study of traditional Hawaiian language and cultural practices through hands-on applications and lectures.

HAW 431.title: Haku Moʻolelo-Creative Writing in Hawaiian
HAW 431.subject: HAW
HAW 431.description: Study and composition of written works in various creative genres of Hawaiian storytelling, with a focus on the adaptation and maintenance of a Hawaiian voice and worldview in writing.

HAW 433.title: I Paʻa Ke Kahua
HAW 433.subject: HAW
HAW 433.description: An experiential approach to the acquisition of vocabulary, which will allow students to broaden and deepen their knowledge of language and the range of domains to perpetuate Hawaiian as a living language.

HAW 434.title: E Pū Paʻakai Kākou: A Study of Traditional Hawaiian and Contemporary Food Culture
HAW 434.subject: HAW
HAW 434.description: A study of traditional Hawaiian and contemporary food culture through hands-on applications and lectures.

HAW 435B.title: Problems in Translation: legal documents
HAW 435B.subject: HAW
HAW 435B.description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

HAW 435C.title: Problems in Translation: newspapers
HAW 435C.subject: HAW
HAW 435C.description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

HAW 435D.title: Problems in Translation: religious writings
HAW 435D.subject: HAW
HAW 435D.description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

HAW 445.title: Nā Politika ma ka Nūhou Hawaiʻi- Politics in Hawaiian Language Media
HAW 445.subject: HAW
HAW 445.description: Study of Hawaiian news media with emphasis on political content. Includes field trips to various archives.

HAW 452.title: Structure of Hawaiian
HAW 452.subject: HAW
HAW 452.description: Descriptive linguistic analysis. Intensive exercises in advanced grammar.

HAW 453.title: ʻŌlelo Niʻihau I
HAW 453.subject: HAW
HAW 453.description: Basic study of ʻŌlelo Niʻihau. Speaking and listening comprehension will be developed through listening to audio recordings, watching video recordings, and participating in face-to-face conversations with Niʻihau native speakers.

HAW 454.title: History of the Hawaiian Language
HAW 454.subject: HAW
HAW 454.description: Development from proto-Polynesian. Phonology, morphology, and grammar; history of research.
HAW 454.prereq_raw: HAW 302 (or concurrent) and HAW 452 , or consent.

HAW 462B.title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: basketball
HAW 462B.subject: HAW
HAW 462B.description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

HAW 462C.title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: volleyball
HAW 462C.subject: HAW
HAW 462C.description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

HAW 462D.title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: football
HAW 462D.subject: HAW
HAW 462D.description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

HAW 462E.title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: baseball
HAW 462E.subject: HAW
HAW 462E.description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

HAW 463.title: Language for the Classroom
HAW 463.subject: HAW
HAW 463.description: Examination of language needs in various classroom settings and introduction to new vocabulary in school content areas.

HAW 466.title: Kuleana Kula Kaiapuni
HAW 466.subject: HAW
HAW 466.description: Examination of the political struggles of the Kula Kaiapuni (Hawaiian Immersion Program)—past and present. Special attention given to federal and state governments, Department of Education, and internal political struggles.

HAW 470.title: Hoʻomōhala Haʻawina Kaiapuni Curriculum Development
HAW 470.subject: HAW
HAW 470.description: Examination of curricular issues of indigenous language programs; weekly participation in an immersion classroom; development of materials.

HAW 471.title: Teaching in Hawaiian Language Immersion Program
HAW 471.subject: HAW
HAW 471.description: Explore the knowledge base needed for teaching in the Hawaiian Language Immersion Program and initiate inquiry into the nature and social context of teaching, learning and schooling.

HAW 475.title: Teaching Residency
HAW 475.subject: HAW
HAW 475.description: Full-time student teaching in a Hawaiian language classroom.

HAW 476.title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
HAW 476.subject: HAW
HAW 476.description: Analysis and resolution of issues in teaching residency; teaching strategies and techniques; curriculum planning, professional growth and development.

HAW 483.title: Papa Mele Wahi Pana
HAW 483.subject: HAW
HAW 483.description: Will provide students with the opportunity to learn mele, mainly poetry and song, composed specifically for a certain area of Hawaiʻi.

HAW 484.title: Hawaiian Poetry
HAW 484.subject: HAW
HAW 484.description: Historical survey and analysis of poetry found in traditional chants, folk songs, modern poetry written in Hawaiian. Interpreting and composing Hawaiian poetry.

HAW 485.title: Haku Hanakeaka-Hawaiian Language Playwriting
HAW 485.subject: HAW
HAW 485.description: The creation and authoring of Hawaiian language play scripts based on traditional motifs.

HAW 486.title: Kahua Hanakeaka (Hawaiian Medium Stage Production)
HAW 486.subject: HAW
HAW 486.description: From design to performance, students mount an original production based on traditional motifs.

HAW 488.title: ʻŌlelo Noʻeau
HAW 488.subject: HAW
HAW 488.description: Survey and analysis of traditional proverbs and their kaona or symbolic meanings.

HAW 490.title: Ka Mākau ʻŌlelo Aʻo Kula Kaiapuni Hawaiʻi
HAW 490.subject: HAW
HAW 490.description: Assess the linguistic competence of prospective Hawaiian language immersion teachers to assure that all teachers entering the state DOE Hawaiian Immersion Program meet the requirements of the program with respect to Hawaiian language proficiency.
HAW 490.prereq_raw: HAW 402 (or concurrent), and HAW 463 (or concurrent), or consent.

HAW 492.title: Analyzing Immersion Hawaiian
HAW 492.subject: HAW
HAW 492.description: Analysis and acquisition of features in Hawaiian spoken by Hawaiian speaking children in Hawaiian immersion education.

HAW 493.title: Learning Hawaiian Through Immersion
HAW 493.subject: HAW
HAW 493.description: Learning Hawaiian in the immersion setting: cultural context, behavioral patterns, and learning concerns.
HAW 493.prereq_raw: HAW 302 , and either HAW 435 or HAW 484 ; or consent.

HAW 499.title: Directed Studies
HAW 499.subject: HAW
HAW 499.description: Study of Hawaiian language through vernacular readings in various academic fields.

HAW 601.title: Kālaimanaʻo
HAW 601.subject: HAW
HAW 601.description: Seminar analyzing various genres of Hawaiian language literature published in the 19th and 20th centuries, with an emphasis on understanding Hawaiian models of theory and debate employed by authors of this era.
HAW 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HAW, HWST, and HSHK majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

HAW 602.title: Kākāʻōlelo Oratory
HAW 602.subject: HAW
HAW 602.description: A survey of oral performance styles to build increased oral skills.
HAW 602.prereq_raw: graduate standing and HAW 601 , or consent.

HAW 604.title: Haku Palapala Noi Laeoʻo/Writing a Hawaiian Master’s Proposal
HAW 604.subject: HAW
HAW 604.description: Seminar to select and develop students’ research topic, proposal, and organizational plan for Plan A or B completion. Majors are encouraged not to take this course in their first semester of the program.

HAW 605.title: Ka Hana Noiʻi (Research Methods)
HAW 605.subject: HAW
HAW 605.description: Research methodology course utilizing active research in the major repositories of Hawaiian language materials and Hawaiian-related knowledge.

HAW 612.title: Nā Manaʻo Politika Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian Political Thought)
HAW 612.subject: HAW
HAW 612.description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods.
HAW 612.prereq_raw: HAW 402 , HAW 428 , and POLS 303 ; or consent.

HAW 615.title: Kuanaʻike
HAW 615.subject: HAW
HAW 615.description: The examination of Hawaiian ways of speaking, as contrasted with English focusing on those features that are uniquely Hawaiian and can be said to constitute a Hawaiian worldview. Section 1 taught in Hawaiian; Section 2 taught in English.

HAW 625.title: Moʻolelo Hawaiʻi
HAW 625.subject: HAW
HAW 625.description: Intensive study, research, and analysis of Hawaiian history.

HAW 638E.title: Nā Mea Kākau/Nā Haku Moʻolelo: J. H. Kanepuʻu
HAW 638E.subject: HAW
HAW 638E.description: Intensive study of an individual author, his/her works and nuances of his/her works. (E) J. H. Kanepuʻu; (I) S. M. Kamakau.

HAW 638I.title: Nā Mea Kākau/Nā Haku Moʻolelo: S. M. Kamakau
HAW 638I.subject: HAW
HAW 638I.description: Intensive study of an individual author, his/her works and nuances of his/her works. (E) J. H. Kanepuʻu; (I) S. M. Kamakau.

HAW 643.title: Ke Aʻo ʻŌlelo Hou ʻAna (Teaching Hawaiian As a Second Language)
HAW 643.subject: HAW
HAW 643.description: Survey of existing texts and teaching resources; analysis of student clientele and needs; review of pedagogical approaches for heritage and non-heritage learners; syllabus and materials development; observation of beginning Hawaiian language or Hawaiian immersion classroom.

HAW 652.title: Pilina ʻŌlelo
HAW 652.subject: HAW
HAW 652.description: In-depth examination and research into the grammar of Hawaiian including discussion of theories of language and incorporation of meta-language.

HAW 653.title: ʻŌlelo Niʻihau
HAW 653.subject: HAW
HAW 653.description: Intensive, advanced study and analysis of traditional Hawaiian Niʻihau dialect through face-to-face conversations with Niʻihau native speakers, listening to audio recordings and watching video recordings of Niʻihau native speakers.
HAW 653.prereq_raw: ( HAW 402 and HAW 453 ) with a minimum grade of B- or consent.

HAW 684.title: Noiʻi Mele
HAW 684.subject: HAW
HAW 684.description: Intensive study focusing on original compositions of Hawaiian poetry and song.

HAW 695.title: Papahana Laeoʻo
HAW 695.subject: HAW
HAW 695.description: Research for Plan B project/non-thesis. May include but not limited to internship with cultural practitioner.

HAW 699.title: Directed Research
HAW 699.subject: HAW
HAW 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and graduate chair.

HDFS 230.title: Human Development
HDFS 230.subject: HDFS
HDFS 230.description: Concepts, issues, theories of human growth and development from conception to death; systems approaches to inquiry into factors affecting growth and development.

HDFS 235.title: Mindfulness & Ethical Mindset
HDFS 235.subject: HDFS
HDFS 235.description: Lecture and experiential mindfulness practices to facilitate ethical engagement in daily life, fostering well-being and peaceful state of mind with others and within oneself. Develop skills to navigate everyday challenges through evidence-informed approaches of mindfulness.

HDFS 331.title: Infancy and Early Childhood
HDFS 331.subject: HDFS
HDFS 331.description: Growth and development from prenatal period to age 5. Historical and current issues and research based on ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on optimal development.

HDFS 332.title: Childhood
HDFS 332.subject: HDFS
HDFS 332.description: Intensive investigation into developmental aspects of 6-12 year old children. Historical and current issues, research, and examination of the role of schools and other community resources. Focus on optimal development.

HDFS 333.title: Adolescence and Early Adulthood
HDFS 333.subject: HDFS
HDFS 333.description: Problems, concepts, and research related to development from puberty through early adulthood. Examination of biological, cognitive, social, and cultural factors affecting the individual.

HDFS 334.title: Middle Age and Aging
HDFS 334.subject: HDFS
HDFS 334.description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences.

HDFS 340.title: Intimacy, Marriages and Families
HDFS 340.subject: HDFS
HDFS 340.description: Study of intimate relationships, marriages and families, their dynamics, strengths, growth and development, challenges, choices and opportunities, in the context of social change and cultural diversity.
HDFS 340.prereq_raw: HDFS 230 or PSY 100 or SOC 100 ; or consent.

HDFS 341.title: Parenting
HDFS 341.subject: HDFS
HDFS 341.description: Parenting theories, methods, skills, issues, and resources; parent-child relations in various cultural contexts.

HDFS 350.title: Leadership and Group Process
HDFS 350.subject: HDFS
HDFS 350.description: Exploration of leadership research and theories and their application to leadership development; designed to enhance personal and interactive leadership.

HDFS 352.title: Community Needs and Resources
HDFS 352.subject: HDFS
HDFS 352.description: Theory and practice in determining community needs and resources; community resources development based on needs identification.

HDFS 360.title: Family Resource Management
HDFS 360.subject: HDFS
HDFS 360.description: Concepts, principles, and practices in managing family and household resources.

HDFS 361.title: Family Financial Planning
HDFS 361.subject: HDFS
HDFS 361.description: Analytical approach to family financial planning from the perspective of changing family demands over the life cycle.
HDFS 361.prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

HDFS 363.title: Consumer Economics
HDFS 363.subject: HDFS
HDFS 363.description: Consumer rights, responsibilities, and resources; consumer decision-making; factors affecting consumer functioning within economy.
HDFS 363.prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

HDFS 365.title: Soft Skills for Success in the Workplace
HDFS 365.subject: HDFS
HDFS 365.description: Employers regard soft skills as key criteria when hiring and retaining employees. Students learn critical skills essential to work place success. This class prepares students to be work ready.

HDFS 380.title: Research Methodology
HDFS 380.subject: HDFS
HDFS 380.description: Fundamental scientific methodology, design and data collection; introduction to statistics and program evaluations, analysis of ethical issues.
HDFS 380.prereq_raw: HDFS 230 or FDM 200 or TPSS 200 / SUST 211 , or consent.
HDFS 380.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.

HDFS 380L.title: Research Methodology Lab
HDFS 380L.subject: HDFS
HDFS 380L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Test design, computer use, data analysis.
HDFS 380L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.

HDFS 425.title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
HDFS 425.subject: HDFS
HDFS 425.description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, prepares students for direct, educational work with parents and children and for continued graduate work in child and family studies, counseling, psychology, social work and/or family life education.

HDFS 435.title: Mindfulness and Skillful Living
HDFS 435.subject: HDFS
HDFS 435.description: Lecture, discussion, and experiential activities of principles and practice of an evidence-based contemplative science discipline. Focuses on development of writing skills and ethical applications to daily life, with implications for youth, families, and society.
HDFS 435.prereq_raw: completed DS course (with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: completed DS course ( with a minimum grade of C

HDFS 442.title: Marriage Development
HDFS 442.subject: HDFS
HDFS 442.description: Marital interaction and development; divorce and remarriage; resources and techniques for marital adjustment, enrichment, and growth.

HDFS 444.title: Contemporary Family Issues
HDFS 444.subject: HDFS
HDFS 444.description: Investigation of current issues with impact upon family quality of life, with emphasis on the interdependent nature of families and their environments.

HDFS 445.title: Family Life Education Methodology
HDFS 445.subject: HDFS
HDFS 445.description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, with service learning on Family Life Education Methodology.

HDFS 446.title: Marriage and Family Therapy
HDFS 446.subject: HDFS
HDFS 446.description: Overview of the field of marriage and family therapy, including history, theory, and practice. Explores professional roles, family systems perspectives, and approaches to helping couples and families across diverse contexts.
HDFS 446.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

HDFS 452.title: Community Program Development
HDFS 452.subject: HDFS
HDFS 452.description: Concepts and theories of community program development; principles, practices, and procedures in administration and supervision of volunteer services surveyed and analyzed.

HDFS 454.title: Family Public Policy
HDFS 454.subject: HDFS
HDFS 454.description: Cross-national survey of family public policy; analysis, revision, and development of family public policy; impacts of policy on consumers and families.

HDFS 455.title: Consumer Communications
HDFS 455.subject: HDFS
HDFS 455.description: Development, production, analysis, and evaluation of consumer materials for print media. Use of desktop publishing computer programs.
HDFS 455.prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

HDFS 468.title: Family Economics
HDFS 468.subject: HDFS
HDFS 468.description: Study of personal family resources and its interaction with the economy. Focuses on contemporary economic problems that affect the welfare of families.
HDFS 468.prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

HDFS 491.title: Topics in Family Resources
HDFS 491.subject: HDFS
HDFS 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

HDFS 492.title: Internship
HDFS 492.subject: HDFS
HDFS 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills in supervised work at an approved internship site and through analytical writing assignments and class discussions.
HDFS 492.prereq_raw: ( HDFS 230 , HDFS 340 , HDFS 360 , HDFS 380 , and HDFS 380L ) with a minimum grade of C.

HDFS 495.title: Capstone Portfolio
HDFS 495.subject: HDFS
HDFS 495.description: Preparation of a senior portfolio to be used as assessment of competence relative to national FCS standards. Includes extensive instruction on writing.
HDFS 495.prereq_raw: ( HDFS 230 , HDFS 340 , HDFS 360 , HDFS 380 , HDFS 380L , and HDFS 492 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.

HDFS 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
HDFS 499.subject: HDFS
HDFS 499.description: Independent reading and research on a topic, done under supervision of a faculty member; outcomes contracted in writing with faculty member at beginning of semester.

HIST 151.title: World History to 1500
HIST 151.subject: HIST
HIST 151.description: Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from prehistory to 1500; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

HIST 152.title: World History since 1500
HIST 152.subject: HIST
HIST 152.description: Continuation of HIST 151 . Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from 1500 to present; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

HIST 155.title: Issues in World History
HIST 155.subject: HIST
HIST 155.description: In examining aspects of the histories of Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe and Oceania, this course highlights the myriad ways in which global contact has transformed our world and narratives of the past.

HIST 156.title: World History of Human Disease
HIST 156.subject: HIST
HIST 156.description: Examines how disease has affected humans in terms of society, culture, politics, religion, and economics. Explores the impact over a broad range of time periods, from pre-history to the present/future.

HIST 157.title: Global Environmental History
HIST 157.subject: HIST
HIST 157.description: Explores the influence of nature-climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms-on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

HIST 158.title: Global History of Food
HIST 158.subject: HIST
HIST 158.description: Exploration of food and eating from historical, cultural, economic, and geopolitical perspectives. Includes both historical and contemporary issues.

HIST 161A.title: World Cultures in Perspective
HIST 161A.subject: HIST
HIST 161A.description: Development of civilizations from prehistoric origins to 1500. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for HIST 151 and HIST 152 ; students in Honors program only.

HIST 162A.title: World Cultures in Perspective
HIST 162A.subject: HIST
HIST 162A.description: Continuation of HIST 161A . Development of civilization from 1500 to the present. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for HIST 151 and HIST 152 ; students in Honors program only.

HIST 230.title: Early European Civilization
HIST 230.subject: HIST
HIST 230.description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states before 1500, including classical and medieval eras.

HIST 231.title: European Civilization 1500-1800
HIST 231.subject: HIST
HIST 231.description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states. 1500-1800.

HIST 232.title: Modern Europe, 1789-Present
HIST 232.subject: HIST
HIST 232.description: Major political, social, economic, and cultural trends from the revolutionary era to the present.

HIST 241.title: Civilizations of Asia
HIST 241.subject: HIST
HIST 241.description: Survey of major civilizations of Asia from earliest times to 1500; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

HIST 242.title: Civilizations of Asia
HIST 242.subject: HIST
HIST 242.description: Continuation of HIST 241 . Survey of major civilizations of Asia from 1500 to the present; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

HIST 281.title: Introduction to American History
HIST 281.subject: HIST
HIST 281.description: A survey of North American history from the Columbian Encounter to the U.S. Civil War.

HIST 282.title: Introduction to American History
HIST 282.subject: HIST
HIST 282.description: Interpretive survey from 1865 to the present.

HIST 284.title: History of the Hawaiian Islands
HIST 284.subject: HIST
HIST 284.description: Survey of state and local history from Polynesian chiefdoms to Hawaiian Kingdom to American territory and state.

HIST 288.title: Oceania Survey
HIST 288.subject: HIST
HIST 288.description: Survey of major events, themes, and issues that make up the diverse histories of Oceania, including Hawaiʻi, from ancestral origins to the present, with an emphasis on instruction in writing.

HIST 294.title: History of the Philippines
HIST 294.subject: HIST
HIST 294.description: Traces developments in Philippine history and society from precolonial to contemporary times and explores ways in which the peoples of the Philippines embraced, resisted or negotiated new modes of thought, behavior and social organization influenced by the Spanish, American, and Japanese regimes as well as the post-colonial global order.

HIST 296.title: Topics in History
HIST 296.subject: HIST
HIST 296.description: Introduction to methods of historical inquiry; current issues in World, American, European, or Pacific history. Emphasis on teaching writing.

HIST 301.title: History of Early India
HIST 301.subject: HIST
HIST 301.description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century.

HIST 302.title: History of Modern India
HIST 302.subject: HIST
HIST 302.description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from the Mughal Empire to the new millennium, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from the 18th century to the present.

HIST 305.title: Early Modern Southeast Asia
HIST 305.subject: HIST
HIST 305.description: Traces the development of Southeast Asia from early beginnings to the 19th century. Ethical issues and effective writing based on essays and ethical responses will form an important part of the course.

HIST 306.title: Modern Southeast Asia
HIST 306.subject: HIST
HIST 306.description: Continuation of HIST 305 , from 18th century to the present.

HIST 309.title: East Asian Civilizations
HIST 309.subject: HIST
HIST 309.description: Characteristics of East Asian civilizations as they developed in premodern China; variant patterns in Japan and Korea; the modernization process to 1500.

HIST 312.title: History of China
HIST 312.subject: HIST
HIST 312.description: Continuation of HIST 311 . Period since the 17th century.

HIST 321.title: History of Japan
HIST 321.subject: HIST
HIST 321.description: Survey of culture, government, economics, and institutions, to 1700.

HIST 323.title: Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
HIST 323.subject: HIST
HIST 323.description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills.

HIST 324.title: The Samurai of Japan
HIST 324.subject: HIST
HIST 324.description: A social, military, and cultural history of Japan’s samurai (warrior) class. Emphasis on teaching oral communication.

HIST 327.title: Beyond Palaces: Origins of Korea
HIST 327.subject: HIST
HIST 327.description: Survey of Korea’s political, economic, social, and cultural developments from earliest times to 1800s. Ethical issues in nationhood, central hegemony, myth-making, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

HIST 328.title: Beyond Kpop: Formation of Modern Korea
HIST 328.subject: HIST
HIST 328.description: Survey of Modern Korea’s political, economic, social, and cultural developments from 1800s to the present. Ethical issues in nationhood, state power, uprisings, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

HIST 330.title: Beyond War: History of North Korea
HIST 330.subject: HIST
HIST 330.description: History of North Korea in terms of industrialism, architecture, militarism, nationalism, culture, and art from 1945 to today. Context of global history is very important. Writing emphasis.

HIST 331.title: Ancient Greece I
HIST 331.subject: HIST
HIST 331.description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Minoan, Mycenean, and Archaic periods.

HIST 332.title: Ancient Greece II
HIST 332.subject: HIST
HIST 332.description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Classical and Hellenistic periods. Emphasis on teaching writing/oral communication.

HIST 333.title: Ancient Rome: The Republic
HIST 333.subject: HIST
HIST 333.description: Political, social, cultural history from the Etruscans to Augustus. Emphasis on discussion of literary and archaeological materials.

HIST 334.title: Ancient Rome: The Empire
HIST 334.subject: HIST
HIST 334.description: Political, social, and cultural history from Augustus to 476 A.D. Emphasis on literary and archaeological materials.

HIST 335.title: Early Medieval Europe 300-1050
HIST 335.subject: HIST
HIST 335.description: Formation of European societies in relation to Byzantine and Islamic cultures. Writing exercises develop historical thinking and the analysis of primary sources through workshops with peer and instructor feedback.

HIST 336.title: Medieval Europe 1050-1350
HIST 336.subject: HIST
HIST 336.description: Main trends in European economy, society, religion, politics, thought, and the arts circa 1050-1350, including interactions with Byzantine and Islamic worlds; oral presentations develop historical empathy for understanding primary sources.

HIST 337.title: European Intellectual History
HIST 337.subject: HIST
HIST 337.description: Undergraduate seminar on great debates in Western thought. Discussion and written analysis of primary source materials; the Scientific Revolution and Enlightenment. Significant attention paid to developing writing and textual analysis skills.

HIST 339.title: Renaissance and Reformation
HIST 339.subject: HIST
HIST 339.description: Political, social, cultural, and intellectual developments in Europe from 1300 to 1600. Emphasis on cultural and intellectual history and its impact on social and political developments; humanism and its influence on thought and reforming movements, Protestant and Catholic Reformations.

HIST 340.title: Comparative Economic History
HIST 340.subject: HIST
HIST 340.description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

HIST 342.title: The History of Economic Thought
HIST 342.subject: HIST
HIST 342.description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy.

HIST 345.title: France in the Old Regime
HIST 345.subject: HIST
HIST 345.description: Major social, political, and intellectual developments: Renaissance, Reformation, religious wars, Richelieu, Louis XIV, Enlightenment, and Revolution.

HIST 346.title: Modern France
HIST 346.subject: HIST
HIST 346.description: Political, social, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments in France from Revolution and Napoleon to the present. Assignments emphasize engagement with course concepts through oral communication and individual and group presentation.

HIST 347.title: Tudor-Stuart Britain
HIST 347.subject: HIST
HIST 347.description: Traces major developments in British politics, society, and culture between the late Medieval and Modern Eras.

HIST 348.title: Modern Britain 1688-1945
HIST 348.subject: HIST
HIST 348.description: Interaction of 17th-, 18th-, and 19th-century intellectual, political, economic, and social changes, which together produced the British Empire and modern Britain.

HIST 349.title: British Empire
HIST 349.subject: HIST
HIST 349.description: Origins and expansion of the British empire between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries. Includes imperial policies affecting Britain, Australia, India, Ireland, and Southern Africa. Open to nonmajors.

HIST 350.title: Iberia in Asia and the Pacific
HIST 350.subject: HIST
HIST 350.description: Comparative exploration of the Iberian empires-Spain and Portugal-and their political, economic, and cultural interactions with indigenous societies in Asia and the Pacific.

HIST 352.title: France and Empire
HIST 352.subject: HIST
HIST 352.description: Lecture/discussion exploring the history of France’s relationship with imperialism from the Renaissance to the present.

HIST 354.title: Introduction to Islamic History
HIST 354.subject: HIST
HIST 354.description: Muhammad, the Arab conquests, the Caliphate; fundamentals of Islam; classical Islamic civilization; development of Islam into modern times with emphasis on the Middle Eastern heartland.

HIST 355.title: The Making of the Modern Middle East
HIST 355.subject: HIST
HIST 355.description: Survey of developments that created the system of nation-states in the Middle East. History of the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Turkey; Egypt; the Arab world; Israel and Iran. Recommended: HIST 354 .

HIST 356.title: Survey of African History
HIST 356.subject: HIST
HIST 356.description: The history of Africa from earliest times to the present: the rise of indigenous civilizations, European and Muslim impact, colonialism and nationalism, and current issues.

HIST 358.title: The World of Mekong
HIST 358.subject: HIST
HIST 358.description: Historical survey, from BC period to present, of the peoples of the Mekong region, an area covering southwestern China, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and southern Vietnam. Open to nonmajors.

HIST 361.title: U.S. Women’s History
HIST 361.subject: HIST
HIST 361.description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work, women in social movements, changing norms regarding gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences of women. Emphasis on ethical issues and oral communication.

HIST 362.title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
HIST 362.subject: HIST
HIST 362.description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. Junior standing or higher.

HIST 366.title: Women in Oceania
HIST 366.subject: HIST
HIST 366.description: Uses research and writing to explore historical processes that have impacted the lives of Indigenous women in Oceania and women’s engagements with those processes over time, with a focus on women’s voices, agency, and empowerment.

HIST 368.title: Global History of Sport
HIST 368.subject: HIST
HIST 368.description: Explores the relationship between sport and society in historical perspective. Analyzes global processes of imperialism, nationalism, globalization, and international relations, and studies themes such as the politics of race, class, and gender.

HIST 371.title: U.S. Foreign Relations to 1898
HIST 371.subject: HIST
HIST 371.description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from initial encounters between Europeans and Native Americans through the 1890s.

HIST 372.title: U.S. Foreign Relations From 1898
HIST 372.subject: HIST
HIST 372.description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from the wars of 1898 to the present.

HIST 373.title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
HIST 373.subject: HIST
HIST 373.description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship within the total society. pre- Colonial to end of the 19th century.

HIST 378.title: History of American Business
HIST 378.subject: HIST
HIST 378.description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

HIST 379.title: American Empire
HIST 379.subject: HIST
HIST 379.description: Examines an “American culture of empire” in the context of Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific, exploring ethical issues of settler colonialism and decolonial movements. Emphasis on teaching writing/oral communication.

HIST 386.title: Caribbean History
HIST 386.subject: HIST
HIST 386.description: Survey of the history of the Caribbean region from 1500 to the present.

HIST 389.title: The Asia-Pacific War
HIST 389.subject: HIST
HIST 389.description: Explores WWII in the Asia-Pacific region, focusing on the intersection of the grand strategy, military operations, and war crimes. Involves source analyses and discussions.

HIST 391.title: History of Warfare to 1850
HIST 391.subject: HIST
HIST 391.description: Classical and guerrilla warfare, revolution, and military systems and institutions.

HIST 392.title: War and Peace Since 1850
HIST 392.subject: HIST
HIST 392.description: Continuation of HIST 391 , from 1850 to present.

HIST 394.title: History of Science to 1700
HIST 394.subject: HIST
HIST 394.description: Evolution of scientific thought and its cultural context. Antiquity to 1700.

HIST 395.title: History of Science Since 1700
HIST 395.subject: HIST
HIST 395.description: Continuation of HIST 394 ; science, technology, and society since 1700.

HIST 396B.title: Historical Theories and Methods: historiography
HIST 396B.subject: HIST
HIST 396B.description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

HIST 396C.title: Historical Theories and Methods: education
HIST 396C.subject: HIST
HIST 396C.description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

HIST 400.title: Digital History in the Global Village
HIST 400.subject: HIST
HIST 400.description: History of the digital age in global perspective connecting people, media, and technology. Faculty and students will use digital media to introduce innovative approaches to doing history.

HIST 401.title: History of the Indian Ocean World
HIST 401.subject: HIST
HIST 401.description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants.

HIST 404.title: Rivers, Seas, and Society in Southeast Asia
HIST 404.subject: HIST
HIST 404.description: The rivers, seas, and extensive coastlines are a dominant environmental feature in Southeast Asia. Focuses on the dynamic interaction of water and society in shaping the history of the region.

HIST 405.title: Themes of War in History
HIST 405.subject: HIST
HIST 405.description: Explores cross-cutting themes of war from ancient times to the present, such as concepts of just war and unjust war, valor and heroism, and war trauma among combatants and civilian populations in conflict zones.

HIST 406.title: Modern Philippines
HIST 406.subject: HIST
HIST 406.description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

HIST 407.title: Modern Malaysia
HIST 407.subject: HIST
HIST 407.description: History of Malay peninsula and northern Borneo, emphasizing developments since 18th century: trade, commerce, foreign migrations, pluralism, nationalism, and Islam.

HIST 408.title: Modern Indonesia
HIST 408.subject: HIST
HIST 408.description: Indonesia from 14th century to present. Emphasis on period from late 18th-century Western colonial impact to struggle for independence and problems of nationhood.

HIST 409.title: History of Islamic Southeast Asia
HIST 409.subject: HIST
HIST 409.description: History of the coming of Islam to Southeast Asia, the spread of its ideas, and its role in the lives of Muslim communities living in the region.

HIST 410.title: Twentieth-Century China
HIST 410.subject: HIST
HIST 410.description: Political, economic, social, and cultural transformations of China from 1900 to the present. This lecture/discussion course examines critical events and explores important issues in the modernization of Chinese life since 1900.

HIST 411.title: Society and Culture in Traditional China
HIST 411.subject: HIST
HIST 411.description: Ch’ing government and Chinese society from local and regional perspectives; modes of control and disorder during the 19th century.

HIST 416.title: Chinese Intellectual History
HIST 416.subject: HIST
HIST 416.description: An interpretive survey of Chinese ideas and values in their cultural, social and political settings from classical age to 1600.

HIST 417.title: Chinese Intellectual History
HIST 417.subject: HIST
HIST 417.description: Interpretive survey of Chinese thought from 1600 to the contemporary period, with special emphasis on the themes of cultural collision and change.

HIST 418.title: China’s Foreign Relations
HIST 418.subject: HIST
HIST 418.description: Systematic review from traditional times, with emphasis on modern and contemporary history, analyses of foreign policy formulation, objectives, and implementation. Recommended: HIST 312 .

HIST 419.title: The Search for Modern China
HIST 419.subject: HIST
HIST 419.description: Origins, development, and meaning of modern revolution in China, 19th century to People’s Republic. Recommended: HIST 311 and HIST 312 .

HIST 420.title: People’s Republic of China
HIST 420.subject: HIST
HIST 420.description: Salient developments from 1949 to the present. Topics include: social revolution and modernization, critically relevant foreign relations. Develops rhetoric and logic skills through practice with oral communications and the written word. Recommended: HIST 312 or HIST 419 .

HIST 421.title: China in World History
HIST 421.subject: HIST
HIST 421.description: Interpretative survey of China’s changing position, significance, and function in the evolution of world history as a way to provide a better understanding of its past and present.

HIST 422.title: Tokugawa Japan
HIST 422.subject: HIST
HIST 422.description: This course covers the major historical aspects of Japan’s Edo/Tokugawa period (1603-1867). Students will learn course content via lectures, discussions, and 2 written assignments of 10 pages each.

HIST 423.title: Okinawa
HIST 423.subject: HIST
HIST 423.description: Survey of social, cultural, economic, and political history from earliest times to present.

HIST 424.title: Twentieth Century Japan
HIST 424.subject: HIST
HIST 424.description: Problems of Japan’s political, economic, and social development since institutional consolidation of Meiji state (c.1890).

HIST 425.title: Women in East Asian History
HIST 425.subject: HIST
HIST 425.description: Survey of the changing political, social, economic, and cultural positions of women in China, Japan, and Korea from ancient times to the present.

HIST 426.title: History of Japanese Cuisine and Foodways
HIST 426.subject: HIST
HIST 426.description: Explores the history of Japanese cuisine and investigates the cultural, economic, and geopolitical aspects of foodways in Japanese domestic and international identity.

HIST 428.title: Topics on Transitional Justice
HIST 428.subject: HIST
HIST 428.description: Explores how societies in the wake of armed conflict, repression, or mass human rights abuses build institutional capacities for promoting justice, human rights, and the rule of law.

HIST 429.title: War Crimes Trials in History
HIST 429.subject: HIST
HIST 429.description: Explores war crimes trials in history since the end of WWII to the present. Involves extensive source analysis, discussion, research, and writing.

HIST 430.title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
HIST 430.subject: HIST
HIST 430.description: Writing and oral presentation-based historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states and the Roman Empire.

HIST 433.title: Medieval Cultures
HIST 433.subject: HIST
HIST 433.description: Topical study of medieval period (circa 300-1500) cross-cultural issues. Class discussion and written work emphasize analysis of primary source documents using an ethics historiography and world history theories. Regional focus and readings vary by semester.

HIST 434.title: History of Christianity to 1500
HIST 434.subject: HIST
HIST 434.description: Historical analysis of the main traditions of Christianity and elements of diversity within Europe and in relation to other parts of the world. Focus on the interpretation of primary sources and discussion of cultural issues.

HIST 436.title: World Environmental History, 1500 to Present
HIST 436.subject: HIST
