HIST 436.description: Explores interactions between humans and the natural world from early modern era to the present. Topics include invader species and biotic exchange; environmental politics; and the ecological impact of industrialization, urbanization, science, technology, war, etc.

HIST 438.title: WWII and the Making of Modern Asia/Pacific
HIST 438.subject: HIST
HIST 438.description: A research seminar that builds knowledge of the transformation of Asia and the Pacific following the end of World War II and that guides students to produce substantial research papers.

HIST 440.title: 20th-Century Europe
HIST 440.subject: HIST
HIST 440.description: Contemporary problems and their historical background.

HIST 441.title: Expansion of Europe
HIST 441.subject: HIST
HIST 441.description: Historical processes in modern European colonization from 16th to 20th century; impact on non-Europeans in Asia and Africa.

HIST 442.title: War and Violence in Early Modern Europe
HIST 442.subject: HIST
HIST 442.description: History of the intellectual, social, and cultural causes and consequences of violence, including military conflicts.

HIST 445.title: French Revolution and Napoleon
HIST 445.subject: HIST
HIST 445.description: Causes and conduct of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods; emphasis on the conflict of ideologies in the Revolutionary process; discussion and written analysis of primary sources; significant attention to developing writing and textual analysis skills.

HIST 446.title: Europe, 1914-1945: War, Peace, and Revolution
HIST 446.subject: HIST
HIST 446.description: Explores war and peace in Europe, from the start of the Great War through the formal end of World War II. Topics include key battles, civilians, peace movements, treaties, the Shoah, Fascism, and Soviet Revolution.

HIST 448.title: Imperial Spain and Portugal
HIST 448.subject: HIST
HIST 448.description: The influence of Spain and Portugal on people and cultures in Europe, Africa, America, and Asia; Portugal’s captivity and the defeat of the Spanish Armada.

HIST 450.title: Topics in African History
HIST 450.subject: HIST
HIST 450.description: Selected themes important in African history, including, for example, the politics, economics, societies, and cultures of pre-colonial, colonial, or modern Africa. Topics to be pre-announced.

HIST 451B.title: History and Literature: United States
HIST 451B.subject: HIST
HIST 451B.description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.

HIST 451C.title: History and Literature: Europe
HIST 451C.subject: HIST
HIST 451C.description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.

HIST 451D.title: History and Literature: Asia/Pacific
HIST 451D.subject: HIST
HIST 451D.description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.

HIST 451E.title: History and Literature: World/Comparative
HIST 451E.subject: HIST
HIST 451E.description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.

HIST 451F.title: History and Literature: Provisional topics
HIST 451F.subject: HIST
HIST 451F.description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.

HIST 452B.title: History and Film: United States
HIST 452B.subject: HIST
HIST 452B.description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (B) United States; (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) world/comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures.

HIST 452C.title: History and Film: Europe
HIST 452C.subject: HIST
HIST 452C.description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (B) United States; (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) world/comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures.

HIST 452D.title: History and Film: Asia/Pacific
HIST 452D.subject: HIST
HIST 452D.description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (B) United States; (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) world/comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures.

HIST 452E.title: History and Film: world/comparative
HIST 452E.subject: HIST
HIST 452E.description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (B) United States; (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) world/comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures.

HIST 453.title: Colonial Medicine
HIST 453.subject: HIST
HIST 453.description: Evolution of Western medical traditions; challenges created by European expansion and colonial interactions; development of modern racial and gender theories. Junior standing or higher.

HIST 458.title: The American Revolution
HIST 458.subject: HIST
HIST 458.description: Lecture/discussion on the origins, development, and consequences of the American Revolution, explored within the context of the broader revolutionary Atlantic world. Emphasis on learning history through writing.

HIST 459.title: African American History
HIST 459.subject: HIST
HIST 459.description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins of racial slavery, slave and free black culture, slave resistance and antislavery, post-emancipation black life, the rise of Jim Crow, the Harlem Renaissance, and the Civil Rights Movement.

HIST 460.title: Native American History
HIST 460.subject: HIST
HIST 460.description: Lecture/ discussion on the history of North American Indians from the seventeenth century to the present. Open to nonmajors.

HIST 461.title: Early America
HIST 461.subject: HIST
HIST 461.description: Lecture/discussion on Native Americans, Africans, and Europeans in North America from contact to independence. Social, cultural, and economic themes and intersections of race, class, and gender explored.

HIST 462.title: The Early American Republic
HIST 462.subject: HIST
HIST 462.description: Lecture/ discussion on the Constitution, the growth of partisan politics, the market revolution, religious revivalism, abolitionism and the expansion of slavery in the U.S. during the age of Jefferson and Jackson.

HIST 463.title: American Civil War Era 1841—1877
HIST 463.subject: HIST
HIST 463.description: The crisis of the Union: antebellum society and culture, slavery, reform, sectionalism, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

HIST 464.title: Transformation of America 1877—1920
HIST 464.subject: HIST
HIST 464.description: Selected themes that explain major changes in American life during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including the westward movement, consolidation of capitalism, world power diplomacy, popular culture, progressivism, and World War I.

HIST 465.title: The United States 1920—1948
HIST 465.subject: HIST
HIST 465.description: The Roaring Twenties, the Depression, New Deal, coming of World War II, America during the war, origins of the Cold War.

HIST 466.title: The U.S.: 1948 to the Present
HIST 466.subject: HIST
HIST 466.description: The atomic age and the Cold War, the age of anxiety, the 1960s, the Vietnam War, the Reagan-Bush era, and beyond.

HIST 467.title: American Television History
HIST 467.subject: HIST
HIST 467.description: Lecture/ discussion examining the impact of television on American society, culture and politics. Analyzed in depth are family sitcoms, presidential politics, Vietnam and the presentation of gender and ethnicity. Open to nonmajors.

HIST 468.title: Viva Las Vegas!
HIST 468.subject: HIST
HIST 468.description: Upper-division lecture on the historical and cultural significance of Las Vegas in twentieth-century America. Open to nonmajors.

HIST 469.title: The Cold War
HIST 469.subject: HIST
HIST 469.description: Cold War as a global struggle. Topics will include U.S.-Soviet economic and political rivalry, Capitalism vs. Communism as practical policy and ideology, and the force of Third World anti-colonial nationalism. Emphasis on writing instruction.

HIST 471.title: Music, Industry, and Society
HIST 471.subject: HIST
HIST 471.description: History of U.S. music and recording industry. How industry relates to economy as a whole, and how it reflects broad patterns and trends in American culture and society.

HIST 473.title: Slavery and Freedom
HIST 473.subject: HIST
HIST 473.description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

HIST 474.title: The American West
HIST 474.subject: HIST
HIST 474.description: Lecture/discussion surveying North American settler colonialism, indigenous resistance, and the consolidation of a US West in the context of a growing transcontinental and Pacific empire. Emphasis on teaching writing.

HIST 475.title: Constitutional History of the U.S.
HIST 475.subject: HIST
HIST 475.description: Origins, development of Constitution, Colonial to modern times.

HIST 476.title: Race and Racism in America
HIST 476.subject: HIST
HIST 476.description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

HIST 477.title: History of American Workers
HIST 477.subject: HIST
HIST 477.description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

HIST 478.title: Colonial Latin America
HIST 478.subject: HIST
HIST 478.description: Pre-Columbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social, and religious evolution to 1810; independence.

HIST 480.title: American Environmental History
HIST 480.subject: HIST
HIST 480.description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

HIST 481.title: Histories of Oceania I
HIST 481.subject: HIST
HIST 481.description: Explores the diverse, interconnected histories of Oceania from ancestral origins through the early colonial period. Topics include voyaging, orality, land, gender, power, exchange, cross-cultural encounter, disease, colonization, resistance, and historiography. Additional focus on oral communication.

HIST 482.title: Histories of Oceania II
HIST 482.subject: HIST
HIST 482.description: Examines Oceania’s histories of protest during the colonial and post-colonial eras as responses to empire expansion. Explores ethical issues concerning these movements, emphasizing Hawaiʻi experiences and their intersection with those across Oceania.

HIST 483.title: United States in the Pacific
HIST 483.subject: HIST
HIST 483.description: Growth of economic and political interests and policies.

HIST 484.title: The Hawaiian Kingdom 1819-1893
HIST 484.subject: HIST
HIST 484.description: Transformation of Hawaiʻi into a state influenced by American and European ideas and institutions and Asian peoples, with an emphasis on instruction on writing.

HIST 485.title: History of 20th-Century Hawaiʻi
HIST 485.subject: HIST
HIST 485.description: Formation of an American Hawaiʻi with its unique local culture from 1898 to the present.

HIST 489.title: World Maritime History
HIST 489.subject: HIST
HIST 489.description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

HIST 492.title: Women and Revolution
HIST 492.subject: HIST
HIST 492.description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

HIST 493.title: Library Treasures: Exploring Special Collections & Archives
HIST 493.subject: HIST
HIST 493.description: Conduct original research using general library materials, special collections, rare books, archives, and manuscripts, maps, and other historical documents that are uniquely available at libraries and archives at UH and beyond.

HIST 496.title: Senior Tutorial in History
HIST 496.subject: HIST
HIST 496.description: Analysis of sources and evaluation of methods of historical writing. Students undertake a major research and writing project in field of special interest. Capstone course requires a 20-25 page minimum final research paper.

HIST 499.title: Directed Reading
HIST 499.subject: HIST
HIST 499.description: Individual projects in various fields. History majors with consent. Maximum 5 credit hours. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean.

HIST 602.title: Seminar in Historiography
HIST 602.subject: HIST
HIST 602.description: History of history and historians; philosophies of history.

HIST 605.title: Seminar in Digital History
HIST 605.subject: HIST
HIST 605.description: Examines the various ways that the production, presentation, and learning of history through digital media is changing the way people access and process information about the past. Graduate standing only.

HIST 607.title: Advanced Topics in Environmental History
HIST 607.subject: HIST
HIST 607.description: Introduction to leading themes, methodologies, and topics in world environmental history. Drawing on new and influential scholarship, readings explore the diverse forces that shape humans’ adaptation to and impact on the natural world.

HIST 608.title: Seminar on Water in History
HIST 608.subject: HIST
HIST 608.description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

HIST 609.title: Seminar in World History
HIST 609.subject: HIST
HIST 609.description: Analysis, research, and discussion of themes and issues in study of history of humankind.
HIST 609.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

HIST 610.title: Topics in World History
HIST 610.subject: HIST
HIST 610.description: Selected themes- feudalism, economic and industrial development, etc.- important in global history. Topics pre-announced.

HIST 611B.title: Advanced Readings in European History: ancient
HIST 611B.subject: HIST
HIST 611B.description: Selected topics for advanced reading; (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual.
HIST 611B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

HIST 611C.title: Advanced Readings in European History: medieval
HIST 611C.subject: HIST
HIST 611C.description: Selected topics for advanced reading; (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual.
HIST 611C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

HIST 611D.title: Advanced Readings in European History: early modern
HIST 611D.subject: HIST
HIST 611D.description: Selected topics for advanced reading; (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual.
HIST 611D.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

HIST 611E.title: Advanced Readings in European History: modern
HIST 611E.subject: HIST
HIST 611E.description: Selected topics for advanced reading; (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual.

HNDI 101.title: Elementary Hindi I

HNDI 101.description: Learn to express yourself in Hindi-a language that comes with a beautiful script, ancient philosophy, spicy food, and Bollywood! The course is communicative, creative, flexibly personalized for student interests. No textbook to buy.

HNDI 102.title: Elementary Hindi II
HNDI 102.subject: HNDI
HNDI 102.description: Build on your HNDI 101 skills. Content includes Bollywood Film Festival at Honolulu Museum of Art. Create your own audio-visual projects-make movie trailers, write children’s books, or perform at South Asian events.

HNDI 201.title: Intermediate Hindi I
HNDI 201.subject: HNDI
HNDI 201.description: Improve your communicative and cultural proficiency. Make Bollywood your language coach. Talk about cross-cultural values and practices of food, family, and friendship. Project-based course that builds bridges to your majors, minors, and other interests.

HNDI 202.title: Intermediate Hindi II
HNDI 202.subject: HNDI
HNDI 202.description: Prepare your proficiency for traveling to India. Create audio-visual presentations, documentaries, movie parodies, poetry, plays, dance, or projects from your majors/minors. Develop critical, cross-cultural, and creative skills. Bollywood built into course content.

HNDI 301.title: Third-Level Hindi: Culture
HNDI 301.subject: HNDI
HNDI 301.description: Continuation of HNDI 202 . Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected cultural themes.

HNDI 302.title: Third-Level Hindi: Film
HNDI 302.subject: HNDI
HNDI 302.description: Continuation of HNDI 202 . Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected Hindi-Urdu films.

HON 101.title: Introduction to Research and Creative Work at Mānoa

HON 299.subject: HON
HON 299.description: Introduction to exploring discover-based investigation, with hands-on experiences in a wide range of science fields. Divided into 4-week learning modules led by researchers at several UH Mānoa research facilities on and off campus.

HON 301.title: Public Policy-Making
HON 301.subject: HON
HON 301.description: Students develop understanding of theory, practice, and ethical issues of public policy-making. Combines lecture/discussion and fieldtrips. Students develop policy analysis and strategic plans that identify issues, interests, and methods of influence.
HON 301.prereq_raw: HON 101 or HON 291 (Alpha), or departmental approval.

HON 303.title: Civic Engagement and Social Justice
HON 303.subject: HON
HON 303.description: Seminar on history, theory, and practice of civic engagement in the U.S. and abroad. Involves comparative study of social justice movements, historically and today. Focus on role of university students in social justice movements.
HON 303.prereq_raw: HON 101 or HON 291 , or departmental approval.

HON 330.title: Off Campus Study Project
HON 330.subject: HON
HON 330.description: Honors students participating in off campus study (via Study Abroad Center, MIX, or NSE) enhance their experience through a project at the host site, designed with and approved with consultation with Honors advisor.
HON 330.prereq_raw: consent of Honors director and Study Abroad director.

children.text: of Honors director and Study Abroad director

HON 333.title: Experiential Learning and Scholarly Engagement
HON 333.subject: HON
HON 333.description: Students develop an understanding of theory and practice of experiential learning through direct engagement and focused scholarly reflection while assimilating and synthesizing new knowledge and developing critical thinking skills.
HON 333.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Honors Program approval only.

HON 340.title: From Ideas to Page: Learn The Publication Process
HON 340.subject: HON
HON 340.description: Learn the publication process through a “hands on” experiential learning, emphasizing diverse knowledge systems, writing, and ethics. Learn how to solicit contributions, review, and edit articles as a part of the Horizons Undergraduate Journal publication cycle.
HON 340.prereq_raw: consent of Honors director and instructor.

HON 380.title: Peer Mentoring
HON 380.subject: HON
HON 380.description: Students develop understanding of dynamics of leadership skills within the contexts of paired to large groups. Significant portion is dedicated to writing and oral communication instruction. Honors Program students only. pre-semester training sessions, on-going training and supervision.

HON 410.title: Research Mentoring
HON 410.subject: HON
HON 410.description: Mentors help others and themselves improve research methods, practice effective project management, and build research support networks. Students will learn the skills of mentoring and develop a mentoring and teaching philosophy.
HON 410.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

HON 420.title: Honors Seminar
HON 420.subject: HON
HON 420.description: Project-based experiential learning involving community-based research or creative work. Focus on project design, practical skills, and teamwork. Significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. Multi-disciplinary topics vary each semester. Honors Program students only.

HON 440.title: Honors Thesis Proposal
HON 440.subject: HON
HON 440.description: Library research skills; scholarship of research and creative work; methodological and ethical issues; development of individual proposal or prospectus for Senior Honors Project. Limited to candidates for the Honors degree.

HON 470.title: Honors Workshop
HON 470.subject: HON
HON 470.description: Supplemental workshop for students beginning independent work on their senior honors thesis. HON students only. Junior or senior standing only.

HON 480.title: Honors Senior Project I
HON 480.subject: HON
HON 480.description: Original research, creative work, performance or other form of scholarly project appropriate to a major and supervised by a faculty member. First semester of project.
HON 480.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

HON 490.title: Honors Senior Project II
HON 490.subject: HON
HON 490.description: Original research, creative work, performance or other form of scholarly project appropriate to a major and supervised by a faculty member. Second semester of project.
HON 490.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

HON 492.title: Honors Colloquium
HON 492.subject: HON
HON 492.description: Weekly meetings for discussion of enduring issues and problems of an interdisciplinary nature. Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

HRM 351.title: Human Resource Management
HRM 351.subject: HRM
HRM 351.description: Survey of the field covering recruitment, selection, training, appraisals, grievance handling, communications, discipline, safety, compensation, and benefits.

HRM 353.title: Leadership and Group Dynamics
HRM 353.subject: HRM
HRM 353.description: Explore frameworks leaders can use to get things done in their teams. Examine how leaders can engage employees, improve decision-making, manage interpersonal dynamics, and adapt to changing internal and external contexts. Emphasis on writing instruction.

HRM 354.title: Organizational Change and Effectiveness
HRM 354.subject: HRM
HRM 354.description: Identify and evaluate methods to promote an effective change transition through efficient integration of corporate goals with the organizational culture.

HRM 361.title: Labor Problems
HRM 361.subject: HRM
HRM 361.description: Problems and economics of labor; history, structure, government, activities of trade unions.

HRM 365.title: Labor and Social Legislation
HRM 365.subject: HRM
HRM 365.description: Evolution, interpretation, and application of labor and social welfare legislation with special emphasis on impact of labor-management relations.

HRM 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
HRM 399.subject: HRM
HRM 399.description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

HRM 453.title: Personnel Compensation
HRM 453.subject: HRM
HRM 453.description: Selected topics. Emphasis on trends, recent issues, job evaluation, incentive systems, salary administration, executive compensation, profit sharing, benefit programs, retirement plans.

HRM 455.title: The Staffing Process
HRM 455.subject: HRM
HRM 455.description: Contemporary practices and trends in personnel planning for a competent work force; legal constraints, recruitment and selection, differential placement, training, career programming.

HRM 463.title: Negotiation and Workplace Dispute Resolution
HRM 463.subject: HRM
HRM 463.description: Theory and practice in negotiating; design and operation of different kinds of workplace dispute resolution (such as mediation, arbitration, and various alternatives); features exercises on bargaining and negotiation and advocacy and decision skills.

HRM 467.title: Labor Management Relations
HRM 467.subject: HRM
HRM 467.description: Review and analysis of basic factors that distinguish employment relations; examination of the development of recent legislation and programs at federal, state, and municipal levels. Specific consideration given to current problems on the mainland and Hawaiʻi.

HRM 468.title: Training and Development
HRM 468.subject: HRM
HRM 468.description: Analysis of the current concepts and practices in the design, delivery, and assessment of training.

HRM 469.title: Seminar in HRM
HRM 469.subject: HRM
HRM 469.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in HRM.

HRM 671.title: Human Resource Management
HRM 671.subject: HRM
HRM 671.description: Analysis and critical evaluation of basic issues, policies, and trends in personnel administration.

HRM 672.title: Training and Development
HRM 672.subject: HRM
HRM 672.description: Covers issues in design, delivery, and assessment of training, theoretical background of training and development process, types of training process, cross cultural and other types of diversity training and development of training modules.

HRM 673.title: Advanced Organizational Behavior
HRM 673.subject: HRM
HRM 673.description: Organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.

HRM 674.title: Finance for Human Resource Management
HRM 674.subject: HRM
HRM 674.description: Intends to give HR professionals a basic overview of the vocabulary and concepts of financial decision-making. Topics include: understanding financial information, budgeting, the finance of retirement and employee benefit and business valuation.

HRM 675.title: Compensation
HRM 675.subject: HRM
HRM 675.description: Survey of compensation methods and procedures including job evaluations, incentive systems, salary administration, fringe benefits, appropriate legislation, policies and strategy issues of compensation systems.

HRM 676.title: The Staffing Process
HRM 676.subject: HRM
HRM 676.description: Recruiting and selection to optimize organizations including job design, job analysis, recruitment and selection methods, such as types of interviews and assessment centers, within legislative environment.

HRM 677.title: Negotiations and Labor Relations
HRM 677.subject: HRM
HRM 677.description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations. MHRM majors only.

HRM 678.title: International Human Resources
HRM 678.subject: HRM
HRM 678.description: Exploring global trends in human resources with focus on the Asia Pacific region.

HRM 679.title: Human Resource Management-Topics
HRM 679.subject: HRM
HRM 679.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in human resources.

HRM 680.title: Human Resource Management Capstone
HRM 680.subject: HRM
HRM 680.description: The final course in the MHRM curriculum. It provides students opportunity to integrate and apply previous course content to their professional organization offering a value-added opportunity to enhance organizational performance.

HRM 688.title: Human Resources Leadership in Healthcare Organizations
HRM 688.subject: HRM
HRM 688.description: Builds on previous leadership and management courses, focus on development of individual leadership skills emphasizing ethical and critical decision making, effective working relationships, and a systems-perspective relevant to healthcare organizations.

HSSW 477.title: Southeast Asian Cultures in Health/ Social Welfare
HSSW 477.subject: HSSW
HSSW 477.description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in Southeast and South Asian region.

HSSW 478.title: Pacific Cultures in Health/Social Welfare
HSSW 478.subject: HSSW
HSSW 478.description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in the Pacific region.

HWST 107.title: Hawaiʻi: Center of the Pacific
HWST 107.subject: HWST
HWST 107.description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawaiʻi and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

HWST 107A.title: Hawaiʻi: Center of the Pacific
HWST 107A.subject: HWST
HWST 107A.description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawaiʻi and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

HWST 207.title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupuaʻa
HWST 207.subject: HWST
HWST 207.description: Examination of the ahupuaʻa system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the mālama ʻāina track designed to build critical writing skills.

HWST 212.title: ʻAʻa Ka Hula: Introduction to Hula
HWST 212.subject: HWST
HWST 212.description: Introductory-level, performance-based Hula (Dance) exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).

HWST 214.title: Kūnihi Ka Mauna: Introduction to Oli
HWST 214.subject: HWST
HWST 214.description: (2 1-hr Lec, 1 2-hr Lab/practice) Introductory-level, performance-based Oli (Chant) exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).

HWST 220.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Visual Culture Studio
HWST 220.subject: HWST
HWST 220.description: Introduction to a variety of material (fiber, bone, wood, and stone) and skills in the media used in the Hawaiian culture. Research and explore basic techniques within the media with emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses, and conservation.

HWST 222.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio-Hana Noʻeau Maʻawe
HWST 222.subject: HWST
HWST 222.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to a variety of fibers used in the Hawaiian culture. Emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses and conservation of the fibers. Areas explored are kapa, plaiting, netting and twining.

HWST 224.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
HWST 224.subject: HWST
HWST 224.description: Research and express personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through Hawaiian visual culture. Introduction to painting and drawing media and exploration of various materials and techniques as applied to individual student styles.

HWST 225.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
HWST 225.subject: HWST
HWST 225.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to Native Hawaiian perspective and world view in images used in print and the basic material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery through the indigenous eyes.

HWST 234.title: Introduction to the Literature of Native Hawaiians and Other Indigenous People Written in English
HWST 234.subject: HWST
HWST 234.description: Surveys literature of Native Hawaiians and other Indigenous Peoples, especially to focus on the situational impetus from which these texts were created.

HWST 235.title: Native Hawaiian Composition
HWST 235.subject: HWST
HWST 235.description: Focus on studying and applying Native Hawaiian composition practices from the nineteenth century into the present day.

HWST 270.title: Hawaiian Mythology
HWST 270.subject: HWST
HWST 270.description: Survey of gods, ʻaumākua, kupua, mythical heroes, heroines, and their kinolau as the basis of traditional Hawaiian metaphor.

HWST 271.title: Papahulilani Hawaiian Astronomy I
HWST 271.subject: HWST
HWST 271.description: Introduction to Hawaiian ancestral understandings of the movements of the sun, moon and stars, and their use in ordering the Hawaiian year in planting, fishing, and ceremony.
HWST 271.prereq_raw: ( HWST 107 and HWST 270 ) with a minimum grade of B.

HWST 281.title: Hoʻokele I: Hawaiian Astronomy
HWST 281.subject: HWST
HWST 281.description: Introduction to Hawaiian views of astronomy and the stars used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators. Introduction and comparison to various Pacific island non-instrument navigation systems and star names.

HWST 281L.title: Hoʻokele I Laboratory
HWST 281L.subject: HWST
HWST 281L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Stargazing laboratory to accompany HWST 281 .

HWST 282.title: Hoʻokele II: Hawaiian Navigation
HWST 282.subject: HWST
HWST 282.description: Hawaiian and other Oceanic canoe design, navigation, Pacific weather, sailing dynamics for canoes, and sail planning strategies used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators for long voyages.

HWST 282L.title: Hoʻokele II Laboratory
HWST 282L.subject: HWST
HWST 282L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands on experience on voyaging skills and sailing canoes to accompany HWST 282 .

HWST 285.title: Lāʻau Lapaʻau: Hawaiian Medicinal Herbs
HWST 285.subject: HWST
HWST 285.description: Presentation of Hawaiian medicinal herbs including basic philosophy, identification, utilization, and preparation of such herbs for human ailments.

HWST 301.title: Perspectives in Hawaiian Studies
HWST 301.subject: HWST
HWST 301.description: Interdisciplinary lectures and discussions examining traditional and contemporary experiences in Hawaiian society and setting; resources, methods, and techniques.

HWST 307.title: Mālama ʻĀina Resource Management Visual Technologies
HWST 307.subject: HWST
HWST 307.description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

HWST 312.title: Ke Haʻa Lā: Intermediate Hula
HWST 312.subject: HWST
HWST 312.description: Intermediate-level, performance-based Hula (Dance) course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).
HWST 312.prereq_raw: HWST 212 , and HAW 201 (or concurrent), or consent.

HWST 314.title: Kū Ka Pūnohu: Intermediate Oli
HWST 314.subject: HWST
HWST 314.description: Intermediate-level, performance-based Oli (Chant) course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).
HWST 314.prereq_raw: HWST 214 , and HAW 201 (or concurrent), or consent.

HWST 320.title: Advanced Art Media
HWST 320.subject: HWST
HWST 320.description: Examine and explore advance techniques within the media and the customary and contemporary uses of a variety of material and skills used in traditional Hawaiian everyday life.

HWST 322.title: Advanced Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio- Hana Noʻeau Maʻawe
HWST 322.subject: HWST
HWST 322.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Examine the customary and contemporary use of fiber materials and the skills used in Hawaiian culture. Research and explore advanced techniques within the media used in traditional Hawaiʻi.

HWST 324.title: Advanced Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
HWST 324.subject: HWST
HWST 324.description: Advanced research and expression of personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through visual culture and language. Students will further their definitions, analysis skills, research, and understandings through painting and drawing media.

HWST 325.title: Advanced Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
HWST 325.subject: HWST
HWST 325.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Advanced Native Hawaiian perspective in imagery in print and the material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery. Lecture-lab with studio work time.

HWST 330.title: Native Hawaiian Traditions in Literature
HWST 330.subject: HWST
HWST 330.description: Discusses theoretical frameworks, main features, and cultural contexts of Hawaiian literature, with significant attention paid to developing writing skills.
HWST 330.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , and HAW 202 ; or consent.

HWST 331.title: Hawaiian and Indigenous Digital Media
HWST 331.subject: HWST
HWST 331.description: Focus on studying, analyzing, and creating various forms of Hawaiian and Indigenous digital storytelling.

HWST 341.title: Hawaiian Genealogies
HWST 341.subject: HWST
HWST 341.description: Survey of major Hawaiian chiefly lineages from the four main islands: Hawaiʻi, Maui, Oʻahu and Kauaʻi. Political history from the Kumulipo to Western contact.

HWST 342.title: Chiefs of Post-Contact Hawaiʻi
HWST 342.subject: HWST
HWST 342.description: Survey of Hawaiian chiefs from 1778 to the present, including genealogy, political function, and historical impact.

HWST 343.title: Myths of Hawaiian History
HWST 343.subject: HWST
HWST 343.description: Thematic exploration of some common myths of Hawaiian history, including infanticide, slavery, feudalism, constant warfare, human sacrifice, and a limited pre-contact population, to determine the role of myth making in perceptions of Hawaiian history. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 351.title: Mahiʻai Kalo I: Taro Cultivation
HWST 351.subject: HWST
HWST 351.description: Historical, cultural and philosophical foundations of the cultivation and uses of taro.

HWST 352.title: Mahiʻai Kalo II: Advanced Taro
HWST 352.subject: HWST
HWST 352.description: In depth-study of taro cultivation techniques and systems.

HWST 353.title: Mālama Loko Iʻa
HWST 353.subject: HWST
HWST 353.description: Study of traditional Hawaiian fishpond management with hands-on experience at Heʻeia fishpond near Kāneʻohe, merging traditional Native knowledge and ways of seeing with Western science.

HWST 356.title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
HWST 356.subject: HWST
HWST 356.description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 362.title: Pana Oʻahu: Famous Place Names
HWST 362.subject: HWST
HWST 362.description: A survey of the famous place names in each ahupuaʻa of Oʻahu, including accounts of mythical heroes, heiau, fishponds, wind, rain names, and their metaphoric value in Hawaiian literature.

HWST 365.title: Pana Paemoku o Kanaloa: The Northwestern Hawaiian Islands
HWST 365.subject: HWST
HWST 365.description: Will look at the use of the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands during precontact times, the historical period of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi, after the islands were ceded to the U.S., and the contemporary politics that surround the region today.

HWST 385.title: Lāʻau Lapaʻau: Hoʻi Ka Mana i Loko
HWST 385.subject: HWST
HWST 385.description: Advanced study and preparation of Hawaiian medicinal herb combinations.

HWST 390.title: Issues in Modern Hawaiʻi
HWST 390.subject: HWST
HWST 390.description: Cultural and political aspects of the current Hawaiian movement; historical colonization; conflicts over tourism, the military, and agriculture; forms of native self-determination. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 396.title: Native Hawaiian Rights and Practices
HWST 396.subject: HWST
HWST 396.description: Students will strengthen their cultural, political, and legal foundations by: (1) reviewing Hawaiʻi’s historical traditions and customs, (2) learning legal analysis techniques, and (3) applying those techniques to issues that govern native Hawaiian “rights” today. Sophomore or higher standing.
HWST 396.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , and HWST 341 (or concurrent) and HAW 102 .

HWST 421.title: Visiting Artist Seminar
HWST 421.subject: HWST
HWST 421.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Explore indigenous concepts through the media of a visiting indigenous master artist by looking at traditional media in indigenous cultures, and the possibilities for contemporary expression in other media.
HWST 421.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , one course in 220 level ( HWST 222 , HWST 224 , HWST 225 ), one course in 320 level ( HWST 322 , HWST 324 , HWST 325 ); or consent.

children.text: ) , one course in 320 level ( HWST 322 , HWST 324 , HWST 325 ) ; or consent

HWST 434.title: Ka Mana Moʻolelo: Topics in Hawaiian and Indigenous Moʻolelo
HWST 434.subject: HWST
HWST 434.description: Advanced course of study focusing on pressing topics connected with Hawaiian and Indigenous literatures, such as land struggle, climate change, or issues of governance and sovereignty.

HWST 440.title: Māhele Land Awards
HWST 440.subject: HWST
HWST 440.description: Practical guide to the researching of land awards and change in title for a single ahupuaʻa, 1848 to present. Focus on field trips.

HWST 441.title: Ceded Lands: Focus on Crown and Government Lands (1848 to Present)
HWST 441.subject: HWST
HWST 441.description: Inventorying “Ceded Lands” in Hawaiʻi with emphasis on historical, legal, and cultural changes from the Kingdom through statehood.

HWST 442.title: Introduction to Indigenous Research
HWST 442.subject: HWST
HWST 442.description: Survey course introduces students to a range of methods by beginning with a critical analysis of dominant research methodologies from the perspective of Indigenous scholars.
HWST 442.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior/senior standing only.

HWST 443.title: Territorial Land Law Changes & Their Effects on Kānaka
HWST 443.subject: HWST
HWST 443.description: Advanced course of study focusing on Hawaiʻi’s post-overthrow (Territorial Era) land law changes and their current day effects.

HWST 445.title: Hawaiian Institutions
HWST 445.subject: HWST
HWST 445.description: Comprehensive analysis of institutions like Bishop Estate/Kamehameha Schools, OHA, Liliʻuokalani Trust, Department of Hawaiian Home Lands and The Queen’s Hospital.

HWST 451.title: Wehe Ka ʻĀina: Cultivating a Sovereign Land Base
HWST 451.subject: HWST
HWST 451.description: A Mālama ʻĀina and Kūkulu Aupuni course that identifies modern options in land access for reestablishing or resuming Hawaiian traditional and customary practices relating to food sovereignty and self-sustainability.
HWST 451.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 and HWST 343 and HWST 351 ; HAW 202 (or concurrent).
HWST 451.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HWST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

HWST 455.title: Ola I Ka Wai; Water and Sovereignty in Hawaiʻi
HWST 455.subject: HWST
HWST 455.description: Focus on Hawaiian relationships with Ka Wai Ola a Kāne (water), traditional and contemporary water management practices, as well as contemporary resource management issues and native Hawaiian community advocacy for water.
HWST 455.prereq_raw: HWST 307 and HAW 202 (or concurrent) or consent.

HWST 456.title: Kiaʻi Kanaloa-Guarding Our Ocean Resources
HWST 456.subject: HWST
HWST 456.description: Students will actively monitor and practice coastal and ocean stewardship in support of local communities and practitioners while also exploring how the Hawaiian worldview can plan a role in aloha ʻāina conservation movements.
HWST 456.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .
HWST 456.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

HWST 457.title: ʻĀina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
HWST 457.subject: HWST
HWST 457.description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawaiʻi.
HWST 457.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

HWST 458.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
HWST 458.subject: HWST
HWST 458.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
HWST 458.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356

HWST 459.title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
HWST 459.subject: HWST
HWST 459.description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of Oʻahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.
HWST 459.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

HWST 460.title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
HWST 460.subject: HWST
HWST 460.description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawaiʻi. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.
HWST 460.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

HWST 461.title: Hawaiʻi & Indigenous Economies
HWST 461.subject: HWST
HWST 461.description: Students will map out indigenous economies by articulating cultural similarity and diversity between academic experience and professional experiences.

HWST 467.title: Mālama ʻĀina Field Methods Course
HWST 467.subject: HWST
HWST 467.description: Intensive field methods program to research Mālama ʻĀina strategies. Introduces students to a variety of field techniques including land research, historical documents, ecological surveys, and Papakū Makawalu.
HWST 467.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 , or consent.
HWST 467.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

HWST 470.title: ʻIke Akua Papakū Makawalu: Ancestral Understanding of Elements
HWST 470.subject: HWST
HWST 470.description: Uses Dr. Pualani Kanahele’s Papakū Makawalu methodology to analyze akua as elements and as a paradigm for understanding ancestral knowledge. Senior standing or higher.
HWST 470.prereq_raw: HWST 270 , HWST 372 (or concurrent), and HAW 301 (or concurrent).

HWST 478.title: Mele Au Hou: Music and Native Identity
HWST 478.subject: HWST
HWST 478.description: Presents Hawaiian music as it has been an avenue for native social, cultural and political expression in traditional and contemporary society.
HWST 478.prereq_raw: HWST 107 or HWST 343 or HWST 390 ; or consent.

HWST 485.title: Mahi Lāʻau Lapaʻau: Hawaiian Medicinal Horticulture
HWST 485.subject: HWST
HWST 485.description: The science of planting and harvesting Hawaiian medicinal plants and exploring production and marketing strategies.
HWST 485.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 285 and HWST 385 ; or consent.

HWST 487.title: Hawaiian Aquatic Medicine
HWST 487.subject: HWST
HWST 487.description: Identification, extraction and preparation of complexes of aquatic herbs to formulate a healing combination to contribute to maintaining overall health.

HWST 490.title: Senior Seminar in Hawaiian Studies
HWST 490.subject: HWST
HWST 490.description: Critical examination of existing research; individual or team development, execution, and evaluation of selected projects.
HWST 490.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior major in Hawaiian studies or consent.

HWST 491.title: Senior Capstone Project in Hawaiian Studies
HWST 491.subject: HWST
HWST 491.description: Capstone seminar designed to provide a culminating academic experience through in-depth examination, analysis, articulation, and projects relevant to a HWST area of concentration.
HWST 491.prereq_raw: HWST 341 , HWST 342 , [ HWST 343 or HWST 390 or HWST 490 (or concurrent)] and [ HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 285 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 ] and [ SUST 222 or HWST 224 or HWST 225 or HWST 372 or HWST 478 ].
HWST 491.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HWST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

HWST 493.title: Hawaiian Political Speech: Haʻi ʻŌlelo Kūʻē
HWST 493.subject: HWST
HWST 493.description: Senior seminar in short, extemporaneous speeches in persuasive, passionate and dynamic styles of Native Hawaiian orators.
HWST 493.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 , HWST 342 , or HAW 202 ; or consent.

HWST 494.title: Modern Pacific Women’s Poetry
HWST 494.subject: HWST
HWST 494.description: Critical examination of modern indigenous women’s poetry from the Pacific Islands. Thematic concentration on land, family, sexual and national oppression.

HWST 495.title: Kumu Kānāwai: Western Law and Hawaiʻi
HWST 495.subject: HWST
HWST 495.description: The rise of Western law in Hawaiʻi, its contribution to nation building and colonialism.
HWST 495.prereq_raw: HWST 342 or HWST 343 or HWST 390 ; or consent.

HWST 496.title: Kānāwai II: Practical Application of Rights
HWST 496.subject: HWST
HWST 496.description: Historical analysis of land use, race and self-determination; introduced to legal case briefing, analysis of legal precedent, practical impacts of rules and regulations and the sociopolitical factors that influence law and law enforcement.

HWST 601.title: Indigenous Research Methodologies
HWST 601.subject: HWST
HWST 601.description: Reading seminar for developing a Native Hawaiian epistemology from sources in comparative indigenous thought.
HWST 601.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

HWST 602.title: Hawaiian Archival Research
HWST 602.subject: HWST
HWST 602.description: Research seminar aimed at familiarizing students with the rich historical primary sources existent in various archives in Honolulu.
HWST 602.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

HWST 603.title: Review of Hawaiian Literature
HWST 603.subject: HWST
HWST 603.description: Seminar in review of Hawaiian literature to understand the significance of secondary sources in Hawaiian subjects. This makes up part of the Hawaiian Studies graduate core.
HWST 603.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

HWST 604.title: Writing a Hawaiian Thesis
HWST 604.subject: HWST
HWST 604.description: Seminar to help fashion student’s research and thesis proposal. To be taken by all HWST MA students as they begin designing their capstone project. Course will be team-taught by HWST faculty.

HWST 620.title: ʻIke Pono-Visual/Cultural Interpretations
HWST 620.subject: HWST
HWST 620.description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that examines (from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint) colonial imaging; collecting and site of contestation; resilience and resistance; and re-righting.
HWST 620.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , and one course from HWST 220 - HWST 225 , and one course from HWST 320 - HWST 325 ; or consent.

HWST 621.title: ʻIke Maka-Visual/Cultural Knowledge
HWST 621.subject: HWST
HWST 621.description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that carefully examines and develops critical consciousness-from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint-visual hegemony, rhetorical tropes; and representation-imag(in)ing and re-imag(in)ing.

HWST 631.title: Pono Science: Ethical Implications of Science in Hawaiʻi
HWST 631.subject: HWST
HWST 631.description: Support student dialogue on the foundations of pono science. Through discussions and structured guidance, students will explore Hawaiian ethics, implications of research, and decolonizing methodology.
HWST 631.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

HWST 640.title: Moʻolelo ʻŌiwi: Historical Perspectives
HWST 640.subject: HWST
HWST 640.description: Research seminar for developing interpretations of the past from Native Hawaiian and foreign world views with particular emphasis on understanding the meaning of culturally-based knowledge systems.

HWST 648.title: Mele Hawaiʻi: Mele as Systems of Knowledge
HWST 648.subject: HWST
HWST 648.description: Seminar on Mele Hawaiʻi (Songs, Poetry, Chants) as systems of knowledge that record, communicate, and critique historical, political, environmental, and cultural information. Will include learning and analysis of mele, culminating with a research project.
HWST 648.prereq_raw: HAW 302 and ( HWST 478 or HAW 384 or HAW 484 ).

HWST 650.title: Hawaiian Geography and Resource Management
HWST 650.subject: HWST
HWST 650.description: Seminar in geography of Hawaiʻi from a Native Hawaiian perspective that will enable the researcher to define and develop resource management methods consistent with Native Hawaiian understandings and traditions.
HWST 650.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent).

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

HWST 651.title: ʻĀina Waiwai: Water, Food Sovereignty, and Ancestral Abundance
HWST 651.subject: HWST
HWST 651.description: Topical graduate seminar focuses on indigenous perspectives on water, food sovereignty, Hawaiian terrestrial and marine food production systems, and ancestral abundance. Seminar perspective to change each term.
HWST 651.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 and HAW 202 or consent.

HWST 652.title: Kānāwai Lawaiʻa: Hawaiʻi’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
HWST 652.subject: HWST
HWST 652.description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance.

HWST 653.title: Historic Preservation Law
HWST 653.subject: HWST
HWST 653.description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws.

HWST 659.title: He Aliʻi Ka ʻĀina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
HWST 659.subject: HWST
HWST 659.description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ʻĀina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ʻĀina future.

HWST 670.title: Kumu Kahiki: Comparative Hawaiian and Tahitian Cosmogonies
HWST 670.subject: HWST
HWST 670.description: Seminar comparing Gods/myths from Ancient Tahiti by Teuira Henry (600 pages) with the six volumes of Hawaiian historians Kamakau and Malo.

HWST 671.title: Kumu Kahiki: Pacific Life Narratives in Mixed Media and Literature
HWST 671.subject: HWST
HWST 671.description: Research seminar in relevant literary traditions, histories of interaction, colonization, and literary politics in the Pacific region through the examination of life narratives in mixed media and literature.

HWST 672.title: Indigenous Futurisms: Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, and Beyond
HWST 672.subject: HWST
HWST 672.description: Seminar on Indigenous Futurisms as developed in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, and other Indigenous contexts, and expressed through art, literature, film, music, and scholarship.

HWST 675.title: Huakaʻi Huli Heiau Hawaiʻinuiākea: Study Abroad on Polynesian Temples
HWST 675.subject: HWST
HWST 675.description: Comparative study of Hawaiian/Polynesian temple design taught over a 3-week period in Hawaiʻi and Polynesia. Travel costs to be paid by student.
HWST 675.prereq_raw: HWST 670 (with a minimum grade of B) and HAW 302 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

HWST 690.title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Envisioning the Nation
HWST 690.subject: HWST
HWST 690.description: A research seminar designed to provide an overview of community activism and Native Hawaiian empowerment in Hawaiʻi in contexts that range from local to international, and to provide a foundation for further study and professional growth.
HWST 690.prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

HWST 691.title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Sovereign Hawaiian State, Domestic Kingdom Law, Governance and Politics
HWST 691.subject: HWST
HWST 691.description: Research seminar on the subject of domestic law, governance, and politics of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the historical relevance of this to the contemporary case for independent, sovereign state continuity under public international law.

HWST 700.title: Thesis Research
HWST 700.subject: HWST
HWST 700.description: Research for master’s thesis. (F) Full-time. S/U for (F) only.

ICS 101.title: Digital Tools for the Information World
ICS 101.subject: ICS
ICS 101.description: Fundamental information technology concepts and computing terminology, productivity software for problem solving, computer technology trends and impact on individuals and society. Emphasizes the utilization of operating systems and the production of professional documents, spreadsheets, etc. Honors Equivalent: ICS 101A

ICS 101A.title: Digital Tools for the Information World
ICS 101A.subject: ICS
ICS 101A.description: Fundamental information technology concepts and computing terminology, productivity software for problem solving, computer technology trends and impact on individuals and society. Emphasizes the utilization of operating systems and the production of professional documents, spreadsheets, etc.

ICS 102.title: Introduction to Data Science
ICS 102.subject: ICS
ICS 102.description: Overview of the field of data science. Introduction to subjects such as data format, processing, visualization, and storage. Special emphasis on historical and wider context, and simple practical examples.

ICS 103.title: Introduction to Computer Science Principles
ICS 103.subject: ICS
ICS 103.description: General course that provides a broad overview of computer science. Will address abstraction, data and information, algorithms, programming, the Internet and the global impact of computers.

ICS 104.title: Introduction to Generative AI
ICS 104.subject: ICS
ICS 104.description: Introduces fundamentals of generative Artificial Intelligence (Al). Through hands-on projects, students will learn prompt engineering, model customization, ethical considerations, and practical uses of generative Al in writing, design, and education.

ICS 110C.title: Introduction to Computer Programming: C
ICS 110C.subject: ICS
ICS 110C.description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.

ICS 110D.title: Introduction to Computer Programming: through animations
ICS 110D.subject: ICS
ICS 110D.description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.

ICS 110P.title: Introduction to Computer Programming: Python
ICS 110P.subject: ICS
ICS 110P.description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.

ICS 111.title: Introduction to Computer Science I
ICS 111.subject: ICS
ICS 111.description: Overview of the fundamentals of computer science emphasizing problem solving, algorithm development, implementation, and debugging/testing using an object-oriented programming language.
ICS 111.prereq_raw: Recommended: computer experience. Honors Equivalent: ICS 111A

prereq_tree.text: Recommended: computer experience. Honors Equivalent: ICS 111A

ICS 111A.title: Introduction to Computer Science I
ICS 111A.subject: ICS
ICS 111A.description: Overview of the fundamentals of computer science emphasizing problem solving, algorithm development, implementation, and debugging/testing using an object-oriented programming language.

ICS 141.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science I
ICS 141.subject: ICS
ICS 141.description: Includes logic, sets, functions, matrices, algorithmic concepts, mathematical reasoning, recursion, counting techniques, and probability theory.

ICS 210.title: Information Systems in Society
ICS 210.subject: ICS
ICS 210.description: Lecture/ discussion critically explores sociopolitical dimensions of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), and the information professions.

ICS 211.title: Introduction to Computer Science II
ICS 211.subject: ICS
ICS 211.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Reinforce and strengthen problem-solving skills using abstract data types and introduce software development practices. Emphasize the use of searching and sorting algorithms and their complexity, recursion, object-oriented programming, and data structures.
ICS 211.prereq_raw: ICS 111 or consent. Honors Equivalent: ICS 211A

ICS 211A.title: Introduction to Computer Science II
ICS 211A.subject: ICS
ICS 211A.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Reinforce and strengthen problem-solving skills using abstract data types and introduce software development practices. Emphasize the use of searching and sorting algorithms and their complexity, recursion, object-oriented programming, and data structures.

ICS 212.title: Program Structure
ICS 212.subject: ICS
ICS 212.description: Program organization paradigms, programming environments, implementation of a module from specifications, the C and C programming languages.

ICS 215.title: Introduction to Scripting
ICS 215.subject: ICS
ICS 215.description: Introduction to scripting languages for the integration of applications and systems. Scripting in operating systems, web pages, server-side application integration, regular expressions, and event handling for languages such as Perl, JavaScript, PHP, Python, shell scripting.

ICS 222.title: Basic Concepts of Computer Science
ICS 222.subject: ICS
ICS 222.description: What is the subject of computer science? What is a computer? Understand the basic models of computation and the concepts of computability, complexity, and network computation, and learn to use them in practice.

ICS 235.title: Machine Learning Methods
ICS 235.subject: ICS
ICS 235.description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning.

ICS 241.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science II
ICS 241.subject: ICS
ICS 241.description: Includes program correctness, recurrence relations and their solutions, relations and their properties, divide and conquer relations, graph theory, trees and their applications, Boolean algebra, introduction to formal languages and automata theory.

ICS 290.title: Computer Science Careers: An Exploration of the Specialties of Computer Science
ICS 290.subject: ICS
ICS 290.description: Exploration of the specialties of computer science. Meets every two week for 2.5 hours to explore specific areas in computer science.

ICS 296.title: Sophomore Project
ICS 296.subject: ICS
ICS 296.description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in a beginner-level design of a software project expected to be continued in ICS 396 .

ICS 311.title: Algorithms
ICS 311.subject: ICS
ICS 311.description: (4 1-hr Lec) Design and correctness of algorithms, including divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming methods. Complexity analyses using recurrence relations, probabilistic methods, and NP-completeness. Applications to order statistics, disjoint sets, B-trees and balanced trees, graphs, network flows, and string matching.
ICS 311.prereq_raw: ICS 211 , and [( ICS 241 or ECE 362 ) and ( MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A )] or ( MATH 301 and MATH 372 ); or consent.

ICS 312.title: Machine-Level and Systems Programming
ICS 312.subject: ICS
ICS 312.description: Machine organization, machine instructions, addressing modes, assembler language, subroutine linkage, linking to higher-level languages, interface to operating systems, introduction to assemblers, loaders and compilers.
ICS 312.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) (or concurrent), ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ), and ICS 314 ; or consent.

ICS 313.title: Programming Language Theory
ICS 313.subject: ICS
ICS 313.description: Syntax, semantics, control structures, variable binding and scopes, data and control abstractions. Programming in functional (LISP) and logic (Prolog) programming styles.
ICS 313.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ), ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ), and ICS 314 ; or consent.

ICS 314.title: Software Engineering I
ICS 314.subject: ICS
ICS 314.description: Problem analysis and design, team-oriented development, quality assurance, configuration management, project planning. These topics are covered in the sequence 314-414.
ICS 314.prereq_raw: ( ICS 211 or ECE 205 ) and [ ICS 241 or ECE 362 or ( MATH 301 and MATH 372 )]; or consent.

ICS 321.title: Database Systems I
ICS 321.subject: ICS
ICS 321.description: Introduction to relational database systems, data modeling, query processing, transaction processing, storage, and indexing.
ICS 321.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 331.title: Logic Design and Microprocessors
ICS 331.subject: ICS
ICS 331.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Basic machine architecture, microprocessors, bus organization, circuit elements, logic circuit analysis and design, microcomputer system design.
ICS 331.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ), ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ), and ICS 314 ; or consent.

ICS 332.title: Operating Systems
ICS 332.subject: ICS
ICS 332.description: Operating system concepts and structure, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, scheduling, file systems, inter-process communication, virtualization, popular operating systems.

ICS 351.title: Network Design and Management
ICS 351.subject: ICS
ICS 351.description: Overview of the internet and its capabilities; introduction to HTTP, TCP/IP, ethernet, and wireless 802.11; routers, switches, and NAT; network and wireless security; practical experience in designing and implementing networks.
ICS 351.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 355.title: Security and Trust I: Resource Protections
ICS 355.subject: ICS
ICS 355.description: Security and trust in computers, networks, and society. Security models. Access and authorization. Availability and Denial-of-Service. Trust processes and network interactions.

ICS 361.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
ICS 361.subject: ICS
ICS 361.description: Introduction to the theory of Artificial Intelligence and the practical application of AI techniques. Students gain practical experience through programming assignments and projects.
ICS 361.prereq_raw: ( ICS 215 or ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 ; or consent.

ICS 369.title: Computational Media Systems
ICS 369.subject: ICS
ICS 369.description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.
ICS 369.prereq_raw: Any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or ECE 160 or instructor approval.
ICS 369.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

ICS 390.title: Computing Ethics for Lab Assistants
ICS 390.subject: ICS
ICS 390.description: Lecture/discussion/internship on ethical issues and instructional techniques for students assisting computer sciences classes in various settings. The class uses multiple significant writing and oral presentation activities to help students learn course content.

ICS 396.title: Junior Project
ICS 396.subject: ICS
ICS 396.description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in intermediate-level design, implementation and presentation of a software project that may have been initiated in ICS 296 .

ICS 414.title: Software Engineering II
ICS 414.subject: ICS
ICS 414.description: Continuation of ICS 314 . Project management, quality, and productivity control, testing and validation, team management. Team-oriented software-implementation project.

ICS 415.title: Introduction to Programming for the Web
ICS 415.subject: ICS
ICS 415.description: Introduction to emerging technologies for construction of World Wide Web (WWW)-based software. Covers programming and scripting languages used for the creation of WWW sites and client-server programming. Students will complete a medium-sized software project that uses languages and concepts discussed in class.
ICS 415.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 419.title: The Science, Psychology and Philosophy of Systems Design
ICS 419.subject: ICS
ICS 419.description: Scientific, psychological and philosophical bases of systems design, including a survey of human-factors and ergonomic standards; the nature of innovation and creativity as it relates to systems design. Web-enhanced course.
ICS 419.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 421.title: Database Systems II
ICS 421.subject: ICS
ICS 421.description: Very large database systems, data integration, data warehousing, designing big data systems, parallel query processing, distributed transactions.

ICS 422.title: Network Science Methodology
ICS 422.subject: ICS
ICS 422.description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages.

ICS 423.title: Data Security and Cryptography I
ICS 423.subject: ICS
ICS 423.description: Secret communication and confidentiality data storage. Elements of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Classical ciphers. Symmetric key cryptography. Public key cryptography. Data security in cyber space.

ICS 424.title: Application Frameworks
ICS 424.subject: ICS
ICS 424.description: Experience producing applications with at least two different applications frameworks.
ICS 424.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 425.title: Computer Security and Ethics
ICS 425.subject: ICS
ICS 425.description: Theoretical results, security policy, encryption, key management, digital signatures, certificates, passwords. Ethics: privacy, computer crime, professional ethics. Effects of the computer revolution on society.

ICS 426.title: Computer System Security
ICS 426.subject: ICS
ICS 426.description: Information flow, confinement, information assurance, malicious programs, vulnerability analysis, network security, writing secure programs.

ICS 427.title: Programming Approaches to Software Quality Assurance
ICS 427.subject: ICS
ICS 427.description: Examination of best practices associated with developing and supporting software applications with respect to potential security risks. Will augment software engineering practices learned in other courses with the basic principles of cybersecurity.

ICS 428.title: Digital Forensics
ICS 428.subject: ICS
ICS 428.description: Provides students with the knowledge of underlying principles and skills to identify, preserve, and extract electronic evidence for further analysis.

ICS 429.title: Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies
ICS 429.subject: ICS
ICS 429.description: Studies the fundamentals and reviews the latest developments in the field of Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies, including programming of introductory Smart Contracts. Knowledge of programming or finance recommended.
ICS 429.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ICS 431.title: Computer Architecture
ICS 431.subject: ICS
ICS 431.description: Memory management, control flow, interrupt mechanisms, multiprocessor systems, special-purpose devices.

ICS 432.title: Concurrent and High-Performance Programming
ICS 432.subject: ICS
ICS 432.description: Principles of concurrent and high performance programming. Multi-threading in C and Java for shared-memory programming. Distributed memory programming with Java. Introduction to cluster computing.
ICS 432.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ICS 332 and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 ; or consent.

ICS 434.title: Data Science Fundamentals
ICS 434.subject: ICS
ICS 434.description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist.

ICS 435.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
ICS 435.subject: ICS
ICS 435.description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory.

ICS 438.title: Big Data Analytics
ICS 438.subject: ICS
ICS 438.description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.

ICS 441.title: Theory of Computation
ICS 441.subject: ICS
ICS 441.description: Grammars, sequential machines, equivalence, minimalization, analysis and synthesis, regular expressions, computability, unsolvability, Gödel’s theorem, Turing machines.
ICS 441.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 442.title: Analytical Models and Methods
ICS 442.subject: ICS
ICS 442.description: Applications of mathematical methods in computer science with emphasis on discrete mathematics, numerical computation, algebraic models, operations research.
ICS 442.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 443.title: Parallel Algorithms
ICS 443.subject: ICS
ICS 443.description: Introduction to parallel models of computation and design and analysis of parallel algorithms.

ICS 444.title: Security Science of Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
ICS 444.subject: ICS
ICS 444.description: Safety is a central concern in applications of machine learning and natural language processing. The course presents a framework for applying dependability models and methodologies to intelligent software.
ICS 444.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

ICS 451.title: Data Networks
ICS 451.subject: ICS
ICS 451.description: Network analysis, architecture, digital signal analysis and design; circuit switching, packet switching, packet broadcasting; protocols and standards; local area networks; satellite networks; ALOHA channels; examples.
ICS 451.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 ; or consent.

ICS 452.title: Software Design for Robotics
ICS 452.subject: ICS
ICS 452.description: Sensors, actuators, signal processing, paradigms of robotic software design, introduction to machine learning, introduction to computer vision, and robot-to-human interaction.
ICS 452.prereq_raw: two ICS 300-level courses or consent. Recommended: ICS 312 and ICS 313 .

ICS 455.title: Security and Trust II: Information Assurance
ICS 455.subject: ICS
ICS 455.description: Channel security. Trojan and noninterference. Basic concepts of cryptology. Cryptographic primitives. Protocols for authentication and key establishment.

ICS 461.title: Artificial Intelligence
ICS 461.subject: ICS
ICS 461.description: Survey of artificial intelligence: natural language processing, vision and robotics, expert systems. Emphasis on fundamental concepts: search, planning, and problem solving, logic, knowledge representation.

ICS 462.title: Artificial Intelligence for Games
ICS 462.subject: ICS
ICS 462.description: Techniques to stimulate intelligence in video games: movement, pathfinding with A* search, decision/ behavior trees, state machines, machine learning, tactics. Extend games with your own AI implementations; experience “shootout” contests for the best AI algorithm/implementation.
ICS 462.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 and ( PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ).

ICS 464.title: Human Computer Interaction I
ICS 464.subject: ICS
ICS 464.description: Application of concepts and methodologies of human factors, psychology and software engineering to address ergonomic, cognitive, and social factors in the design and evaluation of human-computer systems.
ICS 464.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 465.title: Introduction to Hypermedia
ICS 465.subject: ICS
ICS 465.description: Basic issues of interactive access to information in various formats on computers. Available hardware and software: editing, integration, programming. Implementation of a sample information system.

ICS 466.title: Design for Mobile Devices
ICS 466.subject: ICS
