ICS 466.description: Lecture introducing design issues, programming languages, operating systems and mark-up languages for internet-enabled mobile devices, such as cell phones and PDAs.
ICS 466.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 469.title: Cognitive Science
ICS 469.subject: ICS
ICS 469.description: Introduces basic concepts, central problems, and methods from cognitive science. Identifies contributions from disciplines such as cognitive psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosophy, and neuroscience.
ICS 469.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 471.title: Probability, Statistics, and Queuing
ICS 471.subject: ICS
ICS 471.description: A hands-on introduction to probability, statistical inference, regression, Markov chains, queuing theory. Use of an interactive statistical graphics environment such as R.
ICS 471.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 475.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Sequences and Genomes Analysis
ICS 475.subject: ICS
ICS 475.description: Introduction to bioinformatics to computer sciences students by focusing on how computer sciences techniques can be used for the storage, analysis, prediction and simulation of biological sequences (DNA, RNA and proteins).
ICS 475.prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

ICS 476.title: Bioinformatics Algorithms and Tool Development
ICS 476.subject: ICS
ICS 476.description: Study of commonly used bioinformatic algorithms, with an emphasis on string, tree, and graph algorithms. Presentation of probabilistic and clustering methods. Implementation of the studied algorithms and design of applications.

ICS 481.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
ICS 481.subject: ICS
ICS 481.description: Fundamentals of computer graphics including graphics hardware, representation, manipulation, and display of two- and three-dimensional objects, use of commercial software.
ICS 481.prereq_raw: ( ICS 369 or ECE 369 ) and ( MATH 307 or MATH 311 ); or consent.

ICS 482.title: Topics in Computer Graphics
ICS 482.subject: ICS
ICS 482.description: Review of selected graphics literature, with a software development project based on a topic of interest.

ICS 483.title: Computer Vision
ICS 483.subject: ICS
ICS 483.description: Introductory course in computer vision. Topics include image formation, image processing and filtering, edge detection, texture analysis and synthesis, binocular stereo, segmentation, tracking, object recognition and applications.
ICS 483.prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 and ( MATH 307 or MATH 311 or ECE 345 ); or consent.

ICS 484.title: Data Visualization
ICS 484.subject: ICS
ICS 484.description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization.
ICS 484.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ICS 485.title: Video Game Design and Development
ICS 485.subject: ICS
ICS 485.description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments.
ICS 485.prereq_raw: any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or CINE 215 .
ICS 485.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ICS 486.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
ICS 486.subject: ICS
ICS 486.description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.
ICS 486.prereq_raw: any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or CINE 215 .

ICS 487.title: 3D Modeling and Animation Techniques
ICS 487.subject: ICS
ICS 487.description: Principles, techniques, and history of 3D computer graphics. Modeling and animation techniques will be covered, as well as basic lighting and rendering.

ICS 488.title: 3D Rendering Techniques
ICS 488.subject: ICS
ICS 488.description: Software development within a commercial 3D application with a focus on scripting and plugin development for procedural modeling, animation, and shading.

ICS 489.title: Software Techniques for Computer Visual Effects
ICS 489.subject: ICS
ICS 489.description: Principles, techniques, and history of visual effects and underlying software techniques for computer visual effects. Project-based course involving the merging of computer generated imagery with live action footage.

ICS 491.title: Special Topics
ICS 491.subject: ICS
ICS 491.description: Reflects special interests of faculty. Oriented toward juniors and seniors.
ICS 491.prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS classes or consent.

ICS 495.title: Special Topics in Security
ICS 495.subject: ICS
ICS 495.description: Special topics in security oriented toward juniors and seniors.
ICS 495.prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS courses or consent.

ICS 496.title: Capstone Project
ICS 496.subject: ICS
ICS 496.description: Project-based course where students work in teams on a software project. Knowledge acquired in the computer science curriculum will be applied to design and implement a software product with potential real-world applicability.
ICS 496.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

ICS 499.title: Computer Project
ICS 499.subject: ICS
ICS 499.description: Individual or small-group projects in system design or application under faculty supervision.

ICS 601.title: Applied Computing Industry Seminar
ICS 601.subject: ICS
ICS 601.description: Introduction to the importance of building and utilizing AI systems and an exploration of the current industry landscape.
ICS 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 602.title: Practical Problem Solving with Algorithms
ICS 602.subject: ICS
ICS 602.description: Effectively identify and solve problems using various algorithmic approaches. Through hands-on projects and real-world examples, students will learn to analyze, design, and implement foundational algorithms.
ICS 602.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 603.title: Applied Computing Fundamentals
ICS 603.subject: ICS
ICS 603.description: Provides necessary programming skills in Python for data science and AI, and introduces language models as programming copilots. Students also learn AI-assisted programming through validation, testing, documentation, optimization, and software design.
ICS 603.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 604.title: Applied Data Science
ICS 604.subject: ICS
ICS 604.description: Introduces foundational principles of data science, emphasizing elementary concepts and essential tools integral to the data scientist’s role from data wrangling to foundational tools for modeling data, without requiring knowledge of linear algebra or calculus.
ICS 604.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 605.title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
ICS 605.subject: ICS
ICS 605.description: Covers fundamentals of artificial intelligence, and especially machine learning, for students and industry professionals who aim to immediately implement AI and data science solutions in their career.
ICS 605.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 606.title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
ICS 606.subject: ICS
ICS 606.description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
ICS 606.prereq_raw: ICS 313 or ECE 467 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent

ICS 609.title: Practicum / Internship
ICS 609.subject: ICS
ICS 609.description: Designed to provide students with real-world experience in the field of computer science. Aims to bridge the gap between academic theories and practical applications in a professional environment.
ICS 609.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 611.title: Compiler Theory and Construction
ICS 611.subject: ICS
ICS 611.description: Design and implementation of compilers, syntactic and semantic descriptions of programming languages, algorithms for syntactic analysis and object code generation.

ICS 612.title: Theory of Operating Systems
ICS 612.subject: ICS
ICS 612.description: Advanced study in operating systems theory and design with emphasis on case studies and distributed systems.

ICS 613.title: Advanced Software Engineering
ICS 613.subject: ICS
ICS 613.description: Fundamental software engineering procedures, including planning, estimation, design, testing, process definition and improvement, and software quality assurance. Measurement techniques are used to support empirically-driven software process improvement throughout the course.
ICS 613.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 614.title: Medical Informatics I
ICS 614.subject: ICS
ICS 614.description: Introduction to the field of medical informatics, which is found at the intersection of clinical science, public health, information science, computer technology and communications technology. Concentration on current issues.

ICS 615.title: Software Quality and Maintenance
ICS 615.subject: ICS
ICS 615.description: Introduction to software quality concepts and the major activities involved in software maintenance.

ICS 616.title: Information Architecture and Web Design
ICS 616.subject: ICS
ICS 616.description: User-centered design of websites; survey Information Architecture (IA) systems (organization, navigation, labeling, searching); gain experience in methodologies for creating IA, tools for IA, web standards and usability tests.
ICS 616.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in ICS or LIS or related field or consent. ICS and LIS majors only.

ICS 621.title: Analysis of Algorithms
ICS 621.subject: ICS
ICS 621.description: Analysis and design of algorithms: modeling, comparison, measures, applications.
ICS 621.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 622.title: Network Science
ICS 622.subject: ICS
ICS 622.description: Modeling human-made and natural systems as networks to understand their structure and dynamics. Computational and statistical methods and research results they enabled. Use of network analysis software. Applications to topics of interest to students.

ICS 623.title: Advanced Cryptography
ICS 623.subject: ICS
ICS 623.description: Taxonomy of security properties: methods for defining and proving security. Randomness, pseudorandomness, and indistinguishability. Functional encryption and obfuscation. Zero knowledge.
ICS 623.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 624.title: Advanced Data Management
ICS 624.subject: ICS
ICS 624.description: Exploration of information retrieval and object-relational tools and methods for the management of distributed multimedia database systems.
ICS 624.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 632.title: Principles of High Performance Computing
ICS 632.subject: ICS
ICS 632.description: Principles of high performance computing for single-processor and parallel architectures. Detailed coverage of parallel architectures and exposure to shared-memory, distributed-memory, and hybrid parallelism. Hands-on experience with message-passing and multi-threaded programming.
ICS 632.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in computer science or closely related field, or consent.

ICS 635.title: Machine Learning
ICS 635.subject: ICS
ICS 635.description: Introduction to key theoretical concepts of machine learning. Practical experience with decision free methods, artificial neural networks. Bayesian belief networks and contemporary statistical methods including regression, clustering and classification.

ICS 636.title: Information Theory in Machine Learning
ICS 636.subject: ICS
ICS 636.description: Basics of information processing and learning in the brain; neural networks; learning algorithms based on information maximization; applications in molecular biology and bioinformatics.
ICS 636.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in computer science or mathematics background, or consent.

ICS 637.title: Deep Learning with Neural Networks
ICS 637.subject: ICS
ICS 637.description: Graduate course on deep learning with artificial neural networks. Provides practical techniques for modeling image, video, text, and graph data with supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches. Includes instruction in the latest software frameworks.
ICS 637.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 639.title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
ICS 639.subject: ICS
ICS 639.description: Covers the latest developments in human-centered artificial intelligence, including ethics, bias, explainability, privacy, fairness, and usability. Involves discussion, writing assignments, and a final project.

ICS 641.title: Advanced Theory of Computation
ICS 641.subject: ICS
ICS 641.description: Advanced topics in formal languages, automata, computability, computational complexity.

ICS 643.title: Advanced Parallel Algorithms
ICS 643.subject: ICS
ICS 643.description: Design and analysis of parallel algorithms, with emphasis on advanced techniques and latest advances in parallel algorithms.
ICS 643.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 644.title: Advanced Security Science of Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
ICS 644.subject: ICS
ICS 644.description: The advances in machine learning and natural language processing open a gamut of new security challenges and opportunities. Updating security concepts and methods requires a scientific approach.
ICS 644.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 651.title: Computer Networks
ICS 651.subject: ICS
ICS 651.description: Elementary principles of modern computer networking. Detailed coverage of overall architecture and the physical, data link, and network layers, with emphasis on the network layer.
ICS 651.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in ICS, or consent. ICS majors only.

ICS 655.title: Security and Trust III: Cyber Security and Commerce
ICS 655.subject: ICS
ICS 655.description: Tools and methods for security managers. Tools and methods to secure and monetize services and applications. Network as a computer and as a market. Problems of cyber war, cyber crime, cyber bullying.
ICS 655.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 660.title: Computer Architecture I
ICS 660.subject: ICS
ICS 660.description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.

ICS 661.title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence
ICS 661.subject: ICS
ICS 661.description: Current issues in artificial intelligence, including expert systems, knowledge representation, logic programming, learning, natural language processing.
ICS 661.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 663.title: Pattern Recognition
ICS 663.subject: ICS
ICS 663.description: Nature of the problem in pattern recognition and clustering; explanation of various algorithms.
ICS 663.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 664.title: Human-Computer Interaction II
ICS 664.subject: ICS
ICS 664.description: Studies of human performance in designing and using information systems. Emphasizes concepts and methodologies from human factors, psychology, and software engineering relating to human performance.
ICS 664.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 665.title: User Interfaces and Hypermedia
ICS 665.subject: ICS
ICS 665.description: Advanced concepts in construction of interfaces between computers and their users. Hypermedia information structures, guidelines, problems, and tradeoffs. Discussion of selected readings, implementation of prototypes.

ICS 667.title: HCI Design Methods
ICS 667.subject: ICS
ICS 667.description: Advanced analytical and empirical methods for the design and evaluation of usable, useful, and robust human-computer interfaces. Students will apply selected methodologies to a major system design project.

ICS 668.title: Social Informatics
ICS 668.subject: ICS
ICS 668.description: An advanced introduction to the design of human-computer systems and other technological artifacts for supporting human collaboration in learning, work and social contexts, and to theoretical perspectives and empirical studies of collaboration that inform such design.
ICS 668.prereq_raw: ICS 464 or ICS 465 or ICS 664 or ICS 665 or ICS 667 or LIS 677 ; or consent.

ICS 669.title: Social Computing
ICS 669.subject: ICS
ICS 669.description: Participative analysis of online communities and user-generated content collections. Theoretical and practical aspects of online interaction, identity, trust, and virtual social capital.

ICS 674.title: Evolutionary Computation I: Survey of Methods
ICS 674.subject: ICS
ICS 674.description: Evolutionary computation surveys in the field to prepare students for research. Topics include diverse engineering applications, theory, and concepts including search spaces, representation, objective functions, variation operators, selection, and population based search.
ICS 674.prereq_raw: ICS 211 (B or better) and ICS 241 (C or better) and admitted to a graduate program or capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences, or consent.

children.text: capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences,

ICS 675.title: Bioinformatics: Sequences Analysis
ICS 675.subject: ICS
ICS 675.description: To expose students to bioinformatics at the biological sequences analysis level (DNA, RNA, proteins). Several bioinformatics methods and algorithms are introduced. Students are required to present one paper and to participate in a small group project.
ICS 675.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 676.title: Bioinformatics: Microarrays
ICS 676.subject: ICS
ICS 676.description: Introduction to the basic principles of biology relevant for microarray gene expression data and to Bioconductor. Collaborative open-source project to develop a modular general framework for the analysis of cDNA arrays and gene chips.
ICS 676.prereq_raw: ICS 311 or background in biology, or consent.

ICS 681.title: Computer Graphics
ICS 681.subject: ICS
ICS 681.description: Selected advanced topics in computer graphics. Substantial project required.

ICS 682.title: Numerical Computation
ICS 682.subject: ICS
ICS 682.description: Selected topics in numerical analysis, mathematical software, and scientific computation; examples include sparse matrix methods, finite element methods, mathematical programming.

ICS 683.title: Advanced Computer Vision
ICS 683.subject: ICS
ICS 683.description: Fundamental problems and core concepts and techniques in computer vision, covering both theoretical and practical issues in the field.
ICS 683.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

ICS 684.title: Advanced Data Visualization
ICS 684.subject: ICS
ICS 684.description: Explores advanced techniques in data visualization by surveying visualization techniques from the past 5-10 years, and designing and developing data visualizations leveraging those techniques.
ICS 684.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 685.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
ICS 685.subject: ICS
ICS 685.description: Students will learn the science, engineering, art, and applications of virtual reality and augmented reality, with an emphasis on the construction of working virtual environments.
ICS 685.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ICS 686.title: Digital Video Information
ICS 686.subject: ICS
ICS 686.description: Principles and techniques of technical and context analysis of digital video information. Video capture and editing tools, compression and analysis algorithms, visual culture, narrative structure, juxtaposition of multimedia elements and their effects on information transmission.
ICS 686.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ILO 101.title: Beginning Ilokano I
ILO 101.subject: ILO
ILO 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

ILO 102.title: Beginning Ilokano II
ILO 102.subject: ILO
ILO 102.description: Continuation of ILO 101 . Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

ILO 107.title: Ilokano for Health Sciences
ILO 107.subject: ILO
ILO 107.description: Development of listening, speaking, reading, writing and other communication skills designed specifically for Nursing, Dentistry, Dental Hygiene, Public Health and Social Work students. Culture integrated with language study.

ILO 201.title: Intermediate Ilokano I
ILO 201.subject: ILO
ILO 201.description: Continuation of ILO 102 . Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

ILO 202.title: Intermediate Ilokano II
ILO 202.subject: ILO
ILO 202.description: Continuation of ILO 201 . Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

ILO 301.title: Third-Level Ilokano
ILO 301.subject: ILO
ILO 301.description: To further acquire and develop Ilokano language skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing, utilizes ethnographic and sociolinguistic approaches in order to further examine and interrogate the relationship of language and culture.

ILO 315.title: Ilokano Aural Comprehension
ILO 315.subject: ILO
ILO 315.description: Training in listening comprehension of different authentic and simulated materials as presented in documentaries, soap operas, radio and television news and other broadcasts, formal lectures, plays, natural conversations, songs, and student-created sitcoms and dramas.

ILO 331.title: Contemporary Ilokano Literature
ILO 331.subject: ILO
ILO 331.description: Conducted in Ilokano, this course explores the literary landscape of Ilokano literature from the perspective of Ilokano writers based in the Philippines as well as those outside of the country.

ILO 401.title: Fourth-Level Ilokano
ILO 401.subject: ILO
ILO 401.description: Taught in Ilokano; explores the language’s applications in social services, communication, education, and healthcare. Students perform tasks such as writing reports, conducting interviews, and documenting the life stories of immigrant Ilokanos in Hawai’i.

ILO 424.title: Introduction to Ilokano for Interpreters
ILO 424.subject: ILO
ILO 424.description: Techniques for interpreting Ilokano into English and vice versa.

ILO 425.title: Ilokano Interpretation Field Practicum
ILO 425.subject: ILO
ILO 425.description: Provide extensive practical training in consecutive, simultaneous, sight and telephonic interpreting. It requires observation and study of interpretation strategies and techniques in relevant situations.

ILO 451.title: Structure of Ilokano
ILO 451.subject: ILO
ILO 451.description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, and syntax.

ILO 486.title: Ilokano for the Mass Media
ILO 486.subject: ILO
ILO 486.description: Ilokano as the medium for print journalism, for radio show programming, and for television production.

IND 101.title: Elementary Indonesian I
IND 101.subject: IND
IND 101.description: First semester of elementary Indonesian. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Indonesia.

IND 102.title: Elementary Indonesian II
IND 102.subject: IND
IND 102.description: Second semester of elementary Indonesian. Emphasis on the continued development of communicative competence in both oral and written language.

IND 201.title: Intermediate Indonesian I
IND 201.subject: IND
IND 201.description: The first semester of intermediate Indonesian. Emphasis on the continued development of competence in both oral and written language for more advance communication and travel.

IND 202.title: Intermediate Indonesian II
IND 202.subject: IND
IND 202.description: Second semester of intermediate Indonesian. Emphasis on the continued development of competence in both oral and written language for more advanced communication, travel, and further study.

IND 301.title: Third-Level Indonesian
IND 301.subject: IND
IND 301.description: Continuation of IND 202 . Conducted in Indonesian. Meets three hours a week. Reading, discussion, composition, and projects.

IND 305.title: Third Level Indonesian
IND 305.subject: IND
IND 305.description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring the language of the contemporary Indonesian media with an emphasis on reading, writing, and listening comprehension. Not open to students who have taken IND 301 .

IND 306.title: Third Level Indonesian
IND 306.subject: IND
IND 306.description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring colloquial and formal Indonesian with a strong emphasis on listening and writing comprehension. Not open to students who have taken IND 302 .
IND 306.prereq_raw: IND 301 or IND 305 (or equivalent), or consent.

IND 307.title: Third Level Indonesian Conversation
IND 307.subject: IND
IND 307.description: Topic-based course aimed to enhance student’s listening and speaking skills in the Indonesian language. Not open to students who have taken IND 301 .

IND 308.title: Third Level Indonesian Conversation
IND 308.subject: IND
IND 308.description: Topic-based course aimed at enhancing students’ listening and speaking skills in the Indonesian language. Not open to students who have taken IND 302 .

IND 401.title: Fourth-Level Indonesian
IND 401.subject: IND
IND 401.description: Continuation of IND 302 . Conducted in Indonesian. Meets three hours a week. Readings in various materials; speaking in various settings.

IND 405.title: Fourth Level Indonesian
IND 405.subject: IND
IND 405.description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring the language of the contemporary Indonesian media with an emphasis on reading, writing, and listening comprehension.

IND 407.title: Fourth Level Indonesian Conversation
IND 407.subject: IND
IND 407.description: Topic-based course aimed to enhance students’ listening and speaking skills in the Indonesian language.

IND 452.title: Structure of Indonesian
IND 452.subject: IND
IND 452.description: Introduction to grammar; some sociolinguistic background.

IND 454.title: History of Indonesian
IND 454.subject: IND
IND 454.description: Social and linguistic development of Indonesian from roots in earlier Malay to contemporary form and function.

IND 461.title: Modern Indonesian Literature
IND 461.subject: IND
IND 461.description: Selected readings, 1900 to present. Discussion and composition.

INS 300.title: Principles of Insurance
INS 300.subject: INS
INS 300.description: Risk management and insurance application to business and personal financial decision-making. Introduction to basic risk management concepts and techniques. Analyze various types of insurance: including life, property, casualty, liability, health, disability, and long-term care.

INS 411.title: Property and Casualty Insurance
INS 411.subject: INS
INS 411.description: Treatment of risk of financial loss of personal and business property and resulting loss of income occasioned by fire and allied perils. Forms of insurance used by individual business executives and firms including crime, transportation, liability, and worker compensation.

INS 431.title: Life Insurance
INS 431.subject: INS
INS 431.description: Treatment of the risk of premature death through use of various life insurance policies. Policy forms, calculation of premiums, reserves, non-forfeiture values, underwriting, regulation of policy provisions, related coverage.

IP 300.title: History of Early India
IP 300.subject: IP
IP 300.description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century.

IP 303.title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
IP 303.subject: IP
IP 303.description: Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization.

IP 360I.title: Southeast Asian Food, Music, and Rituals: Indonesia & Malaysia
IP 360I.subject: IP
IP 360I.description: Study and analysis of the art and culture of Southeast Asian food, music, and rituals—history, forms, social development, influences, and impact, with an emphasis on oral and written communication. (I) Indonesia & Malaysia; (P) Philippine; (V) Vietnamese.
IP 360I.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent for P.

IP 361.title: Topics in Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
IP 361.subject: IP

IP 362.title: Philippine Drama: History, Art, Culture
IP 362.subject: IP
IP 362.description: Survey of Philippine drama from the perspective of sociocultural and historical experiences of the people in the country and in the diaspora. Emphasis is on ethical inquiry and the teaching of writing and oral communication.

IP 363.title: Philippine Contemporary Literature in English
IP 363.subject: IP
IP 363.description: Critical survey of 20th-century Philippine literature written in English; cultural values and ethical issues. Emphasis on development of written and oral communication skills throughout the semester.
IP 363.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

IP 364P.title: Indo-Pacific Popular Culture: Philippines
IP 364P.subject: IP
IP 364P.description: Explores the Indo-Pacific popular culture; teaches how to produce, act, and perform in a select media form; & engages students in writing a critical analysis of these pop cultural expressions. (P) Philippines; (V) Vietnam.

IP 366.title: Literatures of Ancient India
IP 366.subject: IP

IP 368P.title: Introduction to South/Southeast Asian Film, History, Theory and Appreciation: Philippines
IP 368P.subject: IP
IP 368P.description: Study and analysis of South/Southeast Asian films-history, forms, development, theoretical framework and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical and aesthetic context. (P) Philippines.
IP 368P.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

IP 370P.subject: IP
IP 370P.description: A virtual guided tour of Southeast Asia that explores its multiculture diversity through its people, places, and practices. (P) Philippines; (V) Vietnam–emphasis on writing instruction and developing oral communication skills.
IP 370P.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

IP 370V.title: Southeast Asian Travelogue: People, Places, and Practices: Vietnam
IP 370V.subject: IP
IP 370V.description: A virtual guided tour of Southeast Asia that explores its multiculture diversity through its people, places, and practices. (P) Philippines; (V) Vietnam–emphasis on writing instruction and developing oral communication skills.
IP 370V.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

IP 373.title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
IP 373.subject: IP
IP 373.description: Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. Written communication emphasis.
IP 373.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

IP 374.title: Classical Hindu Mythology
IP 374.subject: IP
IP 374.description: Study of myths and narratives of classical Hinduism through the Sanskrit epics Rāmāyana and Mahābhārata; exploring major concepts such as dharma, karma, and yoga. Intensive, interpretive writing, and peer-review exercises, will hone students’ writing skills.
IP 374.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

IP 375.title: Philippine Games, Sports and Martial Arts
IP 375.subject: IP
IP 375.description: Introduces an experiential approach in the study of Philippine traditional games, sports, and martial arts. It also focuses on the historical and socio-cultural aspects of games, sports, and martial arts. Sophomore standing or higher.

IP 376.title: Philippine Diasporic Literatures
IP 376.subject: IP
IP 376.description: Appreciation, reexamination, and analysis of Philippine literature of exile; a reevaluation of Philippine writing from the diaspora. Sophomore standing or higher or consent.

IP 377.title: Critical Discourses in IPLL Studies: Philippines
IP 377.subject: IP
IP 377.description: Revaluation and analysis of critical discourses in Philippine languages and literatures and an examination of alternative perspectives to the prevailing studies on Philippine culture; an appreciation of emerging knowledge on the Philippines.
IP 377.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

IP 382.title: Philippine Visual Art from Burial Jars to Burning Effigies
IP 382.subject: IP
IP 382.description: Introduction to the arts and material culture of the Philippines from the pre-colonial to the contemporary period through the examination of sculpture, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, and painting from various ethnolinguistic groups. Sophomore standing or higher.

IP 389.title: Theories in Ilokano Studies
IP 389.subject: IP
IP 389.description: Examines the various theories employed in the study of Ilokano society, language, and culture from a variety of historical periods.

IP 391.title: Literary Cultural Relations (Philippines and Southeast Asia)
IP 391.subject: IP
IP 391.description: An appreciation, a re-examination, and an analysis of the literary and cultural relations among the various nation states of Southeast Asia. Various texts are examined to establish the connections of these nation states. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

IP 394.title: Philippine Sociolinguistics: Language Use, Ideologies, and Identities
IP 394.subject: IP
IP 394.description: Examines the intersection between language and society, specifically Philippine languages in various communities. Explores how language policies, discourses, and ideologies shape people’s use of language. Emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills.
IP 394.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

IP 395.title: Polynesian Folklore in Translation
IP 395.subject: IP

IP 396.title: Philippine Literature and Folklore in Translation
IP 396.subject: IP

JPN 305.title: Accelerated Third-Year Japanese

JPN 358.title: Third-Level Japanese Abroad

JPN 370.title: Language in Japanese Society

JPN 399.title: Directed Third-Level Reading
JPN 399.subject: JPN
JPN 399.description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses.

JPN 421.title: Japanese Composition

JPN 423.title: Advanced Listening and Speaking

JPN 730P.description: (C) Japanese/English contrastive analysis; (G) structure; (H) historical change; (K) history of Japanese language studies (Kokugo-gaku-shi); (M) morphophonemics; (P) pedagogy; (S) sociolinguistics.
JPN 730P.prereq_raw: JPN 451 , or JPN 601 and JPN 602 for (C); JPN 634 for (G); JPN 631 for (H) and (K); JPN 601 for (M); JPN 632 for (P); and JPN 633 for (S).

JPN 730S.title: Research Seminar in Japanese Linguistics: sociolinguistics
JPN 730S.subject: JPN
JPN 730S.description: (C) Japanese/English contrastive analysis; (G) structure; (H) historical change; (K) history of Japanese language studies (Kokugo-gaku-shi); (M) morphophonemics; (P) pedagogy; (S) sociolinguistics.
JPN 730S.prereq_raw: JPN 451 , or JPN 601 and JPN 602 for (C); JPN 634 for (G); JPN 631 for (H) and (K); JPN 601 for (M); JPN 632 for (P); and JPN 633 for (S).

KOR 101.title: Elementary Korean I
KOR 101.subject: KOR
KOR 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.

KOR 105.title: Accelerated Elementary Korean
KOR 105.subject: KOR
KOR 105.description: Content of KOR 101 and KOR 102 covered in one intensive course. Four 2-hour sessions per week, Monday-Thursday, plus daily lab work.

KOR 111.title: Elementary Conversational Korean I
KOR 111.subject: KOR
KOR 111.description: Development of basic skills (listening, speaking and grammar) of spoken Korean, with application to some familiar everyday topics.

KOR 201.title: Intermediate Korean I
KOR 201.subject: KOR
KOR 201.description: Continuation of KOR 101 and KOR 102 . Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.
KOR 201.prereq_raw: KOR 102 or placement test; or consent.

KOR 202.title: Intermediate Korean II
KOR 202.subject: KOR
KOR 202.prereq_raw: KOR 201 or placement test; or consent.

KOR 205.title: Accelerated Intermediate Korean
KOR 205.subject: KOR
KOR 205.description: Content of KOR 201 and KOR 202 covered in one intensive course. Four 2-hour sessions per week, Monday- Thursday, plus daily lab work.
KOR 205.prereq_raw: KOR 102 , KOR 105 , KOR 112 , placement test; or consent.

KOR 211.title: Intermediate Conversational Korean I
KOR 211.subject: KOR
KOR 211.description: Further development of listening and speaking skills. The student is expected to be able to comprehend and produce speech at the paragraph level.

KOR 301.title: Third-Level Korean I
KOR 301.subject: KOR
KOR 301.description: Continuation of KOR 201 and KOR 202 . Major emphasis on comprehension of modern written Korean. Chinese characters.

KOR 305.title: Accelerated Third-Level Korean
KOR 305.subject: KOR
KOR 305.description: Content of KOR 301 and KOR 302 covered in one intensive summer course. Five 3-hour sessions per week, Monday- Friday.
KOR 305.prereq_raw: KOR 202 , KOR 205 , placement test, or consent.

KOR 307.title: Readings in Chinese Characters I
KOR 307.subject: KOR
KOR 307.description: Training intermediate and advanced learners of Korean to master the reading, writing and usage of some 250 basic Chinese characters as they are used in a wide variety of Korean reading texts.

KOR 308.title: Readings in Chinese Characters II
KOR 308.subject: KOR
KOR 308.description: Continuation of KOR 307 , covering an additional 250 basic Chinese characters.

KOR 313.title: Reading and Translating Korean Poetry
KOR 313.subject: KOR
KOR 313.description: Introduction to modern Korean poetry and translation for students with third-year level Korean abilities. Students will learn how to interpret poems and translate them from Korean to English.

KOR 380.title: Korean Proficiency Through TV Drama
KOR 380.subject: KOR
KOR 380.description: Increasing Korean proficiency to advanced level through TV drama, which provides culturally and situationally rich contexts. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

KOR 399.title: Directed Third-Level Reading
KOR 399.subject: KOR
KOR 399.description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Offered if staff available.

KOR 403.title: High-Advanced Korean: Korean Society
KOR 403.subject: KOR
KOR 403.description: Emphasis on the highest level of listening, speaking, reading, and writing, with application to Korean society, using authentic materials.

KOR 404.title: High-Advanced Korean: Korean Culture
KOR 404.subject: KOR
KOR 404.description: Continuation of KOR 402 . Emphasis on the highest level of listening, speaking, reading and writing, with application to Korean culture using authentic materials and focusing on training in oral presentation skills.

KOR 411.title: Advanced Oral Communication in Korean
KOR 411.subject: KOR
KOR 411.description: Fourth-year advanced Korean course to increase learners’ oral fluency and accuracy; with an emphasis on formal speaking. Covers linguistic proficiency as well as social and cultural proficiencies.

KOR 420.title: Korean Composition
KOR 420.subject: KOR
KOR 420.description: Training in modern structural and stylistic techniques; writing on designated themes.

KOR 421.title: Media Analysis in Korean: Contemporary Korean Culture
KOR 421.subject: KOR
KOR 421.description: Focus on analyzing, comparing, and evaluating current media materials in South Korea to develop professional language skills and to deepen knowledge and understanding of contemporary Korean society.

KOR 422.title: Media Analysis in Korean: Culture in South and North Korea
KOR 422.subject: KOR
KOR 422.description: Focus on comparing and analyzing cultural or historical issues in South and North Korea using media materials to develop professional language skills and to deepen knowledge and understanding of the two Koreas.

KOR 425.title: Selected Readings in Korean
KOR 425.subject: KOR
KOR 425.description: Selected readings in various disciplines. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

KOR 451.title: Structure of Korean: Phonology/Morphology
KOR 451.subject: KOR
KOR 451.description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, and history.

KOR 470.title: Language and Culture of Korea
KOR 470.subject: KOR
KOR 470.description: Relation of Korean language to literature, history, philosophy, social structure, values, and interpersonal relationships; social and regional varieties. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

KOR 480.title: Korean Proficiency Through Film
KOR 480.subject: KOR
KOR 480.description: Study of Korean culture through films to elevate students’ Korean proficiency level and improve their knowledge of Korea. Emphasis on writing instruction. Requires a minimum of 16 pages of graded writing.

KOR 485.title: Korean for Academic Purposes: Humanities
KOR 485.subject: KOR
KOR 485.description: Focus on expanding students’ Korean literacy and cultural knowledge in various Humanities disciplines, including history, religion, language, education, and literature. Taught entirely in Korean.

KOR 486.title: Korean for Academic Purposes: Social Sciences & Others
KOR 486.subject: KOR
KOR 486.description: Focus on expanding students’ Korean literacy and cultural knowledge in social Science and other disciplines, including politics, economy, society, and writing in Korean.

KOR 493.title: Introduction to Traditional Korean Literature
KOR 493.subject: KOR
KOR 493.description: Critical readings from earliest times and presentations that emphasize genre, style, and context.

KOR 494.title: Introduction to Modern Korean Literature
KOR 494.subject: KOR
KOR 494.description: Critical Korean-language readings of 20th-century literature that emphasize context and the development of style. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.

KOR 495.title: Internship Program
KOR 495.subject: KOR
KOR 495.description: Supervised internship with Korean professional hosts on Oʻahu or in Korea. Students will also attend an on-campus preparatory and follow-up language class.
KOR 495.prereq_raw: KOR 486 , diagnostic assessment procedures; or consent.

KOR 496.title: Korean Abroad
KOR 496.subject: KOR
KOR 496.description: Supervised internship with Korean professional hosts in Korea. Students also undergo a one-week training module designed to prepare them to maximize the benefits of the overseas internship.
KOR 496.prereq_raw: KOR 495 , diagnostic assessment procedures; or consent.

KOR 499.title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
KOR 499.subject: KOR
KOR 499.description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Primarily for graduate students from other departments.

KOR 613M.title: Korean Verse: modern
KOR 613M.subject: KOR
KOR 613M.description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean lyric and didactic verse (e.g., hyangga , changga , hanshi , sijo , kasa , free form): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
KOR 613M.prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

KOR 613T.title: Korean Verse: traditional
KOR 613T.subject: KOR
KOR 613T.description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean lyric and didactic verse (e.g., hyangga , changga , hanshi , sijo , kasa , free form): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
KOR 613T.prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

KOR 614M.title: Korean Narrative: modern
KOR 614M.subject: KOR
KOR 614M.description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean narrative (e.g., myth, p’ansori , shaman song, essay, biography, fiction): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
KOR 614M.prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

KOR 614T.title: Korean Narrative: traditional
KOR 614T.subject: KOR
KOR 614T.description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean narrative (e.g., myth, p’ansori , shaman song, essay, biography, fiction): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
KOR 614T.prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

KOR 615M.title: Korean Drama: modern
KOR 615M.subject: KOR
KOR 615M.description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected materials in Korean performing arts (e.g., spectacle, farce play, mask dance, staged narratives, theatrical drama): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
KOR 615M.prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

KOR 615T.title: Korean Drama: traditional
KOR 615T.subject: KOR
KOR 615T.description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected materials in Korean performing arts (e.g., spectacle, farce play, mask dance, staged narratives, theatrical drama): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
KOR 615T.prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

KOR 621.title: Media Research in Korean
KOR 621.subject: KOR
KOR 621.description: Focuses on searching, analyzing, and evaluating media data for research in areas of student specializations. Students are required to write short analysis papers and a final research paper.
KOR 621.prereq_raw: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

children.text: diagnostic assessment ( equivalent to ILR Level 2)

KOR 622.title: Comparative Studies of Contemporary South and North Korean Language
KOR 622.subject: KOR
KOR 622.description: Comparing and analyzing language data to investigate language heterogeneity problems, its causes, and importance of comparative studies in NK/SK language differences; differences in language policy, grammar, and vocabulary, pronunciation, and discourse style.
KOR 622.prereq_raw: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

children.text: diagnostic assessment ( equivalent to ILR Level 2)

KOR 623.title: Interdisciplinary Research in Korean
KOR 623.subject: KOR
KOR 623.description: Combined lecture-discussion on preparing students to be able to conduct interdisciplinary research in Korean. Require advanced-level Korean proficiency.
KOR 623.prereq_raw: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

children.text: diagnostic assessment ( equivalent to ILR Level 2)

KOR 624B.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: economics
KOR 624B.subject: KOR
KOR 624B.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624C.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: political science
KOR 624C.subject: KOR
KOR 624C.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624D.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: computer science
KOR 624D.subject: KOR
KOR 624D.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624E.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: travel industry management
KOR 624E.subject: KOR
KOR 624E.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624G.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: business
KOR 624G.subject: KOR
KOR 624G.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624H.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: law
KOR 624H.subject: KOR
KOR 624H.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624I.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: medicine
KOR 624I.subject: KOR
KOR 624I.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624J.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: nursing and public health
KOR 624J.subject: KOR
KOR 624J.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 624K.title: Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse: others
KOR 624K.subject: KOR
KOR 624K.description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

KOR 631.title: History and Dialects of Korean Language
KOR 631.subject: KOR
KOR 631.description: Survey of various hypotheses on the genetic relationship of Korean; evolution of Korean from the 15th century to the present; Korean dialects.

KOR 632.title: Korean Phonology and Morphology
KOR 632.subject: KOR
KOR 632.description: Review of Korean vocalic and consonantal phonology. Phonological and morphological analysis of Korean derivation and inflection.

KOR 633.title: Korean Syntax and Semantics
KOR 633.subject: KOR
KOR 633.description: Review of theoretical problems in Korean syntax and semantics; different approaches; and contributions of Korean linguistic study to syntactic and semantic theory.

KOR 634.title: Topics in Korean Sociolinguistics
KOR 634.subject: KOR
KOR 634.description: Korean language in social context, honorifics and politeness, regional and social variation, gendered language, multilingualism, social media discourse, diaspora and globalized Korean, AI and language technology, offered with different focus.

KOR 635.title: Pedagogy of Teaching Korean as a Foreign Language
KOR 635.subject: KOR
KOR 635.description: Identification and analysis of major problems in Korean language learning, teaching, testing, and materials development by examining theoretical issues and conducting classroom research; practical techniques of teaching and testing skills in listening, reading, speaking, writing and culture.

KOR 636.title: Topics in Korean Conversation Analysis
KOR 636.subject: KOR
KOR 636.description: Theoretical framework and methodology of Korean conversation analysis; training for data collection, transcription, and data analysis; offered with different focuses, covering grammar and interaction, second language teaching, as well as language and body.

KOR 640.title: Literary Translation of Korean
KOR 640.subject: KOR
KOR 640.description: The art and craft of translating traditional and modern Korean literary works into English.

KOR 645.title: Korean Language Acquisition
KOR 645.subject: KOR
KOR 645.description: Examining human language acquisition by comparing first (L1) and second language (L2) learning, focusing on unique cognitive and linguistic challenges of acquiring Korean through scientific and statistical analysis of language behavior patterns.

KOR 652.title: Major Authors in Modern Korean Literature
KOR 652.subject: KOR
KOR 652.description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature.

KOR 655.title: Practicum: Teaching Korean as a Foreign Language
KOR 655.subject: KOR
KOR 655.description: Designed for graduate students pursuing Korean language teaching, while developing practical teaching skills through class observation, action research and discussion under supervision.

KOR 664.title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
KOR 664.subject: KOR
KOR 664.description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical socio-cultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history.

KOR 720.title: Research Seminar in Korean Literature
KOR 720.subject: KOR
KOR 720.description: Advanced study of an author, school, period, genre, or problem leading to a research paper.

KOR 730.title: Research Seminar in Korean Language
KOR 730.subject: KOR
KOR 730.description: Advanced study in history and dialects, phonology and morphology, syntax and semantics, sociolinguistics, or pedagogy, leading to a research paper.

KRS 101.title: Physical Fitness
KRS 101.subject: KRS
KRS 101.description: Conditioning exercises and activities to develop and maintain physical efficiency. Motor fitness tests administered to measure status and progress.

KRS 102.title: Aerobic Fitness
KRS 102.subject: KRS
KRS 102.description: Aerobic fitness improvement upon completion of course by regularly attending and practicing safe workout routines. Learn fitness components, names of muscles and exercises associated with each one.

KRS 103.title: Swimming: Beginning
KRS 103.subject: KRS
KRS 103.description: Adjusting to and immersing in water, floating, sculling; correct arm stroke, leg kick, breathing techniques and their coordination. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 104.title: Swimming: Intermediate
KRS 104.subject: KRS
KRS 104.description: Perfecting and integrating basic strokes with added emphasis for speed and distance. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 105.title: Swimming: Advanced
KRS 105.subject: KRS
KRS 105.description: Correct techniques used in competitive swimming, racing starts, correct turning techniques, long-distance swimming. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 106.title: SCUBA Diving: Beginning
KRS 106.subject: KRS
KRS 106.description: Learning watermanship, equipment handling skills, and the knowledge to become safe divers. Additional costs for equipment, diver manual, dive tables, and certification fee.

KRS 107.title: Aqua-Aerobic Fitness
KRS 107.subject: KRS
KRS 107.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on aerobic fitness improvement through total body aquatic workouts with music, and development of individualized aquatics fitness program.
KRS 107.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.

KRS 110.title: Golf: Beginning
KRS 110.subject: KRS
KRS 110.description: Rules, etiquette, grip, stance, drive, normal iron shots, approach shots, putting.

KRS 111.title: Golf: Intermediate
KRS 111.subject: KRS
KRS 111.description: Corrective work on basic swing mechanics and rhythm; adjustments for bunker play, uphill lies, downhill lies, short game around and on the green; handicapping and match play competition.

KRS 112.title: Golf: Advanced
KRS 112.subject: KRS
KRS 112.description: Improving drive, fairway wood shots, long iron shots, control shots, trouble shots, putting, course management, competitive strategy, problems in rules. Greens fees paid by students for play on courses.

KRS 113.title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
KRS 113.subject: KRS
KRS 113.description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of those interested in pursuing health-related careers. Structure and function of major systems examined (gross anatomy, micro-anatomy, physiology, and pathology).

KRS 115.title: Bowling
KRS 115.subject: KRS
KRS 115.description: Rules, etiquette, arm swing, approach, execution, scoring, spare pickups. Students pay charge for use of alley.

KRS 120.title: Badminton
KRS 120.subject: KRS
KRS 120.description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, smash, drive, net play, offensive and defensive strategy; singles and doubles play.

KRS 123.title: Folk and National Dances
KRS 123.subject: KRS
KRS 123.description: Popular dances of various national groups, including square dances.

KRS 124.title: Dances of Hawaiʻi
KRS 124.subject: KRS
KRS 124.description: Background and fundamentals of hula. Selected dances with and without instruments.

KRS 125.title: Dances of Hawaiʻi: Advanced
KRS 125.subject: KRS
KRS 125.description: Advanced techniques in hula movements. Selected dances taught will be more complex, including work with instruments. Individual choreography will be emphasized.

KRS 126.title: Social Dance: Ballroom
KRS 126.subject: KRS
KRS 126.description: Social dances including fox trot, waltz, swing, and other popular dances. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.

KRS 127.title: Social Dance: Latin
KRS 127.subject: KRS
KRS 127.description: Social dances of a Latin flavor including rhumba, cha-cha, tango, samba, and others. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.

KRS 130.title: Tennis: Beginning
KRS 130.subject: KRS
KRS 130.description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, volleying; singles and doubles play.

KRS 131.title: Tennis: Intermediate
KRS 131.subject: KRS
KRS 131.description: Corrective work in three basic strokes and in net play; the lob, drop shot, overhead smash, and half-volley; applying spin in basic strokes; basic strategy in singles and doubles play.

KRS 132.title: Tennis: Advanced
KRS 132.subject: KRS
KRS 132.description: Improving upon the strokes introduced in KRS 130 and KRS 131 ; advanced competitive strategy; problems in rules; officiating; elements of tournament play.

KRS 135.title: Volleyball: Beginning
KRS 135.subject: KRS
KRS 135.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on beginner skills and knowledge relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy.
KRS 135.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.

KRS 136.title: Volleyball: Intermediate
KRS 136.subject: KRS
KRS 136.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on improving skills and knowledge through practice and cognitive activities relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy.
KRS 136.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.

KRS 137.title: Basketball
KRS 137.subject: KRS
KRS 137.description: Rules, passing, shooting, dribbling, rebounding, individual defensive and offensive maneuvers; team offense and defense.

KRS 151.title: Adapted and Prescribed Exercises
KRS 151.subject: KRS
KRS 151.description: Small group and individual guidance and instruction for students recommended by student health service.

KRS 152.title: Weight Training
KRS 152.subject: KRS
KRS 152.description: Kinesiology of lifting and weight training, various types of exercises and methods of training with resistance.

KRS 153.title: Olympic and Power Lifting
KRS 153.subject: KRS
KRS 153.description: Exercise technique and prescription with an emphasis on anaerobic exercise. Explores advanced periodization models and their utilization, mastery of Olympic lifts, and plyometric programs.

KRS 154.title: Tumbling and Rebound Tumbling
KRS 154.subject: KRS
KRS 154.description: Single and combination stunts on tumbling mats and trampoline, balancing stunts; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.

KRS 156.title: Heavy Apparatus
KRS 156.subject: KRS
KRS 156.description: Single and combination stunts on side horse, horizontal bar, parallel bars, still rings; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.

KRS 160.title: Judo
KRS 160.subject: KRS
KRS 160.description: Rules, etiquette, method of falling and breaking the fall, simple throws and their counters, simple holds and breaking of such holds, randori. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 161.title: Aikido
KRS 161.subject: KRS
KRS 161.description: Rules, etiquette, basic rolls, simple holds and the breaking of such holds, specific physical conditioning exercises. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 163.title: T’ai Chi Ch’uan
KRS 163.subject: KRS
KRS 163.description: Classic forms of t’ai chi ch’uan.

KRS 164.title: Karate: Beginning
KRS 164.subject: KRS
KRS 164.description: Rules, etiquette, basic stances, blocks, thrusts, kicks, ippon kumite, and selected kata. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 165.title: Karate: Intermediate
KRS 165.subject: KRS
KRS 165.description: Emphasis on improving the basic techniques (stances, punches, kicks, forms, and sparring); introduction to combination techniques. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 167.title: Wrestling: Beginning
KRS 167.subject: KRS
KRS 167.description: Rules: fundamental defensive and offensive maneuvers and competitive strategy, i.e., takedowns, reversals, escapes, and pinning combinations; conditioning exercises.

KRS 170.title: Yoga: Beginning
KRS 170.subject: KRS
KRS 170.description: Experiencing yoga and its effects on body, mind and consciousness of individual. Encompasses exercise, breathing techniques, deep relaxation, meditation, practice in concentration, and yogic postures.

KRS 171.title: Yoga: Intermediate
KRS 171.subject: KRS
KRS 171.description: Corrective work and improvement of basic techniques. Exercise sets and combinations designed to develop endurance, flexibility, muscle and nerve strength, meditation, and deep relaxation technique.

KRS 173.title: Water Polo
KRS 173.subject: KRS
KRS 173.description: Fundamentals of basic water polo skills, namely, ball handling, passing, shooting, dribbling plus a brief introduction into beginning techniques of individual offense and defense.
KRS 173.prereq_raw: KRS 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 181.title: Sport Proficiency I: Invasion
KRS 181.subject: KRS
KRS 181.description: Knowledge, skill development, and strategy of various invasion type games and sports. Sports like basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee and/or others are introduced within a tactical framework.

KRS 182.title: Sport Proficiency II: Net, Field, and Target
KRS 182.subject: KRS
KRS 182.description: Knowledge, skill development, position, and strategy of net, field and target sports. Sports like volleyball, tennis, softball, and golf are introduced within a tactical framework.

KRS 185.title: Floor Exercise Gymnastics
KRS 185.subject: KRS
KRS 185.description: An entry-level course designed to develop students’ knowledge of men’s and women’s gymnastics floor exercise routines, including injury prevention, skill progression, spotting techniques, and routine choreography. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.

KRS 186.title: Track and Field for Physical Education
KRS 186.subject: KRS
KRS 186.description: Knowledge, skills, and rules of various track and field events. Organization of track meets and strategy in competition. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.

KRS 187.title: Softball
KRS 187.subject: KRS
KRS 187.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on basic skills, rules, etiquette, offensive and defensive strategies, position play, and game situations.
KRS 187.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.

KRS 201.title: School Health Problems: Elementary
KRS 201.subject: KRS
KRS 201.description: Responsibilities of elementary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing teacher’s role in health instruction, health services, school health policies.

KRS 202.title: School Health Problems: Secondary
KRS 202.subject: KRS
KRS 202.description: Responsibilities of secondary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing health instruction, health services, healthful school living, school health policies.

KRS 203.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
KRS 203.subject: KRS
KRS 203.description: Kinesiology as a professional field. Overview of history, philosophy, and current trends in kinesiology. Survey of psychological and sociological foundations of kinesiology, exercise, fitness and sport.
KRS 203.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors or approval.

KRS 208.title: Recreation Services in Contemporary Society
KRS 208.subject: KRS
KRS 208.description: Theories and philosophies in recreation: history; contemporary issues; roles in modern society; relationship to health, physical education, and exercise science.

KRS 210.title: Human Development
KRS 210.subject: KRS
KRS 210.description: Developmental processes across the life span. Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Human growth and development from conception to death with major theories and related research on maintaining healthy lifestyles.

KRS 232.title: Safety and Risk Management
KRS 232.subject: KRS
KRS 232.description: Understanding the fundamental principles and techniques of safety and accident-prevention programming emphasizing school, home, public places, on the job, and motor vehicle situations.

KRS 238.title: Outdoor Recreation Management
KRS 238.subject: KRS
KRS 238.description: Objectives and values of outdoor recreation; characteristics and determinants of programs; planning, organization, leadership, and facilities for recreational uses of natural environments.

KRS 241.title: Health Education Curriculum
KRS 241.subject: KRS
KRS 241.description: Objectives of school health program, emphasizing scope and sequence of health instruction; critical examination of health curriculum guides from various states.

KRS 249.title: Programming and Leadership
KRS 249.subject: KRS
KRS 249.description: Factors in planning and leading recreation programs; characteristics and responsibilities of leadership in relation to nature, scope, and resources of a variety of programs.

KRS 270.title: Introduction to Health and Physical Education
KRS 270.subject: KRS
KRS 270.description: Introduction to foundational knowledge for effective teaching, history, philosophy, and current practices in health and physical education. Provides the basis for later coursework in K-12 health and physical education. Required field experience.

KRS 271.title: Performance Based Assessment in Health and Physical Education
KRS 271.subject: KRS
KRS 271.description: Assessment and evaluative techniques applied to health and physical education, including test construction, performance-based assessment, measurement criteria and instruments, interpretation of data and content, as well as program evaluation.

KRS 302.title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
KRS 302.subject: KRS
KRS 302.description: Understanding standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment in health with a focus on advocacy, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and prevention of disease within sub-topics of health (mental, social, emotional, environmental, financial, etc.).

KRS 305.title: Principles of Sports Medicine
KRS 305.subject: KRS
KRS 305.description: Examines with some depth, principles of risk management and pathology of athletic injuries, major musculoskeletal structures, and concepts of evaluative skills, treatment, and rehabilitation for common athletic injuries.

KRS 310.title: Coaching of Football
KRS 310.subject: KRS
KRS 310.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive football coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 311.title: Coaching of Basketball
KRS 311.subject: KRS
KRS 311.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive basketball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 312.title: Coaching of Baseball
KRS 312.subject: KRS
KRS 312.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive baseball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 313.title: Coaching of Volleyball
KRS 313.subject: KRS
KRS 313.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive volleyball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 323.title: Music and Rhythm in Physical Education
KRS 323.subject: KRS
KRS 323.description: Use of music in physical education programming (K-12), emphasizing selection of appropriate music for specific activities as expressive or creative movement, movement exploration, rhythmic gymnastics, and dancing. A variety of strategies for teaching dance will be shared.

KRS 329.title: Managing Recreation Services
KRS 329.subject: KRS
KRS 329.description: Administrative framework and procedures pertinent to the operation of agencies providing recreational services to the various publics.

KRS 331.title: Water Safety Training
KRS 331.subject: KRS
KRS 331.description: Theory and methods of advanced lifesaving and water safety leading to American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor (WSI) certification.
KRS 331.prereq_raw: KRS 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

KRS 332.title: Emergency Care and First Aid Training
KRS 332.subject: KRS
KRS 332.description: Practicum in training of persons to become qualified in emergency care knowledge, basic life support, and first aid skills. First Aid and CPR certificates may be earned.

KRS 333.title: Movement Education I
KRS 333.subject: KRS
KRS 333.description: A movement-based approach to teaching basic motor skills in preschool/elementary physical education. Students actively participate and learn about developmentally appropriate content and pedagogy for children in grades P-5/6. Peer bit teaching is included.

KRS 334.title: Movement Education II
KRS 334.subject: KRS
KRS 334.description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Content and pedadogy for teaching Pre/K-5 physical education. Students will learn to plan and teach physical education for children. Peer bit and field teaching included.

KRS 335.title: Coaching of Track and Field
KRS 335.subject: KRS
KRS 335.description: Techniques and rules of sprints, distance runs, relays, hurdles, long jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus, and javelin throws; conduct of track and field meets; specific conditioning and training problems.

KRS 336.title: Coaching of Swimming
KRS 336.subject: KRS
KRS 336.description: Theory and methods of coaching competitive swimming. Technical, organizational, and administrative aspects. Emphasis on stroke mechanics and training methods.

KRS 337.title: Fieldwork in Recreation I
KRS 337.subject: KRS
KRS 337.description: Initial supervised leadership experience in recreational agencies. One hour per week in class discussion sessions.
KRS 337.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: For recreation majors only.

KRS 339.title: Special Recreation
KRS 339.subject: KRS
KRS 339.description: Special recreation as a professional field. Overview of special recreation services. Emphasis on recreation services for special populations.

KRS 353.title: Structural Kinesiology
KRS 353.subject: KRS
KRS 353.description: Gross human anatomy, emphasizing identification and description of parts of the musculoskeletal system; selected applications to motor activity. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent.
KRS 353.prereq_raw: KRS 113 or BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 / PHYL 141L or PHYL 301 / PHYL 301L .

KRS 354.title: Exercise and Sport Physiology
KRS 354.subject: KRS
KRS 354.description: Emphasis on physiological responses to exercises and physical training as related to strength, muscular endurance, cardio-respiratory endurance. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent.
KRS 354.prereq_raw: KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L .
KRS 354.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

KRS 354L.title: Exercise and Sport Physiology Lab
KRS 354L.subject: KRS
KRS 354L.description: Laboratory section to accompany KRS 354 . Emphasis will be hands-on data collection and analysis of the physiological responses to exercise and physical training. Lab report development and scientific writing will also be emphasized.
KRS 354L.prereq_raw: KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L .
KRS 354L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

KRS 371.title: Teaching Techniques I: Elementary
KRS 371.subject: KRS
KRS 371.description: Teaching techniques and methods of elementary physical education. Content to include basic skills and games in a school-based experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

KRS 372.title: Teaching Techniques II: Secondary
KRS 372.subject: KRS
KRS 372.description: Teaching techniques and methods of secondary physical education. Content to include invasion, net, field, and target activities. Emphasizes the tactical approach in a school-based experience, as well as writing through lesson planning. Primarily for Health & Physical Education majors.
KRS 372.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Primarily for Health & Physical Education majors.

KRS 384.title: Drugs and Society
KRS 384.subject: KRS
KRS 384.description: Introduction to psychoactive drugs and their effects; drug regulations; education and rehabilitation programs; psycho-social variables related to the decisions to use/abuse drugs.

KRS 385.title: Physical Fitness for Physical Education Teachers
KRS 385.subject: KRS
KRS 385.description: Diagnosis and prescription for basic health and fitness problems, scientific principles of training, guidelines for exercise; essentials of scientifically based individualized physical fitness program.

KRS 388.title: Field Work in Strength and Conditioning I
KRS 388.subject: KRS
KRS 388.description: Supervised practicum in strength training and conditioning. Students will be exposed to the theory and practice of designing and implementing both strength/ power, and general conditioning programs.

KRS 395.title: Personal Health and Wellness
KRS 395.subject: KRS
KRS 395.description: Core concepts in health allow students to take responsibility for their own health-related behaviors by developing basic competencies in identifying, analyzing, and responsibly deliberating contemporary ethical issues related to health and wellness.

KRS 399.title: Directed Reading
KRS 399.subject: KRS
KRS 399.description: Individual problems. Limited to senior majors in health education, physical education, athletic training, or recreation with a minimum GPA of 2.75 in major field.

KRS 401.title: Advanced Health Concepts
KRS 401.subject: KRS
KRS 401.description: Understanding health issues for individuals, families, schools, and communities, in regards to Hawaii K-12 schools. Focusing on the acquisition of functional health content and proficiency in health-related skills to enhance healthy behaviors in learners.
KRS 401.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 402E.title: Teaching Practicum in Physical Education: Elementary
KRS 402E.subject: KRS
KRS 402E.description: Field experience in teaching physical education activities in schools, K-12; techniques in leadership; selection of activities and program evaluation for K-12 licensure. (E) elementary; (S) secondary.
KRS 402E.prereq_raw: admittance to licensure track; pass basic skills tests specified by the Hawaiʻi Teacher Standards Board ( www.htsb.org ) or bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.

KRS 402E.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

KRS 402S.title: Teaching Practicum in Physical Education: Secondary
KRS 402S.subject: KRS
KRS 402S.description: Field experience in teaching physical education activities in schools, K-12; techniques in leadership; selection of activities and program evaluation for K-12 licensure. (E) elementary; (S) secondary.
KRS 402S.prereq_raw: admittance to licensure track; pass basic skills tests specified by the Hawaiʻi Teacher Standards Board ( www.htsb.org ) or bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
