KRS 402S.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

KRS 403.title: Guidance and Classroom Management
KRS 403.subject: KRS
KRS 403.description: Guidance principles applied to classroom management for teachers.

KRS 404.title: K-12 Teaching Methods in Physical Education
KRS 404.subject: KRS
KRS 404.description: Methods and materials in teaching physical education, including techniques, leadership skills, program evaluation, and designing course content using written communication skills.

KRS 405E.title: Teaching Residency: elementary
KRS 405E.subject: KRS
KRS 405E.description: Full-time supervised experience in elementary and secondary school level. School level corresponds to level of licensure desired. (E) elementary; (S) secondary. Each alpha can be taken one time.
KRS 405E.prereq_raw: KRS 402 E (with a minimum grade of B-), KRS 402 S (with a minimum grade of B-), and KRS 404 (with a minimum grade of B-); admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.

children.text: E ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , KRS 402 S ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and KRS 404 ( with a minimum grade of B- ) ; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests

KRS 405E.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Physical Education, and Secondary Education-Physical Education majors only.

KRS 405S.title: Teaching Residency: secondary
KRS 405S.subject: KRS
KRS 405S.description: Full-time supervised experience in elementary and secondary school level. School level corresponds to level of licensure desired. (E) elementary; (S) secondary. Each alpha can be taken one time.
KRS 405S.prereq_raw: KRS 402 E (with a minimum grade of B-), KRS 402 S (with a minimum grade of B-), and KRS 404 (with a minimum grade of B-); admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.

children.text: E ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , KRS 402 S ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and KRS 404 ( with a minimum grade of B- ) ; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests

KRS 405S.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Physical Education, and Secondary Education-Physical Education majors only.

KRS 406.title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
KRS 406.subject: KRS
KRS 406.description: Analysis and resolutions of issues in teaching residency; teaching strategies and techniques; curriculum planning; professional growth and development.
KRS 406.prereq_raw: KRS 402 E, KRS 402 S, and KRS 404 or consent; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.

children.text: E, KRS 402 S, and KRS 404 or consent ; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests

KRS 407.title: Psychosocial Aspects of Sport
KRS 407.subject: KRS
KRS 407.description: Examination and application of sociological and psychological theories and ethical reasoning to the sociocultural and psychological aspects of sport through the medium of writing.

KRS 415.title: Prevent/Care of Athletic Injuries
KRS 415.subject: KRS
KRS 415.description: An examination of the most recent practices and procedures in the prevention and care of athletic and sports injuries. Observational field experiences in athletic training will be required.

KRS 416.title: Fundamentals of Ergonomics
KRS 416.subject: KRS
KRS 416.description: Introduction to ergonomics principles and their application in understanding and prevention of Muscular Skeletal Disorders encountered in the working environment including introduction to legal aspects of ergonomics.
KRS 416.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Post-Master’s Certificate in Nursing majors only.

KRS 419.title: Administration in Athletic Training, Exercise Science, Allied Health
KRS 419.subject: KRS
KRS 419.description: An examination of organization and administration in Athletic Training, Allied Health and Exercise Science. Content includes leadership and motivation models, legal liability, ethical considerations and management strategies for all aspects of Health Care Administration.

KRS 420.title: Lower Extremity Assessment
KRS 420.subject: KRS
KRS 420.description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the lower extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals.

KRS 421.title: Upper Extremity Assessment
KRS 421.subject: KRS
KRS 421.description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the upper extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals.
KRS 421.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

KRS 423.title: Curriculum and Supervision
KRS 423.subject: KRS
KRS 423.description: Effective program development, planning, and supervision, including issues in legal liability and administration of all aspects of physical education programming in grades K-12.

KRS 428.title: Current Issues in Leisure Services
KRS 428.subject: KRS
KRS 428.description: Philosophical foundations and current and emerging issues in leisure services management and programming. Coverage of leisure research and its implications to practice.
KRS 428.prereq_raw: KRS 238 , KRS 249 , and KRS 329 ; or consent.

KRS 429.title: Evaluating and Marketing Leisure Services
KRS 429.subject: KRS
KRS 429.description: Basic methods in marketing, planning, evaluating programs and problem-solving methods, survey research, research design, data analysis, and report generation for park, recreation, and tourism systems.

KRS 432.title: Emergency Care for the Professional Rescuer
KRS 432.subject: KRS
KRS 432.description: Combined lecture-lab on advanced emergency care for injuries and illnesses and includes certifications for CPR/First Aid/AED. Class size of approximately 20 students.
KRS 432.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all majors.

KRS 434.title: Coaching Athletics
KRS 434.subject: KRS
KRS 434.description: Combined lecture-lab with emphasis on scientific principles, theory and practice, and professional qualities of the coach. Writing is integrated with the intent that students will enhance their communication skills through writing.
KRS 434.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 437.title: Camp Resources and Planning
KRS 437.subject: KRS
KRS 437.description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab for camp counselors and camp leadership. Plan and evaluate camp experiences for children and youth, including those with disabilities. Includes field trips.

KRS 438.title: Practicum in Camping
KRS 438.subject: KRS
KRS 438.description: Supervised leadership at a camp setting with children and youth, including those with disabilities. Day or residential camps. One full week camping for each credit hour. Maximum of four credit hours.

KRS 443.title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
KRS 443.subject: KRS
KRS 443.description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.
KRS 443.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 463.title: Sport Biomechanics
KRS 463.subject: KRS
KRS 463.description: Concepts and scientific principles essential to efficient human movement; proper application of biomechanical principles to fundamental movements and selected complex motor skills.
KRS 463.prereq_raw: KRS 353 , and either PHYS 100 , PHYS 151 , or PHYS 170 ; or consent.

KRS 470.title: Fitness for Life
KRS 470.subject: KRS
KRS 470.description: Students will gain knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to plan, implement, and evaluate Fitness for Life curriculum. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.
KRS 470.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 471.title: Teaching Methods in Health Education
KRS 471.subject: KRS
KRS 471.description: Experiences in developing standards-based, interactive learning opportunities to teach quality health education in schools. Focus on creating curriculum and assessments aligned with the National and State Standards for Health Education.

KRS 472.title: Learning Communities
KRS 472.subject: KRS
KRS 472.description: Theory, basic research, interactive process, and methodology of the cooperative learning process known as Tribes. Will develop participants’ abilities to foster and facilitate learning communities in a variety of settings.

KRS 473.title: Sociocultural Issues in Physical Activity
KRS 473.subject: KRS
KRS 473.description: Contemporary and historical perspective on socio-cultural issues that influence health and physical activity settings. Understanding ethics and culturally responsive practice around race, gender, sexuality, class, etc. Emphasis on ethics and teaching writing for the profession.
KRS 473.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 474.title: Statistics
KRS 474.subject: KRS
KRS 474.description: Basic elements for: descriptive statistics, probability, inference, regression, and correlation analysis.
KRS 474.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 476.title: Motor Learning and Performance
KRS 476.subject: KRS
KRS 476.description: Basic consideration is kinesthesis, motor ability, fatigue, developmental factors, practice, motivation in relation to motor learning and human performance.

KRS 477.title: Motor Development and Learning
KRS 477.subject: KRS
KRS 477.description: Motor learning and development through the lifespan with an emphasis on fundamental principles and patterns. Areas such as memory, knowledge of performance, and motivation are incorporated and demonstrated through activities and assignments.
KRS 477.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Primarily for KRS majors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 478.title: Adapted Physical Activity in Early Childhood
KRS 478.subject: KRS
KRS 478.description: Concepts of developmentally appropriate practice, importance of movement in overall development, and design of physical activity sessions and environments for young children with and without disabilities are covered.

KRS 480.title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
KRS 480.subject: KRS
KRS 480.description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.
KRS 480.prereq_raw: ( FSHN 185 , and KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or ( PHYL 141 / PHYL 141L and PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L ) or PHYL 301 ) with a minimum grade of C.

KRS 481.title: Introduction to Research in KRS
KRS 481.subject: KRS
KRS 481.description: Research methods in the study of physical activity, types of research, statistical concepts and techniques, and reporting research results.

KRS 482.title: Commercial Recreation
KRS 482.subject: KRS
KRS 482.description: Overview of leisure services and trends in commercial, private and employee recreation, and resort and recreational tourism. The social, economic, and environmental significance is examined.

KRS 483.title: Recreation Planning and Maintenance
KRS 483.subject: KRS
KRS 483.description: Examination of social, economic, and environmental factors of recreation and tourism development. Emphasis on methods, processes, citizen participation, design issues/regulations, and land use.

KRS 484.title: Drug Abuse, Violence, and Injury Prevention
KRS 484.subject: KRS
KRS 484.description: Standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment on the scientific, socio-cultural, and attitudinal aspects of drug abuse, violence, and injury prevention. Focus on incidence and prevalence, roles, prevention, and high-risk populations.
KRS 484.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

KRS 485.title: Sexual Health Education
KRS 485.subject: KRS
KRS 485.description: Program planning, curriculum development and classroom teaching strategies in the areas of human sexuality, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Focus on research-based curriculum and strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

KRS 487.title: Exercise Assessment and Conditioning Lab
KRS 487.subject: KRS
KRS 487.description: Designed to provide knowledge of laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of aerobic and anaerobic testing results, and individual exercise program/prescription.

KRS 488.title: Practicum in Health and Exercise Science
KRS 488.subject: KRS
KRS 488.description: Requires 160 hours of supervised practicum experience in health, wellness, fitness, lifestyle-management (contingent upon instructor’s approval in the registered semester). Emphasis will be on experimental learning, writing and self-directed research related to students’ internship experiences.
KRS 488.prereq_raw: current CPR and First Aid Certification, KRS 152 , KRS 332 , KRS 353 , KRS 354 , and KRS 463 ; or consent.
KRS 488.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Health and Exercise Science majors only.

KRS 489.title: Program Design in Strength Training and Conditioning
KRS 489.subject: KRS
KRS 489.description: Designed to provide theoretical and practical experience in supervision of a strength training center. Content includes program design, exercise techniques, organization, testing, evaluation, methods of strength development, facility design and special populations.
KRS 489.prereq_raw: KRS 152 , KRS 153 , KRS 353 , KRS 354L , KRS 354 , and KRS 463 ; or consent.
KRS 489.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

KRS 490.title: Introduction to Athletic Training Clinic
KRS 490.subject: KRS
KRS 490.description: Introduction to the Professional Athletic Training Education Program and the Clinical Education Plan. Students are required to document all requirements and demonstrate proficiency in basic clinical skills.

KRS 491.title: AT Practicum I
KRS 491.subject: KRS
KRS 491.description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program.

KRS 492.title: AT Practicum II
KRS 492.subject: KRS
KRS 492.description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program.

KRS 493.title: Athletic Training Practicum III
KRS 493.subject: KRS
KRS 493.description: Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program.

KRS 494.title: Athletic Training Practicum IV
KRS 494.subject: KRS
KRS 494.description: (5 2-hr Practicum) Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program.

KRS 600.title: Foundations of School Counseling
KRS 600.subject: KRS
KRS 600.description: Explores school counseling history, philosophy, and ASCA Model. Covers delivery systems, interventions, roles, and ethics. Examines contemporary challenges and resources in supporting student development. (Meets EdD common core elective.)

KRS 603.title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
KRS 603.subject: KRS
KRS 603.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen with emphasis on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
KRS 603.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

KRS 604.title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
KRS 604.subject: KRS
KRS 604.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
KRS 604.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

KRS 605.title: Human Development Across the Lifespan
KRS 605.subject: KRS
KRS 605.description: Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Major theories and related research on human development; applications in policy planning and service delivery in counseling.

KRS 606.title: Counseling: Theory and Practice
KRS 606.subject: KRS
KRS 606.description: Overview of major counseling theories, techniques, and evidence-based practices as preparation for practicum and internship. Explores integrative approaches and theoretical concepts. Application to diverse populations in school, rehabilitation, and community settings.

KRS 607.title: Scientific Principles of Physical Conditioning
KRS 607.subject: KRS
KRS 607.description: Application of physiological principles to physical conditioning and athletic performance.
KRS 607.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

KRS 608.title: Muscular Strength and Power Development
KRS 608.subject: KRS
KRS 608.description: Interpretation of scientific principles of muscular strength and power development. Examination of muscular adaptations to increased and decreased use.
KRS 608.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

KRS 609.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience I
KRS 609.subject: KRS
KRS 609.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Must be completed during first semester post admission into program.
KRS 609.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 610.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience II
KRS 610.subject: KRS
KRS 610.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum includes duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Practicum must be completed during second semester post admission to the program.
KRS 610.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 611.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience III
KRS 611.subject: KRS
KRS 611.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required.
KRS 611.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 612.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience IV
KRS 612.subject: KRS
KRS 612.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required.
KRS 612.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 613.title: Athletic Training Clinical Practicum
KRS 613.subject: KRS
KRS 613.description: (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced clinical practicum in which the BOC certified or certification-eligible graduate student experiences an enhancement of athletic training knowledge and refinement of athletic training skills.

KRS 614.title: Athletic Training Research Practicum
KRS 614.subject: KRS
KRS 614.description: (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced research practicum in which the BOC certified or certification-eligible graduate student deepens their understanding and enhances their critical thinking abilities in order to contribute to the advancement of the discipline and the athletic training profession.

KRS 615B.title: Clinical Examination of Pathology: lower body
KRS 615B.subject: KRS
KRS 615B.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
KRS 615B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 615H.title: Clinical Examination of Pathology: head, neck, and spine
KRS 615H.subject: KRS
KRS 615H.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
KRS 615H.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 615U.title: Clinical Examination of Pathology: upper body
KRS 615U.subject: KRS
KRS 615U.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
KRS 615U.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 616.title: Advanced Orthopedic Assessment
KRS 616.subject: KRS
KRS 616.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Advanced knowledge and skills of athletic training as they are specifically applied to the understanding, treatment, and rehabilitation of sport-related injuries. (e.g. epidemiology, legal, ethical concerns, sports psychology, pharm, drug abuse, health issues)

KRS 617.title: Therapeutic Interventions: Modalities
KRS 617.subject: KRS
KRS 617.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Physiology principles and operational procedures of contemporary therapeutic modalities as they relate to the care and treatment of athletic injuries.
KRS 617.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 618.title: Therapeutic Interventions: Rehabilitative Exercise
KRS 618.subject: KRS
KRS 618.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Concepts and principles of comprehensive rehabilitation programs (therapeutic goals and objectives, exercise selection, methods of evaluation and recording progress, progression and return to competition criteria, and physiological effects of tissue trauma and inactivity).
KRS 618.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 619.title: General Medical Conditions in Sports Medicine
KRS 619.subject: KRS
KRS 619.description: An examination/evaluation of general medical conditions associated with sports medicine including pathology, care and treatment.
KRS 619.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 620.title: Seminar in Athletic Training
KRS 620.subject: KRS
KRS 620.description: Designed to provide the student with analytical skills and practical experience relative to research as it applies to sports related injuries.

KRS 621.title: Advanced Therapeutic Exercise
KRS 621.subject: KRS
KRS 621.description: Advanced concepts and evidence-based principles of rehabilitation programs. Enhancement of previously learned therapeutic exercise techniques and integration of therapeutic modalities and therapeutic exercise, including objective and functional goal setting and evaluation for appropriate progression and expedited return to activity.
KRS 621.prereq_raw: KRS 617 and KRS 618 or basic therapeutic exercise and therapeutic modalities courses, or consent.

KRS 622.title: Athletic Training Capstone Experience
KRS 622.subject: KRS
KRS 622.description: Capstone culminating experience preparing the student for the computer-based BOC Exam and for a career in athletic training. Follows the students’ didactic and clinical preparation in the 12 competency areas of athletic training.

KRS 623.title: Administration in Kinesiology
KRS 623.subject: KRS
KRS 623.description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings.

KRS 625.title: Introduction to Community Counseling
KRS 625.subject: KRS
KRS 625.description: Philosophy, organization, and function of community service agencies, programs, and institutions as related to professional work in counseling.

KRS 626.title: Introduction to Practicum
KRS 626.subject: KRS
KRS 626.description: Theory and techniques of counseling as preparation for practicum and internship. Emphasis on counseling relationships and basic skill development. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

KRS 627.title: Career Development and Vocational Counseling
KRS 627.subject: KRS
KRS 627.description: Theory and practice in career development and vocational counseling with individuals and groups; utilization of educational, vocational, and social resources in career counseling.

KRS 628.title: Research and Evaluation in Counseling
KRS 628.subject: KRS
KRS 628.description: Framework for understanding basic statistics, methodology, and evaluation of research in counseling and related fields. Students will analyze research, conceptualize research, and apply research to practice.

KRS 629.title: Counseling: Group Theory and Practice
KRS 629.subject: KRS
KRS 629.description: Theories and techniques of group counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.
KRS 629.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and KRS 606 / EDEP 635 , and consent.

KRS 630.title: Assessment and Appraisals in Counseling
KRS 630.subject: KRS
KRS 630.description: Assessment methods and tools for evaluating aptitudes, achievements, and interests. Applications to educational, instructional, and career counseling.

KRS 631.title: School Counseling Approaches to Transition and Adjustment
KRS 631.subject: KRS
KRS 631.description: Principles of behavior affecting interpersonal relationships in school with emphasis on application to actual situations.

KRS 632.title: Theory and Assessment of Intelligence
KRS 632.subject: KRS
KRS 632.description: Theory and supervised experience in individual intelligence testing, psychological report writing; psychometric and social issues in intelligence testing.

KRS 633.title: Trauma and Crisis Counseling
KRS 633.subject: KRS
KRS 633.description: Crisis intervention strategies and counseling skills for schools. Trauma-informed approaches for crises like suicide and violence. Focus on age-appropriate interventions, resilience, and school collaboration.

KRS 634.title: Inclusive Physical Activity
KRS 634.subject: KRS
KRS 634.description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

KRS 635.title: Elementary Physical Education
KRS 635.subject: KRS
KRS 635.description: Content and pedagogy for teaching preschool/elementary physical education. Students will learn appropriate content and pedagogy for learners in elementary school. Bit teaching and field experiences are included.

KRS 636.title: Theory and Assessment of Personality
KRS 636.subject: KRS
KRS 636.description: Personality testing; practice in administration and use of personality assessment; examination of psychometric and social issues.

KRS 637.title: Multicultural Counseling
KRS 637.subject: KRS
KRS 637.description: Significance of cultural factors in counseling relationships, delivery of counseling services in multicultural settings with attention to Hawaiʻi. Emphasis on process of cultural learning and implications for counselor roles and functions.

KRS 640.title: Seminar in Physical Activity
KRS 640.subject: KRS
KRS 640.description: Trends, research, and problems related to physical activity across the lifespan. A variety of topics and contexts will be addressed. Enrolled in KRS graduate program only.

KRS 641.title: Seminar: Health/Exercise Science
KRS 641.subject: KRS
KRS 641.description: Review of selected current literature in exercise/sport science and leisure studies. Practice of presentation in group setting.

KRS 643.title: Secondary Physical Education
KRS 643.subject: KRS
KRS 643.description: Detailed examination of effective physical education curriculum and instruction in middle and high schools.

KRS 646.title: American College Student
KRS 646.subject: KRS
KRS 646.description: Study of psychosocial characteristics of American college students and college environment, from viewpoint of student personnel work.

KRS 650.title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
KRS 650.subject: KRS
KRS 650.description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawaiʻi and our global community.

KRS 651.title: Sexuality & Health
KRS 651.subject: KRS
KRS 651.description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

KRS 660.title: Marriage, Family, and Child Counseling
KRS 660.subject: KRS
KRS 660.description: Theory/practice of marriage, family, and child counseling, including major model in clinical practice; supervised counseling project by each student. Liability insurance required.

KRS 663.title: Biomechanics of Human Motion
KRS 663.subject: KRS
KRS 663.description: Principles of motion as applied to sport and physical rehabilitation. Introduction to the technology used in the analysis of motion.

KRS 664.title: Physiology of Exercise
KRS 664.subject: KRS
KRS 664.description: Physiological bases of modern physical training methods and sports science.

KRS 665.title: Metabolic Analysis
KRS 665.subject: KRS
KRS 665.description: Theory and practice of metabolic analysis of human performance examining each of the power systems used in energy production during exercise and how to use this information to prescribe exercise programs.

KRS 666.title: Advanced Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription
KRS 666.subject: KRS
KRS 666.description: Provides knowledge of field and laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of testing results and individual exercise program/prescription techniques.

KRS 667.title: Body Composition and Weight Management
KRS 667.subject: KRS
KRS 667.description: Analysis of the theory and practice used in the assessment of body composition and human physique. Includes strategies for implementing changes in body composition.

KRS 670.title: Consultation: Theory and Practice
KRS 670.subject: KRS
KRS 670.description: Consultation in educational, business, health, community, and human services agencies.

KRS 673.title: Research Methods in KRS
KRS 673.subject: KRS
KRS 673.description: The use of experimental designs/models in physical education research with emphasis on understanding the concepts, applications, and interpretations of statistical analysis.

KRS 674.title: Assessment in Physical Activity
KRS 674.subject: KRS
KRS 674.description: Overview of assessment purposes, types, practices and procedures used in physical education for those with disabilities. Frequently used motor assessments and practices in collection of data will be specifically addressed.

KRS 675.title: Transdisciplinary Approach to Teaching the Motor Domain
KRS 675.subject: KRS
KRS 675.description: Highlights a transdisciplinary approach for effectively teaching students with disabilities in the motor domain. Important characteristics and components of this approach will be shared. Strategies for its implementation will also be addressed.

KRS 680.title: Principles and Practice of Rehabilitation Counseling
KRS 680.subject: KRS
KRS 680.description: Principles, practices of rehabilitation counseling; review of history and influence of legislation on vocational rehabilitation; current issues, developments, with emphasis on local situation.

KRS 681.title: Medical and Psychosocial Aspects of Disability
KRS 681.subject: KRS
KRS 681.description: Functional implications of chronic illnesses and disabilities on psychological, social and vocational areas of an individuals life. Case studies and presentations will stimulate discussion and help students to apply theoretical information into practical everyday context.

KRS 683.title: Case Management in Rehabilitation
KRS 683.subject: KRS
KRS 683.description: Knowledge and skills required in case and case-load management in public as well as private sector rehabilitation sites. Emphasis on professional/client relationship, interviewing process, decision-making, goal-setting, recording/documentation, time management, and other tasks.

KRS 684.title: Psychopathology in Counseling
KRS 684.subject: KRS
KRS 684.description: Discussion-oriented course (potentially Web-based). Examination of theory and practice of diagnosis in the assessment and treatment of mental disorders and the use of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) multi-axial system. Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues.

KRS 685.title: Ethical and Legal Issues in Counseling
KRS 685.subject: KRS
KRS 685.description: Developing ethical reasoning capabilities for resolution of ethical dilemmas likely to be encountered in counseling, psychology, and specialty practices (e.g., community, rehabilitation, school, mental health, alcohol and substance abuse, marriage and family counseling, and the like).

KRS 686.title: Vocational Evaluation and Assessment in Rehabilitation
KRS 686.subject: KRS
KRS 686.description: Theory, process, and techniques of vocational evaluation and assessment. Assessment methods and processes as they relate to vocational choice and adjustment of special groups.

KRS 687.title: Assistive Technology in Rehabilitation Counseling
KRS 687.subject: KRS
KRS 687.description: Study of application of assistive technologies to enhance the lives of people with disabilities. Case studies provide the vehicle in guiding students toward integration of available information into reality of actual situations. Special emphasis on the importance of using a consumer-centered approach in providing assistive technology services.

KRS 688.title: Theory and Techniques of Job Placement
KRS 688.subject: KRS
KRS 688.description: Theory, process, and techniques of job readiness, job development, and job placement.

KRS 695.title: Promoting Physical Activity
KRS 695.subject: KRS
KRS 695.description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

KRS 699.title: Directed Reading and/or Research
KRS 699.subject: KRS
KRS 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair.

KRS 703C.title: Practicum in Counseling: community service
KRS 703C.subject: KRS
KRS 703C.description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
KRS 703C.prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

KRS 704.title: Contemporary Issues in Counseling
KRS 704.subject: KRS
KRS 704.description: Current issues and problems. (Meets EdD common required elective.)

KRS 733C.description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

KRS 741.title: Seminar in School Counseling
KRS 741.subject: KRS
KRS 741.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in school counseling.
KRS 741.prereq_raw: KRS 703 / EDEP 703 (E or H) and consent.

KRS 751.title: Seminar in Community Counseling
KRS 751.subject: KRS
KRS 751.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in community counseling.

KRS 761.title: Seminar in College Counseling
KRS 761.subject: KRS
KRS 761.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in college counseling.

KRS 775.title: Doctoral Seminar and Research I in Kinesiology
KRS 775.subject: KRS
KRS 775.description: Will expose the PhD student to the basic nature of behavioral and somatic science research. Learning experiences will consist of journal review, laboratory/field techniques, and subject or data collector exposures as directed by faculty mentors.

KRS 776.title: Doctoral Seminar and Research II in Kinesiology
KRS 776.subject: KRS
KRS 776.description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to be involved in research, under the direction of the faculty mentor, as the assistant project director and as the project director for pilot studies. Student will gain experience in these roles with close supervision by the faculty mentor.

KRS 777.title: Doctoral Seminar and Research III in Kinesiology
KRS 777.subject: KRS
KRS 777.description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to assume the role of director of a research project under the supervision of the faculty mentor. The research project will represent a piece of the ongoing line of research of the faculty mentor. Responsibilities will be comparable of a project director of research funded by a research grant.

KRS 778.title: Doctoral Seminar IV in Kinesiology
KRS 778.subject: KRS
KRS 778.description: Designed to enable PhD students to gain a perspective of the discipline, both historically and philosophically, prepare them for the issues they may face in the real world, particularly higher education and help them initiate their dissertation.

KRS 781.title: Seminar in Rehabilitation Counseling
KRS 781.subject: KRS
KRS 781.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in rehabilitation counseling.

LAIS 120.title: Islands/Islas/Ilhas and Global Exchange
LAIS 120.subject: LAIS
LAIS 120.description: Cross-cultural study of global issues of navigation, commerce, and the environment, as expressed by the arts, traditions, and narratives from 1492 to the present. Connections with Europe, Africa, Americas, Asia, Oceania.

LAIS 320.title: Vaqueros, Gauchos, Paniolo: Cowboy Legacies of the Americas and Hawaiʻi
LAIS 320.subject: LAIS
LAIS 320.description: Histories and traditions (literature, music, dance, poetry, food, fashion) of the Hispanic cowboy, Americas to Hawaiʻi. Examines symbolic interpretations of the vaquero concerning nation and identity, and the material consequences of ranching (colonialism, commerce, environment). Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

LAIS 340.title: Chocolate Tales & Culinary Cultures: Latin America to Hawaiʻi
LAIS 340.subject: LAIS
LAIS 340.description: Traces evolution of uses, meanings, and cultural representations of chocolate and other food native to Latin America. Emphasis on how narratives of food and food practices engage with national, ethnic, social, and gender identity constructions. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

LAIS 360B.title: Studies in Culture: Latin America
LAIS 360B.subject: LAIS
LAIS 360B.description: Politics of culture and representation. Will consider issues, traditions, movements, texts, and cultural icons for their significance for national and regional identity formation, intercultural relations and global flows of images, people, and capital. (B) Latin America; (C) Iberian Peninsula.
LAIS 360B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or consent.

LAIS 360C.title: Studies in Culture: Iberian Peninsula
LAIS 360C.subject: LAIS
LAIS 360C.description: Politics of culture and representation. Will consider issues, traditions, movements, texts, and cultural icons for their significance for national and regional identity formation, intercultural relations and global flows of images, people, and capital. (B) Latin America; (C) Iberian Peninsula.
LAIS 360C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or consent.

LAIS 363.title: U.S. Latino Culture and Literature
LAIS 363.subject: LAIS
LAIS 363.description: The culture and history of U.S. Latinos through an analysis of their literature and arts and their sociopolitical relationship to the U.S. mainstream culture.
LAIS 363.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LAIS 365.title: Spanish Film
LAIS 365.subject: LAIS
LAIS 365.description: A chronological survey of films from Spain, from the Silent Era to the present. Conceptually, a cultural history of Spain in the 20th century, as seen through films.
LAIS 365.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LAIS 366.title: Latin American Film
LAIS 366.subject: LAIS
LAIS 366.description: A survey of films from Latin America, the Silent Era to the present, and their representation of the cultural history of the region. Develops written communication skills.
LAIS 366.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LAIS 368.title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
LAIS 368.subject: LAIS
LAIS 368.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households. Sophomore standing or higher.

LAIS 372B.title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Mesoamerica
LAIS 372B.subject: LAIS
LAIS 372B.description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
LAIS 372B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LAIS 372C.title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Andean South America
LAIS 372C.subject: LAIS
LAIS 372C.description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
LAIS 372C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LAIS 380.title: Studies in Culture: Portugal and Brazil
LAIS 380.subject: LAIS
LAIS 380.description: Surveys the cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world from pre-Lusitanian times, including connections with Africa, Asia, the U.S., and Hawaiʻi.
LAIS 380.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LAIS 381.title: Asians and Pacific Islanders in Latin America
LAIS 381.subject: LAIS
LAIS 381.description: Survey of the history and culture of Asian, Polynesian, and Pacific Islander communities in Latin America. Sophomore standing or higher.

LAIS 468.title: Colonial Latin American History
LAIS 468.subject: LAIS
LAIS 468.description: Pre-Columbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social and religious evolution to 1810; independence.

LAIS 478.title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
LAIS 478.subject: LAIS
LAIS 478.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

LAIS 495B.title: Topics in Latin American and Iberian Studies: Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama
LAIS 495B.subject: LAIS
LAIS 495B.description: Combined lecture-discussion on political, social, cultural themes of Iberia and Latin America; (B) Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama; (C) Luso-Hispanic pop culture.
LAIS 495B.prereq_raw: LAIS 360 or LAIS 363 or LAIS 368 or LAIS 372 or LAIS 380 , and SPAN 351 , and SPAN 352 ; or consent.

LAIS 495C.title: Topics in Latin American and Iberian Studies: Luso-Hispanic pop culture
LAIS 495C.subject: LAIS
LAIS 495C.description: Combined lecture-discussion on political, social, cultural themes of Iberia and Latin America; (B) Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama; (C) Luso-Hispanic pop culture.
LAIS 495C.prereq_raw: LAIS 360 or LAIS 363 or LAIS 368 or LAIS 372 or LAIS 380 , and SPAN 351 , and SPAN 352 ; or consent.

LAIS 683.title: Hispanic Cultural Studies
LAIS 683.subject: LAIS
LAIS 683.description: Critical overview of contemporary theories on Hispanic culture. Issues of identity such as mestizaje, hybridity, and pluralism will be discussed from a hemispheric perspective.

LATN 101.title: Elementary Latin
LATN 101.subject: LATN
LATN 101.description: Grammar and vocabulary, with reading of simple Latin.

LATN 201.title: Intermediate Latin
LATN 201.subject: LATN
LATN 201.description: Development of reading and translation skills. Emphasis on prose.

LATN 202.title: Intermediate Latin
LATN 202.subject: LATN
LATN 202.description: Continuation of LATN 201 : emphasis on poetry.

LATN 303.title: Roman Historians
LATN 303.subject: LATN
LATN 303.description: Selections from Caesar, Sallust, and others.

LATN 304.title: Roman Epic
LATN 304.subject: LATN
LATN 304.description: Selections from Virgil, Ovid, and others.

LATN 325.title: Roman Philosophy
LATN 325.subject: LATN
LATN 325.description: Selections from Lucretius, Cicero, and Seneca.

LATN 332.title: Roman Drama
LATN 332.subject: LATN
LATN 332.description: Selections from Plautus, Terence, and Seneca.

LATN 333.title: Roman Lyric
LATN 333.subject: LATN
LATN 333.description: Selections from Catullus, Horace, and others.

LATN 490.title: Seminar in Roman Studies
LATN 490.subject: LATN
LATN 490.description: Study of an author or phase in Roman studies.
LATN 490.prereq_raw: any two 300-level LATN courses, or consent.

LAW 099.title: Exchange Student Program
LAW 099.subject: LAW
LAW 099.description: Designed for students accepted to participate in an exchange program while enrolled at William S. Richardson School of Law. Must obtain prior approval for the transfer credits.

LAW 501.title: Organizing for Social Change
LAW 501.subject: LAW
LAW 501.description: Examines conditions that lead people to become active, self-governing agents. Covered are strategies and tactics of organizers, history of social change movements, anti-subordination theories of justice and organizing case studies.

LAW 503.title: Historic Preservation Law
LAW 503.subject: LAW
LAW 503.description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws.

LAW 504.title: Lawyering Fundamentals I
LAW 504.subject: LAW
LAW 504.description: Comprehensive program that teaches students the analytical and presentational skills necessary for excellent legal writing. Introduces students to legal problem solving and writing through the types of documents lawyers prepare in practice.

LAW 505.title: Lawyering Fundamentals II
LAW 505.subject: LAW
LAW 505.description: A comprehensive program that teaches students the analytical and presentational skills necessary for excellent legal writing. Introduces skills and strategies for preparing written legal arguments and oral advocacy.

LAW 506.title: Contracts
LAW 506.subject: LAW
LAW 506.description: Law of private agreements. Focuses on common law doctrines with some attention to key Uniform Commercial Code provisions. Examines the bases of promissory liability, contract formation, defenses to enforcement, contract interpretation, breach, and remedies.

LAW 507.title: Employment Discrimination
LAW 507.subject: LAW
LAW 507.description: A study of the law of employment discrimination.

LAW 508.title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
LAW 508.subject: LAW
LAW 508.description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice- negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR.

LAW 509.title: Contracts I
LAW 509.subject: LAW
LAW 509.description: Law of private agreements. Explores the evolution and application of common law doctrines, and, where applicable, relevant provisions of the Uniform Commercial Code. Examines the bases of promissory liability, contract formation, mutual assent, defenses to enforcement, excuses, remedies and damages, and the rights and interests of third parties. Attention will be paid throughout the course to the role of contracts in a market society and the conflicting interests of certainty, freedom of contract and fairness.

LAW 510.title: Contracts II
LAW 510.subject: LAW
LAW 510.description: Continuation of LAW 509 . Topics include defenses to enforcement, performance and breach, and remedies.
LAW 510.prereq_raw: LAW 509 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 511.title: Professional Responsibility
LAW 511.subject: LAW
LAW 511.description: Introductory consideration of selected topics relating to functions, structure, and responsibilities of the legal profession and its future role in society.

LAW 512.title: Reparations and Reconciliation
LAW 512.subject: LAW
LAW 512.description: Seminar addresses a legally and socially important contemporary issue-healing present-day wounds of historic injustice. Considers how to repair the continuing social damage of injustice.

LAW 513.title: Criminal Law
LAW 513.subject: LAW
LAW 513.description: Examination of substantive rules, enforcement procedures, and rationales of criminal law in the U.S.

LAW 514.title: Children, Parents and the Law
LAW 514.subject: LAW
LAW 514.description: Exploration of fundamental concepts of law relating to children, ethical issues, and the role of lawyers in assisting children, and how the child’s rights and obligations are balanced with those of parents and state.

LAW 515.title: Business Reorganization in Bankruptcy
LAW 515.subject: LAW
LAW 515.description: Examination of the rights and remedies available to a failing business and its creditors when the business seeks to reorganize its business and financial affairs under chapter 11 of the federal bankruptcy code. The course is structured as a “practicum,” which tracks a single business through restructuring and emphasizes the practical and strategic aspects of lawyering. Recommended: LAW 562 .

LAW 516.title: Civil Procedure I
LAW 516.subject: LAW
LAW 516.description: Study of pre-trial, trial, and appellate procedures in the federal and Hawaiʻi courts.

LAW 517.title: Civil Procedure II
LAW 517.subject: LAW
LAW 517.description: Building upon the principles of LAW 516 , continues the study of pre-trial, trial, and appellate procedures in the federal and Hawaiʻi courts.
LAW 517.prereq_raw: LAW 516 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 518.title: Real Property I
LAW 518.subject: LAW
LAW 518.description: Basic course in property ownership, development, regulation. Emphasis on theory.

LAW 519.title: Real Property II
LAW 519.subject: LAW
LAW 519.description: Contract of sale, equitable conversion, deed.
LAW 519.prereq_raw: LAW 518 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 520.description: Faculty members or visiting scholars present selected topics focusing upon subject areas in their area of specialty or expertise. LAW 521.title: Law, Aging and Medicine
LAW 521.subject: LAW
LAW 521.description: Introduction to basic legal issues at the intersection of law, aging and medicine. Addresses various issues confronting elderly; issues confronting the general population including health care financing, decision-making, and bioethics.

LAW 522.title: Torts
LAW 522.subject: LAW
LAW 522.description: Torts cover the statutory and common law of negligence, causation, defenses, damages, strict liability, intentional torts and tort policy and reform, with emphasis on national and Hawaiʻi law.

LAW 523.title: Law and Psychology
LAW 523.subject: LAW
LAW 523.description: Approaches psychology as a problem solving tool that can facilitate legal analysis. Covers a variety of areas including jury decision-making, research methodology, social cognition, culture, and behavioral economics, among others.

LAW 524.title: Advanced Torts and Insurance Law
LAW 524.subject: LAW
LAW 524.description: Advanced study of several areas of tort law and an introduction to insurance law and policy. This course is of considerable importance to students interested in civil litigation and personal injury law. Recent important developments in Hawaiʻi tort and insurance law will be included.
LAW 524.prereq_raw: LAW 522 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 525.title: Legislation and Statutory Interpretation
LAW 525.subject: LAW
LAW 525.description: The interrelationship between the legislative and judicial branches of government is explored through a review of Federal and Hawaiʻi law-making processes, direct democracy, legislative drafting, and theories of the legislative process and statutory interpretation.

LAW 526.title: Group Directed Study
LAW 526.subject: LAW
LAW 526.description: Designed for maximum flexibility, this course allows a professor to work with a small number of students on a reading/ discussion project of mutual interest.

LAW 527.title: Federal Indian Law
LAW 527.subject: LAW
LAW 527.description: Examines Federal Indian Law, including fundamental concepts and the historical evolution of legal doctrines. Considers the implications of Native Hawaiian sovereignty within the framework of Federal Indian Law.

LAW 530.title: Second-Year Seminar
LAW 530.subject: LAW
LAW 530.description: Seminar required for spring semester of all second-year law students. Substantial paper required. Topics announced in previous fall semester. Placement by lottery.

LAW 531.title: Business Associations
LAW 531.subject: LAW
LAW 531.description: After a brief survey of agency, partnerships, and other forms of business organization, the course will cover the fundamentals of corporations, and securities regulation, including disregarding the corporate entity, management and control of closely held corporations, merger, liability under the federal securities laws, takeovers, public registration, exemptions, and derivative suits.

LAW 532.title: Health Law
LAW 532.subject: LAW
LAW 532.description: Introduction to medical jurisprudence, medical malpractice, informed consent, health care decisions, medical ethics, the health care industry, managed care, financing health care, and the role of government in health care.
LAW 532.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only; NURS DNP majors only

LAW 533.title: Constitutional Law I
LAW 533.subject: LAW
LAW 533.description: Introduction to judicial function in constitutional cases, jurisdiction of the U.S. Supreme Court, and discretionary barriers to judicial review.

LAW 534.title: Constitutional Law II
LAW 534.subject: LAW
LAW 534.description: Advanced course in constitutional law with special emphasis on rights secured by the First, Fifth, and Fourteenth Amendments to the Constitution of the U.S.
LAW 534.prereq_raw: LAW 533 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 535.title: Intellectual Property
LAW 535.subject: LAW
LAW 535.description: A study of the law relating to property rights resulting from intellectual effort, including patents, copyright, trademarks, and trade secrets.

LAW 538.title: Conflict of Laws
LAW 538.subject: LAW
LAW 538.description: Problems respecting the law applicable in transactions or to relationships with elements in more than one state.

LAW 539.title: Remedies
LAW 539.subject: LAW
LAW 539.description: Examines both practice aspects and theoretical underpinnings of equitable remedies. Frequently, compensatory damages cannot adequately protect clients or provide them with the relief they need. Topics include temporary restraining orders, preliminary and permanent injunctions, restitution and unjust enrichment, specific performance, and equitable defenses such as unclean hands, laches, and estoppel. Practice issues concerning appeal, jury trials, and the relationship of equity to law are also explored.

LAW 540.title: Contract Drafting
LAW 540.subject: LAW
LAW 540.description: Hands-on workshop class in drafting contracts, agreement, and similar documents for commercial/business purposes.
LAW 540.prereq_raw: LAW 506 , or LAW 509 and LAW 510 , with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 541.title: Criminal Procedure
LAW 541.subject: LAW
LAW 541.description: Issues of free press and fair trial, illegal search and seizure, arrest and confession, speedy trial, double jeopardy are covered through student interactions as defense or prosecution attorneys and as judges.

LAW 542.title: Advanced Civil Procedure
LAW 542.subject: LAW
LAW 542.description: Addresses various aspects of complex litigation and recent criticism of the civil litigation system itself. Theoretical in emphasis.
LAW 542.prereq_raw: LAW 516 and LAW 517 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 543.title: Evidence
LAW 543.subject: LAW
LAW 543.description: “Objection, your Honor!” This course examines the rules of evidence that govern trials in both federal and Hawaiʻi courts and will focus on such topics as hearsay, witness examination, impeachment, physical and demonstrative evidence, expert testimony, writings, relevance, judicial notice, and presumptions.

LAW 544.title: Race, Culture, and Law
LAW 544.subject: LAW
LAW 544.description: U.S. cases and legal theory emphasizing law in the social construction of racial categories, shifts in race-based anti-discrimination law, and the interaction of culture and law in judicial decision-making.

LAW 545.title: Licensing Intellectual Property
LAW 545.subject: LAW
LAW 545.description: Theory and practice of the law relating to the transfer of rights in information and other intangibles are examined together with end user license agreements and the structure and negotiation of upstream licensing mechanisms.

LAW 546B.title: Intercession-J Term: alternative dispute resolution
LAW 546B.subject: LAW
LAW 546B.description: January term provides students the opportunity to explore contemporary legal topics with national and international experts. (B) alternative dispute resolution; (C) rule of law; (D) law practice; (E) diversity; (F) access to justice; (G) public law; (H) legal theory; (I) legal practice; (J) rights.

LAW 546C.title: Intercession-J Term: rule of law
LAW 546C.subject: LAW

LAW 547.title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
LAW 547.subject: LAW
LAW 547.description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

LAW 548.title: Immigration Law
LAW 548.subject: LAW
LAW 548.description: Introduction to U.S. Immigration and Nationality Law: a brief overview of historical development of immigration law; analysis of exclusion and deportation grounds and remedies; the study of both immigrant and nonimmigrant visa applications and petitions. Current law on asylum and refugee applications and U.S. citizenship and naturalization requirements.

LAW 549.title: Admiralty Law
LAW 549.subject: LAW
LAW 549.description: Introduction to U.S. maritime law and admiralty jurisdiction emphasizing development of rules of maritime law and rights of seamen and maritime workers.

LAW 550.title: Corporate and Partnership Taxation
LAW 550.subject: LAW
LAW 550.description: Examines tax aspects of formation, operation, reorganization, and liquidation of partnerships and corporations.

LAW 552.title: Trusts and Estates
LAW 552.subject: LAW
LAW 552.description: Deals primarily with the disposition of family wealth including: the making of wills; the creation, enforcement, administration, and termination of trusts; and intestate succession, including probate.

LAW 553.title: E-Discovery
LAW 553.subject: LAW
LAW 553.description: Surveys the relevant law, theory, and practice governing the review and production of electronically stored information, focusing on the rules of civil procedure, the rules of evidence, and case law.
LAW 553.prereq_raw: LAW 516 and LAW 517 with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 554.title: Secured Transactions
LAW 554.subject: LAW
LAW 554.description: Introduction to Uniform Commercial Code, particularly Article 9- reducing risk of nonpayment by obtaining an interest in borrowers’ property.

LAW 555H.title: Externship: Hawaiʻi
LAW 555H.subject: LAW
LAW 555H.description: Legal work for judges and attorney supervisors in public agencies, private law firms, and the legislature. (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) outside Hawaiʻi.

LAW 555P.title: Externship: outside Hawaiʻi
LAW 555P.subject: LAW
LAW 555P.description: Legal work for judges and attorney supervisors in public agencies, private law firms, and the legislature. (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) outside Hawaiʻi.

LAW 558.title: Corporate Finance
LAW 558.subject: LAW
LAW 558.description: Provides an understanding of the basic financial concepts and tools for lawyers with transactional practices, preferred stock, common stock and convertible securities.

LAW 559.title: Labor Law I
LAW 559.subject: LAW
LAW 559.description: Regulation of union-management relations under state and federal laws.

LAW 560.title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
LAW 560.subject: LAW
LAW 560.description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses. Recommended: LAW 531 .
LAW 560.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law, MBA, and ME students only.

LAW 561.title: Administrative Law
LAW 561.subject: LAW
LAW 561.description: Procedure and remedies for resolving controversies between citizens and government officials exercising administrative power.

LAW 562.title: Debtors’ and Creditors’ Rights
LAW 562.subject: LAW
LAW 562.description: Bankruptcy laws and rules, laws of liens, receiverships.

LAW 563.title: Trial Practice
LAW 563.subject: LAW
LAW 563.description: Examination of sequential stages of pre-trial and trial practice in a problem setting. Topics include investigation, pleadings, motions, discovery, voir dire examination, opening statements, direct and cross examination, closing argument, selected evidentiary problems, post-trial motions, and appellate practice. Students engage in simulated exercises, and their work is critiqued.

LAW 564.title: Pre-Trial Litigation
LAW 564.subject: LAW
LAW 564.description: Theory and practice of civil pre-trial litigation with focus on pleading, discovery, and pre-trial motions.

LAW 566.title: Non-Profit Organizations
LAW 566.subject: LAW
LAW 566.description: Examines the meaning, scope, and role of non-profit organizations in contemporary society, and focuses on selected non-tax laws and primary tax issues relevant to non-profits. Recommended: LAW 531 and LAW 567 .

LAW 567.title: Federal Income Taxation
LAW 567.subject: LAW
LAW 567.description: Surveys the entire federal income tax system, with emphasis on those areas of greatest importance to non-tax lawyers. Students are expected to develop proficiency in the use of the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury Regulations.

LAW 568.title: Family Law
LAW 568.subject: LAW
LAW 568.description: Legal forms of-and responses to-formation, maintenance, and dissolution of the family. Marriage, annulment, divorce, alimony, separation agreements, child custody and adoption, parentage.

LAW 571.title: Federal Courts
LAW 571.subject: LAW
LAW 571.description: An examination of the jurisdiction and law-making powers of the federal courts, standing issues, appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, federal-question and diversity-of-citizenship jurisdiction of the federal district courts, immunities from suit in the federal courts possessed by governmental entities and officers, intervention by federal courts in state proceedings, and choice of law in the federal courts. Particular emphasis on relevant Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.
LAW 571.prereq_raw: LAW 533 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C-.

LAW 572.title: International Protection of Human Rights
LAW 572.subject: LAW
LAW 572.description: The growing body of international human rights laws, including procedural law and role of nongovernmental organizations.

LAW 573.title: Jurisprudence
LAW 573.subject: LAW
LAW 573.description: Relationships between the concepts of law and morality with views of legal and moral philosophers.

LAW 574.title: State and Local Government Law and Finance
LAW 574.subject: LAW
LAW 574.description: City, town, county, district governments: administrative organization; regulatory powers; police power; local governmental taxation; relationship between local, state, and federal government.

LAW 577.title: Advanced Legal Analysis
LAW 577.subject: LAW
LAW 577.description: Designed to help students enhance their legal writing and analysis skills as law students, bar examinees, and legal professionals.

LAW 578.title: Artificial Intelligence and Social Justice
LAW 578.subject: LAW
LAW 578.description: Introduces you to and engages you directly in the study of artificial intelligence, legislation and regulation, and social justice in a variety of application contexts.

LAW 579.title: Introduction to Space Law & Policy
LAW 579.subject: LAW
LAW 579.description: Acquaints students with the fundamental principles of space law and policy, including the pre- and post-Sputnik history of space exploration.

LAW 580.title: Land Use Management and Control
LAW 580.subject: LAW
LAW 580.description: Survey course of public land use management.

LAW 581.title: Advanced Immigration Law & Policy
LAW 581.subject: LAW
LAW 581.description: Current immigration policy developments as a window into the way law, both legislated and case-law driven, interacts with policy objectives to produce desirable as well as unanticipated outcomes.

LAW 583.title: Real Estate Development and Financing
LAW 583.subject: LAW
LAW 583.description: Federal and state laws in the practice of real estate development and financing law. Condominium, securities, subdivision, consumer protection, and mortgage areas.

LAW 584.title: Civil Rights
LAW 584.subject: LAW
LAW 584.description: Focuses on the civil rights of Americans and introduces alternative remedies and procedures for securing these rights.

LAW 585.title: Refugees, Asylum & Forced Migration
LAW 585.subject: LAW
LAW 585.description: Based on international agreements, implemented through domestic federal statutory law, and administered by Executive Branch agencies who are subject to judicial review, creating a rich context for legal learning.

LAW 587.title: Extended Bar Review I
LAW 587.subject: LAW
LAW 587.description: Provides students with critical skills for success on the bar exam, specifically, MBE and MEE question practice and review of highly tested topics in Civil Procedure, Criminal Law and Procedure, and Real Property.

LAW 588.title: Extended Bar Review II
LAW 588.subject: LAW
LAW 588.description: Provides students with critical skills for success on the bar exam, specifically, MBE and MEE question practice and review of highly tested topics in Contracts, Evidence, and Torts.

LAW 589.title: Labor and Employment Law
LAW 589.subject: LAW
LAW 589.description: Employment law, statutory rights affecting the employment relation, and alternative contract provisions to secure the parties’ intentions. Focus on the practical application of labor and employment law. Materials relating to the unionized employment relationship. Emphasis on the labor arbitration process and possibly, to issues regarding internal union affairs.

LAW 590B.description: (B) Prosecution Clinic; (C) Defense Clinic; (D) Elder Law Clinic; (E) Environmental Law Clinic; (F) Beyond Guilt Hawaiʻi; (G) Estate Planning Workshop; (H) Legal Aid Clinic; (I) Native Hawaiian Rights Clinic; (J) Family Law Clinic; (K) Entrepreneurship and Small Business Clinic; (M) Mediation Clinic; (N) Lawyering Skills Workshop; (P) Mediation Workshop; (Q) Immigration Clinic; (R) Child Welfare Clinic; (S) Hawaiʻi Innocence Project I; (T) Hawaiʻi Innocence Project II; (U) Medical Legal Partnership; (W) Advanced Elder Law Clinic.
