LAW 590U.description: (B) Prosecution Clinic; (C) Defense Clinic; (D) Elder Law Clinic; (E) Environmental Law Clinic; (F) Beyond Guilt Hawaiʻi; (G) Estate Planning Workshop; (H) Legal Aid Clinic; (I) Native Hawaiian Rights Clinic; (J) Family Law Clinic; (K) Entrepreneurship and Small Business Clinic; (M) Mediation Clinic; (N) Lawyering Skills Workshop; (P) Mediation Workshop; (Q) Immigration Clinic; (R) Child Welfare Clinic; (S) Hawaiʻi Innocence Project I; (T) Hawaiʻi Innocence Project II; (U) Medical Legal Partnership; (W) Advanced Elder Law Clinic.
LAW 590U.prereq_raw: LAW 543 for (C); LAW 561 or LWEV 582 for (E); LWPA 581 for (I); LAW 568 or consent for (J); LAW 548 for (Q); LAW 590D for (W).
LAW 590U.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only for (R), (S), (T), (U), and (W).

LAW 590W.title: Workshops and Clinics: Advanced Elder Law Clinic
LAW 590W.subject: LAW
LAW 590W.description: (B) Prosecution Clinic; (C) Defense Clinic; (D) Elder Law Clinic; (E) Environmental Law Clinic; (F) Beyond Guilt Hawaiʻi; (G) Estate Planning Workshop; (H) Legal Aid Clinic; (I) Native Hawaiian Rights Clinic; (J) Family Law Clinic; (K) Entrepreneurship and Small Business Clinic; (M) Mediation Clinic; (N) Lawyering Skills Workshop; (P) Mediation Workshop; (Q) Immigration Clinic; (R) Child Welfare Clinic; (S) Hawaiʻi Innocence Project I; (T) Hawaiʻi Innocence Project II; (U) Medical Legal Partnership; (W) Advanced Elder Law Clinic.
LAW 590W.prereq_raw: LAW 543 for (C); LAW 561 or LWEV 582 for (E); LWPA 581 for (I); LAW 568 or consent for (J); LAW 548 for (Q); LAW 590D for (W).
LAW 590W.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only for (R), (S), (T), (U), and (W).

LAW 593.title: Integrity and Ethics in the Real World
LAW 593.subject: LAW
LAW 593.description: Interactive course addressing important topical ethical issues in areas including the corporate, entertainment, medical, legal, political, education, and sports worlds. Renowned knowledgeable guests will discuss critical issues in their respective fields through panel conversations.

LAW 594.title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
LAW 594.subject: LAW
LAW 594.description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle.

LAW 599.title: Directed Study and Research
LAW 599.subject: LAW
LAW 599.description: Individual research and writing under the direction of faculty.

LING 102.title: Introduction to the Study of Language
LING 102.subject: LING
LING 102.description: Non-formal introduction to language, emphasizing the everyday use of language, its relevance to contemporary issues in society, and local language issues. Content studied through lecture, readings, and writing; emphasis on writing as a grading criterion.

LING 103.title: Language and Symbolic Reasoning
LING 103.subject: LING
LING 103.description: Introduction to language as a formal symbolic system and to the techniques of analysis and reasoning that reveal its workings.

LING 105.title: Language Endangerment, Globalization, and Indigenous Peoples
LING 105.subject: LING
LING 105.description: Focus on language endangerment and globalization. Students are introduced to case studies on language endangerment from around the world and throughout history. Offered through the distance-learning Unit Mastery program.

LING 120.title: Language as a Window to the Mind
LING 120.subject: LING
LING 120.description: Introduction to language-related phenomena, which gives insight into the organization of the human mind. Combines lecture, discussion and group projects.

LING 123.title: Logic and Language
LING 123.subject: LING
LING 123.description: Introduces logic as a way of understanding the meanings of everyday words and sentences, as well as the inferences that humans draw from them. Topics include propositional logic, first-order logic, elementary set theory, and relations.

LING 131.title: Language and AI: A Basic Introduction
LING 131.subject: LING
LING 131.description: This non-mathematical introduction to language and language models critically investigates traditional versus AI-driven editing, translation, language learning, and linguistic research, exploring major and little-studied languages, dangers, ethical issues, future advances and likely limitations.

LING 150B.title: Language in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific: unit mastery
LING 150B.subject: LING
LING 150B.description: Introduction to the study of language and language-related issues, with a focus on Hawaiʻi and the Pacific; (B) unit mastery; (C) lecture discussion with focus on writing as a grading criterion.

LING 150C.title: Language in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific: lecture discussion
LING 150C.subject: LING
LING 150C.description: Introduction to the study of language and language-related issues, with a focus on Hawaiʻi and the Pacific; (B) unit mastery; (C) lecture discussion with focus on writing as a grading criterion.

LING 170.title: The Language of Children
LING 170.subject: LING
LING 170.description: Survey of findings about the child’s acquisition of language.

LING 201.title: Language Documentation for Non- Linguists
LING 201.subject: LING
LING 201.description: Provides training in the fundamentals of language documentation and conservation for non-linguists.
LING 201.prereq_raw: proficiency in a lesser studied language and consent.

children.text: proficiency in a lesser studied language

LING 215.title: Bad Words
LING 215.subject: LING
LING 215.description: An examination of the link between language and society through the use and perception of taboo words.

LING 320.title: General Linguistics
LING 320.subject: LING
LING 320.description: Introduction to the formal analysis of language, focusing on phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, historical linguistics, language acquisition, and related topics.

LING 331.title: Computer Applications
LING 331.subject: LING
LING 331.description: Background; uses for machine translation, dictionary programs, speech synthesis, grammar modeling, etc.

LING 344.title: Languages of the World
LING 344.subject: LING
LING 344.description: Survey of major language families; typological classification and language universals; writing systems, “contact” languages. Variety of grammatical structures illustrated by selected languages.

LING 346.title: The Philippine Language Family
LING 346.subject: LING
LING 346.description: Introduction; phonological and grammatical systems; historical developments; emphasis on Filipino, Cebuano, and Ilokano.
LING 346.prereq_raw: grade of B or better in LING 102 or LING 320 and experience with a Philippine language, or consent.

children.text: grade of B or better in LING 102

LING 347.title: Pidgin and Creole Languages
LING 347.subject: LING
LING 347.description: Nature, history, structure, and geographic distribution of pidgins and creoles.

LING 394.title: Philippine Sociolinguistics: Language Use, Ideologies, and Identities
LING 394.subject: LING
LING 394.description: Examines the intersection between language and society, specifically Philippine languages in various communities. Explores how language policies, discourses, and ideologies shape people’s use of language. Emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills.
LING 394.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

LING 410.title: Articulatory Phonetics
LING 410.subject: LING
LING 410.description: Intensive training in recognition, reproduction, and recording of human speech sounds; preparation for fieldwork with unrecorded languages and for clinical work in speech pathology.

LING 412.title: Psycholinguistics
LING 412.subject: LING
LING 412.description: The mental processes involved in producing, understanding, and acquiring language. Students will conduct a small psycholinguistic experiment.
LING 412.prereq_raw: one of LING 102 , LING 320 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.

LING 414.title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
LING 414.subject: LING
LING 414.description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

LING 415.title: Language and Gender
LING 415.subject: LING
LING 415.description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required.

LING 416.title: Language as a Public Concern
LING 416.subject: LING
LING 416.description: How does language serve as a proxy for larger social questions? Focuses on four main themes: language revitalization, discrimination on the basis of accent, gender miscommunication and the English Only Movement.

LING 417.title: Language Endangerment and Revitalization
LING 417.subject: LING
LING 417.description: An overview of language endangerment, especially in the Pacific and Asia, and a critical examination of the strategies that are being developed to combat it.
LING 417.prereq_raw: one of LING 102 , LING 150B , LING 150C , LING 105 , LING 320 , SLS 150 , SLS 301 , or consent.

LING 418.title: Raciolinguistics
LING 418.subject: LING
LING 418.description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere.

LING 420.title: Morphology
LING 420.subject: LING
LING 420.description: Theory of word structure; analysis of a variety of morphological types.

LING 423.title: Cognitive Linguistics
LING 423.subject: LING
LING 423.description: Conceptual systems and language from a cognitive science perspective. Linguistic evidence on conceptual structure, reasoning, categorization, and understanding.
LING 423.prereq_raw: LING 102 , LING 320 , ICS 111 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.

LING 430.title: Animal Communication
LING 430.subject: LING
LING 430.description: Investigates animal communication from the perspective of modern linguistics. Dispels common misconceptions about “talking animals” and shows how the cognitive, biological, and environmental needs and opportunities of animals determine what and how they communicate.

LING 431.title: Computational Modeling
LING 431.subject: LING
LING 431.description: Hands-on introduction to modeling language. Focuses on connectionism, relations between language perception, and motor control. Requires no programming experience.
LING 431.prereq_raw: LING 102 , LING 320 , ICS 111 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.

LING 440.title: Topics in Linguistics
LING 440.subject: LING
LING 440.description: Variable topics in special areas of Linguistics, depending on instructor interest.

LING 441.title: Meaning
LING 441.subject: LING
LING 441.description: Theories of how literal and figurative language encode meaning and processes of meaning encoding and decoding.
LING 441.prereq_raw: LING 102 , LING 320 , ICS 111 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.

LING 445.title: Polynesian Language Family
LING 445.subject: LING
LING 445.description: Introduction to the language family of Hawaiian, Samoan, Tahitian, Tongan, etc.; models of migration and settlement and linguistic evidence; subgrouping and reconstruction of Proto-Polynesian; linguistic characteristics of present-day languages; language endangerment and conservation in Polynesia.
LING 445.prereq_raw: LING 320 with a grade of B or better, or consent.

LING 451.title: Induction of Linguistic Structure
LING 451.subject: LING
LING 451.description: Phonological and grammatical structures of a previously uncodified language are determined by linguistic analysis of data obtained from speakers of the language.

LING 470.title: Children’s Speech
LING 470.subject: LING
LING 470.description: Child language acquisition, language milestones, multilingualism. Relation of cognitive development to language development. Emphasis on developing research skills, with an emphasis on written communication.

LING 611.title: Acoustic and Auditory Phonetics
LING 611.subject: LING
LING 611.description: Principles of acoustics and audition as they relate to speech sounds, use of computer-based analysis tools to investigate acoustic properties of speech.

LING 615.title: The Nature of Language
LING 615.subject: LING
LING 615.description: Language as a communication system, current theories of grammar, meaning, sociolinguistics, linguistic change and comparison.

LING 617.title: Language Acquisition and Language Revitalization
LING 617.subject: LING
LING 617.description: Provides training relevant to the study and revitalization of heritage languages and endangered languages.

LING 618.title: Data Science for Linguistic Research
LING 618.subject: LING
LING 618.description: Introduction to data science for linguistic research.

LING 619.title: Practical Exercises in Data Science for Linguistic Research
LING 619.subject: LING
LING 619.description: Exercises in data science for linguistic research.

LING 621.title: Phonology
LING 621.subject: LING
LING 621.description: Phonological theory and problems of analysis.

LING 622.title: Grammar
LING 622.subject: LING
LING 622.description: Grammatical theory and problems of analysis.

LING 623.title: Semantics and Pragmatics
LING 623.subject: LING
LING 623.description: Ways in which the interpretation of sentences in natural language depends upon the literal meaning of propositions and their logical (semantic) and conversational (pragmatic) inferences.

LING 624.title: Discourse and Grammar
LING 624.subject: LING
LING 624.description: Usage-based examination of grammar in the context of spontaneous spoken language, including the role of discourse on synchronic and diachronic grammatical structure, discourse in interaction, and discourse in language documentation.

LING 631.title: Language Data Processing
LING 631.subject: LING
LING 631.description: Preparation of language data for computer processing; use readymade programs; write simple language processing programs using SNOBOL4. Applications to student’s research.

LING 632.title: Laboratory and Quantitative Research Methods
LING 632.subject: LING
LING 632.description: Laboratory and quantitative methods for research on language. Introduction to hardware, software, research designs, and basic analysis techniques commonly used in quantitative language research. Combines lecture, laboratory work ,and discussion.

LING 635.title: Linguistics of Sign Languages
LING 635.subject: LING
LING 635.description: Universals and uniqueness in the phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures of sign languages, taught inductively with emphasis on hands-on analysis. Opportunities exist for skills development in American or Ho Chi Minh City sign languages.
LING 635.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LING 636.title: Hawaiʻi Sign Language Linguistics: Documentation, Conservation, and Revitalization of HSL
LING 636.subject: LING
LING 636.description: Descriptive information on the phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures and lexicon of Hawaiʻi Sign Language (HSL); language skills development in HSL; and guided research related to the documentation, conservation, and revitalization of HSL.
LING 636.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LING 640E.title: Topics in Linguistics: English linguistics
LING 640E.subject: LING
LING 640E.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 640F.title: Topics in Linguistics: phonology and phonetics
LING 640F.subject: LING
LING 640F.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 640G.title: Topics in Linguistics: general
LING 640G.subject: LING
LING 640G.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 640H.title: Topics in Linguistics: history of the discipline
LING 640H.subject: LING
LING 640H.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 640S.title: Topics in Linguistics: sociolinguistics
LING 640S.subject: LING
LING 640S.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 640X.title: Topics in Linguistics: syntax
LING 640X.subject: LING
LING 640X.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 640Y.title: Topics in Linguistics: psycholinguistics
LING 640Y.subject: LING
LING 640Y.description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.

LING 641.title: Professionalism in Linguistics
LING 641.subject: LING
LING 641.description: Topics related to career development and professional/scholarly communication in linguistics, including CVs, abstracts, grant proposals, publications, conference planning. Topics vary by instructor.

LING 645.title: Introduction to Historical Linguistics
LING 645.subject: LING
LING 645.description: Introduction to historical-comparative linguistics; attention to both Indo-European and languages with few or no written records.

LING 646.title: Issues in Historical Linguistics
LING 646.subject: LING
LING 646.description: Continuation of LING 645 . Addresses advanced topics in historical linguistics that have generated controversy rather than consensus.

LING 670.title: Developmental Linguistics
LING 670.subject: LING
LING 670.description: Survey of the literature in language acquisition; emphasis on relation to linguistic theory.

LING 680.title: Introduction to Language Documentation
LING 680.subject: LING
LING 680.description: Covers history, method, and theory behind language documentation, and the role of language endangerment in the field. Discussion on skills required to undertake documentation; topics may vary depending on the emphases of the instructor.

LING 685.title: Techniques of Language Documentation
LING 685.subject: LING
LING 685.description: Students learn to conduct best-practice digital language documentation projects, from equipment purchase to data collection to data annotation to archiving and presentation.

LING 690.title: Field Methods
LING 690.subject: LING
LING 690.description: Work with native speakers of lesser-known languages to develop techniques for data collection and analysis.
LING 690.prereq_raw: LING 421 and LING 422 and one of LING 621 or LING 622 ; or consent.

LING 691.title: Advanced Field Methods
LING 691.subject: LING
LING 691.description: Advanced training in linguistic fieldwork and language documentation through first-hand work with a speaker of a non-dominant language.

LING 699.title: Directed Research
LING 699.subject: LING
LING 699.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

LING 720.title: Language Typology
LING 720.subject: LING
LING 720.description: Language typology deals with how and why the elements of language interact and function. Students acquire a broad overview of this grammatical make-up of languages in general and understanding of Functional-Typological linguistics.
LING 720.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LING 730.title: Advanced Laboratory Research
LING 730.subject: LING
LING 730.description: Advanced laboratory methods for research in linguistics. Specialized and/or advanced uses of hardware, software, research designs, and analysis techniques. Specific topic varies: check with department. Combines lecture, laboratory work and discussion.

LING 750E.title: Seminar: ethnolinguistics
LING 750E.subject: LING
LING 750E.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750F.title: Seminar: phonology and phonetics
LING 750F.subject: LING
LING 750F.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750G.title: Seminar: general
LING 750G.subject: LING
LING 750G.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750M.title: Seminar: semantics
LING 750M.subject: LING
LING 750M.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750Q.title: Seminar: language acquisition
LING 750Q.subject: LING
LING 750Q.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750R.title: Seminar: written language
LING 750R.subject: LING
LING 750R.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750S.title: Seminar: sociolinguistics
LING 750S.subject: LING
LING 750S.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750X.title: Seminar: syntax
LING 750X.subject: LING
LING 750X.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 750Y.title: Seminar: psycholinguistics
LING 750Y.subject: LING
LING 750Y.description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

LING 770.title: Areal Linguistics
LING 770.subject: LING
LING 770.description: Structures of languages of various areas of the world; diffusion.

LING 799.title: Apprenticeship in Teaching Linguistics
LING 799.subject: LING
LING 799.description: Experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation.
LING 799.prereq_raw: admission to doctoral program and consent.

LIS 101.title: Think Critically, Click Wisely in the Digital Era: Information, Media and News Literacy
LIS 101.subject: LIS
LIS 101.description: Practice skills to evaluate information, media, and news critically, distinguishing between credible sources and misinformation. Develop essential competencies for navigating today’s digital landscape and fostering a well-informed, democratic society.

LIS 202.title: The Information Environment
LIS 202.subject: LIS
LIS 202.description: Investigates how information flows in society, providing a critical perspective on how technologies shape knowledge, experience and memory.

LIS 591.title: Library and Information Studies Workshop
LIS 591.subject: LIS
LIS 591.description: Designed for in-service librarians and other information specialists needing to update their professional skills, focus on a particular topic, or learn new approaches and concepts.

LIS 601.title: Introduction to Reference and Information Services
LIS 601.subject: LIS
LIS 601.description: Philosophy, principles, and practice of reference services in libraries, information centers and information literacy. Bibliographic control, reference research, reference interview, online searching, evaluation of bibliographic and Webliographic material. Field component. MLISc degree required course.

LIS 602.title: Resource Discovery
LIS 602.subject: LIS
LIS 602.description: Techniques and strategies for discovery of information resources from professional online databases and the Web. Query formulation and use of advanced functions to match retrieved resources with user needs for research and reference work.
LIS 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 605.title: Metadata Creation for Information Organization
LIS 605.subject: LIS
LIS 605.description: Theory and practice of metadata creation for organization of information resources, cataloging code for resource description and access, Library of Congress and Dewey Decimal Classification schemes, use of OCLC.

LIS 610.title: Foundations of the Information Professions
LIS 610.subject: LIS
LIS 610.description: Lecture/discussion/survey of the information professions, development of professional identity, professional values and ethics, historical development, current issues in the information professions.

LIS 611.title: Intellectual Freedom
LIS 611.subject: LIS
LIS 611.description: Seminar surveying the core philosophical principles and practices of intellectual freedom with special application to librarianship and information sciences.

LIS 612.title: History of Information
LIS 612.subject: LIS
LIS 612.description: History of the recording, preservation, and transmission of knowledge. Development of libraries and other information organizations as instruments of cultural transmission.

LIS 614.title: Navigating Information Organizations
LIS 614.subject: LIS
LIS 614.description: Principles of effective management of information organizations, with emphasis on organizational information flows, team skills, communication, planning, resource allocation, assessment, outreach, and advocacy.
LIS 614.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 615.title: Collection Management
LIS 615.subject: LIS
LIS 615.description: Principles and issues of collection management and care. Criteria and tools for selecting and deselecting materials. Relationships with publishers/producers.

LIS 619.title: Preservation Management
LIS 619.subject: LIS
LIS 619.description: Introduction to preservation management. Focus on management strategies for preservation of materials in libraries and archives. Covers preservation planning, condition surveys, disaster planning, grantsmanship, and basic issues relating to deterioration. LIS majors only.

LIS 630.title: Community Engagement
LIS 630.subject: LIS
LIS 630.description: Explores how information professionals in libraries and other settings collaborate with community members and organizations. Provides an overview of theory and practice emphasizing critical analysis of policies, services, and trends. Required course for CALIS.

LIS 631.title: Introduction to Hawaiʻi and Pacific Librarianship
LIS 631.subject: LIS
LIS 631.description: Overview of resources and issues concerning librarianship in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific Islands. Reference strategies and materials to answer common research questions, collection development, and management issues.
LIS 631.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 633.title: Indigenous Librarianship
LIS 633.subject: LIS
LIS 633.description: Development and delivery of information services with and for indigenous communities. Issues include cultural protocols, traditional knowledge organization and ethics of access.
LIS 633.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 634.title: Multicultural Resources for Diverse User Groups
LIS 634.subject: LIS
LIS 634.description: Examines resources and materials targeted for diverse user populations in libraries and community organizations, locally and globally. Surveys issues and trends related to diversity initiatives affecting the publishing industry, libraries, and cultural institutions worldwide.
LIS 634.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 635.title: Traditional Literature and Oral Narration
LIS 635.subject: LIS
LIS 635.description: Analysis of traditional literature including Asian and Pacific Island resources. Selection and evaluation of traditional literature emphasizing cultural values. Introduction to oral tradition, history and techniques of storytelling.

LIS 636.title: Responding to Reading in Libraries
LIS 636.subject: LIS
LIS 636.description: Research-intensive seminar that explores the reading process in library contexts and similar settings. Critical examination of ways in which library and literacy services impact reading engagement and interests of library users.

LIS 641.title: Digital Librarianship
LIS 641.subject: LIS
LIS 641.description: Lecture with demonstrations to introduce the essential types of digital resources and the software tools for finding high quality and relevant information efficiently from digital journal archives and reference databases.

LIS 645.title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
LIS 645.subject: LIS
LIS 645.description: Literature of Asia in Western and Asian languages; bibliography, reference tools, research methods, sources, published and archival repositories.

LIS 648.title: Government Documents
LIS 648.subject: LIS
LIS 648.description: Survey of government documents at the federal, state/local and international levels in all formats. Covers methods of acquisition and organization, including depository arrangements. Current issues of government information dissemination policies and practices discussed.

LIS 650.title: Management of Libraries and Information Centers
LIS 650.subject: LIS
LIS 650.description: Theories and principles of administration for effective management of libraries and information centers, with emphasis on planning, resource allocation, team skills, project management, assessment, leadership, outreach, and advocacy.

LIS 651.title: Archival Arrangement and Description
LIS 651.subject: LIS
LIS 651.description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope and content.

LIS 654.title: Records, Archives and Memory
LIS 654.subject: LIS
LIS 654.description: Introduction to records, archives, and memory including the global history and nature of records, archives, and the archival profession. Topics include cultural memory, ethics and values, tribal and indigenous records, archival theory, practice and perspectives.

LIS 655.title: Digital Archives
LIS 655.subject: LIS
LIS 655.description: The role of technology in archival theory and practice. Topics include digital preservation, authenticity assessment, arrangement and description, content management, and access systems.
LIS 655.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 656.title: Moving Image Archives
LIS 656.subject: LIS
LIS 656.description: Principles and technologies of processing, preservation, and accessibility of archival audiovisual materials in moving image archives. Topics include moving image repositories, critical analysis of archival footage, format identification, digitization strategies, equipment, and vendor considerations.
LIS 656.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only

LIS 657.title: Records Management
LIS 657.subject: LIS
LIS 657.description: Management of records in all media formats. Selection of media format based on government and internal records requirements. Problems associated with electronic media such as legality and shelf life.

LIS 658.title: Archival and Special Collections Management
LIS 658.subject: LIS
LIS 658.description: Management of archives, manuscript collections, and special collections using approaches and best practices from archival studies. Topics include management theory, appraisal theory, facilities issues, privacy, intellectual property, records management, advocacy, fundraising, reference, and educational outreach.

LIS 659.title: Archival Access, Representation and Use
LIS 659.subject: LIS
LIS 659.description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope, and content. LIS majors only.
LIS 659.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 661.title: Informatics
LIS 661.subject: LIS
LIS 661.description: Sociotechnical concepts and processes underlying information systems, services, and use.
LIS 661.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 662.title: Asian Informatics
LIS 662.subject: LIS
LIS 662.description: Lecture/discussion on the transformative effects of information and communication technologies in East Asia. Topics include media, mobile devices, social media, publishing, e-government, and e-commerce.
LIS 662.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 665.title: Digital Instruction
LIS 665.subject: LIS
LIS 665.description: Study and application of principles and practices that influence digital instruction related to information literacy in libraries and other information environments. Focus on application of instructional design and standards-based outcome assessment. Field research component.

LIS 672.title: Technology for Libraries and Information Centers
LIS 672.subject: LIS
LIS 672.description: Survey of theories, concepts, methods and practices relating to the application of information technology to support the administration and use of information resources. Includes digital, printed and audiovisual materials.

LIS 674.title: Database Design and Creation
LIS 674.subject: LIS
LIS 674.description: Designing and creating textual and/or directory databases from the viewpoint of information specialists and content providers. Needs analysis, file design, record content and structuring, software choice. Students implement prototype database.

LIS 676.title: Creating Digital Libraries
LIS 676.subject: LIS
LIS 676.description: Principles, techniques, and technologies supporting the creation of user-centered digital libraries. Selection, organization, maintenance, access, and retrieval of digital collections.
LIS 676.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 677.title: Human Dimension in Information Systems
LIS 677.subject: LIS
LIS 677.description: Lecture/discussion on human element in information systems, including physical, cognitive and affective behavior in interaction with information systems. Information retrieval, human-computer interaction and cognitive science research, quantitative and qualitative research methods. Research component.

LIS 681.title: Books and Media for Children
LIS 681.subject: LIS
LIS 681.description: History and criticism of children’s literature. Contemporary books and media. Trends in book publishing and media production. Developmental needs and interests of children. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

LIS 682.title: Books and Media for Young Adults
LIS 682.subject: LIS
LIS 682.description: History and criticism of literature for young adults. Contemporary books and media. Trends in media for young adults. Developmental needs and interests of adolescents. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

LIS 683.title: Services in Public Libraries
LIS 683.subject: LIS
LIS 683.description: Planning and implementing services and programming in public and school libraries. Trends, issues, networking, public relations, outreach, competencies, services for the disabled and other special groups.

LIS 686.title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
LIS 686.subject: LIS
LIS 686.description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

LIS 690.title: Internship
LIS 690.subject: LIS
LIS 690.description: Field experience in library or information agency settings with supervision of professional librarians or information specialists. Available to classified students only. Selection based on academic advisor approval, application form, interview and possession of required competencies. Students must apply and be accepted before registration. Selection is by agency.

LIS 691.title: Masters Seminar
LIS 691.subject: LIS
LIS 691.description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio and preparation for professional practice. Peer mentoring and student presentations. MLISc degree Plan B required course.

LIS 692.title: Masters Seminar II
LIS 692.subject: LIS
LIS 692.description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio or thesis. Peer mentoring, faculty, and student presentations. MLISc degree required course.
LIS 692.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

LIS 693.title: Special Topics in Information Studies
LIS 693.subject: LIS
LIS 693.description: Includes issues of topical interest in the information professions. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as services for specific groups and special collections. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.

LIS 694.title: Special Topics in Information Technology
LIS 694.subject: LIS
LIS 694.description: Includes issues of topical interest in information technology. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as digital archives, content management systems and informatics. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.

LIS 696.title: Practicum School Librarianship
LIS 696.subject: LIS
LIS 696.description: Skill development and application of academic study through observation and practice in a fieldwork program with accompanying seminar. Required for school library certification in Hawaiʻi.
LIS 696.prereq_raw: 12 credits in LIS degree program and consent of practicum coordinator required.

LIS 699.title: Directed Reading and/or Research
LIS 699.subject: LIS
LIS 699.description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Enrollment requires approval before end of previous semester, with specification of goals, work requirements, number of credits, rationale.

LIS 701.title: Seminar in International Librarianship
LIS 701.subject: LIS
LIS 701.description: International and comparative librarianship; professional organizations; comparative methodology; research; periodicals; international agencies; influence of literacy and social, cultural, political factors.

LLEA 147.title: Death and Dying in Literature and Film
LLEA 147.subject: LLEA
LLEA 147.description: Exploration of death and dying in literature and film as manifested across time and cultures throughout the world. Analysis of narratives from ancient times to the modern era from multiple theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

LLEA 199.title: Directed Language Study
LLEA 199.subject: LLEA
LLEA 199.description: Study in European languages not taught regularly, depending on demand and staff.

LLEA 236.title: Italian Film
LLEA 236.subject: LLEA
LLEA 236.description: Study of Italian film history and technique.

LLEA 237.title: French Film
LLEA 237.subject: LLEA
LLEA 237.description: Study of French film history and technique.

LLEA 247.title: Gods, Heroes, and Dragons: Germanic Myth, Legends, and Fairy Tales
LLEA 247.subject: LLEA
LLEA 247.description: Study of Germanic myth, legends, and fairy tales. Analysis of narratives from ancient times to the modern era from multiple theoretical perspectives.

LLEA 264.title: French Culture for Americans
LLEA 264.subject: LLEA
LLEA 264.description: Study of the shared cultural and historical foundations of France and the U.S. both past and present.

LLEA 270.title: Freaks and Monsters
LLEA 270.subject: LLEA
LLEA 270.description: Monsters, freaks and otherness in literature, film, history and medicine. Suitable for non-literature majors.

LLEA 320.title: German Cinema
LLEA 320.subject: LLEA
LLEA 320.description: Study of German film history, film theory, film analysis, and film style.
LLEA 320.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing only.

LLEA 334.title: Italian Literature as Film
LLEA 334.subject: LLEA
LLEA 334.description: Exploration of the distinction between literature and film as artistic genres as well as study of major works of literature in respect to the present, from the Middle Ages through the 20th century.
LLEA 334.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 335.title: French Literature Since 1800
LLEA 335.subject: LLEA
LLEA 335.description: Rapid reading in translation; lectures, discussions, reports.
LLEA 335.prereq_raw: junior standing or one course in French language or literature.

LLEA 336.title: French African Literature
LLEA 336.subject: LLEA
LLEA 336.description: Black African literature in French in 20th century. Major themes of negritude, national political unity, colonialism, traditional culture.
LLEA 336.prereq_raw: junior standing or one course in French language or literature.

LLEA 337.title: Topics in Italian Literature in Translation
LLEA 337.subject: LLEA
LLEA 337.description: Introduction to Italian literature in translation, with varying topics in different iterations.
LLEA 337.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 339.title: Love, Murder, and Greed in French Cinema
LLEA 339.subject: LLEA
LLEA 339.description: French literature and cinema from the Middle Ages through the 21st century, exploring how stories of passion, betrayal, and ambition reshape the boundaries between classical texts and films.

LLEA 340.title: Classical German Literature
LLEA 340.subject: LLEA
LLEA 340.description: Readings in translation from dramatic works of Lessing, Goethe, Schiller. Philosophic and aesthetic views of leading writers of the Enlightenment, Storm and Stress, and classical periods.

LLEA 341.title: German Opera and Literature
LLEA 341.subject: LLEA
LLEA 341.description: Introduction to German opera, its history, and analysis. Developing critical skills through analysis of German opera music and literature. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

LLEA 342.title: German Fascism and Propaganda
LLEA 342.subject: LLEA
LLEA 342.description: Study of German Fascism and propaganda in German literature, art, film, and associated ethical issues.
LLEA 342.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

LLEA 350.title: Russian Short Story
LLEA 350.subject: LLEA
LLEA 350.description: Origin and development (19th and 20th century); periods, themes, styles, and major authors.
LLEA 350.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 351.title: 19th-Century Russian Literature
LLEA 351.subject: LLEA
LLEA 351.description: Survey in English of major writers from Pushkin through Chekhov; lectures, discussions, short papers.
LLEA 351.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 352.title: Russian Literature 1900—1950
LLEA 352.subject: LLEA
LLEA 352.description: Study of significant works of twentieth century Russian literature with particular focus on its relationship to Europe and Asia. Students will work intensively on their own writing and research in close collaboration with their instructor.
LLEA 352.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 353.title: Russia: Between Europe & Asia
LLEA 353.subject: LLEA
LLEA 353.description: Russian culture (literature, film, theater, music, arts, etc.) as an amalgam of European and Asian traditions and its impact on the world throughout history; develops written communication skills.
LLEA 353.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 354.title: Russia: Faces of Asia
LLEA 354.subject: LLEA
LLEA 354.description: Survey in English of 19th-21st century representations of Asia in the contexts of the Russian Empire, the Soviet Union, and post-Soviet space.
LLEA 354.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 355.title: Russian Film
LLEA 355.subject: LLEA
LLEA 355.description: A study of Russian film from the 1920’s to the present.
LLEA 355.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 360.title: The Art of Western Love
LLEA 360.subject: LLEA
LLEA 360.description: Chronological illustration of romantic love in European and Francophone Pacific literature and films, from its inception in 12th-century French courtly literature to our contemporary age of materialistic disenchantment.
LLEA 360.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

LLEA 364.title: Survey of French Civilizations
LLEA 364.subject: LLEA
LLEA 364.description: A historical survey of the development of French and Francophone cultures. The course is interdisciplinary, dealing with politics, music, art, other forms of cultural expression, and daily life.

LLEA 371.title: Europeans in the Pacific
LLEA 371.subject: LLEA
LLEA 371.description: European presence in the Pacific, in relation to literature, art, culture, and civilization. Not applicable to language requirement.

LLEA 390.title: Teaching Practicum in Large Lecture Courses
LLEA 390.subject: LLEA
LLEA 390.description: Supervised undergraduate teaching practicum in large-lecture LLEA courses.
LLEA 390.prereq_raw: completion of course in which practicum will be done and consent of instructor, no waiver.

LLEA 396C.title: European and Latin American Cinema: Genre

LLEA 396D.description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

LLEA 396E.subject: LLEA
LLEA 396E.description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

LLEA 399.title: Directed Reading
LLEA 399.subject: LLEA
LLEA 399.description: Pre: limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major, and consent of department chair.

LLEA 415.title: Spies, Memory, & The Cold War: Literature, Film, and Culture in Postwar Germany
LLEA 415.subject: LLEA
LLEA 415.description: East and West German literature, film, and culture (1945-1989), focusing on postwar recovery, espionage, and surveillance. Explores how cultural production reflects memory, private/public life, and political tensions in a divided society under geopolitical pressures.
LLEA 415.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

LLEA 416.title: German Literature, Culture and Film: 1989 to Present
LLEA 416.subject: LLEA
LLEA 416.description: Study of German literature, culture and film, 1989 to present. Credit cannot be earned for both LLEA 416 and GER 416 . Sophomore standing or higher.

LLEA 455.title: Learning and Teaching World Languages
LLEA 455.subject: LLEA
LLEA 455.description: Hybrid technology intensive course for pre- or in-service teachers of world languages. Topics: online learning, curriculum and lesson planning, assessment, language teaching approaches, technology for learning world languages. Junior standing or higher.

LLEA 470.title: Freaks and Monsters 2: The Ethics of Otherness
LLEA 470.subject: LLEA
LLEA 470.description: An interdisciplinary examination of corporeal Otherness. Unusual real and fictional bodies from fairground history, art, anatomy, literature, natural history and ethnology. Discussion of the moral, medical, philosophical and aesthetic dilemmas of spectacular difference.

LLEA 471B.title: Fantasy and the Fantastic: fairies, devils and fantasy
LLEA 471B.subject: LLEA
LLEA 471B.description: Cross-cultural study of fantasy and the fantastic in short stories, fairy tales, films and novels from Europe and the Americas in English translation. Discussion of illusion, identity, time, the future, the bizarre and major concepts in fantasy literature. (B) fairies, devils and fantasy; (C) the fantastic, the strange and science fiction.

LLEA 471C.title: Fantasy and the Fantastic: the fantastic, the strange and science fiction
LLEA 471C.subject: LLEA
LLEA 471C.description: Cross-cultural study of fantasy and the fantastic in short stories, fairy tales, films and novels from Europe and the Americas in English translation. Discussion of illusion, identity, time, the future, the bizarre and major concepts in fantasy literature. (B) fairies, devils and fantasy; (C) the fantastic, the strange and science fiction.

LLEA 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
LLEA 499.subject: LLEA
LLEA 499.description: Independent study of approved reading and research with faculty supervision.

LLEA 630.title: Seminar in Research Methods
LLEA 630.subject: LLEA
LLEA 630.description: Study of basic research methods and tools, including technology. Print and electronic source materials. Information literacy.
LLEA 630.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

LLEA 671.title: Western Literature and Cultures in the Pacific
LLEA 671.subject: LLEA
LLEA 671.description: Impact of and reaction to western writings and cultural influences in the Pacific as represented in texts from the 16th century to the present.
LLEA 671.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

MA candidates in European languages read works in their major in the original.

LLEA 680C.subject: LLEA
LLEA 680C.description: Study in English of a topic, period, or genre; aesthetic considerations common to European literatures: (B) the modern novel; (C) European literature as a path to self-knowledge; (D) Middle Ages; (E) introduction to literary theory. LLEA 680E.subject: LLEA
LLEA 680E.description: Study in English of a topic, period, or genre; aesthetic considerations common to European literatures: (B) the modern novel; (C) European literature as a path to self-knowledge; (D) Middle Ages; (E) introduction to literary theory. MA candidates in European languages read works in their major in the original.
LLEA 680E.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent of department chair.

LLEA 681B.title: Topics in Language: comparison of Romance languages
LLEA 681B.subject: LLEA
LLEA 681B.description: Study in English of topics, periods, etc., in the languages taught in the department: (B) comparison of Romance languages; (C) interpersonal communication; (D) social perspectives.

LLEA 681C.subject: LLEA

LLEA 682.title: Masterpieces of Medieval Welsh Literature
LLEA 682.subject: LLEA
LLEA 682.description: Key prose and poetry underlying the Arthurian tradition in Europe. Language instruction leading to reading knowledge of medieval Welsh.

LTEC 112.title: Technologies for Academic Success

LTEC 113.title: Technologies for Academic Success- Business

LTEC 113.description: Virtual and hands-on analysis of technology resources and utilization in learning with an emphasis on business education.

LTEC 414.title: Educational Media Technology

LTEC 414.description: Introduction to educational technology theory and practice with an emphasis on meaningful integration of technology and media into a variety of face-to-face and online learning environments for diverse populations.

LTEC 415.description: Introduction to the application of educational technology in teaching and learning using strategies in design, selection, development, integration, and evaluation. Interactive delivery via distance education technologies.

LTEC 430.description: Overview of video uses in educational contexts. Includes video planning, production, and simple editing procedures, as well as selection, evaluation, and integration into learning plans.

LTEC 448.title: Social Media: Links to Lifelong Learning
LTEC 448.subject: LTEC
LTEC 448.description: Exploration of social media and effects on individuals, communities, and world. Analysis and evaluation of impacts and ethical implications of social media, with emphasis on writing. Includes service learning and research project.
LTEC 448.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing (junior or higher).

LTEC 461.title: Foundations in Design Thinking
LTEC 461.subject: LTEC
LTEC 461.description: Using real-world problems, students learn a creative problem-solving process that is human-centered and iterative, and practice design thinking mindsets (embracing ambiguity, learning from failure, and bias toward action) as they tackle the problem.

LTEC 514.title: Professional Development Education Technology IV

Practical applications of these theories to solve instructional problems in real-life settings.
LTEC 600.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC major or consent.

LTEC 602.title: Innovations in Educational Technology
LTEC 602.subject: LTEC
LTEC 602.description: Innovative technological advances and new media in the field of educational technology and their application in instruction.
LTEC 602.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC major or consent.

LTEC 611.subject: LTEC
LTEC 611.description: Review of existing research in media/ ed technology, with activities leading to the preparation of final study or project proposal.
LTEC 611.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 615.subject: LTEC
LTEC 615.description: Enables students to develop the skills to manage instructional design projects to complete them on time, on budget, and within the scope of client expectations by applying project management tools.
LTEC 615.prereq_raw: LTEC 600 (with a minimum grade of B-), or with instructor permission.
LTEC 615.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC majors only, or consent.

LTEC 620.title: Visual Design
LTEC 620.subject: LTEC
LTEC 620.description: Theory and practice involved in planning educational/instructional graphic and photographic material for print and computer-based media.
LTEC 620.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 622.title: E-learning Theory and Design
LTEC 622.subject: LTEC
LTEC 622.description: Principles of e-learning theory as well as design and development for instruction. Application to new media and web authoring.
LTEC 622.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC majors or consent.

LTEC 623.title: Digital Video Design
LTEC 623.subject: LTEC
LTEC 623.description: Development and utilization of digital video for the purpose of improving the teaching-learning process.
LTEC 623.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC major or consent.

LTEC 632.subject: LTEC

LTEC 632.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 641.title: Emerging Technologies for K-12 Teaching
LTEC 641.subject: LTEC
LTEC 641.description: Exploration and impact of emerging technologies in K-12 classroom teaching and learning and ramifications of these technologies on administrative structure of schools.
LTEC 641.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 642.title: Facilitating E-learning Communities
LTEC 642.subject: LTEC
LTEC 642.description: Exploration of tools and design considerations for effective online communication and development of learning communities.
LTEC 642.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC major or consent.

LTEC 643.title: Educational Technology in Informal Learning Environments
LTEC 643.subject: LTEC
LTEC 643.description: Exploring the nature, application, and use of educational technology in informal learning environments, such as museums, cultural institutions, tourist attractions, and visitor information centers. Focusing on the analysis, selection, and development of various media choices.
LTEC 643.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LTEC major or consent.

LWPA 514.title: Law and Society in Japan
LWPA 514.subject: LWPA
LWPA 514.description: An extended historical review of the foundations of Japanese law in society: Japan’s adoption and adaptation of Chinese legal doctrines, continental European legal structures and ideas, and American influences. Consideration of the structure of contemporary law in Japan: a look at the various players in the legal system, some important legal doctrines, and the real-world operation of Japan’s laws today.

LWPA 553.title: Asian Pacific Insolvency Law
LWPA 553.subject: LWPA
LWPA 553.description: Comparison of corporate insolvency law of selected Asian and Pacific island countries, with a focus on recently enacted laws and pending proposals that have followed the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis. Recommended: LAW 515 , LAW 554 , LAW 562 .

LWPA 556.title: Asian Comparative Labor Law
LWPA 556.subject: LWPA
LWPA 556.description: Area studies of Asian legal systems and issues, focusing on administration of Asian labor laws in a comparative context. Possible effects on foreign direct investment and foreign migrant contract workers. Comparison of Chinese, Japanese and other legal approaches in dealing with common issues.

LWPA 564.title: International Criminal Law
LWPA 564.subject: LWPA
LWPA 564.description: Designed to give an understanding of international criminal law. Will review all aspects of international criminal law from substantive international crimes to criminal liability and sentencing by domestic and international tribunals.

LWPA 565.title: Law and Society in Korea
LWPA 565.subject: LWPA
LWPA 565.description: Provides students with an understanding of the law, society, and legal systems in Korea. Areas of law including constitutional, civil, criminal, and business are discussed. Emphasis on South Korea. Law majors only.

LWPA 569.title: Human Rights in Asia
LWPA 569.subject: LWPA
LWPA 569.description: A survey of human rights norms, institutions, and implementation mechanism of international human rights law in light of the rapid development of regional cooperation and integration in Asia.
