LWPA 579.title: International Business Transactions
LWPA 579.subject: LWPA
LWPA 579.description: An examination of the law, rules, and practices relating to transborder commercial transactions. Roughly half of the semester focuses on international sales transactions, the remaining portion focuses on domestic and multinational governance of the international business arena.

LWPA 580.title: Foundations for Kānāwai
LWPA 580.subject: LWPA
LWPA 580.description: Examines Hawaiʻi’s cultural and legal foundations as essential context for Native Hawaiian Law. Integrating ʻike Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian knowledge), it specifically focuses on Hawaiʻi’s history, culture, and justice through an ʻŌiwi lens.

LWPA 581.title: Native Hawaiian Law
LWPA 581.subject: LWPA
LWPA 581.description: Status and evolution of rights of Native Hawaiians to the land and its usufructs. Potential of utilizing native rights based on statute, custom, and use to develop new and expanded rights.

LWPA 582B.title: Topics-Native Hawaiian Law: policy and governance
LWPA 582B.subject: LWPA
LWPA 582B.description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawaiʻi, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability.

LWPA 582C.title: Topics-Native Hawaiian Law: business and economic development
LWPA 582C.subject: LWPA
LWPA 582C.description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawaiʻi, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability.

LWPA 582D.title: Topics-Native Hawaiian Law: law and culture
LWPA 582D.subject: LWPA
LWPA 582D.description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawaiʻi, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability.

LWPA 582E.title: Topics-Native Hawaiian Law: Indigenous peoples
LWPA 582E.subject: LWPA
LWPA 582E.description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawaiʻi, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability.

LWPA 582F.title: Topics-Native Hawaiian Law: Indigenous environment and sustainability
LWPA 582F.subject: LWPA
LWPA 582F.description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawaiʻi, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability.

LWPA 583.title: Legal History of Hawaiʻi
LWPA 583.subject: LWPA
LWPA 583.description: Designed to acquaint the student with the unique legal history of Hawaiʻi, emphasizing particular legal controversies that have shaped the law of our island society.

LWPA 584.title: Emerging Hawaiʻi Water Issues
LWPA 584.subject: LWPA
LWPA 584.description: Introduction to the legal framework for water resource management in Hawaiʻi; case studies illuminate the litigation process and evolution of the public trust, precautionary principle, and other legal, scientific, and policy areas.

LWPA 585.title: International Law
LWPA 585.subject: LWPA
LWPA 585.description: Evolving process of formulating rules to govern nations and peoples of the world in their attempts to solve problems recognized as requiring global solutions.

LWPA 586.title: Law and Society in China
LWPA 586.subject: LWPA
LWPA 586.description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

LWPA 587.title: Comparative Law
LWPA 587.subject: LWPA
LWPA 587.description: Introduction to the civil law tradition, particularly as exemplified by the legal systems of East and Southeast Asia. After a brief review of comparative law study and the historical development of the civil law, the course will examine the structure and role of the courts, judicial process, the legal profession and constitutional law and administrative law in Western Europe and in the Asian civil law countries.

LWPA 588.title: International Human Rights Advocacy
LWPA 588.subject: LWPA
LWPA 588.description: Applying international human rights law and legal skills to promote and protect human rights by way of United Nations Charter-based human rights mechanism, treaty-based mechanism, or other international human rights institutions.

LWPA 590.title: International Economic Law
LWPA 590.subject: LWPA
LWPA 590.description: Problem-based course teaches theory and practice of interrelated global private regulation and public development consequences, as situated in cross-border transactions and dispute resolution in world law, international investment law, and international financial law.

LWPA 594.title: Pacific Islands Legal Systems
LWPA 594.subject: LWPA
LWPA 594.description: Study of substantive rules of one or more Pacific Islands jurisdictions, development of legal systems, relationship of legal systems to culture and tradition.

LWPA 596.title: International Intellectual Property
LWPA 596.subject: LWPA
LWPA 596.description: Primer on the World Intellectual Property Organization and the treaties it administers. Will explore the various international legislative and judicial developments in intellectual property as well as analyze international methods to harmonize several regional and national laws to protect rights in trademarks, patents, and copyrights. Students will be exposed to issues of territoriality and jurisdiction, international antitrust issues, and international dispute resolution, and human rights implications of international intellectual property rights protections.

LWUL 501.title: American Legal Systems
LWUL 501.subject: LWUL
LWUL 501.description: Introduces foundational concepts in American legal systems. Engages students in legal analysis and techniques of legal advocacy.
LWUL 501.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Ulu Lehua Scholars only.

LWUL 502.title: American Legal Systems II
LWUL 502.subject: LWUL
LWUL 502.description: Introduces conceptual and historical foundations of systems of public and private ordering in the U.S. and its territories. Subjects include federalism, constitutional democracy, separation of powers, and the common law.

MAO 101.title: Beginning Maori I
MAO 101.subject: MAO
MAO 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets three hours weekly.

MAO 102.title: Beginning Maori II
MAO 102.subject: MAO
MAO 102.description: Continuation of MAO 101 . Meets three hours weekly.

MAO 201.title: Intermediate Maori I
MAO 201.subject: MAO
MAO 201.description: Continuation of MAO 102 . Meets three hours weekly.

MAO 202.title: Intermediate Maori II
MAO 202.subject: MAO
MAO 202.description: Continuation of MAO 201 . Meets three hours weekly.

MAO 261.title: Maori Literature and Culture
MAO 261.subject: MAO
MAO 261.description: Survey of literature concerning myths, traditions, poetry and song as well as contemporary literature (in English) relating to the Treaty of Waitangi, Maori prophetic sayings. Students who have previously taken this course as PACS 492 may not take this course.

MAO 361.title: Modern Maori Literature and Culture
MAO 361.subject: MAO
MAO 361.description: Survey of modern Maori and Hawaiian literature and culture from the mid-twentieth and early twenty-first centuries.

MAO 384.title: Te Reo Waiata: Mâori Language in Song
MAO 384.subject: MAO
MAO 384.description: Survey and analysis of Maori song poetry texts, traditional and contemporary, and their development and performance over time.

MAO 401.title: Fourth-Level Maori I
MAO 401.subject: MAO
MAO 401.description: Continuation of MAO 302 . Conducted in Maori. Advanced reading, writing, and conversation. Cultural contemporary and historical topics.

MAO 402.title: Fourth-Level Maori II
MAO 402.subject: MAO
MAO 402.description: Continuation of MAO 401 . Conducted in Maori. Advanced reading, writing, and conversation. Cultural contemporary and historical topics.

MATH 100.title: Survey of Mathematics
MATH 100.subject: MATH
MATH 100.description: Selected topics designed to acquaint non-specialists with examples of mathematical reasoning. May not be taken for credit after MATH 215 or higher.

MATH 111.title: Math for Elementary Teachers I
MATH 111.subject: MATH
MATH 111.description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas, problem solving, and reasoning. Number systems, place value, fractions, and properties of operations. Prospective elementary education majors only.

MATH 112.title: Math for Elementary Teachers II
MATH 112.subject: MATH
MATH 112.description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas; problem solving; reasoning and proof; and using symbolism. Patterns and algebraic thinking, place value and decimals, geometry, and mathematical modeling.

MATH 134.title: Precalculus: Elementary Functions
MATH 134.subject: MATH
MATH 134.description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational exponential and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing.
MATH 134.prereq_raw: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry.

prereq_tree.text: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry

MATH 140X.title: Precalculus
MATH 140X.subject: MATH
MATH 140X.description: Algebra review. Polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing. Trigonometric function, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, and related topics.
MATH 140X.prereq_raw: MATH 134 or MATH 161 or assessment exam.

MATH 161.title: Precalculus and Elements of Calculus for Economics and the Social Sciences
MATH 161.subject: MATH
MATH 161.description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, algebra of functions, techniques of graphing, differentiation and integration of algebraic functions, applications in economics and social sciences.

MATH 190.title: Introduction to Programming
MATH 190.subject: MATH
MATH 190.description: (3 hr) Introduction to numerical algorithms and structured programming using Fortran, MATLAB, or other appropriate language.
MATH 190.prereq_raw: one semester of calculus ( MATH 203 , MATH 215 , MATH 241 , MATH 242 , MATH 243 , MATH 244 , MATH 251A , MATH 252A , or MATH 253A ) (or concurrent), or consent.

MATH 203.title: Calculus for Business and Social Sciences
MATH 203.subject: MATH
MATH 203.description: Basic concepts; differentiation and integration applications to management, finance, economics, and the social sciences.
MATH 203.prereq_raw: MATH 134 or MATH 161 , or placement exam.

MATH 215.title: Applied Calculus I
MATH 215.subject: MATH
MATH 215.description: Basic concepts; differentiation, differential equations and integration with applications directed primarily to the life sciences.

MATH 216.title: Applied Calculus II
MATH 216.subject: MATH
MATH 216.description: Differential calculus for functions in several variables and curves, systems of ordinary differential equations, series approximation of functions, continuous probability, exposure to use of calculus in the literature.

MATH 241.title: Calculus I
MATH 241.subject: MATH
MATH 241.description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration.
MATH 241.prereq_raw: MATH 140X or MATH 215 or placement exam.

MATH 242.title: Calculus II
MATH 242.subject: MATH
MATH 242.description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations,
MATH 242.prereq_raw: MATH 241 or MATH 251A or a grade of B or better in MATH 215 ; or consent.

children.text: a grade of B or better in MATH 215

MATH 243.title: Calculus III
MATH 243.subject: MATH
MATH 243.description: Vector algebra, vector-valued functions, differentiation in several variables, and optimization.

MATH 244.title: Calculus IV
MATH 244.subject: MATH
MATH 244.description: Multiple integrals; line integrals and Green’s Theorem; surface integrals, Stokes’s and Gauss’s Theorems.

MATH 251A.title: Accelerated Calculus I
MATH 251A.subject: MATH
MATH 251A.description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Compared to 241, topics are discussed in greater depth.
MATH 251A.prereq_raw: assessment and consent, or a grade of A in MATH 140X and consent.

children.text: a grade of A in MATH 140X

MATH 252A.title: Accelerated Calculus II
MATH 252A.subject: MATH
MATH 252A.description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations, introduction to vectors.
MATH 252A.prereq_raw: MATH 251A (with a minimum grade of B) or MATH 241 (with a minimum grade of A and consent).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of A and consent )

MATH 253A.title: Accelerated Calculus III
MATH 253A.subject: MATH
MATH 253A.description: Vector calculus; maxima and minima in several variables; multiple integrals; line integrals, surface integrals and their applications.
MATH 253A.prereq_raw: MATH 252A with a grade of B or better, or consent.

MATH 257.title: History of Mathematics
MATH 257.subject: MATH
MATH 257.description: The historical development of mathematical thought.

MATH 301.title: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
MATH 301.subject: MATH
MATH 301.description: Symbolic logic, sets and relations, algorithms, trees and other graphs. Additional topics chosen from algebraic systems, networks, automata.
MATH 301.prereq_raw: one semester of calculus from mathematics department; or consent. Recommended: one semester programming.

children.text: one semester of calculus from mathematics department;

MATH 302.title: Introduction to Differential Equations I
MATH 302.subject: MATH
MATH 302.description: First order ordinary differential equations, constant coefficient linear equations, oscillations, Laplace transform, convolution, Green’s function.
MATH 302.prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent), or consent.

MATH 303.title: Introduction to Differential Equations II
MATH 303.subject: MATH
MATH 303.description: Constant coefficient linear systems, variable coefficient ordinary differential equations, series solutions and special functions, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

MATH 304.title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models
MATH 304.subject: MATH
MATH 304.description: Deterministic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include difference equations, qualitative behavior solutions of ODEs and reaction-diffusion equations. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.
MATH 304.prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A , or consent.

MATH 305.title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models
MATH 305.subject: MATH
MATH 305.description: Probabilistic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include stochastic and Poisson processes, Markov models, estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.
MATH 305.prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A , or consent.

MATH 307.title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
MATH 307.subject: MATH
MATH 307.description: Introduction to linear algebra, application of eigenvalue techniques to the solution of differential equations. Students may receive credit for only one of MATH 307 or MATH 311 .

MATH 311.title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
MATH 311.subject: MATH
MATH 311.description: Algebra of matrices, linear equations, real vector spaces and transformations. Emphasis on concepts and abstraction and instruction of careful writing. Students may receive credit for only one of MATH 307 or MATH 311.

MATH 321.title: Introduction to Advanced Mathematics
MATH 321.subject: MATH
MATH 321.description: Formal introduction to the concepts of logic, finite and infinite sets, functions, methods of proof and axiomatic systems. Learning mathematical expressions in writing is an integral part of the course.

MATH 331.title: Introduction to Real Analysis
MATH 331.subject: MATH
MATH 331.description: A rigorous axiomatic development of one variable calculus. Completeness, topology of the line, limits, continuity, differentiation, integration. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing.
MATH 331.prereq_raw: MATH 242 or MATH 252A , and MATH 321 ; or consent.

MATH 351.title: Foundation of Euclidean Geometry
MATH 351.subject: MATH
MATH 351.description: Axiomatic Euclidean geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method.
MATH 351.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 321 (or concurrent); or consent.

MATH 353.title: Introduction to Euclidean and Non- Euclidean Geometries
MATH 353.subject: MATH
MATH 353.description: Axiomatic geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method; Euclidean geometry; hyperbolic geometry, and other non-Euclidean geometries.
MATH 353.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 321 (or concurrent); or consent.

MATH 370.title: Financial Mathematics
MATH 370.subject: MATH
MATH 370.description: Interest rate measurement, valuation of annuities, loan repayment, bond valuation, rate of return. Term structure of interest rates, cashflow duration, and immunization. Financial mathematics actuarial exam topics.
MATH 370.prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A or ( MATH 203 and BUS 250 ).

MATH 371.title: Elementary Probability Theory
MATH 371.subject: MATH
MATH 371.description: Sets, discrete sample spaces, problems in combinatorial probability, random variables, mathematical expectations, classical distributions, applications.
MATH 371.prereq_raw: MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A ; or consent.

MATH 372.title: Elementary Probability and Statistics
MATH 372.subject: MATH
MATH 372.description: Problem-oriented introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics, providing a foundation for applications and further study.
MATH 372.prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A or consent.

MATH 373.title: Elementary Statistics
MATH 373.subject: MATH
MATH 373.description: Estimation, tests of significance, the concept of power.

MATH 402.title: Partial Differential Equations I
MATH 402.subject: MATH
MATH 402.description: Integral surfaces and characteristics of first and second order partial differential equations. Applications to the equations of mathematical physics.
MATH 402.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , or consent. Recommended: MATH 244 and MATH 302 .

MATH 403.title: Partial Differential Equations II
MATH 403.subject: MATH
MATH 403.description: Laplace’s equation, Fourier transform methods for PDEs, higher dimensional PDEs, spherical harmonics, Laplace series, special functions and applications.

MATH 405.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
MATH 405.subject: MATH
MATH 405.description: Systems of linear ordinary differential equations, autonomous systems, and stability theory applications. Optional topics include series solutions, Sturm theory, numerical methods.

MATH 407.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 407.subject: MATH
MATH 407.description: Numerical solution of equations, interpolation, least-squares approximation, quadrature, eigenvalue problems, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 407- MATH 408 .)
MATH 407.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 , and one semester programming; or consent.

MATH 408.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 408.subject: MATH
MATH 408.description: Continuation of MATH 407 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 407 .

MATH 411.title: Linear Algebra
MATH 411.subject: MATH
MATH 411.description: Vector spaces over arbitrary fields, minimal polynomials, invariant subspaces, canonical forms of matrices; unitary and Hermitian matrices, quadratic forms.
MATH 411.prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 , and MATH 321 ; or consent.

MATH 412.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
MATH 412.subject: MATH
MATH 412.description: Introduction to basic algebraic structures. Groups, finite groups, abelian groups, rings, integral domains, fields, factorization, polynomial rings, field extensions, quotient fields. Emphasis on writing instruction. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 412- MATH 413 .)

MATH 413.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
MATH 413.subject: MATH
MATH 413.description: Continuation of MATH 412 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 412. Emphasis on writing instruction.

MATH 414.title: Optimization: Theory & Methods
MATH 414.subject: MATH
MATH 414.description: Introduction to theory and methods for optimization. Topics may include least square analysis, search methods, conjugate direction methods, linear programming, integer programming, and constrained optimization.
MATH 414.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 ; or consent.

MATH 420.title: Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
MATH 420.subject: MATH
MATH 420.description: Congruences, quadratic residues, arithmetic functions, distribution of primes. Emphasis is on teaching theory and writing, not on computation.

MATH 421.title: Topology
MATH 421.subject: MATH
MATH 421.description: General topology, including compactness and connectedness; the Jordan Curve Theorem and the classification of surfaces; first homotopy or homology groups.

MATH 431.title: Principles of Analysis I
MATH 431.subject: MATH
MATH 431.description: Topology of Rn, metric spaces, continuous functions, Riemann integration, sequences and series, uniform convergence, implicit function theorems, differentials and Jacobians. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 431-432.)
MATH 431.prereq_raw: MATH 311 , MATH 321 , and MATH 331 ; or consent.

MATH 432.title: Principles of Analysis II
MATH 432.subject: MATH
MATH 432.description: Continuation of MATH 431 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 431 . Emphasis on writing instruction continues.

MATH 442.title: Vector Analysis
MATH 442.subject: MATH
MATH 442.description: Vector operations, wedge product, differential forms, and smooth mappings. Theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss, both classically and in terms of forms. Applications to electromagnetism and mechanics.
MATH 442.prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 , or consent.

MATH 443.title: Differential Geometry
MATH 443.subject: MATH
MATH 443.description: Properties and fundamental geometric invariants of curves and surfaces in space; applications to the physical sciences.
MATH 443.prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , and MATH 311 ; or consent.

MATH 444.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 444.subject: MATH
MATH 444.description: Analytic functions, complex integration, introduction to conformal mapping.
MATH 444.prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; recommended MATH 331 ; or consent.

MATH 449.title: Topics in Undergraduate Mathematics
MATH 449.subject: MATH
MATH 449.description: Advanced topics from various areas: algebra, number theory, analysis, and geometry.

MATH 454.title: Axiomatic Set Theory
MATH 454.subject: MATH
MATH 454.description: Sets, relations, ordinal arithmetic, cardinal arithmetic, axiomatic set theory, axiom of choice and the continuum hypothesis.
MATH 454.prereq_raw: MATH 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent.

children.text: in a related field or consent

MATH 455.title: Mathematical Logic
MATH 455.subject: MATH
MATH 455.description: A system of first order logic. Formal notions of well-formed formula, proof, and derivability. Semantic notions of model, truth, and validity. Completeness theorem.
MATH 455.prereq_raw: MATH 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent. Recommended: 454.

children.text: in a related field or consent . Recommended: 454

MATH 471.title: Probability
MATH 471.subject: MATH
MATH 471.description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectations, moment-generating and characteristic functions, limit theorems. Continuous probability emphasized.
MATH 471.prereq_raw: MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent), or consent. Recommended: MATH 305 or MATH 371 or MATH 372 ; or consent.

children.text: Recommended: MATH 305 or MATH 371 or MATH 372 ; or consent

MATH 472.title: Statistical Inference
MATH 472.subject: MATH
MATH 472.description: Sampling and parameter estimation, tests of hypotheses, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, sequential analysis, rank order statistics.

MATH 475.title: Combinatorial Mathematics
MATH 475.subject: MATH
MATH 475.description: Finite configurations. Topics may include counting methods, generating functions, graph theory, map coloring, block design, network flows, analysis of discrete algorithms.

MATH 480.title: Senior Seminar
MATH 480.subject: MATH
MATH 480.description: Seminar for senior mathematics majors, including an introduction to methods of research. Significant portion of class time is dedicated to the instruction and critique of oral presentations. All students must give the equivalent of three presentations.

MATH 490.title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
MATH 490.subject: MATH
MATH 490.description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
MATH 490.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher and consent.

MATH 499.title: Directed Reading
MATH 499.subject: MATH
MATH 499.description: Limited to advanced students who must arrange with an instructor before enrolling.

MATH 511.title: Problem Solving for Teachers
MATH 511.subject: MATH
MATH 511.description: Practicing teachers develop and improve their problem-solving skills by working on challenging mathematical tasks. Students improve their mathematics content knowledge by working on problems and learning to design challenge problems for their own classes. Practicing teachers in grades K-12 only.

MATH 600B.title: Career Skills for Graduate Students in Mathematics: teaching
MATH 600B.subject: MATH
MATH 600B.description: Seminar addresses issues important in the career of a mathematician, beginning from their time in graduate school, through navigating the job market and on to their eventual work in industry or academia. (B) teaching.
MATH 600B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MATH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 601.title: Applied Dynamical Systems
MATH 601.subject: MATH
MATH 601.description: Continuous and discrete dynamical systems; bifurcation theory; chaotic maps. Additional topics from PDEs and linear algebra.
MATH 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 602.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
MATH 602.subject: MATH
MATH 602.description: Linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations. Topics include spectral theory, matrix exponentiation, initial-value problems, dynamical systems, bifurcation theory, first-order PDEs, characteristics, Sturm-Liouville theory, boundary-value problems, Green’s functions.

MATH 603.title: Partial Differential Equations
MATH 603.subject: MATH
MATH 603.description: Classical existence and uniqueness theory for PDEs, qualitative properties, classification, boundary value and initial value problems, fundamental solutions, other topics.

MATH 607.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 607.subject: MATH
MATH 607.description: Numerical linear algebra including iterative methods, SVD, and other matrix factorizations, locating eigenvalues, discrete approximation to partial differential equations. Recommended: MATH 407 , MATH 411 , or consent.

MATH 610.title: Key Elements of Linear Algebra
MATH 610.subject: MATH
MATH 610.description: Key concepts of linear algebra for graduate students in mathematics. Specific topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, multilinear forms, and Jordan decomposition. May not receive credit for both MATH 411 and MATH 610. MATH majors only.
MATH 610.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 611.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 611.subject: MATH
MATH 611.description: Modules, Sylow theorems, Jordan-Holder theorem, unique factorization domains, Galois theory, algebraic closures, transcendence bases. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 611- MATH 612 .)

MATH 612.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 612.subject: MATH
MATH 612.description: Continuation of MATH 611 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 611 .

MATH 613.title: Group Theory
MATH 613.subject: MATH
MATH 613.description: Sylow theorems, solvable groups, nilpotent groups, extension theory, representation theory, additional topics.

MATH 615.title: Commutative Ring Theory
MATH 615.subject: MATH
MATH 615.description: Ideal theory, Noetherian rings, localization, domains, radicals and primes, and additional topics.

MATH 618.title: Lattice Theory
MATH 618.subject: MATH
MATH 618.description: Introduction with applications to general algebra. Partially ordered sets, decomposition theory, representations of lattices, varieties and free lattices, coordinatization of modular lattices.

MATH 619.title: Universal Algebra
MATH 619.subject: MATH
MATH 619.description: Introduction to basic techniques, including subalgebras, congruences, automorphisms and endomorphisms, varieties of algebras, Mal’cev conditions.

MATH 620.title: Key Elements of Topology
MATH 620.subject: MATH
MATH 620.description: Key concepts of Topology for graduate students in mathematics; topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; continuity. MATH majors only.
MATH 620.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 621.title: Topology
MATH 621.subject: MATH
MATH 621.description: Properties of topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; metrizability; convergence and continuity. Additional topics from general and algebraic topology. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 621- MATH 622 .)

MATH 622.title: Topology
MATH 622.subject: MATH
MATH 622.description: Continuation of MATH 621 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 621 .

MATH 623.title: Geometric Group Theory
MATH 623.subject: MATH
MATH 623.description: Geometric, topological, and dynamical methods in the study of finitely generated infinite groups.
MATH 623.prereq_raw: MATH 621 (with a minimum grade of B-).
MATH 623.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 625.title: Differentiable Manifolds I
MATH 625.subject: MATH
MATH 625.description: Differentiable structures on manifolds, tensor fields, Frobenius theorem, exterior algebra, integration of forms, Poincare Lemma, Stoke’s theorem.

MATH 631.title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
MATH 631.subject: MATH
MATH 631.description: Lebesgue measure and integral, convergence of integrals, functions of bounded variation, Lebesgue- Stieltjes integral and more general theory of measure and integration. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 631-632.)

MATH 632.title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
MATH 632.subject: MATH
MATH 632.description: Continuation of MATH 631 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 631 .

MATH 633.title: Functional Analysis
MATH 633.subject: MATH
MATH 633.description: Linear topological spaces, normed spaces, Hilbert spaces, function algebras, operator theory.

MATH 637.title: Calculus of Variations
MATH 637.subject: MATH
MATH 637.description: Simple variational problems, first and second variation formulas. Euler-Lagrange equation, direct methods, optimal control.

MATH 644.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 644.subject: MATH
MATH 644.description: Conformal mapping, residue theory, series and product developments, analytic continuation, special functions. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 644- MATH 645 .)

MATH 645.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 645.subject: MATH
MATH 645.description: Continuation of MATH 644 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 644 .

MATH 649B.title: Topics in Mathematics: logic
MATH 649B.subject: MATH
MATH 649B.description: (B) logic; (D) analysis; (E) commutative rings; (F) function theory; (G) geometric topology; (H) operator theory; ((I) probability; (J) algebra; (K) special; (M) lattice theory and universal algebra; (N) noncommutative rings; (O) transformation groups; (P) partial differential equations; (Q) potential theory; (R) algebraic topology; (S) functional analysis; (T) number theory and combinatorics; (U) differentiable manifolds II.

MATH 654.title: Introduction to Logic
MATH 654.subject: MATH
MATH 654.description: Model theory, computability theory, set theory. In particular syntax and semantics of first order logic; incompleteness, completeness, and compactness theorems; Loewenheim- Skolem theorems; computable and computably enumerable sets; axioms of set theory; ordinals and cardinals.
MATH 654.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 655.title: Set Theory
MATH 655.subject: MATH
MATH 655.description: Axiomatic development, ordinal and cardinal numbers, recursion theorems, axiom of choice, continuum hypothesis, consistency and independence results.

MATH 657.title: Recursive Functions and Complexity
MATH 657.subject: MATH
MATH 657.description: Recursive, r.e., Ptime, and Logspace classes. Nondeterminism, parallelism, alternation, and Boolean circuits. Reducibility and completeness.

MATH 661.title: Introduction to Algebraic Number Theory
MATH 661.subject: MATH
MATH 661.description: Number fields and rings of integers; primes, factorization, and ramification theory; finiteness of the class group; Dirichlet’s Unit Theorem; valuations, completions, and local fields. Further topics.
MATH 661.prereq_raw: MATH 611 (with a minimum grade of B-).
MATH 661.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MATH 671.title: Advanced Probability
MATH 671.subject: MATH
MATH 671.description: Independence and conditioning, martingales, ergodic theory, Markov chains, central limit theorem.
MATH 671.prereq_raw: MATH 631 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

MATH 672.title: Stochastic Processes
MATH 672.subject: MATH
MATH 672.prereq_raw: MATH 671 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

MATH 681.title: Graph Theory
MATH 681.subject: MATH
MATH 681.description: Connected graphs and digraphs. Graph embeddings. Connectivity and networks. Factors and factorizations. Coverings. Coloring. Applications.

MATH 695.title: Directed Reading and Research for Plan B Masters Students
MATH 695.subject: MATH
MATH 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in MATH.

MATH 799.title: Apprenticeship in Teaching
MATH 799.subject: MATH
MATH 799.description: An experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation. Open to graduate students in mathematics only.
MATH 799.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in mathematics and consent.

MBBE 304.title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
MBBE 304.subject: MBBE
MBBE 304.description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering.
MBBE 304.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

MBBE 375.title: Essential Biochemistry
MBBE 375.subject: MBBE
MBBE 375.description: Introduction to basic concepts of cellular biochemistry and metabolic pathways as applied to nutritional, medicinal and environmental biochemistry.
MBBE 375.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 152 or CHEM 272 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

MBBE 401.title: Molecular Biotechnology
MBBE 401.subject: MBBE
MBBE 401.description: General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues.
MBBE 401.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 or consent.

MBBE 401L.title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
MBBE 401L.subject: MBBE
MBBE 401L.description: (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany MBBE 401 . Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
MBBE 401L.prereq_raw: MBBE 304 , or MBBE 375 , or BIOL 275L , or BIOL 375L ; or consent.

MBBE 402.title: Principles of Biochemistry
MBBE 402.subject: MBBE
MBBE 402.description: Molecular basis of living processes in bacteria, plants and animals; emphasis on metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids.
MBBE 402.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L , CHEM 272 and CHEM 273 ; or consent.

MBBE 402L.title: Principles of Biochemistry Lab
MBBE 402L.subject: MBBE
MBBE 402L.description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles and techniques of biochemical laboratory. Teaches biochemistry laboratory methods as well as technical writing in the form of experimental reports.
MBBE 402L.prereq_raw: ( MBBE 402 (or concurrent), BIOL 402 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.

MBBE 405.title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
MBBE 405.subject: MBBE
MBBE 405.description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology.

MBBE 408.title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
MBBE 408.subject: MBBE
MBBE 408.description: Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules.
MBBE 408.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 407 ; or consent.

MBBE 411.title: Food Engineering
MBBE 411.subject: MBBE
MBBE 411.description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
MBBE 411.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 , CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

MBBE 412.title: Environmental Biochemistry
MBBE 412.subject: MBBE
MBBE 412.description: Biochemical and chemical principles of occurrence, distribution, biotic and abiotic conversion, fate, and impact of synthetic and natural molecules in the environment. Important pollutants will be used as case studies to illustrate the principles.

MBBE 422.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
MBBE 422.subject: MBBE
MBBE 422.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
MBBE 422.prereq_raw: ( ECE 160 , ECE 211 , and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

MBBE 447.title: Artificial Intelligence for Bioprocesses
MBBE 447.subject: MBBE
MBBE 447.description: Explores how artificial intelligence can be integrated with bioprocess techniques. Using real-world data and hands-on coding, delves into how machine learning can be used to generate practical insights.
MBBE 447.prereq_raw: (MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A and ECE 110 or ECE 160 or ICS 111) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

MBBE 451.title: Synthetic Biology
MBBE 451.subject: MBBE
MBBE 451.description: Introduction to principles, tools, and applications of synthetic biology; molecular techniques and design/analysis of synthetic gene circuits, synthetic-biology parts/devices, CRISPR-based systems, engineered microbial cell factories, for industrial, agricultural, medical applications.
MBBE 451.prereq_raw: ( PHYS 152 (or PHYS 272 ), BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

children.text: ( or PHYS 272 ) , BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L ) with a minimum grade of C ; or consent

MBBE 460.title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
MBBE 460.subject: MBBE
MBBE 460.description: Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures.
MBBE 460.prereq_raw: ME 322 (with a minimum grade of C-) or BE 373 or CEE 320 ; or consent.

MBBE 461.title: Biotechnology for Teachers
MBBE 461.subject: MBBE
MBBE 461.description: Principles, methods, classical examples, recent development, benefits and concerns of modern biotechnology.

MBBE 483.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Topics for Biologists
MBBE 483.subject: MBBE
MBBE 483.description: Focuses on the use of computational tools and approaches to analyze the enormous amount of biological data (DNA, RNA, protein) available today.
MBBE 483.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 (or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

MBBE 491.title: Special Topics in MBBE
MBBE 491.subject: MBBE
MBBE 491.description: Study and discussion of special topics and problems in molecular biosciences and bioengineering.

MBBE 499.title: Directed Research
MBBE 499.subject: MBBE
MBBE 499.description: Supervised individual instruction in laboratory research problems in biochemistry, molecular and cellular biology, genomics, and genetics.
MBBE 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Limited to qualified undergraduate students.

MBBE 601.title: Molecular Cell Biology
MBBE 601.subject: MBBE
MBBE 601.description: Provide fundamental concepts and dynamic characteristics of the molecules of the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell, their biosynthesis and regulation, and the mechanisms that regulate cellular activities.
MBBE 601.prereq_raw: basic course in cell and molecular biology, or consent.

MBBE 602.title: Molecular Biology and Genetics
MBBE 602.subject: MBBE
MBBE 602.description: Graduate-level basic course on molecular biology and genetics. Prepares students to understand advanced concepts in related subjects such as biochemistry, cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, plant genetics, and genomics.
MBBE 602.prereq_raw: MBBE 402 / BIOL 402 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or with consent from instructor.

MBBE 607.title: Advanced Food Science I
MBBE 607.subject: MBBE
MBBE 607.description: Advanced topics in chemical and physical characteristics of foods as well as their role in human nutrition.
MBBE 607.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent.

MBBE 611.title: Professional Development

MBBE 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MBBE 620.title: Plant Biochemistry
MBBE 620.subject: MBBE
MBBE 620.description: Comprehensive study of chemical constituents and biochemical processes unique to the plant kingdom with emphasis on selected aspects of current interest.
MBBE 620.prereq_raw: MBBE 402 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

MBBE 621.title: Metabolic Engineering
MBBE 621.subject: MBBE
MBBE 621.description: Principles and methodologies of metabolic engineering. Concepts of metabolic networks. Establishment of metabolic flux analysis and metabolic control analysis. Systems biology framework for integration of mathematical modeling and global measurements at metabolite, protein and transcription levels.
MBBE 621.prereq_raw: BIOL 275 , MATH 311 , and MICR 351 ; or consent.

MBBE 625.title: Biological Instrumentation
MBBE 625.subject: MBBE
MBBE 625.description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers.

MBBE 627.title: Molecular Diagnostics: Principles and Practices
MBBE 627.subject: MBBE
MBBE 627.description: Molecular diagnostics principles, comparative genomics, genome annotation and bio-informatics, phylogenetics, gene target selection, advanced primer, and probe design.
MBBE 627.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

MBBE 647.title: Advanced Artificial lntelligence for Bioprocesses
MBBE 647.subject: MBBE
MBBE 647.description: Explores how artificial intelligence can be used to analyze biological systems. Emphasizes data-driven model development, algorithm selection, and interpretation of machine learning outputs.

MBBE 650.title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
MBBE 650.subject: MBBE
MBBE 650.description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.
MBBE 650.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

MBBE 651.title: Signal Transduction and Regulation of Gene Transcription
MBBE 651.subject: MBBE
MBBE 651.description: Lecture/discussion on molecular mechanisms involved in the transmission of regulatory signals from the cell surface to the nucleus.
MBBE 651.prereq_raw: undergraduate level biochemistry, molecular biology, biology, nutrition; or override/consent by professor.

MBBE 652.title: Molecular Plant-Fungal Interactions
MBBE 652.subject: MBBE
MBBE 652.description: Focuses on the actions of plant pathogenic fungi/ oomycetes and their host responses at the molecular and cellular level. Current genetic and genomic approaches to study plant-fungal interactions will be discussed. Graduate standing only.

MBBE 666.title: Fermentation Biochemistry - Theory, Practice, Competency, and Application
MBBE 666.subject: MBBE

MBBE 683.subject: MBBE
MBBE 683.description: Teaches problem-solving with bioinformatic tools. MBIO 603.title: Career Skills for Marine Biologists
MBIO 603.subject: MBIO
MBIO 603.description: Introduction to key professional skills including, but not limited to: grant writing, CV preparation, research logistics, data management, reproducible science, peer review, research ethics, publishing, career options, teaching, and professional presentations.

MBIO 604.title: Current Research in Marine Biology

MBIO 610.title: Mathematical Ecology of Marine Systems
MBIO 610.subject: MBIO
MBIO 610.description: Introduction to a broad range of theories and techniques from mathematical ecology with an emphasis on marine systems. Students will learn to assess model assumptions, construct simple models, and apply analytical methods to describe system behavior.
MBIO 610.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

MBIO 611.title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods in Fisheries Science
MBIO 611.subject: MBIO
MBIO 611.description: Fisheries and population models including growth, stock-recruitment, surplus production, age-structured and size-based, parameter estimation, uncertainty characterization, resampling methods, and scientific computing.
MBIO 611.prereq_raw: MATH 215 or MATH 216 , or MATH 241 or MATH 242 , or consent.
MBIO 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MBIO 612.title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
MBIO 612.subject: MBIO
MBIO 612.description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research.

MBIO 620.title: Behavioral Ecology of Coral Reef Fishes
MBIO 620.subject: MBIO
MBIO 620.description: Introduction to processes that affect animal behavior and their significance. Exploring a broad range of techniques for studying behaviors of fishes, students will use new techniques in their own research.
MBIO 620.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

MBIO 621.title: Respiratory Processes in Coral Reef Organisms
MBIO 621.subject: MBIO
MBIO 621.description: Multidisciplinary course introduces the respiratory system of fishes and other reef taxa and its significance for ecology and behavior. Students will learn theory, principles, and hot to design/execute experiments for their own research.
MBIO 621.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

MBIO 630.title: Remote Sensing Applications in Marine Science

MBIO 640.title: Coral Reef Structure and Function
MBIO 640.subject: MBIO
MBIO 640.description: Linking organismal traits and habitat features with ecosystem function. Hands-on course with coral reef fieldwork, exposure to new technology, and the potential to develop independent projects in publications.
MBIO 640.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

This course is designed for students with majors in the natural sciences.
MCB 314.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or concurrent), or MATH 307 (or concurrent), or MATH 311 (or concurrent), or PHYS 170 (or concurrent), or CHEM 272 (or concurrent); or consent.

ME 113.title: Introduction to Engineering Design I
ME 113.subject: ME
ME 113.description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Introductory experience in analysis, synthesis, and design. Teamwork and project required.

ME 201.title: Space Exploration
ME 201.subject: ME
ME 201.description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication.

ME 213.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
ME 213.subject: ME
ME 213.description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Introductory experience in communication, presentation, professional ethics, social responsibility, engineering economics, quality control, and computer-aided drafting. Teamwork and project required.

ME 271.title: Applied Mechanics II
ME 271.subject: ME
ME 271.description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
ME 271.prereq_raw: C or better in CEE 270 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).
ME 271.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only.

ME 301.title: Space Science and Instrumentation
ME 301.subject: ME
ME 301.description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation. Significant oral and written communication is required.
ME 301.prereq_raw: EPET 201 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107 ; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272 .

ME 311.title: Thermodynamics
ME 311.subject: ME
ME 311.description: (3 Lec, 1 Discussion) Basic laws, closed and open systems. Work, heat, concept of entropy. Properties of pure simple substances. Ideal gases. Introduction to power and refrigeration cycles.
ME 311.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A ), PHYS 170 and MATH 244 (or MATH 253A ).

ME 322.subject: ME
ME 322.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Incompressible and compressible ideal fluids, effects of viscosity. Similitude, boundary layer flow. Measurement techniques in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermos-fluid systems. Emphasis on writing instruction.
ME 322.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of ME 311 and CEE 271 (or ME 271 ).

children.text: grade of C or better in all of ME 311

ME 331.title: Materials Science and Engineering
ME 331.subject: ME
ME 331.description: Electronic, atomic, and crystalline structure of materials and their effect on the mechanical, electrical, optical, and magnetic properties of engineering metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
ME 331.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A ), MATH 242 (or MATH 252A ), and PHYS 170 .

ME 341.title: Manufacturing Processes and Lab
ME 341.subject: ME
ME 341.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Energy requirements for manufacturing methods. Manufacturing methods to obtain components with desired size/shape/properties. Conduct manufacturing experiments. Emphasis on writing instruction.

ME 360.title: Computer Methods in Engineering
ME 360.subject: ME
ME 360.description: Numerical solutions for algebraic and transcendental equations, simultaneous linear algebraic equations, integration and differentiation; integration of ordinary differential equations. Engineering applications.
ME 360.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of ECE 160 (or ECE 110 or ICS 111 ), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A ), and MATH 302 (or MATH 307 ).

ME 371.title: Mechanics of Solids
ME 371.subject: ME
ME 371.description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, constitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading.
ME 371.prereq_raw: C or better in all of the following: CEE 270 ; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

ME 372.title: Component Design
ME 372.subject: ME
ME 372.description: Design, analysis, and selection of machine components: shafts, screws, fasteners, welds, rolling contact bearings, journal bearings, gears, clutches, brakes, belts, and roller chains.
ME 372.prereq_raw: ME 213 , and either ME 371 or CEE 370 .

ME 374.title: Kinematics/Dynamics Machinery
ME 374.subject: ME
ME 374.description: Velocity and acceleration analysis of planar mechanisms; kinematic synthesis of linkages, cams, and gears; static and dynamic force analysis of mechanisms; balancing of machinery.
ME 374.prereq_raw: CEE 271 or ME 271 (C or better), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A )and either MATH 302 or MATH 307 .

ME 375.title: Dynamics of Machines and Systems and Lab
ME 375.subject: ME
ME 375.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Lumped-parameter modeling of dynamic systems. Methods of analysis, including transform techniques. Time and frequency response. Feedback control. Engineering instrumentation. Data acquisition. Dynamic measurements. Design and testing. Lab report writing.
ME 375.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (or ME 271 ) and MATH 302 (or MATH 307 ).

ME 400.title: Space Mission Design
ME 400.subject: ME
ME 400.description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission.

ME 401.title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
ME 401.subject: ME
ME 401.description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing.

ME 402.title: Dynamics Systems Laboratory
ME 402.subject: ME
ME 402.description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Analysis, design, fabrication, testing and characterization of engineering instrumentation. Computer-based data acquisition methods. Techniques and procedures associated with carrying out dynamic measurements within the constraints of cost, time and accuracy.
ME 402.prereq_raw: one of ME 360 , MATH 407 , or PHYS 305 (or concurrent for any); and ME 375 (or concurrent).

ME 403.title: Advanced Mathematics for Engineers
ME 403.subject: ME
ME 403.description: Applications of ordinary differential equations, Laplace transform, vector field theory, matrices, line integrals.

ME 404.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
ME 404.subject: ME
ME 404.description: Basic computational fluid dynamics; four important partial differential equations; introduction to finite element method: Interpolation and Galerkin method; finite element method for transport phenomena; some algorithms for parallel computing.
ME 404.prereq_raw: ME 422 (or concurrent ), and either ME 360 , MATH 407 or PHYS 305 ; or consent.

ME 406.title: Orbital Mechanics
ME 406.subject: ME
ME 406.description: Basic theory of orbits of space objects, including spacecraft, small satellites, planets and small planets, and other fundamentals of astrodynamics and applications to aerospace engineering.
ME 406.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: ME 271 ; ME 375 ; MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; MATH 302 or MATH 307 ; ECE 160 or ICS 111 .

children.text: grade of C or better in all of the following: ME 271

ME 406.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ME 408.title: Optimal Control for Aerospace Applications
ME 408.subject: ME
ME 408.description: Fundamentals of optimal control theory and calculus of variations. Application of this theory to aerospace engineering problems, including mission design problems and a wide range of space maneuvers.
ME 408.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: ME 271 ; ME 375 ; MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; MATH 302 or MATH 307 ; ECE 160 or ICS 111 .
