ME 408.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ME 411.title: Applied Thermodynamics
ME 411.subject: ME
ME 411.description: Gas mixtures, generalized thermodynamic relationships, combustion and thermochemistry, chemical equilibrium, power and refrigeration cycles.
ME 411.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in ME 311 .

prereq_tree.text: grade of C or better in ME 311

ME 417.title: Applied Thermal Engineering
ME 417.subject: ME
ME 417.description: Principles, design and analysis of practical thermal systems. Engineering applications. Valve, compressor, condenser and evaporator technologies. System integration and control. Thermal loads and thermal comfort.

ME 418.title: Power and Propulsion
ME 418.subject: ME
ME 418.description: Principles, performance, and design of gas turbine power plants and propulsion systems.

ME 419.title: Astronautics
ME 419.subject: ME
ME 419.description: The space environment (vacuum, neutral, radiation, and plasma); motion in gravitational fields; orbit transfers; Earth-satellite operations; rocketry; propulsion analysis and performance; reentry dynamics; interplanetary trajectories; attitude dynamics and stabilization.

ME 422.title: Heat Transfer and Lab
ME 422.subject: ME
ME 422.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Steady and unsteady conduction; steady convection and radiation; heat exchangers. Emphasis on writing instruction.

ME 423.title: Mass Transfer
ME 423.subject: ME
ME 423.description: Elementary mass diffusion; diffusion in a stationary medium; diffusion in a moving medium; low and high mass transfer theories; simultaneous heat and mass transfer; condensation, evaporation, and boiling; transpiration cooling; species boundary layers; engineering and design of heat and mass exchangers; current refrigerants and environmental regulations.

ME 424.title: Introduction to Gas Dynamics
ME 424.subject: ME
ME 424.description: One-dimensional compressible flow involving change of area, friction, heat transfer. Normal and oblique shocks. Prandtl-Meyer flow. Application to nozzles, diffusers, airfoils.

ME 425.title: Thermal Management of Electronic Systems
ME 425.subject: ME
ME 425.description: To introduce concepts in the thermal management of electronics, and to develop sound technical tools to approach modern electronic packaging and cooling applications.

ME 426.title: Scaling Methods in Engineering
ME 426.subject: ME
ME 426.description: Scaling methods and optimization under global constraints; multi-scale optimal design of mechanical, thermal, and natural systems; effectiveness of heat, fluid, and convective trees; theoretical design optimization of manmade and natural power systems; analysis of time dependent structures.

ME 428.title: Solar Thermal Engineering
ME 428.subject: ME
ME 428.description: Fundamentals of solar energy, solar engineering material characteristics, and solar thermal and photovoltaic systems. Will learn solar thermal system components, and be able to perform simple system design.

ME 433.title: Failures in Materials
ME 433.subject: ME
ME 433.description: Analysis of component failures due to imperfections, fatigue, brittle fracture, wear, corrosion, bending, impact, and overload. Fracture mechanics. Case studies.

ME 434.title: Materials Selection for Design
ME 434.subject: ME
ME 434.description: Methodology for the selection of materials for mechanical applications to prevent mechanical failure and environmental degradation. Design considerations associated with the use of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.

ME 435.title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
ME 435.subject: ME
ME 435.description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods-theory and hands-on experience.

ME 436.title: Corrosion Engineering
ME 436.subject: ME
ME 436.description: Basics of corrosion processes and emphasis on corrosion control. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosion, metal alloys and their behavior, corrosion control techniques (cathodic protection, anodic protection, coatings, and inhibitors).

ME 442.title: Mechatronics
ME 442.subject: ME
ME 442.description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Modern mechatronics components and design principles; functionality of products, processes and systems; electrical circuits and mechanical components; programming and control; hands on technology; application case studies.
ME 442.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME, EE, CE, ICS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or consent.

ME 446.title: Advanced Materials Manufacturing
ME 446.subject: ME
ME 446.description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Introduction to anisotropic materials, advanced manufacturing techniques for composite and intelligent materials, joining of composites, thin film processing and stereolithography, computer aided manufacturing and rapid prototyping, manufacturing process optimization, open-ended manufacturing projects.
ME 446.prereq_raw: ME 341 , and senior standing; or consent.

ME 447.title: Introduction to Nanotechnology
ME 447.subject: ME
ME 447.description: (3 Lec) Tools and techniques of micro- and nano-technology in design, modeling, simulations, analysis, fabrication, testing and characterization; nano-materials, nanostructures, nano-composites, nano-coating, nano-optics, nano-electronics and nano-biotechnology.
ME 447.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

ME 448.title: Nanosystem and Microsystem Design
ME 448.subject: ME
ME 448.description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale. Microfabrication/nanofabrication, fabrication process design, electrostatistic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, measurements. Course work will focus on process and system design.
ME 448.prereq_raw: ME 331 (with a minimum grade of C-), ME 375 (with a minimum grade of C-), or consent.

ME 450.title: Research Methods in Engineering
ME 450.subject: ME
ME 450.description: Introduces the basic skills of preparing and publishing scientific research. Students will learn how to prepare, write, publish, and present a scientific paper, while working on a research project related to thermofluids.

ME 451.title: Feedback-Control Systems
ME 451.subject: ME
ME 451.description: Analysis/ design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

ME 452.title: Robotics
ME 452.subject: ME
ME 452.description: Principles and design methods for autonomous systems.

ME 453.title: Energy Conversion Systems
ME 453.subject: ME
ME 453.description: Energy conversion and its impact on the environment. Conventional, hydroelectric, nuclear fission and fusion, solar, wind, ocean, geothermal, and biomass power; energy storage, transmission and conservation.
ME 453.prereq_raw: ME 322 , ME 411 , and ME 422 (or concurrent); or consent.

ME 454.title: Introduction to Nuclear Energy & Engineering
ME 454.subject: ME
ME 454.description: Covers the fundamentals of nuclear energy and engineering principles as applied to the operation of nuclear reactors and the design of reactors for electrical power generation.
ME 454.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME, ECE, CE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

ME 455.title: Nuclear Power Engineering
ME 455.subject: ME
ME 455.description: Nuclear reactor principles. Reactor heat transfer, heat generation and removal. Design and analysis of reactor power systems and plants.

ME 463.title: Flow Visualization and Measurement
ME 463.subject: ME
ME 463.description: Overview of flow visualization and measurement techniques including high speed photography of wakes, jets, shear layer, particle motion. Experimental design, statistics, image processing and data analysis. Junior standing or higher.

ME 465.title: Materials for Solar Energy Conversion
ME 465.subject: ME
ME 465.description: Atom structure, electromagnetic waves and energy, electronic and energetic properties of semi-conducting materials, junctions, solar cells operations, bulk and thin film materials synthesis, integration of solar cells into the electric grid.
ME 465.prereq_raw: ( ME 331 or ECE 324 ) with a minimum grade of C-.
ME 465.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE and ME majors only.

ME 466.title: Electrochemical Power Sources: Principles, Applications, and Sustainability
ME 466.subject: ME
ME 466.description: Electrochemistry, batteries, fuel cells, flow batteries, electrochemical capacitors, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage.
ME 466.prereq_raw: ME 331 , CHEM 162 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A (with a grade of C- or better).

ME 471.title: Experimental Stress Analysis
ME 471.subject: ME
ME 471.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Techniques of experimental stress analysis: strain and deflection measurement of beams and shafts, strain to stress conversion, principal and maximum shearing stresses, failure in biaxial stress states, stress concentrations, residual stresses, buckling, creep, electrical resistance strain gages, brittle coatings, photoelastic methods, transducers.

ME 473.title: Mechanical Vibrations
ME 473.subject: ME
ME 473.description: Response of machines and systems to transient and periodic excitation. Vibration isolation and transmissibility. Modal analysis of multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Applications to design.

ME 474.title: Fundamentals of Acoustics
ME 474.subject: ME
ME 474.description: Plane and spherical acoustic waves. Transmission, reflection, radiation, and absorption. Near and far fields, radiation patterns. Applications to noise control. Instruments.

ME 480.title: Thermofluid Measurements and Design
ME 480.subject: ME
ME 480.description: Measurement techniques in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Contemporary engineering ethics issues. Final report and presentation are required.

ME 481.title: Design Project I
ME 481.subject: ME
ME 481.description: (2 1-hr Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Heuristic application of engineering design process and project planning via a significant, open-ended design project that includes realistic constraints involving economics, environmental sustainability, manufacturability, ethics, health, safety, society, and politics. Extensive written communication required.
ME 481.prereq_raw: ME 322 , ME 341 , ME 372 , and ME 375 ; or consent.

ME 482.title: Design Project II
ME 482.subject: ME
ME 482.description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Continuation of design project initiated in ME 481 . Extension of conceptual design to final design. Manufacturing of prototype: material and part selection, procurement, manufacturing specifications/ drawings. Testing of complex systems. Extensive oral communication required.

ME 483.title: Research and Experiment Design
ME 483.subject: ME
ME 483.description: Introduction to research and experimentation via pursuit and reporting of an open-ended design project. Ethical issues in research and experimentation.
ME 483.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering, Biological Engineering, and Ocean & Resources Engineering majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

ME 485.title: System Engineering
ME 485.subject: ME
ME 485.description: Will cover system engineering design, analysis, and development concepts, requirements derivation/management, and program management processes, such as risk identification/ management and fiscal/schedule tools. Senior standing or higher.
ME 485.prereq_raw: ME 213 (with a minimum grade of C).

ME 487.title: Pearl Harbor co-op
ME 487.subject: ME
ME 487.description: Provides real-world engineering experience through project assignment and working alongside a practicing engineer at the Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard. Senior standing or higher.
ME 487.prereq_raw: ( ME 322 , ME 341 , ME 372 , and ME 375 ) with a minimum grade of C.

ME 490B.title: Mentored Projects: Design Project I
ME 490B.subject: ME
ME 490B.description: Investigation of advanced problems, making use of faculty expertise for specific domains of work. (B) Design Project I; (C) Design Project II; (D) Research and Experiment Design.
ME 490B.coreq_raw: ME 481 for (B); ME 482 for (C); ME 483 for (D).
ME 490B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior or senior standing only.

ME 490C.title: Mentored Projects: Design Project II
ME 490C.subject: ME
ME 490C.description: Investigation of advanced problems, making use of faculty expertise for specific domains of work. (B) Design Project I; (C) Design Project II; (D) Research and Experiment Design.
ME 490C.coreq_raw: ME 481 for (B); ME 482 for (C); ME 483 for (D).
ME 490C.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior or senior standing only.

ME 490D.title: Mentored Projects: Research and Experiment Design
ME 490D.subject: ME
ME 490D.description: Investigation of advanced problems, making use of faculty expertise for specific domains of work. (B) Design Project I; (C) Design Project II; (D) Research and Experiment Design.
ME 490D.coreq_raw: ME 481 for (B); ME 482 for (C); ME 483 for (D).
ME 490D.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior or senior standing only.

ME 491.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
ME 491.subject: ME
ME 491.description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

ME 492.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
ME 492.subject: ME
ME 492.description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

ME 499.title: Project
ME 499.subject: ME
ME 499.description: Investigation of advanced problems in mechanical engineering design or development. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering.

ME 610.title: Renewable Energy Engineering and Sustainability
ME 610.subject: ME
ME 610.description: Analysis of principles of operation of renewable energy systems, and its interactions with sustainability. Fundamentals of renewable energy production, storage, and distribution.

ME 611.title: Advanced Thermodynamics
ME 611.subject: ME
ME 611.description: Introduction to general principles of classical thermodynamics. Main topics include equilibrium conditions, thermodynamic relations, Legendre transformations, Maxwell relations, stability of thermodynamic systems, phase transitions, and critical phenomena.
ME 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 612.title: Introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics
ME 612.subject: ME
ME 612.description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics. Main topics include entropy, Boltzmann law, thermodynamic driving forces, statistical mechanics, chemical equilibria, solutions and mixtures, and applications of statistical thermodynamics in biology, chemistry, physics, and nanoscience.

ME 615.title: Advanced Aerodynamics
ME 615.subject: ME
ME 615.description: Advanced topics in aerodynamics, two- and three-dimensional wing theory, slender-body theory, lifting surface methods, vortex and wave drag, analytical and numerical methods, for computing unsteady aerodynamic behavior and introduction to flight-dynamics.

ME 617.title: Thermal Environmental Engineering
ME 617.subject: ME
ME 617.description: Physiological response to thermal environment, designs of passive and active cooling systems, student project.

ME 618.title: Boiling and Two-Phase Flow
ME 618.subject: ME
ME 618.description: Two-phase flow pattern and flow pattern maps; two-phase flow models (homogeneous, separate, drift flux, annular); laminar and turbulent film condensations; boiling incipience; pool boiling heat transfer; flow boiling heat transfer; critical heat flux (CHF).

ME 620.title: Biological Fluid Mechanics
ME 620.subject: ME
ME 620.description: Review of Newtonian fluid mechanics. Blood rheology and flow in elastic tubes. Murray’s Law and pulsatile flow propagation. Microcirculation dynamics and biological transport. Aquatic movement and comparative biological examples.

ME 621.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
ME 621.subject: ME
ME 621.description: Steady and unsteady heat conduction with and without heat sources in solids. Analytical, numerical, graphical, analog methods for solving heat conduction problems.

ME 622.title: Convection Heat Transfer
ME 622.subject: ME
ME 622.description: Heat transfer in laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Analogy between heat, momentum, mass transfer.

ME 623.title: Radiation Heat Transfer
ME 623.subject: ME
ME 623.description: Radiant interchange among surfaces. Gaseous radiation. Combined conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer.

ME 624.title: Microfluidics and Nanofluidics
ME 624.subject: ME
ME 624.description: Introduction to fundamental understanding of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena at micro-nanoscale; electrokinetics; chemical separation; colloids and emulsions; biophysics; micro-nanofabrication.

ME 625.title: Numerical Methods in Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer
ME 625.subject: ME
ME 625.description: Integration of ordinary differential equations. Finite difference solutions of partial differential equations with applications to conduction and convection. Introduction to finite element methods.
ME 625.prereq_raw: ME 422 , and either MATH 190 or ECE 160 .

ME 626.title: Viscous Flows
ME 626.subject: ME
ME 626.description: Formulation and properties of the Navier-Stokes equations; exact solutions; creeping flows; lubrication theory; laminar boundary layers; laminar stability, and transition to turbulence; turbulent boundary layers.

ME 627.title: Environmental Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transfer
ME 627.subject: ME
ME 627.description: Heat and mass transfer in Earth’s interior with applications to geothermal and petroleum reservoir engineering.

ME 628.title: Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design
ME 628.subject: ME
ME 628.description: Chemical kinetics with heat and mass transfer. Balance equations applied to selected ideal reactors. Departures from ideality.

ME 629.title: Renewable Energy Engineering I: Biomass
ME 629.subject: ME
ME 629.description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Experimental methods and theory of thermochemical biomass conversion: static and dynamic temperature and mass measurements, thermogravimetry, differential scanning calorimetry, GCMS and HPLC techniques.

ME 630.title: Rheology
ME 630.subject: ME
ME 630.description: Vector and tensor operations. Constutive equations. Generalized Newtonian fluids and linear viscoelastic fluids. Rheometry and experiments. Flow of suspensions. Advanced topics and rheology of polymers, food products, biomaterials and asphalt, laboratories.

ME 631.title: Advanced Materials Science
ME 631.subject: ME
ME 631.description: Properties of materials interpreted from the atomistic viewpoint. Crystal structure and defects. Thermodynamics of solids; phase transformations; experimental techniques.

ME 632.title: Advanced Transport Phenomena
ME 632.subject: ME
ME 632.description: Theory of momentum, heat, and mass transfer processes. Integral and differential conservation equations, constitutive laws, and interfacial boundary conditions. Dimensional analysis, perturbation theory, asymptotics, similarity, and Green’s function methodology. Applications to problems in engineering.
ME 632.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in ME 322 or ECE 626 , or consent.

children.text: grade of C or better in ME 322

ME 632.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 633.title: Li-ion Battery Mechanistic Modeling: Principles and State of the Art
ME 633.subject: ME
ME 633.description: Electrochemistry, Li-ion batteries, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage.

ME 635.title: Corrosion Theory
ME 635.subject: ME
ME 635.description: Application of electrochemical theory and materials science to corrosion and oxidation reactions. Effect of environment, especially marine. Cathodic protection, coatings, inhibitors, treatment of water systems.

ME 636.title: Fundamentals of Electrochemistry
ME 636.subject: ME
ME 636.description: Thermodynamics of cells, electrode kinetics, mass transfer by migration and diffusion, microelectrode techniques, forced convection, impedance, double-layer structure, and absorbed intermediates in electrode processes.

ME 642.title: Mechanical Behavior of Engineering Materials
ME 642.subject: ME
ME 642.description: Mechanical property tests. Stress concentrations. Fracture mechanics; applications to materials failures and to selection of materials; emphasis on mechanical engineering applications.

ME 645.title: Clinically Driven Design and Development
ME 645.subject: ME
ME 645.description: Exploration of simple, cost-effective alternatives in medicine through different stages of concept generation, design analysis, and prototype validation and investigation of their commercialization potential.
ME 645.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 646.title: Mechanics and Design Composites
ME 646.subject: ME
ME 646.description: Introduction to composites; anisotropic elasticity and laminate theory; hygrothermal effects; composite beams, columns, rods, plates, and shells; energy method; failure theories; joining of composites, computer-aided design in composites.

ME 647.title: Nanoscience and Nanotechnology
ME 647.subject: ME
ME 647.description: Science and applications of nanotechnology. Synthesis of nanostructures; nanoscale structure characterization by electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy; electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of nanostructures; fabrication of nanodevices; energy, environmental, and biological applications of nanomaterials.

ME 648.title: Nanosystems
ME 648.subject: ME
ME 648.description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale, including electrostatic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, and measurements. Course work will focus on literature review and integration of current research.
ME 648.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 650.title: Surface Phenomena
ME 650.subject: ME
ME 650.description: Fundamental and modern concepts of colloid and surface science. Main topics include surface thermodynamics, capillarity and wetting phenomena, surface forces, surfactants, and particles.

ME 651.title: Automatic Control
ME 651.subject: ME
ME 651.description: Linear optimal feedback control, discrete time optimal control, fundamentals of adaptive control, application to motion and force control of robot arms and manipulators.

ME 652.title: Guidance, Navigation and Control
ME 652.subject: ME
ME 652.description: Develop modern and advanced techniques in the design, development, and implementation of guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) systems for flight vehicles and other controllable dynamical systems.
ME 652.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: ME 271 or CEE 271 ; ME 375 ; MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; MATH 302 or MATH 307 ; or consent.

children.text: grade of C or better in all of the following: ME 271

ME 652.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 657.title: Autonomous Marine Systems
ME 657.subject: ME
ME 657.description: Identifies the unique challenges faced by autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, and analyzes approaches to address those challenges. Topics include hydrodynamic vehicle modeling, propeller theory, subsystem integration, and motion control strategies.
ME 657.prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 (or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 (or equivalent), or instructor consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 ( or equivalent), or instructor consent

ME 657.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 660.title: Introduction to Fuel Cell Technology
ME 660.subject: ME
ME 660.description: Working principles of all major fuel cell types; fundamentals of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells; state-of-the-art theoretical models and diagnostic technologies for PEM fuel cells.

ME 661.title: Energy Transport and Conversion at the Nanoscale
ME 661.subject: ME
ME 661.description: Basics of energy transport and conversion processes and emphasis on microscopic behaviors of energy carriers. Introduction to quantum mechanics and solid state physics.
ME 661.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or instructor consent.

ME 662.title: Shape Memory Alloys-Constitutive Modeling, Dynamics, and Nonlinear Control
ME 662.subject: ME
ME 662.description: Shape memory alloys; Shape Memory Effect (SME) and Superelasticity; hysteresis; applications in engineering, medical devices, and robotics; modeling and characterization; nonlineal control; finite element analyses. Engineering and computer science majors only.
ME 662.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ME 671.title: Continuum Mechanics
ME 671.subject: ME
ME 671.description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics, coordinate transformations, analysis of stress and strain, principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations, constitutive relations, field equations. Problems in elasticity.
ME 671.prereq_raw: Recommended: ME 371 or CEE 370 , or consent.

ME 672.title: Finite Element Analysis
ME 672.subject: ME
ME 672.description: Introduction to finite element analysis and design in mechanical engineering. Applications to machine design, vibrations, elasticity, heat transfer.

ME 678.title: Advanced Dynamics
ME 678.subject: ME
ME 678.description: Lecture on rigid-body dynamics. Topics include: dynamical systems; motion representation and constraints; Newtonian mechanics; Lagrangian mechanics; Hamilton’s principle; stability analysis; introduction to multibody dynamics.

ME 680.title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
ME 680.subject: ME
ME 680.description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses. Recommended: LAW 531 .
ME 680.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law, MBA, and ME students only.

ME 686.title: Air Pollution, Toxics, and Control
ME 686.subject: ME
ME 686.description: Chemical mechanisms of formation and destruction of major air pollutants, transport phenomena, and health and environmental impacts. Evolution of source and control technologies. Current and pending regulations and policies.
ME 686.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, ECE, ME, and OE majors only.

ME 691.title: Seminar
ME 691.subject: ME
ME 691.description: Current problems in all branches of mechanical engineering. All graduate students are required to attend; registrants are expected to present talks.

ME 696.title: Advanced Topics in Mechanical Engineering
ME 696.subject: ME
ME 696.description: Highly specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, system, or design.

ME 699.title: Directed Reading or Research
ME 699.subject: ME
ME 699.description: Directed study on subject of mutual interest to student and a staff member. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering.

ME 700.title: Thesis Research
ME 700.subject: ME
ME 700.description: Thesis for degree of MS in mechanical engineering.
ME 700.prereq_raw: admission to candidacy and consent of thesis advisor.

ME 799.title: Directed Instruction
ME 799.subject: ME
ME 799.description: Student assists in undergraduate classroom and/or project instruction under the direction and close supervision of faculty member.
ME 799.prereq_raw: admission to PhD candidacy or consent.

ME 800.title: Dissertation Research
ME 800.subject: ME
ME 800.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD in mechanical engineering.

MED 532.title: Internal Medicine Longitudinal Clerkship
MED 532.subject: MED
MED 532.description: Six-month long clerkship in ambulatory setting, and four-week hospital-based experience.
MED 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.

MED 545B.subject: MED
MED 545B.description: Fourth-year electives in which students study selected topics within field of medicine. (B) allergy/immunology; (C) cardiology; (D) medicine elective in Asia; (E) dermatology; (F) endocrinology; (G) gastroenterology; (H) general internal medicine: ambulatory care; (I) general internal medicine: inpatient; (K) hematology; (M) nephrology; (N) neurology; (O) nuclear medicine; (P) oncology; (Q) pulmonary diseases; (R) research in medicine; (S) rehabilitation medicine; (T) rheumatology; (U) heart failure/electrophysiology; (W) internal medicine sub-internship.

MEDT 151.title: Introduction to Medical Technology
MEDT 151.subject: MEDT
MEDT 151.description: Designed to acquaint students to the field of medical technology (clinical laboratory science).

MEDT 251.title: Introduction to Medical Technology II
MEDT 251.subject: MEDT
MEDT 251.description: Basic principles and lab skills in medical technology (medical lab science). Required for second bachelor’s degree students (not MLT credentialed) wishing to major in medical technology.
MEDT 251.prereq_raw: MEDT 151 , CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L , BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L (or concurrent)
MEDT 251.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Second bachelor’s degree students only.

MEDT 301.title: The Clinical Laboratory
MEDT 301.subject: MEDT
MEDT 301.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Theory and clinical application of medical laboratory methods and healthcare professional relationships.

MEDT 302.title: The Clinical Laboratory II
MEDT 302.subject: MEDT
MEDT 302.description: Theory and clinical application of medical technology methods and healthcare professional relationships. Companion course to MEDT 301 ; and required, for second bachelor’s degree students who were admitted to MEDT major.
MEDT 302.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only. Second Bachelor’s degree standing or higher.

MEDT 331.title: Clinical Laboratory Management
MEDT 331.subject: MEDT
MEDT 331.description: Students will become familiar with fundamental administration of a clinical laboratory to include technical, personnel, and financial management areas. Ethical issues in clinical laboratory management will be discussed, with an emphasis on writing instruction.

MEDT 431.title: Clinical Parasitology
MEDT 431.subject: MEDT
MEDT 431.description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Modern diagnostic practices in parasitology.

MEDT 451.title: Hematology
MEDT 451.subject: MEDT
MEDT 451.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental study of blood in normal and pathological states: formation, development, and classification of blood cells.

MEDT 451L.title: Hematology Lab
MEDT 451L.subject: MEDT
MEDT 451L.description: Laboratory to accompany MEDT 451 . Emphasis on writing to study content.

MEDT 464.title: Immunohematology
MEDT 464.subject: MEDT
MEDT 464.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Antigen-antibody relationships in human blood, study of blood groups, clinical problems in transfusion.

MEDT 468.title: Fundamentals of Clinical Parasitology
MEDT 468.subject: MEDT
MEDT 468.description: Covers epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections. Provides a foundation for successful MLS ASCP board certification, and benefits students pursuing careers related to medicine, public health and biomedical sciences.
MEDT 468.prereq_raw: MICR 130 or any general microbiology course, or consent.

MEDT 471.title: Clinical Biochemistry I
MEDT 471.subject: MEDT
MEDT 471.description: Biochemical processes in human health and disease states.

MEDT 477.title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses I
MEDT 477.subject: MEDT
MEDT 477.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lab experiments illustrating fundamental principles and methods of clinical laboratory analyses.

MEDT 478.title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses II
MEDT 478.subject: MEDT

MEDT 481.title: Professional Issues in Medical Lab Science
MEDT 481.subject: MEDT
MEDT 481.description: Discussions about various professional issues through oral presentations and critiquing of peer presentations.

MEDT 491.title: Clinical Immunology
MEDT 491.subject: MEDT
MEDT 491.description: Explore immunology by studying antigen-antibody structures, biological functions, and antibody synthesis fundamentals. Understand the relationship between immunology, biology, and medical sciences, preparing for advanced study and practical applications in medical technology.

MEDT 493.title: Diagnostic Clinical Bacteriology
MEDT 493.subject: MEDT
MEDT 493.description: Equips students with preanalytical, analytical and post-analytical knowledge on procedures required in the accurate diagnosis of infectious diseases in humans. Benefits students pursuing careers related to medicine, public health and biomedical sciences.
MEDT 493.prereq_raw: MICR 130 or any general microbiology course, or consent.

MEDT 495.title: Special Topics in Medical Technology
MEDT 495.subject: MEDT
MEDT 495.description: Acquaints student with role of the medical technologist and overlap of major sciences in clinical situations to help student develop qualities unique to med technology.

MEDT 581.title: Clinical Microbiology Preceptorship
MEDT 581.subject: MEDT
MEDT 581.description: Clinical training for students with bachelor’s degree in microbiology to be able to qualify as clinical microbiologists in a healthcare setting. Includes specimen procurement, processing, detection and identification, susceptibility testing, and other diagnostic technology.

MEDT 591.title: Clinical Training in Medical Technology
MEDT 591.subject: MEDT
MEDT 591.description: Application of theory and simulated laboratory experiences in immuno-hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, parasitology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, immunology, to meet stated career entry-level competencies.

MEDT 690.title: Seminar in Medical Technology
MEDT 690.subject: MEDT
MEDT 690.description: Analysis of research and recent literature pertaining to various aspects of medical technology.

MGT 320.title: Fundamentals of Entrepreneurship
MGT 320.subject: MGT
MGT 320.description: Covers the role of new ventures and entrepreneurship in the world economy, the formation, funding, marketing, structure and implementation of business ventures.

MGT 342.title: Multinational Business Management
MGT 342.subject: MGT
MGT 342.description: Introduction to the unique problems and challenges in managing multinational business enterprises. Systems approach to the management process in such multinational firms stressed.

MGT 343.title: Comparative Management Systems: United States and Japan
MGT 343.subject: MGT
MGT 343.description: Similarities and differences in managers, in process of management, and in relevant environmental constraints in Japan and the U.S.

MGT 344.title: Seminar in Management
MGT 344.subject: MGT
MGT 344.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration.

MGT 345.title: Entrepreneurial Ventures
MGT 345.subject: MGT
MGT 345.description: Integrative course in entrepreneurship designed around the development of an original business concept and the completion of a comprehensive business plan for a new venture. Intended as final course for students completing entrepreneurship minor.

MGT 348.title: History of American Business
MGT 348.subject: MGT
MGT 348.description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

MGT 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
MGT 399.subject: MGT
MGT 399.description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

MGT 441.title: Behavior in Organizations
MGT 441.subject: MGT
MGT 441.description: Contributions made by sociology, psychology, and related behavioral sciences to the understanding and prediction of human behavior in organizations.

MGT 450.title: Family Business
MGT 450.subject: MGT
MGT 450.description: The exploration of business, personal, and interpersonal issues associated with a family owned and managed company. Topics include: family psychology and organizational structure, life cycles in family business, strategic family and business planning, succession planning, family business conflict resolution, estate planning, the role of professional managers, and others. This is not a course about how to become an entrepreneur or how to start or manage a business. It is most appropriate for those students who are part of a family that owns and manages a business.
MGT 450.prereq_raw: BUS 315 or graduate status, or consent.

MGT 460.title: Asia Pacific Business Systems
MGT 460.subject: MGT
MGT 460.description: Business systems in Asia Pacific countries including Japan, Korea, China, Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong in terms of particular organization strategies and how they relate to the industrial trade policies.
MGT 460.prereq_raw: BBA core excluding BUS 345 , or consent.

MGT 461.title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
MGT 461.subject: MGT
MGT 461.description: Exploration of the nature and role of entrepreneurship behavior inside larger, established organizations. An examination of obstacles to entrepreneurial activity and approaches to creating work environments that foster entrepreneurship.

MGT 643B.title: Advanced Organizational Behavior: experiential learning (EL)
MGT 643B.subject: MGT
MGT 643B.description: (B) experiential learning (EL); (C) organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.
MGT 643B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

MGT 643C.title: Advanced Organizational Behavior: organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior
MGT 643C.subject: MGT
MGT 643C.description: (B) experiential learning (EL); (C) organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.
MGT 643C.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

MGT 644.title: Comparative Management
MGT 644.subject: MGT
MGT 644.description: Crosscultural analysis of the values and environmental constraints that shape management patterns and policies. Emphasis on Pacific area nations.
MGT 644.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

MGT 645.title: New Venture Management
MGT 645.subject: MGT
MGT 645.description: Technical aspects of entrepreneurship, components and requirements for developing a business plan.

MGT 648.title: International Business: Environment and Enterprise
MGT 648.subject: MGT
MGT 648.description: Survey of the environment of international business with theory and policy focusing on strategic planning, international management and operational issues confronting the multinational corporations in the global environment.
MGT 648.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

MGT 650.title: Management Topics
MGT 650.subject: MGT
MGT 650.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration.

MGT 651.title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
MGT 651.subject: MGT
MGT 651.description: Entrepreneurship behavior involving the founding of new business units within established companies; understanding and dealing with barriers to entrepreneurship in corporations; recognizing corporate entrepreneurship opportunities; and learning various approaches organizations can take to increase entrepreneurship.

MGT 652.title: Working with Entrepreneurs and Startups
MGT 652.subject: MGT
MGT 652.description: Project-oriented course in which a team of students will work with a real local startup and entrepreneur to develop a business idea and/or viable business plan.
MGT 652.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MGT 653.title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
MGT 653.subject: MGT
MGT 653.description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses. Recommended: LAW 530 .
MGT 653.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law, MBA, and ME students only.

MGT 660.title: Negotiation
MGT 660.subject: MGT
MGT 660.description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multiparty, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

MGT 670B.subject: MGT
MGT 670B.description: Selected topics in international management and industrial relations: (B) Chinese management systems; (C) Japanese management systems; (D) management of multinational corporations; (F) contemporary issues in international business foreign direct investment; (G) cross-cultural communication in international business; (H) interactive strategies in Asian culture; (I) international human resource management; (J) international joint ventures; (K) international management of technology; (M) Korean management systems; (N) multinational corporation and environmental issues; (O) strategy of the multinational corporation; (P) international transfer of technology.

MGT 671.title: International Strategic Management
MGT 671.subject: MGT
MGT 671.description: Analysis of the strategic management of firms engaged in multinational business including specific content on Asia. Permits students to focus on specific countries such as China and Japan.

MGT 680.title: Entrepreneurship for Science and Technology
MGT 680.subject: MGT
MGT 680.description: Recognizing and screening technology opportunities, the commercialization process, intellectual property acquisition, business model related to high technology strategies needed for growth in high tech firms.

MGT 681.title: Asian/Pacific Entrepreneurship
MGT 681.subject: MGT
MGT 681.description: Innovative ventures, issues related to noticing opportunities, conceptualizing and developing a business model, starting and growing a new venture with specific emphasis on the Asian/Pacific region.

MGT 688.title: Health Policy, Systems, and the Legal Environment
MGT 688.subject: MGT
MGT 688.description: Covers health care policy topics including: analyzing health service needs, access, use, disparities; health professional supply; policy issues for health organizations; health care financing policy; health law/ethical issues.

MGT 701.title: Cross-Cultural Management
MGT 701.subject: MGT
MGT 701.description: Provides tools to compare and contrast management practices across nations and to examine the role of culture in shaping those practices.
MGT 701.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

MGT 704.title: PhD Seminar-Corporate Strategy and International Business
MGT 704.subject: MGT
MGT 704.description: Objectives include: explore research topics in corporate strategy and international business, examine conceptual and empirical literature on management of the multinational corporation, and prepare students for comprehensive examination.
MGT 704.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

MGT 799.title: Directed Reading and Research
MGT 799.subject: MGT
MGT 799.description: Reading and research in an area of management under the direction of faculty member(s).
MGT 799.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

MICR 130.title: General Microbiology
MICR 130.subject: MICR
MICR 130.description: Role of microorganisms; how they affect people, property, and the environment. A basic survey course covering broad aspects of biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, and physiology; host-parasite relationships, public health, bacterial, mycotic and viral diseases; epidemiology; ecology of soils and water; environmental pollution; food microbiology; industrial applications at an introductory level. Not open to those with credit in MICR 351 or equivalent.

MICR 140L.title: Microbiology Laboratory
MICR 140L.subject: MICR
MICR 140L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany MICR 130 . Microbiological techniques and cultivation of microorganisms. Instruction in lab safety. Primarily for students in nursing and dental hygiene.

MICR 314.title: Research Ethics
MICR 314.subject: MICR
MICR 314.description: Introduction to the ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Based on case studies, students will discuss and write about ethical issues in research. Issues include humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data, genetic technologies and record keeping. This course is designed for students with majors in the natural sciences.
MICR 314.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or concurrent), or MATH 307 (or concurrent), or MATH 311 (or concurrent), or PHYS 170 (or concurrent), or CHEM 272 (or concurrent); or consent.

MICR 351.title: Biology of Microorganisms
MICR 351.subject: MICR
MICR 351.description: Anatomy, chemistry, physiology, genetics, development, and environmental interactions of microorganisms.
MICR 351.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 or equivalent, CHEM 272 / CHEM 272L ; or consent.

MICR 351L.title: Biology of Microorganisms Lab
MICR 351L.subject: MICR
MICR 351L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory exercises to accompany MICR 351 .
MICR 351L.prereq_raw: CHEM 272 / CHEM 272L , and BIOL 171 or equivalent.

MICR 361.title: Introductory Bioinformatics
MICR 361.subject: MICR
MICR 361.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introductory bioinformatics will provide a basic foundation of biological information (DNA, protein, genome and proteome) by using information technology (IT).

MICR 401.title: Marine Microbiology
MICR 401.subject: MICR
MICR 401.description: Evolution, ecology, biochemistry, genetics and physiology of marine bacteria by examining defined systems and organisms.
MICR 401.prereq_raw: BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and BIOL 301 (or concurrent)/ BIOL 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201 ; or MICR 351 / MICR 351L ; or consent.

children.text: / BIOL 301L (or concurrent) , and OCN 201 ; or MICR 351 / MICR 351L ; or consent

MICR 401L.title: Marine Microbiology Laboratory
MICR 401L.subject: MICR
MICR 401L.prereq_raw: BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and BIOL 301 (or concurrent)/ BIOL 301L (or concurrent) and OCN 201 ; or MICR 351 / MICR 351L ; and MICR 401 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: / BIOL 301L (or concurrent) and OCN 201 ; or MICR 351 / MICR 351L ; and MICR 401 (or concurrent) ; or consent

MICR 431.title: Microbial Physiology
MICR 431.subject: MICR
MICR 431.description: Fundamental physiological and metabolic processes of bacteria; emphasis on growth, functions of cell structures, varieties of energy metabolism, metabolic regulation, and differentiation at the prokaryote level.

MICR 431L.title: Microbial Physiology Lab
MICR 431L.subject: MICR
MICR 431L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Components and metabolism of the bacterial cell; emphasis on techniques of analysis of metabolism and molecular structure.

MICR 461.title: Immunology
MICR 461.subject: MICR
MICR 461.description: Structure and biological actions of antigens and antibodies; fundamentals of antibody synthesis; the relation of immunology to biology and medical sciences.
MICR 461.prereq_raw: MICR 351 or BIOL 171 , or consent. Recommended: BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L .

MICR 461L.title: Immunology Lab
MICR 461L.subject: MICR
MICR 461L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Basic exercises and experiments in immunology, immunochemistry, immuno-biology to illustrate principles of MICR 461 .

MICR 463.title: Microbiology of Pathogens
MICR 463.subject: MICR
MICR 463.description: Host-parasite relationships in microbial diseases of humans and animals with emphasis on bacterial pathogens.

MICR 463L.title: Microbiology of Pathogens Lab
MICR 463L.subject: MICR
MICR 463L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Characterization of bacterial pathogens. Isolation, identification, and diagnosis. This course develops written communication skills.

MICR 470.title: Bacterial Molecular Pathogenesis
MICR 470.subject: MICR
MICR 470.description: Fundamental mechanisms of bacterial infectious diseases or pathogenesis at the molecular level. Emphasis on bacterial virulence and host-pathogen interactions.

MICR 470L.title: Bacterial Molecular Pathogenesis Laboratory
MICR 470L.subject: MICR
MICR 470L.description: Modern techniques to study infectious diseases. Covers tissue culture and animal models to study virulence of extracellular and intracellular infecting bacteria, bacterial resistance mechanisms toward antibacterial drugs, and virulence factor assays.

MICR 475.title: Bacterial Genetics
MICR 475.subject: MICR
MICR 475.description: Genetic analysis and molecular basis of transmission replication, mutation, and expression of heritable characteristics in prokaryotes.

MICR 475L.title: Bacterial Genetics Lab
MICR 475L.subject: MICR
MICR 475L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of transfer and expression of prokaryotic genes: transformation, conjugation, transposon mutagenesis, preparation and analysis of plasmid and chromosomal DNA. This course develops written communication skills.

MICR 485.title: Microbes and Their Environment
MICR 485.subject: MICR
MICR 485.description: Distribution, diversity, and roles of microorganisms in terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. Importance of bacteria in pesticide degradation, bioremediation of oil spills, sewage treatment, biocontrol, food fermentation.

MICR 485L.title: Microbes and Their Environment Lab
MICR 485L.subject: MICR
MICR 485L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of interaction of microorganisms with and within their natural habitats; symbiosis between microorganisms and plants and animals; role of microorganisms in element cycling; food fermentation by bacteria.

MICR 490.title: Virology
MICR 490.subject: MICR
MICR 490.description: Basic principles of virus biology. Topics include methods for virus study, virus structure, replication, gene expression, pathogenesis and host response.

MICR 490L.title: Virology Lab
MICR 490L.subject: MICR
MICR 490L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) General laboratory techniques and related theories in virology; including isolation, cell culture, assay, purification, and identification of viruses.
MICR 490L.prereq_raw: MICR 351 / MICR 351L or BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and MICR 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

MICR 601.title: Molecular Cell Biology
MICR 601.subject: MICR
MICR 601.description: Provide fundamental concepts and dynamic characteristics of the molecules of the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell, their biosynthesis and regulation, and the mechanisms that regulate cellular activities.
MICR 601.prereq_raw: basic course in cell and molecular biology, or consent.

MICR 602.title: Molecular Biology and Genetics
MICR 602.subject: MICR
MICR 602.description: Graduate-level basic course on molecular biology and genetics. Prepares students to understand advanced concepts in related subjects such as biochemistry, cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, plant genetics, and genomics.
MICR 602.prereq_raw: MBBE 402 / BIOL 402 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or with consent from instructor.

MICR 614.title: Research Ethics
MICR 614.subject: MICR
MICR 614.description: Introduction to ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Moral reasoning, humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data and genetic technologies.
MICR 614.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in MICR or related field, or consent. MICR graduates only.

MICR 625.title: Advanced Immunology
MICR 625.subject: MICR
MICR 625.description: Detailed reports and discussions on selected advanced topics and current research literature.

MICR 630.title: Microbial Genome
MICR 630.subject: MICR
MICR 630.description: Advanced studies of Microbial genome: relation to functional genomics, structural genomics, and proteomics.
MICR 630.prereq_raw: MICR 351 and one 400-level MICR course, or consent.

MICR 652.title: Advanced Marine Microbiology
MICR 652.subject: MICR
MICR 652.description: Advanced studies of marine microorganisms in diverse habitats with consideration of applications of marine microbes, interactions with higher organisms, phylogeny and diversity, and past and current methods.

MICR 655.title: Advanced Virology
MICR 655.subject: MICR
MICR 655.description: Detailed reports and discussions on selected advanced topics and current research literature.

MICR 661.title: Regulations of Gene Expressions in Microorganisms
MICR 661.subject: MICR
MICR 661.description: Use of bioinformatic tools to understand comparative genomics, metabolic pathways, and protein evolution.
MICR 661.prereq_raw: MICR 351 and one 400 level MICR course, or consent.

MICR 671.title: Bacterial Genetics
MICR 671.subject: MICR
MICR 671.description: Directed study and discussion of research literature on bacterial and bacterial virus mutation, genetic recombination, evolution and control mechanisms.
MICR 671.prereq_raw: graduate standing; undergraduates that have taken MICR 475 may register with consent.

children.text: undergraduates that have taken MICR 475 may register with consent

MICR 680.title: Advances in Microbial Ecology
MICR 680.subject: MICR
MICR 680.description: One topic area will be selected for in-depth study of microbial ecology, e.g. beneficial symbioses, responses to environmental changes, or interaction of microorganisms with abiotic and biotic components. Relevant, modern techniques will be discussed.

MICR 681.title: Host-Parasite Relationships
MICR 681.subject: MICR
MICR 681.description: Mechanisms of pathogenicity of microorganisms and defense mechanisms of human and animal hosts. Review of contemporary literature.

MICR 685.title: Molecular and Cellular Bacterial Pathogenesis
MICR 685.subject: MICR
MICR 685.description: Detailed examination of the molecular and cellular mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis. Overview of key literature, synthesis of scientific problems into research proposals.
MICR 685.prereq_raw: MICR 431 , MICR 463 , or MICR 470 ; or consent.

MICR 690.title: Seminar
MICR 690.subject: MICR
MICR 690.description: Seminar required for Microbiology graduate students to present their research progress, practice their presentation skills and receive feedback to help with their research. Outside/faculty speakers broaden students’ knowledge and provide real-life examples.
MICR 690.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Microbiology graduate students only.

MICR 695.title: Research Literature Review
MICR 695.subject: MICR
MICR 695.description: Review of primary literature in a selected area of microbiology.
MICR 695.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate status or consent.

MICR 746.title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
MICR 746.subject: MICR
MICR 746.description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts.
MICR 746.prereq_raw: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent.

MICR 795.title: Special Topics in Microbiology
MICR 795.subject: MICR
MICR 795.description: Selected topics in any aspect of microbiology.

MKT 311.title: Consumer Behavior
MKT 311.subject: MKT
MKT 311.description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects.

MKT 321.title: Marketing Research and Data Analytics
MKT 321.subject: MKT
MKT 321.description: Use of marketing research and marketing management and data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: the research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; and digital media analytics.

MKT 331.title: Marketing Communications
MKT 331.subject: MKT
MKT 331.description: In-depth coverage of the major communication tools used in marketing such as advertising, sales promotion, public relations and the internet. Emphasis on integrated marketing communications.

MKT 332.title: Integrated Communication Campaigns
MKT 332.subject: MKT
MKT 332.description: Management of integrated marketing communications campaigns. Includes: conducting target market and competitor research, developing creative content and media strategies, production of communication materials and completion of major real world project.

MKT 341.title: Retailing Management
MKT 341.subject: MKT
MKT 341.description: Analysis of opportunities and challenges in physical and digital retailing management: physical layout and digital design; merchandise planning; organizational forms; expense analysis; integration of physical/digital programs.

MKT 350.title: Sales and Sales Management
MKT 350.subject: MKT
MKT 350.description: Delves into selling and the sales management process. Through a variety of activities, students experience applying selling techniques, sales planning, recruiting and training salespeople, methods of motivating and compensating, territory management and sales team communications.

MKT 351.title: Professional Selling
MKT 351.subject: MKT
MKT 351.description: Emphasis on selling technique, social-psychological principles of persuasion, and interpersonal communication. Lecture, discussion, and application of relevant principles and techniques. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

MKT 361.title: Seminar in Marketing
MKT 361.subject: MKT
MKT 361.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of marketing.
MKT 361.prereq_raw: BUS 312 and usually senior standing, or consent.

MKT 362.title: Digital Marketing
MKT 362.subject: MKT
MKT 362.description: Provides comprehensive understanding of digital marketing’s growing role in new product development; marketing research; direct sales; and marketing communications. Students learn multiple digital tools for analysis of customer behavior. Real-world projects provide opportunities for application.

MKT 363.title: Customer Relationship Management
MKT 363.subject: MKT
MKT 363.description: Focuses on the evolving field of customer relationship management. Students learn how to manage marketing information and decision-making systems that maximize customer retention and build long-term relationships.

MKT 368.title: Sustainable Marketing
MKT 368.subject: MKT
MKT 368.description: Provides environmental knowledge and managerial tools that help for profit and not-for-profit organizations address pressing issues like global warming, plastic pollution, and fair trade while earning surplus revenue and remaining socially accountable.

MKT 372.title: Marketing for New Ventures
MKT 372.subject: MKT
MKT 372.description: Examines role of marketing in the formation and launch of entrepreneurial ventures within and outside of ongoing businesses. Emphasis on new product development and low cost, high impact marketing activities.

MKT 381.title: International Marketing
MKT 381.subject: MKT
MKT 381.description: Principles and topics related to international marketing, with emphasis on strategic planning and applications.

MKT 391.title: Marketing Strategies
MKT 391.subject: MKT
MKT 391.description: Decision-making by the marketing executive; integration of all elements of the marketing program based on actual business situations.
MKT 391.prereq_raw: MKT 311 , MKT 321 , and BUS 312 ; or consent.

MKT 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
MKT 399.subject: MKT
MKT 399.description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

MKT 410.title: Marketing Analytics
MKT 410.subject: MKT
MKT 410.description: Introduces current quantitative techniques and analytical approaches to better marketing decision-making. Students learn how to solve problems in a data-driven way using software tools.

MKT 411B.title: New Product Innovation and Development
MKT 411B.subject: MKT
MKT 411B.description: Innovation/development processes critical to successful new products. Emphasis on existing larger businesses. Students gain experience in bringing new products from creative idea generation to market launch.

MKT 648.title: Consumer Behavior for Managers
MKT 648.subject: MKT
MKT 648.description: Designed to help students better understand how consumers process information, form attitudes, and make decisions. Draws on theories from social sciences to help students manage consumer needs and satisfaction.
MKT 648.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MKT 650.title: Sales Leadership
MKT 650.subject: MKT
MKT 650.description: Sales managers participate in diverse activities including hiring, designing and implementing training programs, in-field coaching and development, motivating and compensating employees, and team building. Helps students develop knowledge and skills in these areas.
MKT 650.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

MKT 651.title: Advanced Marketing Management
MKT 651.subject: MKT
MKT 651.description: A case course in the application of advanced marketing methods.

MKT 652.title: Japanese Marketing Systems
MKT 652.subject: MKT
MKT 652.description: Specialized study of Japanese marketing systems, considers both global and domestic marketing activities in the context of the Japanese economy.

MKT 653.title: International Marketing Management
MKT 653.subject: MKT
MKT 653.description: Integrated and comparative approach to international marketing management. Emphasis on the development of a competitive strategy in a global environment. Applications to both developing and industrialized markets.

MKT 654.title: Strategic Brand Management
MKT 654.subject: MKT
MKT 654.description: The study of branding and brand management. Explores how managers can formulate and implement integrated marketing strategies to build brand equity. Includes relevant theory and real world applications.

MKT 655.title: Marketing Research Management
MKT 655.subject: MKT
MKT 655.description: Examines use of marketing research/data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; digital media analytics. Real world project reinforce learning.

MKT 656.title: Creativity in Marketing
MKT 656.subject: MKT
MKT 656.description: Thought processes that relate to creativity. Through a series of exercises, students experience enriched creativity and enhanced communication skills.

MKT 657.title: Services Marketing
MKT 657.subject: MKT
MKT 657.description: Conceptual understanding of distinctive aspects of services, services management, and services research.

MKT 658.title: Digital Marketing Management
MKT 658.subject: MKT
MKT 658.description: Examines digital marketing’s role in new product development; direct sales; marketing communications via the internet, social media, and mobile devices; and digital tools such as online tracking and analysis. Real activities provide opportunities for application.

MKT 688.title: Patient Centered Communication Management in Health Care Organizations
MKT 688.subject: MKT
MKT 688.description: Provides training on managing patient communications in general and shared decision making in particular. Increases ability to use tools available to improve patient-provider decision making quality and satisfaction.

MKT 701.title: Seminar in Marketing Theory
MKT 701.subject: MKT
MKT 701.description: Focuses on the building blocks of theory, their use, and evolution within a marketing context. Explores marketing theories, theory construction, and the creation of marketing knowledge.
MKT 701.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

MKT 702.title: Seminar in Consumer Behavior
MKT 702.subject: MKT
MKT 702.description: Focuses on consumer behavior theory. Provides in-depth review of important published work in traditional and cross-cultural consumer behavior fields.
MKT 702.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

MKT 703.title: Seminar in Marketing Strategy
MKT 703.subject: MKT
MKT 703.description: Focuses on theories of strategic marketing and planning. Explores the theoretical principles of marketing concepts, tools, and processes that can be used to help an organization develop a sustainable competitive advantage.
MKT 703.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

MKT 704.title: Seminar in Selected Marketing Topics
MKT 704.subject: MKT
MKT 704.description: Selected topics in any aspect of marketing to increase exposure to the range of issues researchers commonly confront.
MKT 704.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

MKT 799.title: Directed Research
MKT 799.subject: MKT
MKT 799.description: Reading and research in an area of marketing under the direction of faculty member(s).
MKT 799.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

MSL 100.title: Introduction to Physical Fitness
MSL 100.subject: MSL
MSL 100.description: Hands-on participatory course following the Army’s physical fitness program. Classes conducted three days per week with Army ROTC cadets. Focus is on aerobic conditioning, muscular strength and endurance.

MSL 101.title: Introduction to Military Science I
MSL 101.subject: MSL
MSL 101.description: Introduces cadets to personal challenges and competencies critical for effective leadership; personal development of life skills such as goal setting, time management, physical fitness, and stress management related to leadership, officership, and the Army profession. Focus on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of Army Leadership Dimensions while understanding the ROTC program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student.

MSL 101L.title: Introduction to Military Science I Lab
MSL 101L.subject: MSL
MSL 101L.description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

MSL 102.title: Introduction to Military Science II
MSL 102.subject: MSL
MSL 102.description: Overviews leadership fundamentals such as setting direction, problem-solving, listening, presenting briefs, providing feedback and using effective writing skills. Explores leadership values, attributes, skills, and actions in the context of practical, hands-on, and interactive exercises. Cadre role models and building stronger relationships among cadets through common experience and practical interaction are critical.

MSL 102L.title: Introduction to Military Science II Lab
MSL 102L.subject: MSL
MSL 102L.description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

MSL 201.title: Intermediate Military Science I
MSL 201.subject: MSL
MSL 201.description: Explores creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles through historical case studies and engaging in interactive student exercises. Cadets practice aspects of personal motivation and team building by planning, executing, and assessing team exercises. Focus is on continued development of leadership values and attributes through understanding of rank, uniform, customs and courtesies.

MSL 202.title: Intermediate Military Science II
MSL 202.subject: MSL
MSL 202.description: Challenges of leading complex, contemporary operational environments. Dimensions of cross-cultural challenges of leadership in a constantly changing world are highlighted and applied to practical Army leadership tasks and situations. Cadets develop greater self awareness as they practice communication and team building skills, and tactics in real world scenarios. Provides a smooth transition to MSL 301 .

MSL 203.title: ROTC Basic Camp
MSL 203.subject: MSL
MSL 203.description: Four-week summer course conducted at Ft. Knox, Kentucky. Substitutes for ROTC basic course ( MSL 101 , MSL 102 , MSL 201 , and MSL 202 ) and fulfills course requirement for admission to ROTC advanced courses. Credit will be given for MSL 203 or basic courses, but not both.

MSL 301.title: Leading Small Organizations I
MSL 301.subject: MSL
MSL 301.description: (2 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Challenges cadets to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills with demands of the ROTC Advanced Camp. Challenging scenarios related to small unit tactical operations will develop self-awareness and critical thinking skills. Cadets will receive systematic, specific feedback on their leadership abilities, and analyze/evaluate their leadership values, attributes, skills and actions.
MSL 301.prereq_raw: MSL 101 , MSL 102 , MSL 201 , and MSL 202 ; or MSL 203 ; or consent.

MSL 302.title: Leading Small Organizations II
MSL 302.subject: MSL
MSL 302.description: (2 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Intense situational leadership challenges to build awareness and skills in leading small units. Decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members under fire are explored, evaluated, and developed. Military operations are reviewed to prepare for the ROTC Advance Camp. Cadets apply principles of Law of Land Warfare, Army training, and motivation to troop leading procedures; and are evaluated on what they know and do as leaders.

MSL 303.title: ROTC Advanced Camp
MSL 303.subject: MSL
MSL 303.description: Five-week summer field training exercise conducted at Fort Knox, Kentucky. Arduous and intensified leadership training is conducted throughout the five-week period. Required for U.S. Army commissioning.

MSL 391.title: History of Military Warfare
MSL 391.subject: MSL
MSL 391.description: Lecture/ discussion on the art and science of warfare concentrating on U.S. military history from the Colonial Period to present. Generally restricted to Army ROTC students, requiring twenty pages of graded writing assignments.

MSL 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
MSL 399.subject: MSL
MSL 399.description: Limited to military science students who have had at least one previous military science course for which a grade of B or higher was earned and a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or better.

MSL 400.title: Fundamentals of Leadership
MSL 400.subject: MSL
MSL 400.description: Introduces students to the fundamentals of leadership. Activities challenge students to connect theory to practice, develop positive relationships through application of effective leadership concepts with emphasis on teaching writing for personal development and team-building.

MSL 401.title: Leadership Challenges and Goal Setting
MSL 401.subject: MSL
MSL 401.description: (3 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Develops proficiency in planning, execution, and assessment of complex operations; students will learn to assess risk, make ethical decisions, function as a staff member, and provide leadership performance feedback to subordinates; emphasis on oral communication.

MSL 402.title: Transition to Lieutenant
MSL 402.subject: MSL
MSL 402.description: (3 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Explores dynamics of leading in complex situations of current military operations. Examines differences in customs and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism. Interaction with non-government organizations, civilians on the battlefield, and host nation support are examined and evaluated. Case studies, scenarios, and What Now, Lieutenant? exercises prepare cadets to lead as commissioned officers in the U.S. Army.

MSL 499.title: Advanced Military Research
MSL 499.subject: MSL
MSL 499.description: Directs the student to conduct detailed research on a military topic and present to the department leadership plus assist MSL 400 series students on a battle analysis.
MSL 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Must be in Military Science and Leadership Program or Military Service member in junior or greater standing.

MUS 105.title: Musical Meaning: How Music Shapes Identity
MUS 105.subject: MUS
MUS 105.description: The role of music from Africa, Asia, and Hawaiʻi in shaping and expressing cultures in the U.S.
MUS 105.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Freshman or sophomore standing only.

MUS 106.title: Exploring Music
MUS 106.subject: MUS
MUS 106.description: Elements, styles, and forms of music, from listener’s standpoint.

MUS 107.title: Music in World Cultures
MUS 107.subject: MUS
MUS 107.description: Folk, popular, and art music from major regions of the world, with emphasis upon Asia and the Pacific; representative styles and regional characteristics.

MUS 107A.title: Music in World Cultures
MUS 107A.subject: MUS
MUS 107A.description: Folk, popular, and art music from major regions of the world, with emphasis upon Asia and the Pacific; representative styles and regional characteristics.

MUS 108.title: Fundamentals of Music
MUS 108.subject: MUS
MUS 108.description: Basic organization concepts in music and introduction to music theory. Learning through hands-on experience with creative activities in various media. Focused listening, composing original melodies, utilizing technology to explore how music is created, basic notation.

MUS 114.title: University Chorus
MUS 114.subject: MUS
MUS 114.description: Performance of choral literature from Renaissance to present. Previous choral experience not required.

MUS 121B.title: Class Instruction I: voice
MUS 121B.subject: MUS
MUS 121B.description: Basic principles of performance; relevant problems in literature. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) guitar.

MUS 121C.title: Class Instruction I: piano
MUS 121C.subject: MUS
MUS 121C.description: Basic principles of performance; relevant problems in literature. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) guitar.

MUS 121D.title: Class Instruction I: guitar
MUS 121D.subject: MUS
MUS 121D.description: Basic principles of performance; relevant problems in literature. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) guitar.

MUS 122B.title: Class Instruction II: voice
MUS 122B.subject: MUS
MUS 122B.description: Basic principles of performance; relevant problems in literature. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) guitar.

MUS 122C.title: Class Instruction II: piano
MUS 122C.subject: MUS
MUS 122C.description: Basic principles of performance; relevant problems in literature. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) guitar.

MUS 122D.title: Class Instruction II: guitar
MUS 122D.subject: MUS
MUS 122D.description: Basic principles of performance; relevant problems in literature. (B) voice; (C) piano; (D) guitar.

MUS 123B.title: Pacific Music Performance Class: slack key guitar
MUS 123B.subject: MUS
MUS 123B.description: Basic principles of performance of Pacific music. Relevant problems at elementary level. (B) slack key guitar; (C) ʻukulele.
MUS 123B.prereq_raw: MUS 121D or consent for (B); MUS 108 or consent for (C).

MUS 123C.title: Pacific Music Performance Class: ʻukulele
MUS 123C.subject: MUS
MUS 123C.description: Basic principles of performance of Pacific music. Relevant problems at elementary level. (B) slack key guitar; (C) ʻukulele.
MUS 123C.prereq_raw: MUS 121D or consent for (B); MUS 108 or consent for (C).

MUS 125.title: First-Level Secondary Piano
MUS 125.subject: MUS
MUS 125.description: Piano as secondary performance field; application of theory to problems in improvising, harmonizing, creating accompaniments, transposing, and sight-reading at keyboard. For music majors.

MUS 126.title: First-Level Secondary Piano
MUS 126.subject: MUS
MUS 126.description: Piano as secondary performance field; application of theory to problems in improvising, harmonizing, creating accompaniments, transposing, and sight-reading at keyboard. Continuation of MUS 125 . For music majors.

MUS 127B.title: Asian Music Performance Class: koto
MUS 127B.subject: MUS
MUS 127B.description: Basic principles of performance of Asian music. Relevant problems in literature at elementary level. (B) koto; (C) shamisen; (E) shakuhachi.

MUS 127C.title: Asian Music Performance Class: shamisen
MUS 127C.subject: MUS
MUS 127C.description: Basic principles of performance of Asian music. Relevant problems in literature at elementary level. (B) koto; (C) shamisen; (E) shakuhachi.
