MUS 340.title: Electronic Music
MUS 340.subject: MUS
MUS 340.description: Basic techniques of electronic sound synthesis.

MUS 341.title: Audio Recording/Mixing/Sound Design
MUS 341.subject: MUS
MUS 341.description: Preproduction, mixing, setup and recording suitable for film. Mixing techniques in software for small systems. Sound design using original synthesis techniques to enhance film and support stories.

MUS 342.title: Digital Audio Synthesis and Multimedia Applications
MUS 342.subject: MUS
MUS 342.description: Sound control through graphical interfaces. Advanced digital audio synthesis techniques. Audio control of graphics and video. Introduction of alternate controllers.

MUS 348.title: Western Music and Japan
MUS 348.subject: MUS
MUS 348.description: Historical survey of Western music in Japan from modernization through the Meiji Restoration up to the present. Topics include: Western-style symphonic music, J-pop, and Enka by Japanese artists; develops written communication skills.
MUS 348.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

MUS 350.title: Marching Band Design and Techniques
MUS 350.subject: MUS
MUS 350.description: Design and techniques for the modern field marching band.

MUS 353.title: Integrating World Music in Education
MUS 353.subject: MUS
MUS 353.description: Application of musical concepts through an integrated approach. This includes strategies, world music, literature, materials and resources for the classroom curriculum.

MUS 354.title: General Music Methods
MUS 354.subject: MUS
MUS 354.description: Required for K-12 music specialists. Scope and nature of music in the lives of children and adolescents; planning, teaching, learning, and evaluating music in elementary, middle, and high school curriculum.
MUS 354.prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 288 , or consent.
MUS 354.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MUS ED majors only, or consent.

MUS 354L.title: General Music Methods Lab
MUS 354L.subject: MUS
MUS 354L.description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in general music classrooms. Supervised 40 hours of field experiences required.
MUS 354L.prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 288 ; or consent.

MUS 355.title: Instrumental Music Methods
MUS 355.subject: MUS
MUS 355.description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of instrumental music in schools.
MUS 355.prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.
MUS 355.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MUS ED majors only, or consent.

MUS 355L.title: Instrumental Music Methods Lab
MUS 355L.subject: MUS
MUS 355L.description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in instrumental settings. Supervised 30 hours of field experiences required.
MUS 355L.prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.

MUS 356.title: Choral Music Methods
MUS 356.subject: MUS
MUS 356.description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of choral music in schools.
MUS 356.prereq_raw: MUS 122B , MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.
MUS 356.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MUS ED majors only, or consent.

MUS 356L.title: Choral Music Methods Lab
MUS 356L.subject: MUS
MUS 356L.description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in choral settings. Supervised 30 hours of field experiences required.
MUS 356L.prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.

MUS 358.title: Piano Pedagogy
MUS 358.subject: MUS
MUS 358.description: Concepts, materials, and procedures for class and individual instruction in piano. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

MUS 359.title: Piano Pedagogy
MUS 359.subject: MUS
MUS 359.description: Continuation of MUS 358 . Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

MUS 360.title: Music in Film
MUS 360.subject: MUS
MUS 360.description: Lecture investigating the role of music in narrative film, and developing critical skills through close study. Understanding styles, techniques and aesthetics of film music in historical contexts. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

MUS 362.title: Curtain Up! Broadway Musicals, Then and Now
MUS 362.subject: MUS
MUS 362.description: Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the “Hamilton” phenomenon, exploring their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts. Course develops written communication skills.

MUS 364.title: Superstars: A History of Musical Celebrity
MUS 364.subject: MUS
MUS 364.description: Explores how the cultural phenomenon of celebrity has impacted musicians and composers from antiquity to the present.

MUS 370.title: Music in Modern America
MUS 370.subject: MUS
MUS 370.description: Varieties of music, including jazz and other popular forms; relevant antecedents.
MUS 370.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing; freshmen with consent only.

MUS 381.title: Counterpoint
MUS 381.subject: MUS
MUS 381.description: Form, texture, and style in music literature from Renaissance to present. Formal analysis and writing. Contrapuntal textures and forms.

MUS 382.title: Form and Analysis
MUS 382.subject: MUS
MUS 382.description: Form, texture, and style in music literature from Renaissance to present. Formal analysis and writing. Larger forms with various textures; recent contemporary approaches to continuity.

MUS 383.title: Orchestration
MUS 383.subject: MUS
MUS 383.description: Basic principles of scoring for orchestra and band; instrumental ranges, timbres, transpositions; transcribing or composing for band, orchestra, and chorus.

MUS 386.title: Theory and Practice of Jazz Improvisation
MUS 386.subject: MUS
MUS 386.description: Development of an improvising technique through analysis and performance practice. For instrumentalists only.

MUS 399.title: Directed Study
MUS 399.subject: MUS
MUS 399.description: Limited to majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in music.

MUS 400.title: Topics in Music
MUS 400.subject: MUS
MUS 400.description: Topics in history, literature, theory, applied music, music education, and ethnomusicology; for music majors. Consult department for topics and specific dates.
MUS 400.prereq_raw: MUS 281 and appropriate lower division music courses; or consent.

MUS 407.title: Music Cultures of the World
MUS 407.subject: MUS
MUS 407.description: Folk, popular, and art music from major regions of the world, with emphasis upon Asia and the Pacific, representative styles and regional characteristics.
MUS 407.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

MUS 452.title: Advanced String Pedagogy

MUS 454.title: Music in Special Education

NAVL 100L.title: Leadership Laboratory
NAVL 100L.subject: NAVL
NAVL 100L.description: Laboratory instruction will include leadership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed for students pursuing Navy and Marine Corps commissions.

NAVL 101.title: Introduction to Naval Science
NAVL 101.subject: NAVL
NAVL 101.description: Overview of the Navy’s mission, customs, traditions, and the duties required of Junior Officers. Provides students with a basic knowledge of damage control, shipboard organization, and safety procedures prior to their first summer training cruise.

NAVL 102.title: Seapower and Maritime Affairs
NAVL 102.subject: NAVL
NAVL 102.description: Study of the Navy and the influence of seapower upon history that incorporates both an historical and political perspective to explore major events and circumstances that have shaped a bold and proud history.

NAVL 201.title: Leadership and Management
NAVL 201.subject: NAVL
NAVL 201.description: Comprehensive study of organizational behavior and management with a special emphasis on situational leadership in the Navy. Exploration of a variety of leadership and management topics, including classical theories of management, motivation, and communication.

NAVL 202.title: Navigation
NAVL 202.subject: NAVL
NAVL 202.description: Designed to provide midshipmen with an in-depth study of the theory, principles, procedures, and application of plotting, piloting, and electronic navigation, as well as an introduction to maneuvering boards.

NAVL 301.title: Naval Ships System I: Engineering
NAVL 301.subject: NAVL
NAVL 301.description: Will learn ship design and control, hydrodynamic forces, stability, electrical theory, and damage control coupled with design of steam, gas turbine and nuclear propulsion. Case studies merging both ethical and technical challenges.

NAVL 302.title: Naval Ship Systems II: Weapons
NAVL 302.subject: NAVL
NAVL 302.description: Outlines the theory and employment of naval warship weapons systems. Supplemented with review/ analysis of case studies involving the moral and ethical responsibilities of leaders in the employment of weapons.

NAVL 303.title: Evolution of Warfare
NAVL 303.subject: NAVL
NAVL 303.description: Focuses on enhancing students’ writing abilities through an in-depth examination of the historical foundations of contemporary warfighting theories, encompassing philosophies, domains, tactics, and technology.

NAVL 304.title: Fundamentals of Maneuver Warfare
NAVL 304.subject: NAVL
NAVL 304.description: Embark in a writing and oral-focused exploration of the USMC as the premiere Maneuver Warfighting Organization. Delve into theoretical concepts and historical examples, examining foundational principles through written analysis and oral discussion.

NAVL 395.title: United States Pacific Fleet Internship
NAVL 395.subject: NAVL
NAVL 395.description: Leadership development, teamwork, and activities designed for NROTC students. Learn how to write a federal resume, be a Federal Employee, and learn the skills needed to complete and present their U.S. Pacific Fleet capstone project.
NAVL 395.prereq_raw: NAVL 100L , NAVL 101 , NAVL 102 , NAVL 201 , NAVL 202 , NAVL 303 , NAVL 304 , or NAVL 402 .

NAVL 401.title: Naval Operations and Seamanship
NAVL 401.subject: NAVL
NAVL 401.description: Study of U.S. Navy ships professional and efficient operations. Lecture series on Fleet communications, tactical employment, relative motion plotting, seamanship, Joint Warfare, and employment of naval forces as an element of National Security.

NAVL 402.title: Leadership and Ethics
NAVL 402.subject: NAVL
NAVL 402.description: Introduces ethical theories in discussion-based formats, fostering understanding of diverse moral, ethical, and leadership philosophies. Enhances moral character, awareness of ethical decision-making tools, and addresses contemporary dilemmas through discussion, written journaling, and a research paper.

NHH 195.title: E Malama i Ke Ola Loko: The Practice of Self-Care and Wellness from a Kānaka Maoli Perspective
NHH 195.subject: NHH
NHH 195.description: An examination of self-care and wellness models from a Native Hawaiian perspective, exploration of self-care as lahui care, and practical application of wellness through ʻaina-based education.

NHH 450.title: Applied Health Disparities Research
NHH 450.subject: NHH
NHH 450.description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.

NHH 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
NHH 499.subject: NHH
NHH 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

NHH 501.title: Humanities in Medicine I
NHH 501.subject: NHH
NHH 501.description: Introduction to medical science stressing key historical figures and significant events to exemplify the development of scientific methods. Special emphasis on writing skills, health team concept, and culture and contributions of the Pacific.
NHH 501.prereq_raw: admission to Imi Hoʻola Post-Baccalaureate Program.

NHH 503.title: Medical Biology I
NHH 503.subject: NHH
NHH 503.description: (2 Lec, 2 Tutorial, 1 3-hr Lab) Foundation in medical sciences, including anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pathology, and pharmacology (focus on respiratory, cardiovascular, and urinary systems); develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Includes lectures, problem-based tutorials, and histology and gross anatomy labs.
NHH 503.prereq_raw: admission to Imi Hoʻola Post-Baccalaureate Program.

NHH 504.title: Medical Biology II

NHH 505.title: Medical Biochemistry I
NHH 505.subject: NHH
NHH 505.description: Provide background knowledge of chemistry, biochemistry, and molecular biology with emphasis in principles of biochemical processes as well as clinical correlations to medical conditions; develop critical thinking, standardized test taking skills, and problem-solving skills.
NHH 505.prereq_raw: admission to Imi Hoʻola Post- Baccalaureate Program.

NHH 513.title: Native Hawaiian Health and Traditional Healing

NHH 513.description: Introduction to Native Hawaiian health issues and traditional healing practices.

NHH 545.title: Native Hawaiian Health Care
NHH 545.subject: NHH
NHH 545.description: Clinical experience in the Native Hawaiian Health Care System and community health care centers, incorporating both western and traditional Hawaiian medicine. Open to fourth year medical students interested in Native Hawaiian Health Care.

NHH 575.title: Seminar in Issues of Social Medicine
NHH 575.subject: NHH
NHH 575.description: Social medicine provides an analytical and prescriptive framework to understand health inequities, including connections between social forces and health outcomes, and the role of the individual student in improving social welfare in the health system.
NHH 575.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

NHH 595.title: Clinical Skills Preceptorship in the Lau Ola Clinic of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health
NHH 595.subject: NHH
NHH 595.description: Provides a focused experience in clinical medicine with opportunities to practice the history and physical examination in Lau Ola, the clinical setting of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health.

NHH 599.title: Directed Reading/Research in Native Hawaiian Health
NHH 599.subject: NHH
NHH 599.description: Instruction of medical students in the social determinants of health, issues of health equity, specifically in Native Hawaiians, Pacific Islanders and/or disadvantaged people and teach them how these issues can be addressed through research.

NHH 650.title: Advanced Applied Health Disparities Research
NHH 650.subject: NHH
NHH 650.description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.

NHH 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
NHH 699.subject: NHH
NHH 699.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

NREM 105.title: Environmental Service Learning I
NREM 105.subject: NREM
NREM 105.description: Experiential service learning course for students participating in the Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program as team members and leaders.
NREM 105.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program students only.

NREM 192.title: Introduction to Natural Resources and Environmental Management
NREM 192.subject: NREM
NREM 192.description: Introduction to NREM student learning outcomes and scholarly breadth within the department, exposure to on-campus resources, networking with current and former NREM students and external stakeholders, career skills development.

NREM 200.title: Environmental Service Learning II
NREM 200.subject: NREM
NREM 200.description: Experiential service learning course for students participating in the Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program as Hana Hou members. Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program students only.

NREM 203.title: Applied Calculus for Management, Life Sciences, and Human Resilience
NREM 203.subject: NREM
NREM 203.description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Applications of calculus (limits, continuity, derivatives, exponential and logarithmic functions, partials, integrals) to problems in business management, social sciences, and life sciences. Applies symbolic techniques and quantitative methods in problem solving, utilizes concept of proof as a chain of inferences, and promotes development of reasoning skills and mathematical logic in bridging theory and practice.

NREM 210.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
NREM 210.subject: NREM
NREM 210.description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

NREM 220.title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
NREM 220.subject: NREM
NREM 220.description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included.

NREM 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
NREM 251.subject: NREM
NREM 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

NREM 292.title: Internship Preparation
NREM 292.subject: NREM
NREM 292.description: Exploration of internship and career opportunities for NREM majors. Development of career-building skills, including resume, interview, and professional networking.

NREM 301.title: Natural Resources Management
NREM 301.subject: NREM
NREM 301.description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife.
NREM 301.prereq_raw: ( NREM 251 / TPSS 251 or NREM 210 ; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

NREM 301L.title: Natural Resources Management Lab
NREM 301L.subject: NREM
NREM 301L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory and field methods covering biological and physical principles and concepts in natural resource management. Emphasis on basic field measurement techniques, computer skills commonly used in managing natural resources and writing scientific lab reports.
NREM 301L.prereq_raw: NREM 192 with a minimum grade of C-.

NREM 302.title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
NREM 302.subject: NREM
NREM 302.description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawaiʻi state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues.
NREM 302.prereq_raw: NREM 210 / PEPS 210 / SUST 210 or NREM 251 / SOCS 251 / TPSS 251 or ( BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or ( ERTH 101 or higher); and NREM 220 / SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses.

NREM 304.title: Fundamentals of Soil Science
NREM 304.subject: NREM
NREM 304.description: Origin, development, properties, management of tropical soils; classification of Hawaiian soils.
NREM 304.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

NREM 304L.title: Fundamentals of Soil Science Laboratory
NREM 304L.subject: NREM
NREM 304L.description: Field and analytical methods for exploring the origin, development, properties, and management of soils, with an emphasis on tropical and Hawaiian soils.
NREM 304L.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C.

NREM 306.title: Environmental Ethics
NREM 306.subject: NREM
NREM 306.description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making.
NREM 306.prereq_raw: NREM 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103 .

NREM 310.title: Statistics in Agriculture and Human Resources
NREM 310.subject: NREM
NREM 310.description: Theory, applications, and presentation of statistical reasoning. Descriptive, probability, and inferential reasoning for one-variable analysis with extensions to multiple variable cases.

NREM 311.title: Current Topics in Plant Science
NREM 311.subject: NREM
NREM 311.description: An undergraduate seminar that provides the presentation and discussion of topics of current relevance to students preparing for careers in applied plant sciences. Oral focus designation.
NREM 311.prereq_raw: NREM 210 or TPSS 200 / SUST 211 , or consent.

NREM 341.title: Managerial Accounting
NREM 341.subject: NREM
NREM 341.description: Principles and methods of agricultural accounting. Preparing and interpreting financial statements. Sources and costs of credit, capital budgeting, tax management, estate planning.
NREM 341.prereq_raw: NREM 220 / SUST 220 or ECON 130 or consent.

NREM 351.title: Enterprise Management
NREM 351.subject: NREM
NREM 351.description: Introduction of practical concepts and methods used in business management. Introduce broad range of business strategies. Understand the critical role each strategy plays. Facilitate student’s practice of analytical and critical thinking through case studies.

NREM 358.title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
NREM 358.subject: NREM
NREM 358.description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies.
NREM 358.prereq_raw: NREM 220 / SUST 220 or ECON 130 or consent.

NREM 380.title: Tropical Forestry/Agroforestry
NREM 380.subject: NREM
NREM 380.description: Biophysical and socioeconomic description and analysis of major tropical forestry and agroforestry management systems, including Hawaiʻi and the Pacific Basin. The role of traditional land use, pressures from regional and global development, and efforts to create sustainable, diverse systems for rural communities will be discussed.
NREM 380.prereq_raw: CHEM 151 or higher and BIOL 171 or higher.

NREM 399.title: Directed Study
NREM 399.subject: NREM
NREM 399.description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students qualified to carry on advanced study.

NREM 410.title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
NREM 410.subject: NREM
NREM 410.description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.
NREM 410.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

NREM 412.title: Environmental Biochemistry
NREM 412.subject: NREM
NREM 412.description: Biochemical and chemical principles of occurrence, distribution, biotic and abiotic conversion, fate, and impact of synthetic and natural molecules in the environment. Important pollutants will be used as case studies to illustrate the principles.

NREM 420.title: Community and Natural Resource Management
NREM 420.subject: NREM
NREM 420.description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management.
NREM 420.prereq_raw: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: two social science courses ( with a minimum grade of C-

NREM 429.title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
NREM 429.subject: NREM
NREM 429.description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
NREM 429.prereq_raw: NREM 220 / SUST 220 or ECON 130 , and SUST 310 or ECON 321 ; or consent.

NREM 437.title: Applied UAS Operations for Agriculture and Environment
NREM 437.subject: NREM
NREM 437.description: Applied operations with uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), mission planning, safety, photogrammetry and GIS, personnel management, and payload operation. Focus on topics required for commercial certifications as a remote pilot, agricultural operator, and pesticide applicator.
NREM 437.prereq_raw: completion of FS/FQ, DP, DB, and DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

children.text: DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-

NREM 437.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: STEM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

NREM 440.title: Plural Ecologies: Traditional Ecological Knowledge and Natural Resource Management
NREM 440.subject: NREM
NREM 440.description: Through readings, videos, lectures, discussions, and case study analysis, students will learn how TEK systems develop, evolve, are challenged, and persist around the world and how they support the sustainability of landscapes and seascapes globally.
NREM 440.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

NREM 450.title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
NREM 450.subject: NREM
NREM 450.description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawaiʻi.
NREM 450.prereq_raw: BIOL 172 (with a minimum grade of C-)or consent.

NREM 458.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
NREM 458.subject: NREM
NREM 458.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
NREM 458.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356

NREM 460.title: Sustainable Nutrient Management in Agroecosystems
NREM 460.subject: NREM
NREM 460.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Biological, chemical, and physical processes governing the cycling of nutrients in agroecosystems, crop and livestock production, and the effects on surrounding unmanaged ecosystems.
NREM 460.prereq_raw: ( TPSS 304 and CHEM 161 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

NREM 461.title: Soil and Water Conservation
NREM 461.subject: NREM
NREM 461.description: Past and present issues in soil and water conservation will be examined. Principles of erosion, conservation tillage, irrigation, and drainage will be discussed. Land-based threats to coastal zones and watershed management will also be covered.

NREM 463.title: Irrigation and Water Management
NREM 463.subject: NREM
NREM 463.description: Basic soil-water-plant relationships, irrigation water requirements, irrigation efficiencies, different methods of irrigation, planning, design and management of an irrigation system, fertigation and impact of irrigation on soil and water quality.
NREM 463.prereq_raw: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 (or equivalent), or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 ( or equivalent), or consent

NREM 467.title: Natural Resources Conservation Planning
NREM 467.subject: NREM
NREM 467.description: Combined lecture and hands-on field course on theory and practice of natural resource conservation planning. Includes individual and group projects.
NREM 467.prereq_raw: Recommended: at least one upper division course in soils, natural resources, planning, physical geography, or related area; or consent.

children.text: Recommended: at least one upper division course in soils, natural resources, planning, physical geography,

NREM 467.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: undergraduate junior or senior or graduate standing.

NREM 475.title: Plant Nutrient Diagnosis in the Tropics
NREM 475.subject: NREM
NREM 475.description: Designed for students to identify essential nutrients required by plants; diagnose nutrient disorders in plants; and propose environmentally sound solutions to correct disorders.

NREM 477.title: Geographic Information Systems for Resource Managers
NREM 477.subject: NREM
NREM 477.description: Combined lecture-lab on the basic concepts and principles of geographic information systems, remote sensing, and global positioning system. Practical skills to be developed by solving real natural resources and environmental problems.
NREM 477.prereq_raw: either NREM 203 (or concurrent) or NREM 310 (or concurrent), and NREM 301 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

NREM 480.title: Applied Forest Ecology
NREM 480.subject: NREM
NREM 480.description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources).
NREM 480.prereq_raw: ( NREM 301 / SUST 311 and NREM 380 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

NREM 490.title: Hoʻokâhua: ʻāina Based Leadership Education (ABLE)
NREM 490.subject: NREM
NREM 490.description: Hoʻokâhua: is an ʻāina based leadership course encompassing Hawaiian culture, Environmental Science, Law & Policy, Planning and Community Development to equip students to care for, guard, and govern natural resources they care about.

NREM 491.title: Topics in Natural Resources and Environmental Management
NREM 491.subject: NREM
NREM 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

NREM 492.title: Internship Experience
NREM 492.subject: NREM
NREM 492.description: Internship work experience for NREM majors. Completion of writing assignments with a minimum of 4,000 words.

NREM 494.title: Environmental Problem Solving
NREM 494.subject: NREM
NREM 494.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Senior-level capstone for NREM. Ecosystem management within problem-solving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications.
NREM 494.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or consent.

NREM 499.title: Directed Study
NREM 499.subject: NREM
NREM 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

NREM 600.title: Foundations of Natural Resource and Environmental Management and Policy
NREM 600.subject: NREM
NREM 600.description: Critical evaluation of environmental and social components of NREM and policy. Students develop research skills and integrative knowledge important for all resource managers in, e.g., ecology, applied economics, hydrology, policy/management, soils, and human dimensions.
NREM 600.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

NREM 601.title: Social-Ecological Systems Analysis of Natural Resource and Environmental Management
NREM 601.subject: NREM
NREM 601.description: Case study approach to building the structural and behavioral framework for complex, dynamic systems underlying sustainable NREM and policy, emphasizing the transdisciplinary interactions of the ecological and economic components.
NREM 601.prereq_raw: NREM 600 (with a minimum grade of B-), and ( ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and BIOL 171 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

NREM 610.title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
NREM 610.subject: NREM
NREM 610.description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

NREM 611.title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
NREM 611.subject: NREM
NREM 611.description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required.
NREM 611.prereq_raw: grade of C- or above in ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , or consent.

NREM 612.title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
NREM 612.subject: NREM
NREM 612.description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings.
NREM 612.prereq_raw: NREM 301 / SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent

NREM 620.title: Kaiaulu: Care and Collaborative Management of Natural Resources
NREM 620.subject: NREM
NREM 620.description: Engagement with theory and practice of collaboration to care for natural resources. Topics include community based management, common property, Hawaiian knowledge, co-management, and access through readings, discussion, and projects with Hawaiʻi communities.

NREM 625.title: ʻImi ʻIke: Social Science Field Methods for Environmental Research
NREM 625.subject: NREM
NREM 625.description: Students learn and apply social science research methods tailored to natural resource management and environmental issues to a class project with Hawaiʻi community. Emphasis on qualitative and participatory approaches.

NREM 627.title: Applied Microeconomic Analysis
NREM 627.subject: NREM
NREM 627.description: Economic applications to the agricultural and nonagricultural industries are emphasized. Econometric techniques are used to estimate demand, supply, production and cost functions which are analyzed in terms of economic theory and market information.

NREM 631.title: Sustainable Agriculture Seminar
NREM 631.subject: NREM
NREM 631.description: Critical evaluation of existing and alternative cropping systems from a long-term perspective. Value conflicts and resolution.
NREM 631.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing, and consent.

NREM 637.title: Resource Economics
NREM 637.subject: NREM
NREM 637.description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

NREM 640.title: Land Systems Science
NREM 640.subject: NREM
NREM 640.description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socioecological system function.
NREM 640.prereq_raw: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461 .

NREM 650.title: Soil Plant Nutrient Relations
NREM 650.subject: NREM
NREM 650.description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Soil-plant interactions, emphasis on characteristics of tropical soils and plants influencing nutrient uptake by plants. Diagnostic methods to identify nutrient deficiencies and element toxicity.
NREM 650.prereq_raw: TPSS 450 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

NREM 652.title: Information Research Skills
NREM 652.subject: NREM
NREM 652.description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

NREM 658.title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
NREM 658.subject: NREM
NREM 658.description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate.

NREM 660.title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
NREM 660.subject: NREM
NREM 660.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

NREM 662.title: Watershed Hydrology
NREM 662.subject: NREM
NREM 662.description: Theory and application of basic hydrologic processes and management occurring on small islands watersheds.
NREM 662.prereq_raw: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and PHYS 151 (or equivalent) and NREM 477 or GEO 388 (or equivalent); or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and PHYS 151 ( or equivalent) and NREM 477 or GEO 388 ( or equivalent); or consent

NREM 664.title: Small Watershed Modeling
NREM 664.subject: NREM
NREM 664.description: Introduction to process-based modeling of watershed with emphasis on model applications. Deals with the characterization and simulation of small watershed hydrolic and pollutant transport processes.
NREM 664.prereq_raw: CEE 424 (or concurrent) or ERTH 425 / SUST 425 (or concurrent) or BS degree from NREM, or consent.

NREM 665.title: Coastal Resources Management
NREM 665.subject: NREM
NREM 665.description: Study of coastal systems, estuaries, and coral reefs. Emphasis on interdisciplinary science and integration of coastal ecology, geoscience, and social science. Coastal and marine wildlife-human interactions, environmental pertubations, and management strategies will be discussed.
NREM 665.prereq_raw: advanced undergraduate course work in marine biology, oceanography, geoscience, and sustainability recommended.

children.text: advanced undergraduate course work in marine biology, oceanography, geoscience,

NREM 668.title: People and the Sea: Exploring Multiple Perspectives for Coastal and Marine Systems
NREM 668.subject: NREM
NREM 668.description: Through readings and discussion, this course explores how the social sciences have engaged in marine and coastal spaces and how they contribute to advancing effective and equitable resource management and conservation.

NREM 670.title: Interdisciplinary Methods for Agrarian Systems
NREM 670.subject: NREM
NREM 670.description: Interdisciplinary methodologies for conducting research and impact analyses on agrarian systems, sustainable development, and resource management.

NREM 671.title: International Agricultural Systems
NREM 671.subject: NREM
NREM 671.description: Analysis of trends and strategies in international agricultural research and development. International agricultural research centers (IARC), Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), university networks and consortia, and private voluntary organizations (PVOs).
NREM 671.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing, and consent.

NREM 677.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
NREM 677.subject: NREM
NREM 677.description: Fundamentals, techniques, and applications of remote sensing for natural resource assessments and environmental monitoring. Lab consisting of field radiometric exercises, computer modeling of energy-matter interaction, processing, and analysis of remotely sensed imagery.
NREM 677.prereq_raw: one physics course (e.g. PHYS 151 ), one calculus course (e.g. NREM 203 ), and one statistics course (e.g. NREM 310 ), or consent. Recommended: either GEO 470 or ERTH 460 or one introductory remote sensing course.

children.text: ) , one calculus course ( e.g. NREM 203 ) , and one statistics course ( e.g. NREM 310 ) , or consent . Recommended: either GEO 470 or ERTH 460 or one introductory remote sensing course

NREM 680.title: Ecosystem Ecology
NREM 680.subject: NREM
NREM 680.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of ecosystem ecology with emphasis on tropical forests, human impacts, and global environmental change. Factors controlling ecosystem structure, productivity, nutrient cycling, plant-soil-atmosphere interactions, and energy balance. Field and laboratory methods in ecosystem science.
NREM 680.prereq_raw: advanced undergraduate coursework in ecology and soil science; graduate standing; and consent.

NREM 682.title: Restoration Ecology
NREM 682.subject: NREM
NREM 682.description: Graduate seminar on foundations of restoration ecology, application of ecological theory to restoration practice. Emphasis on restoration of structure and function in degraded terrestrial ecosystems using case studies from Hawaiʻi and around the world.
NREM 682.prereq_raw: advanced undergraduate ecology course and graduate standing, or consent. Completion of NREM 680 recommended, but not required.

children.text: Completion of NREM 680 recommended, but not required

NREM 685.title: Landscape Ecology
NREM 685.subject: NREM
NREM 685.description: Focuses on the history, theories, and contemporary views of landscapes; including scale, land cover, land use, landscape metrics, disturbance regimes, land management, landscape change, the relationship of landscapes to species, and modeling.
NREM 685.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students, or consent.

NREM 690.title: Conservation Biology
NREM 690.subject: NREM
NREM 690.description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.

NREM 691.title: Advanced Topics in Natural Resources and Environmental Management
NREM 691.subject: NREM
NREM 691.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems at an advanced level. Offered by visiting or existing faculty as a special course.
NREM 691.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

NREM 695.title: Capstone Preparation in NREM
NREM 695.subject: NREM
NREM 695.description: Preparation for NREM Master’s Plan B capstone experience.
NREM 695.prereq_raw: NREM 600 and NREM 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and one graduate methods course (or concurrent).

NREM 696.title: Capstone Experience in NREM
NREM 696.subject: NREM
NREM 696.prereq_raw: ( NREM 695 and NREM 601 ) with a minimum grade of B-, or consent.

NREM 701.title: Research Seminar
NREM 701.subject: NREM
NREM 701.description: Presentation and discussion of student research proposals, theses and dissertations, and research presentations by NREM faculty, students, and invited speakers.

NSCI 101.title: Natural Sciences and Life-Pulling the Puzzles Apart
NSCI 101.subject: NSCI
NSCI 101.description: Journey through the Natural Sciences finding fun, excitement, and success in science, mathematics, engineering, medicine, and all that is the natural sciences. Focus upon challenging worldviews of belief, invention, impact, and ethics.

NSCI 501.title: Seminar for Science Teachers
NSCI 501.subject: NSCI
NSCI 501.description: Seminar and discussions of current and significant topics and problems in science where teachers can exchange new and innovative teaching ideas and strategies.

NSCI 503.title: Computers in Classroom
NSCI 503.subject: NSCI
NSCI 503.description: Combined lecture, laboratory and discussion on the use of computers as a teaching tool in the classroom. To be taught in a hands-on manner appropriate for the science teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

NSCI 504.title: Mathematics Workshop for Teachers
NSCI 504.subject: NSCI
NSCI 504.description: An in-depth study of topics from intermediate and high school mathematics. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

NSCI 505.title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
NSCI 505.subject: NSCI
NSCI 505.description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

NSCI 619.title: Seminar on Science Teaching
NSCI 619.subject: NSCI
NSCI 619.description: Effective teaching methods; organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audio-visual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

NSEB 099.title: National Student Exchange
NSEB 099.subject: NSEB
NSEB 099.description: Study at another campus through National Student Exchange (NSE). Transfer credits earned upon successful completion of courses on exchange.

NURS 200.title: Introduction to Professional Nursing I
NURS 200.subject: NURS
NURS 200.description: This first level course focuses on nursing practice and education. Professional responsibilities in the practice of nursing are emphasized.

NURS 201.title: Introduction to Professional Nursing II
NURS 201.subject: NURS
NURS 201.description: This second level course builds on the knowledge and skills gained in the first level and focuses on professional responsibilities in nursing practice and education.

NURS 210.title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan
NURS 210.subject: NURS
NURS 210.description: Focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. It introduces the nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.
NURS 210.prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent.

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

NURS 210L.title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan Lab
NURS 210L.subject: NURS
NURS 210L.description: Clinical course focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. Introduces nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.

NURS 211.title: Professionalism in Nursing
NURS 211.subject: NURS
NURS 211.description: Professional responsibilities of nursing practice are examined through the history of nursing, practice and education, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, and nursing roles.
NURS 211.prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent.

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

NURS 212.title: Pathophysiology
NURS 212.subject: NURS
NURS 212.description: Focus on pathophysiological concepts that are basic to understanding illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human responses, which serve as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning.
NURS 212.prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent.

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

NURS 213.title: Pharmacology for Nursing
NURS 213.subject: NURS
NURS 213.description: This course will help students to gain knowledge of the mechanism of action, toxicity, adverse reactions, side effects, therapeutic uses, and nursing implications of the major categories of drugs.

NURS 220.title: Health and Illness I
NURS 220.subject: NURS
NURS 220.description: Focuses on nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness.
NURS 220.prereq_raw: NURS 210 , NURS 210L , and NURS 212 , or departmental approval.

NURS 220L.title: Health and Illness I Lab
NURS 220L.subject: NURS
NURS 220L.description: Clinical course focuses on using nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness. Nursing skills are integrated into clinical experiences.

NURS 301.title: Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Health Promotion
NURS 301.subject: NURS
NURS 301.description: Provides an introduction to the HSNC Competencies and spiraling of concepts and is based on the assumption of student responsibility for learning. Emphasis on writing instruction, and research evidence to support nursing care.

NURS 306.title: Statistics in Nursing Research
NURS 306.subject: NURS
NURS 306.description: Focuses on the basic concepts and applications of statistics as applied to nursing research.

NURS 321.title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health
NURS 321.subject: NURS
NURS 321.description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools for providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care.
NURS 321.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 321L.title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health Lab
NURS 321L.subject: NURS
NURS 321L.description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools when providing culturally sensitive, family-centered care. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession.
NURS 321L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 322.title: Child and Family Health
NURS 322.subject: NURS
NURS 322.description: Nursing care and health promotion for children and families. Emphasis on concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings.
NURS 322.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 322L.title: Child and Family Health Lab
NURS 322L.subject: NURS
NURS 322L.description: Nursing care and health promotion lab for children and families. Application of concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings.
NURS 322L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 340.title: Contemporary Ethical Issues in Health Care
NURS 340.subject: NURS
NURS 340.description: Explore contemporary ethical issues and their legal implications in health care. Focus on decision-making in professional practice and social policy formation.
NURS 340.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

NURS 343.title: Gerontology: Its Nursing Implications
NURS 343.subject: NURS
NURS 343.description: Explores attitudes toward the aged, biological and psychological aspects, ethnicity, sexuality, nutritional problems, community resources, other related topics.
NURS 343.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

NURS 344.title: Nursing in the Multicultural Milieu
NURS 344.subject: NURS
NURS 344.description: Relates values, beliefs, attitudes, family organization, lifestyles, and health practices in different ethnic groups to health-care and nursing practice.
NURS 344.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

NURS 360.title: Health and Illness III
NURS 360.subject: NURS
NURS 360.description: Focuses on complex situations requiring strong recognition skills, and rapid decision making. The evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.
NURS 360.prereq_raw: NURS 321 , NURS 321L , NURS 322 , and NURS 322L , or departmental approval.

NURS 360L.title: Health and Illness III Lab
NURS 360L.subject: NURS
NURS 360L.description: Clinical course focuses on complex situations requiring application of strong recognition skills and rapid decision making. Evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.

NURS 361.title: Health Education and Promotion
NURS 361.subject: NURS
NURS 361.description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups, and the larger public.
NURS 361.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

NURS 363.title: Introduction to Nursing Research
NURS 363.subject: NURS
NURS 363.description: Introduction to the research process and an understanding of the applicability of the scientific approach to nursing. Analysis and resolution of contemporary medical ethics issues in research and general nursing practice are primary focuses.

NURS 364.title: Principles of Nursing Research and Evidence-Based Practice
NURS 364.subject: NURS
NURS 364.description: Introduces the process for research application and evidence-based practice. Includes: EBP questions, evidence sources, literature search and synthesis, levels and quality of evidence, and determination of clinical significance. Focus on contemporary medical ethics issues.

NURS 399.title: Directed Reading/Research I, II
NURS 399.subject: NURS
NURS 399.description: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.

NURS 402.title: Student Ambassador Program
NURS 402.subject: NURS
NURS 402.description: Focuses on professional leadership development, mentorship, and professional skills for nurses. Students learn to be representatives between the Department of Nursing and alumni, prospective students, and the general public.
NURS 402.prereq_raw: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador.

prereq_tree.text: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador

NURS 411.title: NCLEX Review
NURS 411.subject: NURS
NURS 411.description: Overview of the NCLEX-RN licensure examination and regular, systematic practice in taking multiple choice examinations.
NURS 411.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

NURS 420.title: Cooperative Education in Nursing
NURS 420.subject: NURS
NURS 420.description: A two-semester course with seminar in professional role development in addition to paid work experience in nursing at a local agency. Upper division

NURS 421.title: Nursing Internship
NURS 421.subject: NURS
NURS 421.description: Practicum experience for students to learn the role of the professional nurse by building on previously learned knowledge and skills in the nursing program.

NURS 431.title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies
NURS 431.subject: NURS
NURS 431.description: Survey of complementary and alternative therapies used for health promotion of individuals and groups.
NURS 431.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Open to non-nursing majors with consent.

NURS 432.title: Veteran Healthcare, Education, and Cultural Needs
NURS 432.subject: NURS
NURS 432.description: Provides a broad overview of the Veteran-Military population and their unique culture, educational, and health care needs. Open to non-nursing majors.

NURS 449.title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
NURS 449.subject: NURS
NURS 449.description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society. Junior standing or higher.

NURS 450.title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing
NURS 450.subject: NURS
NURS 450.description: Theory course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing with an emphasis on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 450L.title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing Lab
NURS 450L.subject: NURS
NURS 450L.description: Clinical course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing emphasizing application of strategies to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local, national, and international levels. Emphasis on oral and writing instruction.

NURS 451.title: Population Health Nursing
NURS 451.subject: NURS
NURS 451.description: Theory on population and global health nursing with emphasis on analysis of strategies to address concepts of health disparities, inequity, social justice issues, and ethics which impact health outcomes of populations.
NURS 451.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

NURS 451L.title: Population Health Nursing Lab
NURS 451L.subject: NURS
NURS 451L.description: Clinic on population health nursing emphasizing application of strategies to address health disparities, inequity, social justice issues, and ethics impacting population health outcomes. Emphasis on oral and writing instruction.

NURS 452.title: Cultural Aspects of Health Management in Populations Indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia
NURS 452.subject: NURS
NURS 452.description: Focuses on cultural aspects that influence health management in indigenous populations of Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia, with an emphasis on development of culturally sensitive strategies to promote and improve health management.
NURS 452.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Undergraduate majors only.

NURS 453.title: Introduction to Genetics and Genomics in Nursing Practice
NURS 453.subject: NURS
NURS 453.description: Fundamentals of genetics and genomics, including principles of inheritance in humans, cellular function, mutations, epigenetics, and implications for health and disease. Includes overview of topics involving genetics/genomics in clinical settings and health care delivery.

NURS 460.title: Complex Nursing and Leadership
NURS 460.subject: NURS
NURS 460.description: Theory course emphasizes the judgments, knowledge, and skills necessary for nursing practice, including case management and quality management experiences. The experience focuses on complex clinical judgments, interdisciplinary team functioning, and leadership.

NURS 460L.title: Complex Nursing and Leadership Lab
NURS 460L.subject: NURS
NURS 460L.description: Clinical course emphasizes application of knowledge and skills for nursing practice, including case management and quality management experiences. Focuses on complex clinical judgments, interdisciplinary team functioning, and leadership. Emphasis on writing instruction.

NURS 461.title: Advanced Pathophysiology
NURS 461.subject: NURS
NURS 461.description: Provides an advanced understanding of pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying human illness across the lifespan. Provides a foundation for formulating clinical decisions and therapeutic plans of care to promote disease prevention and health promotion.

NURS 462.title: Community Health Nursing for Executive RN
NURS 462.subject: NURS
NURS 462.description: Theory focuses on community health nursing with an emphasis for the Executive RN on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 462L.title: Community Health Nursing for Executive RN Field Work
NURS 462L.subject: NURS
NURS 462L.description: Field work focuses on community health nursing with an emphasis for the Executive RN on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 465.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing
NURS 465.subject: NURS
NURS 465.description: Examination of human responses to psychiatric and mental illness in relation to physiologic, psychological, social, cultural, and environmental concepts. Emphasis on self-awareness, therapeutic communication, and holistic, individualized health-related outcomes.

NURS 465L.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing Lab
NURS 465L.subject: NURS
NURS 465L.description: Application of the nursing process involving human responses to psychiatric and mental illness in relation to physiologic, psychological, social, cultural, and environmental concepts. Emphasis on self-awareness, therapeutic communication, and holistic, individualized health-related outcomes.

NURS 470.title: Nursing and Leadership Immersion
NURS 470.subject: NURS
NURS 470.description: Nursing theory course designed to enhance proficiency in complex clinical judgments, interprofessional team collaboration, and leadership. Focus is on knowledge and skills needed for nursing practice, including case management and quality management.

NURS 470L.title: Nursing and Leadership Immersion Lab
NURS 470L.subject: NURS
NURS 470L.description: Clinical nursing course develops proficiency in complex clinical judgments, interprofessional team collaboration, and leadership skills in nursing. Application of knowledge, incorporation of case management and quality management experiences, and writing instruction are highlighted.

NURS 481.title: Nursing Honors Research Project
NURS 481.subject: NURS
NURS 481.description: Involves directed, mentored research study for Nursing Honors students with their honors advisor. The course grade depends on meeting objectives negotiated each course semester.

NURS 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
NURS 499.subject: NURS
NURS 499.description: Planned individualized study or research in specialized area related to interprofessional collaborative practice.
NURS 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Senior undergraduate NURS students only.

NURS 501.title: Professionalism in Nursing
NURS 501.subject: NURS
NURS 501.description: Introduction to history of nursing and leaders in the field. Will explore contemporary nursing issues and research. Strategies to foster adherence to a professional code of ethics in practice will be examined.
NURS 501.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 502.title: Pathophysiology
NURS 502.subject: NURS
NURS 502.description: Web-enhanced on pathophysiologic concepts as a basis of illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human response, which serves as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning.
NURS 502.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 503.title: Pharmacology for Nursing Practice
NURS 503.subject: NURS
NURS 503.description: Essential principles of pharmacology using a pathophysiologic approach with emphasis on administering medications and evaluating their effects.
NURS 503.coreq_raw: NURS 501 , NURS 502 , NURS 504 , NURS 504L , NURS 505 , NURS 505L .
NURS 503.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 504.title: Health Assessment
NURS 504.subject: NURS
NURS 504.description: Concepts/theories of health assessment, data collection, and analysis to distinguish between health/wellness, risk factors or health deviations across the lifespan. Attention to principles of communication and interviewing.
NURS 504.coreq_raw: NURS 501 , NURS 502 , NURS 503 , NURS 504L , NURS 505 , NURS 505L .
NURS 504.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 504L.title: Health Assessment Lab
NURS 504L.subject: NURS
NURS 504L.description: Application of assessment skills in dry lab and clinical settings, with attention to principles of communication, interviewing and physical examination skills.
NURS 504L.coreq_raw: NURS 501 , NURS 502 , NURS 503 , NURS 504 , NURS 505 , NURS 505L .
NURS 504L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 505.title: Foundations of Nursing Science
NURS 505.subject: NURS
NURS 505.description: Nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities.
NURS 505.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 505L.title: Foundations of Nursing Science and Practice Lab
NURS 505L.subject: NURS
NURS 505L.description: Application of the nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities.
NURS 505L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 507.title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing
NURS 507.subject: NURS
NURS 507.description: Biopsychosocial theories of human behavior related to function, alteration, and/or disruption of mental processes; reviews current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families.
NURS 507.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 507L.title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing Clinic/ Lab
NURS 507L.subject: NURS
NURS 507L.description: Application of current knowledge regarding human behavior related to function, alteration, and/ or disruption of mental processes; applies current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/ psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families.
NURS 507L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 508.title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families
NURS 508.subject: NURS
NURS 508.description: Introduction to the theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care of the perinatal family. Women’s and men’s health issues are discussed.
NURS 508.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 508L.title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families Clinical/Lab
NURS 508L.subject: NURS
NURS 508L.description: Application of the nursing care of the mother and family. The student will apply clinical and theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care for women experiencing customary and complicated perinatal processes.
NURS 508L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 509.title: Nursing Care of Children and Families
NURS 509.subject: NURS
NURS 509.description: Focus on well-child care and nursing care of children with acute and chronic conditions. Pediatric concepts include family-centered, developmentally appropriate, and atraumatic care. Lab course taken concurrently.
NURS 509.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 509L.title: Nursing Care of Children and Families Clinical/Lab
NURS 509L.subject: NURS
NURS 509L.description: Focus on well-child care and nursing care of children with acute and chronic conditions. Pediatric concepts include family-centered, developmentally appropriate, and atraumatic care. Critical thinking, clinical judgment, and EBP are applied.
NURS 509L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 513.title: Acute Care Nursing
NURS 513.subject: NURS
NURS 513.description: Addresses the bio/ psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatment in the acute setting will be covered.
NURS 513.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 513L.title: Acute Care Nursing Lab
NURS 513L.subject: NURS
NURS 513L.description: Application of the bio/psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Application of health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatments in the acute care setting.
NURS 513L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 517.title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice
NURS 517.subject: NURS
NURS 517.description: Examination of continuity of care for clients with complex needs. Emphasis on application of leadership, management, and quality improvement in the clinical setting.
NURS 517.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 517L.title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice Lab
NURS 517L.subject: NURS
NURS 517L.description: Deliver comprehensive nursing care to clients with complex needs in community and/or acute care settings. Leadership, management, and quality improvement competencies are stressed.
NURS 517L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 518.title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing
NURS 518.subject: NURS
NURS 518.description: Introduces community and public health nursing with an emphasis on application to nursing practice in the community and public health settings.
NURS 518.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 518L.title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing Lab
NURS 518L.subject: NURS
NURS 518L.description: Application of health promotion, risk reduction, and disease prevention and detection and nursing care treatments in the community setting.
NURS 518L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 600.title: Epidemiology for Advanced Nursing
NURS 600.subject: NURS
NURS 600.description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods, with an emphasis on its application to nursing practice.

NURS 605.title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
NURS 605.subject: NURS
NURS 605.description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and prevention of common health and illness conditions with culturally diverse individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes didactic (30 hrs) and fieldwork (45 hrs).
NURS 605.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: classified graduate student status in SONDH.

NURS 607.title: Applied Biostatistics and Epidemiology for Nurses in Advance Practice
NURS 607.subject: NURS
NURS 607.description: Investigation of epidemiologic and biostatistical methods for advance practice nurses within healthcare settings and complementary roles of epi/biostatistics in shaping advance nurse practice. Application of epi/biostatistical approaches to the design and analysis of DNP projects.
NURS 607.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or permission.

NURS 608.title: Genetics and Health Care
NURS 608.subject: NURS
NURS 608.description: Addresses the scientific, psycho-social, ethical, cultural, and spiritual issues surrounding genetic disease, genetic testing, and living with an inherited condition.
NURS 608.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

NURS 609.title: Health Politics & Policy
NURS 609.subject: NURS
NURS 609.description: Review of contemporary national health policies, issues and concerns; and international comparison of health policy evolution; includes didactic and 45 hours of fieldwork experience learning.

NURS 611.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Assessment and Diagnosis
NURS 611.subject: NURS
NURS 611.description: Identification and synthesis of pertinent biopsychosocial and cultural data to complete advanced psychiatric-mental health assessments and diagnoses.

NURS 612.title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning
NURS 612.subject: NURS
NURS 612.description: Provides a framework for the development of advanced skills for systematic and comprehensive data collection, organization, precise recording, accurate assessment and communication of data reflecting the biopsychophysical status of individuals across the life span.
NURS 612.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 612L.title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning Lab
NURS 612L.subject: NURS
NURS 612L.description: Clinical lab and practicum for advanced practice nursing. Emphasis on integration of knowledge, skills and outcome evaluation.
NURS 612L.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 613.title: Pathophysiology for Advanced Practice
NURS 613.subject: NURS
NURS 613.description: Provides an understanding of normal physiological mechanisms and pathological processes to serve as a foundation for clinical assessment, decision making, and clinical management across the lifespan.
NURS 613.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrollment as a classified student in a graduate program in SONDH. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 615.title: Clinical Skills and Procedures for Advanced Practice Nursing
NURS 615.subject: NURS
NURS 615.description: Clinical laboratory that focuses on clinical skills and procedures performed by advanced practice nurses (nurse practitioners and/or clinical nurse specialists). Topics will vary by section and semester.
NURS 615.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS and NURD majors only.

NURS 616.title: Mental Health in Primary Care
NURS 616.subject: NURS
NURS 616.description: Augment APRN students’ understanding, evaluation, treatment plan development, and competence to care for patients with mental health and psychiatric disorders treatment plans across the lifespan in the primary care settings.
NURS 616.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 617.title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-A
NURS 617.subject: NURS
NURS 617.description: The first of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis, and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting.
NURS 617.prereq_raw: NURS 612 , NURS 612L , and NURS 613 ; no waiver.

NURS 618.title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-B
NURS 618.subject: NURS
NURS 618.description: Second of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting.
NURS 618.prereq_raw: NURS 612 , NURS 612L , and NURS 613 ; no waiver.

NURS 619.title: Emerging Diseases & Implications for Advanced Nursing Practice
NURS 619.subject: NURS
NURS 619.description: Selected emerging diseases are examined within historical context, known science (past and present) and societal factors that influence prevention, detection, treatment and containment strategies. Considerations for advanced public health nursing practice are identified and examined.

NURS 620.title: Nursing Research, Theory, and Evidence-Based Practice
NURS 620.subject: NURS
NURS 620.description: Examination of theory, research, and evidence-based inquiry to support evidence-based practice among MS prepared nurses.
NURS 620.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: enrollment as a classified student in the graduate degree program in SONDH.

NURS 621.title: Acute and Episodic Care Management
NURS 621.subject: NURS
NURS 621.description: Diagnosis and management of health and illness with emphasis on clients with common acute/episodic conditions seen in context of family and community. Advanced practice nurse-client relationship, practice roles, and culturally relevant care are included.
NURS 621.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 622.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Issues and Roles
NURS 622.subject: NURS
NURS 622.description: Exploration of major issues and roles in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing.
NURS 622.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 623.title: Psychopharmacology
NURS 623.subject: NURS
NURS 623.description: Survey of biopsychological bases of and biotherapies for major mental disorders, including the schizophrenias, affective and personality disorders, pediatric and geriatric problems, and neurological dysfunctions with appropriate applications to health care.
NURS 623.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

NURS 624.title: Adolescent and Family Psychiatric- Mental Health Care
NURS 624.subject: NURS
NURS 624.description: Seminar on theory/research in advanced psychiatric-mental health nursing of adolescents and families representing diverse populations. Emphasis on developmental and nursing theories, evidence-based practice, therapeutic modalities and disease management of psychiatric illness.

NURS 625.title: Advanced Nursing Roles
NURS 625.subject: NURS
NURS 625.description: Provides students with an understanding of different roles of the advanced professional nurse; an ability to proactively manage the environment of their specialty practice; includes 45 hours of field work experience.

NURS 626.title: Advanced Population Health Nursing
NURS 626.subject: NURS
NURS 626.description: Introduction to the core competencies, key theoretical models and concepts that guide advanced population health nursing. The student will initiate their professional portfolio, which must be completed during the last semester of the MS program.

NURS 627.title: Child/Family Health Assessment
NURS 627.subject: NURS
NURS 627.description: (2 Sem, 8-hr Lab) Opportunity to develop specialized clinical competence in assessment of children as a basis for the development of clinical specialization. Development of the individual’s potential toward health maintenance functioning.
NURS 627.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 628.title: Child Health: Special Health Needs
NURS 628.subject: NURS
NURS 628.description: Provides a theoretical basis required for specialized clinical competence in adapting recent findings on child/ parent assessments, social and health risk indicators, the role of environment, and multidisciplinary settings in the care of pediatrics.
NURS 628.prereq_raw: NURS 612 / NURS 612L , NURS 633 and NURS 634 ; or consent.

NURS 629.title: Pharmacology for Nurses in Advanced Practice
NURS 629.subject: NURS
NURS 629.description: Prepares APNs to evaluate, monitor, and prescribe pharmaceuticals to treat acute and chronic illness across lifespan. Emphasis on drug indications, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, adverse effects, interactions, monitoring, education, and cost effectiveness. Enrollment as a classified student in a SONDH graduate degree program.
NURS 629.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 630.title: Introduction to Information Technology in Healthcare
NURS 630.subject: NURS
NURS 630.description: Introduction to the use of information systems in healthcare. Selected information systems and data sets are explored with application of results to various patient populations and clinical practice settings.

NURS 631.title: Advanced Psychopharmacology Across the Lifespan
NURS 631.subject: NURS
NURS 631.description: Examines the legal, ethical and therapeutic role of the psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioner (PMHNP) in prescribing psychotropic medications for diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Diverse biopsychosocial perspectives will be considered.

NURS 632.title: Therapeutic Modalities
NURS 632.subject: NURS
NURS 632.description: Therapeutic modalities used in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations.

NURS 633.title: Child Health: Promotion and Maintenance
NURS 633.subject: NURS
NURS 633.description: Presents normal developmental, physiological and social needs of children within the context of family; then focuses on the management of common acute and chronic illnesses of children.
NURS 633.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 634.title: Child Health: Advanced Pediatric Acute/ Chronic Care
NURS 634.subject: NURS
NURS 634.description: Focuses on the evaluation of pediatric clients with higher acuity and more complex management issues. Emphasizes critical analysis of evidence based research in pediatric health care.
NURS 634.prereq_raw: Admission into the PNP and FNP program; NURS 612 / NURS 612L , and NURS 633 .
NURS 634.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.
