NURS 635.title: Women’s Health: Promotion and Maintenance
NURS 635.subject: NURS
NURS 635.description: Provides a foundation of concepts necessary to maintain and promote women’s health, including developmental, physiological and social needs of women of all ages and the management of common health problems and concerns specific to women.
NURS 635.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 636.title: Women’s Health: Special Problem
NURS 636.subject: NURS
NURS 636.description: (2 Sem, 12-hr Lab) Focuses upon assessment and intervention of at-risk and high-risk women during pregnancy, interconception, and the menopausal years. Emphasizes critical analysis of research in pregnancy, family planning, and common gynecological problems.
NURS 636.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 637.title: Population Health Intervention Strategies for Advanced Nurses
NURS 637.subject: NURS
NURS 637.description: Develops advanced skills and knowledge in population health nursing by using epidemiological and system-level data to identify gaps and inequities in care and health outcomes, with a focus on management of chronic conditions.

NURS 638.title: Child and Adolescent Psychiatric-Mental Health
NURS 638.subject: NURS
NURS 638.description: Theory and research in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing of children and adolescents representing culturally diverse populations. Emphasis on growth and development, assessment and diagnosis, and therapeutic modalities.

NURS 639.title: Disciplinary Knowledge I
NURS 639.subject: NURS
NURS 639.description: Exploration of a variety of philosophies of science and examination of factors influencing the development of nursing theory and the emergence of nursing as a discipline.

NURS 640.title: Chronic Illness Management
NURS 640.subject: NURS
NURS 640.description: Management of chronic illness using selected health care systems in culturally diverse communities. Management includes practice, consultation, education, research, and evaluation.
NURS 640.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 641.title: Advanced Nursing in the Global Health Environment
NURS 641.subject: NURS
NURS 641.description: Exploration and analysis of key global health topics of concern for advanced nurses.

NURS 642.title: Health Care Technology and Informatics
NURS 642.subject: NURS
NURS 642.description: Introduction to the field of health care technology and informatics for clinicians through the application of health care information systems.
NURS 642.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to students in other healthcare fields by permission.

NURS 645.title: Health Law
NURS 645.subject: NURS
NURS 645.description: Introduction to medical jurisprudence, medical malpractice, informed consent, health care decisions, medical ethics, the health care industry, managed care, financing health care, and the role of government in health care.
NURS 645.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only; NURS DNP majors only

NURS 646.title: Advanced Psychiatric-Mental Health Practicum
NURS 646.subject: NURS
NURS 646.description: Supervised application of theories, research, and skills for advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations. Includes the program’s capstone experience.

NURS 647.title: Family Systems in Health and Illness
NURS 647.subject: NURS
NURS 647.description: Family systems approach to include selected family theories, family research and family centered culturally sensitive clinical assessment and intervention in health and illness situations.
NURS 647.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

NURS 650.title: Complementary and Traditional Care
NURS 650.subject: NURS
NURS 650.description: A review of theoretical systems and approaches to complementary and traditional care in culturally diverse populations with a focus on wellness. Appropriate for all health-care professionals.

NURS 655.title: Tests and Measurement in Nursing Education
NURS 655.subject: NURS
NURS 655.description: Testing and evaluation applied to nursing education.

NURS 660D.title: Selected Topics in Nursing: developmentally disabled children and their families
NURS 660D.subject: NURS
NURS 660D.description: Advanced study, exploration of special topics in clinical nursing. (D) developmentally disabled children and their families; (I) current issues in professional nursing.
NURS 660D.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent for (D).

NURS 660I.title: Selected Topics in Nursing: current issues in professional nursing
NURS 660I.subject: NURS
NURS 660I.description: Advanced study, exploration of special topics in clinical nursing. (D) developmentally disabled children and their families; (I) current issues in professional nursing.
NURS 660I.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent for (D).

NURS 661.title: Human Resource Management in Healthcare Agencies
NURS 661.subject: NURS
NURS 661.description: Analyze and critically evaluate basic issues, policies and trends in human resource management as it applies to health care agencies.

NURS 662.title: Leadership, Role, Identity and Organizational/System Change
NURS 662.subject: NURS
NURS 662.description: Seminar focused on theoretical and conceptual models of leadership and management as applied to relevant advanced nurses’ roles, their respective populations, and changing healthcare environments.

NURS 663.title: Analysis of Healthcare Delivery Models
NURS 663.subject: NURS
NURS 663.description: Analysis of various clinical management concepts and health-care delivery systems influencing outcomes, process, and costs in the delivery of care.

NURS 664.title: Seminar and Practicum in Nursing Executive Leadership
NURS 664.subject: NURS
NURS 664.description: Supervised practicum to build mid to senior level nursing leadership competencies and facilitate change in complex healthcare organizations.

NURS 665.title: Clinical Economics and Finance
NURS 665.subject: NURS
NURS 665.description: Economic and financial concepts and tools for use in developing and managing patient care processes.

NURS 668.title: Community Based Participatory Research (CBPR) Methods
NURS 668.subject: NURS
NURS 668.description: Focuses on use of CBPR methods to address population level issues amendable to interventions; 15 hours of didactic and 90 hours of field experience are included.

NURS 669.title: Evaluating Research for Evidence-based Practice
NURS 669.subject: NURS
NURS 669.description: Introduces evidence-based practice methods for improving the quality of nursing practice. Develops skills in differentiating quantitative and qualitative research, statistical methods, and searching, critiquing, and synthesizing literature, pertinent to health care issues.

NURS 670.title: Advanced Practice Nursing During Public Health Disasters
NURS 670.subject: NURS
NURS 670.description: The role of the advanced professional nurse in public health preparedness, planning, and response.

NURS 671.title: Biostatistics: Application in the Advanced Nursing Practice Setting
NURS 671.subject: NURS
NURS 671.description: Includes basic bio-statistical techniques and the application of statistical findings to practice programmatic decisions.
NURS 671.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in the Department of Nursing or consent. NURS majors only.

NURS 672.title: Advanced Practice Population Health Nursing Practicum
NURS 672.subject: NURS
NURS 672.description: Student will conduct a complex service project for a public or community based agency. May be taken for 1-6 credits. (45 hours of practicum experience awarded for each one credit of the course)
NURS 672.prereq_raw: 24 credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing or consent.

children.text: 24 credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing

NURS 673.title: Implementation and Evaluation Strategies for Evidence-Based Practice
NURS 673.subject: NURS
NURS 673.description: Using knowledge of translational science, designs an implementation plan for a practice guideline. Determines evaluation methods and selects outcome variables that best measure success. Discusses institutionalization of, and identifies facilitators and barriers to, practice change.
NURS 673.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

NURS 675.title: Advanced Practice Clinical
NURS 675.subject: NURS
NURS 675.description: Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing.
NURS 675.prereq_raw: NURS 612 / NURS 612L , NURS 613 , and NURS 629 (or concurrent).
NURS 675.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 676.title: Primary Care I Seminar: Health Assessment
NURS 676.subject: NURS
NURS 676.description: Seminar to discuss the evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management. Utilization of clinical cases and current literature on health care assessment.

NURS 676L.title: Primary Care I Lab (beginning level): Health Assessment
NURS 676L.subject: NURS
NURS 676L.description: Beginning level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients for advanced practice nursing students in primary care settings.

NURS 677.title: Primary Care II Seminar: Management of the Adult
NURS 677.subject: NURS
NURS 677.description: Intermediate level seminar where students discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients.

NURS 677L.title: Primary Care II Lab (intermediate level): Acute & Chronic Conditions (Adult)
NURS 677L.subject: NURS
NURS 677L.description: Intermediate level practicum. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management, and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing focusing on adults with acute or chronic diagnoses in primary care.

NURS 678.title: Primary Care III Seminar: Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
NURS 678.subject: NURS
NURS 678.description: Intermediate level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).

NURS 678L.title: Primary Care III Lab (intermediate level): Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
NURS 678L.subject: NURS
NURS 678L.description: Intermediate level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients in a primary care setting for advanced practice nursing students focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).

NURS 679.title: Primary Care IV Seminar: Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
NURS 679.subject: NURS
NURS 679.description: Advanced level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management focusing on primary care of clients across the lifespan.

NURS 679L.title: Primary Care IV Lab (advanced level): Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
NURS 679L.subject: NURS
NURS 679L.description: Advanced level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients across the lifespan in primary care settings for advanced practice nursing students.

NURS 680.title: Cultural Competency in Nursing Education
NURS 680.subject: NURS
NURS 680.description: Evaluates the impact of history on the culture of nursing and nursing education. Explore strategies to provide education in a culturally sensitive manner to culturally diverse students.
NURS 680.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

NURS 681.title: Diagnosis & Management of Complex Care Across the Lifespan
NURS 681.subject: NURS
NURS 681.description: Culminating seminar synthesizing and applying concepts from all APRN didactic course work, using case/problem-based learning via student and faculty-guided discussions.

NURS 682.title: Health and Healing Practices of Populations with Health Disparities in Hawaiʻi and Other Places
NURS 682.subject: NURS
NURS 682.description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and the prevention of common conditions of disease among populations with health disparities in Hawaiʻi and other places; includes didactic and 45 hours of field experience.

NURS 683.title: Psychobiology of Mental Health Disorders
NURS 683.subject: NURS
NURS 683.description: Focuses on the psychological and biological factors that influence mental health and illness among diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Relevant biopsychosocial theories and research findings are applied.

NURS 684.title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
NURS 684.subject: NURS
NURS 684.description: First of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

NURS 684L.title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
NURS 684L.subject: NURS
NURS 684L.description: Complements NURS 684; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.

NURS 685.title: Individual Psychotherapy for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioners
NURS 685.subject: NURS
NURS 685.description: Major modalities of individual psychotherapy, such as psychodynamic, cognitive-behavioral, brief solution-focused, and multicultural approaches will be examined. Critical dialogue about race, gender, culture, sexuality and socioeconomic status will be applied to case studies and reenactments.

NURS 686.title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan II
NURS 686.subject: NURS
NURS 686.description: The second of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

NURS 686L.title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan II
NURS 686L.subject: NURS
NURS 686L.description: Complements NURS 686; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.

NURS 687.title: Family and Group Psychotherapy for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioners
NURS 687.subject: NURS
NURS 687.description: Major approaches in family and group psychotherapy are examined in this course. The role of the PMHNP and issues in providing care across the lifespan, among diverse populations, in traditional and non-traditional settings are addressed.

NURS 688.title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan III
NURS 688.subject: NURS
NURS 688.description: The final of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).

NURS 688L.title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan III
NURS 688L.subject: NURS
NURS 688L.description: Complements NURS 688; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.

NURS 692.title: Introduction to Research Methods
NURS 692.subject: NURS
NURS 692.description: Nursing research methods for qualitative and quantitative studies, institutional review board procedures, and how to develop a research proposal.

NURS 693.title: Advanced Practice Clinical for Clinical Nurse Specialists
NURS 693.subject: NURS
NURS 693.description: Application of concepts and principles of education, consultation, research, and management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for adult health clinical nurse specialist students.
NURS 693.prereq_raw: NURS 612 (or concurrent), NURS 612L (or concurrent), NURS 613 (or concurrent), and NURS 629 (or concurrent); or consent.

NURS 695.title: Successful Aging: Physiologic
NURS 695.subject: NURS
NURS 695.description: Advanced study of the functional, cultural, psychological, and socioeconomic phenomena that impact the physiology of normal and abnormal aging. Emphasis is on promoting successful aging among elder residents of the Pacific Basin and applications to primary health care.
NURS 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 696.title: Nursing Education Capstone
NURS 696.subject: NURS
NURS 696.description: A culminating experience in nursing education program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program.

NURS 699.title: Directed Study or Research
NURS 699.subject: NURS
NURS 699.description: Directed study of problems related to nursing theory and practice.

NURS 701.title: Advanced Gerontology: Promotion and Maintenance
NURS 701.subject: NURS
NURS 701.description: Analyze biologic, psychosocial, physiologic, and health disparity aspects with conceptual application to healthcare of the aging population. Demonstrate understanding and distinguish normal changes from common disease-related changes.

NURS 702.title: Philosophical Thoughts
NURS 702.subject: NURS
NURS 702.description: Introduces the major fields of philosophy for use in research. Frameworks for the evaluation and critique of philosophical approaches to research will be explored, debated, analyzed, and applied as relevant to the PhD student’s dissertation.

NURS 703.title: Philosophical Thought and Disciplinary Knowledge for Nursing
NURS 703.subject: NURS
NURS 703.description: Exploration of a variety of philosophies of science and examination of factors influencing the development of nursing theory and disciplinary thought.
NURS 703.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 704.title: Research Design and Methods for Nursing Science
NURS 704.subject: NURS
NURS 704.description: Overview of scientific approaches relevant to nursing and health care research. Application of quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods research approaches for answering questions and generating knowledge relevant to the discipline and practice of nursing.
NURS 704.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 705.title: Seminar I: Nursing Science
NURS 705.subject: NURS
NURS 705.description: Development and refinement of the student’s research area of interest. Synthesis of theory from nursing and related disciplines. Articulation of the problem, significance, purpose of inquiry, related question(s), hypotheses (as applicable) and specific aims.
NURS 705.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 706.title: Seminar II: Literature Review
NURS 706.subject: NURS
NURS 706.description: In-depth review, critique, evaluation, and synthesis of a body of literature. Students will use standardized approaches to systematically search, locate, and evaluate evidence in a focused area to generate an integrative review.
NURS 706.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 707.title: Seminar III: Refining the Research Plan
NURS 707.subject: NURS
NURS 707.description: Continued research and scholarly development in an area of nursing scientific concentration. Student refines the research plan (in terms of quantitative, qualitative, and/or mixed methods approaches).
NURS 707.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 708.title: Seminar IV: Building a Program of Research
NURS 708.subject: NURS
NURS 708.description: Students advance skills for development and peer critique of research proposals, honing grant and scientific writing skills. Emphasis placed on dissemination strategies relevant and affirming to culturally diverse/marginalized populations and multidisciplinary professional audiences.
NURS 708.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 710.title: Designing and Conducting Clinical Trials
NURS 710.subject: NURS
NURS 710.description: Small group sections will guide students as they produce their own clinical trial protocol. Topics like ethics and statistical power will be addressed briefly.

NURS 721.title: Instrument Development and Evaluation in Research
NURS 721.subject: NURS
NURS 721.description: Theory of testing and evaluation applied to nursing research in culturally diverse populations.

NURS 730.title: Principles of Evidence-based Practice for Advanced Nursing
NURS 730.subject: NURS
NURS 730.description: Evaluates conceptual models for use in evidence-based practice. Refines skills in searching and critiquing the literature for application to practice change. Synthesizes a body of literature to design interventions pertinent to a practice problem.

NURS 732.title: Best Practices & Innovation in Teaching and Learning in Nursing Education
NURS 732.subject: NURS
NURS 732.description: Current best practices and innovative teaching and learning strategies in nursing education.

NURS 735.title: Effective Program Evaluation for Quality Improvement
NURS 735.subject: NURS
NURS 735.description: Integration of program evaluation and translational science for assessment and communication of programmatic health impacts to improve well-being of patients, families, and stakeholders/communities at local, regional, national/ international levels.

NURS 739.title: Advanced Nursing Science
NURS 739.subject: NURS
NURS 739.description: Provides opportunities to know and practice the process of theory development in nursing and to test concepts, relationships, and models about health behavior in culturally diverse populations.

NURS 740.title: Health Policy and Economics
NURS 740.subject: NURS
NURS 740.description: Evaluate the implications of policies on health care funding and regulations, provider payments, and other variables shaping the ability of health care systems (Western and other) on advanced practice.

NURS 741.title: Quantitative Methods and Measures
NURS 741.subject: NURS
NURS 741.description: Critical analysis of quantitative research methods used to analyze problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
NURS 741.prereq_raw: NURS 620 or equivalent course and an advanced statistics course; or consent.

NURS 743.title: Qualitative Methods
NURS 743.subject: NURS
NURS 743.description: Qualitative methods and approaches to research used in nursing and health sciences will be examined. Multiple paradigms and traditions will be reviewed, including culturally safe approaches and indigenous methodologies.

NURS 744.title: Seminar on Women and Health
NURS 744.subject: NURS
NURS 744.description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.

NURS 745.title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
NURS 745.subject: NURS
NURS 745.description: Analysis of forces that affect adult learners. Concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities.

NURS 746.title: Methods of Program Evaluation & Quality Improvement
NURS 746.subject: NURS
NURS 746.description: Principles of and frameworks for program evaluation. Students develop logic models and evaluation plans for a community program and collect and analyze evaluation data.

NURS 747.title: Curriculum Development and Assessment Strategies in Nursing Education
NURS 747.subject: NURS
NURS 747.description: Current theories, issues, and trends of curriculum development and assessment strategies in nursing education.

NURS 748.title: Nursing Education & Leadership Capstone Practicum
NURS 748.subject: NURS
NURS 748.description: A culminating experience in nursing education and leadership program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program.
NURS 748.prereq_raw: ( NURS 732 and NURS 747 ) with a minimum grade of B-.

NURS 749.title: Curriculum Evaluation & Accreditation in Nursing Education
NURS 749.subject: NURS
NURS 749.description: Current trends of planning for evaluation and critical analysis and application of curriculum evaluation in nursing curriculum.
NURS 749.prereq_raw: NURS 747 with a minimum grade of B-.

NURS 750.title: Foundation of Health Systems and Translation Science
NURS 750.subject: NURS
NURS 750.description: Integrate scientific findings from various fields of study to the leadership and management of healthcare systems to ensure the delivery of quality and safe care.

NURS 751.title: Concept Development and Analysis
NURS 751.subject: NURS
NURS 751.description: First course offering in-depth analysis of specific concepts and theoretical formulations of nursing and other disciplines pertinent to the student’s area of research interest. Addresses human responses to health in culturally diverse populations.

NURS 752.title: Advanced Statistics I
NURS 752.subject: NURS
NURS 752.description: Advanced application of general linear model theory to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
NURS 752.prereq_raw: NURS 741 (or equivalent) or consent. Once a year.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or consent . Once a year

NURS 753.title: Advanced Statistics II
NURS 753.subject: NURS
NURS 753.description: Advanced application of multivariate statistics to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
NURS 753.prereq_raw: NURS 741 and NURS 752 or equivalent courses, or consent. Once a year.

NURS 755.title: DNP Scholarly Project A: Proposal
NURS 755.subject: NURS
NURS 755.description: Prepares students to implement a Doctor of Nursing Practice Scholarly Project Evidenced Based Practice problem by identifying a practice problem, developing a PICO(T) statement, conducting a literature review and synthesis, and developing an implementation plan.

NURS 756.title: DNP Scholarly Project B: Implementation
NURS 756.subject: NURS
NURS 756.description: Experiential learning course where students implement their Evidence Based Practice (EBP) change in collaboration with content experts, team members, and stakeholders within SONDH and the organization where the change is occurring.

NURS 757.title: DNP Scholarly Project C: Evaluation & Dissemination
NURS 757.subject: NURS
NURS 757.description: Prepares Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) students to evaluate the effectiveness of their evidence based practice change, synthesize findings of the project, and disseminate results and conclusions.

NURS 760.title: Trends in Healthcare
NURS 760.subject: NURS
NURS 760.description: Evaluates the historical foundations of healthcare systems and their relationship to current issues and trends in healthcare services. Analyzes the variations in healthcare delivery systems across nations and the impact on health outcomes.

NURS 761.title: Translation Science
NURS 761.subject: NURS
NURS 761.description: Synthesis and analysis of interventions and variables that influence the rate of adoption of innovations. Application of concepts to patient populations and systems of healthcare.

NURS 767.title: Culturally Competent Research Methods
NURS 767.subject: NURS
NURS 767.description: Analysis of concepts, issues, and methods in conducting culturally competent research in the health field.

NURS 768.title: Advanced Clinical Economics and Finance
NURS 768.subject: NURS
NURS 768.description: Theory and practice of financial management to achieve high quality and cost effectiveness in healthcare. Hybrid course which combines face-to-face with online learning.

NURS 769.title: Dissertation Proposal Writing Seminar
NURS 769.subject: NURS
NURS 769.description: Provides students with advanced study and critique from faculty leading to the development of a draft dissertation proposal. Peer exchange facilities individual scholarship, research topic mastery, and ability to conduct rigorous critique.

NURS 774.title: Best Practices in Leading Healthcare Patient Safety and Quality
NURS 774.subject: NURS
NURS 774.description: Examination of quality of health care, the process of managing health-care outcomes and costs in the delivery of care through the interdisciplinary process.

NURS 775.title: Capstone Field Study
NURS 775.subject: NURS
NURS 775.description: Supervised experience in executive nursing leadership to address important health issues for high-risk or under-served populations utilizing an interdisciplinary systems-based approach.
NURS 775.prereq_raw: NURS 664 and NURS 774 (or concurrent), or consent.

NURS 776.title: Doctor of Nursing Practice Project
NURS 776.subject: NURS
NURS 776.description: Under the guidance of their DNP Project Team members, students will synthesize, integrate, and translate newly acquired knowledge and skills in the implementation and evaluation of their DNP Project.

NURS 777.title: Nursing Research Practicum
NURS 777.subject: NURS
NURS 777.description: Faculty guided research opportunity to gain mastery of research skills and techniques through participation in mentored research.
NURS 777.prereq_raw: NURS 741 (with a minimum grade of B-), NURS 742 (with a minimum grade of B-), NURS 751 (with a minimum grade of B-) and a quantitative methods course.
NURS 777.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

NURS 796.title: Grant Writing and Grant Management
NURS 796.subject: NURS
NURS 796.description: Designed to introduce students to grants, grant writing, and grant management. Combined lecture discussion, seminar, and exercises on grants, grant writing, and grant management for health sciences. Open to NURS students only, others with approval.

OBGN 499.title: Directed Clinical and Translational Research in Obstetrics and Gynecology
OBGN 499.subject: OBGN
OBGN 499.description: Directed research within the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at JABSOM in a clinical or translational context.

OBGN 532.title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Longitudinal Clerkship
OBGN 532.subject: OBGN
OBGN 532.description: Year-long clerkship in outpatient setting, covering assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and/ or management of common gynecologic problems and normal and complicated pregnancies. Emphasis on prevention and health maintenance.
OBGN 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing, and concurrent registration in OBGN 532 courses.
OBGN 532.coreq_raw: FMCH, MED, PED, PSTY, and SURG 632.

OBGN 545B.title: Electives in OB/GYN: labor and delivery
OBGN 545B.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545B.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OBGN 545D.title: Electives in OB/GYN: Sub-internship in family planning
OBGN 545D.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545D.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OBGN 545E.title: Electives in OB/GYN: high-risk OB
OBGN 545E.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545E.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OBGN 545F.title: Electives in OB/GYN: endocrinology
OBGN 545F.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545F.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OBGN 545G.title: Electives in OB/GYN: oncology
OBGN 545G.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545G.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OBGN 545H.title: Electives in OB/GYN: topics with individual preceptor
OBGN 545H.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545H.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OBGN 545I.title: Electives in OB/GYN: extramural electives
OBGN 545I.subject: OBGN
OBGN 545I.description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

OCN 100.title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
OCN 100.subject: OCN
OCN 100.description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST.

OCN 102.title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
OCN 102.subject: OCN
OCN 102.description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

OCN 102L.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
OCN 102L.subject: OCN
OCN 102L.description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
OCN 102L.prereq_raw: OCN 102 (or concurrent) or GES 102 or (or concurrent) SUST 112 (or concurrent).

OCN 105.title: Sustainability in a Changing World
OCN 105.subject: OCN
OCN 105.description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawaiʻi/Oceania. Active learning environment.

OCN 120.title: Global Environmental Challenges
OCN 120.subject: OCN
OCN 120.description: Scientific approach to evaluating human-caused environmental challenges and their potential solutions.

OCN 196.title: Research Experiences in Marine Science
OCN 196.subject: OCN
OCN 196.description: Inquiry-driven and experimental marine biology summer program based on the expertise of HIMB researchers whose specialties demonstrate how human impacts and global change affect coral reef ecosystems. Emphases on student team research projects.
OCN 196.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: High school or UG freshman only.

OCN 199.title: Introduction to Directed Research
OCN 199.subject: OCN
OCN 199.description: Reading and research in any area of Oceanography under the direction of a faculty member.

OCN 201.title: Science of the Sea
OCN 201.subject: OCN
OCN 201.description: Origin and features of ocean basins and seawater; global cycles of carbon and nutrients; currents; waves; tides; characteristics of marine organisms; marine ecological principles; marine pollution; climate change causes and consequences. Online asynchronous; synchronous format.

OCN 201L.title: Science of the Sea Laboratory
OCN 201L.subject: OCN
OCN 201L.description: Experiments, computer exercises, and field trips demonstrating the geological, physical, chemical, and biological principles of earth and ocean sciences.

OCN 310.title: Global Environmental Change
OCN 310.subject: OCN
OCN 310.description: Delve into global environmental change issues such as geometric population growth, food production, plastic waste, and global warming that are of growing interest and importance to our society.
OCN 310.prereq_raw: OCN 201 , ATMO 200 , or similar environmental/ natural sciences course.
OCN 310.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Designed for non-GES majors.

OCN 312.title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
OCN 312.subject: OCN
OCN 312.description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

OCN 315.title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
OCN 315.subject: OCN
OCN 315.description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models.
OCN 315.prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent.

OCN 318.title: Introduction to Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
OCN 318.subject: OCN
OCN 318.description: Introduction to environmental monitoring systems for earth science students. Students will learn how to construct, program, and deploy simple environmental monitoring systems to collect in-situ environmental data.
OCN 318.prereq_raw: OCN 201 / OCN 201L or ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L , CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L , and MATH 241 ; or consent.
OCN 318.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES, ERTH, ATMO majors only.

OCN 319L.title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
OCN 319L.subject: OCN
OCN 319L.description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311 . Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
OCN 319L.prereq_raw: GES 311 , MATH 242 , PHYS 170 / PHYS 170L , and CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ; or consent.

OCN 320.title: Aquatic Pollution
OCN 320.subject: OCN
OCN 320.description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives. This course develops written communication skills.

OCN 321.title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
OCN 321.subject: OCN
OCN 321.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each.
OCN 321.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.
OCN 321.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

OCN 330.title: Mineral and Energy Resources of the Sea
OCN 330.subject: OCN
OCN 330.description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration, and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

OCN 331.title: Living Resources of the Sea-Mai ke Kai Mai ke Ola
OCN 331.subject: OCN
OCN 331.description: Marine fisheries, aquaculture, and law of the sea. Principles of management of renewable resources. Political and scientific constraints and limitations.
OCN 331.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

OCN 340.title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
OCN 340.subject: OCN
OCN 340.description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawaiʻi.
OCN 340.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

OCN 360.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
OCN 360.subject: OCN
OCN 360.description: Covers principles of remote sensing technologies for land, ocean, and climate applications. Students will explore the fundamentals of electromagnetic radiation, and learn to critically interpret patterns in environmental changes over time and space.

OCN 395.title: Undergraduate Internship
OCN 395.subject: OCN
OCN 395.description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work.
OCN 395.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Undergraduate SOEST majors only. Open to GES majors. Class Standing Restrictions: junior/senior standing and consent.

OCN 399.title: Directed Reading
OCN 399.subject: OCN
OCN 399.description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

OCN 401.title: Biogeochemical Systems
OCN 401.subject: OCN
OCN 401.description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills.
OCN 401.prereq_raw: OCN 201 , GES 311 , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L , ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L , GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES 499 / OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent.
OCN 401.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

OCN 403.title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
OCN 403.subject: OCN
OCN 403.description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology.

OCN 411.title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
OCN 411.subject: OCN
OCN 411.description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

OCN 418.title: Advanced Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
OCN 418.subject: OCN
OCN 418.description: Builds upon OCN 318 using more advanced microprocessors and environmental sensors, 3D printing, programming, etc. to construct, program, and deploy environmental monitoring systems to collect and stream in-situ time-series environmental measurements.
OCN 418.prereq_raw: OCN 318 , MATH 242 , PHYS 272 / PHYS 272L , and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L ; or consent.
OCN 418.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN, ERTH, ATMO majors only.

OCN 423.title: Marine Geology
OCN 423.subject: OCN
OCN 423.description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

OCN 430.title: Introduction to Deep-Sea Biology
OCN 430.subject: OCN
OCN 430.description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including benthopelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction and global climate change.

OCN 435.title: Climate Change and Urbanization
OCN 435.subject: OCN
OCN 435.description: The following topics will be addressed: How are cities impacted by, and impacting climate change? How do urbanization, alteration of atmospheric processes, and extreme weather events affect urban systems and populations?

OCN 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
OCN 441.subject: OCN
OCN 441.description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.
OCN 441.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

OCN 442.title: Environmental Management Systems
OCN 442.subject: OCN
OCN 442.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
OCN 442.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

OCN 444.title: Plate Tectonics
OCN 444.subject: OCN
OCN 444.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

OCN 450.title: Aquaculture Production
OCN 450.subject: OCN
OCN 450.description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics, and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
OCN 450.prereq_raw: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445 : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher.

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher

OCN 454.title: Earth’s Microbiome
OCN 454.subject: OCN
OCN 454.description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
OCN 454.prereq_raw: OCN 201 or BOT 305 / BIOL 305 or BOT 201 or BIOL 275 or MICR 351 or consent.

OCN 454L.title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
OCN 454L.subject: OCN
OCN 454L.description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
OCN 454L.prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305 , or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 .

OCN 457.title: Ridge to Reef: Coastal Ecosystem Ecology and Connectivity
OCN 457.subject: OCN
OCN 457.description: Watershed and coastal biogeochemistry/ecosystem science. Emphasis on field surveying and sampling of stream and reef habitats; laboratory chemical/biological analyses. Analysis of land use impacts on ecosystem health and ahupuaʻa resource management.
OCN 457.prereq_raw: OCN 201 / OCN 201L ; and either OCN 310 / ATMO 310 , or GES 311 ; or consent.

OCN 463.title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
OCN 463.subject: OCN
OCN 463.description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.

OCN 480.title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
OCN 480.subject: OCN
OCN 480.description: Combined lecture and discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
OCN 480.prereq_raw: OCN 201 / OCN 201L , GES 311 , GES 319L , and PHYS 272 / PHYS 272L ; and consent.

OCN 481.title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
OCN 481.subject: OCN
OCN 481.description: Introduction to modeling biogeochemical and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on plankton blooms. Students learn ecosystem dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.
OCN 481.prereq_raw: ( GES 311 and either OCN 312 / ERTH 312 (or concurrent) or MATH 307 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-.

OCN 490.title: Communication of Research Results
OCN 490.subject: OCN
OCN 490.description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material.
OCN 490.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only in their final semester.

OCN 496.title: Topics in Global Environmental Science
OCN 496.subject: OCN
OCN 496.description: Lecture and discussion or seminar. Current topics in environmental science explored in detail. Typically offered by faculty in their specialties, or developed in response to student interest.

OCN 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
OCN 499.subject: OCN
OCN 499.description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

OCN 620.title: Physical Oceanography
OCN 620.subject: OCN
OCN 620.description: Introduction to properties of seawater, oceanographic instruments and methods, heat budget, general ocean circulation, regional oceanography, waves, tides, sea level. Formation of water masses, dynamics of circulation.

OCN 621.title: Biological Oceanography
OCN 621.subject: OCN
OCN 621.description: Factors governing productivity, population dynamics, distribution of organisms in major ecosystems of the ocean, emphasis on ecology of pelagic zone.

OCN 622.title: Geological Oceanography
OCN 622.subject: OCN
OCN 622.description: Marine geological processes, ocean basin structure and tectonics, sedimentation.

OCN 623.title: Chemical Oceanography
OCN 623.subject: OCN
OCN 623.description: Chemical processes occurring in marine waters; why they occur and how they affect oceanic environment.

OCN 625.title: Aquatic Photosynthesis
OCN 625.subject: OCN
OCN 625.description: Biochemical and biophysical concepts of photosynthesis. Application and interpretation of ecological processes of photosynthesis in aquatic systems.

OCN 626.title: Marine Microplankton Ecology
OCN 626.subject: OCN
OCN 626.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Distribution, abundance, and ecology of marine microplankton, including bacteria, algae, and protozoans, with an emphasis on metabolic rates and processes.

OCN 627.title: Ecology of Pelagic Marine Animals
OCN 627.subject: OCN
OCN 627.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ecology of pelagic animals including feeding, energetics, predation, and anti-predation tactics. Life-history strategies, vertical flux of materials, population dynamics, fisheries.

OCN 628.title: Benthic Biological Oceanography
OCN 628.subject: OCN
OCN 628.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Processes controlling the structure and function of benthic communities, including organism-sediment-flow interactions, sediment geochemistry, feeding strategies, recruitment, succession, and population interactions.
OCN 628.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN and MB majors only.

OCN 629.title: Molecular Methods in Marine Ecology
OCN 629.subject: OCN
OCN 629.description: Molecular methods for studying marine functional ecology; emphasis on hand-on tools for ecological and biogeochemical processes of microbes; developing practical skills for research project in marine microbial ecology and biological oceanography.
OCN 629.prereq_raw: OCN 403 , OCN 626 , OCN 627 , or OCN 628 ; or consent.

OCN 630.title: Deep-Sea Biology
OCN 630.subject: OCN
OCN 630.description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction, and global climate change.

OCN 631.title: Ocean Minerals
OCN 631.subject: OCN
OCN 631.description: Distribution, origin, processes of formation. Sulfides, oxides, and placer minerals. Comparative studies of continental ore bodies. Submarine rift, subduction, and abduction.
OCN 631.prereq_raw: one of OCN 622 , OCN 623 , ERTH 407 , or ERTH 603 .

OCN 632.title: Fisheries Oceanography: From Physics to Landings
OCN 632.subject: OCN
OCN 632.description: Overview of how oceanographic processes influence the distribution, life history, and abundance of fishery-relevant species. Topics will largely center on applications to Hawaiʻi, tropical/sub-tropical ecosystems, and the broader Pacific.
OCN 632.prereq_raw: C or better in OCN 620 or OCN 621 , and a background in biological oceanography and/or physical oceanography required.

OCN 633.title: Biogeochemical Methods in Oceanography
OCN 633.subject: OCN
OCN 633.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Current methods of analysis used in the ocean sciences, both in the field and in the laboratory. An ocean-going field trip provides students with hands-on training in sample collection and processing. The latter is followed by laboratory analyses of the collected samples throughout the remainder of the semester.
OCN 633.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and CHEM 161 and ERTH 101 ; or consent.

OCN 636.title: Aquatic Chemistry
OCN 636.subject: OCN
OCN 636.description: Chemical reactions support life and stabilize Earth’s climate. We explore marine and fresh waters through chemical equilibrium and reaction kinetics. Topics include mineral stability, ocean acidification, complexation/bioavailability, pollution, and quantitative approximation of natural systems.

OCN 637.title: Aquatic Microbial Geochemistry
OCN 637.subject: OCN
OCN 637.description: The synergy between the biogeochemistry of element cycling and the microbial organisms involved, interfacing across disciplines from the perspective of a practical blend of aquatic chemistry, microbiology, biogeochemistry, and molecular biology.

OCN 638.title: Earth System Science and Global Change
OCN 638.subject: OCN
OCN 638.description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmosphere-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota.
OCN 638.prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus.

OCN 640.title: Observational Physical Oceanography
OCN 640.subject: OCN
OCN 640.description: Application of the scientific method; physical regimes in the ocean; ocean processes and observational strategies; resolution, sampling, array design and observing systems; models and data assimilation; major field programs; operational oceanography and climate prediction.

OCN 641.title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
OCN 641.subject: OCN
OCN 641.description: Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

OCN 642.title: Elemental Composition Changes
OCN 642.subject: OCN
OCN 642.description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

OCN 643.title: Topics in Marine Geochemistry
OCN 643.subject: OCN
OCN 643.description: Seminar on a broad topic; discussion and critique of research papers.

OCN 644.title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
OCN 644.subject: OCN
OCN 644.description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.

OCN 650.title: Math Techniques for Oceanographers
OCN 650.subject: OCN
OCN 650.description: (3 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Introduction to numerical methods, data analysis, error propagation, box models, linear and nonlinear least squares, perturbation theory, numerical integration.

OCN 653.title: Methods in Microbiology Oceanography
OCN 653.subject: OCN
OCN 653.description: (1 8-hr Lab) Modern methods for sampling microbial populations from the sea and for quantifying biomass and in siturates of metabolism. Integrated field projects, theme varies.
OCN 653.prereq_raw: OCN 621 or OCN 623 , and OCN 626 ; or consent.

OCN 660.title: Ocean Waves I
OCN 660.subject: OCN
OCN 660.description: Survey of wave types-acoustic, capillary, gravity, inertial, vorticity. Basic wave concepts emphasized: phase and group velocities, standing waves, energy conservation, dispersion, refraction, diffraction. Rotation and boundary effects are covered: reflection, basin modes, trapping, tides.

OCN 661.title: Ocean Waves II
OCN 661.subject: OCN
OCN 661.description: Baroclinic gravity waves, inertial waves, mid-latitude Rossby waves, topographic waves, equatorial waves.

OCN 662.title: Marine Hydrodynamics
OCN 662.subject: OCN
OCN 662.description: Introduction to classical hydrodynamics and continuum mechanics. Techniques for solution of Navier Stokes equations on various scales of oceanic motion; potential theory, dynamic modeling, and viscous and rotational processes.

OCN 663.title: Satellite Oceanography
OCN 663.subject: OCN
OCN 663.description: Techniques of satellite observations of the ocean, including temperature, pigment concentration, currents, and winds; analysis of a satellite data set as term project.

OCN 664.title: Oceanographic Instrumentation and Technology
OCN 664.subject: OCN
OCN 664.description: Measurement techniques in physical oceanography, including pressure, temperature, salinity, oxygen, optical sensors, current meters, navigation systems, ocean acoustics, and mooring structures. Includes a laboratory research project.

OCN 665.title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
OCN 665.subject: OCN
OCN 665.description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
OCN 665.prereq_raw: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either OCN 620 or ATMO 600 , or consent.

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either OCN 620 or ATMO 600 , or consent

OCN 666.title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
OCN 666.subject: OCN
OCN 666.description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Nino/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

OCN 667.title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics I
OCN 667.subject: OCN
OCN 667.description: Basic concepts and equations to describe large-scale ocean circulation; numerical models; boundary layers; models of wind-driven circulation of a homogeneous ocean.

OCN 668.title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics II
OCN 668.subject: OCN
OCN 668.description: Thermodynamics of stratified fluids; convection; mixing; models of the thermohaline circulation; the role of eddies in the large-scale ocean circulation.

OCN 671.title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
OCN 671.subject: OCN
OCN 671.description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with Bayesian inference, predictions using artificial neural networks, and analyze data in space and time using the Python language with biological and geophysical datasets.
OCN 671.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN, ATMO, and ERTH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

OCN 674.title: Paleoceanography
OCN 674.subject: OCN
OCN 674.description: Study of the paloeceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere, and biosphere.

OCN 680.title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
OCN 680.subject: OCN
OCN 680.description: Combined lecture/discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
OCN 680.prereq_raw: previous course in marine science, or consent.

OCN 681.title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
OCN 681.subject: OCN
OCN 681.description: Introduction to modeling biological and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on biological production. Students will learn biological-physical dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.

OCN 682.title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
OCN 682.subject: OCN
OCN 682.description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research.

OCN 683.title: Advanced Statistics in R
OCN 683.subject: OCN
OCN 683.description: (2-hr Lec, 1-hr Lab) In-depth introduction to the modern statistical methods necessary for analyzing biological/ecological data, including GLMs, GAMs, mixed models, ordination, etc. Students will learn how to perform these methods in R.

OCN 750.title: Topics in Biological Oceanography
OCN 750.subject: OCN
OCN 750.description: Seminar. Literature and concepts in one of several active fields considered in detail.

OCN 760.title: Topics in Physical Oceanography
OCN 760.subject: OCN
OCN 760.description: Near-shore processes, advanced mathematical techniques, recent developments, etc. Typically given by visiting professors in their specialties, or in response to student interest.

OCN 791.title: Proposal Development
OCN 791.subject: OCN
OCN 791.description: Introduction to the organization and functioning of oceanography funding agencies, the peer-review process, and the design and development of a research proposal.
OCN 791.prereq_raw: two of the following: OCN 621 , OCN 626 , OCN 627 (or concurrent), or OCN 628 (or concurrent); or consent.

OEST 099.title: International Exchange Study/Research
OEST 099.subject: OEST
OEST 099.description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program.
OEST 099.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES, ERTH, and MET majors only.

OEST 100.title: The College Experience
OEST 100.subject: OEST
OEST 100.description: Required for entering SOEST majors to develop skills and applications for a successful college experience. Students will examine academic goals and implement strategies to achieve goals including time management and career exploration.

OEST 101.title: Natural Hazards
OEST 101.subject: OEST
OEST 101.description: Science of natural hazards: impact on human civilization of events in the lithosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere (e.g., earthquakes, hurricanes, red tides, and floods), and impact of humans on their exposure to and mitigation of the hazards.

OEST 103.title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
OEST 103.subject: OEST
OEST 103.description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

OEST 109.title: Contemporary Issues in Energy Systems
OEST 109.subject: OEST
OEST 109.description: Introductory experience in energy systems including current status of fossil fuel, renewable energy technologies, energy utilization and conservation; environmental and policy aspects.

OEST 350.title: Ethics in Scientific Research
OEST 350.subject: OEST
OEST 350.description: Introduction to issues of ethics in scientific research and scientific misconduct.
OEST 350.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH, GES, or ATMO majors only.

OEST 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
OEST 441.subject: OEST
OEST 441.description: Introduction to the principles of sustainability analysis through execution of Life Cycle Analysis applied to products, processes, or systems. LCA and the evaluation of environmental impact will be presented. Personal computer or laptop (Word 97 or higher) OS, and minimum of 4GB RAM.
OEST 441.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and PHYS 170 ) with a minimum grade of C-; Junior standing or higher, or consent.

OEST 499.title: Undergraduate Directed Research
OEST 499.subject: OEST
OEST 499.description: Student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. Student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.
OEST 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

OEST 510.title: Earth Sciences Professional Development Education
OEST 510.subject: OEST
OEST 510.description: Specialized Earth Science topics workshops designed for in-service teachers who wish to learn new approaches and content areas in geology and geophysics, meteorology and oceanography. Credits earned cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

OEST 696.title: Communicating Ocean Sciences
OEST 696.subject: OEST
OEST 696.description: Application of current learning theory and pedagogical practices in formal and informal learning environments to improve communication and instructional skills. Graduate students from multiple science disciplines welcome. Requires knowledge of biology, earth sciences, and/or chemistry.
OEST 696.prereq_raw: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry or marine science, an interest in ocean science, and enthusiasm for teaching science; or consent.

children.text: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry
marine science, an interest in ocean science,

OEST 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
OEST 699.subject: OEST
OEST 699.description: Selected interdisciplinary ocean/earth-related topics involving science, technology, engineering, and/or policy.

OEST 735.title: Ocean Policy and Management
OEST 735.subject: OEST
OEST 735.description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

ORE 202.title: Ocean Technology—Man in the Sea
ORE 202.subject: ORE
ORE 202.description: Survey of human activities in the ocean, from the most traditional to the most innovative technical and engineering accomplishments.

ORE 203.title: Surf Science and Culture
ORE 203.subject: ORE
ORE 203.description: Introduction to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the human interaction with the ocean using multiple perspectives.
ORE 203.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

ORE 203L.title: Surf Science and Culture Lab
ORE 203L.subject: ORE
ORE 203L.description: Practical laboratory dedicated to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the ocean environment through technology.

ORE 330.title: Mineral and Energy Resources
ORE 330.subject: ORE
ORE 330.description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

ORE 411.title: Buoyancy and Stability
ORE 411.subject: ORE
ORE 411.description: Ship nomenclature and geometry, hydrostatic principles of surface ships and underwater vehicles in free-floating, partially waterborne, and damaged conditions. Subdivision of ships. Launching.

ORE 601.title: Ocean and Resources Engineering Laboratory
ORE 601.subject: ORE
ORE 601.description: Design, construction, and evaluation of an engineering system. Laboratory and field experience and data analysis supplemented with appropriate theory.

ORE 603.title: Oceanography for Ocean Engineers
ORE 603.subject: ORE
ORE 603.description: Physical, chemical, biological, and geological ocean environments for ocean engineers. Introduction to ocean dynamical processes and general circulation. Ocean measurement techniques, theory of underwater acoustics. Sonar, swath bathymetry, and tomography applications.

ORE 607.title: Water Wave Mechanics
ORE 607.subject: ORE
ORE 607.description: Governing equations in free surface flow, deterministic and probabilistic wave theories, wave transformation, wave-induced coastal currents, tides, ocean engineering operational sea state, and design wave criteria.

ORE 608.title: Probability and Statistics for Ocean Engineers
ORE 608.subject: ORE
ORE 608.description: Probability and statistical analysis including distributions, multiple regression and correlation, autocovariance, cross-spectra, and practical applications in ocean engineering.

ORE 609.title: Hydrodynamics of Fluid-Body Interaction
ORE 609.subject: ORE
ORE 609.description: Hydrodynamics of ships, coastal and offshore structures. Wave forces by potential theory and by Morison’s equation. Method of source distribution for potential flow problems. Flows with prescribed body motion, fixed and freely floating bodies.

ORE 612.title: Dynamics of Ocean Structures
ORE 612.subject: ORE
ORE 612.description: Response of floating platforms and vessels to wave action, spectral analysis in sea keeping. Frequency and time domain analyses of rigid body motions in six degrees of freedom.

ORE 621.title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
ORE 621.subject: ORE
ORE 621.description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
ORE 621.prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

ORE 624.title: Coastal Modeling
ORE 624.subject: ORE
ORE 624.description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

ORE 630.title: Structural Analysis in Ocean Engineering
ORE 630.subject: ORE
ORE 630.description: Structural and finite element analyses and design of ocean structures to withstand hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loading of the sea. Considerations include material type, safety factor, stress concentration, and fatigue.

ORE 641.title: Environmental Fluid Dynamics
ORE 641.subject: ORE
ORE 641.description: Fluid dynamics for coastal and estuarine environments. Turbulent mixing processes in homogeneous and stratified fluids. Buoyancy driven flows, internal hydraulics, topographic effects and estuarine circulation. Spill and pollutant dispersal.

ORE 653.title: Ocean Instrumentation and Technology
ORE 653.subject: ORE
ORE 653.description: Overview of past, present, and emerging technologies and instrumentation that support oceanographic and marine operations. Will cover the design, operation, and maintenance of the mechanical, electrical, and computing components of these systems.

ORE 654.title: Applications in Ocean Acoustics
ORE 654.subject: ORE
ORE 654.description: Using sound to observe the ocean. Fundamentals of propagation. Topics include marine mammals, navigation and communication, seismics, ships, wind and rain, ocean dynamics, flow and biological imaging and measurement, seafloor mapping, and the forward/inverse problem.

ORE 657.title: Autonomous Marine Systems
ORE 657.subject: ORE
ORE 657.description: Identifies the unique challenges faced by autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, and analyzes approaches to address those challenges. Topics include hydrodynamic vehicle modeling, propeller theory, subsystem integration, and motion control strategies.
ORE 657.prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 (or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 (or equivalent), or instructor consent.

ORE 661.title: Coastal and Harbor Engineering
ORE 661.subject: ORE

ORE 664.title: Nearshore Processes and Sediment Transport
ORE 664.subject: ORE
ORE 664.description: Sediment transport by waves and currents in coastal areas and its effect on morphological processes. Effect of man-made structures on littoral drift and shoreline.

ORE 677.title: Marine Renewable Energy
ORE 677.subject: ORE
ORE 677.description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.
ORE 677.prereq_raw: ORE 607 ; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable.

ORE 678.title: Marine Mineral Resources Engineering
ORE 678.subject: ORE
ORE 678.description: Activities in marine minerals development are examined in a multidisciplinary systems approach involving engineering, Earth and environmental sciences and economics.
ORE 678.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

ORE 680.title: Ocean Engineering and Resilience in a Changing Climate
ORE 680.subject: ORE
ORE 680.description: Focus on understanding the changing ocean conditions (e.g. waves and sea levels) relevant to the resilience of practical ocean engineering applications.

ORE 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
ORE 695.subject: ORE

ORE 766.subject: ORE
ORE 766.description: Formulation and application of analytical and numerical methods for simulating and solving ocean engineering problems. ORE 791.subject: ORE

PACE 201.title: Problems of War and Peace
PACE 201.subject: PACE
PACE 201.description: Introduction to the problems individuals and political communities currently face with respect to war, peace, and international conflict. Includes questions of human nature, economy, morality, nuclear deterrence, arms control and disarmament, and alternatives to war.

PACE 247.title: Survey of Conflict Management
PACE 247.subject: PACE
PACE 247.description: Survey of contemporary conflict management and resolution: negotiation, mediation, conciliation, ombuds, fact-finding, facilitation techniques, arbitration, and litigation.

PACE 301.title: Governing, Policy, and Political Journalism
PACE 301.subject: PACE
PACE 301.description: Survey of the institutions of democratic governance and the role of journalism in covering and analyzing public policy.

PACE 310.title: Survey Peace and Conflict Studies
PACE 310.subject: PACE
PACE 310.description: Survey of basic concepts, ethical relationships, methods, and debates in modern peace research and the oral skills needed for conflict resolution studies.
PACE 310.prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent.

PACE 315.title: Personal Peace: Stories of Hope
PACE 315.subject: PACE
PACE 315.description: Interviewing, writing, and publishing stories of those who have overcome great difficulties to find personal peace.

PACE 316.title: Environmental Governance
PACE 316.subject: PACE
PACE 316.description: Centers around the ethical dilemmas of environmental and climate challenges and examines available mechanisms for solving them. Develops written communication skills through a critical lens from a political ecology and environmental justice perspective.

PACE 323.title: Model United Nations
PACE 323.subject: PACE

PACE 325.title: Greek and Roman War Literature
PACE 325.subject: PACE
PACE 325.description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world.

PACE 345.title: Aggression, War, and Peace
PACE 345.subject: PACE
PACE 345.description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

PACE 373.title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
PACE 373.subject: PACE
PACE 373.description: Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics.
PACE 373.prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course; or consent.

PACE 380.title: Media Communications and Conflict
PACE 380.subject: PACE
PACE 380.description: Uses an ethical lens to see the role of news media in influencing conflict, and introduces conflict-sensitive communication movements working to resolve conflicts. Writing/discussion used as mediums for reflecting on ethical dilemmas.
PACE 380.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 387.title: The Meaning of War
PACE 387.subject: PACE
PACE 387.description: Exploration of ethical questions related to the many facets of war—e.g., patriotism, tribalism, holy war, self—sacrifice, cowardice, media coverage, propaganda, torture, genocide, pillage, suicide tactics, battlefield immunity.

PACE 399.title: Directed Reading
PACE 399.subject: PACE
PACE 399.description: Directed reading in peace and conflict resolution.

PACE 401.title: Mindfulness Meditation and Stress Reduction

PACE 401.description: Practice mindfulness meditation to reduce burnout and live life in the present moment. Learn life skills to handle life better and be more resilient. Respond rather than react to life. No experience necessary.

PACE 405.title: Media Ethics

PACE 405.description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects through writing assignments.

PACE 407.title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawaiʻi

PACE 407.description: (75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students) History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation.
PACE 407.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing only.

PACE 410.title: History of Peace Movements
PACE 410.subject: PACE
PACE 410.description: Examination of two centuries of U.S., European, Australian, and Hawaiian peace, thought, and action. Also surveys early Christian and secular attitudes to war. Open to nonmajors.

PACE 412.title: Gandhi, King, and Nonviolence
PACE 412.subject: PACE
PACE 412.description: Life and thought of Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King, Jr.
PACE 412.prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent.

PACE 413.title: Terrorism
PACE 413.subject: PACE
PACE 413.description: Multidisciplinary approach to the origins, dynamics, and consequences of international terrorism, including the psychological, legal, ethical and operational concerns of counterterrorism.

PACE 420.title: Introduction to Human Rights: International and Comparative Perspectives
PACE 420.subject: PACE
PACE 420.description: Introduction to international, regional, and domestic human rights law; comparative perspectives on the theoretical origins of human rights and policy debates on the protection of human rights, dispute resolution, and enforcement mechanisms.
PACE 420.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level social sciences course, or consent.

PACE 429.title: Negotiation

PACE 429.prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent.

PACE 430.title: Leadership for Social Change

PACE 430.description: In-depth study of current models and emerging theories of ethical leadership in community service; development of tangible leadership skills, including communication, conflict resolution, team-building, and management skills.
PACE 430.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 436.title: Geography of Peace and War

PACE 443.title: Statecraft and Diplomacy in East Asia

PACE 445.title: Race and Gender in Global Affairs and Diplomacy

PACE 447.title: Introduction to Mediation
PACE 447.subject: PACE
PACE 447.description: Learn the core components of the mediation process and the tools for empowering mediation participants to reach customized resolutions. Emphasis on learning and applying the skills through exercises and mock mediation sessions.

PACE 450.title: Protest Under Occupation
