PACE 450.description: Explore nonviolent protests when one Independent State controls the territory of another Independent State (or international organization, such as the United Nations), without the transfer of sovereign title. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 460.title: Indigenous Nonviolent Action in the Asia-Pacific

PACE 460.description: Study of nonviolent methods (i.e., United Nations structures, international law, boycotts, and peaceful protest) used to gain political goals and examines their successes, failures, and the prospects for those that remain ongoing.

PACE 468.title: Introduction to Facilitating Organizational Change
PACE 468.subject: PACE
PACE 468.description: Explores the characteristics of organizations from different perspectives including structural, political, ethical, and cultural frames from organizational theory and practice. Focuses on how to design organizational change strategies and facilitate their implementation.
PACE 468.prereq_raw: any 200-level DS course (with a minimum grade of C+).

PACE 477.title: Culture and Conflict Resolution

PACE 478.title: International Law and Disputes

PACE 479.title: ’Ike Kūpuna: Introduction to Indigenous Frameworks for Peace Building

PACE 480.title: Managing Human Conflict

PACE 482.title: Research and Peace
PACE 482.subject: PACE
PACE 482.description: Introduction to and survey of the interdisciplinary field of peace research, combining theory, methodology, and empirical aspects. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 485.title: Topics in Peace and Conflict Resolution
PACE 485.subject: PACE
PACE 485.description: Recent issues, practices in peace and conflict resolution.

PACE 489.title: Hiroshima & Peace
PACE 489.subject: PACE
PACE 489.description: 10-day intensive course at Hiroshima City University, Japan, in the 2-weeks before the annual August 6 commemoration of the atomic bombing. Home-stay with Japanese family.
PACE 489.prereq_raw: any 200 level social science course, or consent.

PACE 495.title: Practicum and Internship
PACE 495.subject: PACE
PACE 495.description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
PACE 495.prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent.

PACE 621.title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
PACE 621.subject: PACE
PACE 621.description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict.
PACE 621.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PACE 629.title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
PACE 629.subject: PACE
PACE 629.description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills.

PACE 634.description: Substantive and pedagogical approaches to using Model United Nations simulation for teaching and conflict resolution.

PACE 637.title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
PACE 637.subject: PACE
PACE 637.description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

PACE 640.title: Seminar: Social Studies

PACE 647.title: Mediation: Theory and Practice
PACE 647.subject: PACE
PACE 647.description: Combined lecture, discussion, and mediation simulations. Theory of ADR field. Theory of major different models of mediation, both in the U.S. and internationally. Application of mediation process to categories of disputes, family, workplace, and international.
PACE 647.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or departmental approval.

PACE 650.title: Dispute Resolution System Design
PACE 650.subject: PACE
PACE 650.description: Conflict prevention, management and resolution in the workplace. Design and implementation of effective systems integrating ADR and recent advances in dispute resolution methodology to government, health, nonprofit, educational, private sector and other institutions.
PACE 650.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or departmental approval.

PACE 652.title: Conflict Management for Educators
PACE 652.subject: PACE
PACE 652.description: Conflict resolution theory and practice for administrators, faculty and staff in educational organizations. K-12, community colleges and universities. Application and theory of negotiation, mediation, facilitation and hybrid ADR processes.

PACE 660.title: Family Mediation
PACE 660.subject: PACE
PACE 660.description: Theory and skills for practicing divorce and custody mediation. Negotiation and conflict intervention skills used by social workers, lawyers, and other intervenors in family conflict. Focus on Hawaiʻi’s divorce and custody laws and practices.
PACE 660.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PACE 661.title: Collaboration Between Sectors
PACE 661.subject: PACE
PACE 661.description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems.

PACE 668.title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
PACE 668.subject: PACE
PACE 668.description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations.
PACE 668.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or departmental approval.

PACE 690.title: Topics: Conflict Theory
PACE 690.subject: PACE
PACE 690.description: Recent issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory.
PACE 690.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PACE 695.subject: PACE
PACE 695.description: Practice in conflict resolution skills. Open to candidates for Certificate in Conflict Resolution.

PACE 725.title: Political Ecology

PACE 790.title: Advanced Topics: Conflict Theory
PACE 790.subject: PACE
PACE 790.description: Advanced seminar covering issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory.
PACE 790.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

PACS 108.title: Pacific Worlds: An Introduction to Pacific Islands Studies
PACS 108.subject: PACS

PACS 120.title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Oceania
PACS 120.subject: PACS
PACS 120.description: Uses interdisciplinary approaches to examine the causes, impacts, and responses to climate change in Oceania, while drawing on examples and lessons from the broader Asia-Pacific with an emphasis on a writing intensive assessment.

PACS 201.title: Islands of Globalization
PACS 201.subject: PACS
PACS 201.description: Combined lectures, service-learning. Examines the nature and impact of globalization on Pacific Island societies, viewed from the perspective of islanders who engage with global forces and processes, and create strategies to survive. Limit 20 students.

PACS 202.title: Pacific Islands Movement and Migration
PACS 202.subject: PACS
PACS 202.description: Combined lecture and service-learning activities. Examines the diaspora of Pacific Islanders. Includes a service-learning activity examining cultural, political, and economic status of groups of Pacific Islanders living in other Pacific places. Limit of 20 students.

PACS 203.title: Arts in Oceania—An Introduction
PACS 203.subject: PACS
PACS 203.description: Practical and theoretical study of arts in Oceania in relevant cultural contexts.

PACS 301.title: Pacific Communities in Hawaiʻi
PACS 301.subject: PACS
PACS 301.description: Examines Pacific Islander communities’ experiences in Hawaiʻi through service learning, reading, writing, lecture, and discussion. Concerns about housing, employment, education, health, language, and culture are central.

PACS 302.title: Contemporary Issues in Oceania
PACS 302.subject: PACS
PACS 302.description: Combines lectures and discussions to examine contemporary political, social, and economic issues in the Pacific Islands region. It also develops and strengthens students’ written communication skills by emphasizing reading, writing, and referencing.

PACS 303.title: Thinking Through Pacific Arts, Ritual, and Performance
PACS 303.subject: PACS
PACS 303.description: Lecture, discussion, and workshop series surveys arts, ritual, and performance practices throughout the Pacific. Engaging with Pacific traditions of thought, and creative approaches to research, students also return findings to Pacific communities.
PACS 303.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PACS 320.title: Climate Change, Resilience, and Sustainability in Oceania
PACS 320.subject: PACS
PACS 320.description: Examines Pacific Island experiences and responses to climate change, contrasting Indigenous and local impacts with regional and global models, emphasizing resilience, sustainability, and community strategies confronting rising seas, biodiversity loss, pollution, and ecological disruption.
PACS 320.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PACS 333.title: Islands and Archipelagos
PACS 333.subject: PACS

PACS 333.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PACS 371.title: Literature of the Pacific
PACS 371.subject: PACS
PACS 371.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the literature of the Pacific, including Pacific voyagers and contemporary writings in English by Pacific Islanders.
PACS 371.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

PACS 401.title: Pacific Islander Collaborative Research
PACS 401.subject: PACS
PACS 401.description: Engage in intensive collaborative research with a Pacific Islander community in Hawaiʻi, culminating in a research paper and public presentation. Oral communication is an essential component of this course.
PACS 401.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

PACS 462.title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
PACS 462.subject: PACS
PACS 462.description: Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawaiʻi, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand.

PACS 474.title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
PACS 474.subject: PACS

PACS 474.prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course.

PACS 493.title: Moving Images in the Pacific Islands
PACS 493.subject: PACS

PACS 494.title: Culture and Consumption in Oceania
PACS 494.subject: PACS
PACS 494.description: Lecture on changing patterns of consumption in Oceania, and the historical, political, cultural, artistic, and economic forces shaping such practices.
PACS 494.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing, or consent.

PACS 601.title: Learning Oceania
PACS 601.subject: PACS

PACS 602.title: Re/Presenting Oceania: Pacific and American Perspectives
PACS 602.subject: PACS
PACS 602.description: Graduate seminar. Critical analysis of the way physical, social and cultural aspects of Oceania have been represented in scholarly and popular media.

PACS 603.title: Researching Oceania: Creative and Conventional Methods of Inquiry
PACS 603.subject: PACS
PACS 603.description: Graduate seminar. Literacy, theory and method in the creation of a Master’s research project.

PACS 640.title: Women in Oceania

PACS 655.title: Community Fisheries in Oceania
PACS 655.subject: PACS
PACS 655.description: Explores Pacific communities’ fisheries management, cultural practices, and reciprocal relationships, highlighting their beliefs, traditions, and innovations in sustaining marine resources for present and future generations.

PACS 675.title: Topics in Histories of Oceania
PACS 675.subject: PACS
PACS 675.description: Reading and research on major issues, topics, and themes in the history of Oceania.
PACS 675.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PACS 690.title: Graduate Seminar: Change in the Pacific

PATH 515.title: Unit V Concurrent Elective

PATH 525.title: Unit V Block Elective
PATH 525.subject: PATH
PATH 525.description: Required elective for second-year medical students, objectives to be determined by contract. One option is a review of USMLE Part I.

PATH 541.title: Pathology Practicum
PATH 541.subject: PATH
PATH 541.description: Required autopsy experience involving dissection and microscopic examination of tissues and detailed evaluation of disease process.
PATH 541.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: third- or fourth-year standing.

PATH 545B.title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: advanced topics in clinical immunology
PATH 545B.subject: PATH
PATH 545B.description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

PATH 545C.title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: anatomic pathology

PATH 545C.description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

PATH 595.title: Introduction to Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
PATH 595.subject: PATH
PATH 595.description: Provides an introduction to the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine and the role pathologists and the laboratory play in the diagnosis and management of disease.

PATH 599.title: Electives in Pathology
PATH 599.subject: PATH
PATH 599.description: Individualized instruction in clinical and/or anatomic pathology. Third-year elective.

PED 501.title: Pediatric Seminars
PED 501.subject: PED
PED 501.description: Interactive weekly lecture/seminar designed to teach topics in pediatrics and supplemented by small group 2-hour encounters with faculty clinicians in pediatric emergency medicine, inpatient pediatric, and enonatology to gain exposure in pediatric hospital care.

PED 503.title: Pediatric Shadowing Encounters
PED 503.subject: PED
PED 503.description: Clinical Shadowing — Students are paired with Pediatric Subspecialists in chosen area(s) for 8-10 half days. Required: Log book file describing one concept that the student learned during each of the sessions.

PED 506.title: Introduction to Research Methodology, Biostatistics, and Epidemiology
PED 506.subject: PED
PED 506.description: Interactive seminar series to cover the following topics: data types, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, selecting a statistical test, data distributions, measures of data spread, statistical test assumptions, standard deviation vs. standard error, etc.

PED 532.title: Pediatrics Longitudinal Clerkship
PED 532.subject: PED
PED 532.description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, covering evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of childhood diseases. Emphasis on primary prevention, normal growth and development of the neonate to adolescent, and arrangement of pediatric care, including outpatient, inpatient, and emergency room experiences.
PED 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.
PED 532.coreq_raw: MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532, PSTY 532 , and SURG 532 .

PEPS 210.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
PEPS 210.subject: PEPS
PEPS 210.description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

PEPS 250.title: The World of Insects
PEPS 250.subject: PEPS
PEPS 250.description: Biology/ecology of insects with emphasis on relationships to plants, animals, and especially people in Hawaiʻi and the tropics. Open to nonmajors.

PEPS 310.title: Environment and Agriculture
PEPS 310.subject: PEPS
PEPS 310.description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

PEPS 340.title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
PEPS 340.subject: PEPS
PEPS 340.description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawaiʻi.
PEPS 340.prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

PEPS 350.title: Invasive Pest Species
PEPS 350.subject: PEPS
PEPS 350.description: Ecological, economic and sociological impacts of invasive species on tropical ecosystems; characteristics of invasive species and vulnerability of habitats; ethical issues on impacts of management options on evolution, biodiversity and eco-stability and human life. Open to nonmajors.

PEPS 363.title: General Entomology
PEPS 363.subject: PEPS
PEPS 363.description: Biology, diversity, and ecology of insects with emphasis on Hawaiian fauna. Classification to order level.
PEPS 363.prereq_raw: ( BOT 101 or ZOOL 101 or BIOL 171 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

PEPS 363L.title: General Entomology Laboratory
PEPS 363L.subject: PEPS
PEPS 363L.description: Laboratory in the biology and classification to family level of Hawaiʻi’s insects and arthropods.
PEPS 363L.prereq_raw: ( PEPS 363 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

PEPS 371.title: Genetics: Theory to Application
PEPS 371.subject: PEPS
PEPS 371.description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

PEPS 401.title: Agricultural Biosecurity and Food Safety
PEPS 401.subject: PEPS
PEPS 401.description: Introduction and overview to concepts of agricultural biosecurity and food safety (including plant and animal biosecurity), the global impacts of introduced pests and diseases, and current mechanisms for interception of pests and mitigation of disease.

PEPS 403.title: Tropical Fruit Production
PEPS 403.subject: PEPS
PEPS 403.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices and recent innovations in tropical and subtropical fruit crops, emphasizing botanical aspects and commercial production in Hawaiʻi and beyond.

PEPS 405.title: Plant Pathogens and Diseases
PEPS 405.subject: PEPS
PEPS 405.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Classification, morphology, ecology, and biology of bacteria, fungi, nematodes, and viruses that attack economic crops. Etiology and control of plant diseases.
PEPS 405.prereq_raw: PEPS 210 / SUST 210 or BOT 101 or MICR 130 , or consent.

PEPS 410.title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
PEPS 410.subject: PEPS
PEPS 410.description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

PEPS 418.title: Turfgrass Pest Management
PEPS 418.subject: PEPS
PEPS 418.description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawaiʻi, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

PEPS 421.title: Foundations of Pest Management
PEPS 421.subject: PEPS
PEPS 421.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles and concepts of insect pest management; biological, cultural, physical, and chemical control; sampling protocol; pests of fruit and vegetable crops, turf and urban landscape plants, urban structures, and environments including medically important insects.
PEPS 421.prereq_raw: one of the following: PEPS 250 or PEPS 363 , BIOL 171 , BIOL 172 , or BOT 101 ; or consent.

children.text: or PEPS 363 , BIOL 171 , BIOL 172 , or BOT 101 ; or consent

PEPS 422.title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
PEPS 422.subject: PEPS
PEPS 422.description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

PEPS 430.title: Plant Disease Epidemiology and Management
PEPS 430.subject: PEPS
PEPS 430.description: Epidemiological principles and integrated disease management of important pathogens and diseases affecting key crops in various agroecosystems in Hawaiʻi and the global tropics. This course develops writing skills.

PEPS 437.title: Applied UAS Operations for Agriculture and Environment
PEPS 437.subject: PEPS
PEPS 437.description: Applies operations with uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), mission planning, safety, photogrammetry and GIS, personnel management, and payload operation. Focus on topics required for commercial certifications as a remote pilot, agricultural operator, and pesticide applicator.
PEPS 437.prereq_raw: completion of FS/FQ, DP, DB, and DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

children.text: DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-

PEPS 437.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: STEM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

PEPS 445.title: Insects as Food & Feed
PEPS 445.subject: PEPS
PEPS 445.description: Biology, ecology, and nutritional value of edible insects. Explores the use of edible insects as alternative protein sources for human consumption and animal feed as solutions to global food security.
PEPS 445.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Undergraduate students only.

PEPS 451.title: Environmental Law
PEPS 451.subject: PEPS
PEPS 451.description: Exploration of federal laws, regulations, and precedents that govern our interaction with the environment. Analysis of laws regulating air, water, toxins, pests, endangered species, and environmental justice.
PEPS 451.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing.

PEPS 463.title: Medical and Urban Entomology
PEPS 463.subject: PEPS
PEPS 463.description: (2 Lec, 1-3-hr hybrid Lab) Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.
PEPS 463.prereq_raw: ( PEPS 363 or BIOL 265 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

PEPS 481.title: Weed Science
PEPS 481.subject: PEPS
PEPS 481.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Weed classification, identification, adaptations for weediness; principles of weed control; properties, uses, and action of herbicides. Lab: pesticide application equipment and techniques, no-till farming, greenhouse and field experiments.
PEPS 481.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 152 and TPSS 200 / SUST 211 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

PEPS 486.title: Insect-Plant Interactions
PEPS 486.subject: PEPS
PEPS 486.description: Study of the coevolutionary relationships between insects and plants, with emphasis on the behavior, physiology, and symbiotic relationships of insects. Discussed in the context of sustainable agriculture, anthropogenic change, and climate change.
PEPS 486.prereq_raw: PEPS 363 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

PEPS 491.title: Topics in Plant & Environmental Protection
PEPS 491.subject: PEPS
PEPS 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. May be offered by visiting faculty, extension faculty or research faculty.

PEPS 495.title: PEPS Capstone
PEPS 495.subject: PEPS
PEPS 495.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development, Directed Research, field studies, employment with cooperating businesses, government or schools are all options.

PEPS 499.title: Directed Research
PEPS 499.subject: PEPS
PEPS 499.description: Conduct original research in environmental protection sciences. Limited to qualified undergraduate students.

PEPS 601.title: Advanced Agrosecurity and Food Safety
PEPS 601.subject: PEPS
PEPS 601.description: Concepts of agrosecurity and food safety (including plant and animal biosecurity), global impacts of introduced pests and diseases, and current mechanisms for interception of pests and mitigation of disease.

PEPS 605.title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Fungi and Nematodes
PEPS 605.subject: PEPS
PEPS 605.description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr. Lab) Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology and management of plant diseases caused by fungi, oomycetes, and nematodes. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.

PEPS 606.title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Bacteria and Viruses
PEPS 606.subject: PEPS
PEPS 606.description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology, and management of plant diseases caused by bacteria and viruses. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.
PEPS 606.prereq_raw: PEPS 605 (with a minimum grade of B).

PEPS 611.title: Professional Development
PEPS 611.subject: PEPS
PEPS 611.description: Lecture/ discussion targets students exiting from graduate degree programs and provides preparation as a career professional; topics include establishing a professional identity; CV and cover letters, job-seeking due diligence, and negotiation skills.
PEPS 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PEPS 615.title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases
PEPS 615.subject: PEPS
PEPS 615.description: Iterative and interactive course integrating plant pathogen and pest biology with diagnostic and management approaches. Will use biological information about pathogens, anthropods, and abiotic stresses to diagnose diseases, disorders, or other injuries of plants.
PEPS 615.prereq_raw: ( PEPS 605 and PEPS 606 ) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

PEPS 615L.title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases Laboratory
PEPS 615L.subject: PEPS
PEPS 615L.description: Diagnosis and management of plant pathogen and pest problems in laboratory and field. Taught concurrently with PEPS 615 .
PEPS 615L.prereq_raw: ( PEPS 605 and PEPS 606 ) with a minimum grade of B, or equivalent.

PEPS 620.title: Plant Biochemistry
PEPS 620.subject: PEPS
PEPS 620.description: Comprehensive study of chemical constituents and biochemical processes unique to the plant kingdom with emphasis on selected aspects of current interest.
PEPS 620.prereq_raw: MBBE 402 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

PEPS 627.title: Molecular Diagnostics: Principles and Practices
PEPS 627.subject: PEPS
PEPS 627.description: Molecular diagnostics principles, comparative genomics, genome annotation and bio-informatics, phylogenetics, gene target selection, advanced primer, and probe design.
PEPS 627.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

PEPS 640.title: Insect Nutrient Regulation
PEPS 640.subject: PEPS
PEPS 640.description: Focuses on nutrient intake and utilization by insects with emphasis on herbivory and agricultural pests. A multitude of environmental factors that influence nutrient regulation will be discussed.
PEPS 640.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PEPS 641.title: Insect Physiology
PEPS 641.subject: PEPS
PEPS 641.description: (2 Lec) Study of the principal physiological and biochemical functions in insects, with emphasis on hormonal interactions.

PEPS 645.title: Advanced Entomophagy
PEPS 645.subject: PEPS
PEPS 645.description: This advanced course examines the scientific, technological, and socio-economic dimensions of entomophagy–the use of insects and insect-derived materials as sustainable sources of food and feed for an expanding global population.
PEPS 645.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PEPS 652.title: Molecular Plant-Fungal Interactions
PEPS 652.subject: PEPS
PEPS 652.description: Focuses on the actions of plant pathogenic fungi/ oomycetes and their host responses at the molecular and cellular level. Current genetic and genomic approaches to study plant-fungal interactions will be discussed. Graduate standing only.

PEPS 660.title: Seminar in Plant Pathology
PEPS 660.subject: PEPS
PEPS 660.description: Seminar on research and topics in plant pathology.
PEPS 660.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PEPS 662.title: Systematics and Phylogenetics
PEPS 662.subject: PEPS
PEPS 662.description: Classification and study of diversity among insects and other life forms. Use of morphological and molecular characters to reconstruct evolutionary histories.
PEPS 662.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

PEPS 671.title: Insect Ecology
PEPS 671.subject: PEPS
PEPS 671.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Insects as living units in an environment of physical and biotic factors.

PEPS 675.title: Biological Control of Pests
PEPS 675.subject: PEPS
PEPS 675.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental concepts. Critical study of major biological control projects.
PEPS 675.prereq_raw: PEPS 421 or consent. Recommended: PEPS 662 ; and ZOOL 631 or ZOOL 632 .

children.text: Recommended: PEPS 662 ; and ZOOL 631 or ZOOL 632

PEPS 676.title: Biological Control of Weeds
PEPS 676.subject: PEPS
PEPS 676.description: Examine approaches to weed biological control of invasive plants in various environments with different agents (insects, pathogens, and vertebrates), integration with other management tactics, sociopolitical aspects, and history of the practice.
PEPS 676.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PEPS 686.title: Invertebrate Microbiology
PEPS 686.subject: PEPS
PEPS 686.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) In-depth study of the molecular and cellular interactions between microbes and animals. Topics will cover types of symbioses, gut microbiome, parasites, and agricultural pathogens, and disease and human health disease.

PEPS 690.title: Seminar in Entomology
PEPS 690.subject: PEPS
PEPS 690.description: Seminars on research and topics in entomology.
PEPS 690.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PEPS 691.title: Special Topics
PEPS 691.subject: PEPS
PEPS 691.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in plant and environmental protection sciences at an advanced level. Offered by visiting or existing faculty as a special course.
PEPS 691.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PEPS 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
PEPS 695.subject: PEPS
PEPS 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
PEPS 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in entomology or tropical plant pathology.

PEPS 699.title: Directed Research
PEPS 699.subject: PEPS
PEPS 699.description: Directed research, critical reviews in environmental protection sciences, entomology, or plant pathology.

PEPS 716.title: Advanced Plant Nematology
PEPS 716.subject: PEPS
PEPS 716.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Advanced study of nematode taxonomy, genetics, behavior, host interactions, and sustainable management in an integrated lecture-laboratory.
PEPS 716.prereq_raw: PEPS 605 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

PEPS 730.title: Advanced Plant Virology
PEPS 730.subject: PEPS
PEPS 730.description: Characterization, genome organization, gene expression, and molecular mechanisms of plant viruses.
PEPS 730.prereq_raw: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

PEPS 746.title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
PEPS 746.subject: PEPS
PEPS 746.description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts.
PEPS 746.prereq_raw: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent.

PEPS 799.title: Proposal/Defense Seminar
PEPS 799.subject: PEPS
PEPS 799.description: Thesis/ dissertation proposal and defense seminars.
PEPS 799.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PH 201.title: Introduction to Public Health
PH 201.subject: PH
PH 201.description: Introduces public health concepts with an emphasis on principles and tools for population health, disease prevention, health professions and healthcare systems, and public health professions and systems.

PH 202.title: Public Health Issues in Hawaiʻi
PH 202.subject: PH
PH 202.description: Application of general public health concepts and tools with broader public health issues as they relate to the State of Hawaiʻi.

PH 203.title: Introduction to Global Health
PH 203.subject: PH
PH 203.description: Introduction to the basic principles of global PH. Topics include the application of these principles to global PH issues, exploration of links between health, economic, and social status, health disparities and global interventions.

PH 210.title: Quantitative Reasoning for Public Health
PH 210.subject: PH
PH 210.description: Inductive and deductive reasoning; tabular, symbolic, verbal, and graphical forms of functions and relations; graphs and pictorial representations of data; interpretations of probabilistic data; surveys and statistical studies as related to public health.

PH 211.title: Public Health Student Success in the College Experience
PH 211.subject: PH
PH 211.description: Required for entering PH majors to gain strategies for a successful college experience while studying public health. Students will examine academic and career goals and implement strategies to achieve them.

PH 301.title: Seminar in Public Health Issues
PH 301.subject: PH
PH 301.description: Seminar will explore current issues and case studies in epidemiology, issues and causes of chronic and infectious diseases, how the environment interacts with health, and how social and behavioral factors affect personal health.

PH 305.title: Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
PH 305.subject: PH
PH 305.description: Seminar to work with faculty in applying evidence-based knowledge on social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians. Junior standing or higher.

PH 310.title: Introduction to Epidemiology
PH 310.subject: PH
PH 310.description: Lecture/discussion on the fundamental principles of epidemiology, exploring patterns of disease, threats to health and EPI methods for prevention, control, and treatment.
PH 310.prereq_raw: PH 201 , and PH 210 or MATH 140X or MATH 161 or higher; or instructor approval.

PH 325.title: Youth Risk and Protection—Public Health Research, Practice, and Policy
PH 325.subject: PH
PH 325.description: Application of public health, related to youth health risks and protective factors using an eco-developmental framework.

PH 330.title: The United States Health Care System
PH 330.subject: PH
PH 330.description: Overview of the U.S. health care system. Topics will include health economics, health service expenditures, comparative health systems, health policy, and issues of cost containment, access, and quality of care.

PH 340.title: Public Health and the Environment
PH 340.subject: PH
PH 340.description: Examines a variety of issues associated with environmental effects on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Sophomore standing and above.

PH 341.title: Public Health Biology and Pathophysiology
PH 341.subject: PH
PH 341.description: Explores the biological basis of human disease and the role public health measures play in reducing both the extent and impact of chronic and acute diseases on individuals and society.
PH 341.prereq_raw: PH 201 , and one of the following: BIOL 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 or FSHN 185 .

PH 350.title: Introduction to Biostatistics
PH 350.subject: PH
PH 350.description: Basic biostatistics methods in public health and biomedical research. Topics covered include data collection, data analyses, and interpretation of statistical results. Sophomore standing or higher.

PH 410.title: Advanced Epidemiology
PH 410.subject: PH
PH 410.description: Students will gain a deeper understanding of the core concepts used in epidemiologic research and practice. Upon completion, students will have the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct an epidemiologic study. Junior standing or higher.

PH 411.title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
PH 411.subject: PH
PH 411.description: Lecture/discussion. Examines a variety of issues associated with the effects of diet on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Junior standing or higher.

PH 420.title: Social Behavioral Health I: Health Promotion for Individuals and Groups
PH 420.subject: PH
PH 420.description: Focus on the application of social and behavioral theory in health education, and how health promotion programs are constructed for various populations with an emphasis on cultural diversity and social determinants of health.
PH 420.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PH 422.title: Social Behavioral Health II: Health Promotion in Communities
PH 422.subject: PH
PH 422.description: Introduction to health education and health promotion programming in public health, and to social/behavioral theories used to develop health interventions that affect communities, institutions, and policies. Introduction to common program planning models.

PH 425.title: Tobacco & Community Disparities
PH 425.subject: PH
PH 425.description: Assessing the facilitators and barriers of smoking initiation, cessation, and exposure to second-hand smoke within communities. Use of photovoice and its application to policy and addressing disparities.

PH 430.title: Health Policy and Management
PH 430.subject: PH
PH 430.description: Examines the role that health policy and management plays in population-based public health practice, including the delivery, quality, and costs of health care and the structure, process, and outcomes of health services delivery. Sophomore standing or higher.

PH 435.title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
PH 435.subject: PH
PH 435.description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
PH 435.prereq_raw: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200 ; or consent.

PH 441.title: Introduction to One Health
PH 441.subject: PH
PH 441.description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health—an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections. Junior standing or higher.
PH 441.prereq_raw: ( PH 201 , or ANSC 200 , or BIOC 141 , or BIOL 101 , or BIOL 171 , or BOT 101 , or ERTH 101 , or GES 102 , or OEST 101 , or OCN 102 , or ATMO 150, or SOC 180 ) with a minimum grade of C or better; or consent.

PH 445.title: Introduction to Environmental Microbiology
PH 445.subject: PH
PH 445.description: Lecture/discussion. Will define the nature and biological activities of microorganisms in different environments and evaluate the effects of these microbes on human activities and health. Junior standing or higher.

PH 460.title: Social Determinants of Indigenous Peoples’ Health
PH 460.subject: PH
PH 460.description: Examines indigenous peoples’ health inequities using social determinants of health framework: considers this approach within the historical, political, cultural, and social context of Indigenous population’s health status to generate solutions.

PH 480.title: Application of Public Health Principles in Research and Practice
PH 480.subject: PH
PH 480.description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health projects and associated methods while working to develop a written applied learning project literature review. Students will present their findings at a public forum.
PH 480.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

PH 485.title: Public Health Applied Learning Experience
PH 485.subject: PH
PH 485.description: Allows students to execute an independent, mentor-supervised, applied learning project as implementation of skills learned in previous public health coursework. Applied project is a required component of the public health undergraduate degree program.

PH 489.title: Public Health Undergraduate Capstone Seminar
PH 489.subject: PH
PH 489.description: Synthesis of public health knowledge, skills, and practice acquired during the public health undergraduate degree. Students also reflect on, finalize, and present written applied learning experience projects at a public form. Senior standing and higher.
PH 489.prereq_raw: completed public health applied learning experience and consent.

children.text: completed public health applied learning experience

PH 492B.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: biostatistics
PH 492B.subject: PH
PH 492B.description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
PH 492B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

PH 492E.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: epidemiology
PH 492E.subject: PH
PH 492E.description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
PH 492E.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

PH 492H.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: health policy and management
PH 492H.subject: PH
PH 492H.description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
PH 492H.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

PH 492S.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: social and behavioral health sciences
PH 492S.subject: PH
PH 492S.description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
PH 492S.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

PH 492T.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: public health
PH 492T.subject: PH
PH 492T.description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
PH 492T.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

PH 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
PH 499.subject: PH
PH 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

PH 600.title: Public Health Foundations
PH 600.subject: PH
PH 600.description: Focus will provide a broad introduction to the field of public health and orientation to overarching issues in the field.

PH 602.title: U.S. Health Care Services and Policy
PH 602.subject: PH
PH 602.description: Overview of the historical, conceptual, ethical and political context for health care delivery in the U.S. Explores current trends, practices and issues in the delivery of health care services in both private and public sector.

PH 610.title: Public Health Biology
PH 610.subject: PH
PH 610.description: Writing-intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management.

PH 611.title: Fundamentals to One Health
PH 611.subject: PH
PH 611.description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health—an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections.
PH 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 623.title: Introduction to Health Promotion Theory and Methods
PH 623.subject: PH
PH 623.description: Individual and community health; implications for public health practice, individual and social change processes.

PH 626.title: Health Economics
PH 626.subject: PH
PH 626.description: Integrated concepts in health economics and its application towards health policy issues; market failures in health care; factors affecting U.S. health care spending potential impact on equity/efficiency stemming from changes in health care delivery.

PH 630.title: Cultural Competency in Health Care
PH 630.subject: PH
PH 630.description: Presents both analytical and practical approaches to cultural competency domains, concepts, models, frameworks, patterns and communication that occur in cross-cultural healthcare situations.

PH 633.title: Indigenous Health Activism
PH 633.subject: PH
PH 633.description: Examines how Indigenous Peoples and their allies (individually and collectively) accomplish social change in society.
PH 633.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 635.title: Indigenous Health Seminar
PH 635.subject: PH
PH 635.description: Examines public health through an Indigenous lens, integrates competencies across all public health disciplines, and will apply them in context of working for and with Indigenous communities to improve health and wellness.
PH 635.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 641.title: Advanced Topics in Health Policy
PH 641.subject: PH
PH 641.description: Examines major federal and local policies that impact health and health care delivery in the U.S. and other nations; considers effectiveness of these policy-making institutions for improving population health; covers methods in policy analysis.

PH 646.title: Grant Writing in Public Health
PH 646.subject: PH
PH 646.description: Lecture/ discussion on grant writing with public health focus. Includes basic components of grant proposals, assessing appropriate funding opportunities, data sources/resources for justifying grants, and the funder’s perspective. Student will prepare a brief foundation grant proposal.

PH 648.title: Program Planning, Management, Evaluation, and Leadership
PH 648.subject: PH
PH 648.description: Foundation to inform, educate, and improve health for individuals, communities, and populations. Knowledge/acquisition of skills through program planning, management, evaluation and leadership that span the social-ecological range from individual-level to population-level programs.
PH 648.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EPID and PH majors only.

PH 649.title: Needs Assessment
PH 649.subject: PH
PH 649.description: Knowledge and skills acquisition in conducting needs assessment in public health practice.

PH 650.title: Ecological Epidemiology
PH 650.subject: PH
PH 650.description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

PH 652.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
PH 652.subject: PH
PH 652.description: Topics such as contemporary issues in global health and population studies, international health programs, demographic methods, global economy and health, human right and humanitarian assistance, social justice, global environmental changes and health.

PH 653.title: Global Health and Human Security
PH 653.subject: PH
PH 653.description: Provides the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to successfully manage health security crises and protect human vulnerability in the global context with a special focus on problems with high likelihood and risk in the Pacific.

PH 655.title: Biostatistics I
PH 655.subject: PH
PH 655.description: Introduction to statistical methods for public health sciences. Probability, experimental design, t tests and analysis of variance, 2X2 contingency tables, linear regression, introduction to life tables.

PH 656.title: Biostatistics II
PH 656.subject: PH
PH 656.description: Poisson distribution, Fisher’s exact test, contrasts in ANOVA, two way ANOVA, multiple linear regression and analysis of covariance, path analysis, logistic regression, method of maximum likelihood, likelihood ratio tests.
PH 656.prereq_raw: PH 655 , completion of one semester of calculus; or consent.

children.text: completion of one semester of calculus;

PH 658.title: Computer Applications in Public Health
PH 658.subject: PH
PH 658.description: Applications of computers to problems common to public health. Emphasis on data analysis and processing using existing computer programs.

PH 659.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
PH 659.subject: PH
PH 659.description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, and urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

PH 663.title: Principles of Epidemiology I
PH 663.subject: PH
PH 663.description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods. Topics covered include: outbreak investigation, measures of morbidity and mortality, measurements of risk, biological variability, screening, measurements of error, sampling, statistical significance, study design, and association and causation.

PH 664.title: Principles of Epidemiology II
PH 664.subject: PH
PH 664.description: Lecture/ discussion on: design and interpretation of experimental and observational studies; causation and casual inference; biases in study design; random error and statistics role in epidemiology; and epidemiological data analysis.

PH 665.title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
PH 665.subject: PH
PH 665.description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

PH 666.title: Seminar in Infectious Disease Control
PH 666.subject: PH
PH 666.description: Strategies for controlling important infectious diseases in the Pacific area. Emphasis on epidemiology, ecology, and public health principles.
PH 666.prereq_raw: PH 663 (or concurrent) and one semester in microbiology, or consent.

PH 667.title: Infectious Disease Micro II
PH 667.subject: PH
PH 667.description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

PH 669.title: Epidemiological Study Design Critique
PH 669.subject: PH
PH 669.description: Critique of study design using published public health literature. Emphasis on exchange of ideas, alternative approaches; stresses epidemiology as science of public health.

PH 671.title: Community and Public Health Practice
PH 671.subject: PH
PH 671.description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

PH 672.title: Leading and Managing Health Programs
PH 672.subject: PH
PH 672.description: Assess how to organize community partnerships to create and communicate a shared vision for a changing future; discuss solutions to organizational and community challenges; maximize motivation to reach public health goals.

PH 673.title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
PH 673.subject: PH
PH 673.description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle.

PH 674.title: Advanced Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
PH 674.subject: PH
PH 674.description: Applications of evidence-based knowledge about the social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians.

PH 675.title: Community Engaged Research and Practice
PH 675.subject: PH
PH 675.description: Explores collaborative and engaged approaches with communities in public health research and practice. With a focus on Indigenous Peoples’ health, we delve into Indigenous knowledge and empowerment in evaluation, needs assessment, intervention, and health promotion.
PH 675.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 676.title: Hawaiʻi Public Health Policies on Infectious Diseases
PH 676.subject: PH
PH 676.description: Examines quarantine/isolation of patients infected with Hanson’s disease. Focus on PH policies before 1823 and after; analysis of other infections in Hawaiʻi and the world to examine differences in policies and their effect on the public.
PH 676.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 677.title: Managing Global Health Service Delivery
PH 677.subject: PH
PH 677.description: Provides knowledge, skills, attitudes and resources that health managers require to manage and maintain the quality of partnerships, facilities, programs, community services, people, drugs, and information in limited resources settings.

PH 680.title: Health Emergencies in Large Populations
PH 680.subject: PH
PH 680.description: Health Emergencies in Large Populations is run by the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance and the Red Cross. It provides knowledge, practical skills, and networking for global health practitioners.

PH 681.title: Environmental Determinants of Health
PH 681.subject: PH
PH 681.description: Environmental factors in personal and community health; implications for public health practice. Consideration of major issues from local, U.S., and international perspectives.

PH 683.title: Global Nutrition
PH 683.subject: PH
PH 683.description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

PH 684.title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
PH 684.subject: PH
PH 684.description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.

PH 686.title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
PH 686.subject: PH
PH 686.description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

PH 688.title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
PH 688.subject: PH
PH 688.description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored.
PH 688.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 689.title: Nutritional Epidemiology
PH 689.subject: PH
PH 689.description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

PH 690.title: Global Health Challenges
PH 690.subject: PH
PH 690.description: Addresses critical, contemporary, and transnational issues best addressed by cooperative international action. Health issues are examined in the context of intersecting effects of limited resources, socioeconomics, politics, and environmental change.

PH 691.title: Fundamentals of Environmental Epidemiology
PH 691.subject: PH
PH 691.description: Examines the complex relationship between environmental contaminants and human health. Emphasis on environmental epidemiology study design, environmental exposure monitoring and risk assessment, disease and environmental exposure mapping, and spatial data analysis and modeling with GIS.

PH 692.title: Preparation for Public Health Practice
PH 692.subject: PH
PH 692.description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health workforce readiness and professional skills while exploring possible field experience options.
PH 692.prereq_raw: PH 600 and completion of 9 graduate PH credit hours.

children.text: completion of 9 graduate PH credit hours

PH 695.title: Promoting Physical Activity
PH 695.subject: PH
PH 695.description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

PH 701.title: Health Communication
PH 701.subject: PH
PH 701.description: Skills-oriented course introduces the basic structure of health communication strategies in different settings, selected elements of communication theory, the development of health communication material, and a practical training in motivational counseling skills.

PH 702.title: Health Promotion Research
PH 702.subject: PH
PH 702.description: Focus on research methods commonly used in health promotion. Topics will include randomized trials, quasi-experimental design, sampling, measurement, and correlational studies. Labwork will focus on the use of SPSS to analyze data for applied research problems.

PH 704.title: Community-Based Participatory Research
PH 704.subject: PH
PH 704.description: Explores ways academic and lay communities collaborate on research, key theoretical perspectives in the development of CBPR, and the challenges in implementing CBPR approaches. Format includes lectures, discussions, readings, writing assignments, and a fieldwork project.

PH 720.title: Systematic Literature Review in Public Health
PH 720.subject: PH
PH 720.description: Imparts skills in conducting a systematic review of the literature. Students provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work. Intended for doctoral students to complete their qualifying paper.
PH 720.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only. Consent or PhD in PH or EPID only. Class Standing Restrictions: Doctoral students only.

PH 728.title: Indigenous Applied Research Methods
PH 728.subject: PH
PH 728.description: Qualitative research methods design, implementation, and analysis with special focus on methodological, ontological, and ethical issues unique to conducting research with Indigenous communities.

PH 729.title: Survey Methods for Indigenous People
PH 729.subject: PH
PH 729.description: Advanced application of health disparities research methodologies to address health and social injustices faced by Indigenous people. Grounded in survey design, implementation, and analyses through a public health and Indigenous lens.
PH 729.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 742.title: Qualitative Research for Public Health Sciences
PH 742.subject: PH
PH 742.description: Provides a basic understanding of qualitative research approaches, methodologies, and techniques and for public health research and practice (needs assessment, program development, and evaluation strategies).
PH 742.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 747.title: Statistical Methods in Epidemiological Research
PH 747.subject: PH
PH 747.description: Multiple variable statistical methods currently used in chronic disease epidemiology. Logistic regression, conditional logistic regression, proportional hazards regression modelling, generalized estimating equation-based methods, delta method approximations, exact tests.

PH 748.title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology
PH 748.subject: PH
PH 748.description: Will cover selected topics in chronic diseases with critical analysis of the current epidemiologic literature. Methodologic issues, contemporary findings and recommendations for future research will be discussed.

PH 749.title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
PH 749.subject: PH
PH 749.description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.

PH 750.title: Health Behavior Change
PH 750.subject: PH
PH 750.description: Provide an understanding of the relationship between health behaviors and outcomes including psychological, physiological, and quality of life aspects. It will also focus on the major theories of behavior and behavior change. Emphasis will be placed on understanding concepts, principles, explanations, and how these are translated into practical interventions for adoption and maintaining behavior change.

PH 751.title: Social Epidemiology
PH 751.subject: PH
PH 751.description: Examine the epidemiologic study of the social distribution and social determinants of states of health, including the identification of social-environmental exposures and their relation to physical and mental health outcomes.

PH 752.title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
PH 752.subject: PH
PH 752.description: Covers modern methods for longitudinal data analysis. Topics include random effects and growth curve models, generalized linear models for longitudinal data including generalized estimating equations, and generalized linear mixed models.

PH 753.title: Survival Analysis
PH 753.subject: PH
PH 753.description: Construction and interpretation of various types of life tables, treatment of censored data, proportional hazards, relative risk regression models, and parametric survival analysis.

PH 754.title: Neuroepidemiology
PH 754.subject: PH
PH 754.description: Lecture/discussion providing an overview of the epidemiology of neurological and neurodegenerative diseases and their risk factors, and methodological considerations for the study of these diseases.

PH 755.title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
PH 755.subject: PH
PH 755.description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

PH 756.title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
PH 756.subject: PH
PH 756.description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health.

PH 757.title: Evolution, Epidemiology, and Public Health
PH 757.subject: PH
PH 757.description: Will explore several aspects of human health through the perspective of how natural selection and evolution influence disease risk, with the aim of improving treatment and prevention.
PH 757.prereq_raw: PH 663 (with a minimum grade of B).
PH 757.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PH 765.title: Health Program Evaluation
PH 765.subject: PH
PH 765.description: Examines advanced principles of and frameworks for evaluation. Students integrate utilization-focused evaluation methods to improve service delivery and quality, outcomes and impact to improve community and population health.

PH 770D.title: Doctoral Seminar in Translational Research: evidence-based public health
PH 770D.subject: PH
PH 770D.description: Required for students in the PhD PH program. (D) evidence-based public health; (E) health policy and leadership.

PH 770E.title: Doctoral Seminar in Translational Research: topics in health policy and leadership
PH 770E.subject: PH
PH 770E.description: Required for students in the PhD PH program. (D) evidence-based public health; (E) health policy and leadership.

PH 771.title: Teaching Practicum
PH 771.subject: PH
PH 771.description: Provide doctoral students with theoretical and practical teaching and course development experiences under the guidance of a faculty mentor. Students will have a portfolio documenting their accomplishments.
PH 771.prereq_raw: PH 602 and PH 623 and PH 655 and PH 633 and PH 681 and PH 770 (Alpha), or departmental approval.
PH 771.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in PH only.

PH 772.title: Research Practicum
PH 772.subject: PH
PH 772.description: Hands-on research experience with a faculty mentor. Meet in small groups to discuss issues related to research in public health. Final project will be submission of a publishable quality paper.
PH 772.prereq_raw: PH 602 and PH 623 and PH 655 and PH 663 and PH 681 and PH 770 (Alpha), or departmental approval.
PH 772.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in PH only.

PH 775.title: Public Health Proposal and Dissertation Writing
PH 775.subject: PH
PH 775.description: Intended for doctoral students to complete and defend their proposals and dissertations. Research and presentation methods will be reviewed, and students will be provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work.
PH 775.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: consent or PhD in PH or EPID only.

PH 781.title: Environmental Health Lab Methods
PH 781.subject: PH
PH 781.description: Hands-on training for laboratory methods used in monitoring and detecting environmental health risk factors; learning and application of immunological-, animal cell culture- and molecular biology-based techniques for studying environmental pathogens and toxic pollutants.

PH 788.title: Seminar in Public Health Sciences
PH 788.subject: PH
PH 788.description: Topics related to recent developments in major areas; student and faculty research activities. Sections: (1) biostatistics; (2) environmental health; (3) epidemiology; (4) public health nutrition.

PH 789.title: Integrative Seminar
PH 789.subject: PH
PH 789.description: Integrative seminar in public health required as part of the student capstone experience to bring together key aspects of their courses, competencies, and practicum.
PH 789.prereq_raw: completed PH field practicum and consent.

PH 791.title: Advanced Public Health Practice
PH 791.subject: PH
PH 791.description: Observation, study, and supervised practical work in student’s area of specialization.
PH 791.prereq_raw: public health degree candidate; PH 692 and completion of 15 PH credit hours, and consent.

PH 792B.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: biostatistics
PH 792B.subject: PH
PH 792B.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792B.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).

PH 792D.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: environmental health
PH 792D.subject: PH
PH 792D.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792D.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).

PH 792E.subject: PH
PH 792E.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792E.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).
