PH 792H.subject: PH
PH 792H.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792H.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).

PH 792I.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health
PH 792I.subject: PH
PH 792I.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792I.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).

PH 792S.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: social and behavioral health sciences
PH 792S.subject: PH
PH 792S.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792S.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).

PH 792U.title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: public health
PH 792U.subject: PH
PH 792U.description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.
PH 792U.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only for (D) and (I).

PH 793.title: Special Practicum/Project
PH 793.subject: PH
PH 793.description: Supervised practical training beyond the required practicum in an area of particular interest. Provides additional opportunity to synthesize, integrate, and apply practical skills and knowledge in a public health work environment.

PH 794B.title: Exploration in Public Health: biostatistics
PH 794B.subject: PH
PH 794B.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PH 794D.title: Exploration in Public Health: environmental health
PH 794D.subject: PH
PH 794D.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PH 794E.title: Exploration in Public Health: epidemiology
PH 794E.subject: PH
PH 794E.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PH 794H.title: Exploration in Public Health: health policy and management
PH 794H.subject: PH
PH 794H.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PH 794I.title: Exploration in Public Health: Native Hawaiian and Indigenous health
PH 794I.subject: PH
PH 794I.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PH 794S.title: Exploration in Public Health: social and behavioral health sciences
PH 794S.subject: PH
PH 794S.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PH 794U.title: Exploration in Public Health: public health
PH 794U.subject: PH
PH 794U.description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

PHIL 100.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Survey of Problems
PHIL 100.subject: PHIL
PHIL 100.description: Introduction to the kinds of problems that concern philosophers and to some of the solutions that have been attempted.

PHIL 100A.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Survey of Problems
PHIL 100A.subject: PHIL
PHIL 100A.description: Introduction to the kinds of problems that concern philosophers and to some of the solutions that have been attempted.

PHIL 101.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Morals and Society
PHIL 101.subject: PHIL
PHIL 101.description: Philosophical attempts to evaluate conduct, character, and social practices.

PHIL 101A.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Morals and Society
PHIL 101A.subject: PHIL
PHIL 101A.description: Philosophical attempts to evaluate conduct, character, and social practices.

PHIL 102.title: Asian Traditions
PHIL 102.subject: PHIL
PHIL 102.description: Universal themes and problems from Asian perspective.

PHIL 102A.title: Asian Traditions
PHIL 102A.subject: PHIL
PHIL 102A.description: Universal themes and problems from Asian perspective.

PHIL 103.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Environmental Philosophy
PHIL 103.subject: PHIL
PHIL 103.description: A critical examination of environmental issues; analyzing the nature of the human being, the nature of nature, and the relationship of the human being to nature.

PHIL 104.title: Philosophy Through Computer Science
PHIL 104.subject: PHIL
PHIL 104.description: Introduction to classic philosophical issues (e.g., external world skepticism and free will) through computational concepts grounded in an introduction to computer science using Python.

PHIL 110.title: Introduction to Deductive Logic
PHIL 110.subject: PHIL
PHIL 110.description: Principles of modern deductive logic. Honors Equivalent: PHIL 110A

PHIL 111.title: Introduction to Inductive Logic
PHIL 111.subject: PHIL
PHIL 111.description: Introduction to the theory of arguments based on probabilities and to the theory of decision-making in the context of uncertainty.

PHIL 112.title: Introduction to Critical Thinking
PHIL 112.subject: PHIL
PHIL 112.description: (LED) Introduction to critical thinking and its application in everyday life. The materials progress from logic and the structure of argument to fallacies and the nature of science.

PHIL 114.title: Philosophy of Sport
PHIL 114.subject: PHIL
PHIL 114.description: Sport, from ancient ritual to modern spectacle, embodies ethics, aesthetics, and identity. This course examines Western and non-Western traditions, exploring sport as bodily cultivation, cultural practice, and philosophical lens on human flourishing and social division.

PHIL 121.title: How To Be Happy
PHIL 121.subject: PHIL
PHIL 121.description: Everyone wants to be happy. What is happiness? How do we become happy? Students examine and practice proposals from ancient philosophy and tragedy and recent psychology about the ingredients, methods, and difficulties of living well.

PHIL 130.title: Introduction to World Philosophy I
PHIL 130.subject: PHIL
PHIL 130.description: Introduction to philosophy as it has manifested itself differently across cultures throughout the world. Focus on the development of philosophical thought from its beginnings up until 1500 CE.

PHIL 131.title: Introduction to World Philosophy II
PHIL 131.subject: PHIL
PHIL 131.description: Philosophy attempts to understand the human being and the societies they form. Introduces students to the notion of world philosophy, focusing upon thinkers who have helped to shape our present.

PHIL 211.title: Ancient Philosophy
PHIL 211.subject: PHIL
PHIL 211.description: What is happiness? reality? the best political community? Students explore ancient Greek and Roman philosophical responses to these and other fundamental questions, and develop skills of writing, reading, and oral communication.

PHIL 212.title: Medieval to Enlightenment Philosophy
PHIL 212.subject: PHIL
PHIL 212.description: Introduction to the history of philosophy based on translations of texts originally written by men and women in post-classical Latin and Arabic. Significant attention is paid to developing writing skills.

PHIL 213.title: Modern Philosophy
PHIL 213.subject: PHIL
PHIL 213.description: Introduction to the history of philosophy based on texts or translations of “modern” works, that is works originally written in a modern European language.

PHIL 218.title: Women Philosophers
PHIL 218.subject: PHIL
PHIL 218.description: Introduces students to the ideas of women philosophers.
PHIL 218.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

PHIL 222.title: Existentialism: Freedom, Being, Death
PHIL 222.subject: PHIL
PHIL 222.description: Introduction to major thinkers and fundamental concepts and debates of Existentialism, taking Existentialism as a global movement expressed in philosophical texts, literature, and film. Significant attention is paid to developing writing skills.

PHIL 242.title: Philosophy and Science Fiction
PHIL 242.subject: PHIL
PHIL 242.description: Will use important works of science fiction and philosophy to explore philosophical questions, such as the nature of personal identity and the meaning of human life.

PHIL 270.title: Love and Sex
PHIL 270.subject: PHIL
PHIL 270.description: Survey of classical and contemporary perspectives of the philosophy of love, marriage, relationships, sex, sexual identity, representations of sex and sexuality.
PHIL 270.prereq_raw: one PHIL 100-level course or consent of instructor.

PHIL 300.title: Business Ethics
PHIL 300.subject: PHIL
PHIL 300.description: Case studies and critical analyses of ethical issues in business. Readings from business, philosophy, law, etc.
PHIL 300.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or BUS or BLAW, or consent.

PHIL 301.title: Ethical Theory
PHIL 301.subject: PHIL
PHIL 301.description: Problems and methods in theory of moral conduct and decision.
PHIL 301.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC; or consent.

PHIL 302.title: Political Philosophy
PHIL 302.subject: PHIL
PHIL 302.description: Problems and methods in philosophical theories of political legitimacy.
PHIL 302.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC, or consent.

PHIL 303.title: Social Philosophy
PHIL 303.subject: PHIL
PHIL 303.description: Problems and methods in examination of contemporary life, values, and institutions in light of traditional philosophical problems of freedom, justice, authority, equality.
PHIL 303.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC, or consent.

PHIL 304.title: Metaphysics
PHIL 304.subject: PHIL
PHIL 304.description: Problems arising from attempts to categorize rationally what is, and what appears to be. Among others, topics may include universals and particulars, personal identity, freedom and determinism, and time.
PHIL 304.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL, or consent.

PHIL 305.title: Philosophy of Religion
PHIL 305.subject: PHIL
PHIL 305.description: Problems and methods. Nature of religious experience, alternatives to theism, existence of god, relation between faith and reason, nature of religious language.

PHIL 306.title: Philosophy of Art
PHIL 306.subject: PHIL
PHIL 306.description: Problems and methods in aesthetic valuation and in appreciation, creation, and criticism of artworks.

PHIL 307.title: Theory of Knowledge
PHIL 307.subject: PHIL
PHIL 307.description: Problems and methods in epistemology. Nature of knowledge, its varieties, possibilities, and limitations.
PHIL 307.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 100 or above in PHIL, or 200 or above with either DB or DP or DS designation; or consent.

PHIL 308.title: Philosophy of Science
PHIL 308.subject: PHIL
PHIL 308.description: Philosophical questions about the methods of scientific inquiry. Significant attention given to developing writing skills.
PHIL 308.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 100 or above in PHIL, or 200 or above with either DB or DP designation; or consent.

PHIL 309.title: Philosophy of Education
PHIL 309.subject: PHIL
PHIL 309.description: Uses tools of philosophical inquiry to explore historical and contemporary perspectives on the nature of education, including concepts of knowledge, teaching, learning, and human flourishing.
PHIL 309.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL, or consent.

PHIL 310.title: Ethics in Health Care
PHIL 310.subject: PHIL
PHIL 310.description: Ethical issues in application and organization of biomedical resources; professional responsibility, confidentiality, euthanasia, experimentation on human subjects, etc.
PHIL 310.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or MED or NURS or with a DB designation; or consent.

PHIL 311.title: Philosophy and Aesthetics of Film
PHIL 311.subject: PHIL
PHIL 311.description: Aesthetics and ontology of film and video, based on readings in the philosophy of film and the viewing of a number of films per semester.

PHIL 312.title: Ethics in Practice
PHIL 312.subject: PHIL
PHIL 312.description: Team-taught exploration of five contemporary ethical issues using a variety of philosophical approaches and methods.
PHIL 312.prereq_raw: any PHIL 101 course or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC; or consent.

PHIL 313.title: Philosophy and Evolution
PHIL 313.subject: PHIL
PHIL 313.description: Explores the ethical and epistemological implications of the theory of evolution.

PHIL 314.title: Critical Thinking: Pre-Medicine
PHIL 314.subject: PHIL
PHIL 314.description: Scientific and social perspectives on the nature of disease and their impact on medical practice. Exploration of these topics through reading, writing and critical inquiry.
PHIL 314.prereq_raw: any course in PHIL, PHIL 100 or above; or any two BIOL, CHEM or PHYS courses; or consent.

PHIL 315.title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
PHIL 315.subject: PHIL
PHIL 315.description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models.
PHIL 315.prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent.

PHIL 316.title: Science, Technology, and Society
PHIL 316.subject: PHIL
PHIL 316.description: Investigation of some of the complex interconnections between science, technology, and society.
PHIL 316.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 100 or above in PHIL or in a course with either DB or DP or DS designation, or consent.

children.text: in a course with either DB

PHIL 317.title: Critical Thinking: Pre-Law
PHIL 317.subject: PHIL
PHIL 317.description: Introduction to concepts and techniques for evaluating arguments with special emphasis on their application both to questions of law and to issues in jurisprudence.
PHIL 317.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or POLS or SOC, or consent.

PHIL 318.title: Philosophy of Law
PHIL 318.subject: PHIL
PHIL 318.description: Historical and contemporary issues in law and legal theory. Law and morality; legal responsibility, justice, rights, punishment, judicial reasoning.
PHIL 318.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in BLAW or POLS or SOC, or consent.

PHIL 319.title: Ethical Issues in the Law
PHIL 319.subject: PHIL
PHIL 319.description: Exploration of ethical issues that have come before (mainly U.S.) courts, including but not confined to, medical and criminal justice ethics.
PHIL 319.prereq_raw: PHIL 101 or a course numbered 200 or above in PHIL or HIST or ENG or with a DS designation; or consent.

PHIL 320.title: American Philosophy
PHIL 320.subject: PHIL
PHIL 320.description: Survey of major philosophers and schools in development of American thought up to modern times.
PHIL 320.prereq_raw: any course PHIL 100 or above in PHIL, or consent.

PHIL 321.title: Bodies, Minds, and Selves
PHIL 321.subject: PHIL
PHIL 321.description: Explores the nature of the mind. Questions addressed include: How does the mind relate to the body? What is the nature of consciousness? Are you the same person today as you were yesterday?
PHIL 321.prereq_raw: any 100-level PHIL course or above, or consent.

PHIL 322.title: Critical Race Theory and Philosophy
PHIL 322.subject: PHIL
PHIL 322.description: (LED) Introduction to the work of philosophers whose writings aim to contribute to movements for racial justice.
PHIL 322.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PHIL 324.title: Philosophy of Disability
PHIL 324.subject: PHIL
PHIL 324.description: Uses tools of philosophical inquiry to explore philosophical concepts emerging from the study of disability. Ethical issues of personhood and justice are discussed, with significant attention given to helping students express their thinking through writing.

PHIL 326.title: Artificial Intelligence Ethics
PHIL 326.subject: PHIL
PHIL 326.description: Addresses selected moral, social, and political issues raised by the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies.
PHIL 326.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL, or consent.

PHIL 417.title: Philosophy in Literature

PHIL 418.title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy
PHIL 418.subject: PHIL

PHIL 422.title: Philosophical Psychology
PHIL 422.subject: PHIL

PHIL 436.title: Philosophy of Language

PHIL 445.title: Symbolic Logic

PHIL 448.title: Individual Philosophers/Topics

PHIL 449.title: Undergraduate Capstone
PHIL 449.subject: PHIL
PHIL 449.description: Capstone seminar for undergraduate majors. Concentration on a topic of current philosophical concern.
PHIL 449.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: declared major in PHIL with at least six courses 200 or above in PHIL, or consent.

PHIL 473.title: Understanding Place: Philosophical Inquiry and Community
PHIL 473.subject: PHIL
PHIL 473.description: Uses tools of philosophical inquiry, specifically p4cHI pedagogy, to develop a deep understanding of lived environment in a Hawaiian context while drawing on urban planning theories and methods to empower students as agents of change.

PHIL 622.title: Studies in Hermeneutics

PHIL 630.title: History and Theory of Science

PHIL 630.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PHIL 670.title: Confucianism
PHIL 670.subject: PHIL

PHIL 670.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PHIL 671.subject: PHIL

PHIL 672.title: Daoism
PHIL 672.subject: PHIL
PHIL 672.description: Critical examination and evaluation of major philosophical ideas in Lao Zi, Zhuang Zi, and the Neo-Daoists.
PHIL 672.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PHIL 699.title: Directed Research
PHIL 699.subject: PHIL
PHIL 699.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

PHIL 700.title: Thesis Research

PHIL 720.title: Seminar on Individual Philosophers

PHIL 725.title: Seminar in Philosophical Topics

PHIL 740.title: Seminar in Philosophical Texts
PHIL 740.subject: PHIL

PHIL 750.title: Seminar in Indian Philosophy
PHIL 750.subject: PHIL

PHIL 760.title: Seminar in Buddhist Philosophy
PHIL 760.subject: PHIL
PHIL 760.description: Major philosophical problems in the development of Buddhist thought during its formative period.
PHIL 760.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PHIL 770.title: Seminar in Chinese Philosophy
PHIL 770.subject: PHIL
PHIL 770.description: Fundamental issues, problems, movements, and schools of Chinese philosophy, such as classical Confucianism, Daoism, Legalism, Chinese logic, and Neo-Confucianism.

PHIL 771.subject: PHIL

PHIL 771.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PHIL 780.title: Seminar in Japanese Philosophy
PHIL 780.subject: PHIL

PHIL 790.title: Seminar in Comparative Philosophy
PHIL 790.subject: PHIL

PHRM 201.title: Introduction to General Pharmacology
PHRM 201.subject: PHRM
PHRM 201.description: Drugs discussed with emphasis on sites and mechanism of action, toxicity, fate, and uses of major therapeutic agents.
PHRM 201.prereq_raw: mammalian physiology and dental hygiene major.

PHRM 203.title: General Pharmacology
PHRM 203.subject: PHRM
PHRM 203.description: Similar to PHRM 201 but wider in scope of drugs discussed. Intended for undergraduates in the health sciences and related fields.

PHRM 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
PHRM 499.subject: PHRM
PHRM 499.description: Directed reading and research in experimental pharmacology.

PHRM 590.title: Selected Topics in Pharmacology
PHRM 590.subject: PHRM
PHRM 590.description: Elective for medical students in Pharmacology.

PHRM 595.title: Principles of Pharmacology
PHRM 595.subject: PHRM
PHRM 595.description: Pharmacology elective course for medical students.

PHRM 599.title: Research in Pharmacology
PHRM 599.subject: PHRM
PHRM 599.description: Pharmacology research elective for medical students.

PHRM 601.title: General Pharmacology
PHRM 601.subject: PHRM
PHRM 601.description: Pharmacodynamics, receptor theory, modeling, clinical trials and the FDA will be covered. Concepts in ADME/T and clinical research are also considered.

PHRM 602.title: Systemic Pharmacology
PHRM 602.subject: PHRM
PHRM 602.description: Provides instruction at an organ systems/functional level covering major organ and functional systems of the human body. Concepts in pharmacological research at the animal, organ system and whole human level will also be considered.

PHRM 640.title: Neuropharmacology
PHRM 640.subject: PHRM
PHRM 640.description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling.
PHRM 640.prereq_raw: CMB 606 , or consent from the course director.

PHYL 103.title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
PHYL 103.subject: PHYL
PHYL 103.description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of dental hygiene students and others interested in pursuing health-related careers.

PHYL 141.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I
PHYL 141.subject: PHYL
PHYL 141.description: First in a two-semester human anatomy & physiology series. Topics include terminology, tissues, integumentary, musculoskeletal, and nervous systems. Designed to fulfill prerequisites for students pursuing nursing, PA, PT, dentistry, pharmacology, or allied healthcare careers.

PHYL 141L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I Lab
PHYL 141L.subject: PHYL
PHYL 141L.description: Anatomy & physiology lab using microscopy, anatomical models, and dissection to complement lecture material and develop practical skills. Topics include anatomical terminology, integumentary, musculoskeletal, and nervous systems.

PHYL 142.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
PHYL 142.subject: PHYL
PHYL 142.description: Continuation of a two-semester human anatomy & physiology series. Topics include endocrine, cardiovascular, lymphatic, immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, and reproductive systems. Designed to fulfill prerequisites for nursing, PA, PT, dentistry, pharmacology, or allied healthcare careers.
PHYL 142.prereq_raw: should have an understanding of basic physiology concepts as presented in PHYL 141 or equivalent.

PHYL 142L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II Lab
PHYL 142L.subject: PHYL

PHYL 301.title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology I
PHYL 301.subject: PHYL
PHYL 301.description: In-depth studies of human anatomy and physiology. Topics include medical terminology, histology, integumentary, skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems. Designed and oriented toward students pursuing careers in medicine, medical technology, or medical research.
PHYL 301.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 , or any PHYL course; and CHEM 161 (or higher) or any BIOC course; or consent.

PHYL 301L.title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology I Lab
PHYL 301L.subject: PHYL
PHYL 301L.description: Laboratory study of human anatomy and physiology using models, histology slides, experiments, and demonstrations. Topics include cell physiology, histology, skin, bones, muscle, and neurology. Complements PHYL 301 lecture.

PHYL 302.title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology II
PHYL 302.subject: PHYL
PHYL 302.description: In-depth studies of human anatomy and physiology. Topics include endocrine, cardiovascular, immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, & reproductive systems. Designed and oriented toward students pursuing careers in medicine, medical technology, or medical research. Continuation of PHYL 301 .
PHYL 302.prereq_raw: ( PHYL 141 and PHYL 142 ) with A- or better, or PHYL 301 with C or better, or consent.

PHYL 302L.title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology II Lab
PHYL 302L.subject: PHYL
PHYL 302L.description: Laboratory study of human anatomy and physiology using models, histology slides, experiments, and demonstrations. Topics include endocrine, cardiovascular, immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, & reproductive systems. Complements PHYL 302 lecture.

PHYL 401.title: Integrated Physiology: Organ Systems
PHYL 401.subject: PHYL
PHYL 401.description: Advanced integrated studies of human organ systems. Covers cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, acid-base, and gastrointestinal physiology. Includes elements of pathophysiology and pharmacology. Designed for students pursuing medicine or graduate healthcare careers.
PHYL 401.prereq_raw: PHYL 301 with B or better, or PHYL 302 with C or better, or consent.

PHYL 402.title: Integrated Physiology: Regulatory Systems
PHYL 402.subject: PHYL
PHYL 402.description: Senior-level integrated studies of human regulatory systems (neurology and endocrinology) from a medical perspective. Includes elements of pathophysiology and pharmacology. Complements PHYL 401 . Designed for students pursuing medicine or graduate healthcare careers.
PHYL 402.prereq_raw: one of PHYL 301 (B or better), PHYL 302 (C or better), or PHYL 401 (C or better); and one of BIOC 341 , BIOC 441 , or CHEM 272 (C or better).

PHYL 499.title: Directed Reading or Research
PHYL 499.subject: PHYL
PHYL 499.description: Students will learn fundamental concepts and multiple techniques in molecular biology, physiology, and histology for cardiovascular research through the projects in the lab.
PHYL 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior or senior standing only.

PHYS 100.title: Survey of Physics
PHYS 100.subject: PHYS
PHYS 100.description: Mechanics, electricity and magnetism, waves, optics, atomic and nuclear physics. Only algebra and geometry used. For non-science majors.

PHYS 100L.title: Survey of Physics Lab
PHYS 100L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 100L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hooke’s law, falling bodies, collisions, Boyle’s law, electric and magnetic fields, induction, waves, optics.

PHYS 109.title: Physics in the Arts
PHYS 109.subject: PHYS
PHYS 109.description: Introduction to physics of sound and light, with applications to music and visual arts: sound perception, harmony, musical scales, instruments; lenses, cameras, color perception and mixing. Uses algebra and geometry. Intended primarily for non-science majors.

PHYS 121.title: How Things Work: Physics for Everyday Life
PHYS 121.subject: PHYS
PHYS 121.description: Introduction to physics and science in everyday life. It considers objects from our daily environment, and focuses on the principles such as motion, forces, heat, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics.

PHYS 151.title: College Physics I
PHYS 151.subject: PHYS
PHYS 151.description: Non-calculus physics. Mechanics, wave motion, heat.
PHYS 151.prereq_raw: MATH 140X , or MATH 215 or higher; or qualifying score on math assessment exam.

children.text: qualifying score on math assessment exam

PHYS 151L.title: College Physics Lab I
PHYS 151L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 151L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to experimental analysis, physical observation and measurement, experiments on conservation laws, fluid friction, oscillations.

PHYS 152L.title: College Physics Lab II
PHYS 152L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 152L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Optics, electric and magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry.
PHYS 152L.prereq_raw: PHYS 151L or PHYS 170L , and PHYS 152 (or concurrent).

PHYS 170.prereq_raw: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent.

children.text: MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

PHYS 170A.title: Honors General Physics I
PHYS 170A.subject: PHYS
PHYS 170A.description: Special format for topics: mechanics of particles and rigid bodies, wave motion, thermodynamics and kinetic theory.
PHYS 170A.prereq_raw: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent.

children.text: MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

PHYS 170L.title: General Physics I Lab
PHYS 170L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 170L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to PHYS 151L but at 170 level.

PHYS 272.title: General Physics II
PHYS 272.subject: PHYS
PHYS 272.description: Electricity and magnetism and geometric optics.
PHYS 272.prereq_raw: PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A , MATH 216 may be substituted with consent.

PHYS 272A.title: Honors General Physics II
PHYS 272A.subject: PHYS

PHYS 450.title: Electromagnetic Waves
PHYS 450.subject: PHYS
PHYS 450.description: Field equations, plane, spherical and guided waves.

PHYS 460.title: Physical Optics
PHYS 460.subject: PHYS
PHYS 460.description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
PHYS 460.prereq_raw: PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C) or ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-), or consent.

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) or ECE 372 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) , or consent

PHYS 470.title: General Relativity & Cosmology
PHYS 470.subject: PHYS
PHYS 470.description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation.
PHYS 470.prereq_raw: PHYS 274 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: ASTR 242 .

PHYS 475.title: Electronics for Physicists
PHYS 475.subject: PHYS
PHYS 475.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Investigation of Kirchhoff’s Laws, electromagnetic circuit theory. Fourier analysis and stability theory with circuits. Applications to physical measurements are stressed. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.

PHYS 476.title: Modern Electronics for Physicists
PHYS 476.subject: PHYS
PHYS 476.description: Introduction to high performance solid state instrumentation by means of practical research electronics: printed circuit board design/fabrication; complex programmable logic design/verification; integrated circuit SPICE simulation. Detector fabrication and test emphasis during final project.

PHYS 480.title: Quantum Mechanics I
PHYS 480.subject: PHYS
PHYS 480.description: Wave mechanics, Schroedinger equation, angular momenta, potential problems.
PHYS 480.prereq_raw: PHYS 274 , PHYS 310 , PHYS 350 , PHYS 400 (or concurrent); either MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; and either MATH 311 or MATH 307 ; or consent.

PHYS 480L.title: Advanced Physics Laboratory I
PHYS 480L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 480L.description: Advanced experiments involving nuclear spectroscopy, angular correlations in positronium annihilation, optical polarization, chaos, measurement of speed of light, numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
PHYS 480L.prereq_raw: PHYS 274L and PHYS 480 (or concurrent), or consent.

PHYS 481.title: Quantum Mechanics II
PHYS 481.subject: PHYS
PHYS 481.description: Continuation of PHYS 480 ; atomic physics, scattering, perturbation theory.

PHYS 481L.title: Advanced Physics Laboratory II
PHYS 481L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 481L.description: Advanced experiments involving measurement of the muon lifetime, crystal x-ray diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance, the Mössbauer effect, and numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
PHYS 481L.prereq_raw: PHYS 274L , PHYS 480 , and PHYS 480L ; or consent.

PHYS 485.title: Professional Ethics for Physicists
PHYS 485.subject: PHYS
PHYS 485.description: Seminar on ethical principles and their application to physics, astronomy, and closely-related fields. Participants present and discuss current and historical examples of ethical issues. Emphasis on developing oral communication skills.
PHYS 485.prereq_raw: PHYS 310 or ASTR 300 (or concurrent), or consent.
PHYS 485.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PHYS, ASTP, and ASTR majors only.

PHYS 490.title: Modern Physics
PHYS 490.subject: PHYS
PHYS 490.description: Introduction to nuclear and elementary-particle physics.

PHYS 505.title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
PHYS 505.subject: PHYS
PHYS 505.description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

PHYS 600.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
PHYS 600.subject: PHYS
PHYS 600.description: Mathematical tools of theoretical physics. Continuation of PHYS 400 but with an independent selection of topics.

PHYS 610.title: Analytical Mechanics
PHYS 610.subject: PHYS
PHYS 610.description: Dynamics of particles, particle systems; rigid bodies; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian equations; special relativity.

PHYS 650.title: Electrodynamics I
PHYS 650.subject: PHYS
PHYS 650.description: Potential theory, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, boundary value problems.
PHYS 650.prereq_raw: PHYS 450 ; and PHYS 600 (or concurrent), or MATH 402 .

PHYS 651.title: Electrodynamics II
PHYS 651.subject: PHYS
PHYS 651.description: Relativistic electrodynamics, radiation by charged particles.

PHYS 660.title: Advanced Optics
PHYS 660.subject: PHYS
PHYS 660.description: Contemporary advanced applications in optics including nonlinear optics and optical parametric oscillators, atomic lasers and laser systems, and free-electron lasers.

PHYS 670.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 670.subject: PHYS
PHYS 670.description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.
PHYS 670.prereq_raw: PHYS 400 or PHYS 481 or PHYS 600 and MATH 402 .

PHYS 671.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 671.subject: PHYS
PHYS 671.description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

PHYS 690.title: Seminar
PHYS 690.subject: PHYS
PHYS 690.description: Discussions and reports on physical theory and recent developments.
PHYS 690.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PHYS 694.title: Condensed Matter Seminar
PHYS 694.subject: PHYS
PHYS 694.description: Results and discussions of current topics in condensed matter physics.

PHYS 695.title: Seminar on Atomic and Solid-State Physics
PHYS 695.subject: PHYS
PHYS 695.description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in atomic, surface, and solid-state physics.

PHYS 696.title: Seminar on Elementary Particle Physics
PHYS 696.subject: PHYS
PHYS 696.description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in elementary particle physics.

PHYS 711.title: Topics in Particles and Fields
PHYS 711.subject: PHYS
PHYS 711.description: Topics in current theoretical research; e.g., unified field theories, general relativity, gravitation, and cosmology.

PHYS 712.title: Special Topics: Experimental Physics
PHYS 712.subject: PHYS
PHYS 712.description: Topics in current experimental research in low-energy physics, high-energy physics, cross-disciplinary physics.

PHYS 713.title: Advanced Topics in Condensed Matter Theory
PHYS 713.subject: PHYS
PHYS 713.description: Topics in condensed matter theory, e.g., group theory, many-body techniques, renormalization group, density functional theory, other topics of current interest.

PHYS 730.title: Statistical Physics I
PHYS 730.subject: PHYS
PHYS 730.description: Equilibrium thermodynamics; Gibbs ensembles; quantum statistics; ideal and non-ideal Fermi; Bose and Boltzmann gases; phase transitions; and critical phenomena.

PHYS 731.title: Statistical Physics II
PHYS 731.subject: PHYS
PHYS 731.description: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics, transport theory, fluctuation dissipation theorem, many-body Green’s function methods, normal Fermi and Bose liquids, superfluidity, superconductivity.

PHYS 760.title: Modern General Relativity
PHYS 760.subject: PHYS
PHYS 760.description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques.
PHYS 760.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR.

PHYS 772.title: Quantum Field Theory I
PHYS 772.subject: PHYS
PHYS 772.description: Relativistic wave equations and their solutions. Dirac’s theory of the electron, propagator techniques. Applications to quantum electrodynamics.

PHYS 773.title: Quantum Field Theory II
PHYS 773.subject: PHYS
PHYS 773.description: Local gauge invariance, Yang-Mills theory: quantum chromodynamics, spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone bosons; the standard electroweak theory; grand unified theories.

PHYS 777.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
PHYS 777.subject: PHYS
PHYS 777.description: Nuclear physics; electrodynamics; hadron structure and partons. Techniques of particle physics.

PHYS 778.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics II
PHYS 778.subject: PHYS
PHYS 778.description: Quantum chromodynamics; electroweak interactions; the standard model. Techniques of particle physics.

PHYS 785.title: Solid-State Theory
PHYS 785.subject: PHYS
PHYS 785.description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, electron-electron interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

PHYS 786.title: Solid-State Theory
PHYS 786.subject: PHYS
PHYS 786.description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

PLAN 101.title: Sustainable Cities
PLAN 101.subject: PLAN
PLAN 101.description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction.

PLAN 301.title: Survey of Urban Sociology
PLAN 301.subject: PLAN
PLAN 301.description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawaiʻi.
PLAN 301.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent.

PLAN 310.title: Introduction to Planning
PLAN 310.subject: PLAN
PLAN 310.description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawaiʻi planning—research problems from a multidisciplinary approach. Emphasis on writing instruction.
PLAN 310.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

PLAN 399.title: Directed Reading in Planning
PLAN 399.subject: PLAN
PLAN 399.description: Independent research on topics in urban and regional planning.

PLAN 412.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
PLAN 412.subject: PLAN
PLAN 412.description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
PLAN 412.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

PLAN 414.title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
PLAN 414.subject: PLAN
PLAN 414.description: Examines resilience thinking as it relates to making cities resilient to environmental hazards in the context of climate change. Draws on relevant theories, policy, and case studies in urban planning. Emphasis on instruction in writing.
PLAN 414.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

PLAN 421.title: Urban Geography
PLAN 421.subject: PLAN
PLAN 421.description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.
PLAN 421.prereq_raw: GEO 102 or GEO 151 or GEO 330 , or consent.

PLAN 438.title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
PLAN 438.subject: PLAN
PLAN 438.description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.
PLAN 438.prereq_raw: PLAN 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312 , or consent.

PLAN 442.title: Principles of Environmental Management Systems
PLAN 442.subject: PLAN
PLAN 442.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
PLAN 442.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

PLAN 449.title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
PLAN 449.subject: PLAN
PLAN 449.description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
PLAN 449.prereq_raw: PLAN 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312 , or consent.

PLAN 473.title: GIS for Community & Environmental Planning
PLAN 473.subject: PLAN
PLAN 473.description: Exploration of geographic information systems (GIS) area analysis techniques for spatial information management in community planning. Students will learn the basic concepts and principles, and practical skills of GIS through lectures, discussions, and labs.
PLAN 473.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

PLAN 495.title: Housing, Land, and Community
PLAN 495.subject: PLAN
PLAN 495.description: Analyzes housing availability, particularly affordable housing, and its relationship to land use and community building. Examines public policies impacting housing, land use, community development, and ways they can be improved. Emphasis on instruction in writing.

PLAN 600.title: Public Policy and Planning Theory
PLAN 600.subject: PLAN
PLAN 600.description: Designed to a) impart a historic and comparative perspective on the evolution of urban and regional planning in public policy; b) explore the spatial and built environment dimensions of society, planning and policy; c) assess the justifications for planning and differing processes of planning in the U.S. and Asia-Pacific with a focus on the role of the planner in policy formulation and implementation.
PLAN 600.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or with permission.

PLAN 601.title: Planning Methods
PLAN 601.subject: PLAN
PLAN 601.description: Introduction of the basic methods in planning, including problem definition, research design, hypothesis testing, statistical reasoning, forecasting and fundamental data analysis techniques required by the planning program and the planning profession.
PLAN 601.prereq_raw: one of ECON 321 , GEO 380 , or SOC 476 .
PLAN 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN and ARCH majors only.

PLAN 602.title: Advanced Planning Theory
PLAN 602.subject: PLAN
PLAN 602.description: Advanced planning theory for PhD students (others by petition) to prepare for careers in planning education and/or high level professional practice. Covers key contemporary planning policy issues and themes from the perspective of values, explanations of the real world, policy alternatives and implementation. Students must have passed PLAN 600 or equivalent (by petition) with a B or better.
PLAN 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only or by consent.

PLAN 603.title: Urban Economics
PLAN 603.subject: PLAN
PLAN 603.description: Reviews and builds skills in applying basic theories and principles of urban and regional economics in contemporary U.S., Hawaiʻi and Asia-Pacific.

PLAN 604.title: Qualitative Methods in Planning
PLAN 604.subject: PLAN
PLAN 604.description: Provides a general introduction to qualitative research methods for planning and planning research. Includes data collection methods (focus groups, interviews, ethnography, participant observation, and participatory action research) and various analytic methods and approaches.
PLAN 604.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

PLAN 605.title: Planning Models
PLAN 605.subject: PLAN
PLAN 605.description: Allocation, decision, derivation, and forecasting models used in the analysis of demographic, economic, land use, and transportation phenomena in urban and regional planning.

PLAN 606.title: Comparative Planning Histories
PLAN 606.subject: PLAN
PLAN 606.description: Provides students with an overview of the history of urban and regional planning in the U.S., Europe, and Asia, and the role that planning has played in shaping contemporary urban settlements.
PLAN 606.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

PLAN 607.title: Introduction to Public Policy
PLAN 607.subject: PLAN
PLAN 607.description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation.

PLAN 608.title: Politics and Development: China
PLAN 608.subject: PLAN
PLAN 608.description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

PLAN 609.title: Causality in the Social Sciences: A Relatively Gentle Introduction
PLAN 609.subject: PLAN
PLAN 609.description: An introduction to the statistical methods used to identify plausibly causal effects with non-experimental data.
PLAN 609.prereq_raw: PLAN 601 with a minimum grade of A- or equivalent.

PLAN 610.title: Community Planning and Social Policy
PLAN 610.subject: PLAN
PLAN 610.description: Social issues and conditions; consequences of social policies experienced by different groups; community social plans and programs organized by various kinds of agencies and organizations.

PLAN 611.title: Foundations in Indigenous Planning
PLAN 611.subject: PLAN
PLAN 611.description: Examines the gaps in conventional planning curricula by centering Indigenous planning, with emphasis on Native Hawaiian knowledge. Students explore culturally grounded frameworks often marginalized in conventional urban and regional planning discourse.
PLAN 611.prereq_raw: PLAN 600 with a minimum grade of B.

PLAN 615.title: Housing
PLAN 615.subject: PLAN
PLAN 615.description: Housing delivery systems as an aspect of urban and regional planning.

PLAN 616.title: Community-Based Planning
PLAN 616.subject: PLAN
PLAN 616.description: Planning and programmatic aspects of community-based development projects. East-West and local planning perspectives on participatory development and intentional communities.

PLAN 618.title: Community Economic Development
PLAN 618.subject: PLAN
PLAN 618.description: Community-based economic development approaches and methods explored with an emphasis on low income communities.

PLAN 619.title: Multiculturalism in Planning and Policy
PLAN 619.subject: PLAN
PLAN 619.description: Graduate seminar focuses on issues of governance, policy and planning in diverse multicultural societies. Differences in backgrounds, languages, privilege, preferences and values are often expressed in planning and policy controversies such as affirmative action and land use planning. Will examine these controversies and explore theories of governance in a multicultural setting.

PLAN 620.title: Environmental Planning and Policy
PLAN 620.subject: PLAN
PLAN 620.description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

PLAN 621.title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
PLAN 621.subject: PLAN
PLAN 621.description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict.
PLAN 621.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PLAN 622.title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
PLAN 622.subject: PLAN
PLAN 622.description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

PLAN 623.title: Coastal Planning and Management
PLAN 623.subject: PLAN
PLAN 623.description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture.

PLAN 624.title: Environmental Valuation and Policy
PLAN 624.subject: PLAN
PLAN 624.description: Build valuation skills to assess best use, conservation, and policies relating to environmental amenities. Provides an overview of policy solutions to environmental degradation used by planners.

PLAN 625.title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
PLAN 625.subject: PLAN
PLAN 625.description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/ Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via video-conferencing.

PLAN 626.title: Topics in Resource Management
PLAN 626.subject: PLAN
PLAN 626.description: Issues, analytic techniques and management strategies for different resource systems including land, water, energy, coastal resources, forests and fisheries. Course focus varies from year to year.

PLAN 627.title: Negotiation and Mediation in Planning
PLAN 627.subject: PLAN
PLAN 627.description: Applicability and limitations of selected approaches; role of planners; impact on planning.

PLAN 628.title: Urban Environmental Problems
PLAN 628.subject: PLAN
PLAN 628.description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

PLAN 629.title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
PLAN 629.subject: PLAN
PLAN 629.description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills.
PLAN 629.prereq_raw: one of the following courses with a minimum grade of B: PLAN 627 ; or PACE 429 , PACE 447 , PACE 477 , PACE 647 , PACE 652 , or PACE 668 ; or COMG 455 or SOC 730 ; or LAW 508 ; or MGT 660 .

children.text: courses with a minimum grade of B : PLAN 627
; or PACE 429 , PACE 447 , PACE 477 , PACE 647 , PACE 652 , or PACE 668 ; or COMG 455 or SOC 730 ; or LAW 508 ; or MGT 660

PLAN 629.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

PLAN 630.title: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia
PLAN 630.subject: PLAN
PLAN 630.description: Key issues and policies in urban planning, rural-urban relations, rural regional planning, and frontier settlement in Asia and the Pacific.

PLAN 632.title: Planning in Hawaiʻi and Pacific Islands
PLAN 632.subject: PLAN
PLAN 632.description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.
PLAN 632.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PLAN 633.title: Globalization and Urban Policy
PLAN 633.subject: PLAN
PLAN 633.description: Urbanization and urban policies in the Asia and Pacific region with focus on the international dimension of national and local spatial restructuring.

PLAN 634.title: Shelter and Services in Asia
PLAN 634.subject: PLAN
PLAN 634.description: Examines government and non-government organizations’ responses to urban and rural shelter issues and services in Asia.

PLAN 636.title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
PLAN 636.subject: PLAN
PLAN 636.description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

PLAN 637.title: Environment and Development
PLAN 637.subject: PLAN
PLAN 637.description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

PLAN 639.title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
PLAN 639.subject: PLAN
PLAN 639.description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy.
PLAN 639.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PLAN 640.title: Land Use Policies and Programs
PLAN 640.subject: PLAN
PLAN 640.description: Land use public policy planning in urban and regional settings. Growth management and land use guidance systems.

PLAN 641.title: Neighborhood and Community Land Use Planning
PLAN 641.subject: PLAN
PLAN 641.description: Land use planning for urban neighborhoods and small towns. Theory and practice of neighborhood planning. Neighborhood and community dynamics, reinvestment, and stabilization.

PLAN 642.title: Planning Urban Infrastructure
PLAN 642.subject: PLAN
PLAN 642.description: Introduction to the planning of various urban infrastructures. Explores approaches and tools to plan, evaluate, and regulate urban infrastructure systems in support of sustainable and resilient cities and communities.

PLAN 643.title: Project Planning and Management
PLAN 643.subject: PLAN
PLAN 643.description: Examines project management in theory and practice and the roles and responsibilities of the project manager. Focuses on planning, organizing, and controlling the efforts of projects.

PLAN 645.title: Land Use Planning
PLAN 645.subject: PLAN
PLAN 645.description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

PLAN 647.title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
PLAN 647.subject: PLAN
PLAN 647.description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered.
PLAN 647.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PLAN 648.title: Urban Transportation Policy and Planning
PLAN 648.subject: PLAN
PLAN 648.description: Theory and practice of urban transportation planning in developed and developing countries with an emphasis on the U.S., Asia, and Pacific region.

PLAN 649.title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
PLAN 649.subject: PLAN
PLAN 649.description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

PLAN 650.title: Research Design Seminar
PLAN 650.subject: PLAN
PLAN 650.description: Research design and preparation of thesis proposal. Normally taken after admission to candidacy in MURP.
PLAN 650.prereq_raw: ( PLAN 600 or PLAN 601 or PLAN 603 ) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

PLAN 652.title: Policy Implementation and Program Evaluation
PLAN 652.subject: PLAN
PLAN 652.description: Implementation and evaluation in public policy analysis; philosophical and methodological issues; impact of policies and plans; use of evaluation research in program implementation.

PLAN 654.title: Applied Geographic Information Systems: Public Policy and Spatial Analysis
PLAN 654.subject: PLAN
PLAN 654.description: Use of advanced and specialized spatial methods and models in urban and regional planning. Uses GIS software and builds upon PLAN 601 . Skills are useful applied to planning, economic development, and environmental planning and resource management.
PLAN 654.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

PLAN 655.title: Planning Research Methods
PLAN 655.subject: PLAN
PLAN 655.description: Advanced methods and deterministic and stochastic models used in urban and regional planning.

PLAN 661.title: Collaboration Between Sectors
PLAN 661.subject: PLAN
PLAN 661.description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems.

PLAN 668.title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
PLAN 668.subject: PLAN
PLAN 668.description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations.
PLAN 668.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or departmental approval.

PLAN 670.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
PLAN 670.subject: PLAN
PLAN 670.description: Overview to the field of disaster management and humanitarian assistance with a specific focus on risk reduction. Includes background knowledge and skills for preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and adaptation to hazards and threats.
PLAN 670.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

PLAN 671.title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
PLAN 671.subject: PLAN
PLAN 671.description: Combined lecture/discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and and planning.

PLAN 672.title: Humanitarian Assistance: Principles, Practices and Politics
PLAN 672.subject: PLAN
PLAN 672.description: Combined lecture/discussion aimed at understanding the theoretical basis and working structure of humanitarian assistance programs and international responses to natural and human-induced disasters.

PLAN 673.title: Information Systems for Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
PLAN 673.subject: PLAN
PLAN 673.description: Combined lecture/laboratory in disaster management focusing on essential methodological and practical issues that are involved in spatial analyses using GIS and other information technologies to inform decision making related to natural hazards, disasters, and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning activities.
PLAN 673.prereq_raw: PLAN 473 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

PLAN 674.title: Disaster Recovery: Theory and Practice
PLAN 674.subject: PLAN
PLAN 674.description: How do communities recover from disaster? Provides students with an overview of recovery theory and an understanding of how planners, policy makers, and ordinary citizens rebuild communities, cities, and nations following catastrophic events.
PLAN 674.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

PLAN 675.title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
PLAN 675.subject: PLAN
PLAN 675.description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

PLAN 676.title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
PLAN 676.subject: PLAN
PLAN 676.description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.
PLAN 676.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

PLAN 677.title: Historic Preservation Planning
PLAN 677.subject: PLAN
PLAN 677.description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

PLAN 678.title: Site Planning
PLAN 678.subject: PLAN
PLAN 678.description: Fundamental principles that guide site planning, including planning and design determinants of the site taking into account its regional context, site-specific characteristics and applicable codes, ordinances, and standards.
PLAN 678.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN and ARCH majors only.

PLAN 680.title: Land Use Management and Control
PLAN 680.subject: PLAN
PLAN 680.description: Survey course of public land use management.

PLAN 682.title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
PLAN 682.subject: PLAN
PLAN 682.description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises.
PLAN 682.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PLAN 699.title: Directed Reading and Research
PLAN 699.subject: PLAN
PLAN 699.prereq_raw: Consent of instructor and department chair.

PLAN 700.title: Thesis Research
PLAN 700.subject: PLAN
PLAN 700.description: Limited to MURP students under Plan A.

PLAN 721.title: Homeland Security: Terrorism
PLAN 721.subject: PLAN

POLS 615C.title: Topics in Political Thought: feminist theory
POLS 615C.subject: POLS
POLS 615C.description: Specific traditions and individuals, or particular issues and problems. (C) feminist theory.
POLS 615C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

POLS 620.title: Introduction to Indigenous Politics
POLS 620.subject: POLS
POLS 620.description: Historical treatment of the contact between state and indigenous peoples and a survey of contemporary indigenous political initiatives: social movements, media, indigenous studies programs, and events.

POLS 621.title: Politics of Indigenous Representation
POLS 621.subject: POLS
POLS 621.description: Politics of indigenous representations in media, literature, and academic scholarship.

POLS 630.title: International Relations
POLS 630.subject: POLS
POLS 630.description: Analysis of theories: actors, decisions, systems, conflict, integration, alternative approaches to validation.
POLS 630.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 633.title: International Conflict Resolution
POLS 633.subject: POLS
POLS 633.description: Analysis of international conflict and conflict resolution. Theory and practice of negotiation, mediation, conciliation, facilitation, and other “third-party” methods of peaceful settlement.
POLS 633.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 634.title: Teaching Model United Nations
POLS 634.subject: POLS
POLS 634.description: Substantive and pedagogical approaches to using Model United Nations simulation for teaching and conflict resolution.
POLS 634.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 635B.title: Topics in International Relations: international relations and war
POLS 635B.subject: POLS
POLS 635B.description: (B) international relations and war; (E) international organization; (F) modeling international systems.
POLS 635B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 635E.title: Topics in International Relations: international organization
POLS 635E.subject: POLS
POLS 635E.description: (B) international relations and war; (E) international organization; (F) modeling international systems.
POLS 635E.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 635F.title: Topics in International Relations: modeling international systems
POLS 635F.subject: POLS
POLS 635F.description: (B) international relations and war; (E) international organization; (F) modeling international systems.
POLS 635F.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 640.title: Comparative Politics
POLS 640.subject: POLS
POLS 640.description: Emphasis on Asia, theories of development, and comparative methods. At least one section a semester.

POLS 642.title: Indigenous Peoples and Western Imperialism
POLS 642.subject: POLS
POLS 642.description: Historical examination of U.S. and European imperialisms, including national narratives, politics, and impacts upon indigenous peoples in the Americas, Pacific, and Asia.

POLS 645C.title: Politics and Development: Regional: China
POLS 645C.subject: POLS
POLS 645C.description: Politics of particular regions; particular development processes. (C) China.

POLS 646F.title: Politics and Development: Topical: political ecology and development
POLS 646F.subject: POLS

POLS 647.title: American Political Institutions in Comparative Perspective
POLS 647.subject: POLS
POLS 647.description: Consideration of American political institutions and development relative to American philosophical foundations and non- American political forms. Federalism as an expansive devise will be emphasized, as will American influence and penetration abroad.
POLS 647.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

POLS 650.title: Public Administrative Theory
POLS 650.subject: POLS
POLS 650.description: Focus varies among theoretical, comparative and developmental approaches to study of administration. One section each semester.

POLS 651.title: Political Leadership
POLS 651.subject: POLS
POLS 651.description: Exploration of political leadership as a focus for research, teaching, and applied political science.

POLS 652.title: Comparative Public Administration
POLS 652.subject: POLS
POLS 652.description: Detailed examination of implementation of governmental policy in different countries.
POLS 652.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 660.title: Law and Politics
POLS 660.subject: POLS
POLS 660.description: Law, courts, and rights as a political resource; analyses of public law (including court decisions), other forms of dispute management, and judicial behavior and policy-making.

POLS 665.title: Topics in Public Law and Judicial System
POLS 665.subject: POLS
POLS 665.description: Recent issues and practices in public law; particular judicial systems.
POLS 665.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 670.title: Introduction to Public Policy
POLS 670.subject: POLS
POLS 670.description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation.

POLS 672.title: Politics of the Future
POLS 672.subject: POLS
POLS 672.description: Introduction to political futures studies; images of future, theories of social change, methods of social forecasting and designing preferred futures.
POLS 672.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 673.title: The Future of Political Systems
POLS 673.subject: POLS
POLS 673.description: Normative and descriptive forecasts of political institutions, systems, subsystems, and behaviors. Design of preferred systems.

POLS 675.title: Topics in Public Policy
POLS 675.subject: POLS
POLS 675.description: Particular political processes, specific political institutions, or particular policy area.
POLS 675.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 676.title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
POLS 676.subject: POLS
POLS 676.description: Exploration of nonviolent, non-killing alternatives in political science research, teaching, and public service.

POLS 680.title: Asian and/or Pacific Politics
POLS 680.subject: POLS
POLS 680.description: Political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in all or part of Asia and/or the Pacific.

POLS 684.title: Contemporary Native Hawaiian Politics
POLS 684.subject: POLS
POLS 684.description: Study of political and social movements, political status, national and cultural identities, and issues of representation of Native Hawaiians.

POLS 685C.title: Topics in Asian and/or Pacific Politics: Korean politics
POLS 685C.subject: POLS
POLS 685C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 686.title: Politics of Hawaiʻi
POLS 686.subject: POLS
POLS 686.description: Examinations from several perspectives of the political, economic, and cultural forces that historically formed Hawaiʻi and contemporary political themes, issues, and processes.
POLS 686.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

POLS 692.title: Teaching Initiative in Political Science
POLS 692.subject: POLS
POLS 692.description: Combines the study of the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching political science with supervised classroom teaching of POLS 110 .

POLS 696.title: Graduate Intern Seminar
POLS 696.subject: POLS
POLS 696.description: Seminar for those seeking internship experience.
POLS 696.prereq_raw: POLS 672 and POLS 673 or consent for the alternative futures option; POLS 620 or consent for the indigenous politics option; consent of advisor for all other options.

POLS 702.title: Seminar: Research Methods
POLS 702.subject: POLS
POLS 702.description: Conceptual strategies, data collection approaches, and data analysis techniques appropriate to political inquiries.

POLS 703.title: Writing Politics
POLS 703.subject: POLS
POLS 703.description: Seminar on the politics of writing, grammar, translation, argument, genre, and style with significant content on indigenous issues of oral traditions, alternative modes of writing and argument, and language continuance.

POLS 720.title: Seminar: Indigenous Theory
POLS 720.subject: POLS
POLS 720.description: Preannounced topics may include gender and sexuality studies, postcolonial theory, colonial discourse analysis, globalization, historiography; emphasis on indigenous epistemologies and the work of native scholars.

POLS 730.title: Seminar: International Relations
POLS 730.subject: POLS
POLS 730.description: Preannounced problems of both international organization and politics.

POLS 750.title: Seminar: Public Administration
POLS 750.subject: POLS
POLS 750.description: Pre-announced administrative theory, comparative and development administration, and functional aspects.

POLS 776.title: Indigenous Nations and the Problems of Sovereignty
POLS 776.subject: POLS
POLS 776.description: Examines intersections of sovereignty and indigenity from comparative and critical perspectives. Engages indigenous studies of sovereignty and of alternative political frameworks.

POLS 777.title: Decolonial Futures
POLS 777.subject: POLS
POLS 777.description: Topic engages probable and preferable futures of indigenous struggles and resistances. Emphasis placed on the ethics and responsibilities used to move towards those futures.

POLS 780.title: Seminar: Politics of Regions
POLS 780.subject: POLS
POLS 780.description: Analysis of political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in regions and subregions of the world.

PORT 102.title: Elementary Portuguese
PORT 102.subject: PORT
PORT 102.description: Conversation, grammar and reading. Continuation of PORT 101 .

PORT 103.title: Intensive Elementary Portuguese
PORT 103.subject: PORT
PORT 103.description: Intensive elementary Portuguese course covers content of PORT 101 and PORT 102 combined. Hybrid format combines 3 credits online and 3 credits face to face.

PORT 203.title: Intensive Intermediate Portuguese
PORT 203.subject: PORT
PORT 203.description: Intensive Intermediate Portuguese course covers content of PORT 201 and PORT 202 combined. Hybrid format combines 3 credits online and 3 credits face to face.

PORT 303.title: Conversation
PORT 303.subject: PORT
PORT 303.description: Intensive practice in spoken Portuguese, focusing on the preparation and completion of oral tasks and presentations. 40 or more of the grade is based on 3-4 oral communication presentations.

PORT 360.title: Third-Level Portuguese Abroad
PORT 360.subject: PORT
PORT 360.description: Intensive, formal instruction at the third-year level in Portuguese language: reading, writing, pronunciation, grammar, or conversation in a Portuguese-speaking country.

PORT 460.title: Fourth-Level Portuguese Abroad
PORT 460.subject: PORT
PORT 460.description: Intensive formal instruction at the fourth-year level in Portuguese language, linguistics, culture, civilization, film, or literature in a Portuguese-speaking country.

PPC 340.title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
PPC 340.subject: PPC
PPC 340.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
PPC 340.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.

PRAK 481.title: Introduction to Prakrit I
PRAK 481.subject: PRAK
PRAK 481.description: Survey of principal Prakrit languages; selected readings and analysis.
PRAK 481.prereq_raw: PALI 381 , PALI 382 , SNSK 281, and SNSK 282; or equivalent.

PSTY 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
PSTY 499.subject: PSTY
PSTY 499.description: Individualized directed readings and/or research in mental health and psychiatry under the supervision of an instructor.

PSTY 532.title: Psychiatry Longitudinal Clerkship
PSTY 532.subject: PSTY
PSTY 532.description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, including knowledge, skills, attitudes for assessment, diagnosis, and management of psychiatric problems in medical practice, inpatient, and emergency room settings. Emphasis on development and application of psychosocial cultural formulations in all areas of psychiatric and medical practice.
PSTY 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.
PSTY 532.coreq_raw: FMCH 532 , MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532 , SURG 532 , and SURG 535.

PSTY 595.title: Philosophy & Human Suffering
PSTY 595.subject: PSTY
PSTY 595.description: To see how various philosophies and religions have tackled the question, “why is there suffering in the world?” Read short excerpts from “classic” texts and discuss in a welcoming atmosphere and draw own conclusions. Medical students only.

PSY 100.title: Survey of Psychology
PSY 100.subject: PSY
PSY 100.description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

PSY 100A.title: Survey of Psychology
PSY 100A.subject: PSY
PSY 100A.description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

PSY 170.title: Personal Development
PSY 170.subject: PSY
PSY 170.description: The application of psychology to the understanding, management, and enhancement of one’s life.

PSY 202.title: Psychology of Gender
PSY 202.subject: PSY
PSY 202.description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to gender and its impact on the lives of women and men: socialization of gender, mental health, racial identity, majority-minority status, sexual orientation, life-span issues and violence.

PSY 212.title: Survey of Research Methods
PSY 212.subject: PSY
PSY 212.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Survey of standard methods and related conceptual issues employed in psychological research. Both experimental and non-experimental methods will be reviewed.

PSY 220.title: Introduction to Behavioral Psychology
PSY 220.subject: PSY
PSY 220.description: Outline of basic learning principles. A general, unified approach to study of human personality and behavior. Based upon a learning conception; various areas of psychology and the other social sciences are treated.

PSY 225.title: Statistical Techniques
PSY 225.subject: PSY
PSY 225.description: Frequency distributions; graphic methods; central tendency; variability; correlation; reliability; tests of significance.

PSY 230.title: Introduction to Psychobiology
PSY 230.subject: PSY
PSY 230.description: Survey of study of behavior from a natural sciences viewpoint. Evolution, ethological analysis of behavior genetics, neural mechanisms, drugs and behavior, biological development.

PSY 240.title: Developmental Psychology
PSY 240.subject: PSY
PSY 240.description: Emotional, mental, physical, social development from infancy to adulthood; interests and abilities at different age levels.

PSY 250.title: Social Psychology
PSY 250.subject: PSY
PSY 250.description: Cognitive, behavioral, and emotional effects of people: interpersonal relations, attribution, attitudes, group behavior, stereotypes, social roles, aggression, helping, self-concept; applications.

PSY 260.title: Psychology of Personality
PSY 260.subject: PSY
PSY 260.description: Scientific study of personality, its meaning, assessment, development, relation to cultural-social determinants.

PSY 270.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
PSY 270.subject: PSY
PSY 270.description: History, theories, nature of psychological problems, methods of assessment, forms of intervention, current developments.

PSY 280.title: Introduction to Community Psychology
PSY 280.subject: PSY
PSY 280.description: Examination of human functioning in social and ecological context. Topics include stress, health, intergroup relations, culture, ethnicity, social competence, and community empowerment.

PSY 301.title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
PSY 301.subject: PSY
PSY 301.description: Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research.
