Develops knowledge and written communication skills through an introduction to classroom assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing.

PSY 322.title: Learning and Motivation
PSY 322.subject: PSY
PSY 322.description: Theoretical interpretations; survey of major theorists and contemporary controversial issues; major influences in classical and instrumental conditioning.

PSY 324.title: Psychology of Emotion
PSY 324.subject: PSY
PSY 324.description: Survey of traditional views and leading theories, and research in related topics.

PSY 325.title: Cognitive Psychology
PSY 325.subject: PSY
PSY 325.description: Survey of cognitive processes involved in perception, attention, memory, language, problem-solving, reasoning, judgment, intelligence and consciousness, among others.

PSY 331.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
PSY 331.subject: PSY
PSY 331.description: Coverage of the relationship between the brain and body on learning and memory, stress, motivated and regulatory behavioral functions, and mental disorders.

PSY 333.title: Psychopharmacology
PSY 333.subject: PSY
PSY 333.description: Coverage of the principles of pharmacology in relation to the effects of drug actions on the brain and behavior.

PSY 336.title: Sensation and Perception
PSY 336.subject: PSY
PSY 336.description: In-depth coverage of the basic principles involved in sensing and perceiving our environment.

PSY 341.title: Social Development of Children
PSY 341.subject: PSY
PSY 341.description: Survey of the social and emotional development of children and adolescents.

PSY 342.title: Adult Development and Aging
PSY 342.subject: PSY
PSY 342.description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death.

PSY 351.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
PSY 351.subject: PSY
PSY 351.description: Psychological theories and cultural systems; understanding of own and other cultures; psychological and cultural perception of social motivation; cultural similarities and differences in interpersonal relations.

PSY 352.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
PSY 352.subject: PSY
PSY 352.description: Psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, and societal regulation of intimate relationships.

PSY 371.title: Abnormal Psychology
PSY 371.subject: PSY
PSY 371.description: Nature and causes of psychological disorders.

PSY 385.title: Consumer Behavior
PSY 385.subject: PSY
PSY 385.description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects.

PSY 402.title: History of Psychology
PSY 402.subject: PSY
PSY 402.description: Origin and development of contemporary points of view.
PSY 402.prereq_raw: PSY 100 . Recommended: 9 credit hours in psychology.

PSY 403.title: Seminar on the Psychology of Knowledge
PSY 403.subject: PSY
PSY 403.description: Selected topics in the psychology of knowledge and mind from Western and/or non-Western perspectives.

PSY 407.title: Practicum in Psychology
PSY 407.subject: PSY
PSY 407.description: Supervised psychological experience in school, clinic, hospital, industry, social welfare, government, etc.

PSY 408.title: Teaching General Psychology
PSY 408.subject: PSY
PSY 408.prereq_raw: PSY 100 , at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology, and written consent.

children.text: at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology,

PSY 409.title: General Psychology: Advanced Topics
PSY 409.subject: PSY
PSY 409.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research.

PSY 419.title: Psychometrics: Advanced Topics
PSY 419.subject: PSY
PSY 419.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory, research, or methodology relevant to individual differences, measurement, or aspects of psychometrics.

PSY 429.title: Experimental Psychology: Advanced Topics
PSY 429.subject: PSY
PSY 429.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research, in cognitive psychology.

PSY 439.title: Psychobiology: Advanced Topics
PSY 439.subject: PSY
PSY 439.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in psychobiology, physiological psychology, or sensory processes.

PSY 442.title: Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology
PSY 442.subject: PSY
PSY 442.description: Social and emotional maladjustment in children and adolescents, developmental disabilities, pediatric psychology, psychological interventions with children and adolescents.

PSY 449.title: Development Psychology: Advanced Topics
PSY 449.subject: PSY
PSY 449.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in developmental psychology.

PSY 459.title: Social Psychology: Advanced Topics
PSY 459.subject: PSY
PSY 459.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in social psychology.

PSY 476.title: Health Psychology
PSY 476.subject: PSY
PSY 476.description: Psychological principles for understanding and dealing with wellness and illness. Theories and research on stress-related disorders; prevention of stress through lifestyle and healthy behaviors.
PSY 476.prereq_raw: PSY 100 or consent. Recommended: PSY 220 or PSY 322 .

PSY 477.title: Communicating Social Support
PSY 477.subject: PSY
PSY 477.description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships and professional relationships.

PSY 478.title: Teaching Personal Development
PSY 478.subject: PSY
PSY 478.description: Supervised experience in leading a seminar in personal development.
PSY 478.prereq_raw: PSY 170 and 12 additional credits in PSY and written consent.

children.text: additional credits in PSY and written consent

PSY 479.title: Advanced Topics in Adjustment/Treatment/Prevention
PSY 479.subject: PSY
PSY 479.description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in clinical psychology.

PSY 489.title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
PSY 489.subject: PSY
PSY 489.description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research.

PSY 496.title: Special Topics in Psychology
PSY 496.subject: PSY
PSY 496.description: Covers topics of current or special interest not covered in regular course offerings or advanced topics seminars.

PSY 600.title: Methodologic Foundations of Psychology
PSY 600.subject: PSY
PSY 600.description: Methods used in psychological research; observational, correlational, and experimental types of design.

PSY 610.title: Introduction to Regression
PSY 610.subject: PSY
PSY 610.description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences and the general linear model with a focus on regression. Topics include correlation, bivariate and multiple regression, mediation, and moderation. Requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

PSY 611.title: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Related Methods
PSY 611.subject: PSY
PSY 611.description: Introduction to ANOVA and its extensions from both traditional and general linear model approaches. Topics include single and multi-factor ANOVA, multiple comparisons, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and repeated-measures ANOVA.

PSY 613.title: Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Models (SEM)
PSY 613.subject: PSY
PSY 613.description: Theories and applications to latent variables models. Topics include path analysis, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation models (SEM), multi-sample SEM, mean structure, latent growth curve models, and multilevel SEM. Requires basic knowledge of regression.

PSY 614.title: Multivariate Analysis
PSY 614.subject: PSY
PSY 614.description: Analysis of multiple dependent variables. Topics include multivariate normal distribution, Hotelling’s 72, multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA), discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis (PCA).

PSY 616.title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
PSY 616.subject: PSY
PSY 616.description: Test theories and applications in education and social sciences. Topics include the true score model; reliability; generalizability theory; validity; item response theory; and applications in research. Class requires knowledge in ANOVA and regression.

PSY 617.title: Advanced Psychometrics
PSY 617.subject: PSY
PSY 617.description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include unidimensional and multidimensional models of item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, scaling methods, and current issues in psychometrics.

PSY 618.title: Categorical Data Analysis
PSY 618.subject: PSY
PSY 618.description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables. Topics include contingency tables; logistic regression; log-linear models; and introduction to generalized linear models.

PSY 619.title: Analysis of Multilevel Models and Longitudinal Data
PSY 619.subject: PSY
PSY 619.description: Theories and applications of analysis of nested (clustered) data. Topics include fixed and random effects, intra-class correlation, cross-sectional multilevel models, and multilevel models, and multilevel models with repeated measures and longitudinal data. Requires basic knowledge of regression.

PSY 622.title: Principles of Learning
PSY 622.subject: PSY
PSY 622.description: Survey of the principles of learning, including important discoveries in the development of the study of learning, major theories, and both basic and applied research in contemporary literature.

PSY 626.title: Cognitive Psychology
PSY 626.subject: PSY
PSY 626.description: In-depth survey of the computational and representational structures and processes of cognition. Special attention devoted to consideration of the relationship between brain, mind, and computation.

PSY 627.title: Thinking
PSY 627.subject: PSY
PSY 627.description: Provides an introduction to higher cognition (thinking and reasoning) and its foundations, particularly as they relate to the larger field of cognitive science.

PSY 631.title: Comparative Cognition
PSY 631.subject: PSY
PSY 631.description: Survey of the historical and contemporary study of cognition across species, including learning, memory, attention, navigation, reasoning, social interaction, and communication.

PSY 632.title: Selected Topics in Comparative Psychology
PSY 632.subject: PSY
PSY 632.description: Intensive review of comparative, communicative, sensory, or learning mechanisms in animals.

PSY 633.title: Psychopharmacology
PSY 633.subject: PSY
PSY 633.description: Basic principles of pharmacology as they apply to the brain and specific psychological disorders such as anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorders, schizophrenia, psychosis, memory, and drug use.

PSY 634.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
PSY 634.subject: PSY
PSY 634.description: Relation of central and peripheral nervous systems to behavior.

PSY 640.title: Developmental Foundations
PSY 640.subject: PSY
PSY 640.description: Historical, theoretical, and methodological foundations of developmental psychology.

PSY 642.title: Cognitive Development
PSY 642.subject: PSY
PSY 642.description: Familiarizes students with current research and theory in cognitive development through readings of original journal articles and monographs.

PSY 650.title: Social Psychology
PSY 650.subject: PSY
PSY 650.description: Theories and research in social cognition and behavior.

PSY 653.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
PSY 653.subject: PSY
PSY 653.description: Application of psychological theories to cross-cultural phenomena; assessment of cross-cultural processes and social motivations; culture and personality; research evaluation and design.

PSY 654.title: Psychology and Social Issues
PSY 654.subject: PSY
PSY 654.description: Conflict, dissent, community issues, problems; social change and its relation to mental disorder.

PSY 655.title: Applied Social Psychology
PSY 655.subject: PSY
PSY 655.description: Problems in use of social psychology principles in human affairs; multidisciplinary considerations.

PSY 656.title: Social Psychology of Love and Sex
PSY 656.subject: PSY
PSY 656.description: Seminar in psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of cognitive, emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, mate selection, and antecedents and consequences of intimate relationships.

PSY 670.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
PSY 670.subject: PSY
PSY 670.description: Preparation for becoming a clinical psychologist with emphasis on scientist-practitioner model, professional ethics, diversity and professional development.
PSY 670.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate student in psychology or consent of instructor.

PSY 671.title: Introduction to Assessment I
PSY 671.subject: PSY
PSY 671.description: Psychometric theory; ethics; diversity issues; principles and methods of cognitive-intellectual, neuropsychological, and personality assessment.

PSY 672.title: Introduction to Assessment II
PSY 672.subject: PSY
PSY 672.description: Administration and interpretation of cognitive-intellectual and personality assessment devices.
PSY 672.prereq_raw: PSY 670 and PSY 671 or consent and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program.

PSY 673.title: Advanced Assessment
PSY 673.subject: PSY
PSY 673.description: Conceptual and methodological foundations of clinical applications of assessment.
PSY 673.prereq_raw: PSY 671 and PSY 672 and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program, or consent.

PSY 675.title: Treatment Research
PSY 675.subject: PSY
PSY 675.description: Idiographic and nomothetic approaches to clinical treatment research methods and findings.
PSY 675.prereq_raw: PSY 670 (or concurrent) and PSY 671 , or consent.

PSY 676.title: Psychopathology
PSY 676.subject: PSY
PSY 676.description: Comprehensive study of the mental disorders across the lifespan.

PSY 677.title: Child Practicum
PSY 677.subject: PSY
PSY 677.description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of children and adolescents.

PSY 678.title: Adult Practicum
PSY 678.subject: PSY
PSY 678.description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of adults.

PSY 679.title: Practicum in Clinical Psychology
PSY 679.subject: PSY
PSY 679.description: This supervision-style class will cover cases and issues related to students’ clinic work, supervision, or educational goals while training in external practicum sites.

PSY 680.title: Cultural Community Psychology
PSY 680.subject: PSY
PSY 680.description: Graduate seminar on cultural considerations and issues in the history, methods, theories, interventions, and professional roles in community psychology. Small class size (up to 10). Open to graduate students.

PSY 682.title: Practicum: Behavioral Change and Community
PSY 682.subject: PSY
PSY 682.description: Supervised experience in educational, mental health, correctional, consulting, or community action agencies.

PSY 700.title: Thesis Research
PSY 700.subject: PSY
PSY 700.description: Research for master’s thesis. Minimum of six credit hours is required.

PSY 702.title: Seminar in History and Theory of Psychology
PSY 702.subject: PSY

PSY 711.title: Seminar in Quantitative Psychology
PSY 711.subject: PSY
PSY 711.description: Specific and newly emerging topics in statistics, including casual inference, analysis of missing data, and statistical machine learning. Content varies and focuses on advanced topics not covered in other PSY methods and statistics courses.
PSY 711.prereq_raw: PSY 610 (with a minimum grade of B) or instructor consent.

PSY 719.title: Research in Psychometrics
PSY 719.subject: PSY
PSY 719.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PSY 729.title: Research in Experimental Psychology
PSY 729.subject: PSY
PSY 729.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PSY 739.title: Research in Psychology
PSY 739.subject: PSY
PSY 739.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PSY 749.title: Research in Developmental Psychology
PSY 749.subject: PSY
PSY 749.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PSY 759.title: Research in Social Psychology
PSY 759.subject: PSY
PSY 759.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PSY 771.title: Child Treatment
PSY 771.subject: PSY
PSY 771.description: Psychological interventions for youth, as well as parent training.

PSY 772.title: Adult Treatment: Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy
PSY 772.subject: PSY
PSY 772.description: Training in cognitive-behavioral strategies for treating adults.
PSY 772.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in Clinical Studies Program only. PSY major only.

PSY 776.title: Health Psychology: Behavioral and Biological Bases
PSY 776.subject: PSY
PSY 776.description: Psychological and biological bases of health psychology and behavioral medicine. Overview of cognitive, behavioral, and psychophysiological mechanisms; theories and methods of prevention in physical disease.

PSY 779.title: Research in Clinical Psychology
PSY 779.subject: PSY
PSY 779.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PSY 789.title: Community Psychology Research
PSY 789.subject: PSY
PSY 789.description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

PUBA 330.title: Survey of Public Policy and Analysis
PUBA 330.subject: PUBA
PUBA 330.description: Students will learn about the policy making process, the results of policy decisions and how public policy is assessed, analyzed, and responded to. Also discusses important policy issues that currently fill the political landscape.
PUBA 330.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

PUBA 350.title: Research Methods for Policy Evaluation
PUBA 350.subject: PUBA
PUBA 350.description: Explores methodological approaches to the evaluation of public policies and strengths and weaknesses of various social science research methods. Students will learn how to employ them to determine the effectiveness of various public policies.
PUBA 350.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

PUBA 360.title: Foundations of Nonprofit Management
PUBA 360.subject: PUBA
PUBA 360.description: Broad overview of nonprofit organizations, including what it means to be a nonprofit, strategies of nonprofit organizations, and the management of nonprofits. Topics include advocacy, leadership, and evaluating success. Sophomore standing or higher.

PUBA 424.title: Multicultural Leadership in Public Service
PUBA 424.subject: PUBA
PUBA 424.description: Develop students’ culturally agile leadership to allow them effectively lead in work on international, regional, and local projects and problems of compelling public interest that cross cultures. Junior standing or higher.

PUBA 495.title: Practicum and Internship
PUBA 495.subject: PUBA
PUBA 495.description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
PUBA 495.prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent.

PUBA 499.title: Directed Reading and Research in Public Administration
PUBA 499.subject: PUBA
PUBA 499.description: Independent research and reading on topics in public administration, public service, and community development.

PUBA 601.title: Introduction to Research Approaches for Public and Nonprofit Organizations
PUBA 601.subject: PUBA
PUBA 601.description: Introduction to research approaches for conducting and evaluating the effectiveness of programs in the public and nonprofit sectors; performance measurement to inform managerial decision making.
PUBA 601.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only.

PUBA 602.title: Introduction to Public Administration
PUBA 602.subject: PUBA
PUBA 602.description: Develop a comprehension of the history and foundation of public administration. Topics include economic, political, and social dynamics; decision-making and leadership theories, management challenges, human resources, budgeting, program evaluation, policy, and technology.
PUBA 602.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PUBA 603.title: Organizations: Theory and Change
PUBA 603.subject: PUBA
PUBA 603.description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations.
PUBA 603.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PUBA 604.title: Leadership and Ethics
PUBA 604.subject: PUBA
PUBA 604.description: Applies leadership and ethical theories to public and non-profit sectors, focusing on ethical leadership; emphasizes critical thinking to address value conflicts; and teaches moral reasoning as a practical professional skill.
PUBA 604.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PUBA 605.title: Effective Communication in Public Administration
PUBA 605.subject: PUBA
PUBA 605.description: Knowledge and skills to effectively communicate in the public sector. Focus on communication foundations and skills, levels and contexts of public sector communication, and handling challenges such as diverse and multi-cultural settings.
PUBA 605.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PUBA 606.title: Public Administration Personnel Management
PUBA 606.subject: PUBA
PUBA 606.description: Understand the pivotal role that effective human resource management (also known as personnel management) plays in improving organizational effectiveness. Topics include managing diversity, employment law and discrimination, performance appraisal, and labor-management relations.
PUBA 606.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PUBA 607.title: Public Administration Research Methods
PUBA 607.subject: PUBA
PUBA 607.description: Introduction to research methods for public administrators to understand the principles and methods used to conduct and analyze valid research. Examples are oriented to the field; theory and hands-on practice utilized.
PUBA 607.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

PUBA 608.title: Public Budgeting
PUBA 608.subject: PUBA
PUBA 608.description: Institutions and issues related to public-sector budgeting at federal, state, and local levels. Process of developing public budgets and constraints on public policy reflected in budgets.

PUBA 609.title: Policy Analysis and Implementation
PUBA 609.subject: PUBA
PUBA 609.description: Explore contemporary policy issues relating to public administration practice. Develop analytic techniques and models of public policy-making processes, administrative rules, and policy implementation strategies. Learn how social forces, political, and economic pressures influence policy orientation.

PUBA 620.title: Reforming Public Organizations
PUBA 620.subject: PUBA
PUBA 620.description: Looks at the challenges and opportunities for changing public organizations so that they may be more successful in meeting their public responsibilities and better places for people to work. Focus is on the creation of positive images of organization and effective change strategies.

PUBA 621.title: The Political Environment of Public Organizations
PUBA 621.subject: PUBA
PUBA 621.description: Seminar on the role of public managers in shaping public opinion and public policy. Using evidence from theory and practice presents students with tools for understanding management roles within a political context.
PUBA 621.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PUBA 622.title: Strategies of Change: Leaders and Leadership
PUBA 622.subject: PUBA
PUBA 622.description: Explores the key elements of leadership in public settings by examining what leaders actually do, looking at popular media portrayals of leadership, and talking together with guests about the challenges of leadership, effective followership, and positive change.

PUBA 625.title: Law, Economics, and Public Administration
PUBA 625.subject: PUBA
PUBA 625.description: Explore U.S. law as applied to public institutions using economic lens. Rationale of property, contract, and tort law; evolution of administrative law, economic efficiency of common law system, effects of legal rules on economic behavior.

PUBA 626.title: Collaboration for Public and Nonprofit Leaders
PUBA 626.subject: PUBA
PUBA 626.description: Theories, skills, and tools needed to effectively manage networks in government and nonprofit organizations; explores how to administer, assess performance, and evaluate success in these dynamic new partnerships.
PUBA 626.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

PUBA 627.title: Managing Workplace Diversity and Inclusion
PUBA 627.subject: PUBA
PUBA 627.description: Examines rationales, impacts, and various dimensions of diversity and inclusion beyond race and gender. Students learn and apply public management tools used to foster workplace diversity and inclusion.

PUBA 628.title: ICT Policy and Planning
PUBA 628.subject: PUBA
PUBA 628.description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

PUBA 629.title: Public Policy and Advocacy
PUBA 629.subject: PUBA
PUBA 629.description: Designed to deepen students’ ability to understand and influence the policy process in Hawaiʻi and the U.S.. Topics include theories of the policy process, and advocacy strategies, legal constraints, and coalition building.
PUBA 629.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA majors only or approval of instructor.

PUBA 630.title: Nonprofit Management
PUBA 630.subject: PUBA
PUBA 630.description: Fundamental aspects of managing a nonprofit organization: overview of the nonprofit sector; mission and scope of nonprofit organizations; organizational structures and functions; resource and volunteer development; major management issues.
PUBA 630.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

PUBA 631.title: Nonprofit Management Practices and Tools
PUBA 631.subject: PUBA
PUBA 631.description: Skills and tools needed by nonprofit managers. Topics include but are not limited to grant-writing, strategic planning, business practices, program evaluation, and advocacy.

PUBA 640.title: International Perspectives on Public Administration
PUBA 640.subject: PUBA
PUBA 640.description: Key dimensions of public administration systems on a global scale; historic and contemporary forces shaping national systems; the dimensions that distinguish them, the opportunities and constraints for comparison and the transfer of knowledge and experience.
PUBA 640.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or departmental approval.

PUBA 641.title: Indigenous Governance
PUBA 641.subject: PUBA
PUBA 641.description: Overview of indigenous governing systems, particularly in the Americas and the Pacific. Students will learn the legal frameworks and principles of these systems, and how services are provided to citizens.

PUBA 667.title: Special Topics
PUBA 667.subject: PUBA
PUBA 667.description: Topics of current interest in the field of public service and public administration, taught by regular and visiting faculty.

PUBA 690.title: MPA Practicum
PUBA 690.subject: PUBA
PUBA 690.description: Placement in public, private, and nonprofit organizations to observe and analyze organizational functions and processes while undertaking projects of use to the host agency.
PUBA 690.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B: PUBA 602 , PUBA 603 , and PUBA 604 .

PUBA 691.title: Certificate Practicum
PUBA 691.subject: PUBA
PUBA 691.description: Students in the nonprofit management track of the certificate will learn by doing and observing in a nonprofit organization selected in consultation with the student’s advisor.
PUBA 691.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA graduate certificate students only.

PUBA 696.title: Capstone Seminar
PUBA 696.subject: PUBA
PUBA 696.description: Culminates public administration core courses by incorporating theoretical, analytical, and practicum observations into examination of public issues of importance to Hawaiʻi and the region.
PUBA 696.prereq_raw: ( PUBA 601 , PUBA 602 , PUBA 607 ) with a minimum grade of B.

QHS 401.title: Mathematic Preparation for Quantitative Health Sciences
QHS 401.subject: QHS
QHS 401.description: Mathematics preparation for quantitative health sciences. Includes selective topics in linear algebra, advanced calculus and probability theory.

QHS 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
QHS 499.subject: QHS
QHS 499.description: Directed reading/research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through quantitative methodologies and/or the process of conducting a research study.

QHS 600.title: Biostatistics Concepts for Clinical Researchers
QHS 600.subject: QHS
QHS 600.description: Provide biostatistical concepts to clinical researchers. Students will obtain the ability to demonstrate an understanding of key biostatistical concepts in clinical research; and interpret statistical findings most commonly reported in clinical and healthcare literature.
QHS 600.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

QHS 601.title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
QHS 601.subject: QHS
QHS 601.description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

QHS 602.title: Generalized Linear Model
QHS 602.subject: QHS
QHS 602.description: Statistical theory of Linear Model and Generalized Linear Model, algorithms use for estimation, inference concepts, and assessment of goodness-of-fit. Covers Proportional Hazard Model and Generalized Estimating Equations.
QHS 602.prereq_raw: QHS 601 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

QHS 605.title: Data Management and Visualization for Health Sciences
QHS 605.subject: QHS
QHS 605.description: Data management and visualization is essential to all aspects of health sciences. Through hands-on experiences in R, will introduce data processing, manipulation, visualization and reproducibility, with an emphasis on clinical, medical, and health science problems.

QHS 610.title: Bioinformatics I
QHS 610.subject: QHS
QHS 610.description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis.

QHS 611.title: Bioinformatics II
QHS 611.subject: QHS
QHS 611.description: Focus on bioinformatics approaches for functional genomics related to DNA, RNA, and protein. It will provide of virus, bacteria, and human genome and bioinformatics approaches to human disease.
QHS 611.prereq_raw: QHS 610 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

QHS 612.title: Machine Learning for Biomedical Data Science
QHS 612.subject: QHS
QHS 612.description: Introduction to machine learning techniques with a focus on hands-on training. Topics include supervised, unsupervised, and ensemble methods, using R and/or Python to explore data, train models, and evaluate performance in practical projects.

QHS 620.title: Introduction to Clinical Trials
QHS 620.subject: QHS
QHS 620.description: Introduction to clinical trials. Topics include history, definitions/terminology, adverse events, FDA and government regulatory agencies, ethics; monitoring committees, recruitment, introduction to protocol development, basis designs.

QHS 621.title: Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
QHS 621.subject: QHS
QHS 621.description: Covers basic and advanced statistical methods utilized in clinical trials design, conduct, and data analysis. Topics cover statistician’s role in drug development and DSMB, statistical theory in phases I-IV clinical trial designs and analysis.
QHS 621.prereq_raw: QHS 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent

QHS 640.title: Introduction to Clinical Research
QHS 640.subject: QHS
QHS 640.description: Provides an overview of concepts, methodology, and various practical aspects of clinical research.

QHS 644.title: Translational Research Methods
QHS 644.subject: QHS
QHS 644.description: Focus on translational research methods through selected genetic and acquired diseases including cancer, neurodevelopmental, inflammatory immune, and metabolic conditions with insight into analyses of DNA, RNA, genomics-proteomics, cell and animal models, and advanced imaging.

QHS 646.title: Quantitative Health and Clinical Research Seminar
QHS 646.subject: QHS
QHS 646.description: Provides overview of research related to health in Hawaiʻi and advances in quantitative health and clinical research. Topics include ethnic disparities in health, social and cultural factors, ethics, biostatistics and bioinformatics.

QHS 647.title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
QHS 647.subject: QHS
QHS 647.description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective.

QHS 650.title: Secondary Data Analysis
QHS 650.subject: QHS
QHS 650.description: Will allow students who are new to using secondary data to become comfortable with accessing the data, forming hypotheses, and designing study proposals. Will introduce examples with basic and advanced techniques.
QHS 650.prereq_raw: QHS 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B- .

children.text: ( or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B-

QHS 654.title: Medical Genetics
QHS 654.subject: QHS
QHS 654.description: Focus on heritable disorders, genetic mechanisms, patterns of inheritance, phenotype-genotype correlations, genetic/environmental factors, clinical diagnoses, genomic and precision medicine.

QHS 670.title: Special Topics in Quantitative Health Sciences
QHS 670.subject: QHS
QHS 670.description: Special topics in quantitative health sciences. Reflects special research interest of QHS faculty or guest lecturers.

QHS 675.title: Biostatistical Consulting
QHS 675.subject: QHS
QHS 675.description: Investigate the roles and responsibilities of the biostatistician as both consultant and collaborator with biomedical researchers, guide students in enhancing problem-solving and communication skills, and provide opportunity to observe real-life biostatistical consultations.
QHS 675.prereq_raw: QHS 601 and QHS 602 (or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent

QHS 676.title: Biostatistical Consulting Practicum
QHS 676.subject: QHS
QHS 676.description: Under the supervision of biostatistics faculty members, students will have the opportunity to provide statistical consultations to biomedical researchers and gain hands-on experience conducting biostatistical analysis in solving real-life analytic problems.
QHS 676.prereq_raw: QHS 675 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B.

QHS 680.title: Critical Appraisal of Clinical Research Literature
QHS 680.subject: QHS
QHS 680.description: Introduces key literature appraisal concepts and processes. Students will practice and sharpen their skills by engaging in the review and discussion of a set of clinical research publications representing major study designs.
QHS 680.prereq_raw: QHS 640 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

QHS 699.title: Directed Research
QHS 699.subject: QHS
QHS 699.description: Directed research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through the process of conducting a research study.

RE 300.title: Principles of Real Estate
RE 300.subject: RE
RE 300.description: Principles affecting the allocation and utilization of real estate resources, including legal, physical, economic elements; valuation; market analysis; finance; investments, and public and private externalities affecting the allocation and utilization of real estate resources.

RE 310.title: Real Estate and Environmental Law
RE 310.subject: RE
RE 310.description: Property rights, land tenure, agency, contracts and negotiation theory, title conveyancing and escrow, mortgage instruments, fair housing, state and federal environmental policy.

RE 330.title: Real Estate Appraisal/Analysis
RE 330.subject: RE
RE 330.description: Analysis of real property, including feasibility analysis, market analysis, income property capitalization, and general real estate valuation techniques.

RE 340.title: Administration of Real Property Assets
RE 340.subject: RE
RE 340.description: How business firms and investors manage their real property assets in terms of the legal, financial, and physical dimensions of real property. Case studies in hotels, condominiums, and office buildings in the environment in Hawaiʻi.

RE 390.title: Current Topics in Real Estate Analysis
RE 390.subject: RE
RE 390.description: Consideration of various special concepts and problems in real estate.

RE 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
RE 399.subject: RE
RE 399.description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

RE 420.title: Real Estate Finance and Investment
RE 420.subject: RE
RE 420.description: Financial and investment techniques used to evaluate real property and real estate security investments.

RE 674.title: Real Estate Investment Analysis
RE 674.subject: RE
RE 674.description: Development of strategic business plans for the optimization of a firm’s real property assets. Includes facilities utilization audits, contingency planning, and the impact of new techniques.

REL 149.title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
REL 149.subject: REL
REL 149.description: Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E.

REL 150.title: Introduction to the World’s Major Religions
REL 150.subject: REL
REL 150.description: Buddhism, Christianity, Confucianism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Shinto, Taoism and indigenous traditions of Hawaiʻi and/or Oceania.

REL 151.title: Religion and the Meaning of Existence
REL 151.subject: REL
REL 151.description: Basic ideas and issues in contemporary religious thought about the meaning of existence.

REL 151A.title: Religion and the Meaning of Existence
REL 151A.subject: REL
REL 151A.description: Basic ideas and issues in contemporary religious thought about the meaning of existence.

REL 153.title: Introduction to World Mythology
REL 153.subject: REL
REL 153.description: Reading and analysis of myths and legends from around the globe, from before the dawn of writing to 1500 C.E. Students will learn to interpret traditional stories from several theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

REL 160.title: Religion and Social Justice
REL 160.subject: REL
REL 160.description: Religious persons and organizations play significant roles in fighting for issues of social justice worldwide. Introduces students to the relationship between religions and social justice in China, South America, U.S., and Hawaiʻi.

REL 170.title: Religion and the Environment
REL 170.subject: REL
REL 170.description: Examines the roles contemporary religious groups play in ground movements for sustainability. Introduces students to key scholars, religious leaders, and activists who are implementing sustainable solutions to pressing environmental problems.

REL 200.title: Understanding the Old Testament (Hebrew Bible)
REL 200.subject: REL
REL 200.description: Examines the Old Testament (Hebrew Bible) as an expression of the religious life, history, and thought of ancient Israel and as a sacred text within later Judaism and Christianity.

REL 201.title: Understanding the New Testament
REL 201.subject: REL
REL 201.description: Origin and development of early Christian message as set forth in the New Testament; special attention to Jesus and Paul.

REL 202.title: Understanding Indian Religions
REL 202.subject: REL
REL 202.description: Historical survey of the teachings and practices of major religious traditions of India.

REL 203.title: Understanding Chinese Religions
REL 203.subject: REL
REL 203.description: Taoist, Confucian, Buddhist and folk beliefs and practices in their social and historical context.

REL 204.title: Understanding Japanese Religions
REL 204.subject: REL
REL 204.description: Broad survey, with primary focus on Shinto, Buddhist, and modern sectarian movements, analyzed in relation to social and cultural themes of major historical periods.

REL 205.title: Understanding Hawaiian Religion
REL 205.subject: REL
REL 205.description: Major teachings and practices from ancient times to present, their cultural influence; analysis of religious texts; relation to other traditions of Oceania and to Christianity.

REL 207.title: Understanding Buddhism
REL 207.subject: REL
REL 207.description: Survey of major forms and practices.

REL 208.title: Understanding Judaism
REL 208.subject: REL
REL 208.description: Survey from origin to modern times with an emphasis on writing-based analysis of Jewish thought in Talmudic and Medieval Periods

REL 209.title: Understanding Islam
REL 209.subject: REL
REL 209.description: Historical survey of the beliefs and practices of Islam as a world religion, including the prophet Muhammad, scriptures, philosophy and science, theology, law, major sectarian movements, relations with other religious traditions, and fundamentalism.

REL 210.title: Understanding Christianity
REL 210.subject: REL
REL 210.description: History of ideas concentrating on events, persons, and issues with the greatest impact on the evolution of Christianity.

REL 211.title: Understanding Ancient Religions
REL 211.subject: REL
REL 211.description: Comparative and historical survey of the religious beliefs and practices in ancient times throughout Egypt, Mesopotamia, Syria-Canaan, Anatolia, Persia, Greece, and Rome.

REL 214.title: Viking Religion
REL 214.subject: REL
REL 214.description: Introduction to the Scandinavian religions in the Viking Age, their depiction in popular culture, and reconstruction in the form of new religious movements.

REL 216.title: Priestesses and Prophetesses
REL 216.subject: REL
REL 216.description: Legendary priestesses and prophetesses from ancient to modern religions around the world including ancient Sumeria, Egypt, Greece, China, India, the Middle East, Japan, and Hawaiʻi. This course develops written communication skills.

REL 300.title: Myth, Religion, and Society
REL 300.subject: REL
REL 300.description: Survey of major theories and methods for analyzing myth, ritual, and religious practice, drawing on anthropology, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, and sociology. Emphasis on developing core analytical skills.
REL 300.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

REL 301.title: Biblical Hebrew I
REL 301.subject: REL
REL 301.description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible.
REL 301.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

REL 302.title: Biblical Hebrew II
REL 302.subject: REL
REL 302.description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; essay-based analysis of literary forms, with attention given both to stories important to the development of the Abrahamic religions and writing-based interpretation of religious traditions.
REL 302.prereq_raw: REL 301 / CLAS 301 with C- or better.

REL 303.title: Creation and Evolution
REL 303.subject: REL
REL 303.description: An exploration of interactions between science and religion with a focus on cosmogonies.

REL 304.title: Indigenous & Decolonial Approaches to Religion and Culture
REL 304.subject: REL
REL 304.description: Introduction to indigenous and decolonial approaches to the study of religion and culture. Includes a critical assessment of tools and terminology traditionally used in academia. Sophomore standing or higher.

REL 305.title: Sacred Animals
REL 305.subject: REL
REL 305.description: Critical study of the ethical treatment of nonhuman animals and the religious beliefs and practices associated with them throughout history and across various cultures. Emphasis on teaching oral communication.
REL 305.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

REL 308.title: Zen (Ch’an) Buddhist Masters
REL 308.subject: REL
REL 308.description: Study of lives, teachings, practices of Zen masters in China, Japan, Korea, and the West.

REL 310.title: Global Christianity
REL 310.subject: REL
REL 310.description: Christianity as a transcultural religion, through the study of Christian art, literature, ritual, and theology in diverse cultures; including the Near East, Africa, Latin America, and the Pacific.
REL 310.prereq_raw: REL 150 , REL 201 , or REL 210 ; or consent.

REL 311.title: Ka Baibala ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi (The Bible in Hawaiian)
REL 311.subject: REL
REL 311.description: Survey of and selected readings from the Hawaiian Bible (Baibala Hemolele). Conducted in Hawaiian.

REL 333.title: Cults and New Religions
REL 333.subject: REL
REL 333.description: Study of cults and new religious movements in America, the Pacific, and East Asia; examining types, causes, and functions of these movements.

REL 345.title: Religion and Conflict in American History
REL 345.subject: REL
REL 345.description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion. Sophomore standing or higher.

REL 348.title: Religion, Politics, and Society
REL 348.subject: REL
REL 348.description: Exploration of the diverse approaches and perspectives that American religious groups embrace in addressing controversial and diverse issues of contemporary American life. Emphasis on considering and discussing ethical approaches and practicing oral communication.

REL 351.title: Christian Ethics in Modern Life
REL 351.subject: REL
REL 351.description: The meaning of Christian faith for the moral life with reference to contemporary moral issues.

REL 352.title: Sufism: Mystical Traditions of Islam
REL 352.subject: REL
REL 352.description: Introduction to the history, literature, and worldview of Sufism. Students will encounter the following topics in relation to Islamic mysticism: asceticism, monotheism, philosophy, love, union, sainthood, ecstatic experience, and spiritual uses of art.
REL 352.prereq_raw: REL 209 or REL 383 or PHIL 330 or HIST 354 , or consent.

REL 353.title: Witches and Witchcraft
REL 353.subject: REL
REL 353.description: Persecution of witches, witchcraft in Europe, 1300-1700, examined as crisis of church and theology; origins, effects on church and society.
REL 353.prereq_raw: one of REL 201 , HIST 151 , HIST 152 , PSY 100 , or consent.

REL 354.title: Islam in History
REL 354.subject: REL
REL 354.description: Examination of the historical connections between Islam and other civilizations will focus on the role of Islam in world history.

REL 356.title: Women and Religion
REL 356.subject: REL
REL 356.description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through reading autobiographies, films, and primary texts, and through the development of research and writing skills.
REL 356.prereq_raw: REL 149 or WGSS 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151 .

REL 357.title: Heroes and Villians in Religious Literature
REL 357.subject: REL
REL 357.description: Explores the depictions of heroes and villains in the religious literature of the world. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

REL 361.title: Love, Sex, and Religion
REL 361.subject: REL
REL 361.description: Love and sex as themes in religions of Asia and the West.

REL 363.title: Religion and Art
REL 363.subject: REL
REL 363.description: The uses of art in religion are studied with historical examples.

REL 371.title: Prophecies of the Last Days
REL 371.subject: REL
REL 371.description: In-depth look at ancient Judeo-Christian apocalyptic texts and the communities in which they originated, followed by a survey of the medieval and modern day heirs of apocalyptic traditions.

REL 373.title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
REL 373.subject: REL
REL 373.description: Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. Written communication emphasis.
REL 373.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

REL 374.title: Classical Hindu Mythology
REL 374.subject: REL
REL 374.description: Study of myths and narratives of classical Hinduism through the Sanskrit epics Rāmāyana and Mahābhārata; exploring major concepts such as dharma, karma, and yoga. Intensive, interpretive writing, and peer-review exercises, will hone students’ writing skills.
REL 374.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

REL 383.title: Mysticism East and West
REL 383.subject: REL
REL 383.description: Mystic traditions of the West from desert monasticism to Renaissance mystics compared with those of South and East Asia. Focuses on the ethical lives of these mystics, and developing oral communication skills. Sophomore standing or higher.

REL 390.title: Hawaiian Gods
REL 390.subject: REL
REL 390.description: The traditions and practices related to one or more major indigenous gods, or class of gods, will be studied by the interpretation and analysis of primary texts. Develops written communication skills.

REL 394.title: On Death and Dying
REL 394.subject: REL
REL 394.description: Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves.

REL 409.title: Life and Teachings of Jesus
REL 409.subject: REL
REL 409.description: Critical study of synoptic gospels and of extra-Biblical sources with an emphasis on teaching students to present their research in both written and oral formats.
REL 409.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

REL 422.title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
REL 422.subject: REL
REL 422.description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

REL 431.title: Health/Medicine in Religion
REL 431.subject: REL
REL 431.description: Issues of health and disease in the light of religious beliefs and practices with a focus on ethical matters shaping policies in the U.S. and the world.

REL 433.title: Religion and Food
REL 433.subject: REL
REL 433.description: Writing-based seminar exploring foodways as a basic component in the practice of religions. Examines theoretical issues, foodways as creators of community and identity, sustainability, and other ethical issues, abstinence and fasting, and healing.

REL 443.title: Anthropology of Buddhism
REL 443.subject: REL
REL 443.description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

REL 444.title: Spiritual Ecology
REL 444.subject: REL
REL 444.description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism.
REL 444.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

REL 445.title: Sacred Places
REL 445.subject: REL
REL 445.description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects.
REL 445.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

REL 452.title: Sociology of Religion
REL 452.subject: REL
REL 452.description: Seminar on research in sociological aspects of religious sectarianism, historical and current; special reference to Hawaiʻi.

REL 475.title: Seminar on Buddhism
REL 475.subject: REL
REL 475.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Buddhism; topics and geographical focus to be announced each semester.

REL 476.title: Daoism: Philosophy and Religion
REL 476.subject: REL
REL 476.description: Seminar on religious Taoism, its historical development and its role in the present-day context. Sophomore standing or higher.

REL 478.title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
REL 478.subject: REL
REL 478.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

REL 480.title: Field Methods in Religion
REL 480.subject: REL
REL 480.description: Introduction to theoretical and methodological approaches to doing fieldwork in the study of religion. Application of these in studying Hawaiʻi’s diverse religious environment.

REL 490.title: Buddhism in Japan
REL 490.subject: REL
REL 490.description: Major features and trends in thought, institutions, and practices in the context of Japanese history and culture, 6th-20th century.

REL 492.title: Polynesian Religions
REL 492.subject: REL
REL 492.description: Introduction to field, comparison of several traditions; beliefs and practices from analysis of texts. Historical interactions with Christianity. Sophomore standing or higher.

REL 495.title: Seminar in Religion
REL 495.subject: REL
REL 495.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

REL 499.title: Directed Reading or Research
REL 499.subject: REL
REL 499.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair.

REL 600.title: History and Theory of the Study of Myth and Religion
REL 600.subject: REL
REL 600.description: Study of major theories and methods for analyzing religion, building on anthropological, historical, and sociological approaches. Emphasis on historiography, comparative frameworks, and applying interdisciplinary methods to original research.

REL 601.title: Sacred Space
REL 601.subject: REL
REL 601.description: Introduces ways that sacred sites are used by religious adherents in Asia and the Pacific. Students will survey different methodologies, and develop a final project on a single sacred site.
REL 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

REL 602.title: The Study of the Ways Religion is Practiced
REL 602.subject: REL
REL 602.description: The study of rituals and practices in the religious traditions of Asia and the Pacific, with a focus on the importance and significance they play in people’s lives.
REL 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

REL 603.title: The Study of New Religious Movements
REL 603.subject: REL
REL 603.description: Seminar exploring methods developed for the study of New Religions, particularly in the U.S., Asia, and the Pacific. Considers implications of these methodologies for studies of other religious traditions.
REL 603.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

REL 604.title: Indigenous Religions & Decolonial Theories and Methods
REL 604.subject: REL
REL 604.description: Surveys decolonial approaches to the study of religion(s) and focuses on a specific Indigenous religion of Asia and the Pacific to examine the ways that historical paradigms have adversely influenced the study of Indigenous religions.
REL 604.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

REL 605.title: Healing in the Religious Traditions of Asia and the Pacific
REL 605.subject: REL
REL 605.description: Seminar focused on approaches to healing in the religious traditions of Asia and the Pacific. Explores commonalities between religious traditions, geographical areas, historical periods, and disciplines.
REL 605.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

REL 661B.title: Seminar on East Asian Religions: Chinese religions
REL 661B.subject: REL
REL 661B.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in East Asian religions and traditions: (B) Chinese religions; (C) Japanese religions; (D) East Asian Buddhism.

REL 661C.title: Seminar on East Asian Religions: Japanese religions
REL 661C.subject: REL
REL 661C.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in East Asian religions and traditions: (B) Chinese religions; (C) Japanese religions; (D) East Asian Buddhism.

REL 661D.title: Seminar on East Asian Religions: East Asian Buddhism
REL 661D.subject: REL
REL 661D.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in East Asian religions and traditions: (B) Chinese religions; (C) Japanese religions; (D) East Asian Buddhism.

REL 662B.title: Seminar on South Asian Religions: Indian religions
REL 662B.subject: REL
REL 662B.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Indian religious traditions: (B) Indian religions; (D) Indian Buddhism.

REL 662D.title: Seminar on South Asian Religions: Indian Buddhism
REL 662D.subject: REL
REL 662D.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Indian religious traditions: (B) Indian religions; (D) Indian Buddhism.

REL 663B.title: Seminar in Polynesian Religions: Polynesian religions
REL 663B.subject: REL
REL 663B.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Polynesian and Hawaiian religious traditions: (B) Polynesian religions; (C) Hawaiian religion.

REL 663C.title: Seminar in Polynesian Religions: Hawaiian religion
REL 663C.subject: REL
REL 663C.description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Polynesian and Hawaiian religious traditions: (B) Polynesian religions; (C) Hawaiian religion.

REL 680B.title: Pedagogy in Religion: teaching religion
REL 680B.subject: REL
REL 680B.description: Theory, preparation, and practice in the teaching of religious studies at the community college level: (B) teaching religion; (C) teaching religion practicum.

REL 680C.title: Pedagogy in Religion: teaching religion practicum
REL 680C.subject: REL
REL 680C.description: Theory, preparation, and practice in the teaching of religious studies at the community college level: (B) teaching religion; (C) teaching religion practicum.

REL 688.title: Plan B Research
REL 688.subject: REL
REL 688.description: Research for master’s degree Plan B. Restricted to students in the Religion Masters Program in Plan B. Enrollment must be approved by student’s project committee.

REL 695.title: Topics in Religious Studies
REL 695.subject: REL
REL 695.description: Topics in the study of religion with special emphasis on theoretical approaches and concerns. Specific topics to be preannounced.

REPR 611.title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
REPR 611.subject: REPR
REPR 611.description: Presentation and discussion of current research topics in biomedical sciences.

REPR 705.title: Special Topics in Reproductive Biology
REPR 705.subject: REPR
REPR 705.description: In-depth discussion of selected areas of reproductive biology, with special emphasis on recent research results and methodologies. May be retaken for credit.

RUS 209.title: Russian Phonetics
RUS 209.subject: RUS
RUS 209.description: Basic theory of Russian sound system; practice in pronunciation, intonation, and fluency.

RUS 260.title: Intensive Intermediate Russian Abroad
RUS 260.subject: RUS
RUS 260.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the second-year level in Russian language and culture in Russia.

RUS 303.title: Advanced Russian
RUS 303.subject: RUS
RUS 303.description: Systematic practice for control of spoken and written Russian, vocabulary building, fluency in various subjects, accuracy in sentence structure, phrasing stylistic appropriateness.

RUS 306.title: Russian Structure
RUS 306.subject: RUS
RUS 306.description: Advanced grammar; complexities of standard contemporary Russian; word formation and verb system.

RUS 311.title: Readings in Russian Civilization and Literature
RUS 311.subject: RUS
RUS 311.description: Mid-level readings in Russian civilization and literature of edited and adapted texts.

RUS 312.title: Readings in Russian Civilization and Literature
RUS 312.subject: RUS

RUS 360.title: Intensive Third-Level Russian Abroad
RUS 360.subject: RUS
RUS 360.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the third-year level in Russian language and culture in Russia.

RUS 399.title: Directed Reading
RUS 399.subject: RUS
RUS 399.description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision.
RUS 399.prereq_raw: RUS 202 and consent and departmental approval.

RUS 403.title: Advanced Conversation and Composition
RUS 403.subject: RUS
RUS 403.description: Systematic practice on selected topics; vocabulary building and development of fluency; writing short reports, narratives.

RUS 418.title: Advanced Reading and Translation: Modern Prose
RUS 418.subject: RUS
RUS 418.description: Readings in various fields, emphasizing idiomatic usage.

RUS 419.title: Advanced Reading of Russian Press
RUS 419.subject: RUS
RUS 419.description: Materials from Soviet/Russian newspapers and magazines.

RUS 431.title: Russian Folklore
RUS 431.subject: RUS
RUS 431.description: Selected Russian folk narratives, bylinas, songs, and proverbs. Influence of folklore on major Russian authors.

RUS 441.title: Russian Short Story
RUS 441.subject: RUS
RUS 441.description: Origin and development (19th and 20th century); the major writers.
RUS 441.prereq_raw: three years of Russian or consent.

RUS 442.title: Russian Novel
RUS 442.subject: RUS
RUS 442.description: Origin and development from 18th century to present.
RUS 442.prereq_raw: three years of Russian language or consent.

RUS 451.title: Topics in 19th- and 20th-Century Russian Literature
RUS 451.subject: RUS
RUS 451.description: Focus upon the selected writings of one major Russian writer of the 19th century (e.g., Pushkin, Gogol, Lermontov, Dostoevsky, or Tolstoy) or 20th century (e.g., Bely, Blok, Bulgakov, Chekhov, Pasternak, Sholokhov, or Solzhenitsyn).

RUS 460.title: Intensive Fourth-Level Russian Abroad
RUS 460.subject: RUS
RUS 460.description: Intensive advanced courses of formal instruction on the fourth-year level in Russian language and culture in Russia.

RUS 495.title: Seminar
RUS 495.subject: RUS
RUS 495.description: Literary or linguistic topics, movements, genres, or their representatives.

RUS 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
RUS 499.subject: RUS
RUS 499.description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision.
RUS 499.prereq_raw: RUS 303 (or equivalent), consent or departmental approval.

children.text: ( or equivalent), consent or departmental approval

SAM 101.title: Elementary Samoan
SAM 101.subject: SAM
SAM 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. History and culture. Meets four hours weekly.

SAM 201.title: Intermediate Samoan
SAM 201.subject: SAM
SAM 201.description: Continuation of SAM 102 . Meets four hours weekly. Intermediate-level reading, writing, and conversation practice.

SAM 227.title: Overview of Samoan Literature in English
SAM 227.subject: SAM
SAM 227.description: Survey of major writers of Samoan literature in English; lectures, discussions, short paper.

SAM 301.title: Third-Level Samoan: Traditional Culture
SAM 301.subject: SAM
SAM 301.description: Continuation of SAM 202 . Advanced reading and composition with development of language structure integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected traditional cultural topics. Meets three times weekly; additional lab work.

SAM 302.title: Third-Level Samoan: Contemporary Culture
SAM 302.subject: SAM
SAM 302.description: Continuation of SAM 202 . Advanced reading and composition with development of language structure integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected contemporary cultural topics.

SAM 321.title: Samoan Conversation: Traditional Contexts
SAM 321.subject: SAM
SAM 321.description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Samoan in traditional contexts.

SAM 322.title: Samoan Conversation: Contemporary Contexts
SAM 322.subject: SAM
SAM 322.description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Samoan in modern contexts.

SAM 421.title: Samoan Ceremonial Speech
SAM 421.subject: SAM
SAM 421.description: Development of oratory skills in Samoan ceremonial speech. Emphasis on institutionalized applications such as the kava ceremony and formal speechmaking.

SAM 431.title: Samoan Oral Traditions
SAM 431.subject: SAM
SAM 431.description: Historical survey and analysis of the oral traditions and genealogies of Samoa with special emphasis on the relationship of these traditions with Samoan ceremonial speech.

SAM 452.title: Structure of Samoan
SAM 452.subject: SAM
SAM 452.description: Study of modern Samoan grammar including some sociolinguistic background. Intensive reading and writing in Samoan and English.

SAM 461.title: Traditional Samoan Literature
SAM 461.subject: SAM
SAM 461.description: A survey of the major genres of traditional Samoan literature. Taught in the Samoan language.

SLS 130.title: Introduction to Pidgin in Hawaiʻi
SLS 130.subject: SLS
SLS 130.description: Introduction to contemporary Pidgin in Hawaiʻi, in relation to the role of Hawaiian and Languages of the Asia-Pacific region; language rights; sociolinguistics of Pidgin and Hawaiian in institutional, educational, and interpersonal contexts.

SLS 150.title: Learning Languages and Communicating Interculturally in a Global Multilingual World
SLS 150.subject: SLS
SLS 150.description: Historical/global perspective on being/becoming multilingual/multicultural, encompassing cases of second language learning, teaching, use, growth, change, loss across the world, ancient times to present, supporting individuals’ motivations and abilities concerning second languages and cultures.

SLS 170.title: Language by the Numbers
SLS 170.subject: SLS
SLS 170.description: Understanding quantitative information and analyses related to language and language learning/multilingualism. Topics include data description and visualization, basic statistics, and evaluating quantitative analyses.

SLS 218.title: Introduction to Second Language Learning and Technology
SLS 218.subject: SLS
SLS 218.description: Introduction to the use of technology in second language learning; pros and cons of specific new applications and established technologies; project-based and oriented; developing multilingual/multicultural understanding through technology. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

SLS 250.title: Topics in Learning and Using Second Languages
SLS 250.subject: SLS
SLS 250.description: Reviews practices of second language learning, use, and maintenance. Introductory exploration and analysis of selected topics with a specific theme indicated by course title listed in the class schedule.

SLS 280.title: Bilingualism: Cognition and Culture
SLS 280.subject: SLS
SLS 280.description: Introduction to bi-/multilingualism as a phenomenon at the level of society and as a characteristic of individual speakers; discussion of recent media reports and popular myths about bilingualism in relation to research-based evidence.

SLS 301.title: Basic Language Concepts for Second Language Learning, Teaching, and Use
SLS 301.subject: SLS
SLS 301.description: Introduction to language structure and function in the domains of sound, words, sentences, and discourse, with specific focus on description, analysis, and research into learner language.
SLS 301.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 302.title: Second Language Learning
SLS 302.subject: SLS
SLS 302.description: Theoretical foundations for the learning and teaching of second/ foreign languages. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.
SLS 302.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 303.title: Second Language Teaching
SLS 303.subject: SLS
SLS 303.description: Survey of methodology; basic concepts and practices; emphasis on teaching second languages through oral instruction.
SLS 303.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 304.title: Sociolinguistics of Multilingualism
SLS 304.subject: SLS
SLS 304.description: Explores themes in sociolinguistics relevant to L2/ multilingual contexts, including language ideology, language variation, language and culture, and language and identity; how L2 users and multilingual people grapple with these issues. Includes emphasis on writing instruction. Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 311.title: Second Language Testing
SLS 311.subject: SLS
SLS 311.description: Measurement and evaluation of achievement and proficiency in second language learning.
SLS 311.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 312.title: Techniques in Second Language Teaching: Reading and Writing
SLS 312.subject: SLS
SLS 312.description: Methods and materials. Issues in teaching; survey of available materials and practice in their adaptation. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.
SLS 312.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 313.title: Techniques in Second Language Teaching: Listening and Speaking
SLS 313.subject: SLS
SLS 313.description: Methods and materials. Issues in teaching; survey of available materials and practice in their adaptation. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.
SLS 313.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 318.title: Digital Literacies, Media and Language Learning
SLS 318.subject: SLS
SLS 318.description: Explores learning technologies and media in digital literacies, language learning and identity development. Students examine agency through curricular and app design and multilingual identities, with a focus on writing instruction and oral communication.
SLS 318.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 408.title: Multilingual Education
SLS 408.subject: SLS
SLS 408.description: Survey and analysis of current thinking and practices in multilingual and multicultural education, including bilingual education; special emphasis on ESL/EFL. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.
SLS 408.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 430.title: Pidgin and Creole English in Hawaiʻi
SLS 430.subject: SLS
SLS 430.description: Major historical descriptive, pedagogical aspects; pidgin and creole languages, linguistic change, language variation with an emphasis on Hawaiian, Asian, and Pacific issues. Work with actual language data.

SLS 455.title: Learning and Teaching World Languages
SLS 455.subject: SLS
SLS 455.description: Hybrid technology intensive course for pre- or in-service teachers of world languages. Topics: online learning, curriculum and lesson planning, assessment, language teaching approaches, technology for learning world languages. Junior standing or higher.

SLS 460.title: English Phonology
SLS 460.subject: SLS
SLS 460.description: Introduction to English phonetics and phonology. Includes an emphasis on the oral presentation of key phonological concepts and provides experience in English pronunciation tutoring.
SLS 460.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 475.title: Practicum for Future Language Professionals
SLS 475.subject: SLS
SLS 475.description: Students observe and assist mentor teachers (minimum of 40 hours) at cooperating schools in multilingual contexts, examining the intersection of theory and practice in language learning and teaching and applying knowledge from other SLS courses.

SLS 480E.title: Topics in Second Language Studies: second language learning
SLS 480E.subject: SLS
SLS 480E.description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research; (U) second language use.
SLS 480E.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 480N.title: Topics in Second Language Studies: second language analysis
SLS 480N.subject: SLS
SLS 480N.description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research; (U) second language use.
SLS 480N.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 480P.title: Topics in Second Language Studies: second language pedagogy
SLS 480P.subject: SLS
SLS 480P.description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research; (U) second language use.
SLS 480P.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 480R.title: Topics in Second Language Studies: second language research
SLS 480R.subject: SLS
SLS 480R.description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research; (U) second language use.
SLS 480R.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 480U.title: Topics in Second Language Studies: second language use
SLS 480U.subject: SLS
SLS 480U.description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research; (U) second language use.
SLS 480U.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SLS 485.title: Professionalism in SLS
SLS 485.subject: SLS
SLS 485.description: Capstone for SLS majors. Reflection on experiences via the major, articulation of professional values, exploration of diverse approaches to professionalism in SLS, and formal compilation of a professional portfolio. Senior standing or higher.

SLS 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
SLS 499.subject: SLS
SLS 499.prereq_raw: a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major, or consent of department chair.

children.text: a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major,

SLS 600.title: Introduction to Second Language Studies
SLS 600.subject: SLS
SLS 600.description: Introduction to basic professional and research issues in second language studies; integration of theory, research, and practice for prospective second or foreign language teachers and researchers.
SLS 600.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SLS 601.title: Language Concepts for Second Language Learning and Teaching
SLS 601.subject: SLS
SLS 601.description: Language analysis- phonology, syntax, semantics, discourse for teaching second languages.

SLS 610.title: Introduction to Teaching Second Languages
SLS 610.subject: SLS
SLS 610.description: Survey and analysis of second language teaching traditions and perspectives.
SLS 610.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SLS 611.title: Introduction to Second Language Assessment
SLS 611.subject: SLS
SLS 611.description: Assessment of second language knowledge and skills. Topics include design, use, and analysis of assessments. Graduate standing only or consent.

SLS 612.title: Alternative Approaches to Second Language Teaching
SLS 612.subject: SLS
SLS 612.description: Examination, comparison with conventional approaches; interpersonal relationships in language teaching.

SLS 613.title: Second Language Listening and Speaking
SLS 613.subject: SLS
SLS 613.description: Key issues; overview and critique of published materials; practice in developing syllabi and other materials.

SLS 614.title: Second Language Writing
SLS 614.subject: SLS
SLS 614.description: Problems in teaching second language composition. Survey materials; use, modification, and development. Error analysis.

SLS 618.title: Language and Learning Technologies
SLS 618.subject: SLS
SLS 618.description: A wide range of emerging technologies for language learning and research will be explored. Online/face-to-face discussions and hands-on experiential learning are integrated with learner’s goals, best practices, and theoretical foundations.

SLS 620.title: Second Language Reading
SLS 620.subject: SLS
SLS 620.description: Survey of research in reading process; teaching methodology; psycholinguistic investigations; comparison of reading in first and second languages.

SLS 630.title: Second Language Program Development
SLS 630.subject: SLS
SLS 630.description: Designing, implementing, and evaluating language programs; systems-based approach to program and curriculum development.

SLS 640.title: English Grammar
SLS 640.subject: SLS
SLS 640.description: Descriptive English grammar in relation to second language learning and teaching.

SLS 642.title: Comparative Grammar and Second Languages
SLS 642.subject: SLS
SLS 642.description: Comparative study of two or more languages. Consideration of language transfer in second language learning, role of typological features.

SLS 644.title: Multilingual/EL Pedagogy
SLS 644.subject: SLS
SLS 644.description: Examines practices, theories, research, and perspectives on multilingual/EL teaching approaches.
