Topics include culturally and linguistically responsive approaches, collaboration, lesson planning, and adapting materials to promote the growth and development of multilingual/ EL learners.

SLS 650.title: Second Language Acquisition
SLS 650.subject: SLS
SLS 650.description: Survey of theories and research on second language learning by children and adults, learning naturalistically and in formal settings. Relationships are explored between SLA research and language teaching.

SLS 660.title: Sociolinguistics and Second Languages
SLS 660.subject: SLS
SLS 660.description: Theoretical and applied aspects of language, culture, and society, and research methods in sociolinguistics, as they relate to second and foreign language issues.

SLS 664.title: Multilingual Multicultural Hawaiʻi
SLS 664.subject: SLS
SLS 664.description: Concepts, theories, policies, and practices of multilingual language use (spoken and written), supported by multicultural orientations and practices, within the contemporary context of Hawaiʻi as a society with substantial linguistic and cultural diversity.

SLS 670.title: Second Language Quantitative Research
SLS 670.subject: SLS
SLS 670.description: Quantitative research methods; design of research studies; techniques in collecting data; statistical inference; and analysis and interpretation of data.

SLS 671.title: Research in Language Testing
SLS 671.subject: SLS
SLS 671.description: Advanced issues in language testing research including recent developments in the following areas: language testing hypotheses, item analysis, reliability, dependability, and validity.

SLS 672.title: Second Language Classroom Research
SLS 672.subject: SLS
SLS 672.description: Survey of research on second language classrooms and analysis of methodological issues.

SLS 673.title: Applied Psycholinguistics and Second Language Acquisition
SLS 673.subject: SLS
SLS 673.description: Theory and research in psycholinguistics as related to second language perception, production, acquisition, and instruction.

SLS 674.title: Survey Research Methods in Second Language Studies
SLS 674.subject: SLS
SLS 674.description: Hands-on experience in language survey research including planning and creating survey instruments (both interviews and questionnaires), administering, compiling and analyzing survey data (quantitatively and qualitatively), and reporting the results.

SLS 675.title: Second Language Qualitative Research
SLS 675.subject: SLS
SLS 675.description: Philosophical and theoretical approaches, methodology, and ethics in second language qualitative research.

SLS 678.title: Discourse Analysis in Second Language Research
SLS 678.subject: SLS
SLS 678.description: Survey of approaches to discourse; microanalytic qualitative research; theory and methodology.

SLS 680E.title: Topics in Second Language Studies: second language learning
SLS 680E.subject: SLS
SLS 680E.description: Variable topics in special areas of second language studies: (E) second language learning; (N) second language analysis; (P) second language pedagogy; (R) second language research methodology; (U) second language use.
SLS 680E.prereq_raw: SLS 650 for (E); consent for (N) and (P); SLS 660 or consent for (U).

SLS 690.title: Second Language Teaching Practicum
SLS 690.subject: SLS
SLS 690.description: Student teaching in a language learning classroom.

SLS 695.title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
SLS 695.subject: SLS
SLS 695.prereq_raw: master’s Plan B or C candidate and consent.

SLS 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
SLS 699.subject: SLS
SLS 699.description: Individual reading in various fields of second language studies.

SLS 700.title: Thesis Research
SLS 700.subject: SLS
SLS 700.description: Individual research in the various fields of second language studies.

SLS 701.title: Professional Development in Second Language Studies
SLS 701.subject: SLS
SLS 701.description: Discipline-specific professional development for PhD students in SLS/Applied Linguistics; promotes understanding of expectations in PhD study; building of professional identity.

SLS 750.title: Seminar in Second Language Acquisition
SLS 750.subject: SLS
SLS 750.description: Issues in theory and research in second language acquisition of child and adult.

SLS 760.title: Seminar in Second Language Use
SLS 760.subject: SLS
SLS 760.description: Second language/dialect use in multilingual communities.

SLS 775.title: Seminar in Second Language Research
SLS 775.subject: SLS
SLS 775.description: Research methodologies in second language and multilingual contexts.

SLS 799.title: Apprenticeship in Teaching
SLS 799.subject: SLS
SLS 799.description: An experienced-based introduction to college-level teaching; graduate students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, and participation in planning and evaluation.
SLS 799.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

SLS 800.title: Dissertation Research
SLS 800.subject: SLS
SLS 800.description: One credit is necessary for dissertation writing.

SNSK 101.title: Introduction to Sanskrit I
SNSK 101.subject: SNSK
SNSK 101.description: Introduction to basic Sanskrit grammar; reading and analysis of progressively difficult classical texts.

SNSK 201.title: Intermediate Sanskrit I
SNSK 201.subject: SNSK
SNSK 201.description: Continuation of SNSK 102 . Reading and analysis of classical texts with review of grammar.

SNSK 381.title: Third-Level Sanskrit
SNSK 381.subject: SNSK
SNSK 381.description: Continuation of 282. Reading and analysis of various classical texts.

SNSK 382.title: Third-Level Sanskrit
SNSK 382.subject: SNSK
SNSK 382.description: Continuation of SNSK 381 . Introduction to Veda.

SNSK 481.title: Fourth-Level Sanskrit
SNSK 481.subject: SNSK
SNSK 481.description: Continuation of SNSK 382 . Reading, analysis, and interpretation of various Vedic or Sanskrit texts selected according to students’ interests.

SNSK 685.title: Advanced Readings in Sanskrit
SNSK 685.subject: SNSK
SNSK 685.description: Advanced study of Sanskrit literature (kâvya) and systematic thought (sâstra), alongside reading and discussion of scholarship on these topics. Specific content will change each semester.
SNSK 685.prereq_raw: intermediate-level SNSK (or equivalent). Contact instructor with questions.

SOC 100.title: Introduction to Sociology
SOC 100.subject: SOC
SOC 100.description: Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

SOC 100A.title: Introduction to Sociology
SOC 100A.subject: SOC
SOC 100A.description: Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

SOC 176.title: Introduction to Data Analysis
SOC 176.subject: SOC
SOC 176.description: Basic analytic skills widely used in quantitative analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, rates and probability, comparison of groups, introduction to causal relationships, and application of these techniques to real life examples.

SOC 180.title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
SOC 180.subject: SOC
SOC 180.description: Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawaiʻi and the Asia-Pacific region.

SOC 214.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
SOC 214.subject: SOC
SOC 214.description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

SOC 218.title: Introduction to Social Problems
SOC 218.subject: SOC
SOC 218.description: Theoretical and substantive survey of the nature and causes of social problems; selected types: poverty, inequality, deviance, etc.

SOC 230.title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
SOC 230.subject: SOC
SOC 230.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

SOC 231.title: Introduction to Juvenile Delinquency
SOC 231.subject: SOC
SOC 231.description: Forms of juvenile deviance; conditions and processes that result in alienation and deviance of youth. Juvenile corrections as institutionalized societal responses.

SOC 232.title: Introduction to the Sociology of Punishment
SOC 232.subject: SOC
SOC 232.description: Multiple social theories about different forms of formal and informal punishments and social control across different societies and times.

SOC 251.title: Introduction to Sociology of the Family
SOC 251.subject: SOC
SOC 251.description: Family patterns, mate selection, parent-child interaction, socialization of roles, legal sanctions, trends in organization, functions.

SOC 259.title: East Asian Popular Cultures
SOC 259.subject: SOC
SOC 259.description: East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective.

SOC 300.title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
SOC 300.subject: SOC
SOC 300.description: (3 Lec, 2 50-min Lab) Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics.

SOC 300A.title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
SOC 300A.subject: SOC
SOC 300A.description: (3 Lec, 2 50-min Lab) Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics. Restricted to students in the honors program and required for students taking the honors track in sociology.

SOC 301.title: Survey of Urban Sociology
SOC 301.subject: SOC
SOC 301.description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawaiʻi.

SOC 305.title: Women and Health
SOC 305.subject: SOC
SOC 305.description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
SOC 305.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or WGSS 202 , or POLS 110 ; or consent.

SOC 311.title: Survey of Social Inequality and Stratification
SOC 311.subject: SOC
SOC 311.description: Introduction to social stratification theory and research; definition and measurement of socioeconomic status; racial, ethnic and gender inequality; differences in lifestyles and life chances; social mobility.

SOC 313.title: Survey of Sociology of Work
SOC 313.subject: SOC
SOC 313.description: Work from viewpoint of individuals; meaningfulness versus productivity; how work, economics, and the industrial system affect individual goals.

SOC 316.title: Survey of Social Change
SOC 316.subject: SOC
SOC 316.description: Causes, processes, and effects of social change and movements, using a variety of cases in and outside the US. Develops written communication skills.

SOC 318.title: Women and Social Policy
SOC 318.subject: SOC
SOC 318.description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
SOC 318.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

SOC 321.title: Survey of Sociological Theory
SOC 321.subject: SOC
SOC 321.description: Major theorists and their influences, from Comte to today.

SOC 332.title: Sociology of Law
SOC 332.subject: SOC
SOC 332.description: Law as a political enforcement of the social order; how it is organized and operates; determinants of effectiveness; ways it adapts to and facilitates changing social conditions.

SOC 333.title: Criminology
SOC 333.subject: SOC
SOC 333.description: Concepts used in crime, law enforcement, criminal justice, and corrections. Types of criminal behavior; costs and effects of control.

SOC 335.title: Drugs and Society
SOC 335.subject: SOC
SOC 335.description: Use of mood- and mind-altering drugs in America among adults, youth, and cross-culturally. Illicit drug culture, psychedelics, and perception; social norms and deviant behavior.

SOC 336.title: Deviance and Social Control
SOC 336.subject: SOC
SOC 336.description: Interrelations of deviance, criminology, juvenile delinquency, corrections, social control, sociology of law. Key concepts, theories.

SOC 337.title: Criminal Justice Organizations
SOC 337.subject: SOC
SOC 337.description: Examines major criminal justice organizations-police, courts, and prisons. Using organizational theory, identifies the role of organizational goals, structure, resources, legitimacy, culture, and front-line workers in shaping criminal justice policy and practice.
SOC 337.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent.

SOC 341.title: Survey of Social Psychology
SOC 341.subject: SOC
SOC 341.description: Major principles; social attitudes, theories of conformity and change, person perception and attribution theory, social role, role conflict and role behavior, group structure, and behavior.

SOC 344.title: Sociology of Happiness in Unsettled Times
SOC 344.subject: SOC
SOC 344.description: Combines theoretical, scientific and ‘hands-on’ learning to explore how happiness and well-being can be cultivated, even in this challenging era of extreme global climate events.

SOC 352.title: Survey of Sociology of Education
SOC 352.subject: SOC
SOC 352.description: Formal education as one aspect of socialization. Emphasis on the American system; including business, military, and religious institutions’ role in educating people. Significant time will be spent practicing and developing writing skills.

SOC 353.title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
SOC 353.subject: SOC
SOC 353.description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research.

SOC 354.title: Survey of Medical Sociology
SOC 354.subject: SOC
SOC 354.description: Social factors in disease and treatment; illness behavior, roles of patients and healers; nature of healing professions; use of medical services; alternative systems of medical organization.

SOC 356.title: Chinese Society and Culture
SOC 356.subject: SOC
SOC 356.description: Social institutions, family, community, education, stratification, government, economy; impact of modernization and revolution on their contemporary transformation.

SOC 357.title: Japanese Society and Culture
SOC 357.subject: SOC
SOC 357.description: Persistence and change in economy, policy, religion, education, family, and other institutions of modern Japan.

SOC 358.title: Sociology of Korea
SOC 358.subject: SOC
SOC 358.description: Social institutions, family, education, religion, cultural values, social classes, economic development, social movements, gender relations, North-South relations, and unification issues.
SOC 358.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

SOC 362.title: Sociology of Gender
SOC 362.subject: SOC
SOC 362.description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
SOC 362.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

SOC 367.title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
SOC 367.subject: SOC
SOC 367.description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
SOC 367.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or consent.

SOC 374.title: Law, Politics and Society
SOC 374.subject: SOC
SOC 374.description: Relationships between law, politics, and society will be explored. Emphasis is placed on several dimensions of legality: legal “indeterminacy” and some of the many things that law does for us and to us; law’s response to violence; the connections between law and social change; access to the law and its sociological dimensions; how/why law fails and what happens when it does.
SOC 374.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200 level SOC course, or a 100 level or 200 level POLS course, or consent.

SOC 394.title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
SOC 394.subject: SOC
SOC 394.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues.
SOC 394.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

SOC 400.title: Food, Body, and Women: Analysis of Biopolitics
SOC 400.subject: SOC
SOC 400.description: Explores how food, body, and other “matter of life” are imbedded in biopolitics from the feminist perspectives.
SOC 400.prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or consent.

SOC 401.title: Analysis in Urban Sociology
SOC 401.subject: SOC
SOC 401.description: Urbanization in developed and developing countries, the rural-urban continuum, structure and process of metropolitan regions, theories of urban location and growth, housing and urban renewal.

SOC 411.title: Analysis in Social Stratification
SOC 411.subject: SOC
SOC 411.description: Approaches to research in social inequality: community studies; historical and cross-cultural analyses of poverty, working class, middle class, power structure, social mobility, etc.

SOC 412.title: Analysis in Population and Society
SOC 412.subject: SOC
SOC 412.description: Global and U.S. patterns of population growth; composition and distribution, elementary demographic techniques; development issues and population policy.

SOC 413.title: Economy and Society
SOC 413.subject: SOC
SOC 413.description: Study of the dominant trend of economic change and its impact on society; globalization of economic activities and transformation of industrial society to postindustrial one; corporate restructuring and downsizing and their impact on employment and income distribution; gender relations in workplaces; the impact of globalization on the newly industrializing countries.

SOC 415.title: Technology and Society
SOC 415.subject: SOC
SOC 415.description: Nature of technology, social forces that affect its adoption; impact on society; innovation.

SOC 418.title: Gender and Work
SOC 418.subject: SOC
SOC 418.description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
SOC 418.prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or one 300-level WGSS or ES course; or consent.

SOC 419.title: Organizations and Society
SOC 419.subject: SOC
SOC 419.description: Schools, hospitals, industries, prisons, and government agencies analyzed in terms of self-actualization, alienation, human relations, communication, leadership, organizational conflicts.

SOC 431.title: Advanced Criminology & Delinquency
SOC 431.subject: SOC
SOC 431.description: Advanced topics related to crime, juvenile delinquency, and criminal justice explored sociologically.

SOC 432.title: Punishment & Society
SOC 432.subject: SOC
SOC 432.description: Institutions, organizations, and individuals charged with carrying out punishment in the criminal justice system and beyond.

SOC 433.title: Analysis in Law and Social Change
SOC 433.subject: SOC
SOC 433.description: Interrelationships between legal orders and other social institutions; use of “law” to change major status relationships, e.g., boss-worker, woman-man, child-adult.

SOC 435.title: Women and Crime
SOC 435.subject: SOC
SOC 435.description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
SOC 435.prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

SOC 438.title: Prisons
SOC 438.subject: SOC
SOC 438.description: Prisons, jails, and other detention facilities across historical, social, and/or international contexts.

SOC 441.title: Social Structure and the Individual
SOC 441.subject: SOC
SOC 441.description: Effects of social institutions on individuals. Role of socioeconomic status, cultural background, family structure, peer group, schools, and occupational roles in socialization.

SOC 445.title: Analysis in Gender Violence
SOC 445.subject: SOC
SOC 445.description: Historical and structural theories of gender-based violence, including domestic and sexual abuse, prostitution, trafficking, cross-cultural perspectives, social policy and practices. Junior standing or graduate standing only.

SOC 446.title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
SOC 446.subject: SOC
SOC 446.description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
SOC 446.prereq_raw: SOC 300 , WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

SOC 451.title: Analysis in Marriage and the Family
SOC 451.subject: SOC
SOC 451.description: Theory and methods of studying social interaction in marriage and the family; examination of marriage, mating, love, and choice. Empirical research emphasizing Hawaiʻi.

SOC 452.title: Marriage and Family: A Feminist Perspective
SOC 452.subject: SOC
SOC 452.description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
SOC 452.prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

SOC 453.title: Analysis in Sociology of Aging
SOC 453.subject: SOC
SOC 453.description: Social and research issues significant to delivery of long-term care services to the elderly; cost, quality, availability of services, evaluation of programs, role of family, formal and informal care services.

SOC 454.title: Analysis in Medical Sociology
SOC 454.subject: SOC
SOC 454.description: Application of sociological theories and concepts to medical social situations and behavior; problems of obtaining data for research.

SOC 455.title: Sociology of Religion
SOC 455.subject: SOC
SOC 455.description: Seminar in research on sociological aspects of religious sectarianism; attention to Hawaiʻi.

SOC 456.title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawaiʻi
SOC 456.subject: SOC
SOC 456.description: Historical and contemporary social processes involved in race, racism, and inter-ethnic relations in Hawaiʻi. Focus on intersection of Asian and/or Pacific Island cultures with Native Hawaiian culture.
SOC 456.prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent.

SOC 457.title: Sociology of the Arts
SOC 457.subject: SOC
SOC 457.description: Relation of art to society; role of artist, audience, critic, patron, museum; Western and other societies; attitudes toward new styles.

SOC 458.title: Analysis in Sports and Society
SOC 458.subject: SOC
SOC 458.description: Critical perspectives on sports and society. Topics include power and inequality; mobility, status, and economics; youth development; globalization; gender; and violence in sports and the wider society.

SOC 459.title: Popular Culture
SOC 459.subject: SOC
SOC 459.description: Popular culture as manifested in film, sports, TV, comics, magazines, etc.; relation to sociological theories and studies.

SOC 475.title: Analysis in Survey Research
SOC 475.subject: SOC
SOC 475.description: Survey research design and analysis, including theory selection instrument construction, sampling techniques, data collection, computerized data analysis, and writing up research reports of the findings.

SOC 476.title: Social Statistics
SOC 476.subject: SOC
SOC 476.description: Common statistical procedures emphasizing univariate and bivariate description; some attention to multivariate techniques and statistical inference, within context of research procedures.

SOC 476L.title: Social Statistics Laboratory
SOC 476L.subject: SOC
SOC 476L.description: Required lab for computer applications for analysis of sociological data.

SOC 478.title: Analysis in Field Research Methods
SOC 478.subject: SOC
SOC 478.description: Techniques for collecting and analyzing qualitative data. Participant observation; small groups in natural settings; community studies. Grounded theory; theories of everyday life; reality construction.

SOC 491.title: Discussion Group Leader-Freshman Seminar
SOC 491.subject: SOC
SOC 491.description: A unique opportunity for students to gain leadership, teaching, and public speaking skills as a SOC 100 leader for a section of 10 freshmen students while being mentored weekly by a faculty course coordinator.

SOC 492.title: Politics of Multiculturalism
SOC 492.subject: SOC
SOC 492.description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
SOC 492.prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent.

SOC 494.title: Social Sciences Internship
SOC 494.subject: SOC
SOC 494.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester;

SOC 495.title: Topics in Sociology
SOC 495.subject: SOC
SOC 495.description: Topics course that explore current issues and try new ideas.

SOC 496.title: Topics in Sociology: Student Projects
SOC 496.subject: SOC
SOC 496.description: Students create their own study group and solicit an advisor from faculty. Consult department for assistance.

SOC 600.title: Professional Development Seminar
SOC 600.subject: SOC
SOC 600.description: Introduces sociology as a professional field. Provides skills for successful graduate degree completion, building a research agenda, preparing work for publication, and navigating the employment market for sociologists.
SOC 600.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Sociology majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 605.title: Statistics for Regression Analysis
SOC 605.subject: SOC
SOC 605.description: Dealing with the multiple linear regression and logistic regression models, focusing on modeling, i.e., specification of the explanatory variables to answer different research questions. Emphasis on applications using statistical package programs. SOC 605L is required.

SOC 605L.title: Regression Analysis Laboratory
SOC 605L.subject: SOC
SOC 605L.description: Lab for computer analysis skills is required for students taking SOC 605 .

SOC 606.title: Research Methods and Design
SOC 606.subject: SOC
SOC 606.description: Emphasis on theory selection, theory construction, and choice of research strategies.

SOC 607.title: Seminar in Methods of Content Analysis
SOC 607.subject: SOC
SOC 607.description: Content analysis combines quantitative and qualitative methods to analyze text systematically. Covers sampling and case selection; manual and computer-assisted methods of coding and analyzing textual data; writing reports using content analysis data.

SOC 608.title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
SOC 608.subject: SOC
SOC 608.description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

SOC 609.title: Seminar Qualitative Research
SOC 609.subject: SOC
SOC 609.description: Advanced seminar on conducting fieldwork in natural social settings with emphasis on qualitative techniques, political and ethical considerations, data management and assessment, interpretation and reflexive writing.

SOC 611.title: Classical Sociological Theory
SOC 611.subject: SOC
SOC 611.description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociological theory from 19th-century to the 1960s, including intellectual contexts and historical development.
SOC 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 612.title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
SOC 612.subject: SOC
SOC 612.description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociology theory from the 1960s to the present, including intellectual contexts and historical development.
SOC 612.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 613.title: Organizational Analysis
SOC 613.subject: SOC
SOC 613.description: Theoretical approaches to organizations; organizational structure and process; organizational pathologies and effectiveness; the organization and its environment.

SOC 615.title: Medical Sociology
SOC 615.subject: SOC
SOC 615.description: Covers the major paradigms in medical sociology for analyzing social epidemiology, the political economy of health systems, health service organizations, health and wellness behaviors, illness perception and help-seeking, doctor-patient interaction, and adaptations to illness.
SOC 615.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 616.title: Seminar in Stress and Health
SOC 616.subject: SOC
SOC 616.description: Analysis of current theory and empirical research on relationship of stress and health; sociological, psychological, and community psychiatry models and current issues.

SOC 617.title: Sociology of Mental Health and Illness
SOC 617.subject: SOC
SOC 617.description: Examines sociological research and theories about mental health and illness. A key question in medical sociology will be addressed: What is the relationship between society and mental health?

SOC 620.title: Seminar in Social Stratification
SOC 620.subject: SOC
SOC 620.description: Classical theories of social class, contemporary developments; crucial research issues, appropriate methodologies.
SOC 620.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Classified graduate students only.

SOC 625.title: Feminist Criminology
SOC 625.subject: SOC
SOC 625.description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

SOC 631.title: Seminar in Criminology
SOC 631.subject: SOC
SOC 631.description: Major current theories, history of their development, elaborations of typologies, implications for treatment modalities.

SOC 632.title: Criminal Justice System
SOC 632.subject: SOC
SOC 632.description: Examination of the criminal justice system; the exercise of discretion and limits placed upon it.

SOC 638.title: American Punishment
SOC 638.subject: SOC
SOC 638.description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex.
SOC 638.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 651.title: Introduction to Human Population
SOC 651.subject: SOC
SOC 651.description: Comparative analysis of quantitative and qualitative aspects of population; factors affecting size, distribution, and composition; impact of population size and composition on society.

SOC 659.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
SOC 659.subject: SOC
SOC 659.description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

SOC 660.title: Teaching Seminar
SOC 660.subject: SOC
SOC 660.description: Examines research on teaching, learning, and ethics, as well as practical skills for teaching at the university level. Syllabi and teaching philosophies are developed, which are useful for the academic job market.
SOC 660.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

SOC 670.title: Sociology of Sustainability
SOC 670.subject: SOC
SOC 670.description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives.
SOC 670.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 701.title: Seminar in Evaluation Research
SOC 701.subject: SOC
SOC 701.description: Research design, data collection, field problems and analysis in the evaluation of social programs. Examples from criminal justice, corrections, drug treatment, mental health, and public health.

SOC 705.title: Advanced Statistics
SOC 705.subject: SOC
SOC 705.description: Dealing with advanced statistical methods beyond multiple linear regression, such as logit, event history analysis, and multi-level analysis. Emphasis is on applications of the techniques to social science research.

SOC 706.title: Cultural Analysis
SOC 706.subject: SOC
SOC 706.description: Contemporary issues in cultural sociology, covering key theoretical perspectives, analytic methods and substantive areas for empirical research.

SOC 711.title: Seminar in Sociology of Knowledge
SOC 711.subject: SOC
SOC 711.description: Sociological theory applied to bases of knowledge in everyday life, professional communities, and the sciences. Research and theory-building activities of sociologists; ethnomethodology; construction of social structure, culture, and consciousness.

SOC 715.title: Seminar in Current Issues in Sociology
SOC 715.subject: SOC
SOC 715.description: Substantive areas that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other courses.

SOC 716.title: Advanced Medical Sociology
SOC 716.subject: SOC
SOC 716.description: Application of theoretical paradigms and methodologies to the examination of selected research topics in the field of medical sociology.

SOC 718.title: Seminar in Aging, Culture, and Health
SOC 718.subject: SOC
SOC 718.description: Overview of the major theories, perspectives, and empirical findings relating to aging in various cultural contexts.
SOC 718.prereq_raw: SOC 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.
SOC 718.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SOC, PSY, NURS, SW, PH majors only.

SOC 719.title: Comparative Family and Gender
SOC 719.subject: SOC
SOC 719.description: Discusses the major perspectives on family and gender relations and examines related empirical research. Emphasis is on the cross-cultural comparisons across the U.S. and Asia in the context of globalizing economies and cultures.

SOC 720.title: Comparative Study of East Asia
SOC 720.subject: SOC
SOC 720.description: Comparative analysis of social organization, social processes, and change of both capitalist and communist countries of East Asia, with each other and other areas of the world.

SOC 721.title: Social Change—Pacific Islands
SOC 721.subject: SOC
SOC 721.description: Analysis of social change; transformation from subsistence societies to commodified, wage-labor societies with participation in world economy.

SOC 722.title: Modern Japanese Society
SOC 722.subject: SOC
SOC 722.description: Social and behavioral studies of Japanese values, social organization, and personality development. Problems of value conflict, political protest, world role, tradition, and social change.

SOC 723.title: Seminar in Modern Chinese Society
SOC 723.subject: SOC
SOC 723.description: Developmental policies, social change, and impact on modern Chinese social institutions. Includes China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. May include social and demographic change, population, social stratification, gender, and family problems.

SOC 725B.title: Seminar in Race and Ethnicity: anti-racism studies
SOC 725B.subject: SOC
SOC 725B.description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.
SOC 725B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 725C.title: Seminar in Race and Ethnicity: ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict
SOC 725C.subject: SOC
SOC 725C.description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.
SOC 725C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 725D.title: Seminar in Race and Ethnicity: race, place, and inequity
SOC 725D.subject: SOC
SOC 725D.description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.
SOC 725D.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 730.title: Conflict Analysis/Resolution
SOC 730.subject: SOC
SOC 730.description: Seminar on the analysis of conflict resolution. Faculty from law, planning, political science and guest practitioners will present multidisciplinary analysis and intervention strategies on contemporary conflicts.
SOC 730.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 741.title: Seminar in Social Structure and the Individual
SOC 741.subject: SOC
SOC 741.description: Intensive study and individual research projects in a selected topic. Theoretical and methodological issues in relating social and individual levels of analysis. Recommended: SOC 612 .

SOC 750.title: Seminar in Social Movements
SOC 750.subject: SOC
SOC 750.description: Study of sociology of social movements, plus independent student research.

SOC 751.title: Development in Asia
SOC 751.subject: SOC
SOC 751.description: Theories and available research methods examined for applicability to developing areas; specific examples from Asia.
SOC 751.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SOC 753.title: Urban Sociology
SOC 753.subject: SOC
SOC 753.description: Demographic trends in urban growth: nature and dimensions of urbanization and urbanism; ancient, American, and Third World cities; ecological theories of urban growth; lifestyles.

SOCS 101.title: First Year Experience
SOCS 101.subject: SOCS
SOCS 101.description: Brings together topics, discussion, and peer support to increase success at UH Mānoa and the College of Social Sciences. The emphasis is on knowledge, skills, and behaviors leading to graduation and sharing the first-year experience.

SOCS 124.title: Leadership and Social Issues
SOCS 124.subject: SOCS
SOCS 124.description: Fosters understanding of key societal and community issues, social science perspectives on them, the qualities of effective leadership, and invites examination of personal responsibilities, intentions, and abilities to make a difference on those issues.

SOCS 150.title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
SOCS 150.subject: SOCS
SOCS 150.description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

SOCS 150A.title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
SOCS 150A.subject: SOCS
SOCS 150A.description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

SOCS 225.title: Statistical Analysis for Social Sciences
SOCS 225.subject: SOCS
SOCS 225.description: Statistical reasoning in the analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, inference measures of association, decomposition of variance, and regression analysis. Lab required.
SOCS 225.prereq_raw: any 100 level social science course or consent.

SOCS 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
SOCS 251.subject: SOCS
SOCS 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

SOCS 270.title: Introduction to Digital Media for the Social Sciences
SOCS 270.subject: SOCS
SOCS 270.description: Incorporates hands on instruction for creating informational media content, to include learning how to use camera and sound equipment, learning how to edit and create graphics, and learning presentation techniques.
SOCS 270.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SOCS 370.title: Intermediate Digital Media and Production
SOCS 370.subject: SOCS
SOCS 370.description: Focus on theoretical and practical methods for media design and production of high-quality creative digital content. Emphasis on social media strategies and oral communication skills to attract mass online audiences.
SOCS 370.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

SOCS 385.title: Social Sciences Service Learning and Micro Internship
SOCS 385.subject: SOCS
SOCS 385.description: For students undertaking service-learning or micro-internship options separately or for another class. Discussions and research related to learning experiences and issues encountered while in the field.

SOCS 396.title: Pilina: Topics in Indigenous Social Sciences
SOCS 396.subject: SOCS
SOCS 396.description: Explores pilina (relationship, connection) of selected topics and issues of interest in the social sciences through Indigenous voices, perspectives, and scholarship.

SOCS 470.title: Advanced Digital Media for Social, Cultural, and Community Engagement
SOCS 470.subject: SOCS
SOCS 470.description: Advanced digital media techniques for creating high-quality video content that promotes social, cultural, and community engagement. Focus on writing and oral skills with emphasis on visual storytelling and distribution on broadcast and social media platforms.
SOCS 470.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

SOCS 489.title: Social Sciences Internship
SOCS 489.subject: SOCS
SOCS 489.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester;

SOCS 601.title: Topics in Teaching Innovations
SOCS 601.subject: SOCS
SOCS 601.description: Examination and critical analysis of contemporary curriculum and instruction issues in social sciences. Concepts, theories, principles underlying active learning, critical thinking, values inquiry, assessment, and multidisciplinary approaches to integration of knowledge.

SOCS 735.title: Ocean Policy and Management
SOCS 735.subject: SOCS
SOCS 735.description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

SPAN 103.title: Intensive Elementary Spanish
SPAN 103.subject: SPAN
SPAN 103.description: Course content of SPAN 101 and SPAN 102 covered in one semester. Three two-hour sessions per week.

SPAN 201.title: Intermediate Spanish I
SPAN 201.subject: SPAN
SPAN 201.description: Continuation of oral practice and grammar study; increasing emphasis on reading and written composition. Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 201 and SPAN 258 .

SPAN 202.title: Intermediate Spanish II
SPAN 202.subject: SPAN
SPAN 202.description: Continuation of SPAN 201 . Oral practice and grammar study; increasing emphasis on reading and written composition. Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 202 and SPAN 259 .

SPAN 203.title: Intensive Spanish for Business
SPAN 203.subject: SPAN
SPAN 203.description: SPAN 201 and SPAN 202 content combined, oriented to business Spanish. Three 50-minute sessions per week plus online work.

SPAN 258.title: Intermediate Spanish Abroad I
SPAN 258.subject: SPAN
SPAN 258.description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the second-year level in Spanish language and culture in a Spanish-speaking country. Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 201 and SPAN 258.

SPAN 259.title: Intermediate Spanish Abroad II
SPAN 259.subject: SPAN
SPAN 259.description: Continuation of SPAN 258 . Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 202 and SPAN 259.

SPAN 300.title: Legends, Stories, and Current Events
SPAN 300.subject: SPAN
SPAN 300.description: Development of language skills through reading of literary and cultural texts.
SPAN 300.prereq_raw: SPAN 202 (or concurrent) or SPAN 203 or SPAN 259 .

SPAN 301.title: Language and Writing I
SPAN 301.subject: SPAN
SPAN 301.description: Improvement of Spanish vocabulary, language accuracy, and expression of ideas in Spanish through writing.
SPAN 301.prereq_raw: SPAN 202 or SPAN 203 or SPAN 259 , or consent.

SPAN 303.title: Conversation I
SPAN 303.subject: SPAN
SPAN 303.description: Intensive practice in spoken Spanish, focusing on the preparation and completion of oral tasks and presentations. Not open to (near)-native speakers.

SPAN 305.title: Introduction to Spanish-English Translation
SPAN 305.subject: SPAN
SPAN 305.description: Practical introduction to written Spanish-English translation through the translations of texts from Spanish to English and the reverse. Includes an emphasis on composition and style.

SPAN 306B.title: Spanish in Use: marketing
SPAN 306B.subject: SPAN
SPAN 306B.description: Spanish language as used in specific professions; (B) marketing, tourism & business; (C) health & public safety. Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 306C.title: Spanish in Use: health & public safety
SPAN 306C.subject: SPAN
SPAN 306C.description: Spanish language as used in specific professions; (B) marketing, tourism & business; (C) health & public safety. Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 308.title: Introduction to Spanish-English Interpreting
SPAN 308.subject: SPAN
SPAN 308.description: Students will begin to develop the listening and memory skills for direct and inverse interpretation. Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 320.title: From Comics to Classics
SPAN 320.subject: SPAN
SPAN 320.description: Introduction and development of Spanish skills for critical reading and writing, rhetoric, and vocabulary. Choices with particular emphasis on literary analysis and academic writing.

SPAN 330.title: Phonetics and Pronunciation Practice
SPAN 330.subject: SPAN
SPAN 330.description: Analysis of the Spanish phonological system, in contrast with English. Practice in pronunciation.

SPAN 351.title: Spain: Traditions & Trending
SPAN 351.subject: SPAN
SPAN 351.description: Survey of the history and cultures of Spain.

SPAN 352B.title: Latin American Cultural Studies: empires and traditions
SPAN 352B.subject: SPAN
SPAN 352B.description: Survey of the history, traditions, and cultures of Latin America; (B) empires and traditions; (C) nations, identity & the arts.

SPAN 352C.title: Latin American Cultural Studies: nations, identity & the arts
SPAN 352C.subject: SPAN
SPAN 352C.description: Survey of the history, traditions, and cultures of Latin America; (B) empires and traditions; (C) nations, identity & the arts.

SPAN 358.title: Third-Level Spanish Abroad
SPAN 358.subject: SPAN
SPAN 358.description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in Spanish language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a Spanish-speaking country.

SPAN 360.title: Intensive Third-Level Spanish Abroad
SPAN 360.subject: SPAN
SPAN 360.description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in Spanish language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a Spanish-speaking country.

SPAN 361B.title: Reading Spain: heroines, knights, witches
SPAN 361B.subject: SPAN
SPAN 361B.description: Reading and discussion of narratives from and about Spain; (B) heroines, knights, witches; (C) love, loss, liberty.
SPAN 361B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 361C.title: Reading Spain: love, loss, liberty
SPAN 361C.subject: SPAN
SPAN 361C.description: Reading and discussion of narratives from and about Spain; (B) heroines, knights, witches; (C) love, loss, liberty.
SPAN 361C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 371B.title: Reading Latin America: warriors, nuns, and rebels
SPAN 371B.subject: SPAN
SPAN 371B.description: Culture and history of Spanish America through literature; (B) warriors, nuns, and rebels; (C) the magical and the real.
SPAN 371B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 371C.title: Reading Latin America: the magical and the real
SPAN 371C.subject: SPAN
SPAN 371C.description: Culture and history of Spanish America through literature; (B) warriors, nuns, and rebels; (C) the magical and the real.
SPAN 371C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SPAN 396.title: Introduction to Hispanic Film
SPAN 396.subject: SPAN
SPAN 396.description: Introduction to the study and analysis of genres, techniques, and cinematic styles as used in Hispanic film.

SPAN 399.title: Directed Reading
SPAN 399.subject: SPAN
SPAN 399.description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision.
SPAN 399.prereq_raw: SPAN 301 (or concurrent), consent and departmental approval.

SPAN 400.title: Spanish Language in Society
SPAN 400.subject: SPAN
SPAN 400.description: Explores issues in Spanish language in society (media, communication, advertising, government, technology). Introduces and examines current sociolinguistic and sociopragmatic issues.

SPAN 403.title: Building Advanced Fluency
SPAN 403.subject: SPAN
SPAN 403.description: Advanced practice; emphasis on building active vocabulary.

SPAN 405.title: Spanish-English Translation
SPAN 405.subject: SPAN
SPAN 405.description: Factors in the art of translation. Practice in translating material from Spanish to English and the reverse. Includes an emphasis on composition and style.

SPAN 451.title: Historical Spanish Linguistics
SPAN 451.subject: SPAN
SPAN 451.description: Evolution of Spanish from Latin; modern social and geographical dialects.

SPAN 452.title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics
SPAN 452.subject: SPAN
SPAN 452.description: Analysis of morphology, syntax, and semantics.

SPAN 458.title: Fourth-Level Spanish Abroad
SPAN 458.subject: SPAN
SPAN 458.description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the fourth-year level in Spanish linguistics, civilization, culture, and literature in a Spanish-speaking country.
SPAN 458.prereq_raw: any two of SPAN 301 ; SPAN 303 , SPAN 358 , SPAN 359 , or SPAN 360 .

SPAN 460.title: Intensive Fourth-Level Spanish Abroad
SPAN 460.subject: SPAN
SPAN 460.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-year level in Spanish language and culture in a Spanish-speaking country. For semester programs only.

SPAN 477.title: U.S. Latino Literature
SPAN 477.subject: SPAN
SPAN 477.description: Study of the literature of U.S. Hispanics written in Spanish or bilingually.

SPAN 478.title: Hispanic Women’s Literature
SPAN 478.subject: SPAN
SPAN 478.description: Women’s literary and cultural expressions in Latin America and Spain.

SPAN 480.title: Spanish & Latin American Theater
SPAN 480.subject: SPAN
SPAN 480.description: Study of representative authors and plays from Spain and Latin America.

SPAN 495B.title: Topics in Hispanic Scholarship: literature and society
SPAN 495B.subject: SPAN
SPAN 495B.description: Hispanic authors, periods, or themes. (B) literature and society; (D) literature and film.

SPAN 495D.title: Topics in Hispanic Scholarship: literature and film
SPAN 495D.subject: SPAN
SPAN 495D.description: Hispanic authors, periods, or themes. (B) literature and society; (D) literature and film.

SPAN 496.title: Studies in Latin American and Iberian Film
SPAN 496.subject: SPAN
SPAN 496.description: Intensive study of selected topics in Latin American and/or Iberian cinemas; e.g. national or regional cinemas, periods, movements or issues, major filmmakers, film theory and criticism.

SPAN 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
SPAN 499.subject: SPAN

SPAN 499.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and departmental approval.

SPAN 605.title: Spanish Translation Studies
SPAN 605.subject: SPAN

SPAN 659.prereq_raw: Spanish Proficiency assessment: B- (CERFL) or Advanced low (ACTFL).

SPAN 660.title: Medieval Spanish Literature
SPAN 660.subject: SPAN
SPAN 660.description: Representative readings in prose and poetry, from origins through 15th century.
SPAN 660.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 665B.title: Golden Age Literature: theater

SPAN 665B.description: Spanish literature from the 16th and 17th centuries. (B) theater; (C) prose; (D) poetry; (E) Cervantes.

SPAN 665C.title: Golden Age Literature: prose

SPAN 665C.description: Spanish literature from the 16th and 17th centuries. (B) theater; (C) prose; (D) poetry; (E) Cervantes.

SPAN 665D.title: Golden Age Literature: poetry
SPAN 665D.subject: SPAN
SPAN 665D.description: Spanish literature from the 16th and 17th centuries. (B) theater; (C) prose; (D) poetry; (E) Cervantes.

SPAN 665E.title: Golden Age Literature: Cervantes
SPAN 665E.subject: SPAN
SPAN 665E.description: Spanish literature from the 16th and 17th centuries. (B) theater; (C) prose; (D) poetry; (E) Cervantes.

SPAN 669.title: 19th-Century Spanish Realism
SPAN 669.subject: SPAN
SPAN 669.description: Nineteenth-century Spanish realism in the novel. Authors include Galdós, Clarin, Alarcón, Pardo Bazán, Blasco- Ibáñez, Valera.
SPAN 669.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 670B.title: 20th-Century Spanish Literature: generation of 1898
SPAN 670B.subject: SPAN
SPAN 670B.description: Representative works from 20th-century literature. Genres: poetry, theater, essay, novel. (B) generation of 1898; (C) pre-Civil War; (D) post-Civil War.
SPAN 670B.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 670C.title: 20th-Century Spanish Literature: pre-Civil War
SPAN 670C.subject: SPAN
SPAN 670C.description: Representative works from 20th-century literature. Genres: poetry, theater, essay, novel. (B) generation of 1898; (C) pre-Civil War; (D) post-Civil War.
SPAN 670C.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 670D.title: 20th-Century Spanish Literature: post-Civil War
SPAN 670D.subject: SPAN
SPAN 670D.description: Representative works from 20th-century literature. Genres: poetry, theater, essay, novel. (B) generation of 1898; (C) pre-Civil War; (D) post-Civil War.
SPAN 670D.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 680.title: Spanish-American Novel

SPAN 680.description: Critical analysis of major Spanish-American novels.
SPAN 680.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 681.title: Colonial Spanish-American Literature
SPAN 681.subject: SPAN
SPAN 681.description: Spanish-American literature from period of discovery to independence. Representative authors such as Sor Juana, Bernal Díaz del Castillo.
SPAN 681.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 682.title: Spanish-American Poetry
SPAN 682.subject: SPAN
SPAN 682.description: Study of representative poets from all periods: Martí, Darió, Mistral, Guillén, Neruda, Paz, etc.
SPAN 682.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 683.title: Spanish-American Short Story and Essay
SPAN 683.subject: SPAN
SPAN 683.description: Study of representative writers from various periods: Sor Juana, Palma, Quiroga, Reyes, Borges, etc.
SPAN 683.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPAN 695.title: Seminar in Hispanic Literature
SPAN 695.subject: SPAN
SPAN 695.description: A period, author, genre, or region.
SPAN 695.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SPED 201.title: Disability and Diversity in the Media
SPED 201.subject: SPED
SPED 201.description: Explores the changing disability experience as described in contemporary film, literature, advertising, news, sports and dialogue with persons with disabilities in the Pacific region and around the world.

SPED 202.title: Global and Historical Perspectives of Disability in the Media
SPED 202.subject: SPED
SPED 202.description: Explores the history of disability representation across cultures. Emphasis is placed on examining evolving perceptions of disability as depicted in art, literature, print, film, and digital media.

SPED 304.title: Foundations of Inclusive Schooling
SPED 304.subject: SPED
SPED 304.description: Foundations of “special education” exploring philosophies, diverse and historical viewpoints, laws, and service delivery. Students reflect upon texts, films and interviews with persons with disabilities, their families and professionals to understand the culture of disability.

SPED 306.title: Special Education Law and Compliance
SPED 306.subject: SPED
SPED 306.description: Analysis of legislation, litigation, and administrative rulings in special education, with an emphasis on teaching expository writing and developing legally sound policies/procedures that ensure educationally meaningful and legally correct education for students with disabilities.

SPED 310.title: Introduction to Special Education Assessment
SPED 310.subject: SPED
SPED 310.description: Assessment methods and techniques to inform special education decisions, including the use of standardized assessments for initial eligibility, reevaluations, and annual reviews for special education services.

SPED 311.title: Introduction to Specialized Instruction
SPED 311.subject: SPED
SPED 311.description: Characteristics and educational programming for students with disabilities. Role and responsibilities of the special educator, founding principles and current practices in special education with an emphasis on teaching writing.

SPED 315.title: Field Experience - ECE
SPED 315.subject: SPED
SPED 315.description: Supervised field experience in an early childhood setting. Minimum of 2 full days per week in classrooms, plus mandatory seminar with UH Mānoa field supervisor. Taken concurrently with education classes.

SPED 332.title: Young Children with Communication Needs
SPED 332.subject: SPED
SPED 332.description: Communication development of infants and young children, ages birth through age 8, with and without disabilities. Assessment and intervention to support the development of communication skills in inclusive community and school environments.

SPED 390B.title: Student Teaching in Special Education: elementary/special education
SPED 390B.subject: SPED
SPED 390B.description: Supervised student teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe autism); supervision provided by master teacher and university supervisor with emphasis on writing instruction. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.
SPED 390B.coreq_raw: SPED 391B for (B); SPED 391C for (C); SPED 391D for (D).

SPED 390C.title: Student Teaching in Special Education: early childhood education/special education
SPED 390C.subject: SPED
SPED 390C.description: Supervised student teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe autism); supervision provided by master teacher and university supervisor with emphasis on writing instruction. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.
SPED 390C.coreq_raw: SPED 391B for (B); SPED 391C for (C); SPED 391D for (D).

SPED 390D.title: Student Teaching in Special Education: unclassified
SPED 390D.subject: SPED
SPED 390D.description: Supervised student teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe autism); supervision provided by master teacher and university supervisor with emphasis on writing instruction. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.
SPED 390D.coreq_raw: SPED 391B for (B); SPED 391C for (C); SPED 391D for (D).

SPED 391B.title: Seminar for Student Teachers in Special Education: elementary/special education
SPED 391B.subject: SPED
SPED 391B.description: Seminar relating current educational theories with experiences; includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.
SPED 391B.prereq_raw: requirements for registration listed under “student teaching.”

SPED 392.subject: SPED

SPED 392.prereq_raw: requirements for registration listed under “Student Teaching,” approval of review committee and consent.
