SPED 400B.title: Field Training in Special Education: First Semester
SPED 400B.subject: SPED
SPED 400B.description: Students participate in classroom settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by department field supervisor; (B) first semester; (C) second semester, with ethical issues in education discussed and applied in field settings; (D) third semester, with emphasis on writing and oral communication for application in field settings.
SPED 400B.prereq_raw: SPED 304 (or concurrent) or consent for (B); SPED 400B for (C); SPED 400C for (D).

SPED 400C.title: Field Training in Special Education: Second Semester
SPED 400C.subject: SPED
SPED 400C.description: Students participate in classroom settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by department field supervisor; (B) first semester; (C) second semester, with ethical issues in education discussed and applied in field settings; (D) third semester, with emphasis on writing and oral communication for application in field settings.
SPED 400C.prereq_raw: SPED 304 (or concurrent) or consent for (B); SPED 400B for (C); SPED 400C for (D).

SPED 400D.title: Field Training in Special Education: Third Semester
SPED 400D.subject: SPED
SPED 400D.description: Students participate in classroom settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by department field supervisor; (B) first semester; (C) second semester, with ethical issues in education discussed and applied in field settings; (D) third semester, with emphasis on writing and oral communication for application in field settings.
SPED 400D.prereq_raw: SPED 304 (or concurrent) or consent for (B); SPED 400B for (C); SPED 400C for (D).

SPED 402.title: Writing for Educational Professionals
SPED 402.subject: SPED
SPED 402.description: Instruction on learning to write as professional educators. Strategies for developing and enhancing professional writing for the field of education. Peer and instructor feedback on writing throughout course. Technologies used to assist with writing.

SPED 412.title: Individuals with Extensive Support Needs
SPED 412.subject: SPED
SPED 412.description: Etiology, characteristics, and development of individuals with extensive support needs; historical, theoretical, and legal issues affecting individuals with extensive support needs; multicultural, family, and consumer issues; professional and ethical issues in providing services.

SPED 414.title: Education of Gifted Students
SPED 414.subject: SPED
SPED 414.description: Characteristics and educational provisions for gifted children and youth with particular attention to psychological aspects of creativity.

SPED 415.title: Education Program for the Gifted/Talented
SPED 415.subject: SPED
SPED 415.description: Utilization and evaluation of teaching/learning models for gifted/talented students, including consideration of roles, expectancies for learning, and organizational procedures.

SPED 419.title: Developing Oral Language and Phonetic Awareness in Students with Disabilities
SPED 419.subject: SPED
SPED 419.description: Focuses on the sound-symbol correspondences of language and the relationship of phonemic awareness and the phonological system of language to the reading process in students with disabilities and other diverse learners.

SPED 421.title: Strategies for Reading Difficulties
SPED 421.subject: SPED
SPED 421.description: Overview of methods, programs, and strategies for reading instruction designed to improve the performance of students, grades K-12, who experience difficulties in reading acquisition, fluency, and comprehension.

SPED 422.title: Literacy (Writing) for Students - Mild/Moderate Support Needs
SPED 422.subject: SPED
SPED 422.description: Research-based practices, programs, and strategies for writing instruction for students with mild/moderate support needs. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with disabilities while enhancing students’ writing abilities.
SPED 422.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BEd in SPED majors only.

SPED 423.title: Vocabulary Comprehension, Fluency & Writing Interventions for Students with Disabilities
SPED 423.subject: SPED
SPED 423.description: Development of and intervention for fluent reading vocabulary acquisition, comprehension and writing in students with disabilities. Explicit and systematic instruction of core aspects of reading and writing.

SPED 425.title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
SPED 425.subject: SPED
SPED 425.description: Knowledge and skills for relating effectively with families and professionals on behalf of the children and youth with and without disabilities. Coverage of the context in which family members and school personnel interact.

SPED 443.title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
SPED 443.subject: SPED
SPED 443.description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.

SPED 444.title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Elementary
SPED 444.subject: SPED
SPED 444.description: Teaching elementary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

SPED 445.title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Secondary
SPED 445.subject: SPED
SPED 445.description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction. Collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

SPED 446.title: Seminar in Special Education
SPED 446.subject: SPED
SPED 446.description: Study of issues, trends, and research into special education programming and service delivery.

SPED 451.title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
SPED 451.subject: SPED
SPED 451.description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers including criteria for evaluation and planning.
SPED 451.prereq_raw: HDFS 230 (or concurrent) and HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent.

SPED 452.title: Preschool Children–Special Needs
SPED 452.subject: SPED
SPED 452.description: Examination of application of current research and practices for serving preschool children with special needs.

SPED 453.title: Physical and Medical Needs: Students with Extensive Support Needs
SPED 453.subject: SPED
SPED 453.description: Learning to teach students with physical and medical needs, with a focus on developing independence. Instructional and assistive strategies in collaboration with related service providers.

SPED 454.title: Non-School-Age Individuals with Extensive Support Needs
SPED 454.subject: SPED
SPED 454.description: Effective planning, instruction, and support for non-school-age individuals (infants, toddlers, and adults) with extensive support needs across natural environments.

SPED 455.title: Secondary Transition for Students with Disabilities
SPED 455.subject: SPED
SPED 455.description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for postsecondary education, employment, and community living.

SPED 460.title: Introduction to Assessment and Instruction-Extensive Support Needs
SPED 460.subject: SPED
SPED 460.description: Assessment methods and tools, instructional and assistive strategies, and special procedures to support the participation of students with extensive support needs in inclusive settings.

SPED 461.title: Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Mild/Moderate Support Needs
SPED 461.subject: SPED
SPED 461.description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate support needs. Stress on program development to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities into general education environment.

SPED 462.title: Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Extensive Support Needs
SPED 462.subject: SPED
SPED 462.description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with extensive support needs. Focus on program development to facilitate the inclusion of students with disabilities into general education settings

SPED 463.title: Inclusive Practices Across the Curriculum-Mild/Moderate Support Needs
SPED 463.subject: SPED
SPED 463.description: Strategies for teaching science, math, and social studies to students with mild/moderate support needs in secondary settings; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, and curriculum development.

SPED 478.title: Assistant-Level Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
SPED 478.subject: SPED
SPED 478.description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis at the assistant level supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

SPED 480.title: Instructional and Assistive Technology
SPED 480.subject: SPED
SPED 480.description: Addresses instructional/assistive technologies and strategies that support inclusion for special/general education; application of Universal Design for Learning to support diverse student access to the PreK-12 general curriculum.

SPED 485.title: Classroom Organization and Management
SPED 485.subject: SPED
SPED 485.description: Knowledge and skills related to basic organizational management of an inclusive classroom, including scheduling, grouping, and stress and time management; techniques of applied behavior management, emphasizing behavior change and practical implementation of learning principles.

SPED 486.title: Theoretical Basis for Teaching Special-Needs Students
SPED 486.subject: SPED
SPED 486.description: Survey of biophysical, behavioral, social/ecological, psychodynamic/psychoeducational, cognitive/developmental, counter-theoretical approaches to teaching exceptional students. Opportunity for the development and/or strengthening of one’s own theoretical frame of reference.

SPED 487.title: Characteristics/Strategies for Teaching At-Risk Students
SPED 487.subject: SPED
SPED 487.description: Survey of educational, behavioral, and emotional characteristics of students who are at-risk for school failure and strategies to work with such students.

SPED 489.title: Intensive Behavioral Interventions
SPED 489.subject: SPED
SPED 489.description: Principles of behavior, emphasizing positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems and improving behavior and learning for students with extensive support needs.

SPED 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
SPED 499.subject: SPED
SPED 499.description: Individual reading, research, and/or projects under direct supervision of instructors.
SPED 499.prereq_raw: consent of instructor or department chair.

SPED 501.title: Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education Program Seminar
SPED 501.subject: SPED
SPED 501.description: Mandatory program seminar for Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education (PB-SPED) teacher candidates; access to tools and skills necessary for distance education program success; Introduction to the Special Education teaching profession.
SPED 501.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Post-Bac in SPED majors only.

SPED 526.title: Field Experience in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate
SPED 526.subject: SPED
SPED 526.description: Students spend 12 hours weekly throughout the semester in settings appropriate to SPED-PCert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by participating teacher and/or college supervisor.
SPED 526.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education only.

SPED 527.title: Student Teaching in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate Programs
SPED 527.subject: SPED
SPED 527.description: Supervised student teaching with a master teacher in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert emphasis (mild-moderate, severe/autism); minimum 280 hours in minimum 11 weeks. Supervision by master teacher and university supervisor.

SPED 528.title: Internship in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate Programs
SPED 528.subject: SPED
SPED 528.description: Supervised teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by master teacher/university mentor, and university supervisor. Must enroll for two consecutive semesters.

SPED 590.title: Internship, Special Education
SPED 590.subject: SPED
SPED 590.description: Supervised field activities involving the programming and instruction of special-needs students within training programs in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific Basin.

SPED 600.title: Foundations of Exceptionality
SPED 600.subject: SPED
SPED 600.description: Theoretical, legal and multicultural foundations for assessing, teaching and developing individual service plans across the lifespan for persons with disabilities.

SPED 601.title: Instructional/Assistive Technology and Universal Design for Learning
SPED 601.subject: SPED
SPED 601.description: Strategies for using instructional and assistive technology, digital tools and media, and Universal Design for Learning to support learning needs of students with disabilities and other diverse learners in the K-12 classroom.
SPED 601.prereq_raw: one of SPED 480, LTEC 414 , or LTEC 442 .

SPED 602.title: Special Education Law and Compliance
SPED 602.subject: SPED
SPED 602.description: Examination of the federal, state, and local government roles in special education with special emphasis on case and regulatory law. Focus on understanding special education law necessary in providing services to students with disabilities in a variety of placements. Appropriate for special/general education teachers, administrators, or related service providers.

SPED 603.title: Principles of Behavior
SPED 603.subject: SPED
SPED 603.description: Principles and laws governing behavior and methods that can be used to accomplish educationally relevant changes in student performance. Emphasis on the conceptual basis for changing behavior and use of technologies for changing behavior in school and community settings.

SPED 605.title: Collaboration in School and Community Settings
SPED 605.subject: SPED
SPED 605.description: Collaboration skills necessary to function as team members and to ensure the success of students with disabilities in inclusive school and community settings.

SPED 606.title: Language Development for Deaf Children
SPED 606.subject: SPED
SPED 606.description: General theories of first and second language development applied to development of ASL and English in deaf children. Relationship of theory to educational practice. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 606.prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent.

SPED 607.title: Audiology and Spoken English for Deaf Students
SPED 607.subject: SPED
SPED 607.description: Developmental principles of audiology and speech (i.e., spoken English) will be used to examine assessment procedures and intervention strategies appropriate to deaf students in a variety of educational placements. Classroom applications will be presented. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 607.prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent.

SPED 608.title: Literacy Development for Deaf Students
SPED 608.subject: SPED
SPED 608.description: Basic concepts related to language, language development and recognition of language-related learning problems of deaf students; strategies for teaching reading and writing to deaf students.

SPED 609.title: Seminar in Bilingual Deaf Education
SPED 609.subject: SPED
SPED 609.description: Study of issues, trends and methods in ASL/English bilingual education for deaf students. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 609.prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

SPED 610.title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development–Deaf
SPED 610.subject: SPED
SPED 610.description: Assessment methods and techniques used with deaf students that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming through planning and providing cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment. Taught in ASL and English.

SPED 611.title: Methods and Strategies for Students with Mild/Moderate Support Needs
SPED 611.subject: SPED
SPED 611.description: Techniques for providing effective instruction including: best instructional practice, lesson planning, teacher-directed and student-mediated instructional strategies, and curricular approaches for working with students with mild/moderate support needs.

SPED 613.title: Assessment and Data-Based Decision Making
SPED 613.subject: SPED
SPED 613.description: Assessment methods focused on curriculum-based measurement and diagnostic assessment. Connecting formal and informal assessment to instructional decision making. Formulating and implementing plans to meet the learning needs of students who require mild to moderate support.

SPED 614.title: Assessment and Instruction—Severe Disabilities and Autism
SPED 614.subject: SPED
SPED 614.description: Basic principles of assessment, instruction, and curriculum development; application of formal and informal assessment procedures for goal selection, formulating instructional plans, and adapting instructional materials to accommodate learning needs of students with severe disabilities and autism.

SPED 615.title: Family-Centered Approaches in Deaf Education
SPED 615.subject: SPED
SPED 615.description: Prepare teachers to deliver family-centered home-based services to families of deaf children using the SKI-HI model. Course will be taught in ASL and English.
SPED 615.prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

SPED 616.title: Collaboration–Working with Deaf Students in Inclusive Settings
SPED 616.subject: SPED
SPED 616.description: Collaboration skills for working with general education teachers, specialists, paraprofessionals, families and community members to support the success of deaf students in inclusive settings. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 616.prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

SPED 617.title: Transition Strategies for Deaf Students
SPED 617.subject: SPED
SPED 617.description: Collaborative model for facilitating the transition of deaf and hard-of-hearing students to develop appropriate transition plans and effective plans of study. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 617.prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

SPED 618.title: Adaptations and Special Procedures- Students/Severe Disabilities/Autism
SPED 618.subject: SPED
SPED 618.description: Adaptations and special intervention procedures to support the participation of individuals with severe motor, communication, and/or adaptive behavior disabilities in inclusive school and community settings. Includes lab work.

SPED 620.title: Strategies Across Content Area
SPED 620.subject: SPED
SPED 620.description: Strategies for teaching math, science, and social sciences to students of all ages with mild/moderate disabilities; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, curriculum development.

SPED 621.title: Language Arts Strategies: Students with Mild/Moderate Support Needs
SPED 621.subject: SPED
SPED 621.description: Basic concepts related to language, language development, and recognition of language-related learning difficulties of students with mild/moderate support needs; strategies for teaching language arts curricula (listening, speaking, reading, writing) to students of all ages.

SPED 622.title: Children’s Literature for Deaf Students
SPED 622.subject: SPED
SPED 622.description: Introduction to English literature translated into American Sign Language (ASL) including discussion of ASL literature genres, the importance of translation, selection of literature; story reading, book reading, and retelling. Taught in ASL.

SPED 625.title: Teaching Skills for Social Competence
SPED 625.subject: SPED
SPED 625.description: Issues in social development, self-determination, and social skills competence training for children and youth with disabilities; experience in group social skills training and development of individualized programs.
SPED 625.prereq_raw: either SPED 485 or SPED 630 , and either SPED 611 or SPED 614 ; or consent.

SPED 626.title: Field Experiences in Special Education
SPED 626.subject: SPED
SPED 626.description: Students spend a minimum of nine hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

SPED 627.title: Advanced Practicum
SPED 627.subject: SPED
SPED 627.description: Supervised education/community experiences; minimum of 20 hours weekly with special-needs population (MR, LD, SED, SMH); pre-school through postsecondary settings (public/private). Related seminar or equivalent and completion of SPED core required.

SPED 628.title: Internship
SPED 628.subject: SPED
SPED 628.description: Supervised education/community experiences with special needs populations, preschool through postsecondary settings.

SPED 629.title: Clinical Practice Special Projects
SPED 629.subject: SPED
SPED 629.description: Development and implementation of a field-based research professional development project under the direction of the student’s advisor; limited to students enrolled in the interdisciplinary program.

SPED 630.title: Positive Behavior Support
SPED 630.subject: SPED
SPED 630.description: Principles and laws governing human behavior and positive methods for addressing significant challenging behaviors for diverse students. Emphasis on functions of behavior, experimental techniques for documenting behavior change, and use of technology for improving behavior.

SPED 631.title: Early Intervention for Special Populations
SPED 631.subject: SPED
SPED 631.description: Issues important to early childhood special education. Early screening and assessment, working with families, curriculum options/models, program evaluation.

SPED 632.title: Language/Communication Assessment and Intervention
SPED 632.subject: SPED
SPED 632.description: Current research in typical language learning, assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of verbal behavior for individuals with social and communication needs, including complex communication needs. Procedures for developing functional communication objectives in ongoing routines/activities.

SPED 633.title: Motor Development/Intervention for Students with Severe Disabilities
SPED 633.subject: SPED
SPED 633.description: Normal/abnormal motor development; description/etiology of physically disabling conditions influencing motor development; analysis/application of assessment/ intervention strategies to promote motor development; positioning and handling skills.

SPED 634.title: Inclusive Physical Activity
SPED 634.subject: SPED
SPED 634.description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

SPED 635.title: Procedures for Early Childhood Special Education
SPED 635.subject: SPED
SPED 635.description: Assessment and intervention strategies to promote behavior change with young children with disabilities. Promoting child skill gains and integrated programming options.

SPED 637.title: Topics and Issues in Reading Difficulties
SPED 637.subject: SPED
SPED 637.description: Introduction of foundational knowledge of language and literacy development. Current topics and issues related to literacy development in students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

SPED 638.title: Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
SPED 638.subject: SPED
SPED 638.description: Introduction of basic linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for beginning or struggling readers. Covers evidence-based practices for teaching literacy to students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

SPED 639.title: Advanced Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
SPED 639.subject: SPED
SPED 639.description: Advanced linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for older students. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with Dyslexia or related reading difficulties.

SPED 640.title: Seminar on Mild/Moderate Disabilities
SPED 640.subject: SPED
SPED 640.description: Study of issues, research, program development in the area of mild/moderate disabilities.

SPED 641B.title: Seminar in Issues in Special Education: current issues and trends
SPED 641B.subject: SPED
SPED 641B.description: Seminar on issues, trends, research, and program development in the field of special education. (B) current issues and trends; (C) technology; (D) foundations; (E) developmental disabilities; (F) cultural and linguistic diversity; (G) evidence-based practices; (H) single case research.

SPED 641C.subject: SPED

SPED 641H.subject: SPED

SPED 642.subject: SPED

SPED 644.title: Seminar on Severe/Multiple Disabilities
SPED 644.subject: SPED
SPED 644.description: Research, program development trends/issues in the area of severe/multiple disabilities (birth through adulthood).
SPED 644.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: College of Education majors only.

SPED 645.title: Seminar in Early Childhood Special Education
SPED 645.subject: SPED
SPED 645.description: Study of issues/trends. Research and program development in early childhood special education.
SPED 645.prereq_raw: ( SPED 631 and SPED 635 ) with a minimum grade of B- or better, or consent.

SPED 647.title: Leadership in Special Education
SPED 647.subject: SPED
SPED 647.description: Seminar on topics related to leadership in the field of special education, including issues for teacher leaders, administrators, and teacher preparation personnel.

SPED 650.title: Seminar on Universal Design for Learning
SPED 650.subject: SPED
SPED 650.description: Seminar on issues of research and practice on the application of universal design for learning in K-12 and higher education settings. Focus on culturally and linguistically diverse students diversity, non-traditional students and students with disabilities.

SPED 652.title: Transition/Supported Employment
SPED 652.subject: SPED
SPED 652.description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for employment as adults in private and public sector businesses.

SPED 655.title: Reading Assessment & Tiered Intervention for Students with Disabilities
SPED 655.subject: SPED
SPED 655.description: Selection and administration of formal and informal assessments within a problem-solving model for designing robust reading instruction for struggling readers. Guiding planning and reading intervention using data-based decision-making.
SPED 655.prereq_raw: SPED 421B or SPED 421C or SPED 421D, and SPED 423 .
SPED 655.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SPED 656.title: Advanced Diagnostic-Prescriptive Reading Intervention
SPED 656.subject: SPED
SPED 656.description: Structural and functional features of reading development using diagnostic-prescriptive reading intervention. Advanced diagnostic-prescriptive intervention selection and design for students with reading disabilities using tool-component-composite analysis.
SPED 656.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SPED 671.title: Advanced Principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)
SPED 671.subject: SPED
SPED 671.description: Focuses on the definitions and characteristics of applied behavior analysis and the concepts, principles, and processes. Concepts related to ethics and behavior change procedures will also be introduced.

SPED 672.title: Collaboration and Supervision in Applied Behavior Analysis
SPED 672.subject: SPED
SPED 672.description: Students hone interpersonal communication and problem-solving skills and explore strategies for successful collaboration in school and community settings, developing expertise in fostering effective supervision to enhance outcomes for neurodivergent learners.

SPED 673.title: Ethics and Professional Conduct
SPED 673.subject: SPED
SPED 673.description: Focuses on content on the Behavior Analysis Certification Board’s code for ethical conduct as well as advanced concepts, principles, and processes of applied behavior analysis.

SPED 678.title: Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
SPED 678.subject: SPED
SPED 678.description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

SPED 688.title: Research Practicum in Special Education
SPED 688.subject: SPED
SPED 688.description: Directed research experience to demonstrate mastery of research skills and techniques through developing and writing research proposals.
SPED 688.prereq_raw: SPED 642 or consent, or departmental approval.

SPED 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
SPED 695.subject: SPED
SPED 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project.
SPED 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in Special Education.

SPED 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
SPED 699.subject: SPED
SPED 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair.

SPED 705.title: Seminar in Exceptionalities
SPED 705.subject: SPED
SPED 705.description: Current and historical topics, issues, and trends in the field of exceptionalities.

SPED 706.title: Doctoral Internship
SPED 706.subject: SPED
SPED 706.description: Supervised internship (minimum 18 hours per week) in program development and administration or research in the student’s area of emphasis.

SPED 710.title: Professional Seminar in Exceptionalities
SPED 710.subject: SPED
SPED 710.description: Professional norms, duties, and expectations of leaders in exceptionalities; transitioning from practitioner to researcher and leadership roles; familiarity with current research and trends in the field of exceptionalities.
SPED 710.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD in EDUC majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SPED 740.title: Single-Case Experimental Design
SPED 740.subject: SPED
SPED 740.description: Advanced single-case experimental design; examines the logic of internal and external validity of small “N” design and its functionalist foundations.

SPED 745.title: Special Topics in Exceptionalities
SPED 745.subject: SPED
SPED 745.description: Critical examination and discussion of historical or current topic in early intervention, special education, and/or developmental disabilities.

SPED 760.title: Grant Development/Procurement
SPED 760.subject: SPED
SPED 760.description: Overview of grant development and procurement processes related to special education personnel preparation and research and demonstration programs. Students design a grant proposal related to a particular problem or need within their employment settings.

STE 312B.title: Introduction to Teaching, Elementary: dual preparation in ECE and elementary education
STE 312B.subject: STE
STE 312B.description: Standards-based planning, assessment, instruction, reflection; inclusive classroom management; unique multicultural environment; issues in education and curriculum. Developing knowledgeable, effective, caring professionals to support student’s academic, social, emotional, physical needs. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

STE 312C.subject: STE
STE 312C.description: Standards-based planning, assessment, instruction, reflection; inclusive classroom management; unique multicultural environment; issues in education and curriculum. STE 313C.subject: STE

STE 314B.subject: STE

STE 314C.title: Principles and Methods of Writing Instruction: elementary education
STE 314C.subject: STE
STE 314C.description: Second of two methods courses focusing on theories and research-based practices related to writing instruction in elementary classrooms. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

STE 315.title: Field Experience - ECE
STE 315.subject: STE
STE 315.description: Supervised field experience in an early childhood setting. Minimum of 2 full days per week in classrooms, plus mandatory seminar with UH Mānoa field supervisor. Taken concurrently with education classes.

STE 316.title: Field Experience
STE 316.subject: STE
STE 316.description: Supervised field experience in schools. Minimum of 8 hours per week in conjunction with professional education courses.

STE 317B.title: Field Experience: dual preparation in ECE and elementary education
STE 317B.subject: STE
STE 317B.description: Supervised field experience in schools. Minimum of 2 full days per week in classrooms, plus mandatory seminar scheduled by UH Mānoa field supervisor. STE 317C.title: Field Experience: elementary education

STE 321.subject: STE
STE 321.description: Assessment, instructional methods, and materials for teaching social studies and science to children in preschool through grade 3. Emphasis on developmentally appropriate practices and lesson planning for teaching social studies and science.

STE 322B.title: Social Studies, Elementary: dual preparation in ECE and elementary education
STE 322B.subject: STE

STE 322C.title: Social Studies, Elementary: elementary education

STE 415.title: Observation and Assessment in Early Childhood Education

STE 416.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children

STE 417.title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education

STE 420.title: Supervision of Student Teaching

STE 425.title: Family and Community Centered Partnerships

STE 438.title: Foundations of Vocational Education

STE 438.description: Historical and philosophical foundations of vocational technical education, overview of federal and state legislation and contemporary practices. Special emphasis on vocational education program in Hawaiʻi.

STE 439.title: Office and Marketing Technology
STE 439.subject: STE
STE 439.description: Understanding and use of word processing, spreadsheet, and database software for business applications. Explore software across the office and marketing content areas.

STE 440.title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education

SURG 545Y.description: Advanced clinical experience in: (B) urology; (C) ophthalmology; (D) otolaryngology; (E) plastic surgery; (F) neurosurgery; (G) orthopaedics; (H) anesthesia; (I) surgical intensive care; (J) Sub-I-general surgery; (K) Sub-I-pediatric surgery; (M) diagnostic radiology; (N) radiation oncology; (O) EM Sub-I; (P) extramural elec in surg; (Q) Sub-I- cardiovascular; (R) surgical research; (S) surgical anatomy; (T) preceptorship in Asia; (U) biomedical technology design; (X) transplant surgery; (Y) bedside ultrasounds; (Z) laparoscopic skills.

SURG 545Z.description: Advanced clinical experience in: (B) urology; (C) ophthalmology; (D) otolaryngology; (E) plastic surgery; (F) neurosurgery; (G) orthopaedics; (H) anesthesia; (I) surgical intensive care; (J) Sub-I-general surgery; (K) Sub-I-pediatric surgery; (M) diagnostic radiology; (N) radiation oncology; (O) EM Sub-I; (P) extramural elec in surg; (Q) Sub-I- cardiovascular; (R) surgical research; (S) surgical anatomy; (T) preceptorship in Asia; (U) biomedical technology design; (X) transplant surgery; (Y) bedside ultrasounds; (Z) laparoscopic skills.

SUST 101.title: Dynamic Earth
SUST 101.subject: SUST
SUST 101.description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

SUST 102.title: The Natural Environment
SUST 102.subject: SUST
SUST 102.description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards.

SUST 102L.title: The Natural Environment Lab
SUST 102L.subject: SUST
SUST 102L.description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers.

SUST 103.title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
SUST 103.subject: SUST
SUST 103.description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

SUST 111L.title: Biology & Society Laboratory
SUST 111L.subject: SUST
SUST 111L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawaiʻi. Not a BIOL major elective.

SUST 112.title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
SUST 112.subject: SUST
SUST 112.description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

SUST 112L.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
SUST 112L.subject: SUST
SUST 112L.description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
SUST 112L.prereq_raw: SUST 112 (or concurrent) or GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent).

SUST 113.title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
SUST 113.subject: SUST
SUST 113.description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

SUST 114.title: Sustainable Cities
SUST 114.subject: SUST
SUST 114.description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction.

SUST 115.title: Sustainability in a Changing World
SUST 115.subject: SUST
SUST 115.description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawaiʻi/Oceania. Active learning environment.

SUST 116.title: Humans and the Environment
SUST 116.subject: SUST
SUST 116.description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

SUST 120.title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
SUST 120.subject: SUST
SUST 120.description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. Students who successfully completed CHEM 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in SUST 120/ CHEM 110 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete SUST 120/ CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override.

SUST 121.title: Politics & Poetics of Climate Change in Asia
SUST 121.subject: SUST
SUST 121.description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in Asia through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions.

SUST 122.title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Oceania
SUST 122.subject: SUST
SUST 122.description: Uses interdisciplinary approaches to examine the causes, impacts, and responses to climate change in Oceania, while drawing on examples and lessons from the broader Asia-Pacific with an emphasis on a writing intensive assessment.

SUST 156.title: Sustainable Food and Energy Field Course
SUST 156.subject: SUST
SUST 156.description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawaiʻi for sustainable development.

SUST 157.title: Global Environmental History
SUST 157.subject: SUST
SUST 157.description: Explores the influence of nature-climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms-on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

SUST 170.title: Religion and the Environment
SUST 170.subject: SUST
SUST 170.description: Examines the roles contemporary religious groups play in ground movements for sustainability. Introduces students to key scholars, religious leaders, and activists who are implementing sustainable solutions to pressing environmental problems.

SUST 201.title: Climate Change
SUST 201.subject: SUST
SUST 201.description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors.
SUST 201.prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102 , or consent.

SUST 204.title: Historical Ecology of Hawaiʻi
SUST 204.subject: SUST
SUST 204.description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

SUST 210.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
SUST 210.subject: SUST
SUST 210.description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

SUST 211.title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
SUST 211.subject: SUST
SUST 211.description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi as a model system.

SUST 217.title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupuaʻa
SUST 217.subject: SUST
SUST 217.description: Examination of the ahupuaʻa system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the mālama ʻāina track designed to build critical writing skills.

SUST 220.title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
SUST 220.subject: SUST
SUST 220.description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included.

SUST 221.title: Organic Food Crop Production
SUST 221.subject: SUST
SUST 221.description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors.

SUST 222.title: Hawaiians
SUST 222.subject: SUST
SUST 222.description: The social system, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians in a Pacific context. Transformation of the Hawaiian system by a capitalist economy. Native Hawaiian regeneration and quest for sovereign governance as an Oceanic society.

SUST 250.title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
SUST 250.subject: SUST
SUST 250.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

SUST 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
SUST 251.subject: SUST
SUST 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

SUST 260.title: Introduction to Environmental Humanities
SUST 260.subject: SUST
SUST 260.description: Introduction to the environmental humanities, which rests at the intersection of the arts, humanities, and environmental studies.

SUST 290.title: Topics in Sustainability
SUST 290.subject: SUST
SUST 290.description: Emphasizes understanding of interconnectivity of human and natural systems, and critical thinking towards proposed solutions.

SUST 304.title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
SUST 304.subject: SUST
SUST 304.description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawaiʻi.
SUST 304.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only.

SUST 308.title: Introduction to Planning
SUST 308.subject: SUST
SUST 308.description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawaiʻi planning—research problems from a multidisciplinary approach. Emphasis on writing instruction.
SUST 308.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 309.title: Environmental Issues
SUST 309.subject: SUST
SUST 309.description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
SUST 309.prereq_raw: one of BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 , or GEO 101 ; or consent.

SUST 310.title: Conservation Ethics
SUST 310.subject: SUST
SUST 310.description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.

SUST 311.title: Natural Resources Management
SUST 311.subject: SUST
SUST 311.description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife.
SUST 311.prereq_raw: ( NREM 251 / TPSS 251 or NREM 210 / TPSS 210 ; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

SUST 312.title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
SUST 312.subject: SUST
SUST 312.description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawaiʻi state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues.
SUST 312.prereq_raw: NREM 210 / PEPS 210 / SUST 210 or NREM 251 / SOCS 251 / TPSS 251 or ( BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or ( ERTH 101 or higher); and NREM 220 / SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses.

SUST 313.title: Plant Conservation Biology
SUST 313.subject: SUST
SUST 313.description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-in-practice in Hawaiʻi and elsewhere.

SUST 313L.title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
SUST 313L.subject: SUST
SUST 313L.description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

SUST 314.title: Global Environmental Issues
SUST 314.subject: SUST
SUST 314.description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment.
SUST 314.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SUST 315.title: Water and Society
SUST 315.subject: SUST
SUST 315.description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
SUST 315.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 316.title: Environmental Ethics
SUST 316.subject: SUST
SUST 316.description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making.
SUST 316.prereq_raw: SUST 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103 .

SUST 317.title: Mālama ʻāina Resource Management Visual Technologies
SUST 317.subject: SUST
SUST 317.description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

SUST 318.title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
SUST 318.subject: SUST
SUST 318.description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
SUST 318.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

SUST 319.title: Environmental Governance
SUST 319.subject: SUST
SUST 319.description: Centers around the ethical dilemmas of environmental and climate challenges and examines available mechanisms for solving them. Develops written communication skills through a critical lens from a political ecology and environmental justice perspective.
SUST 319.prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent.

SUST 320.title: Environment and Agriculture
SUST 320.subject: SUST
SUST 320.description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

SUST 321.title: Hawaiʻi and the Pacific
SUST 321.subject: SUST
SUST 321.description: Hawaiʻi as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

SUST 322.title: Globalization and Environment
SUST 322.subject: SUST
SUST 322.description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change. Junior standing or higher.

SUST 323.title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
SUST 323.subject: SUST
SUST 323.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each.
SUST 323.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.
SUST 323.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

SUST 324.title: Global Environmental Politics
SUST 324.subject: SUST
SUST 324.description: Evolution of international politics, law and decision-making on a variety of environmental concerns; from endangered species to pollution to climate change. Interaction of population, development, and environment in global governance.

SUST 325.title: Communicating Sustainability
SUST 325.subject: SUST
SUST 325.description: Application of project-based science communication, strategic communication, and digital media techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.
SUST 325.prereq_raw: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

SUST 326.title: Geography, Environment, and Society
SUST 326.subject: SUST
SUST 326.description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems. Sophomore standing or higher.

SUST 327.title: Climate Change, Resilience, and Sustainability in Oceania
SUST 327.subject: SUST
SUST 327.description: Examines Pacific Island experiences and responses to climate change, contrasting Indigenous and local impacts with regional and global models, emphasizing resilience, sustainability, and community strategies confronting rising seas, biodiversity loss, pollution, and ecological disruption.
SUST 327.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

SUST 330.title: Culture and Environment
SUST 330.subject: SUST
SUST 330.description: Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures.

SUST 332.title: Economics of Global Climate Change
SUST 332.subject: SUST
SUST 332.description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
SUST 332.prereq_raw: SUST 120 or SUST 130 or SUST 131, or consent.

SUST 333.title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
SUST 333.subject: SUST
SUST 333.description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future.

SUST 335.title: Society and Environment
SUST 335.subject: SUST
SUST 335.description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

SUST 336.title: Energy Economics and Policy
SUST 336.subject: SUST
SUST 336.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

SUST 338.title: Inter-woven Structures
SUST 338.subject: SUST
SUST 338.description: Studio investigation of threads under tension. Thematic lens of environmental vulnerability and resiliency. Exploration of art practice as embodied knowledge. Specific attention to weaving as meaning and place-making. Engages writing as a significant tool for analysis.

SUST 340.title: Human Values and the Environment
SUST 340.subject: SUST
SUST 340.description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts-literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics-in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature.
SUST 340.prereq_raw: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent.

SUST 341.title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawaiʻi
SUST 341.subject: SUST
SUST 341.description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

SUST 350.title: Sustainable Development
SUST 350.subject: SUST
SUST 350.description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawaiʻi. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.

SUST 351.title: Economic Change and Hawaiʻi’s People
SUST 351.subject: SUST
SUST 351.description: Hawaiʻi’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

SUST 356.title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
SUST 356.subject: SUST
SUST 356.description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

SUST 358.title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
SUST 358.subject: SUST
SUST 358.description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies.
SUST 358.prereq_raw: SUST 220 / NREM 220 or ECON 130 or consent.

SUST 367.title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
SUST 367.subject: SUST
SUST 367.description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
SUST 367.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200 -level SOC course, or consent

SUST 368.title: Sustainable Marketing
SUST 368.subject: SUST
SUST 368.description: Provides environmental knowledge and managerial tools that help for profit and not-for-profit organizations address pressing issues like global warming, plastic pollution, and fair trade while earning surplus revenue and remaining socially accountable

SUST 371.title: Genetics: Theory to Application
SUST 371.subject: SUST
SUST 371.description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

SUST 380.title: Environmental Law and Politics
SUST 380.subject: SUST
SUST 380.description: Focuses on theories, laws, policies, ethics, and sustainable futures of Hawaiʻi and the U.S. Sophomore standing or higher.
SUST 380.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level POLS course, or consent.

SUST 387.title: Politics of the Ocean
SUST 387.subject: SUST
SUST 387.description: Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. Sophomore standing or higher.
SUST 387.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

SUST 388.title: Literature and the Environment
SUST 388.subject: SUST
SUST 388.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of intersections between literature and the environment, including issues such as climate change, technology, pollution, land and land use, interspecies relationships.
SUST 388.prereq_raw: One ENG DL course or consent.

SUST 394.title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
SUST 394.subject: SUST
SUST 394.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues.
SUST 394.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 401.title: History of the Indian Ocean World
SUST 401.subject: SUST
SUST 401.description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants.

SUST 404.title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
SUST 404.subject: SUST
SUST 404.description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legla aspects of pollution control.
SUST 404.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 410.title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
SUST 410.subject: SUST
SUST 410.description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

SUST 411.title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
SUST 411.subject: SUST
SUST 411.description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

SUST 412.title: The Ocean Economy
SUST 412.subject: SUST
SUST 412.description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

SUST 413.title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
SUST 413.subject: SUST
SUST 413.description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
SUST 413.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 414.title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
SUST 414.subject: SUST
SUST 414.description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

SUST 415.title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
SUST 415.subject: SUST
SUST 415.description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

SUST 417.title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
SUST 417.subject: SUST
SUST 417.description: Examines resilience thinking as it relates to making cities resilient to environmental hazards in the context of climate change. Draws on relevant theories, policy, and case studies in urban planning. Emphasis on instruction in writing.
SUST 417.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

SUST 420.title: Community and Natural Resource Management
SUST 420.subject: SUST
SUST 420.description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management.
SUST 420.prereq_raw: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: two social science courses ( with a minimum grade of C-

SUST 421.title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
SUST 421.subject: SUST
SUST 421.description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

SUST 422.title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
SUST 422.subject: SUST
SUST 422.description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

SUST 423.title: Agriculture, Food and Society
SUST 423.subject: SUST
SUST 423.description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to non-majors.
SUST 423.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 425.title: Environmental Geochemistry
SUST 425.subject: SUST
SUST 425.description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/ agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

SUST 426.title: Environment, Resources and Society
SUST 426.subject: SUST
SUST 426.description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

SUST 427.title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
SUST 427.subject: SUST
SUST 427.description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites.
SUST 427.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 433.title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
SUST 433.subject: SUST
SUST 433.description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

SUST 436.title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
SUST 436.subject: SUST
SUST 436.description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis.

SUST 439.title: Installation/Performance—Material in Context
SUST 439.subject: SUST
SUST 439.description: Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools.

SUST 440.title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
SUST 440.subject: SUST
SUST 440.description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation. Senior standing or higher.

SUST 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
SUST 441.subject: SUST
SUST 441.description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. Junior standing or higher.

SUST 442.title: Environmental Management Systems
SUST 442.subject: SUST
SUST 442.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
SUST 442.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 445.title: Biocultural Ecology and Conservation
SUST 445.subject: SUST
SUST 445.description: Examines some perspectives on Ecology within the context of Indigenous and Local Knowledge systems, and some approaches to conservation by Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities.
SUST 445.prereq_raw: BIOL 265 or BIOL 301 or BIOL 305 / BOT 305 or consent.

SUST 446.title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
SUST 446.subject: SUST
SUST 446.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

SUST 449.title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
SUST 449.subject: SUST
SUST 449.description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results.

SUST 450.title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
SUST 450.subject: SUST
SUST 450.description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
SUST 450.prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level.

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

SUST 451.title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
SUST 451.subject: SUST
SUST 451.description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawaiʻi.
SUST 451.prereq_raw: BIOL 172 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

SUST 455.title: Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict: Hawaiian Sovereignty in Pacific Context
SUST 455.subject: SUST
SUST 455.description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution. Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
SUST 455.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

SUST 456.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
SUST 456.subject: SUST
SUST 456.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
SUST 456.prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356

SUST 457.title: ʻāina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
SUST 457.subject: SUST
SUST 457.description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawaiʻi.
SUST 457.prereq_raw: SUST 217 / HWST 207 or SUST 317 / HWST 307 or SUST 356 / HWST 356 .

SUST 458.title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
SUST 458.subject: SUST
SUST 458.description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

SUST 459.title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
SUST 459.subject: SUST
SUST 459.description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O’ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.
SUST 459.prereq_raw: SUST 217 / HWST 207 or SUST 317 / HWST 307 or SUST 356 / HWST 356 .

SUST 460.title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
SUST 460.subject: SUST
SUST 460.description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawaiʻi. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.
SUST 460.prereq_raw: SUST 217 / HWST 207 or SUST 317 / HWST 307 or SUST 356 / HWST 356 .

SUST 461.title: Global Ethnic Conflict
SUST 461.subject: SUST
SUST 461.description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher.
SUST 461.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.

SUST 473.title: GIS for Community & Environmental Planning
SUST 473.subject: SUST
SUST 473.description: Exploration of geographic information systems (GIS) area analysis techniques for spatial information management in community planning. Students will learn the basic concepts and principles, and practical skills of GIS through lectures, discussions, and labs.
SUST 473.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 480.title: Applied Forest Ecology
SUST 480.subject: SUST
SUST 480.description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources).
SUST 480.prereq_raw: ( SUST 311 / NREM 310 and NREM 380 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

SUST 481.title: American Environmental History
SUST 481.subject: SUST
SUST 481.description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

SUST 482.title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
SUST 482.subject: SUST
SUST 482.description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

SUST 484.title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
SUST 484.subject: SUST
SUST 484.description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning.

SUST 490.title: Advanced Topics in Sustainability
SUST 490.subject: SUST
SUST 490.description: Emphasizes understanding of interconnectivity of human and natural systems, and critical thinking towards proposed solutions.

SUST 494.title: Environmental Problem Solving
SUST 494.subject: SUST
SUST 494.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Senior-level capstone for NREM and related majors. Ecosystem management within problem-solving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications.
SUST 494.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or consent.

SUST 495.title: Sustainability Capstone
SUST 495.subject: SUST
SUST 495.description: Capstone for undergraduate students in interdisciplinary studies focusing on sustainability. The capstone experience provides an opportunity for students to gain knowledge and research experience in an applied setting.
SUST 495.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: IS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

SUST 496.title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
SUST 496.subject: SUST
SUST 496.description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

SUST 608.title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
SUST 608.subject: SUST
SUST 608.description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts.
SUST 608.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SUST 610.title: Seminar on Water in History
SUST 610.subject: SUST
SUST 610.description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

SUST 611.title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
SUST 611.subject: SUST
SUST 611.description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required.
SUST 611.prereq_raw: grade of C- or above in ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , or consent.

SUST 612.title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
SUST 612.subject: SUST
SUST 612.description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings.
SUST 612.prereq_raw: NREM 301 / SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent

SUST 613.title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
SUST 613.subject: SUST
SUST 613.description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

SUST 618.title: Sustainable Business Management
SUST 618.subject: SUST
SUST 618.description: Overview of sustainable business management in the firm’s functional areas, including sustainable strategic planning, climate risk assessment, sustainable asset financing, supply chain management, fair trade, and green/ethical consumption behavior management.
SUST 618.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SUST 620.title: Environmental Planning and Policy
SUST 620.subject: SUST
SUST 620.description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

SUST 621.title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
SUST 621.subject: SUST
SUST 621.description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
SUST 621.prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

SUST 623.title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
SUST 623.subject: SUST
SUST 623.description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

SUST 624.title: Coastal Modeling
SUST 624.subject: SUST
SUST 624.description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

SUST 625.title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
SUST 625.subject: SUST
SUST 625.description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/ Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via video-conferencing.

SUST 627.title: Coastal Geology
SUST 627.subject: SUST
SUST 627.description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.

SUST 628.title: Urban Environmental Problems
SUST 628.subject: SUST
SUST 628.description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

SUST 632.title: Planning in Hawaiʻi and Pacific Islands
SUST 632.subject: SUST
