SUST 632.description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.
SUST 632.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SUST 636.title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
SUST 636.subject: SUST
SUST 636.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
SUST 636.prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent.

SUST 637.title: Resource Economics
SUST 637.subject: SUST
SUST 637.description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

SUST 638.title: Environmental Resource Economics
SUST 638.subject: SUST
SUST 638.description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

SUST 640.title: Land Systems Science
SUST 640.subject: SUST
SUST 640.description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socioecological system function.
SUST 640.prereq_raw: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461 .

SUST 641.title: Seminar: place-based education
SUST 641.subject: SUST
SUST 641.description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field. (P) place-based education.
SUST 641.prereq_raw: graduate and/or undergraduate courses in education and/or social sciences or consent.

SUST 647.title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
SUST 647.subject: SUST
SUST 647.description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered.
SUST 647.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SUST 652.title: KāNāwai Lawaiʻa: Hawaiʻi’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
SUST 652.subject: SUST
SUST 652.description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance.

SUST 658.title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
SUST 658.subject: SUST
SUST 658.description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate.

SUST 659.title: He Aliʻi Ka ʻāina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
SUST 659.subject: SUST
SUST 659.description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ʻāina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ʻāina future.

SUST 661.title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
SUST 661.subject: SUST
SUST 661.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

SUST 670.title: Sociology of Sustainability
SUST 670.subject: SUST
SUST 670.description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives.
SUST 670.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SUST 677.title: Marine Renewable Energy
SUST 677.subject: SUST
SUST 677.description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.
SUST 677.prereq_raw: ORE 607 ; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable.

SUST 695.title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
SUST 695.subject: SUST
SUST 695.description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought.
SUST 695.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SUST 696.title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
SUST 696.subject: SUST
SUST 696.description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

SUST 725.title: Political Ecology
SUST 725.subject: SUST
SUST 725.description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

SUST 750.title: Topics in Biocultural Diversity and Conservation
SUST 750.subject: SUST
SUST 750.description: Biological, cultural, and linguistic conservation are intimately linked, but rarely studied simultaneously. Adopts a trans-disciplinary view of diversity and conservation of nature, cultures, and languages, along with issues in anthropology, law, and ethics.

SW 200.title: The Field of Social Work
SW 200.subject: SW
SW 200.description: Orientation to the profession of social work; historical development, values and philosophy, scope and aims.

SW 302.title: General Social Work Practice I
SW 302.subject: SW
SW 302.description: Orientation to practice principles, concepts, values, knowledge base, and their application.
SW 302.prereq_raw: SW 200 (complete with C or better) and majors only.

children.text: ( complete with C or better ) and majors only

SW 303.title: General Social Work Practice II
SW 303.subject: SW
SW 303.description: Introduction to practice skills with individuals, families, groups, and communities. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.
SW 303.prereq_raw: SW 302 (complete with C or better) and majors only.

children.text: ( complete with C or better ) and majors only

SW 325.title: History of Social Welfare
SW 325.subject: SW
SW 325.description: Historical developments and implications of social welfare activities, institutions, and policies and European backgrounds; introduce social welfare developments in selected non-European countries. Recommended: SW 200 .

SW 326.title: Social Welfare as a Social Institution
SW 326.subject: SW
SW 326.description: Study of U.S. social welfare institutional structures, programs, and policies addressing human need; focus on Hawaiʻi’s legislative processes and social service programs; emphasis on oral communication inherent to advocacy, legislative, and policymaking processes.

SW 360.title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment
SW 360.subject: SW
SW 360.description: Examination of complex sociocultural factors that privilege some and oppress/marginalize others. Challenges commonly held tropes and complicates the discourse regarding individual, family, group, organizational and community development within the social environment. Recommended: SW 200 .

SW 361.title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment II
SW 361.subject: SW
SW 361.description: Focus on human development across the lifespan with attention given to unique challenges and opportunities faced in each phase. Emphasis on “populations at risk” and the strengths and assets unique to diverse populations.
SW 361.prereq_raw: SW 360 with a grade of C or better. Recommended: SW 200 .

SW 380.title: Topics in Social Welfare
SW 380.subject: SW
SW 380.description: An examination of current trends in the field of social welfare.

SW 391.title: Undergraduate Field Education I
SW 391.subject: SW
SW 391.description: Introduction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
SW 391.prereq_raw: SW 302 , SW 325 , SW 326 (or concurrent), SW 360 , and SW 361 (or concurrent) complete with C or better; and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better ; and majors only

SW 402.title: General Social Work Practice III
SW 402.subject: SW
SW 402.description: Use of problem-solving processes and ethical models of decision-making in practice with individuals, families, groups, and communities.
SW 402.prereq_raw: SW 303 , SW 326 , and SW 361 complete with C or better; and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better ; and majors only

SW 403.title: General Social Work Practice IV
SW 403.subject: SW
SW 403.description: Examination of practice methods and intervention models; identification and analysis of issues related to practice. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.
SW 403.prereq_raw: SW 402 (C or better) and majors only.

SW 435.title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
SW 435.subject: SW
SW 435.description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
SW 435.prereq_raw: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200 ; or consent.

SW 440.title: Research Development in Social Welfare
SW 440.subject: SW
SW 440.description: Introduction to and application of language of research, theoretical concepts underlying advancement of knowledge, practical steps in research.
SW 440.prereq_raw: completion of required junior-level SW courses (i.e., SW 302 , SW 303 , SW 325 , SW 326 , SW 360 , SW 361 , and SW 391 ) with C or better.

children.text: completion of required junior-level SW courses ( i.e., SW 302

SW 470.title: Native Hawaiian Perspectives: A Cultural Context for Well-Being
SW 470.subject: SW
SW 470.description: To preserve the cultural knowledge of kupuna as it relates to health and wellbeing. Disseminate cultural knowledge of health and well-being to social work students and students in allied health professions.
SW 470.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW or Social Welfare students only.

SW 471.title: Ke Aʻo Mau: Learning Preserved
SW 471.subject: SW
SW 471.description: To provide a holistic examination of issues and to explore culturally-anchored resolutions and practices to achieve social justice and health and well-being.
SW 471.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW, Social Welfare, or PH students only.

SW 472.title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
SW 472.subject: SW
SW 472.description: Provides students with a body of knowledge, skills, and values that facilitate social work with Native Hawaiians.
SW 472.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW or Social Welfare students.

SW 475.title: Social Services with Children
SW 475.subject: SW
SW 475.description: Study of current social services for children in the U.S. with focus on familiarization of child welfare programs and services in Hawaiʻi.
SW 475.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

SW 477.title: Social Welfare Concepts and Issues in Gerontology
SW 477.subject: SW
SW 477.description: Aging and its effect on the individual, family groups, associations, and communities. Impact of aging on social service delivery systems, public policy and role of social work.
SW 477.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

SW 480.title: Topics in Social Welfare
SW 480.subject: SW
SW 480.description: An examination of current trends and issues in social work.

SW 490.title: Undergraduate Field Education II
SW 490.subject: SW
SW 490.description: Intermediate instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
SW 490.prereq_raw: SW 391 complete with C or better, and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better , and majors only

SW 491.title: Undergraduate Field Education III
SW 491.subject: SW
SW 491.description: Advanced instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
SW 491.prereq_raw: SW 490 complete with C or better, and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better , and majors only

SW 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
SW 499.subject: SW
SW 499.description: Planned individualized study or research in special area related to social work practice interest. Up to 3 credit hours.
SW 499.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: majors only, senior standing, and consent of program chair and faculty advisor.

SW 606.title: Social Work Practice with Individuals
SW 606.subject: SW
SW 606.description: Beginning practice course introduces students to the basic processes of social work and the roles and skills needed for generalist practice. Relevant theories of social work practice with individuals are explored for the efficacy with various problems and for their applicability to practice with various ethnocultures, social classes, and oppressed populations. Interviewing and interpersonal skill development are incorporated.

SW 607.title: Social Work Practice with Families and Groups
SW 607.subject: SW
SW 607.description: Practice course builds upon the generalist framework and foundation content presented in 606. Special emphasis is given on models for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of practice with families and groups. Relevant theories of groups and the principles of group dynamics and group work methods are examined in regard to task, therapeutic, psychoeducational, and social development groups. Family content includes structural, behavioral, communication/experiential, and culturally-specific theories of intervention.

SW 630.title: Social Welfare Policy and Services
SW 630.subject: SW
SW 630.description: Examines in a historical and comparative framework the economic, social, political, organizational, and administrative factors influencing the development, formulation, and implementation of social welfare policies in the U.S. Provides opportunity for the application of various models of social policy analysis in major areas of social welfare programming and service delivery.
SW 630.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 631.title: Social Work Practice in Communities and Organizations
SW 631.subject: SW
SW 631.description: Community conceptualization; organized roles of developer, enabler, broker, mediator, and advocate; diagnostic and problem-solving technology; the special characteristics of the social worker as community organizer; matrix of structural objectives; sources and use of power; how to build an organization; and interorganizational negotiation.

SW 633.title: Organization and Administration in Social Work
SW 633.subject: SW
SW 633.description: Introduction to formal organization theory. Social service administration examined and implications for service delivery systems developed.
SW 633.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 636.title: Policies, Programs and Services on Aging
SW 636.subject: SW
SW 636.description: Explores policies, programs, and services for older adults. Students learn about the aging network, assess older adults’ needs, link older adults to appropriate services in the community, and track legislative bills that address older adults’ quality of life.
SW 636.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SW 637.title: Death and Dying
SW 637.subject: SW
SW 637.description: Physical, social, cultural, psychological, and spiritual dimensions of dying, death, and bereavement.
SW 637.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SW 639.title: Social and Cultural Aspects of Aging
SW 639.subject: SW
SW 639.description: Overview of aging from the biopsycho, socioeconomic and cultural perspectives. Explores common theories of aging. Emphasis on bridging the gap between the realm of concepts and theories, and the world of practice in gerontology.
SW 639.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SW 640.title: Introduction to Scientific Methods and Principles in Social Work
SW 640.subject: SW
SW 640.description: Understanding and interpreting results of nomothetic and idiographic research; design principles and statistical analyses and their relationship to practices; use of published research.
SW 640.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 650.title: Research Designs and Data Analyses for the Evaluation of Practice Effectiveness
SW 650.subject: SW
SW 650.description: Extending the study of scientific methods introduced in SW 640 . Covers the range of empirical research methods and data analytic procedures suitable for knowledge building and practice evaluation at all levels of intervention from case to program.

SW 651.title: Quantitative Methods I
SW 651.subject: SW
SW 651.description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences. Introduction to general linear model as principle of data analysis. Course requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

SW 654.title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
SW 654.subject: SW
SW 654.description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.

SW 656.title: Multivariate Methods
SW 656.subject: SW
SW 656.description: Multivariate forms of multiple linear regression, analysis of variance, and analysis of co-variance. Multiple discriminant analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis are discussed.

SW 659.title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment I
SW 659.subject: SW
SW 659.description: Examination of complex factors that privilege some and oppress/marginalize others; challenges commonly held tropes and complicates the discourse regarding individual, family, group, organizational and community development within the social environment.
SW 659.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 660.title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment II
SW 660.subject: SW
SW 660.description: Focus on human development across the lifespan with attention given to unique challenges and opportunities faced in each phase. Emphasis is placed on “populations at risk” and the strengths and assets unique to diverse populations.

SW 663.title: Treatment of Chemical Dependency
SW 663.subject: SW
SW 663.description: Introduction to treatment of alcoholism and other chemical dependencies. Application of social work strategies in work with individuals and families in the disease and recovery process.
SW 663.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 665.title: Diagnosis and Assessment in Clinical Practice
SW 665.subject: SW
SW 665.description: Augments existing courses, enhances practicum, and satisfies students’ expressed need for firmer understanding and working knowledge of the DSM, the prevailing diagnostic system for psychological disorders in the United States.
SW 665.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SW 672.title: Child Welfare as a Field of Social Work
SW 672.subject: SW
SW 672.description: Emphasis on the developments in child welfare; issues, concerns with regard to needs and rights, and the application of social work services to problems associated with needs for protection. Review of historical, theoretical, empirical, and legal findings for skill development in intervening in dysfunctional parent/ child interaction.
SW 672.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 674.title: Community and Public Health Practice
SW 674.subject: SW
SW 674.description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

SW 680.title: Topics in Social Welfare
SW 680.subject: SW
SW 680.description: Current trends in field of social welfare. Recent courses have focused on forensic social work, immigrants and refugees, and leadership in human services. Meets seminar requirement.
SW 680.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 682.title: Marriage and Family Therapy
SW 682.subject: SW
SW 682.description: Introduction to couple and family therapy offers an overview of family systems perspective, theory and technique relevant to informing effective social work case planning, case management, advocacy, and interaction with clients.
SW 682.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

SW 690.title: Generalist Field Education I
SW 690.subject: SW
SW 690.description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice.
SW 690.prereq_raw: SW 606 (or concurrent)(with a minimum grade of C).

SW 691.title: Generalist Field Education II
SW 691.subject: SW
SW 691.description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice.
SW 691.prereq_raw: SW 690 and SW 607 (or concurrent) and SW 631 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of C )

SW 696.title: Health and Aging
SW 696.subject: SW
SW 696.description: Biological and physiological changes associated with aging. Social and psychological factors associated with health maintenance. Major threats to health, changing patterns of morbidity and mortality of the aged.

SW 699.title: Directed Reading and Research
SW 699.subject: SW
SW 699.description: Students, on the basis of special interest, select a faculty member to work with on a problem for which planned individualized study or research is deemed advisable.

SW 700.title: Thesis Research
SW 700.subject: SW
SW 700.description: Independent research under supervision of a thesis committee. Includes formal proposal and defense of finished research.

SW 707.title: Methods of Group Psychotherapy
SW 707.subject: SW
SW 707.description: Designed specifically to train students in the theory and practice of leading psychotherapy groups; it includes historical developments, research, theories, and application of group psychotherapy, group techniques and exercises.

SW 715.title: Therapeutic Strategies with the Older Adult
SW 715.subject: SW
SW 715.description: Focuses on interdisciplinary strategies with older adults: individual, family, and group therapy; eclectic mental health approaches; case management; and environmental intervention. Emphasis placed on the use of these strategies as preventive, as well as supportive, measures for the well, transition, and frail elderly. Meets seminar requirement.
SW 715.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 717.title: Social Work Practice with Children and Families
SW 717.subject: SW
SW 717.description: Advanced practice course for students specializing in social work with children and families. Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of both theoretical formulations and therapeutic techniques for practice in the field of family and child welfare. Emphasis placed on the development of specialized knowledge and skills for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of a variety of common child and family practice situations.

SW 718.title: Seminar in Social Work Practice with Children and Families
SW 718.subject: SW
SW 718.description: Designed for students in the child and family concentration and builds upon past knowledge and skill development in practice classes and in the practicum. Students integrate, demonstrate, and extend earlier learning, acquire new knowledge, and learn and practice new skills. Organized around student case presentations in a consultation format. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 722.title: Social Work Practice in Health Care
SW 722.subject: SW
SW 722.description: Didactic and experiential learning activity focuses on the major role functions of the social worker in the health field including assessment, contracting, counseling, advocacy, case management, discharge planning, family group work, community and team building. Covers health care policy, research directions in practice and social work management issues.

SW 723.title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Health Care
SW 723.subject: SW
SW 723.description: Through the use of case studies developed by the students, social work practice is examined in three areas of health care: primary care provided in health departments and medical groups, hospital-based services, and long-term care. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 724.title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Mental Health
SW 724.subject: SW
SW 724.description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings. Focused on engagement and assessment while emphasizing cultural, person in environment, and strengths-based approaches.

SW 725.title: Social Work Practice in Mental Health
SW 725.subject: SW
SW 725.description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings, with a focus on history and policy in the U.S. and Hawaiʻi, as well as culturally-grounded and evidence-based practice.

SW 726.title: Social Work Practice with Older Adults
SW 726.subject: SW
SW 726.description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of theoretical formulations and intervention strategies for working with older adults and their families. Emphasis on diversity/justice.

SW 727.title: Seminar in Social Work with Older Adults
SW 727.subject: SW
SW 727.description: Designed for gerontology specialization students to gain advanced knowledge for working with diverse older adults and their families. Emphasis on strength perspectives on aging.

SW 731.title: Social Policy Analysis
SW 731.subject: SW
SW 731.description: Students pursue in-depth a specific topic in the areas of social planning, social policy analysis, evaluation of social programs, administration, supervision, and consultation. Selectively a comparative perspective is introduced and case studies used to illustrate concepts, principles, and techniques, with implications for practice. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 737.title: Social Work and the Law
SW 737.subject: SW
SW 737.description: Knowledge of judicial systems and law relevant to social work practice in corrections, child-family welfare, health, and mental health. Skills for effective participation in the legal process are acquired in moot court and in practice for testifying.
SW 737.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

SW 741.title: Review of Research in Social Work
SW 741.subject: SW
SW 741.description: In-depth study of research in a substantive area. Each seminar will be devoted to a particular topic: e.g., foster care of children, effectiveness of social work intervention, etc.

SW 743.title: Individual or Group Research Project—Plan B
SW 743.subject: SW
SW 743.description: Independent research (group of two to seven students or by an individual student) undertaken under the sponsorship of a faculty advisor. Elements are selection of a topic related to the practice of social work or knowledge relevant to that practice, utilization of empirical research methodology in collecting and analyzing original data, and preparation of a scholarly paper.

SW 744.title: Individual or Group Research Project–Plan B
SW 744.subject: SW

SW 746.title: Individual or Group Research Project–Plan B
SW 746.subject: SW

SW 750.title: Analysis and Development of Knowledge for Social Work
SW 750.subject: SW
SW 750.description: Focuses on developing an understanding of philosophy of science, theory development, social work epistemology, and the analysis and development of knowledge for social work practice.
SW 750.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent.

SW 751.title: Quantitative Methods II
SW 751.subject: SW
SW 751.description: Empirical research methodology with emphasis on design principles and measurement theory; design and measurement issues and problems in cross-cultural research.
SW 751.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent.

SW 752.title: Qualitative Research: Philosophical, Methodological and Analytic Approaches
SW 752.subject: SW
SW 752.description: Theories and methods of qualitative research; problem formulation, informant selection, study design, data collection and analysis utilizing qualitative approaches.
SW 752.prereq_raw: SW 640 or SW 651 or equivalent; departmental approval.

SW 755.title: Dissertation Seminar
SW 755.subject: SW
SW 755.description: Culminating experience in social welfare doctoral specialization; integration of PhD core and specialization course work.
SW 755.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: classified student in PhD in social welfare program or consent.

SW 772.title: Seminar in International Social Work
SW 772.subject: SW
SW 772.description: Approaches to social problems and trends in the profession in international, cross-cultural perspectives. Emphasis on developmental aspects of social work. Political, economic, social, and cultural forces shaping social welfare in national development. Meets seminar requirement.
SW 772.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SW 774.title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
SW 774.subject: SW
SW 774.description: Hawaiian culture, past and present. Explores and examines possible approaches to working with Hawaiians and part-Hawaiians. Special emphasis on supports in the Hawaiian system that may promote maximal functioning for those Hawaiians experiencing problems in today’s society. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 776.title: Seminar on Women and Health
SW 776.subject: SW
SW 776.description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.
SW 776.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

SW 790.title: Specialist Field Education I
SW 790.subject: SW
SW 790.description: Instruction in the field is continued. The field experience in the second year provides an opportunity for the student to test out concepts, principles, theories, and alternate approaches in actual practice settings.
SW 790.prereq_raw: SW 717 (or concurrent) or SW 722 (or concurrent) or SW 724 (or concurrent) or SW 726 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B -).

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of B -)

SW 791.title: Specialist Field Education II
SW 791.subject: SW
SW 791.prereq_raw: SW 790 and; SW 718 (or concurrent); or SW 723 (or concurrent); or SW 725 (or concurrent); or SW 727 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B-).

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of B- )

SW 797.title: Advanced Social Welfare Policy Analysis and Change
SW 797.subject: SW
SW 797.description: Builds on SW 630 and emphasizes a more thorough and comprehensive examination of major policies, programs, and populations central to a concentration (Health, Mental Health, Gerontology, Child and Family). Students learn a more focused and applied analysis of the relationship between social policy, research, and social work practice.
SW 797.prereq_raw: SW 606 and SW 607 ; SW 630 and SW 631 ; SW 640 and SW 650 ; SW 659 and SW 660 ; SW 690 and SW 691 .

TAHR 099.title: International Exchange Study/Research
TAHR 099.subject: TAHR
TAHR 099.description: Study overseas in an approved international or similar exchange program.

TAHR 250.title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
TAHR 250.subject: TAHR
TAHR 250.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

TAHR 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
TAHR 251.subject: TAHR
TAHR 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

TAHR 415.title: Extension Education & Outreach
TAHR 415.subject: TAHR
TAHR 415.description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program development and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures.
TAHR 415.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

TAHT 101.title: First Year Tahitian I
TAHT 101.subject: TAHT
TAHT 101.description: Basic core skills of listening, speaking and grammar of spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

TAHT 201.title: Second Year Tahitian I
TAHT 201.subject: TAHT
TAHT 201.description: Intermediate core skills of listening, speaking and knowledge of grammar for spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

TAHT 301.title: Third-Level Tahitian
TAHT 301.subject: TAHT
TAHT 301.description: Continuation of TAHT 202 . Conversation, advanced reading, composition.

TAHT 401.title: Fourth-Level Tahitian
TAHT 401.subject: TAHT
TAHT 401.description: Continuation of TAHT 302 . Advanced conversation, reading, and writing with focus on modern formal and colloquial Tahitian styles. The language in the realms of storytelling, radio, folklore, traditional and modern writing. Survey of modern and classical language.

TAHT 458.title: Fourth-Level Tahitian Abroad
TAHT 458.subject: TAHT
TAHT 458.description: Fulltime formal instruction at the University of French Polynesia in Tahiti. Fourth-year level in Tahitian language and culture.

THAI 101.title: Elementary Thai I
THAI 101.subject: THAI
THAI 101.description: First semester of elementary Thai. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Thailand.

THAI 102.title: Elementary Thai II
THAI 102.subject: THAI
THAI 102.description: Continuation of THAI 101 . Emphasizes reading, writing, listening, and speaking modern standard Thai. Structural points are introduced inductively. Regular on-line lab work and review of audiovisual materials.

THAI 112.title: Accelerated Elementary Thai
THAI 112.subject: THAI
THAI 112.description: Content of 101-102 covered in one semester. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Thailand.

THAI 201.title: Intermediate Thai I
THAI 201.subject: THAI
THAI 201.description: Continuation of THAI 102 . Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Thai script.

THAI 202.title: IntermediateThai II
THAI 202.subject: THAI
THAI 202.description: Continuation of THAI 201 . Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Thai script.

THAI 212.title: Accelerated Intermediate Thai
THAI 212.subject: THAI
THAI 212.description: Content of 201-202 covered in one semester. Emphasis on the continued development of competence in both oral and written language for more advanced communication, travel, and further study.

THAI 301.title: Third-Level Thai I
THAI 301.subject: THAI
THAI 301.description: Continuation of THAI 202 . Advanced conversation and reading, emphasis on modern written texts. Regular on-line lab work.

THAI 303.title: Accelerated Third-Level Thai
THAI 303.subject: THAI
THAI 303.description: Continuation of THAI 202 . Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading; emphasis on modern written texts. Lab work.

THAI 401.title: Fourth-Level Thai I
THAI 401.subject: THAI
THAI 401.description: Continuation of THAI 302 / THAI 303 . Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

THAI 404.title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Thai
THAI 404.subject: THAI
THAI 404.description: Continuation of THAI 303 . Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

THAI 415.title: Thai Language in the Media
THAI 415.subject: THAI
THAI 415.description: Development of reading and aural comprehension of authentic Thai language used in print and broadcast media through reading Thai newspapers, viewing and listening to Thai television and radio programs. Oral and written reports.

THAI 451.title: Structure of Thai
THAI 451.subject: THAI
THAI 451.description: Introduction to information structure of Thai as a basis for developing reading skills. Analysis of rhetorical, sentence, and word structure from different types of written texts.

THAI 461B.title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Short Story: 1930-1969
THAI 461B.subject: THAI
THAI 461B.description: Selected readings in Thai short stories from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.

THAI 461C.title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Short Story: 1970-present
THAI 461C.subject: THAI
THAI 461C.description: Selected readings in Thai short stories from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.

THAI 462B.title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Novel: 1930-1969
THAI 462B.subject: THAI
THAI 462B.description: Selected readings in Thai novels from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews. (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.
THAI 462B.prereq_raw: THAI 402 , THAI 461B , or THAI 461C , or consent.

THAI 462C.title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Novel: 1970-present
THAI 462C.subject: THAI
THAI 462C.description: Selected readings in Thai novels from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews. (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.
THAI 462C.prereq_raw: THAI 402 , THAI 461B or THAI 461C , or consent.

THEA 100.title: Introduction to Stage, Screen, and New Media Writing
THEA 100.subject: THEA
THEA 100.description: Introduction to college level writing and information literacy for and about the stage (theatre, dance, performance), the screen (film, television), and new media (digital platforms, social media).

THEA 101.title: Introduction to World Drama and Theatre
THEA 101.subject: THEA
THEA 101.description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Performance traditions of Africa, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and the Pacific from the 5th century B.C. to the present. Analysis of political, religious, and technological conditions of theatre. Includes practical theatre workshop. Emphasis on writing instruction.

THEA 152.title: Live on Stage
THEA 152.subject: THEA
THEA 152.description: Students view locally-produced theatre and dance productions and write performance reviews. Readings, writing, and class discussion will guide students to understand each performance. Performances include theatre, dance, musical theatre, opera, and performance art.

THEA 188.title: Beginning Hula
THEA 188.subject: THEA
THEA 188.description: Designed for students with no hula experience. Introduces students to the basic foundational skills of hula and emphasizes the importance of language, basic body movements and vocal techniques.

THEA 200B.title: Beginning Practicum: performance
THEA 200B.subject: THEA
THEA 200B.description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography.
THEA 200B.prereq_raw: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

THEA 200C.title: Beginning Practicum: stagecraft
THEA 200C.subject: THEA
THEA 200C.description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography.
THEA 200C.prereq_raw: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

THEA 200D.title: Beginning Practicum: costume
THEA 200D.subject: THEA
THEA 200D.description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography.
THEA 200D.prereq_raw: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

THEA 200E.title: Beginning Practicum: performing arts management
THEA 200E.subject: THEA
THEA 200E.description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography.
THEA 200E.prereq_raw: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

THEA 200F.title: Beginning Practicum: directing dramaturgy state management choreography
THEA 200F.subject: THEA
THEA 200F.description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography.
THEA 200F.prereq_raw: (B) audition and performance of role in a Department of Theatre and Dance production; (F) consent.

THEA 201.title: Introduction to the Art of the Film
THEA 201.subject: THEA
THEA 201.description: Introduction to the aesthetics of silent and sound movies. Technical subjects analyzed only as they relate to theme and style.

THEA 205.title: Introduction to Long-Form Improvisation
THEA 205.subject: THEA
THEA 205.description: Introduction to long-form improvisation as developed by companies such as Second City and iO Chicago. Focus will be on games, situations, creating characters, and forming narratives from those elements.

THEA 214.title: Development of the Sound Film
THEA 214.subject: THEA
THEA 214.description: Growth and changes in aesthetics of the sound film from 1929 to present; films by Renoir, Welles, Eisenstein, etc.

THEA 220.title: Beginning Voice and Movement
THEA 220.subject: THEA
THEA 220.description: Introduction to vocal and movement techniques to increase self-awareness and potential for self-expression.

THEA 221.title: Introduction to Acting for Stage and Screen
THEA 221.subject: THEA
THEA 221.description: Beginning acting techniques for theatre and screen media including exercises, improvisations, monologues, and scenes. Focus on voice, relaxation, body awareness, and freedom from self-consciousness. Emphasis on writing instruction as appropriate to discipline.

THEA 222.title: Acting I: Foundations and Techniques for Stage and Screen
THEA 222.subject: THEA
THEA 222.description: Fundamentals of contemporary acting styles for stage and screen, including self-awareness, character, and scene work.
THEA 222.prereq_raw: THEA major or THEA 221 , or consent.
THEA 222.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only.

THEA 224.title: Pidgin/HCE Drama
THEA 224.subject: THEA
THEA 224.description: Introduction to Hawaiian Creole English (HCE) multicultural comedy and drama in Hawaiʻi. Emphasis on acting exercises, local dialects, and the performance of Pidgin/HCE plays.

THEA 240.title: Introduction to Stage Production
THEA 240.subject: THEA
THEA 240.description: Survey class introducing theater management, lighting, costuming, scenery, and other aspects of theatre that relate to producing stage performances.

THEA 240L.title: Theatre Production Lab
THEA 240L.subject: THEA
THEA 240L.description: Lab observations and projects illustrating basic principles of theatre production.

THEA 241.title: Film/TV Production Process
THEA 241.subject: THEA
THEA 241.description: Entry-level course details three phases of the production process for film and video projects: pre-production, production, and post-production.

THEA 245.title: Principles of Design
THEA 245.subject: THEA
THEA 245.description: Introduction to general design principles as applied to theatre. Will introduce the language and tools of visual literacy and visual communications via individual projects and collaboration.

THEA 259.title: Introduction to Voice Function and Singing Styles
THEA 259.subject: THEA
THEA 259.description: Students will study how the singing voice works in various styles, including classical, musical theater, jazz, choral, and pop/rock. Students will learn historical contexts, aural characteristics, and musical vocabulary through lecture, discussion, and listening.

THEA 288.title: Intermediate Hula
THEA 288.subject: THEA
THEA 288.description: Intermediate level hula course for students with some hula experience that builds upon existing cultural knowledge, performance and language skills. Students will prepare costumes and adornments for a public performance.

THEA 311.title: World Theatre I: Script Analysis
THEA 311.subject: THEA
THEA 311.description: Script analysis methods for world drama. Develops written and oral communication skills. Required of all majors.
THEA 311.prereq_raw: One of THEA 101 , THEA 221 , THEA 222 , THEA 240 ; or consent.

THEA 312.title: World Theatre II: Myth to Drama
THEA 312.subject: THEA
THEA 312.description: Myth and ritual into drama, 1000 BCE-1700 CE. Development of secular drama from sacred and ritual beginnings. Required of all majors.

THEA 314.title: Experimental Art and Animation
THEA 314.subject: THEA
THEA 314.description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
THEA 314.prereq_raw: CINE 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or CINE 353 / DNCE 353 / THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE 356 / DNCE 356 / THEA 356 (or concurrent).
THEA 314.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

THEA 318.title: Playwriting
THEA 318.subject: THEA
THEA 318.description: One-act plays; practice in writing in dramatic form.
THEA 318.prereq_raw: Grade of B or better in composition or consent.

children.text: Grade of B or better in composition

THEA 319.title: Screenplay Writing
THEA 319.subject: THEA
THEA 319.description: Characterization, structure, theme, image, and other components of writing for film.
THEA 319.prereq_raw: THEA 201 and grade of B or better in composition, or consent.

children.text: grade of B or better in composition,

THEA 321.title: Auditioning
THEA 321.subject: THEA
THEA 321.description: Preparation of material from different audition situations, including monologues, cold readings, dance, singing, and TV/film.

THEA 322.title: Acting II: Advanced Scene Study
THEA 322.subject: THEA
THEA 322.description: Further exploration of character development and dramatic action through textual analysis.

THEA 323.title: Film/TV Acting
THEA 323.subject: THEA
THEA 323.description: Acting techniques for film and TV production. Students appear in scenes from TV and film scripts.
THEA 323.prereq_raw: One of THEA 101 , THEA 221 , THEA 222 , COM 201 , or consent.

THEA 324.title: Advanced Film/TV Acting
THEA 324.subject: THEA
THEA 324.description: Advanced acting techniques for film and TV production. Taping/filming of scenes and full-length scripts.

THEA 325.title: Introduction to Asian Acting Styles
THEA 325.subject: THEA
THEA 325.description: Principles of acting based on traditional Asian models. Voice, movement exercises.

THEA 334.title: Taiji (T’ai Chi) for Actors I
THEA 334.subject: THEA
THEA 334.description: Basic Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) movement training.
THEA 334.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

THEA 335.title: Taiji Round Form for Actors
THEA 335.subject: THEA
THEA 335.description: Introduction to basic Asian movement skills through learning the Wu-style taijiquan round form, a faster and more fluid version of the full 108 taiji sequence of forms.
THEA 335.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

THEA 336.title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
THEA 336.subject: THEA
THEA 336.description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course.

THEA 343B.title: Topics in Theatre Production: entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas
THEA 343B.subject: THEA
THEA 343B.description: Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing exercises, color theory, and practical projects; (E) props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre.
THEA 343B.prereq_raw: any course in THEA or DNCE, or production experience; or consent.

THEA 343C.title: Topics in Theatre Production: technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas
THEA 343C.subject: THEA
THEA 343C.description: Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing exercises, color theory, and practical projects; (E) props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre.
THEA 343C.prereq_raw: any course in THEA or DNCE, or production experience; or consent.

THEA 343D.title: Topics in Theatre Production: scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing excercises, color theory, and practical projects
THEA 343D.subject: THEA
THEA 343D.description: Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing exercises, color theory, and practical projects; (E) props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre.
THEA 343D.prereq_raw: any course in THEA or DNCE, or production experience; or consent.

THEA 343E.title: Topics in Theatre Production: props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre
THEA 343E.subject: THEA
THEA 343E.description: Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing exercises, color theory, and practical projects; (E) props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre.
THEA 343E.prereq_raw: any course in THEA or DNCE, or production experience; or consent.

THEA 345.title: Lighting I: Beginning Lighting Design
THEA 345.subject: THEA
THEA 345.description: Basic principles of lighting design and associated technologies. Includes functions and properties of light, lighting and control equipment, working procedures, and drafting and paperwork techniques.

THEA 353.title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
THEA 353.subject: THEA
THEA 353.description: Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process.
THEA 353.prereq_raw: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent. (Consent required for production experience option)

children.text: ( Consent required for production experience option)

THEA 354.title: Introduction to Costume Construction
THEA 354.subject: THEA
THEA 354.description: Workshop on basic principles of costume construction for theatre and dance. Professional practices, materials, and methods.

THEA 356.title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
THEA 356.subject: THEA
THEA 356.description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices.

THEA 357.title: Stage Makeup Workshop
THEA 357.subject: THEA
THEA 357.description: Western and traditional Asian makeup theory and application practice. Western corrective, period, and old age makeup. Asian may include Jingju, Kabuki, Wayang.

THEA 360.title: Performance and Medicine
THEA 360.subject: THEA
THEA 360.description: Survey of key texts on medicine and performance, and on how these two areas intersect, including representations of medicine and illness in contemporary drama and performance-based practices within medicine.

THEA 362.title: Curtain Up! Broadway Musicals, Then and Now
THEA 362.subject: THEA
THEA 362.description: Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the “Hamilton” phenomenon, exploring their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts. Course develops written communication skills.

THEA 370.title: Movement Improvisation
THEA 370.subject: THEA
THEA 370.description: Introduces movement improvisation to all levels and disciplines. Movement studies will explore improvisation approaches, devices, elements, exercises, and implications to gain skills in and appreciation for the art of improvisation.

THEA 380.title: Beginning Directing
THEA 380.subject: THEA
THEA 380.description: Basic practical course in how to direct a play. Students will direct scenes. Emphasis on writing instruction.
THEA 380.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: upper division theatre majors or consent.

THEA 388.title: Advanced Hula I
THEA 388.subject: THEA
THEA 388.description: Advanced level hula course for students with hula experience that builds upon existing cultural knowledge, performance and language skills presented in THEA 288 / DNCE 288 .

THEA 400B.title: Advanced Practicum: performance

THEA 412.title: World Theatre: Modern
THEA 412.subject: THEA

THEA 413B.title: Approaches to Dramatic Texts: contemporary British and American drama
THEA 413B.subject: THEA
THEA 413B.description: Intensive analysis and discussion of dramatic texts from a variety of authors. Understanding trends and variations in dramatic form and content. (B) contemporary British and American drama; (C) political drama in the West.
THEA 413B.prereq_raw: one of THEA 311 , THEA 312 , THEA 411 , THEA 412 , or consent.

THEA 413C.title: Approaches to Dramatic Texts: political drama in the West
THEA 413C.subject: THEA
THEA 413C.description: Intensive analysis and discussion of dramatic texts from a variety of authors. Understanding trends and variations in dramatic form and content. (B) contemporary British and American drama; (C) political drama in the West.
THEA 413C.prereq_raw: one of THEA 311 , THEA 312 , THEA 411 , THEA 412 , or consent.

THEA 414.title: Women, Gender, & Sexuality in Performance
THEA 414.subject: THEA
THEA 414.description: Feminist and performance studies approaches to performances by women and other genders; focus on the representation and status of women

THEA 418.title: Advanced Playwriting
THEA 418.subject: THEA

THEA 421.title: Musical Theatre
THEA 421.subject: THEA
THEA 421.description: Training in skills required to perform in musicals. Students present scenes from musical comedies for criticism and review.
THEA 421.prereq_raw: one of THEA 321 , THEA 322 , MUS 231B , or consent; and/or audition.

THEA 422.title: Period Styles in Acting
THEA 422.subject: THEA
THEA 422.description: Presentational acting in comedy and tragedy; emphasis on performance styles in Elizabethan, Restoration, and 18th-century drama.

THEA 423.title: Acting Shakespeare
THEA 423.subject: THEA
THEA 423.description: Techniques for acting in Shakespearean and heightened language texts.

THEA 424.title: Hawaiian Performance Workshop
THEA 424.subject: THEA
THEA 424.description: Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Hawaiian performance forms and Hawaiian medium theatre. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique.
THEA 424.prereq_raw: one of: THEA 101 , THEA 221 , THEA 224 , THEA 468 , HAW 202 , HAW 321 , HAW 384 , HAW 486 , DNCE 312 , DNCE 411 , DNCE 412 ; or consent.

THEA 426.title: South/Southeast Asian Acting Workshop
THEA 426.subject: THEA
THEA 426.description: Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional south and southeast Asian theatre forms. Emphasis on movement and vocal techniques.

THEA 427.title: Chinese Acting Workshop
THEA 427.subject: THEA
THEA 427.description: Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Chinese theatre forms. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique.
THEA 427.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only.

THEA 428.title: Japanese Acting Workshop
THEA 428.subject: THEA
THEA 428.description: Training in skills and techniques for selected traditional Japanese theatre forms. Emphasis on movement and vocal technique.

THEA 429.title: Contemporary Performance Practices
THEA 429.subject: THEA
THEA 429.description: Focus on individual training in the skills and techniques of contemporary experimental theatre including acting, directing, and self-scripting.
THEA 429.prereq_raw: one of THEA 222 , THEA 318 , THEA 380 , or consent.

THEA 432.title: Stage Combat
THEA 432.subject: THEA
THEA 432.description: Techniques for performing unarmed and armed stage combat.
THEA 432.prereq_raw: one of THEA 221 , THEA 222 , THEA 321 , THEA 322 ; or consent.

THEA 433.title: Movement Workshop
THEA 433.subject: THEA
THEA 433.description: Special workshops in movement relating to specific departmental theatrical productions beyond the scope of movement taught in THEA 437 and THEA 438.

THEA 434.title: Taiji (T’ai Chi) for Actors II
THEA 434.subject: THEA
THEA 434.description: Intermediate-level Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) movement training.

THEA 435.title: Movement for Actors
THEA 435.subject: THEA
THEA 435.description: Training actors to discover experientially the sources of movement; to teach skills for analyzing movement for its mechanical, anatomical, spatial, and dynamic content; and then to apply these skills in a role.

THEA 436.title: Advanced Movement for Actors
THEA 436.subject: THEA
THEA 436.description: Detailed development of material presented in THEA 435 . Focus on Bartenieff fundamentals and movement analysis as it applies to the physical interpretation of theatrical roles.
THEA 436.prereq_raw: one of THEA 435 , DNCE 435 , or consent.

THEA 439.title: Musical Theatre Dance Forms
THEA 439.subject: THEA
THEA 439.description: Theatrical dance forms used in 20th-century musical theatre.
THEA 439.prereq_raw: 100 level or above dance technique class, THEA 421 , or consent.

children.text: level or above dance technique class, THEA 421 , or consent

THEA 446.title: Topics in Costume Construction
THEA 446.subject: THEA
THEA 446.description: Costume production techniques, both Western and Asian, for theatre and dance. Topic rotation includes: understructures and armatures, patterning, tailoring, dyeing, fabric modification, millenery and crafts, within the context of current industry practice.

THEA 447.title: Stage Management
THEA 447.subject: THEA
THEA 447.description: Business, organization and management for theatre and dance productions.
THEA 447.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

THEA 448.title: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design for the Theatre
THEA 448.subject: THEA
THEA 448.description: Basic concepts and techniques of 2D computer-aided design. Lecture/workshop covers language and commands common to most CAD packages with a focus on drafting specific to theatre. A laptop with Vectorworks installed is required.

THEA 456.title: Costumes II: Intermediate Costume Design
THEA 456.subject: THEA
THEA 456.description: Advanced costume design for theatre and dance. Introduction to collaborative process in costume. Intensive work on rendering skills, applied to various design problems. Cost analysis and organizational techniques.

THEA 462.title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
THEA 462.subject: THEA
THEA 462.description: Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawaiʻi, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand.

THEA 464.title: Drama and Theatre of Southeast Asia and India
THEA 464.subject: THEA
THEA 464.description: Court, folk, popular traditions, and the manner of their production.

THEA 465.title: Drama and Theatre of China
THEA 465.subject: THEA
THEA 465.description: Yuan, southern, spoken drama; Beijing opera and the manner of their production.

THEA 466.title: Drama and Theatre of Japan
THEA 466.subject: THEA
THEA 466.description: Survey of Japanese theatre forms, from traditional to contemporary. Includes examination of dramatic texts, performance elements, and historical context, utilizing written, aural, and visual materials. Emphasis on writing instruction.
THEA 466.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or above.

THEA 468.title: Drama and Theatre of Hawaiʻi
THEA 468.subject: THEA
THEA 468.description: Survey of indigenous theatre forms of Hawaiʻi, Native Hawaiian, and other ethnic playwrights, and contemporary multicultural landscape of drama and theatre in Hawaiʻi.
THEA 468.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

THEA 469.title: Chinese Music and Sound Culture
THEA 469.subject: THEA
THEA 469.description: Situates the Chinese musical sound in the interdisciplinary field of sound culture. Students will learn to read music literature and listen to historical sounds critically and to analyze aspects of Chinese sound culture.

THEA 470.title: Creative Drama
THEA 470.subject: THEA
THEA 470.description: Dramatic activities for young people. For teachers, group workers, recreation majors, and others dealing with children. Supervised field activities.

THEA 472.title: Masked Performance
THEA 472.subject: THEA
THEA 472.description: History, techniques, construction, and performance of theatrical masks.
THEA 472.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

THEA 473.title: Storytelling
THEA 473.subject: THEA
THEA 473.description: Storytelling development through focused activities on personal artistic practice, story content, and public performative techniques.

THEA 474.title: Theatre for Young Audiences
THEA 474.subject: THEA
THEA 474.description: Theories and principles of formal theatre for young audiences. Study of and practice in the selection, direction, and production of plays.

THEA 475.title: Puppetry for Young Children
THEA 475.subject: THEA
THEA 475.description: Methods of constructing puppets and stages with and for children 3 to 8 years of age. Use of puppets in the creative arts. Fieldwork.

THEA 476.title: Puppetry
THEA 476.subject: THEA
THEA 476.description: History and scope of puppetry. Construction and presentation of puppets for adult and child audiences.

THEA 477.title: Giant Puppetry
THEA 477.subject: THEA
THEA 477.description: History, construction, and performance techniques for large-scale and giant puppets. For teachers, recreation directors, and others working with students aged 10 to 18 and adults.

THEA 478.title: Hula Kiʻi: Hawaiian Puppetry and Image Dancing
THEA 478.subject: THEA
THEA 478.description: History, techniques, construction, and performance of Hawaiian puppetry and traditional image dancing.
THEA 478.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

THEA 488.title: Advanced Hula II: Traditional and Modern Hula Choreography
THEA 488.subject: THEA
THEA 488.description: Advanced hula course designed for students with extensive hula and language experience. It shares hula choreography of the same hula in both hula kahiko and hula auana.

THEA 490.title: Experimental Theatre Studio
THEA 490.subject: THEA
THEA 490.description: Working collectively, students research, write, design, develop, and perform a full-length production.
THEA 490.prereq_raw: 6 credits above the 200 level in acting, directing, playwriting, dancing; or consent.

THEA 612.title: Theatre in Europe: Classical to 1700
THEA 612.subject: THEA

THEA 616.title: Script Analysis

THEA 619.subject: THEA

THEA 620.title: Advanced Voice for the Actor
THEA 620.subject: THEA

THEA 621.title: Great Roles in Acting
THEA 621.subject: THEA

THEA 621.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

THEA 625.title: Experimenting with Asian Acting Styles
THEA 625.subject: THEA
THEA 625.description: Integration of movement, vocal technique, and concepts of traditional Asian genres into the actor’s repertory. Exploration of application to contemporary Asian and non-Asian texts. Workshop format.
THEA 625.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

THEA 626.title: Advanced Topics in Performance
THEA 626.subject: THEA

THEA 626.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

THEA 634.title: Taiji Weapons for Actors
THEA 634.subject: THEA
THEA 634.description: Advanced level Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) weapons training.

THEA 641.title: Historic Costume and Decor
THEA 641.subject: THEA
THEA 641.description: Overview of visual styles in fashion, textiles, architecture, ornament, and furniture for production and entertainment design through lecture, lab, and discussion.

THEA 642.title: Drawing and Rendering for Performing Arts
THEA 642.subject: THEA
THEA 642.description: Exploration of materials and principles of drawing and rendering for the performing arts through lecture and studio practice. Focus placed on rendering as a mode of communication for designers and technicians in the performing arts.
THEA 642.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

THEA 644.title: Lighting II: Intermediate Lighting Design
THEA 644.subject: THEA
THEA 644.description: Workshop in intermediate techniques and skills of lighting design; storytelling, analysis, research, envisioning, and communicating a design plan, execution of successful design projects. Use of communication tools such as mini-plots, light renderings, LightWright, and VectorWorks.
THEA 644.prereq_raw: THEA 345 (with a minimum grade of B) or equivalent experience.

THEA 645.title: Lighting III: Advanced Lighting Design
THEA 645.subject: THEA
THEA 645.description: Workshop dealing with special topics in theatrical lighting design and related skills.
THEA 645.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

THEA 650.title: Professional Advancement in Entertainment Design
THEA 650.subject: THEA
THEA 650.description: Directed study designed to help MFA candidates in Design acquire the tools helpful in obtaining future employment. Portfolios, resumes, and related application tools will be developed along with other necessary skills. Must be current MFA candidate in theatre.
THEA 650.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

THEA 652.title: Scenic II: Intermediate Scene Design
THEA 652.subject: THEA
THEA 652.description: Workshop in advanced techniques and skills of scenic design; research, presentation, rendering, drafting, and model making.
THEA 652.prereq_raw: THEA 353 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

THEA 653.title: Scenic III: Advanced Scenic Design
THEA 653.subject: THEA
THEA 653.description: Workshop dealing with special topics in scenic design, related skills, and portfolio preparation.

THEA 654.title: Advanced Topics in Costume Construction
THEA 654.subject: THEA
THEA 654.description: Advanced costume production techniques for entertainment design. Topics may include corset, draping, patterning, tailoring, dye work, fabric modification, millinery, leatherwork, and crafts. Topics presented within the context of both current entertainment industry and traditional practices.
THEA 654.prereq_raw: THEA 354 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

THEA 656.title: Costumes III: Advanced Costume Design
THEA 656.subject: THEA
THEA 656.description: Workshop dealing with special topics in costume design and related skills.

THEA 657.title: Seminar in Design
THEA 657.subject: THEA
THEA 657.description: Research, design, and discussion exploring collaborative design problems and solutions.

THEA 658.title: Business for the Arts
THEA 658.subject: THEA
THEA 658.description: Seminar offering overview and foundation for launching or advancing enterprises in the arts. A focus on the processes and method for creating economically successful grants and project development applications.

THEA 660.title: Field Research Methods
THEA 660.subject: THEA
THEA 660.description: Goals and methods. Grant writing, interview, questionnaire, observation, and performance study as research techniques. Practical application by designing a research project.

THEA 663B.title: Topics in Asian Theatre: origins
THEA 663B.subject: THEA
THEA 663B.description: Comparative and cross-cultural examination. (B) origins; (C) theories and systems; (D) modern Asian drama.

THEA 663C.title: Topics in Asian Theatre: theories and systems
THEA 663C.subject: THEA
THEA 663C.description: Comparative and cross-cultural examination. (B) origins; (C) theories and systems; (D) modern Asian drama.

THEA 663D.title: Topics in Asian Theatre: modern Asian drama
THEA 663D.subject: THEA
THEA 663D.description: Comparative and cross-cultural examination. (B) origins; (C) theories and systems; (D) modern Asian drama.

THEA 668.title: Advanced Topics in Theatre of Hawaiʻi
THEA 668.subject: THEA

THEA 668.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

THEA 670.title: Seminar in Advanced Creative Dramatics
THEA 670.subject: THEA
THEA 670.description: Advanced seminar in applied methods and theories of creative dramatics.
THEA 670.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

THEA 674.title: Interdisciplinary Collaborations
THEA 674.subject: THEA
THEA 674.description: Hybrid performance works for dancers, musicians, actors, visual artists, poets, and writers to explore the nature of the collaboration process in various settings.
THEA 674.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, MUS, ART, ENG, THDN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

THEA 678B.title: Topics in Theatre for Young Audiences: production concepts
THEA 678B.subject: THEA
THEA 678B.description: Creative movement/drama, puppetry, and theatre/dance; (B) production concepts.
THEA 678B.prereq_raw: one of THEA 470 , THEA 474 , THEA 475 , THEA 476 , THEA 477 , DNCE 490 ; or consent.

THEA 680.title: Directing Multicultural Performance
THEA 680.subject: THEA
THEA 680.description: Directing multicultural/intercultural performance; development of new performance styles based on the study of diverse performance traditions from around the world; directing of scenes and one-acts.
THEA 680.prereq_raw: graduate theatre major and one directing course with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

THEA 680.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only.

THEA 681.title: Advanced Topics in Theatre Directing
THEA 681.subject: THEA

THEA 681.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only.

THEA 682.title: Graduate Workshop in Directing
THEA 682.subject: THEA

THEA 685.title: Directing Western Styles

THEA 688.title: Hula Genealogy: Lineage & Legacy
THEA 688.subject: THEA
THEA 688.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

THEA 690.title: Graduate Theatre Workshop
THEA 690.subject: THEA

THEA 690.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only.

THEA 691.title: Seminar in Teaching Dance/Theatre
THEA 691.subject: THEA

THEA 692.title: Practicum in Teaching
THEA 692.subject: THEA
THEA 692.description: Supervised teaching experience at the introductory or undergraduate level. Students will teach an appropriate level course in their field of expertise under faculty supervision.
THEA 692.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

THEA 693.title: Internship: Youth Theatre/Dance
THEA 693.subject: THEA

THEA 693.prereq_raw: one of THEA 470 , THEA 476 , or DNCE 490 ; or consent.
THEA 693.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DANC, DNTH, THDN majors only.

THEA 695.title: Creative Projects

THEA 696B.title: Professional Internship: entertainment design: costume, lighting, scenery, props, sound, or other related disciplines

THEA 779.title: Seminar in Theatre for Young Audiences
THEA 779.subject: THEA

THEA 779.prereq_raw: one of THEA 470 , THEA 474 , THEA 475 , THEA 476 , THEA 477 , or DNCE 490 .

TI 405.title: Court Interpreting I
TI 405.subject: TI
TI 405.description: Introduction to the legal system, as well as theoretical principles, ethics, practical techniques, and current issues surrounding the practice and profession of court and other legal interpreting.

TI 406.title: Community Interpreting
TI 406.subject: TI
TI 406.description: Basic principles, ethics and skills involved in community interpreting in medical, legal, and social service settings; practical information about the community interpreter’s role and profession; practice of various community interpreting situations and techniques.

TI 407.title: Court Interpreting II
TI 407.subject: TI
TI 407.description: Combined lecture/ discussion/practice. Continuation of TI 405 - Court Interpreting I , diving deeper into the practical side of oral interpreting for various proceedings, including arraignments, trials, witness testimonies, etc. Must be bilingual. Real courtroom observations required.

TI 408.title: Medical Interpreting
TI 408.subject: TI
TI 408.description: Healthcare interpreting requires students to understand basic biosystems, common illnesses and treatments, as well as interpreting skills. Students must have 402 or above equivalency of second language skills (or instructor approval).
