TI 499.subject: TI
TI 499.description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision.

TIM 099.title: International Exchange Programs
TIM 099.subject: TIM
TIM 099.description: UH Mānoa School of Travel Industry Management majors participating in approved international exchange programs.

TIM 100.title: Internship I
TIM 100.subject: TIM
TIM 100.description: Introduction to travel industry. Discussion of job search strategies, TIM internship requirements, career and academic planning.

TIM 101.title: Introduction to Travel Industry Management
TIM 101.subject: TIM
TIM 101.description: Overview of travel industry and related major business components. Analysis of links between hotel, food, transportation, recreation, and other industries comprising tourism.

TIM 102.title: Food and World Cultures
TIM 102.subject: TIM
TIM 102.description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

TIM 102A.title: Food and World Cultures
TIM 102A.subject: TIM
TIM 102A.description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

TIM 200.title: Internship II
TIM 200.subject: TIM
TIM 200.description: A minimum of two hundred hours of travel industry experience. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

TIM 300.title: Internship III
TIM 300.subject: TIM
TIM 300.description: A minimum of two hundred hours of travel industry experience. Position must be different from TIM 200 position and of a more responsible nature or in a different organization. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

TIM 301.title: Legal Environment of the Travel Industry
TIM 301.subject: TIM
TIM 301.description: Origin, development, and principles of common, statutory, constitutional, international, and maritime law relating to the travel industry, including applicable ethical precepts.

TIM 302.title: Information Systems Technology
TIM 302.subject: TIM
TIM 302.description: Computer applications in the travel industry; operation and evaluation of specific travel industry systems and applied business systems. TIM majors only.
TIM 302.prereq_raw: TIM 101 ; and either ICS 101 , or both LTEC 112 and LTEC 113 .

TIM 303.title: Management of Service Enterprises
TIM 303.subject: TIM
TIM 303.description: Principles and philosophies of management with special emphasis on those principles and theories that are most relevant to management in service-based industries. Students may not earn credit for TIM 303 and BUS 315 . TIM majors only.

TIM 304.title: Principles of Travel Industry Marketing
TIM 304.subject: TIM
TIM 304.description: Concepts, problems, processes of marketing within the travel industry; development of marketing strategies including product, place, promotion, and price for travel institutions. Students may not earn credit for TIM 304 and BUS 312 . TIM majors only.

TIM 305.title: Financial Management for the Travel Industry
TIM 305.subject: TIM
TIM 305.description: Cash flow determination and management strategies for financing hospitality ventures and expansion. Determining the financial viability of proposed and existing operations through traditional and state-of-the-art techniques. TIM majors only.
TIM 305.prereq_raw: TIM 101 , ACC 200 and ACC 210 ; and NREM 203 , MATH 203 , MATH 215 , MATH 241 , or BUS 250 .

TIM 306.title: Human Resource Management: Travel Industry
TIM 306.subject: TIM
TIM 306.description: Comprehensive overview of human resources management (HRM) with emphasis on the supervision in the travel industry, including HRM as a firm’s strategic asset, contemporary theories, issues and developments, to improve employee recruitment productivity and retention.

TIM 310.title: Institutional Purchasing
TIM 310.subject: TIM
TIM 310.description: Procurement responsibilities in hospitality management. Emphasis on institutions supplying hospitality operations and legislation which controls standards of industrial supplies and goods.
TIM 310.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM and FSHN majors only.

TIM 311.title: Club Management
TIM 311.subject: TIM
TIM 311.description: Introduction to club and institutional management, including operations, services, and facilities.

TIM 313.title: Foodservice Management
TIM 313.subject: TIM
TIM 313.description: Critical and essential aspects of managing foodservice operations including principles of food safety and sanitation, procedural knowledge in front and back of the house and guest relations.

TIM 314.title: Hotel Management
TIM 314.subject: TIM
TIM 314.description: Comprehensive understanding of hotel management and functional departments including front office, accounting, housekeeping, food and beverage, marketing, security and safety. Simulation of management trainee programs by hotel chains. Synthesis of concepts, tools and theories of decision-making relevant to hotel operations.
TIM 314.prereq_raw: TIM 101 , TIM 302 , and TIM 303 (with a minimum grade of C- in TIM 302 and TIM 303 ).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- in TIM 302 and TIM 303 )

TIM 315.title: Quality Food Management
TIM 315.subject: TIM
TIM 315.description: Explore various aspects of the quality in foodservice operations and develop strategies to measure and improve the quality.

TIM 316.title: Events Planning and Marketing
TIM 316.subject: TIM
TIM 316.description: Introduction to special event planning processes and techniques. Emphasis on designing, planning, marketing, management, staging events, legal compliances, risk management, financial control, and successful event evaluation.
TIM 316.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

TIM 319.title: Quantity Foods and Institutional Purchasing
TIM 319.subject: TIM
TIM 319.description: Quantity food and beverage operations, menu development and costing, dietary menu claims, purchasing procedures, inventory control, procurement, transportation, legislation. Institutional foodservice sanitation, Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and National Restaurant Association Certification.

TIM 320.title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
TIM 320.subject: TIM
TIM 320.description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.
TIM 320.prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 ; or consent.

TIM 321.title: Sociocultural Issues in Tourism
TIM 321.subject: TIM
TIM 321.description: Issues arising from the impacts of tourism on societies and cultures. Class discussions of the ethical dimensions of such impacts. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.

TIM 324.title: Geography of Global Tourism
TIM 324.subject: TIM
TIM 324.description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. Emphasis on Writing.
TIM 324.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

TIM 327.title: Travel Distribution Management
TIM 327.subject: TIM
TIM 327.description: History, development, operations, and management of travel distribution organizations including: travel agents, tour operators and wholesalers, specialty channelers, meeting planners, incentive houses, travel associations, and other destination management organizations. Evolution and economics of the distribution of travel products through destination databases and electronic commerce.

TIM 333.title: Hotel/Resort Facilities and Design
TIM 333.subject: TIM
TIM 333.description: Comprehensive understanding of facilities management and design including maintenance systems, sustainable development options and design and environmental management.

TIM 334.title: Hospitality Sales & Negotiation
TIM 334.subject: TIM
TIM 334.description: Personal selling by hospitality and tourism firms engaged in business-to-business marketing. Emphasis will be placed on negotiation case studies, exercises, and role-plays.

TIM 350.title: Introduction to Tourism Transportation
TIM 350.subject: TIM
TIM 350.description: Introduction to managerial and operational issues related to all modes of transportation used by tourists into or within a tourist destination. Passenger behavior; transport infrastructure; transport networks; regulation; sustainable transport.

TIM 351.title: Principles of Logistics
TIM 351.subject: TIM
TIM 351.description: Management of logistics systems: inventory control, warehousing, materials management, physical distribution, transportation. Emphasis on Hawaiʻi’s location and unique problems.

TIM 353.title: Air Transportation Management
TIM 353.subject: TIM
TIM 353.description: Marketing, management and strategies used by airlines, airports, catering, and aircraft manufacturers.

TIM 354.title: Surface Transportation Management
TIM 354.subject: TIM
TIM 354.description: Management of surface transportation such as cars, buses, intercity rail, etc. Includes marketing, ownership and financing, supply chain, operations, regulation and promotion, and human resources. Emphasis on written communication.

TIM 365.title: Economics in Travel Industry
TIM 365.subject: TIM
TIM 365.description: Microeconomic theory of consumer behavior and demand production cost analysis, market structure and pricing in travel companies. Economic impact of tourism. Students may not earn credit for TIM 365 and BUS 313 .

TIM 368.title: TIM Study Abroad
TIM 368.subject: TIM
TIM 368.description: Study abroad instructional experience emphasizing international travel, tourism and hospitality-related topics at equivalent, accredited programs. Content varies depending on locus of instruction and instructor. Course qualifies as either a TIM or general elective with pre-approval or department.

TIM 399.description: Reading and research into problems in hotel, restaurant, transportation or tourism sectors of the travel industry.
TIM 399.prereq_raw: A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and consent of dean’s office and instructor based upon student’s written proposal of content and objectives of course program.

TIM 400B.title: Internship IV: executive internship
TIM 400B.subject: TIM
TIM 400B.description: Requires a minimum of 150 hours of internship, a business presentation, and an analytical report synthesizing experience and related theories. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, which will enhance and improve students’ writing skills. (B) executive internship; (C) community service internship. Restricted to majors.

TIM 400C.title: Internship IV: community service internship
TIM 400C.subject: TIM
TIM 400C.description: Requires a minimum of 150 hours of internship, a business presentation, and an analytical report synthesizing experience and related theories. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, which will enhance and improve students’ writing skills. (B) executive internship; (C) community service internship. Restricted to majors.

TIM 401.title: Resort, Spa and Wellness Management
TIM 401.subject: TIM
TIM 401.description: Principles of resort and spa development. Essential aspects of understanding the leadership and interrelationships of managing/operating and marketing resorts, spas, and wellness.

TIM 402.title: Resort Mixed Use Development
TIM 402.subject: TIM
TIM 402.description: Critical and essential aspects of developing and managing resort mixed use facilities. Includes multidimensional and dynamic interrelationships of site development and facilities, business mix, management structures and systems, and industry practices.
TIM 402.prereq_raw: TIM 313 or TIM 369 ; and TIM 314 . Recommended: TIM 333 and TIM 401 .

TIM 403.title: Revenue Management in Travel Industry
TIM 403.subject: TIM
TIM 403.description: An in-depth comprehensive introduction to the theory and practice of revenue management and provides recognition of thorough knowledge of the fundamental metrics and methodologies used within the hotel industry.

TIM 415.title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
TIM 415.subject: TIM
TIM 415.description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems.
TIM 415.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

TIM 420.title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
TIM 420.subject: TIM
TIM 420.description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

TIM 425.title: Destination Development and Marketing
TIM 425.subject: TIM
TIM 425.description: Analysis of key factors in the marketing and management of tourism destinations, including destination branding, product development, integrated marketing, stakeholder relations, and the role of destination marketing/marketing organizations. Emphasis on written communication.

TIM 431.title: Strategic Management for the Travel/ Hospitality Industry
TIM 431.subject: TIM
TIM 431.description: Strategic management in the travel/hospitality industry. Case study analysis, discussion and written reports, covering strategies, management problems and industry issues. Emphasis on writing instruction.
TIM 431.prereq_raw: TIM 301 , TIM 302 , TIM 303 , TIM 304 , TIM 305 and graduating senior.

TIM 442.title: Advanced Topics in Transportation
TIM 442.subject: TIM
TIM 442.description: Advanced level of discussion in terms of transportation, including management, economics, strategy, regulation, operating performance, fleet management, and network management. Emphasis on written communication.

TIM 462.title: Environmental Management Systems
TIM 462.subject: TIM
TIM 462.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
TIM 462.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

TIM 601.title: Research Application in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
TIM 601.subject: TIM
TIM 601.description: Analysis of methodologies appropriate for research in travel industry management. Survey of the literature of applied techniques and approaches including exploratory approaches. Familiarization with research design and implementation of development of research proposals.
TIM 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 602.title: Strategic Marketing in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
TIM 602.subject: TIM
TIM 602.description: In-depth study of marketing principles and problems related to travel industry organizations. Emphasis on strategic marketing. Research applications, international and domestic marketing of travel industry services.
TIM 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 603.title: Information Technology, e-Commerce, and Travel Industry in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
TIM 603.subject: TIM
TIM 603.description: Planning, implementation, management, evaluation, and impact of information and electronic communication technologies, including e-commerce applications in the travel industry. Analysis of new information technology use as an area of research and strategic application.
TIM 603.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 604.title: Managerial Accounting for Travel Industry
TIM 604.subject: TIM
TIM 604.description: Advanced study of management accounting within travel industry: responsibility accounting, pricing decisions, concepts and application of central systems, financial planning, price level impacts, performance evaluation.
TIM 604.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 605.title: Hospitality Management
TIM 605.subject: TIM
TIM 605.description: Advanced human relations and operating issues; use of accounting, behavioral, financial, marketing, and informational systems in managing hospitality organizations.
TIM 605.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 606.title: Managerial Economics in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
TIM 606.subject: TIM
TIM 606.description: Advanced study analysis of economics and management of passenger transportation systems serving the travel industry. Emphasis on topics such as government policy, transport economics, marketing and management, and the relationships between transportation systems and tourism development.
TIM 606.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 607.title: Global Tourism Analysis
TIM 607.subject: TIM
TIM 607.description: International trade theory and regional analysis methodologies applied to tourism and the service industry, including travel balance account, inter-regional transactions flow, economic impacts, environmental economics, demand theory and forecasting.
TIM 607.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 640.title: Financial Management in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
TIM 640.subject: TIM
TIM 640.description: Applications of financial analysis to both the domestic and international travel industry.
TIM 640.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TIM 645.title: Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation Field Studies
TIM 645.subject: TIM
TIM 645.description: Integration of concepts and application of knowledge and skills from other courses to a selected field study project.
TIM 645.prereq_raw: Any two 600-level TIM courses completed and a third concurrent; or consent.

TIM 694.title: Professional Paper
TIM 694.subject: TIM
TIM 694.description: Independent project or paper under faculty supervision in lieu of Plan A, TIM 700 thesis. Requires proposal approved by supervisor and graduate chair prior to registration.
TIM 694.prereq_raw: Three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent.

TIM 695.title: Seminar: Travel Industry Management Policy
TIM 695.subject: TIM
TIM 695.description: Integration of learning through analysis of policy issues, trends, and problems in the travel industry.
TIM 695.prereq_raw: Three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent.

TIM 699.title: Directed Reading
TIM 699.subject: TIM
TIM 699.description: Independent study of approved, advanced reading with faculty supervision. Requires proposal prepared by student and approved by supervisor and graduate chair before registration.

TIM 700.title: Thesis Research
TIM 700.subject: TIM
TIM 700.description: Independent supervised research. Formal and oral written presentation of research findings.

TIM 702.title: Advanced Topics in Global Tourism Management
TIM 702.subject: TIM
TIM 702.description: Sustainable management of global tourism to minimize its negative impacts and optimize its positive ones. Deliberation and analysis of major issues related to global tourism from the perspectives of ethics and sustainability. PhD students only.
TIM 702.prereq_raw: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B.

TIM 703.title: Advanced Topics in Global Hospitality Management
TIM 703.subject: TIM
TIM 703.description: Advanced hospitality management aims to critically explore the key areas that comprise hospitality management, integrate theories and practice, and explore the linkages between hospitality research, management, and business strategies. PhD students only.
TIM 703.prereq_raw: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B.

TIM 704.title: Advanced Topics in Global Transportation Management
TIM 704.subject: TIM
TIM 704.description: Transport economics and management, and their applications for the travel and tourism industry. Focuses on analytical thinking, problem-solving. and research skills using transportation issues. PhD students only.
TIM 704.prereq_raw: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B.

TONG 101.title: Beginning Tongan
TONG 101.subject: TONG
TONG 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

TONG 201.title: Intermediate Tongan
TONG 201.subject: TONG
TONG 201.description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

TPSS 120B.title: Plants for People: beverage crops
TPSS 120B.subject: TPSS
TPSS 120B.description: The origins: social, cultural, and ceremonial traditions; culture; food and nutritional properties. Processing of a variety of tropical horticultural plants are presented, with tasting sessions and optional field trips. Topics will rotate among (B) beverage crops (e.g., coffee, tea, chocolate, kava, fruit juices); (C) herbs, spices, and flavoring (selection of examples to be determined); (D) tropical fruits (assortment offered depends on availability during semester); (E) ornamental plants (flowers, houseplants, popular landscape plans, bonsai, ethnic ornamentals). Does not count towards TPSS major.

TPSS 120C.title: Plants for People: herbs, spices, and flavoring
TPSS 120C.subject: TPSS
TPSS 120C.description: The origins: social, cultural, and ceremonial traditions; culture; food and nutritional properties. TPSS 120E.subject: TPSS

Does not count towards TPSS major.

TPSS 156.title: Sustainable Food and Energy (Field Course)
TPSS 156.subject: TPSS
TPSS 156.description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawaiʻi for sustainable development.

TPSS 156L.title: Natural History Field Trips on Hawaiʻi Island
TPSS 156L.subject: TPSS
TPSS 156L.description: Field trips for Natural history and Conservation of the Hawaiian Islands.

TPSS 200.title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
TPSS 200.subject: TPSS
TPSS 200.description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi as a model system.

TPSS 210.title: Aquaponics
TPSS 210.subject: TPSS
TPSS 210.description: Basic online course integrates aquaculture (raising fish and prawns) with hydroponics plant cultivation in water. Includes the basic design and construction of an aquaponics feed system.

TPSS 220.title: Organic Food Crop Production
TPSS 220.subject: TPSS
TPSS 220.description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors.

TPSS 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
TPSS 251.subject: TPSS
TPSS 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

TPSS 300.title: Tropical Production Systems
TPSS 300.subject: TPSS
TPSS 300.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Comparisons and contrasts of crop management systems, techniques, and technologies in protected and open field production of tropical crops.

TPSS 304.title: Fundamentals of Soil Science
TPSS 304.subject: TPSS
TPSS 304.description: Origin, development, properties, management of tropical soils; classification of Hawaiian soils.
TPSS 304.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

TPSS 304L.title: Fundamentals of Soil Science Laboratory
TPSS 304L.subject: TPSS
TPSS 304L.description: Field and analytical methods for exploring the origin, development, properties, and management of soils, with an emphasis on tropical and Hawaiian soils.
TPSS 304L.prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C.

TPSS 311.title: Current Topics in Plant Science
TPSS 311.subject: TPSS
TPSS 311.description: Undergraduate seminar that provides the presentation and discussion of topics of current relevance to students preparing for careers in applied plant sciences. Oral focus designation.
TPSS 311.prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 or NREM 210 , or consent.

TPSS 322.title: Farm & Food Marketing
TPSS 322.subject: TPSS
TPSS 322.description: Problems, agencies, functions, costs, prices, regulations affecting marketing: proposed improvements.

TPSS 333.title: Applied Statistics for Food and Landscape Systems
TPSS 333.subject: TPSS
TPSS 333.description: Designed for students interested in developing a critical framework for understanding different ways of measuring, visualizing, and interpreting the different goals humans have for agroecosystems.

TPSS 336.title: Renewable Energy and Society
TPSS 336.subject: TPSS
TPSS 336.description: Combined lecture/discussion regarding the ability of renewable energy technologies to meet local, national, and global energy demands and their potential impacts on the environment and society.

TPSS 341.title: Managerial Accounting
TPSS 341.subject: TPSS
TPSS 341.description: Principles and methods of agricultural accounting. Preparing and interpreting financial statements. Sources and costs of credit, capital budgeting, tax management, estate planning.
TPSS 341.prereq_raw: ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , or consent.

TPSS 350.title: Tropical Landscape Practices
TPSS 350.subject: TPSS
TPSS 350.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Concepts and techniques of landscape installation and management in the tropics.
TPSS 350.prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and TPSS 369 ; or consent.

TPSS 351.title: Enterprise Management
TPSS 351.subject: TPSS
TPSS 351.description: Introduction of practical concepts and methods used in business management. Introduce broad range of business strategies. Understand the critical role each strategy plays. Facilitate student’s practice of analytical and critical thinking through case studies.

TPSS 352.title: Landscape Architecture History
TPSS 352.subject: TPSS
TPSS 352.description: Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes.

TPSS 353.title: Landscape Graphics Studio
TPSS 353.subject: TPSS
TPSS 353.description: Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics.

TPSS 354.title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
TPSS 354.subject: TPSS
TPSS 354.description: Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale.

TPSS 364.title: Horticulture: Theory and Practice
TPSS 364.subject: TPSS
TPSS 364.description: Techniques of culture and management of horticulture crops.

TPSS 369.title: Ornamental Plant Materials
TPSS 369.subject: TPSS
TPSS 369.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, origin, use, and cultural requirement of trees, shrubs, vines, and groundcovers used in Hawaiian landscapes.

TPSS 371.title: Genetics: Theory to Application
TPSS 371.subject: TPSS
TPSS 371.description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

TPSS 401.title: Vegetable Crop Production
TPSS 401.subject: TPSS
TPSS 401.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Crop biology, requirements, and production techniques for commercial vegetable production in Hawaiʻi will be stressed.

TPSS 402.title: Flower and Foliage Crop Production
TPSS 402.subject: TPSS
TPSS 402.description: Biology and production of cut flowers, blooming potted plants, foliage plants under field and protected cultivation in Hawaiʻi and globally.

TPSS 403.title: Tropical Fruit Production
TPSS 403.subject: TPSS
TPSS 403.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices and recent innovations in tropical and subtropical fruit crops, emphasizing botanical aspects and commercial production in Hawaiʻi and beyond.

TPSS 405.title: Turfgrass Management
TPSS 405.subject: TPSS
TPSS 405.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Adaptability and selection, establishment, and cultural practices of grasses for various types of turf.

TPSS 409.title: Cultural Biogeography
TPSS 409.subject: TPSS
TPSS 409.description: Co-evolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens.
TPSS 409.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

TPSS 410.title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
TPSS 410.subject: TPSS
TPSS 410.description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

TPSS 415.title: Extension Education & Outreach
TPSS 415.subject: TPSS
TPSS 415.description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program develoopment and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures.
TPSS 415.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

TPSS 416.title: Introduction to Social, Ethical and Political Issues Associated with Biotechnology
TPSS 416.subject: TPSS
TPSS 416.description: Introduces concepts of biotechnology, fundamental issues associated with use of this technology, with special emphasis on agricultural biotechnology.
TPSS 416.prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 or BIOL 171 or NREM 210 , or consent.

TPSS 418.title: Turfgrass Pest Management
TPSS 418.subject: TPSS
TPSS 418.description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawaiʻi, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

TPSS 420.title: Plant Propagation
TPSS 420.subject: TPSS
TPSS 420.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Theoretical and applied aspects of seed and vegetative propagation technology involving fruits, flowers, vegetables, and landscape plants.

TPSS 421.title: Tropical Seed Science
TPSS 421.subject: TPSS
TPSS 421.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of seed science, seed physiology, seed production, and genetic modification. Hawaiʻi’s seed industry and biotechnology.

TPSS 429.title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
TPSS 429.subject: TPSS
TPSS 429.description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
TPSS 429.prereq_raw: ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and ECON 321 or NREM 310 ; or consent.

TPSS 430.title: Nursery Management
TPSS 430.subject: TPSS
TPSS 430.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices in production and operations of commercial nurseries in Hawaiʻi.
TPSS 430.prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and TPSS 364 ; or consent.

TPSS 431.title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
TPSS 431.subject: TPSS
TPSS 431.description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems.
TPSS 431.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

TPSS 432.title: The Biology of Fungi
TPSS 432.subject: TPSS
TPSS 432.description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
TPSS 432.prereq_raw: BOT 201 or BIOL 172 with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

TPSS 432L.title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
TPSS 432L.subject: TPSS
TPSS 432L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

TPSS 435.title: Environmental Soil Chemistry
TPSS 435.subject: TPSS
TPSS 435.description: Study of soil chemical processes such as weathering, adsorption, precipitation, and ion exchange; causes of soil acidity, alkalinity, and salinity; reactions between soils and fertilizers, pesticides, or heavy metals. Management strategies to minimize environmental contamination by nitrate, phosphate, and trace elements such as As, Pb, and Se.

TPSS 437.title: Applied UAS Operations for Agriculture and Environment
TPSS 437.subject: TPSS
TPSS 437.description: Applied operations with uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), mission planning, safety, photogrammetry and GIS, personnel management, and payload operation. Focus on topics required for commercial certifications as a remote pilot, agricultural operator, and pesticide applicator.
TPSS 437.prereq_raw: completion of FS/FQ, DP, DB, and DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

children.text: DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-

TPSS 440.title: Tissue Culture/Transformation
TPSS 440.subject: TPSS
TPSS 440.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of plant tissue culture for plant scientists; study of the growth and development of plant tissues in culture as influenced by chemical and environmental factors, and the regeneration of plants following plant transformation by biolistics and other molecular approaches.

TPSS 450.title: Sustainable Nutrient Management in Agroecosystems
TPSS 450.subject: TPSS
TPSS 450.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Biological, chemical, and physical processes governing the cycling of nutrients in agroecosystems, crop and livestock production, and the effects on surrounding unmanaged ecosystems.
TPSS 450.prereq_raw: ( TPSS 304 and CHEM 161 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

TPSS 453.title: Plant Breeding and Genetics
TPSS 453.subject: TPSS
TPSS 453.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Unique aspects of plant genetics and applications to crop improvement, with emphasis on breeding plants in Hawaiʻi.

TPSS 460.title: Soil Plant Environment
TPSS 460.subject: TPSS
TPSS 460.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Bio-physical processes in the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum that influence crop growth and development. Methods to estimate the impact of soil and climate on crop performance. Use of crop models to simulate effects of planting date, plant spacing and density, fertilizer rate, rainfall or irrigation, and daily weather on crop yield and farm income.
TPSS 460.prereq_raw: TPSS 304 and either PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 , or consent.

TPSS 463.title: Irrigation and Water Management
TPSS 463.subject: TPSS
TPSS 463.description: Basic soil-water-plant relationships, irrigation water requirements, irrigation efficiencies, different methods of irrigation, planning, design and management of an irrigation system, fertigation and impact of irrigation on soil and water quality.
TPSS 463.prereq_raw: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 (or equivalent), or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 ( or equivalent), or consent

TPSS 470.title: Plant Physiology
TPSS 470.subject: TPSS
TPSS 470.description: Integration of form and function from cellular to whole plant levels in processes from seed germination, through photosynthesis, growth, and morphogenesis, to flowering and senescence.

TPSS 470L.title: Principles of Plant Physiology Lab
TPSS 470L.subject: TPSS
TPSS 470L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Principles of experimentation in plant physiology, includes individual investigations.

TPSS 473.title: Post-Harvest Physiology
TPSS 473.subject: TPSS
TPSS 473.description: Comparative physiological and biochemical processes during growth, maturation, ripening, and senescence in fruits, vegetables, and flowers related to changes in quality and storage life. Tropical commodities emphasized.
TPSS 473.prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 , BIOL 171 , or BOT 201 ; CHEM 152 ; or consent.

TPSS 475.title: Plant Nutrient Diagnosis in the Tropics
TPSS 475.subject: TPSS
TPSS 475.description: Designed for students to identify essential nutrients required by plants; diagnose nutrient disorders in plants; and propose environmentally sound solutions to correct disorders.

TPSS 480.title: Life in the Soil Environment
TPSS 480.subject: TPSS
TPSS 480.description: An interdisciplinary study of the diverse life in the soil beneath our feet that includes bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, invertebrate, viruses, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
TPSS 480.prereq_raw: TPSS 371 / PEPS 371 / SUST 371 or BIOL 375 , or MICR 351 , or consent.

TPSS 480L.title: Life in the Soil Environment Lab
TPSS 480L.subject: TPSS
TPSS 480L.description: Laboratory to accompany TPSS 480 . Technical examination of bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, and other invertebrate, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
TPSS 480L.prereq_raw: BIOL 171L and BIOL 172L , or MICR 351L , or consent.

TPSS 481.title: Weed Science
TPSS 481.subject: TPSS
TPSS 481.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Weed classification, identification, adaptations for weediness; principles of weed control; properties, uses, and action of herbicides. Lab: pesticide application equipment and techniques, no-till farming, greenhouse and field experiments.
TPSS 481.prereq_raw: ( TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and CHEM 152 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

TPSS 484.title: Plants in Design
TPSS 484.subject: TPSS
TPSS 484.description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples.

TPSS 491.title: Experimental Topics
TPSS 491.subject: TPSS
TPSS 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

TPSS 492.title: Internship
TPSS 492.subject: TPSS
TPSS 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

TPSS 492L.title: Internship Experience
TPSS 492L.subject: TPSS
TPSS 492L.description: Internship field experience for TPSS majors.

TPSS 499.title: Directed Studies
TPSS 499.subject: TPSS
TPSS 499.description: Supervised individual instruction in field laboratory and library.

TPSS 601.title: Crop Modeling
TPSS 601.subject: TPSS
TPSS 601.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of modeling crop growth and development, model types, techniques, simulation. Modeling influence of climate/environment on phenology, growth, development of horticultural crops.

TPSS 603.title: Experimental Design
TPSS 603.subject: TPSS
TPSS 603.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design of experiments and variance analyses in biological and agricultural research.
TPSS 603.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

TPSS 604.title: Advanced Soil Microbiology
TPSS 604.subject: TPSS
TPSS 604.description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Study of biochemical and biogeochemical transformations mediated by soil microorganisms, emphasis on processes important to plant growth productivity and environmental quality.

TPSS 610.title: Nutrition of Tropical Crops
TPSS 610.subject: TPSS
TPSS 610.description: (1 2-hr Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Mineral nutrition of plants in relation to plant metabolism, mechanisms of ion uptake, long-distance transport of solutes, and interactions at the root-soil interface. Special emphasis on problems associated with tropical crops.

TPSS 611.title: Professional Development
TPSS 611.subject: TPSS
TPSS 611.description: Lecture/discussion targets students exiting from graduate degree programs and provides preparation as a career professional; topics include establishing a professional identity; CV and cover letters, job-seeking due diligence, and negotiation skills.
TPSS 611.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TPSS 614.title: Molecular Genetics of Crops
TPSS 614.subject: TPSS
TPSS 614.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Applications of molecular genetics to crop improvement.
TPSS 614.prereq_raw: ( TPSS 453 and MBBE 402 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

TPSS 615.title: Quantitative Genomics and Evolution
TPSS 615.subject: TPSS
TPSS 615.description: Overview and lab-based course exploring theory and methods to understand genome evolution and adaptation; focus will be on a range of organisms.

TPSS 620.title: Plant Biochemistry
TPSS 620.subject: TPSS
TPSS 620.description: Comprehensive study of chemical constituents and biochemical processes unique to the plant kingdom with emphasis on selected aspects of current interest.
TPSS 620.prereq_raw: MBBE 402 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

TPSS 634.title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
TPSS 634.subject: TPSS
TPSS 634.description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawaiʻi and the tropics.

TPSS 640.title: Advanced Soil Chemistry
TPSS 640.subject: TPSS
TPSS 640.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Physio-chemical processes in soils and soil solutions, with emphasis on ionic equilibria, mineral stability, organic complexation, and surface sorption of major plant nutrients and heavy metals.

TPSS 650.title: Soil Plant Nutrient Relations
TPSS 650.subject: TPSS
TPSS 650.description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Soil-plant interactions, emphasis on characteristics of tropical soils and plants influencing nutrient uptake by plants. Diagnostic methods to identify nutrient deficiencies and element toxicity.
TPSS 650.prereq_raw: TPSS 450 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

TPSS 652.title: Information Research Skills
TPSS 652.subject: TPSS
TPSS 652.description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

TPSS 654.title: Communications in the Sciences
TPSS 654.subject: TPSS
TPSS 654.description: (3-hr Lec/Lab combination) Laboratory-type course for improving communication abilities in the sciences and engineering. Presentations to lay audiences are emphasized. Hands-on experience in techniques and methods is provided.

TPSS 656.title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
TPSS 656.subject: TPSS
TPSS 656.description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design.
TPSS 656.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TPSS and LAND majors only.

TPSS 657.title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
TPSS 657.subject: TPSS
TPSS 657.description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review.
TPSS 657.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent.

TPSS 658.title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
TPSS 658.subject: TPSS
TPSS 658.description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes.

TPSS 664.title: Orchidology
TPSS 664.subject: TPSS
TPSS 664.description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Classification, culture, cytogenetics, breeding of orchids.
TPSS 664.prereq_raw: Consent. Recommended: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and TPSS 402 .

TPSS 667.title: Graduate Seminar
TPSS 667.subject: TPSS
TPSS 667.description: Presentation of research reports; reviews of current literature in plant and soil sciences.
TPSS 667.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

TPSS 670.title: Sustainability of Food Systems
TPSS 670.subject: TPSS
TPSS 670.description: Explores sustainability and resilience of food systems with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi, using interdisciplinary approaches to assess impacts.

TPSS 674.title: Plant Growth and Development
TPSS 674.subject: TPSS
TPSS 674.description: Contemporary literature is used as the basis for understanding the physiology for whole plant growth and development. Aspects covered include vegetative and reproductive development, seed dormancy, senescence, abscission, and relevant biochemical and molecular processes.

TPSS 680.title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
TPSS 680.subject: TPSS
TPSS 680.description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included.

TPSS 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
TPSS 695.subject: TPSS
TPSS 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
TPSS 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in TPSS program.

TPSS 711.title: Special Topics
TPSS 711.subject: TPSS
TPSS 711.description: Specialized topics from various areas of plant and soil research such as experimental techniques, growth regulation, morphogenesis, genetics and breeding, culture and nutrition of tropical crops.

TRMD 350.title: One Health: Preparing for the Next Pandemic
TRMD 350.subject: TRMD
TRMD 350.description: Focuses on the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study of a global health problem that is optimally approached from a One Health perspective.
TRMD 350.prereq_raw: ANSC 200 , BIOL 101 , MICR 130 , PH 201 , or consent of instructor.

TRMD 395.title: One Health Journal Club
TRMD 395.subject: TRMD
TRMD 395.description: Students gain critical reading skills in the presentation and discussion of published literature on One Health-related topics.

TRMD 431.title: Principles of Medical Parasitology
TRMD 431.subject: TRMD
TRMD 431.description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.
TRMD 431.prereq_raw: MICR 351 with a grade of B or higher or equivalent.

TRMD 440.title: International Training in Biosciences Research
TRMD 440.subject: TRMD
TRMD 440.description: Combines weekly lectures by faculty for discussion of the 9 Steps of Research and completion of training courses for working with human subjects, including research ethics, laboratory safety, blood-borne pathogens, and principles of health disparity. MHIRT cohort only.

TRMD 441.title: Health Disparities
TRMD 441.subject: TRMD
TRMD 441.description: Overview of biosciences research related to health and health disparities in a global setting as well as in Hawaiʻi. Workshop topics include health research, Native Hawaiian health, global health, and cultural competency. MHIRT cohort only.

TRMD 442.title: Summer Research Experience
TRMD 442.subject: TRMD
TRMD 442.description: Hands-on research experience at assigned international sites. Students learn research and analytical skills in the field and laboratory setting, and present data to peers and faculty upon completion of the training. MHIRT cohort only.

TRMD 463.title: Medical and Urban Entomology
TRMD 463.subject: TRMD
TRMD 463.description: (2 Lec, 1-3-hr hybrid Lab) Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.
TRMD 463.prereq_raw: ( PEPS 363 or BIOL 265 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

TRMD 485.title: One Health Practicum
TRMD 485.subject: TRMD
TRMD 485.description: Provide certificate students with real-world experience and opportunity to integrate and apply classroom learning in a professional environment. Intended for students who prefer to pursue a supervised, practical experience rather than a research-based project.

TRMD 490.title: One Health Seminar
TRMD 490.subject: TRMD
TRMD 490.description: Weekly presentations and discussions on current events and research in the field of One Health. Presentation topics may include research progress, literature reviews, or research proposals.

TRMD 499.title: Reading and Research
TRMD 499.subject: TRMD
TRMD 499.description: Directed reading and research in laboratory; diagnostic aspects of bacterial, parasitic, and viral infections.

TRMD 545.title: Topics in Tropical Medicine
TRMD 545.subject: TRMD
TRMD 545.description: Elective for fourth-year medical students for advanced study of selected topics within the field of tropical medicine and medical microbiology.
TRMD 545.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Fourth-year standing or MD degree.

TRMD 546.title: One Health Elective
TRMD 546.subject: TRMD
TRMD 546.description: Foundation in One Health concepts and practical application to management of disease through recognition of the interconnection of human, animal, and ecosystem health. MD student at JABSOM only.
TRMD 546.prereq_raw: Completion of MD 3rd year clerkships and consent.

TRMD 590.title: Selected Topics in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases
TRMD 590.subject: TRMD
TRMD 590.description: Elective for medical students in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases.

TRMD 595B.title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: infectious diseases
TRMD 595B.subject: TRMD
TRMD 595B.description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 595C.title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: parasitology
TRMD 595C.subject: TRMD
TRMD 595C.description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 595D.title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: epidemiology
TRMD 595D.subject: TRMD
TRMD 595D.description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 595E.title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: immunology
TRMD 595E.subject: TRMD
TRMD 595E.description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 599B.title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: infectious diseases
TRMD 599B.subject: TRMD
TRMD 599B.description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 599C.title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: parasitology
TRMD 599C.subject: TRMD
TRMD 599C.description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 599D.title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: epidemiology
TRMD 599D.subject: TRMD
TRMD 599D.description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 599E.title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: immunology
TRMD 599E.subject: TRMD
TRMD 599E.description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

TRMD 601.title: Tropical Medicine Journal Club
TRMD 601.subject: TRMD
TRMD 601.description: Students gain experience in the presentation and discussion of topics of current interest in the fields of tropical medicine and infectious diseases.
TRMD 601.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TRMD 602.title: Laboratory Methods in Tropical Medicine
TRMD 602.subject: TRMD
TRMD 602.description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety.
TRMD 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

TRMD 603.title: Infectious Disease Microbiology I: Medical Parasitology
TRMD 603.subject: TRMD
TRMD 603.description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.

TRMD 604.title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
TRMD 604.subject: TRMD
TRMD 604.description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

TRMD 605.title: Infectious Disease Micro II
TRMD 605.subject: TRMD
TRMD 605.description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

TRMD 606.title: Tropical Medicine Laboratory Rotations
TRMD 606.subject: TRMD
TRMD 606.description: Practical experience in use of equipment and procedures in infectious disease and immunology research; introduction to research in tropical medicine.

TRMD 607.title: Neurovirology
TRMD 607.subject: TRMD
TRMD 607.description: Seminar on neuroinvasive viruses giving basics of viruses causing nervous system diseases and discussing recent advances in the research field of neurovirology.

TRMD 608.title: Infectious Disease Microbiology III
TRMD 608.subject: TRMD
TRMD 608.description: Basic structure, physiology, epidemiology, and genetics of pathogenic bacteria as well as the host response to these organisms. Correlation of these characteristics to disease pathogenesis in humans and animal models.

TRMD 609.title: Advances In Medical Immunology
TRMD 609.subject: TRMD
TRMD 609.description: Presentations/discussions of current literature concerning recent advances in immunology relevant to disease and to disease processes.

TRMD 610.title: Infection and Immunity
TRMD 610.subject: TRMD
TRMD 610.description: Combined lecture/discussion of interactions of pathogens with the innate and acquired immune systems. Topics will include the role of novel receptors in pathogen detection, inflammation in disease pathogenesis, pathogen immune evasion, and neuroimmunology.

TRMD 650.title: Ecological Epidemiology
TRMD 650.subject: TRMD
TRMD 650.description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

TRMD 651.title: Vaccinology
TRMD 651.subject: TRMD
TRMD 651.description: History/evolution of vaccines, current and next generation vaccines, vaccine immunology, adjuvants, vaccine strategies, vaccines for viral, bacterial, and parasitic diseases, vaccine-proof-of-concept and downstream developmental studies; vaccine safety production processes.
TRMD 651.prereq_raw: ( TRMD 604 and TRMD 605 ) with a minimum grade of B.
TRMD 651.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

TRMD 652.title: Advanced Genetics and Evolution of Infectious Diseases
TRMD 652.subject: TRMD
TRMD 652.description: An evolutionary perspective to examine the interactive responses between infectious agents and the immune system. Topics will include natural selection, life history evolution, population genetics of pathogens and hosts, and anti-microbial resistance.
TRMD 652.prereq_raw: TRMD 604 (or concurrent) and TRMD 605 (or concurrent), or consent.

TRMD 653.title: Bioinformatics I
TRMD 653.subject: TRMD
TRMD 653.description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis.

TRMD 654.title: Advances in HIV/AIDS
TRMD 654.subject: TRMD
TRMD 654.description: History of HIV, basic biology and virology, epidemiology, HIV pathogenesis and immunology, clinical features, and co-morbidities. Treatment and prevention of HIV/AIDS, including research methods, statistics, cultural competence, genetics, pathophysiology, drug and vaccine development.

TRMD 655.title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
TRMD 655.subject: TRMD
TRMD 655.description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

TRMD 671.title: Advanced Medical Parasitology
TRMD 671.subject: TRMD
TRMD 671.description: Consideration of ultrastructure, physiology, biochemistry, in-vitro cultivation and host-parasite relationship of parasites of medical importance.

TRMD 672.title: Advanced Medical Virology
TRMD 672.subject: TRMD
TRMD 672.description: In-depth study of the major groups of viruses pathogenic for human; virus replication, host range, pathogenesis, immunology, and epidemiology.

TRMD 673.title: Advanced Medical Bacteriology
TRMD 673.subject: TRMD
TRMD 673.description: Role of bacteria in infectious diseases, with emphasis on clinical aspects and identification of etiological agents.

TRMD 675.title: Epidemiology of Tropical Infectious Diseases
TRMD 675.subject: TRMD
TRMD 675.description: Epidemiology of infectious diseases as it relates to tropical medicine. Lecture/seminar format.
TRMD 675.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TRMD graduate standing or consent.

TRMD 690.title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
TRMD 690.subject: TRMD
TRMD 690.description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

TRMD 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
TRMD 695.subject: TRMD
TRMD 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
TRMD 695.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in TRMD.

TRMD 699.title: Directed Research
TRMD 699.subject: TRMD
TRMD 699.description: Directed research in medical microbiology (bacteriology, parasitology, virology).

TRMD 705.title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
TRMD 705.subject: TRMD
TRMD 705.description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health.

TRMD 800.title: Dissertation Research
TRMD 800.subject: TRMD
TRMD 800.prereq_raw: Approval of department faculty is required.

UNIV 110.title: University Experience
UNIV 110.subject: UNIV
UNIV 110.description: An introduction to the university community; topics include critical thinking, the value of higher education, cultural and transition issues; emphasis on writing.

UNIV 131.title: Academic and Personal Exploration
UNIV 131.subject: UNIV
UNIV 131.description: Introduction to goal setting, time management, major exploration, academic planning, service-learning opportunities, student/faculty meetings, financial literacy, and encourages frequent self-reflection.

UNIV 132.title: Academic and Career Exploration
UNIV 132.subject: UNIV
UNIV 132.description: Introduces exploratory students to major and career exploration resources, guides students in developing personal, academic, and career goals and plans, and encourages frequent self-reflection. Develops written communication skills.

UNIV 140.title: Introduction to Majors and UH Mānoa
UNIV 140.subject: UNIV
UNIV 140.description: Major exploration providing incoming students with an understanding of the tools to navigate UH Mānoa and explore the programs of study available. Introduction to career development, goal setting, and action planning. Freshmen only.

UNIV 199.title: Topics in Learning Techniques & Technologies
UNIV 199.subject: UNIV
UNIV 199.description: Student-centered topics on techniques and technologies used for successful learning. Emphasizes the cultivation of learning dispositions and strategies for achievement in higher education and beyond.

UNIV 240.title: Your Academic Journey
UNIV 240.subject: UNIV
UNIV 240.description: Provides exploratory students with the knowledge/skills to thrive in college and beyond. Utilizes writing as a tool for research, analysis, exploration, and reflection. Topics include major and career exploration, personal interests, and goal-setting. May not be taken concurrently or after UNIV 340 . Freshmen and sophomores only.

UNIV 301.title: ACE Mentoring: Facilitating Student Development
UNIV 301.subject: UNIV
UNIV 301.description: Theoretical foundations in student learning and holistic development. Practical leadership skills acquisition and application through the facilitation of a seminar for new freshmen. Emphasis on developing proficiency in writing and public speech.

UNIV 340.title: Academic Exploration Through Advising
UNIV 340.subject: UNIV
UNIV 340.description: Major exploration designed to assist exploratory students in the process of researching personal, career, and educational goals through writing and the impact of these goals on the decision-making process. Emphasis on written self-reflection and identity. Sophomore standing.

UNIV 345.title: Major Exploration: Strategic Review
UNIV 345.subject: UNIV
UNIV 345.description: Designed to guide students who, as designated, require additional support in selection of best fit major.

UNIV 350.title: Mānoa Peer Advisor Training Course
UNIV 350.subject: UNIV
UNIV 350.description: Intensive course designed for peer advisor trainees to learn General Education requirements, university policies and procedures, and campus resources. Trainees also develop skills and strategies necessary to provide quality advising to their fellow students.

UNIV 387.title: Collaborative Learning: Foundations of Tutoring
UNIV 387.subject: UNIV
UNIV 387.description: Theory and practice of collaborative learning in academic contexts. Sophomore standing or higher.

UNIV 440.title: Topics in Major and Career Exploration
UNIV 440.subject: UNIV
UNIV 440.description: Major and career development for Exploratory students, using written and oral communication to facilitate learning across varied topics.
UNIV 440.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

UNIV 445.title: Major Exploration: Major Selection for Seniors
UNIV 445.subject: UNIV
UNIV 445.description: Specially designed for designated seniors to review, reflect upon, and analyze their choice of major in order to ensure selection of best fit major and graduate efficiently with that major.
UNIV 445.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Seniors only.

UNIV 450.title: Mānoa Peer Advisor Leader Training and Leadership Practicum
UNIV 450.subject: UNIV
UNIV 450.description: A reflective apprenticeship in which Peer Advisor Leaders solidify their understanding of advising and learn more about leadership and deepen their facilitation, communication, collaboration, and leadership skills by mentoring a cohort of peer advisor trainees.
UNIV 450.prereq_raw: UNIV 350 (or equivalent course) (with a minimum grade of B).

children.text: ( or equivalent course) ( with a minimum grade of B )

UNIV 499.title: Directed Study
UNIV 499.subject: UNIV
UNIV 499.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

URDU 205.title: Reading and Writing in Urdu
URDU 205.subject: URDU
URDU 205.description: Introduces students to the Nastaliq (Urdu) script, alphabets, their various forms, and combination rules. Reading and writing is emphasized.

UROP 299.title: Transformational Research Experiences for Early Undergraduates
UROP 299.subject: UROP
UROP 299.description: Introduction to exploring discover-based investigation, with hands-on experiences in a wide range of science fields. Divided into 4-week learning modules led by researchers at several UH Mānoa research facilities on and off campus.

UROP 399.title: Faculty Mentored Research and Creative Work Project
UROP 399.subject: UROP
UROP 399.description: Directed research for undergraduate students conducting faculty-mentored research or creative work projects.
UROP 399.prereq_raw: Consent of UROP director and student faculty mentor.

children.text: of UROP director and student faculty mentor

VIET 101.title: Elementary Vietnamese I
VIET 101.subject: VIET
VIET 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets one hour, three times a week.

VIET 201.title: Intermediate Vietnamese I
VIET 201.subject: VIET
VIET 201.description: Continuation of VIET 102 . After completion, most students should be able to use all major sentence patterns to produce sounds, combinations of sounds, tones, and intonation and have some understanding of Vietnamese culture.

VIET 301.title: Third-Level Vietnamese
VIET 301.subject: VIET
VIET 301.description: Continuation of VIET 202 . Emphasis on increased proficiency and cultural understanding through interaction with Vietnamese media, including newspapers, radio, film, etc.

VIET 401.title: Fourth-Level Vietnamese
VIET 401.subject: VIET
VIET 401.description: Continuation of VIET 302 . Emphasis on cultural understanding through modern literary Vietnamese.

VIET 461.title: Introduction to Vietnamese Literature
VIET 461.subject: VIET
VIET 461.description: Selected readings in major genres; emphasis on analysis. Modern literature.

WGSS 141.title: Introduction to LGBTQ Studies
WGSS 141.subject: WGSS
WGSS 141.description: Introduction to a survey of the key terms, texts, and histories of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities with special attention to Hawaiʻi and Oceania.

WGSS 149.title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
WGSS 149.subject: WGSS
WGSS 149.description: Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E.

WGSS 151.title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
WGSS 151.subject: WGSS
WGSS 151.description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures, with a focus on gender, race, class, and sexual dynamics; exploration of women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics.

WGSS 151A.title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
WGSS 151A.subject: WGSS
WGSS 151A.description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures. Focus on gender, race, class, sexual dynamics, and women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics. Honors students only.

WGSS 175.title: History of Gender, Sex, and Sexuality in Global Perspectives to 1500 CE
WGSS 175.subject: WGSS
WGSS 175.description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from prehistory to 1500 CE. Examines ancient world civilizations from multiple perspectives stressing issues and forces still influential today.

WGSS 176.title: History of Gender, Sex and Sexuality in Global Perspective, 1500 CE to the Present
WGSS 176.subject: WGSS
WGSS 176.description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from 1500 CE to present. Examines world cultures from multiple perspectives, stressing issues and forces of continuing influence.

WGSS 200.title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
WGSS 200.subject: WGSS
WGSS 200.description: Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance.

WGSS 202.title: Psychology of Gender
WGSS 202.subject: WGSS
WGSS 202.description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to women’s lives: socialization of gender, mental health, violence against women, achievement motivation, lifespan issues, domestic violence.

WGSS 216.title: Priestesses and Prophetesses
WGSS 216.subject: WGSS
WGSS 216.description: Legendary priestesses and prophetesses from ancient to modern religions around the world including ancient Sumeria, Egypt, Greece, China, India, the Middle East, Japan, and Hawaiʻi. This course develops written communication skills.

WGSS 219.title: Women Philosophers
WGSS 219.subject: WGSS
WGSS 219.description: Introduces students to the ideas of women philosophers.
WGSS 219.prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

WGSS 245.title: Women Writers of World Literature
WGSS 245.subject: WGSS
WGSS 245.description: Major women writers of world literature examined in context of female literary tradition.
WGSS 245.prereq_raw: ENG 100 , ENG 100A , or ESL 100 ; or consent.

WGSS 257.title: Sexual Identity in Literature
WGSS 257.subject: WGSS
WGSS 257.description: Selected themes in major works of various types, cultures, periods. Requires a minimum of 3,000 words of writing.

WGSS 304.title: Women, War, and the Military
WGSS 304.subject: WGSS
WGSS 304.description: The military as it includes and excludes women as soldiers, nurses, wives, prostitutes, and victims. Women and war economics; feminism, war, and peace.
WGSS 304.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 362 , WGSS 375 or SOC 362 ; or consent.

WGSS 305.title: Women and Health
WGSS 305.subject: WGSS
WGSS 305.description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
WGSS 305.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or WGSS 202 , or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or POLS 110 ; or consent.

WGSS 306.title: Indigenous Women’s Health
WGSS 306.subject: WGSS
WGSS 306.description: Examines issues of indigenous women’s health pre and post colonial in Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific regions.
WGSS 306.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 305 ; or HWST 107 , HWST 270 or HWST 285 ; or consent.

WGSS 311.title: U.S. Women’s History
WGSS 311.subject: WGSS
WGSS 311.description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work, women in social movements, changing norms regarding gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences of women. Emphasis on ethical issues and oral communication.

WGSS 315.title: Sex and Gender
WGSS 315.subject: WGSS
WGSS 315.description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual difference; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

WGSS 318.title: Women and Social Policy
WGSS 318.subject: WGSS
WGSS 318.description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
WGSS 318.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent.
