WGSS 330.title: Gender and Sport
WGSS 330.subject: WGSS
WGSS 330.description: Explores the influence of gender in sport from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives. Through extensive writing, students examine gendered experiences of participants, spectators, and employees in sports organizations.

WGSS 339.title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
WGSS 339.subject: WGSS
WGSS 339.description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation.
WGSS 339.prereq_raw: one ES or WGSS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent.

WGSS 343.title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
WGSS 343.subject: WGSS
WGSS 343.description: Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality.
WGSS 343.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

WGSS 345.title: 20th-Century Literature by Women
WGSS 345.subject: WGSS
WGSS 345.description: Twentieth-century women writers and their works; novels, short stories, poems, autobiographies. Interrelations of gender and literature.
WGSS 345.prereq_raw: (one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 ), and WGSS 245 ; or consent.

WGSS 346.title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
WGSS 346.subject: WGSS
WGSS 346.description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
WGSS 346.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

WGSS 350.title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
WGSS 350.subject: WGSS
WGSS 350.description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

WGSS 351.title: Women, Ideas, and Society
WGSS 351.subject: WGSS
WGSS 351.description: Status of women in American society today in light of the cultural, historical, and philosophical forces that have produced it.

WGSS 356.title: Women and Religion
WGSS 356.subject: WGSS
WGSS 356.description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through reading autobiographies, films, and primary texts, and through the development of research and writing skills.
WGSS 356.prereq_raw: WGSS 149 or REL 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151 .

WGSS 357.title: Queer Dance Exploratory
WGSS 357.subject: WGSS
WGSS 357.description: Queer dance exploration in movement practices and performance.
WGSS 357.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all majors.

WGSS 360.title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawaiʻi
WGSS 360.subject: WGSS
WGSS 360.description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawaiʻi; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
WGSS 360.prereq_raw: any ANTH, SOC, or WGSS course.

WGSS 361.title: Seminar: Women and International Development
WGSS 361.subject: WGSS
WGSS 361.description: Topics: Women’s role, status, work and treatment; ethical considerations of economic development, changing work/family roles, agriculture and business, improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World global feminization of poverty. Open to nonmajors.
WGSS 361.prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent.

WGSS 362.title: Sociology of Gender
WGSS 362.subject: WGSS
WGSS 362.description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
WGSS 362.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200 -level SOC course; or consent

WGSS 367.title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
WGSS 367.subject: WGSS
WGSS 367.description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
WGSS 367.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200 -level SOC course, or consent

WGSS 371.title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
WGSS 371.subject: WGSS
WGSS 371.description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher.
WGSS 371.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

WGSS 375.title: Women and the Media
WGSS 375.subject: WGSS
WGSS 375.description: Role and representation of women and non-binary communities in the media. Feminist alternatives to mainstream media and dominant narratives. Emphasis on oral communication to empower marginalized voices.

WGSS 381.title: Gender, Sexuality and Literature
WGSS 381.subject: WGSS
WGSS 381.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literary constructions of gender and sexuality; emphasis on teaching gender and sexuality through writing and oral communication.
WGSS 381.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

WGSS 382.title: Island Feminisms: Art, Literature, and Culture
WGSS 382.subject: WGSS
WGSS 382.description: Examines island feminisms and explores ways women have engaged in various forms of cultural production (art, literature, film). Interdisciplinary, intersectional, and transnational. Key themes discussed: settler-colonialism, race, gender, and sexuality.

WGSS 384.title: Women and Politics
WGSS 384.subject: WGSS
WGSS 384.description: Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries; female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions.
WGSS 384.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 (or concurrent) or WGSS 362 (or concurrent) or any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent); or consent.

WGSS 390.title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
WGSS 390.subject: WGSS
WGSS 390.description: Intersecting processes of racial and gender oppression and privilege; institutional contexts and lived experiences; ethical issues in past and present anti-racist feminist thought and activism in the United States and in Hawaiʻi.
WGSS 390.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or ES 101 or junior standing.

WGSS 392.title: Sexualities
WGSS 392.subject: WGSS
WGSS 392.description: Multi-disciplinary course that draws from various disciplines in Social Science to explore human sexualities. Significant focus on ethical dilemmas and the utilization of ethical frameworks anchored in utilitarianism, rights, justice, virtue, and the common good.
WGSS 392.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 315 or WGSS 350 ; or consent.

WGSS 394.title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives
WGSS 394.subject: WGSS
WGSS 394.description: Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change.
WGSS 394.prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or POLS 390 (or concurrent) or POLS 382 , WGSS 151 , or consent.

children.text: -level POLS course or POLS 390 (or concurrent) or POLS 382 , WGSS 151 , or consent

WGSS 410.title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
WGSS 410.subject: WGSS
WGSS 410.description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

WGSS 412.title: Gender, Sexuality, and the Geopolitics of Korean Popular Culture
WGSS 412.subject: WGSS
WGSS 412.description: Using South Korean popular culture as a case study, this lecture/discussion/seminar examines the relationship between popular culture and a range of forces including: politics, international relations, military, social movements, fandoms, and industries.
WGSS 412.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

WGSS 414.title: Women, Gender, & Sexuality in Performance
WGSS 414.subject: WGSS
WGSS 414.description: Feminist and performance studies approaches to performances by women and other genders; focus on the representation and status of women

WGSS 418.title: Gender and Work
WGSS 418.subject: WGSS
WGSS 418.description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
WGSS 418.prereq_raw: one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

WGSS 419.title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy
WGSS 419.subject: WGSS
WGSS 419.description: Examination of basic feminist issues in philosophy, and of responses to them.
WGSS 419.prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

WGSS 424.title: Gender, Sexuality and Digital Media
WGSS 424.subject: WGSS
WGSS 424.description: Students learn how gender and sexuality are constructed online and produce a website to post their analysis and contribute to knowledge production about gender and sexuality in cyberspace.

WGSS 426.title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
WGSS 426.subject: WGSS
WGSS 426.description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.
WGSS 426.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

WGSS 430.title: Seminar in the Biology of Women
WGSS 430.subject: WGSS
WGSS 430.description: Embryological, anatomical, and physiological development of human female; hormonal, neural, and behavioral determinants of female sexual behavior; psychobiology of pregnancy, ovariectomy, and menopause.
WGSS 430.prereq_raw: WGSS 350 or BIOL 172 or BIOL 350 , or consent.

WGSS 433.title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
WGSS 433.subject: WGSS
WGSS 433.description: Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication.

WGSS 434.title: Women and Madness
WGSS 434.subject: WGSS
WGSS 434.description: Interdisciplinary critical examination of the relationship between gender and mental health. Psychological research, feminist theory, autobiography, literature, and cinema.
WGSS 434.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 202 , WGSS 245 , PSY 202 ; or consent.

WGSS 435.title: Women and Crime
WGSS 435.subject: WGSS
WGSS 435.description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
WGSS 435.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

WGSS 436.title: Gender, Justice and Law
WGSS 436.subject: WGSS
WGSS 436.description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.
WGSS 436.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 381 , or consent.

WGSS 437.title: Gender and Violence
WGSS 437.subject: WGSS
WGSS 437.description: Interdisciplinary course will examine western constructs of gender violence on its correlates with ethnicity, class, sexuality, nation, and empire.
WGSS 437.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 361 , WGSS 439 , WGSS 460 , WGSS 462 , or consent.

WGSS 438.title: Gender and Environmental Philosophy
WGSS 438.subject: WGSS
WGSS 438.description: Interdisciplinary approach to feminist perspectives on environmental issues; critical analysis of eco-feminism as political movement with reference to race and coloniality; cross-cultural comparison of differently-imagined relationships to non-human others, with emphasis on ethics and writing.
WGSS 438.prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS or any course 200 or above with a DB or DP designation, or consent.

WGSS 439.title: Feminist Theory
WGSS 439.subject: WGSS
WGSS 439.description: Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.”
WGSS 439.prereq_raw: any 300 level WGSS or POLS course, or consent.

WGSS 440.title: Feminist Methods and Research
WGSS 440.subject: WGSS
WGSS 440.description: Overview of feminist issues with dominant theories of knowledge and major methodologies employed in the social sciences; and exploration of role of gender theory and feminist politics in feminist research.

WGSS 441.title: Queer Theory
WGSS 441.subject: WGSS
WGSS 441.description: Intensive survey of the key theories, texts, and questions of the interdisciplinary fields that make up queer theory.
WGSS 441.prereq_raw: WGSS 141 or WGSS 151 or WGSS 392 or consent.

WGSS 444.title: Gender and Consumption in a Global World
WGSS 444.subject: WGSS
WGSS 444.description: Students learn theories of the global economy, histories of consumerism, constructions of gendered public spaces, and how the cultural production of consumers and consumer culture functions in the process of globalization.

WGSS 445.title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
WGSS 445.subject: WGSS
WGSS 445.description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

WGSS 446.title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
WGSS 446.subject: WGSS
WGSS 446.description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
WGSS 446.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, SOC 300 ; or consent.

WGSS 450.title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawaiʻi
WGSS 450.subject: WGSS
WGSS 450.description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai’i. The course develops written communication skills.
WGSS 450.prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

WGSS 450.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

WGSS 452.title: Marriage and Family: Feminist Perspective
WGSS 452.subject: WGSS
WGSS 452.description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
WGSS 452.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

WGSS 453.title: Gender Issues in Education
WGSS 453.subject: WGSS
WGSS 453.description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper.

WGSS 454.title: Gender, Sexuality, and Global Popular Culture
WGSS 454.subject: WGSS
WGSS 454.description: A study of gender, race, and sexuality as constructed in contemporary global popular culture, including music, films, novels, television shows, and internet culture.

WGSS 456.title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
WGSS 456.subject: WGSS
WGSS 456.description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.
WGSS 456.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , or WGSS 202 ; or consent.

WGSS 460.title: Feminism, Nation and Empire
WGSS 460.subject: WGSS
WGSS 460.description: Examines U.S. feminist movements in the 19th and 20th century by exploring how U.S. racism, nationalism and imperialism have provided the context from which feminism emerged.

WGSS 462.title: Women and Globalization in Asia
WGSS 462.subject: WGSS
WGSS 462.description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
WGSS 462.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 360 , WGSS 361 , WGSS 439 , AMST 310 , AMST 316 , AMST 318 , AMST 373 , AMST 455 , POLS 339 ; or consent.

WGSS 463.title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
WGSS 463.subject: WGSS
WGSS 463.description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g. with class, religion, ethnicity).

WGSS 465.title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
WGSS 465.subject: WGSS
WGSS 465.description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

WGSS 466.title: Gender in Action Cinema
WGSS 466.subject: WGSS
WGSS 466.description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

WGSS 481.title: Women and Film
WGSS 481.subject: WGSS
WGSS 481.description: Exploration of film as a philosophical and artistic form in the context of gender, race, and sexuality.
WGSS 481.prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , or THEA 201 ; or consent.

WGSS 482.title: Indigenous Feminisms
WGSS 482.subject: WGSS
WGSS 482.description: Examines the origins and futures of Indigenous feminist theory and praxis. Topics explored include cultural revitalization, colonialism, and sexual violence in Indigenous communities, citizenship and sovereignty, and contemporary Native gender roles and identity.

WGSS 483.title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
WGSS 483.subject: WGSS
WGSS 483.description: Intensive study of selected questions and issues in the construction and representation of sexuality and gender in specific genres, social and cultural contexts, or thematic/figurative clusters.
WGSS 483.prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

WGSS 485.title: Women and Disasters
WGSS 485.subject: WGSS
WGSS 485.description: Explores disasters and their consequences for women, with attention to gender, race, sexuality, and class.
WGSS 485.prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS, or consent of instructor.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS,

WGSS 489.title: Social Sciences Internship
WGSS 489.subject: WGSS
WGSS 489.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories.

WGSS 492.title: Women and Revolution
WGSS 492.subject: WGSS
WGSS 492.description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

WGSS 493.title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
WGSS 493.subject: WGSS
WGSS 493.description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration. Junior standing or higher.

WGSS 495.title: Selected Topics
WGSS 495.subject: WGSS
WGSS 495.description: Problems and issues for reading and research: feminist theory, criticism, affirmative action, etc.
WGSS 495.prereq_raw: any WGSS course in appropriate area.

prereq_tree.text: any WGSS course in appropriate area

WGSS 496.title: Teaching Women’s Studies
WGSS 496.subject: WGSS
WGSS 496.description: Strategies for teaching women’s studies; addressing complex issues of gender, race, nation, class, sexuality and culture in a contemporary multiethnic campus environment. Emphasis on classroom techniques, teaching pedagogies, and hands-on experience.
WGSS 496.prereq_raw: WGSS 151 and one or more WGSS course with a grade of B or better in all relevant courses, instructor recommendation; or consent.

children.text: more WGSS course with a grade of B or better in all relevant courses, instructor recommendation;

WGSS 602.title: Transnational Feminist Teaching and Research
WGSS 602.subject: WGSS
WGSS 602.description: Introductory graduate seminar designed to develop common vocabulary and explore the core debates in transnational feminist teaching and research to encourage critical reflection about teaching assumptions, approaches, and techniques in the contemporary college or university environment.
WGSS 602.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 610.title: Faculty Seminar Series
WGSS 610.subject: WGSS
WGSS 610.description: Seminar/discussion to introduce students pursuing the Graduate Certificate to the Women’s Studies faculty and their areas of research, and to initiate student’s graduate studies in a women’s studies field.
WGSS 610.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 612.title: Women in American Culture
WGSS 612.subject: WGSS
WGSS 612.description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

WGSS 613.title: Feminist Research and Methods of Inquiry
WGSS 613.subject: WGSS
WGSS 613.description: Examination of an emergent body of literature about how to shape questions concerning gender, sex, race, class, colonialism, and other vectors of power. Includes methods from social sciences and humanities and debates in the philosophy of science.
WGSS 613.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 614.title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
WGSS 614.subject: WGSS
WGSS 614.description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

WGSS 615.title: Feminist Theory
WGSS 615.subject: WGSS
WGSS 615.description: Selected ideas from contemporary feminist theory concerning power, knowledge, and self; articulating women’s voice; deconstructing gender.

WGSS 616.title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
WGSS 616.subject: WGSS
WGSS 616.description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance.

WGSS 618.title: Writing and Publishing in an Interdisciplinary Field
WGSS 618.subject: WGSS
WGSS 618.description: Writing-intensive and publishing-focused class, students learn how to publish in an interdisciplinary field. Readings and assignments are designed to help students succeed in academic publishing.
WGSS 618.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 620.title: Feminism and Its “Others”
WGSS 620.subject: WGSS
WGSS 620.description: Relationship between feminist and other sites of critical insight and scholarship that have contributed to creating anticolonial, antiracist, antihomophobic theory, method and action. Questions the legacy of feminist coalition practices and engages the ongoing transformations that have begun to produce new alliances and coalitions that disrupt traditional boundaries of identity and power.
WGSS 620.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 623.title: Topics in Feminist Social Policy Research
WGSS 623.subject: WGSS
WGSS 623.description: Feminist social scientists from a variety of fields have explored issues of gender, social change and social justice. Draws from their work to critically examine strategies for conducting social policy research that is feminist in values and impact.
WGSS 623.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 625.title: Feminist Criminology
WGSS 625.subject: WGSS
WGSS 625.description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

WGSS 641.title: Advanced Queer Theory
WGSS 641.subject: WGSS
WGSS 641.description: Advanced graduate seminar on the key ideas within queer theory. Students will become familiar with theories of queer relationality, queer of color critique, globalization of sexuality, disability and transgender studies, and queer indigeneities.
WGSS 641.prereq_raw: undergraduate or graduate course work in women’s, gender, sexuality, or LGBTQ studies.

WGSS 647.title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
WGSS 647.subject: WGSS
WGSS 647.description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

WGSS 650.title: Research in Feminist Studies: Capstone Experience
WGSS 650.subject: WGSS
WGSS 650.description: Provide women’s studies graduate certificate students with an opportunity to design, develop and complete a research project culminating in a publishable quality work and a professional quality seminar presentation.
WGSS 650.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

WGSS 699.title: Directed Reading and Research

ZOOL 101.title: Principles of Zoology
ZOOL 101.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 101.description: Structure, development, physiology, reproduction, evolution, behavior, and ecology of animals.

ZOOL 200.title: Marine Biology
ZOOL 200.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 200.description: Biology and ecology of marine plants and animals; coral reefs, the deep sea, rocky shores, marine mammals, fisheries, aquaculture, pollution, and conservation of marine resources.

ZOOL 200L.title: Marine Biology Lab
ZOOL 200L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 200L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory, field trips to accompany ZOOL 200 .

ZOOL 420.title: Developmental Biology
ZOOL 420.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 420.description: Fundamental principles, methods, concepts, and significance of developmental biology, emphasizing experimental methods.

ZOOL 420L.title: Developmental Biology Lab
ZOOL 420L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 420L.description: (2 3-hr Labs) Analysis of animal development by experimental methods, using local organisms. Emphasis on biology writing instruction.
ZOOL 420L.prereq_raw: ZOOL 420 (or concurrent) and BIOL 275 , or consent. Recommended: BIOL 407 .

ZOOL 430.title: Animal Physiology
ZOOL 430.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 430.description: Lecture/laboratory introduction to animal physiology, especially vertebrates. Topics include nerve and muscle physiology, metabolism, circulation, respiration, excretion, and thermoregulation in a project-driven format. Labs develop skills in experimental biology, morphology, data analysis, and scientific writing.

ZOOL 432.title: Comparative Physiology
ZOOL 432.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 432.description: Physical-chemical cellular mechanisms underlying function of organ systems; general principles inferable from study of adaption to diverse environments.
ZOOL 432.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 , and MBBE 402 (or concurrent) or BIOC 441 (or concurrent); or consent.

ZOOL 442.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
ZOOL 442.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 442.description: Nerve cells, their signaling capabilities and the developmental organization of nervous systems, both invertebrate and vertebrate, for sensory reception, integration, behavioral command and learning; insights from on-going research using molecular, genetic, biophysical, and imaging methods.

ZOOL 460.title: Avian Biology
ZOOL 460.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 460.description: Broad coverage of the morphology, physiology, ecology, behavior, and evolution of birds, emphasizing the relation of birds to general theory in biology.

ZOOL 490B.title: Seminar in Zoology: general zoology
ZOOL 490B.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 490B.description: Reports on research, reviews of literature, or research experience. Required of students majoring in zoology or entomology. (B) general zoology; (D) animal behavior; (E) ecology; (F) physiology; (G) developmental biology; (H) marine biology.
ZOOL 490B.prereq_raw: ZOOL 306 or equivalent or consent for (D).

ZOOL 490D.subject: ZOOL

ZOOL 490H.subject: ZOOL

ZOOL 490H.prereq_raw: ZOOL 306 or equivalent or consent for (D).

ZOOL 606.title: Animal Behavior
ZOOL 606.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 606.description: Lectures and critical discussions on the mechanisms of animal behavior, social and interspecific behaviors, behavioral ecology, and evolutionary theory.
ZOOL 606.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ZOOL 606L.title: Principles of Animal Behavior Lab
ZOOL 606L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 606L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Group or individual research projects depending on interest of students.

ZOOL 607.title: Genetics of Behavior and Evolution
ZOOL 607.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 607.description: Introduction to concepts and techniques in the genetics of behavior. Techniques include next gen sequencing, GWAS, and more. Students may use real data to analyze associations between genotype and phenotype.
ZOOL 607.restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

ZOOL 608.title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology
ZOOL 608.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 608.description: Lectures, readings and presentations on sensory systems and behavior of fishes.
ZOOL 608.prereq_raw: ZOOL 430 , ZOOL 606 , BIOL 306 , BIOL 465 ; or consent.

ZOOL 608L.title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology Laboratory
ZOOL 608L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 608L.description: Laboratory study of fish sensory systems and behavior.
ZOOL 608L.prereq_raw: ZOOL 430 , ZOOL 606 , BIOL 306 , BIOL 465 ; or consent.

ZOOL 610.title: Topics in Development and Reproductive Biology
ZOOL 610.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 610.description: Discussion and survey of literature on specific topics; some field and lab work may be required.

ZOOL 615.title: Quantitative Genomics and Evolution
ZOOL 615.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 615.description: Overview and lab-based course exploring theory and methods to understand genome evolution and adaptation; focus will be on a range of organisms.

ZOOL 619.title: Seminar on Science Teaching
ZOOL 619.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 619.description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audio-visual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

ZOOL 620.title: Marine Ecology
ZOOL 620.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 620.description: Principles of ecology of marine biota and environment.
ZOOL 620.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in zoology, oceanography, or botany; or consent.

ZOOL 623.title: Quantitative Field Ecology
ZOOL 623.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 623.description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab, 1 Discussion) Formal quantitative approach in identifying, designing, performing, analyzing, and interpreting ecological field problems.
ZOOL 623.prereq_raw: ZOOL 439, ZOOL 439L, and ZOOL 631 ; or consent.

ZOOL 625.title: Evolution in Marine Systems
ZOOL 625.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 625.description: Fundamental elements of modern evolutionary theory and research, with a strong focus on marine organisms and ecosystems.

ZOOL 631.title: Introduction to Statistical Modeling in Biology
ZOOL 631.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 631.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Statistical methods for biological research. Covers: probability; likelihood-based inference; hypothesis testing; linear and generalized linear models; common statistical tests; statistical programming.
ZOOL 631.prereq_raw: MATH 215 or MATH 216 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A or NREM 203 (or equivalent), or consent.

ZOOL 632.title: Advanced Biometry
ZOOL 632.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 632.description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Multivariate statistical methods: multiple regression and correlation; multiway anova; general linear models; repeated measures and multivariate anova; loglinear analysis and logistic regression.

ZOOL 642.title: Cellular Neurophysiology
ZOOL 642.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 642.description: Biophysical and membrane mechanisms of conduction, synaptic transmission, and other electrical responses of nerve cells.

ZOOL 652.title: Population Biology
ZOOL 652.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 652.description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology.
ZOOL 652.prereq_raw: one of the following: ZOOL 620 , ZOOL 623 , BOT 456 , NREM 680 , PEPS 671 ; or consent.

ZOOL 670.title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
ZOOL 670.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 670.description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques.
ZOOL 670.restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only.

ZOOL 690.title: Conservation Biology
ZOOL 690.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 690.description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.
